# Workflow system

The technical design and the build of the workflow platform: an editor in which authors build their own workflows, an engine that runs them, and the connections to other systems.

Status: started 2026-11-15. Design first, then code. The engine's core package (`engine/packages/core`) is built and runs the kernel spec's cases in its tests; the server (`engine/packages/server`) runs requests on PGlite, and its development host serves both APIs with the mock systems (`engine/DEV-HOST.md`).

## Layout and ownership

Two sessions work in this repo. Each writes only its own folder, plus the files it holds the pen on in `docs/` and `contract/`.

| Path | What it is | Pen |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/` | The technical design: one Markdown file per document, diagrams in Mermaid. Each file's header names its owner. | Per file |
| `contract/` | The interface between frontend and engine: the authored workflow format, the authoring API, the runtime API, the catalogue of connections. | Per file |
| `engine/` | The backend: kernel, compiler, checks, server, workers, connectors, mock outside systems. | Engine owner |
| `engine/spec/` | A read-only copy of the engine design package (kernel spec v2.20), made by `npm run sync-spec` in `engine/`. See `engine/spec/SOURCE.md`. | Nobody edits it here |
| `frontend/` | The editor and the pages. | Frontend owner |

Related folders outside this repo, kept beside it (paths relative to this repo's root):

- `../workflow-platform`: requirements, the engine design package's source, research and the decision log. `engine/scripts/sync-spec.mjs` reads it from there.
- `../workflow`: the mockups and UX work. The UX reference.

## Rules

- Commit with explicit paths (`git commit -- <paths>`), so one session never sweeps up the other's work.
- No npm workspaces at the repo root. `engine/` and `frontend/` each have their own `package.json` and `node_modules`.
- Platform code never names a customer workflow. "Change request" is sample data.
- A decision made by a session overnight is logged in that session's decision file in `docs/` and stays pending the product owner's review.

# Contract Drafts 2 and 3: changes for the frontend

Engine owner, 2026-11-15. Revised 2026-11-15 after E-21 to E-26, and 2026-11-16 for E-27 and E-28 (kernel spec v2.19). What E-27 and E-28 settle is listed at the end of `core-api.md` section 16, not repeated here.

Covers `core-api.md`, `authoring-api.md`, `runtime-api.md` and `catalogue.ts` at Draft 3, against `frontend/src/services/CONTRACT-NOTES.md` and `types-*.ts`, under decisions E-1 to E-28. Sections (a) to (c) were written for Draft 2; where Draft 3 changes an item, the item says so. Section (d) lists Draft 3's changes as first sent, (d2) what changed since that Draft 3 (the revision after E-21 to E-23), (d3) E-24's wording decisions, none of which changes a type, (d4) E-25's and E-26's changes, (e) the engine's asks to the frontend, (f) the questions still open. The file keeps its Draft 2 name so links to it hold. Where an earlier section and (d2), (d3) or (d4) disagree, the later section holds.

## (a) CONTRACT-NOTES.md, item by item (Draft 2)

Taken as drafted

- Imported contract types (`AuthoredWorkflow`, IDs, `Location`, `Catalogue`, `DirectoryApi`, `Ref` = `{ type, id }`): confirmed.
- core-api.md items (`check`, `valuesInScope`, `checkFormula`, `diff`, `createTestHost`, `upgrade`, `CoreMeta`, findings, changes, `CallFake`, host methods): confirmed, with the changes in (b) 11 to 13 and (d).
- authoring-api.md items: confirmed. Eleven operations (`getCatalogue` added as `GET /catalogue`, which serves `CatalogueService`).
- runtime-api.md items: confirmed, with the renames in (b) 7 to 9. Draft 2's stop causes (`StuckCause`) are replaced in Draft 3 by `StuckReason` (d 1).
- R1 to R6, Settings with `description`, locations `{ item, part? }`: confirmed.

Chosen by the frontend

1. One `Result<T>` with `errors[]`: adopted (core 2.6).
2. `TurnResult<T>` with `refusals`, `Refusal` = `ApiError`: adopted.
3. Typed params per code, always present: adopted. The engine always sends `params`, `{}` when empty.
4. Unknown codes as `code: 'unknown'`: client-side; nothing changes in the contract. Every code list is open.
5. One code per meaning (`unauthenticated`, `invalid-body`, `not-found` with `what`); `check`'s message at top level: adopted.
6. Expression error list `no-such-key` ...: adopted as `ExpressionErrorKind`.
7. No `null`: adopted for every API body. Events keep their nullable fields, seen only under `debug`. Draft 3 adds two exceptions that follow `integrations-shapes.md`: the catalogue and the inbound answer (core 1).
8. `Facts`: adopted unchanged.
9. `ValueInScope.kind` optional; Requester and Started on not values: adopted.
10. `evaluate` shape: adopted. A `Template` evaluates to `MessagePart[]`. Added `evaluateSent` (missing item 5).
11. `formState` fifth argument: adopted. Added a sixth, `lookups`, and a `needsLookups` result (missing item 2). `FormState` gains `choices`. Draft 3 makes the catalogue the second parameter and limits `choices` to formula questions (d 3, d 4).
12. `Fakes.clock` as a function: not adopted. Replaced by `Fakes.startAt` (data): core reads no clock, and a function cannot cross into a worker.
13. One `RequestView`: adopted.
14. One `OpenTask`: adopted without `required` (R8: every task must be answered).
15. One `ButtonState` with `refusals[]`: adopted.
16. Problems `stuck` / `nobody-asked` / `action-retrying`: adopted in Draft 2. Draft 3 replaces them with one `stuck` state and moves the action's live detail into `OpenAction.admin` (d 1).
17. Story entries: adopted. Added `value.saved`. `moved.why.reads` changed shape; `notFitting` optional (b 4).
18. Outbox: adopted. Built-in message codes are the words file's keys, with params (b 5); `BuiltInTold` adds `unstuck` (E-17's six event types).
19. `startFrom` result: adopted unchanged. The inbound answer maps onto it (runtime 8).
20. `Fakes.stuckRequestsGoTo`: adopted.
21. `ServerWorkflowId`, `VersionNumber`: adopted.
22. `Settings` with optional `stuckRequestsGoTo`, no revision, no runtime admin endpoints: adopted. An empty list is refused (`invalid-body`, `empty`).
23. `Version` without the compiled definition: adopted.
24. `createWorkflow` with optional `description`; `WorkflowSummary.description`: adopted.
25. `getMeta(): Result<CoreMeta>`: adopted.
26. `RuntimeService` operations; `previewStart`, `previewTask`, `listAttempts` dropped; `TurnDone`: adopted. Added `listBindings`, `setBindingPaused` (E-17: a binding can be paused without publishing).
27. `choices` by catalogue source: not adopted. E-17 decides it: the page names the question; the server works out the source's inputs, and looks the answer up by stored value when the person acts. Draft 3 extends the same call to directory choices (d 3).
28. `TaskView` with `requester?`, `startedOn`, `askedOf`: adopted, without `required`, `form`, `buttons`, with `lookups`. In Draft 3 `lookups` serves the form's conditions only (d 3).
29. `RequestQuery.stuck: boolean`: adopted.
30. `SessionService`: adopted as development-host HTTP (runtime 7); `signInAs` elsewhere is `forbidden` with `need: "devHost"`.
31. `CatalogueService`, `DirectoryService`: adopted; HTTP in authoring 5 and runtime 7.

Contradictions between the drafts

2. Part names: the authored field names. Complete list: core 2.3.
3. Refusal parts `requesterCanAnswer`, `enabledWhen`: in the list (core 2.3). See ask (e) 3.

## (b) Shapes in `types-*.ts` that differ from Draft 2, most disruptive first

1. `RuntimeService.choices`: args `{ form: { workflow, version } | { requestId, task }; question; answers; search?; cursor?; limit? }`. Draft 2 served source questions only; Draft 3 also serves directory questions and changes the page's items (d 3). Error `source-unavailable`.
2. `CoreService.formState` returns `{ result: 'state'; state: FormState } | { result: 'needsLookups'; lookups }`. Draft 3's parameters are `(workflow, catalogue, task, answers, values, request?, lookups?)` (d 4). A Show when that cannot be worked out counts as shown, a choices formula that cannot be worked out gives no entry, and every button's `refusal` is that `rule-error`.
3. `StartForm`: no `form`, `buttons`. `TaskView`: no `form`, `buttons`, `required`; new `lookups: KnownLookups`.
4. `MoveWhy`: `reads: WhyRead[]` with `WhyRead = { of: ReadOf; value? }`, `ReadOf` = value (+ path) | request field | `pressed: TaskId` | list cell. `notFitting` optional.
5. Outbox notification `from`: `{ action } | { builtIn: { code, params } }`, codes `task.assigned`, `request.stuck`, `start.refused`, and in Draft 2 a separate nobody-to-ask message, which E-21 drops (d2 3); `location` moves into params. Draft 3 renames `request.stuck`'s `cause` to `reason` (d 1).
6. `By.type`: `'connector'` is `'connection'` (E-17).
7. Error codes renamed: `directory-unavailable` is `membership-unavailable`; `choices-unavailable` is `source-unavailable`. New: `invalid-document`, `mapping-error`, `unfinished` (Try it: `startFrom` on a binding, or `start` when the start task, has a To do that stops a request from running). `membership-unavailable` can also refuse `saveDraft`, `publish` and `saveSettings` when a group must admit the author. Draft 2's inbound-only codes `unreadable` and `connection-disabled` are removed in Draft 3: the inbound endpoint has its own bodies (d 7).
8. Error params: `check` is `{ button }` (no `checkId`); `rule-error` is `{ error }` (no `rule`, `checkId`; the location says where); `invalid-data` is `{ rule }` (no `question`; the location is the question); `wait-not-open.by` is `By`; `invalid-body` is `{ field, problem }` (no `path`; problems add `empty`, `tooLong`, `format`); `stale` is `{ lastSeq }`; `not-found.what` adds `binding`, `question`; `forbidden.need` is `'author' | 'devHost'`.
9. `InvalidDataRule` adds `hidden-answered`.
10. `required` removed from `OpenTask`, `TaskView` and `task.opened`.
11. Findings renamed: `action.unknownOperation` is `catalogue.unknownEntry` `{ entry, expected }`; `action.connectionNotSetUp` is `catalogue.connectionNotSetUp`; `action.inputMissing` is `catalogue.inputMissing`; `action.inputKindMismatch` is `expression.kindMismatch` `{ expected: ValueKind[]; found }`. Params: `action.failureHasNowhereToGo` `{ failed?, code? }`. New: `start.notOneTask`, `start.needsStatus`, `start.directoryInCondition`, `startsWhen.neededNotFilled`, `clause.wordsDoNotFit`, `clause.pressedOutsideStage`, `arrow.otherCasesNotLast`, `catalogue.unknownField`, `requester.mayBeEmpty` (worth knowing). Draft 3 changes to findings: (d 5), (d 9), (d 10).
12. `Fakes`: `clock` removed; `startAt: Timestamp` required; `sources?` added.
13. `TestHost`: `preview` removed; `openTasks` filter adds `as`; `request(requestId, as?)`; `choices(...)` added. `startFrom` on an unknown binding is `not-found` (`binding`); a refused start puts one `start.refused` message in the outbox. An unfinished start stage still starts and is then stuck with `unfinished`.
14. `OpenAction.admin.state`: `'in-flight'` is `'inFlight'`; adds `'accepted'`.
15. `StoryParams` adds `value.saved`; `StoryEntry.debug` is `{ events: unknown[] }`, live only for platform admins with `debug=true`; `GetRequestArgs` adds `debug?: boolean`. `RequestView.stage.part` may also be `arrows`.
16. `BuiltInTold` adds `unstuck`.
17. Draft 2 added `action-overdue` to the problems; Draft 3 moves it to `OpenAction.admin.overdue` (d 1).
18. `WorkflowSummary` adds `triggers: { live: CatalogueRef[]; draft: CatalogueRef[] }`.
19. `RuntimeService` adds `listBindings`, `setBindingPaused`; new type `BindingState`.
20. `CoreService` adds `parse` (`ParseProblem`), `evaluateSent`, `sampleValues`; core exports `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS`.
21. `Answers` and `Values`: content fixed by core 2.4; an empty answer is a missing key (`""` and `[]` are refused, `too-short`).
22. `SessionService` over HTTP returns `Result`; the client may unwrap.
23. An authored document inside a body or a result keeps the nulls the authored format allows (`goTo`, `when.button`), so an unfinished draft saves. `part.changed` may name any field of an item, not only the parts in core 2.3.

## (d) Draft 3: what changed, most disruptive first

1. **Stuck is one state (E-19, E-20).** `Stuck { reason, at, location?, admin? }`, the same in `RequestView.stuck`, `RequestRow.stuck` (lists never carry `admin`) and the story's `stuck` entry, whose params are a `Stuck`. Reasons, kebab-case: `action-failed`, `nobody-to-ask`, `nothing-fits`, `error`, and `unfinished` in Try it. From Draft 2: `action-failed` stays; `expression-error` and `too-many-moves` are `error` (`admin.fault` tells them apart: `cel-error` ..., `firing-limit`); `no-way-on` is `nothing-fits`; the `nobody-asked` problem is `nobody-to-ask`. `RequestView.problems`, `Problem`, `ProblemParams` and `StuckCause` are removed. The engineers' detail (`fault`, `error`, `key`, `index`, `text`, `outsideText`) sits under `Stuck.admin`, filled only for the people who look after stuck requests and platform admins. `ApiErrorBase.outsideText` is removed. `action-retrying` and `action-overdue` become `OpenAction.admin` fields (`attempts`, `lastError`, `expectedBy`, `overdue`). `request.stuck`'s param `cause` is `reason`. `StartResult.stopped` and `TurnDone.stopped` count every reason, `nobody-to-ask` included. Core 8, 9; runtime 6.
2. **Retry and close (E-19, E-20; narrowed by E-23, d2 2).** Retry only for a stuck request, else the new refusal `not-stuck` (409, an attempt). Close for any open request, so a request with a merely slow call can be ended (core 15 explains why Close is not limited to stuck requests). Runtime 5.1 says what Retry does per reason and states E-19's two limits.
3. **Choices (E-20).** One question-scoped call, `runtime.choices` and `TestHost.choices`, for every question whose choices come from the directory or a data source, on the start form too. Its items are `ChoiceOption { value, label }`, where `value` is exactly the answer to send: `{ stored, label }` from a source, `{ type: "user", id }` from the directory. Directory choices are read through the directory connection's group-members data source, so they behave as any other source. When the person acts, each answer is looked up again: not found is the new code `choice-unknown` (422, an attempt), which replaces `invalid-data` / `not-a-choice` for these questions; a source that cannot be asked, the directory's included, is `source-unavailable` (503, try again, not an attempt). `membership-unavailable` stays for the caller's own groups. `not-a-choice` now covers only typed-in choices and list rows. The recorded-list path for directory choices is removed: `FormState.choices` holds formula choices only. `TaskView.lookups` stays, narrowed to what the form's conditions read; the `needsLookups` round trip in `formState` and `evaluate` stays for conditions. A published start form never needs lookups.
4. **`formState` takes the catalogue** as its second parameter (E-20).
5. **`Finding.debug`.** `compile.internal`'s params are `{}`; its detail is `debug.detail`, like the story's `debug` (E-20).
6. **Try it and unfinished drafts (E-20).** A draft is unfinished only where a To do stops a request from running. Core 4 marks each finding in a "Stops Try it" column and lists the `item.partMissing` parts that do. Words and labels never block Try it. Other To dos are left for the request to meet (stuck with `error` or `nothing-fits`, or a start refused as live).
7. **Inbound endpoint.** `POST {hooks}/hooks/v1/events/{connection}`, with the bodies and codes of `integrations-shapes.md` 3.6 to 3.8: every non-200 answer is `{ "error": string }` (`too-large`, `unknown-connection`, `connection-unavailable`, `unauthenticated`, `unparsable`, `event-invalid`, `unavailable`). Verification is the connector's job (E-20). A refused result carries `problems: InboundProblem[]` with `where`, not `refusals`; `readableId` is a number; `started` has no `stopped`. A try-again answer is `503 unavailable` and tells nobody; only final refusals alert. Runtime 8.
8. **Spelling of codes** stated once (core 1.1, E-17, E-20).
9. **Findings.** `action.repeatNotChosen` withdrawn. New: `formula.notInProfile` (todo; a time zone, or `\p` / `\P` in a pattern), `catalogue.connectionDisabled` and `catalogue.entryDisabled` (worth knowing). `formula.argumentMismatch` and `formula.kindMismatch` use `FormulaType`.
10. **`FORMULA_FUNCTIONS`** has its content (core 6.4): every operator and function of profile `cel-1`, what is refused, and `days(n)` (changed by E-23, d2 12). `FormulaType` adds `int`, `timestamp`, `duration`, `map`, `optionalOf:`; `FormulaFunction.style` adds `operator`.
11. **A person or group is `{ type, id }`** in every value, sample and payload (E-20). Core 2.4.
12. **Story.** `moved.arrow` is required: the "absent arrow: moved by a retry" case could not occur, because a retry stays in the same authored stage (core 9).
13. **`catalogue.ts`** matches `integrations-shapes.md` section 2 and `fixtures/catalogue.json`: `ValueKind` imported from `authored-format.ts`; `Connection.status` adds `disabled`; `description` and `supersededBy` may be `null`; entries carry `name`, `version` and `status` (`ready` or `disabled`, E-20); operations carry `onRepeat` (required: written for write and await, `null` for read), `timeoutSeconds`, `expectedWithinSeconds`, `await` and `sample.failure`; data sources carry `cacheSeconds` and `timeoutSeconds` and document `list` and `get`; `Field.kind` excludes `choiceFromList`. No longer provisional; what is still unsettled is listed at its top.
14. **Paths.** `{base}` on the development host is `/api/workflow/v1`, as `integrations-shapes.md` and `integrated-sample.md` use it.
15. **Bindings.** `BindingState.held` counts the deliveries a paused binding holds; resuming runs them again, for up to 30 days (E-20).
16. Headers cite decisions E-1 to E-20.

## (d2) Since the Draft 3 you last saw: the revision after E-21 to E-23, most disruptive first

1. **`Catalogue.directoryConnection: string` is required** (`catalogue.ts`, one edit; E-23, `integrations-shapes.md` 2.9). It names the connection that is the directory; `compile` learns it there. The catalogue's `version` hash now covers it. `fixtures/catalogue.json` has it (`"directory"`) and its directory connection declares `membersOf@1` and the data source `groupMembers@1`. **This breaks your build where a `Catalogue` literal lacks the field:** `SAMPLE_CATALOGUE` (`services/standin/catalogue.ts`), `testCatalogue` (`model/describe/__tests__/test-catalogue.ts`) and `madeUpCatalogue` (`features/actions/made-up-catalogue.ts`). Add `directoryConnection: "directory"` (or the stand-in's directory connection ID) to each. `catalogue.ts`'s "Still unsettled" list is gone: the fixture now follows section 2.
2. **Retry per reason (E-23).** Retry is offered only for `action-failed` (the action is tried again) and `nobody-to-ask` (the group is read again and the stage's tasks are asked again). A retry on a request that is not stuck is refused `not-stuck`; on one stuck with `nothing-fits`, `error` or `unfinished`, the new code `not-retryable` (409, `{ reason }`, an attempt). Close is offered for any open request. `RequestView.viewer.isAdmin` keeps its meaning; the page shows Retry by reason. Runtime 5.1; core 2.6, 8, 10.2.
3. **One stuck message (E-21).** The separate nobody-to-ask message is gone: `BuiltInMessageParams` has `task.assigned`, `request.stuck` and `start.refused` only, and a request stuck for any reason, `nobody-to-ask` included, sends `request.stuck` with its reason. The built-in messages are those three and one per alert reason, keyed `alert.<reason>` (`integrations-shapes.md` section 8 plus `call-outcome-unknown`). Try it's outbox holds only the three. Core 1.1, 10.3; runtime 5.2.
4. **Stuck reason and detail (E-21, E-23).** The reason is read from the fault: kind error with code `call-failed` is `action-failed`, whatever added the call (a directory read included); any other kind error is `error`; kind stuck is `nothing-fits`; `nobody-to-ask` is the match of the definition's `nobodyToAsk` block: nobody can answer the task (who can answer is (d3) 1). A membership read that fails contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts. `StuckDetail` gains `failureCode` and `attempts` (admin-only). Core 8.
5. **Refused starts (E-21).** New runtime operations `listRefusedStarts({ workflow? })` -> `Page<RefusedStart>` (`{ id, workflow, startsWhen, at, code, params, location? }`, 30 days, for the people who look after stuck requests and platform admins) and `retryRefusedStart(id)` -> `RetriedStart`, which runs the start again on the live version's bindings while the sent body is kept. `not-found.what` adds `refusedStart`. Runtime 5.4. This answers part of (f) 2.
6. **Who and when (E-23).** `getSettings` and `saveSettings` return `SettingsRead`: `Settings` plus `changedBy` and `changedAt`; a body sent back with them is accepted and they are ignored. Every settings change is a `settings_log` row, every pause or resume a `binding_pauses` row; `BindingState.changedBy` and `changedAt` return the last. Authoring 3, 6; runtime 5.3.
7. **The order of steps when a person acts (E-23).** The unlocked check that the task is open comes first, then the lookups (the actor's groups, the choices) without the lock, then the lock, the task checked again, and the kernel's reasons in order with the lookup results applied at their step. Step numbers are now 1 to 11. An act on a task that is no longer open answers `wait-not-open` even while the directory is down. In retry and close, `membership-unavailable` now comes before `busy`. Runtime 4.3, 5.1.
8. **Findings (E-22, E-23).** New To dos, each marked in core 4's "Stops Try it" column: `action.resultSavedTwice`, `question.choicesNotSupported`, `arrow.otherCasesWithCondition`, `condition.noClauses`, `reference.stepsNotSupported`, `template.kindNotJoinable` (all block Try it), and `startsWhen.showWhenReadsStartedOn` (blocks `startFrom` on that binding only). New Worth knowing: `action.repeatOnRead`. `value.mayBeEmpty` is raised only for who is asked, a notification's recipient, a directory group and a needed connection input; `task.askedMayBeEmpty` no longer uses `reason: "valueMayBeEmpty"`. `start.directoryInCondition` keeps its meaning with E-23's reason.
9. **Try it shapes.** `TestHost.choices` takes the runtime's `ChoicesArgs` and returns `ChoicesPage` (runtime 3.4 is the one statement of the shape; for the start form, `form` is any `{ workflow, version }`). `CallFake` and `CallAnswer` failures may carry `message`; the outbox's `failure` is `{ code, message }`, as a failed call is recorded. Core 10.
10. **Empty values (E-22).** An empty value in a "when" clause makes the clause not true, except "is empty" and the negative words, which are true; it is never an error. In a list comparison, empty items are ignored ((d3) 3). A message shows an empty value as nothing. Core 2.4.
11. **What is told (E-22).** A Tell sends each value as the request holds it: a connection choice as `{ stored, label }`, a person as `{ type, id }`. The built-in outbound events carry IDs, status and reason only. Core 8, 10.3.
12. **Formula functions (E-23).** `days(n)` takes a whole number; `asDate(t)` gives a timestamp's UTC date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and the compiler applies it where a formula's result is used as a date, so a formula can now fill a date value. The pinned list is `engine/design/definition-format.md` section 5. Both are now built ((d4) 10). Core 6.4.
13. **Compile rules stated (E-22, E-23).** The `types` block; the `nobodyToAsk` block and the membership read beside each task that may ask a group; the tasks step leaves when every task is answered; a `members` step's read, inside a condition, just before the step that uses it ("people in [group]" under who is asked is (d3) 2); "once" as the explicit key `'once.' + request.id + '.' + <action ID>`; after-response actions before the arrows; the later task in the document wins; the `Lookup` shape and origin keys `<element key>#<JSON Pointer>`. Core 5, 12. `TaskView.lookups` now means the read placed just before the task's step.
14. **IDs.** Authored IDs are at most 40 characters (core 3, already in `authored-format.ts`); a request ID matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (core 2.2).
15. **Calls when a wait closes (E-23, narrowed by E-24).** A write or await sent at least once with no clear answer whose wait closes is kept, asked about, and raises one `call-outcome-unknown` alert; a read in that state, and any call never sent, is dropped quietly ((d3) 5). Runtime 5.1.
16. Pointers to formats name `engine/design/definition-format.md` and `event-payloads.md`. Headers cite E-1 to E-23 and carry the line "Revised 2026-11-15 after E-21 to E-23".
17. **Paused deliveries (E-20).** New runtime operation `listPausedDeliveries({ workflow, binding })` -> `PausedDelivery[]` (`{ id, binding, eventId, at }`, oldest first, for the people who look after stuck requests and platform admins). `setBindingPaused` now returns `BindingChanged`: `BindingState` plus `rerun` and `gone`, present on a resume. Runtime 5.3.

## (d3) E-24: wording decisions for the frontend

E-24 settles how the engine reads several things the editor and the pages put into words. None of them changes a type in `core-api.md`, `authoring-api.md`, `runtime-api.md`, `catalogue.ts` or `authored-format.ts`.

1. **Who can answer a task** is the people asked directly plus the recorded members of the groups asked, minus the Requester where the Requester may not answer. Nobody-to-ask means that set is empty. A membership read that fails contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts. A task asked only of the Requester, who may not answer, is nobody-to-ask. Core 8.
2. **"People in [group]" under "Who is asked" is the same as asking the group.** No separate directory read is made for it, so Retry for nobody-to-ask always reads the group again. Core 12; runtime 5.1.
3. **In a list comparison** (is one of, is not one of, includes any of, includes all of), **empty items are ignored.** Core 2.4.
4. **Removing a value that is not there records nothing.** A person's start records no "remove" for the Requester, so the story shows no such change.
5. **`call-outcome-unknown` is for actions only:** a write or await sent with no clear answer whose task then closes. A read in that state, such as a task's membership read, is dropped quietly. The alert goes to the people who look after stuck requests. Runtime 5.1, 5.2.
6. **The integrated sample's cases** (`engine/design/integrated-sample.md`) are asserted on what a person or an outside system can see: inputs, refusals, the story, alerts, messages and published events. Its engine event lists are illustrations.
7. **`workflow_settings.admins` is `stuck_requests_go_to`;** empty means the authors. `Settings.stuckRequestsGoTo` is unchanged: absent means the authors, and an empty list is still refused on save. Authoring 3, 6.

## (d4) E-25 and E-26: the checker, the formulas and the package, most disruptive first

E-25 takes two rules from the frontend's verifiers; E-26 settles what the first code wave found unclear. Where (d) to (d3) and this section disagree, this section holds.

1. **Two package entries (E-26).** `@workflow/core` is the contract surface, with the authored-format and catalogue types; the frontend imports only this one. `@workflow/core/kernel` holds the stored formats, `decide`, `evolve`, the turn function, the schema validator, the kernel publish check, the in-memory host and the call-result check. The two share names with different meanings (`Status`, `ValueKind`, `MessagePart`). Core 14.
2. **`arrow.neverUsed` is a To do (E-25),** no longer Worth knowing, so it now stops a publish. It does not stop Try it. It is raised only where that is provable, not for an arrow whose "when" is not chosen yet (that has `item.partMissing`), and not for an arrow out of an unreachable stage. Core 4.
3. **An empty "when" or "only when" is never "always true" (E-25).** An arrow with no "when" chosen, or a `when.condition` with no clauses, is `item.partMissing`; an "only when" present with an empty list is `condition.noClauses`. Core 4.
4. **Three new codes (E-26).** To dos `group.readInSameStep` (a directory step or "is in" a group over a group that the same tasks step fills, read by that step's own Show when, "Also only when", lookup input or early arrow; stops Try it) and `startsWhen.buttonNotOnStart` (the binding presses a button that is not the start task's; refuses `startFrom` on that binding only). Parse problem `parse.badFormat` (`{ pointer, format: "catalogueRef" | "date" }`). Core 3, 4.
5. **Date chips read as a point in time (E-26).** A date value or "Started on" in a formula is already a timestamp at 00:00 UTC: write `{{v_due}} + days(3)`, and `asDate({{v_due}} + days(3))` to give a date. `date({{v_due}})` is refused at check. The earlier examples that wrapped the chip in `date()` are corrected. Core 2.4, 6.4.
6. **Wider findings (E-26).** `clause.pressedOutsideStage` also covers an arrow whose `when.button` is another stage's button (location the arrow, part `when.button`). `catalogue.unknownField` also covers a binding's `requester`, `answers.<question>` and `onlyWhen` clause sides when a sent field is not a field of the trigger's event. `expression.kindMismatch` also covers a clause's right side and `choices.peopleIn`. `action.failureReadButStops` covers any read. `start.directoryInCondition` covers "is in" and "is not in" a group. Core 4.
7. **Narrower findings (E-26).** `task.askedMayBeEmpty` is raised only for a list cell left "(not given)" by a row that can reach the task. `requester.mayBeEmpty` is not raised at the start task's `whoIsAsked` when no arrow leads back to the start stage. `item.partMissing` no longer lists `choices.list`: a missing one is `parse.missingField`. Core 4.
8. **Facts (E-26).** `facts.values` lists only the values in the registry. `facts.arrows` judges an arrow as if its stage is reached. An early arrow ("Don't wait for the others") taken while tasks are open reads the values after the tasks step, before the after-response actions. Core 5.
9. **Smaller rules (E-26).** A choice question whose choices are the people in a group gives a value of kind `person`. Template text is empty only when it is `''`. A task's own question wins over its "save which button was pressed" for the same value. Core 2.4, 4; `engine/design/compiler.md` 4.6.
10. **Formula functions built.** `days`, `asDate`, a UTC `getDayOfYear`, the refusal of `\p` and `\P` at check, of a duration plus a timestamp and of `json()` on bytes, and a whole number modulo 0 as `division-by-zero` are in the engine's environment. Core 6.4.
11. **Runtime refusals (E-26).** The kernel reasons E-26 named reach a page only as `requires-not-met` on Retry; the others are answered by the server's own checks first. Runtime 5.1.
12. Headers cite kernel spec v2.17 and E-1 to E-26 and carry the line "Revised 2026-11-15 after E-21 to E-26".

===\ncontract/D16-publish-then-act.md\n===
# D16. Publish, then act

What happens between the editor's publish and a person's press on a task of a request that runs on the published version. The server checks and compiles again with the same core package the browser runs, and stores the version with its authored source; a task page later renders its form from that source and works out its state with core, and the engine judges the press and answers in authored terms.
Names are those of `authoring-api.md` and `runtime-api.md`. Drawn by the engine owner for document 6, 2026-11-15; nothing in it has run.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant ED as Editor
  participant AU as Authoring API
  participant SC as core on the server
  actor P as Person
  participant PG as Task page, with core
  participant RT as Runtime API
  participant LK as Directory and data sources
  ED->>AU: publish(workflow, revision, coreVersion), POST {base}/workflows/{id}/versions
  AU->>SC: check and compile the draft again, with the server's catalogue
  SC-->>AU: compiled definition, form schemas, origin map, no To do
  Note over AU: one transaction: the version stored in definitions with its authored source
  AU-->>ED: 201 PublishResult, the version and the worth-knowing findings
  P->>PG: opens a task of a request on that version
  PG->>RT: getTask(requestId, task)
  RT-->>PG: TaskView, with version, values, lookups, buttonStates
  PG->>RT: publishedSource(workflow, version)
  RT-->>PG: PublishedSource, the authored form of that version
  Note over PG: core.formState works out which questions show and which buttons can be pressed
  P->>PG: presses a button
  PG->>RT: act(requestId, task, button, answers)
  RT->>LK: before the lock: the person's groups, and each chosen item by its stored value
  LK-->>RT: groups and items found
  Note over RT: lock taken. Checked in the kernel's order: still open, groups, asked, may, answers, choices, checks. Recorded in one transaction
  RT-->>PG: 200 TurnDone, or errors: a Refusal with its code and authored Location
```

*D16. What happens when an author publishes, and then a person acts on a live request?*
===\ncontract/authored-format.md\n===
# Authored workflow format, version 0 (draft for review)

The **authored format** is the JSON document the workflow editor saves as a draft and the engine's compiler turns into a published definition. It is part A of the frontend/engine contract. The types in `authored-format.ts` are the source of truth; this page explains them. Words follow `spec/editor-model.md`.

Layout, under `contract\`:

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `authored-format.ts` | The types (source of truth) |
| `authored-format.md` | This page |
| `fixtures\<name>.authored.json` | The fixtures as plain JSON: what the engine reads, also its parser tests |
| `fixtures\src\<name>.authored.ts` | The typed sources of those fixtures. **The `.ts` is the source; the `.json` is emitted from it** |
| `fixtures\records.json` | Stand-in for the server's workflow records: per fixture, `{ name, description, stuckRequestsGoTo: [{ type: "user" \| "group", id, label }] }`. Not part of the format |
| `check\` | `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `check.ts` |

Fixtures: `change-request` (the demo), `blank` ("New workflow"), `several-at-once` (Domain approval with a second task), `integrated-sample` (Starts when, catalogue choices, look-up, wait-for, tell other systems). In `contract\check`: `npm install`, then `npm run verify` type-checks the sources against `..\authored-format.ts`, confirms each `.json` is exactly what its source emits, checks that IDs are unique, follow the ID rule and that every reference points at an existing ID, and checks the shape of `records.json`. `npm run emit` rewrites the `.json` from the sources.

## Rules

1. **Editor words only.** Fields are named with the words authors see: stage, task, whoIsAsked, form, page, question, button, action, arrow, value, list, formula, status, ending. No engine words.
2. **Stable IDs.** Everything that can be pointed at (an **item**) has an ID, generated once and never reused. Names and labels are separate and can change; every reference is by ID. The ID's prefix says what kind of item it names (`st_` stage, `stat_` status, `tk_` task, `pg_` page, `q_` question, `tx_` form text, `ch_` choice, `btn_` button, `act_` action, `ar_` arrow, `v_` value, `ls_` list, `col_` column, `row_` row, `sw_` Starts-when binding, `wf_` workflow; exported as the data table `ITEM_KINDS`); after the prefix it is opaque. The types reject a stage ID where a value ID belongs. **ID rule:** every ID matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$` (`ID_PATTERN`): it starts with a letter and is at most 40 characters long, so every name the compiler builds from it fits in 64. It never contains a double underscore `__` (reserved for names the compiler adds); IDs the editor generates are `<prefix>_<base36>` (e.g. `st_8f3k2q`). The fixtures use readable IDs that follow the same rule; `check` enforces it.
3. **A draft may be unfinished.** The editor saves continuously, so the format accepts things not done yet: nobody asked (`whoIsAsked` absent), an arrow that goes nowhere (`goTo: null`), an empty label or name, a clause with only its left side, an action without its operation, a reference to a deleted thing. Fields marked "(draft: optional)" in the types are optional for this reason only. Completeness is the checker's job (To do), not the format's.
4. **Values are implicit** (section "Values").
5. **Order.** A working stage runs: *when this stage starts* actions in order, then the tasks, then *after they respond* actions in order, then the arrows, checked from the top. Within one section, actions run in listed order and saves take effect in listed order, so a later action, a later section, or an arrow sees an earlier save.
6. **Catalogue by reference.** Outside systems appear only as catalogue IDs `<connection>.<name>@<version>` (e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`). The workflow has no connections section; connections are set up by a platform admin. No connector name is built into the types. The catalogue IDs in `integrated-sample` are **sample data**.

## The workflow (root)

```json
{ "formatVersion": 0, "id": "wf_change_request",
  "start": { "by": "personSubmitsForm", "stage": "st_request_form", "startsWhen": [] },
  "stages": [...], "statuses": [...], "thingsTold": [...], "values": [...], "lists": [...],
  "sampleRequest": {...}, "diagram": {...} }
```

`formatVersion` stays 0 until the engine has compiled the format once. `id` is the document's own item ID, which workflow-level findings point at; it is **not** the server's workflow ID. The workflow's **name, description, authors and "Stuck requests go to" are not in the document**: they live in the server's workflow record, so renaming a workflow or changing who looks after stuck requests is not an edit to any version.

`sampleRequest` (the request used for every sample), `diagram` (positions; absent means automatic layout) and `removedNames` (names of deleted things still referenced, for To do wording) are for the editor; the compiler ignores them. A person or group is `{ "directoryId", "name" }` wrapped as `{ "person": ... }` or `{ "group": ... }`; the name is a display copy.

## How a request starts

Always: a person submits the start stage's form and becomes the Requester. In addition, zero or more **Starts when** bindings: when a catalogue trigger fires, a request starts as if the start form were submitted with the binding's answers. A binding reads **only** the fields of what the other system sent (`{ "sentField": "title" }`, dotted for nested fields); the types (`SentExpression`, `SentCondition`, `SentTemplate`) allow no value references inside it. `button` says which of the start form's buttons the binding presses; it may be absent when the start task has one button, otherwise that is a To do. The start form's "Needed to press" is checked against the binding's answers: if it fails, no request starts and the people who look after stuck requests are told. `requester` names the Requester from a sent field of kind person (e.g. `{ "sentField": "raisedBy" }`): the request is still recorded as started by the connection, and the Requester value is this person. Without `requester` the request has no person as Requester, so `{ "request": "requester" }` is empty and its `ifEmptyUse` applies.

```json
{ "id": "sw_helpdesk_ticket", "trigger": "helpdesk.ticketCreated@1", "button": "btn_rf_submit", "requester": { "sentField": "reporter" },
  "onlyWhen": { "allOf": [{ "left": { "sentField": "category" }, "words": "text.is", "right": { "text": "Service change" } }] },
  "answers": { "q_summary": { "sentField": "title" }, "q_helpdesk_ticket": ["Helpdesk ", { "sentField": "key" }] } }
```

## Stages

A **stage** is `kind` + `name` + status + the fixed anatomy: `whenThisStageStarts` (actions), `tasks` (0..n, usually 1), `afterTheyRespond` (actions), `arrows`. The kind (`form`, `approval`, `work`, `automatic`, `blank`) pre-fills and labels the stage; it does not change which fields are legal. An **ending** (`kind: "ending"`) has only name and status. An Automatic stage has no tasks; its "What it does" is `whenThisStageStarts`. A new request begins at the start stage's form, so the start stage's `whenThisStageStarts` actions run only when a request is sent back there. A start stage with a connection action in "After they respond" needs a status, because a request can be seen sitting (or stuck) there; that is a To do raised by the check, not a format rule.

**Statuses** are a registry (`id`, `words`, `colour`); stages point at one, so two stages showing the same words share it. `status` is what people see while a request is at the stage; `ifSentBackStatus` (legal on any working stage) is shown instead when it arrived by a send-back arrow. "Sent back" is never stored: an arrow sends back when it goes to a stage that every request must already have passed through to reach the arrow's own stage; the engine works this out. The start stage has only `ifSentBackStatus` ("If sent back: Needs changes"), because a request is never seen sitting there otherwise.

## Tasks and forms

A **task** asks people: `whoIsAsked` (an expression giving a person, group or several people; the fallback is written on the reference as `ifEmptyUse`), `groupRule` (only `"firstAnswerDecides"` in version 0: "One answer is enough: the first person in the group to answer decides."), `requesterCanAnswer` (false = "The requester can't answer their own request"), `form`, `buttons`, and optionally which values keep its two extra answers (`savesButtonPressedAs`, `savesAnsweredByAs`; created when the author first uses them). With several tasks, each gets a `name` only if the author renamed it; otherwise the editor names it after who is asked. A task cancelled by a `goAsSoonAsTrue` arrow has its "Button pressed" and "Answered by" values emptied for that visit; its questions' values keep what they had.

```json
{ "id": "tk_development",
  "whoIsAsked": { "value": "v_eng_lead", "ifEmptyUse": { "value": "v_primary_domain", "steps": [{ "column": "col_default_lead" }] } },
  "groupRule": "firstAnswerDecides", "requesterCanAnswer": true,
  "form": { "pages": [{ "id": "pg_development_1", "items": [
    { "type": "question", "id": "q_release_notes", "label": "Release notes", "kind": "longText", "savedAs": "v_release_notes" } ] }] },
  "buttons": [{ "id": "btn_dev_mark_released", "label": "Mark released", "look": "primary", "neededToPress": ["q_release_notes"] }] }
```

A **form** has pages; a page has an optional title, `showWhen`, and items: **questions** (`label`, `kind`, `savedAs`, `choices`, `showWhen`) and read-only **text** (`content`, a template; `showWhen`). Hidden means empty and never needed. **Choices** come `from`: `typedIn`, a `list` (with `shownColumn`; the answer is a row), the `directory` (the people in a group given by an expression), a catalogue `source` (`source`, `inputs`, `labelField`, `storedField`), or a `formula`.

A **button** has `label`, `look`, `neededToPress` (questions that must be answered first), `enabledWhen` ("Also only when ...") and `messageWhileDisabled` (absent: the editor reads back the needs). A question may set `neededForEveryButton: true` (the "All" tick, which also covers buttons added later). **The effective set for a button is its own `neededToPress` plus every question of its task with `neededForEveryButton`.** A hidden question is never needed.

## Expressions and "when ..."

One union, usable in every slot that needs something:

| Level | Shape | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Value, with steps | `{ "value", "steps"?, "ifEmptyUse"? }` | Primary domain's approvers: `{ "value": "v_primary_domain", "steps": [{ "column": "col_approvers" }] }` |
| Request | `{ "request": "requester" \| "startedOn" }` | Requester |
| Constant | `{ "text" }`, `{ "number" }`, `{ "yesNo" }`, `{ "date" }`, `{ "weekday" }`, `{ "choice" }`, `{ "choices": [...] }`, `{ "row" }`, `{ "button" }`, `{ "person" }`, `{ "group" }`, `{ "people": [...] }`, `{ "connectionChoice": { "stored", "label" } }` | `{ "text": "CHG" }` |
| Sentence | `{ "allOf" \| "anyOf": [clause] }` | below |
| Formula | `{ "formula", "readsAs" }` | below |

Every question kind has a constant, so the sample request can answer any question. Steps: `{ "column": col }` reads a cell of the row a list choice holds; `{ "directory": "members" }` goes from a group to its people. Choices from the directory (`from: "directory"`) and from a connection are read live while the form is shown, on the start form too, and the answer is checked by a lookup when the person answers; for a connection, the source's label is recorded with that lookup. A `members` step or an "is in [group]" test inside a "when" is a recorded read of the group's members, made just before the step that uses it; a condition on the start form cannot use one (a To do). Under Who is asked, "people in [group]" is the same as asking the group. A task that may ask a group gets a recorded membership read beside the task; if that read fails, those groups count as nobody to ask, but a person asked directly still counts. In an "is one of" list, items that are empty when the condition is checked are ignored. **`ifEmptyUse`**: "empty" means the value has nothing in it. A group that exists but has nobody in it is not empty; that case is "nobody to ask", and the request goes to the people who look after stuck requests. A **template** (text with value chips) is an array of strings and expressions.

A **sentence** is what the condition builder makes: clauses joined by "and" (`allOf`) or "or" (`anyOf`), flat. A clause is `{ left, words, right? }` or `{ pressed: buttonId }` ("Approve is pressed", legal only in the stage that owns the button). `words` is a closed list per set of words, exported at run time as `WORDS` (text, number, yesNo, date, choice, person, people, list); `WORDS_FOR_KIND` says which set each value kind gets; `WORDS_WITH_NOTHING_AFTER` and `WORDS_WITH_A_LIST` say what `right` must be.

```json
{ "allOf": [{ "left": { "value": "v_primary_domain", "steps": [{ "column": "col_needs_approval" }] }, "words": "yesNo.isNo" }] }
```

A **formula** is the escape hatch: text in the engine's formula language (CEL), with chips written `{{<value id>}}`, `{{request.requester}}`, `{{request.startedOn}}`, and `{{sent.<field>}}` (inside a binding only). There is no "today": the engine has no clock. Nothing else about its syntax belongs to this format. It carries the required plain sentence shown instead of it:

```json
{ "formula": "{{v_planned_release_date}} < {{request.startedOn}} + days(3)",
  "readsAs": "Planned release date is less than 3 days after the request was started" }
```

## Actions

Each has `id`, `type`, and optional `onlyWhen`. No nesting.

- `saveValue`: "Save [save] as [as]". When `onlyWhen` is not true the value keeps what it had.
- `notify`: `to` (expression), `message` (template, sent with the values as they were at that moment). The channel is the platform's. Never stops a request.
- `tellOtherSystems`: tells other systems something happened: `tell` (an entry of the root registry `thingsTold`, `{ id: "told_...", words }`, e.g. "Change released"; two actions may tell the same thing) and `values` (field name to expression or template). Outside systems key on the `told_` ID, so it survives rewording; the keys of `values` are what the outside system receives, so renaming one is a visible change. Who receives it is chosen outside the workflow by a platform admin. Never stops a request.
- `useConnection`: `operation` (catalogue ID), `inputs` (keyed by the catalogue's input field ids, to expression or template), `saveResults` (keyed by the catalogue's result field ids, to value ID), `ifItFails`, `saveFailureAs`, `ifStageEntersAgain`. Whether it gives data (a look-up), does something, or waits until the other system reports back is the catalogue's business, not the format's.
  - `ifItFails` ("If it fails") applies to every connection action, look-ups included. `"stuck"`: the request is stuck at the stage; the people in "Stuck requests go to" are told and can retry or close it. `"carryOn"`: the failure is an ordinary result; `saveFailureAs: { failed, code }` saves a Yes/No "it failed" and the failure code, so an arrow can test them. The failure-code value is a choice whose choices are the operation's failure codes from the catalogue (the code is held; its label is what people read); a clause compares it with `{ "failureCode": "tests-failed" }`, written wherever a `button` constant may be written.
  - `ifStageEntersAgain`: `"once"` reuses the first result on a re-entry after a send-back (one Jira issue per request); `"again"` does it again. Absent: the catalogue's default.

```json
{ "id": "act_create_jira_issue", "type": "useConnection", "operation": "jira.createIssue@1",
  "inputs": { "project": { "text": "CHG" }, "summary": { "value": "v_title" },
              "assignee": { "value": "v_eng_lead", "ifEmptyUse": { "value": "v_primary_domain", "steps": [{ "column": "col_default_lead" }] } } },
  "saveResults": { "key": "v_jira_issue" }, "ifItFails": "stuck", "ifStageEntersAgain": "once" }
```

`jira.createIssue@1` field ids: inputs `project` (text, required), `summary` (text, required), `assignee` (person), `description` (longText; the demo leaves it empty); results `key`, `url`.

## Arrows

An arrow belongs to its source stage. `when` is one of `{ "type": "buttonPressed", "button" }`, `{ "type": "condition", "condition" }`, `{ "type": "inAllOtherCases" }`, `{ "type": "whenDone" }` (Automatic). Optional: `onlyWhen` ("+ only when ..."), `words` (the author's words on the arrow; absent = the arrow's sentence), `goAsSoonAsTrue` ("Don't wait for the others", several tasks only). `goTo` is a stage ID or `null`. Array order is the order they are checked. An arrow carries only a "when" and a destination; everything that happens lives in the stage's two action sections, with `onlyWhen`.

```json
{ "id": "ar_da_reject", "goTo": "st_rejected", "goAsSoonAsTrue": true,
  "when": { "type": "condition", "condition": { "anyOf": [{ "pressed": "btn_da_reject" }, { "pressed": "btn_sec_reject" }] } } }
```

## Values

The registry holds `{ id, name, description? }` only. A value exists because something fills it: a question (`savedAs`), a save (`as`), an action's results (`saveResults`, `saveFailureAs`), or a task's extra answers. Its **kind** (`ValueKind`) is never stored: it comes from the filler, and two fillers of different kinds is a red To do. If two places fill a value, the later one replaces the earlier. Within one stage, when two tasks fill the same value, the task later in the document wins, not the later answer in time. The nine question kinds plus: `choiceFromList` (holds a row), `choiceFromConnection` (holds one value of two parts, `{ stored, label }`: what was stored and the source's label for it, recorded by the lookup made when the person answered, so the request page can show it even if the other system renames or removes the item; conditions compare `stored`), `people`, `list`, `fieldGroup` (from catalogue results). "Button pressed" is a `choice` of the task's buttons.

**"Used in N places"** is derived: scan the document for `{ "value": id }` anywhere and `{{id}}` in formula text, excluding the filling positions; N is the number of distinct items (question, text, button, action, arrow, task, binding) containing one. "Filled in N places" counts the filling positions.

## Lists

`{ id, name, columns: [{ id, name, kind }], rows: [{ id, cells: { columnId: constant } }] }`. An absent cell is "(not given)". Versioned with the workflow. The Domains list: Domain (text), Needs approval (yesNo), Approvers (group), Engineering group (group), Default lead (person).

## Locations

A **location** points at a place in the document: `{ item, part? }` (exported as `Location`). Findings (To do, Worth knowing), refusals, problems, story entries and the compiler's origin table use it. `item` is an item's ID (the workflow's own `id` for workflow-level findings). Without `part` it means the item as a whole. Otherwise `part` is the path from the item's own object to the field: the authored field names joined by dots, never entering another item. Array positions and pieces are numeric segments counted from 0: `onlyWhen.2` is the third clause of an "Only when" and may continue into it (`onlyWhen.2.right`); `message.1` is the second piece of a template. A key chosen by the catalogue or the form is a segment (`inputs.summary`, `saveResults.key`, `answers.q_summary`, `values.ticket`). A formula is reported at the part that holds the `Formula` object, and its sentence at `<part>.readsAs`.

The complete list of parts reported, per kind of item (exported as `LOCATION_PARTS`; `<...>` is a key chosen by the catalogue or the form). A listed part may be followed by deeper segments by the rule above. A diff's "changed" part may name any field by the same rule, including fields not listed.

| Item | Parts reported |
|---|---|
| workflow (`wf_`) | `start.stage` |
| stage (`st_`) | `name`, `status`, `ifSentBackStatus`, `whenThisStageStarts`, `tasks`, `afterTheyRespond`, `arrows` (the last four also say where a request is) |
| status (`stat_`) | `words` |
| task (`tk_`) | `whoIsAsked`, `whoIsAsked.ifEmptyUse`, `requesterCanAnswer`, `buttons`, `savesButtonPressedAs`, `savesAnsweredByAs` |
| page (`pg_`) | `showWhen` |
| question (`q_`) | `label`, `savedAs`, `choices`, `choices.list`, `choices.shownColumn`, `choices.peopleIn`, `choices.source`, `choices.inputs`, `choices.inputs.<field>`, `choices.labelField`, `choices.storedField`, `choices.formula`, `showWhen` |
| text (`tx_`) | `content`, `showWhen` |
| button (`btn_`) | `label`, `neededToPress`, `enabledWhen` |
| action (`act_`) | `onlyWhen`. Save a value: `save`, `as`. Notify: `to`, `message`. Use a connection: `operation`, `inputs`, `inputs.<field>`, `saveResults.<field>`, `ifItFails`, `saveFailureAs.failed`, `saveFailureAs.code`, `ifStageEntersAgain`. Tell other systems: `tell`, `values.<key>` |
| arrow (`ar_`) | `when`, `when.button`, `when.condition`, `onlyWhen`, `goTo`, `goAsSoonAsTrue` |
| value (`v_`), choice (`ch_`), list (`ls_`), column (`col_`) | none: the item as a whole |
| row (`row_`) | `cells.<column>` |
| startsWhen (`sw_`) | `trigger`, `onlyWhen`, `button`, `requester`, `answers`, `answers.<question>` |
| thingTold (`told_`) | `words` |

```json
{ "item": "act_create_jira_issue", "part": "inputs.summary" }
```

## Editor word to field

| Editor word | Field |
|---|---|
| Stage / Kind (of stage) / Ending | `stages[]` / `kind` / `kind: "ending"` |
| Status, "If sent back: ..." | `statuses[]`, `status`, `ifSentBackStatus` |
| When this stage starts / What it does | `whenThisStageStarts` |
| Task / Who is asked / If empty, use | `tasks[]` / `whoIsAsked` / `ifEmptyUse` |
| One answer is enough ... | `groupRule: "firstAnswerDecides"` |
| The requester can't answer their own request | `requesterCanAnswer: false` |
| Form / page / question / + Add text | `form.pages[].items[]`, `type: "question"` / `type: "text"` |
| Saved as / Show when / Needed to press | `savedAs` / `showWhen` / `button.neededToPress` |
| Button / Also only when | `buttons[]` / `enabledWhen` |
| Button pressed / Answered by | `savesButtonPressedAs` / `savesAnsweredByAs` |
| After they respond | `afterTheyRespond` |
| Then go to / Arrow / Words on the arrow | `arrows[]` / `goTo` / `words` |
| + only when ... / In all other cases / When done | `onlyWhen` / `inAllOtherCases` / `whenDone` |
| Don't wait for the others | `goAsSoonAsTrue` |
| Only when (action) / Save a value / Notify | `onlyWhen` / `saveValue` / `notify` |
| Create Jira issue, Look up, Wait for ... | `useConnection` with a catalogue `operation` |
| Tell other systems / Starts when | `tellOtherSystems` + `thingsTold[]` / `start.startsWhen[]` |
| "All" under Needed to press | `question.neededForEveryButton` |
| Value / Formula / "when ..." | `values[]` / `{ formula, readsAs }` / `Sentence` |
| Domains list / Directory | `lists[]` / `{ person \| group: { directoryId, name } }` |
| Workflow name, Stuck requests go to | not in the document: the server's workflow record |
| Sample request | `sampleRequest` |

## Decided, differs from editor-model.md

- **Arrows carry no actions.** editor-model.md says an arrow "can carry 'and also: save / notify'". Decided: an arrow carries only a "when" and a destination; a save or notification for one arrow goes in the stage's "After they respond" with a matching `onlyWhen` (e.g. "Notify Requester, only when Reject is pressed").
- **"Send an event" is called "Tell other systems"** (`tellOtherSystems`, with the `thingsTold` registry), and fields of what another system sent are `sentField`, so no author-facing field says "event".

## Answered by the engine owner (2026-11-15)

1. **Status by entry:** yes, for any working stage. `ifSentBackStatus` is legal on any working stage; "sent back" is never stored, the engine works it out from the arrows.
2. **Directory references:** the format keeps `{ person | group: { directoryId, name } }`; the compiler maps it to the catalogue's `{ type, id }`.
3. **Directory timing** (as revised by E-20 and E-23): choices from the directory and from a connection are read live while the form is shown, on the start form too, and the answer is checked by a lookup when the person answers, which records a connection source's label. A `members` step or an "is in [group]" test inside a "when" is a recorded read just before the step that uses it; a start-form condition cannot use one. A task that may ask a group gets a recorded membership read beside it; a failed read counts as nobody to ask for those groups only.
4. **Notification messages:** a `notify` compiles to an inline template; values are as they were at that moment.
5. **Ending type:** dropped (`endingType` removed).
6. **Several tasks:** confirmed. A task cancelled by a `goAsSoonAsTrue` arrow has its "Button pressed" and "Answered by" emptied for that visit; its questions' values stay; "In all other cases" covers the remaining combinations.
7. **Catalogue field ids** are the keys of `inputs` and `saveResults`. `jira.createIssue@1`: inputs `project`, `summary` (both required text), `assignee` (person), `description` (longText); results `key`, `url`.
8. **Requester of a request started by another system (E-16):** the binding's `requester` names it from a sent field of kind person; the request is still recorded as started by the connection. Without `requester` there is no person as Requester: `{ "request": "requester" }` is empty, so `ifEmptyUse` applies. The start form's "Needed to press" is checked against the binding's answers; a failing start is refused and the people who look after stuck requests are told. A binding names the button it presses (`button`).
9. **Tell other systems:** sinks are chosen outside the workflow by a platform admin; the identity is the `told_` ID in `thingsTold`.
10. **Hidden questions:** a hidden question is never needed and comes with no answer.
11. **Flat sentences:** fine for version 0.

Earlier answers: "Stuck requests go to" lives in the server's workflow record; the formula language is CEL with chips and has no "today" (`checkFormula` in `core-api.md`); value IDs are data paths and button IDs are outcome IDs (`core-api.md` section 5).

### Still open

None. (Directory unreachable was answered too: the request waits and the read is retried; if the directory clearly refuses, the request becomes stuck.)

## Changes since first draft

- Arrows carry no actions (`andAlso` removed).
- "Send an event" became `tellOtherSystems`; Starts-when expressions use `sentField` (`SentExpression`, `SentCondition`, `SentTemplate`, `SentClause`) and formula chips `{{sent.<field>}}`.
- Constants `{ choices }` and `{ people }` added, so every question kind has a sample constant.
- `neededForEveryButton` on questions (the "All" tick).
- Files relocated to `contract\` with `fixtures\src\` sources and a self-checking `check\` package.
- `name`, `description` and `settings` (with `Settings`, `PersonOrGroup`) removed from the document; they live in the server's workflow record (`fixtures\records.json` is the stand-in).
- ID rule (no `__`, generated IDs `<prefix>_<base36>`) documented, exported as `ID_PATTERN`, and enforced by `check`. The pattern first read `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`; it is now `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$` (at most 40 characters, see below).
- `Location` and the `ITEM_KINDS` table added.
- Formula text defined as the engine's formula language (CEL) with the four chip forms, no "today"; nothing else about its syntax is part of this format.
- `StartsWhen.button`: which start-form button a binding presses.
- `endingType` removed from endings.
- "Tell other systems" got the root registry `thingsTold` (`{ id: "told_...", words }`); the action's `whatHappened` became `tell` (a `told_` ID). `told` added to `ITEM_KINDS`.
- Rules stated (no shape change): start stage's `whenThisStageStarts` runs only on a send-back; `ifEmptyUse` and "nobody to ask"; `ifSentBackStatus` on any stage; cancelled tasks; Requester of a request started by another system; directory timing; catalogue field ids as `inputs`/`saveResults` keys.
- `StartsWhen.requester` (E-16): names the Requester from a sent field of kind person; replaces the rule that a request started by another system never has a Requester.
- Rules stated: "If it fails" applies to every connection action, look-ups included; a start stage with a connection action in "After they respond" needs a status (a To do raised by the check, not a format rule).
- `LOCATION_PARTS`: the complete list of reported parts per kind of item (from `core-api.md` section 2.3), replacing the examples; `ReportedPart` type.
- IDs are at most 40 characters (in `ID_PATTERN` and the ID rule); within one stage, the task later in the document wins when two tasks fill the same value (E-23).
- Comments made true to E-20 and E-23: when directory and connection choices, `members` steps and membership reads happen; the `choiceFromConnection` label is the source's, recorded when the person answers; empty items in an "is one of" list are ignored.
- `formatVersion` unchanged (0).===\ncontract/authored-format.ts\n===
/**
 * Authored workflow format, version 0 (draft for review).
 *
 * The JSON document the workflow editor saves as a draft and the engine's compiler turns into a
 * published definition. Field names use the editor's words only (see spec/editor-model.md).
 *
 * Reading guide, top to bottom:
 *   1. IDs                      6. Forms (pages, questions, text)
 *   2. Expressions              7. Buttons
 *   3. "When ..." sentences     8. Actions
 *   4. Workflow (root)          9. Arrows
 *   5. Stages and tasks        10. Values, lists, sample request, diagram
 *
 * Drafts may be unfinished. Every field marked "(draft: optional)" may be missing while the author
 * is still working; the checker reports it under To do. The format never rejects an unfinished
 * draft; it only rejects things that are malformed (wrong shape).
 */

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 1. IDs
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Every addressable thing has a stable ID, generated once by the editor and never reused, even
 * after the thing is deleted. Names and labels are separate and renamable; every reference is by
 * ID, so a rename changes one place.
 *
 * The prefix is part of the ID and says what sort of thing it names (so a stage ID can never be
 * used where a value ID is expected; see `ITEM_KINDS`). After the prefix the ID is opaque.
 *
 * ID rule (the compiler turns IDs into formula identifiers and element names):
 *  - every ID matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$` (`ID_PATTERN`): it starts with a letter and
 *    is at most 40 characters long, so every name the compiler builds from it fits in 64;
 *  - no ID contains a double underscore `__` (reserved for names the compiler adds);
 *  - IDs the editor generates are `<prefix>_<base36>`, e.g. `st_8f3k2q`. Fixtures use readable
 *    ones that follow the same rule, e.g. `st_domain_approval`.
 *
 * A reference may point at an ID that no longer exists (an arrow to a deleted stage). That is
 * legal in a draft and is a red To do.
 */
export type WorkflowId = `wf_${string}`;
export type StageId = `st_${string}`;
export type StatusId = `stat_${string}`;
export type TaskId = `tk_${string}`;
export type PageId = `pg_${string}`;
export type QuestionId = `q_${string}`;
/** Read-only text on a form ("+ Add text"). */
export type TextId = `tx_${string}`;
/** A typed-in choice of a choice or multiple-choice question. */
export type ChoiceId = `ch_${string}`;
export type ButtonId = `btn_${string}`;
export type ActionId = `act_${string}`;
export type ArrowId = `ar_${string}`;
export type ValueId = `v_${string}`;
export type ListId = `ls_${string}`;
export type ColumnId = `col_${string}`;
export type RowId = `row_${string}`;
/** A "Starts when" binding on the start block. */
export type StartsWhenId = `sw_${string}`;
/** An entry of `thingsTold`: something the workflow tells other systems happened. */
export type ToldId = `told_${string}`;

/** Each ID prefix and the kind of item it names. Data only. */
export const ITEM_KINDS = {
  wf: "workflow",
  st: "stage",
  stat: "status",
  tk: "task",
  pg: "page",
  q: "question",
  tx: "text",
  ch: "choice",
  btn: "button",
  act: "action",
  ar: "arrow",
  v: "value",
  ls: "list",
  col: "column",
  row: "row",
  sw: "startsWhen",
  told: "thingTold",
} as const;
export type ItemKind = (typeof ITEM_KINDS)[keyof typeof ITEM_KINDS];

/** The pattern every ID matches: a letter, then letters, digits or `_`, at most 40 characters in
 *  all (and none contains `__`). */
export const ID_PATTERN = "^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$";

/**
 * A place in the document, used by findings (To do, Worth knowing), refusals, problems, story
 * entries and the compiler's origin table. `item` is an item's ID (the workflow's own `id` for
 * workflow-level findings). `part` is absent for the item as a whole; otherwise it is the path
 * from the item's own object to the field: the authored field names, joined by dots, never
 * entering another item (an object with its own `id`). Array positions and pieces are numeric
 * segments counted from 0: `onlyWhen.2` is the third clause of the item's "Only when" and may
 * continue into it (`onlyWhen.2.right`); `message.1` is the second piece of a template. A key
 * chosen by the catalogue or by the form is a segment (`inputs.summary`, `saveResults.key`,
 * `answers.q_summary`, `values.ticket`). A formula is reported at the part that holds the
 * `Formula` object, and its sentence at `<part>.readsAs`.
 * The parts reported are listed, complete, in `LOCATION_PARTS`.
 */
export interface Location {
  item: string;
  part?: string;
}

/**
 * Every `Location.part` that findings, refusals, problems and story entries report, per kind of
 * item, for format version 0 (the engine's list, contract `core-api.md` section 2.3). Word tables
 * may key on it. A segment in angle brackets stands for a key chosen by the catalogue or the form
 * (`<field>`, `<key>`, `<column>`, `<question>`). A listed part may be followed by deeper segments
 * by the path rule on `Location` (a clause or template index, `readsAs`, `whoIsAsked.ifEmptyUse`).
 * A diff's "changed" part may name any field of an item by the same rule, including fields not
 * listed here. Items with an empty list are reported only as a whole. A stage's
 * `whenThisStageStarts`, `tasks`, `afterTheyRespond` and `arrows` also say where a request is.
 */
export const LOCATION_PARTS = {
  workflow: ["start.stage"],
  stage: ["name", "status", "ifSentBackStatus", "whenThisStageStarts", "tasks", "afterTheyRespond", "arrows"],
  status: ["words"],
  task: ["whoIsAsked", "whoIsAsked.ifEmptyUse", "requesterCanAnswer", "buttons", "savesButtonPressedAs", "savesAnsweredByAs"],
  page: ["showWhen"],
  question: [
    "label", "savedAs", "choices", "choices.list", "choices.shownColumn", "choices.peopleIn", "choices.source",
    "choices.inputs", "choices.inputs.<field>", "choices.labelField", "choices.storedField", "choices.formula", "showWhen",
  ],
  text: ["content", "showWhen"],
  choice: [],
  button: ["label", "neededToPress", "enabledWhen"],
  action: [
    "onlyWhen",
    // Save a value
    "save", "as",
    // Notify
    "to", "message",
    // Use a connection
    "operation", "inputs", "inputs.<field>", "saveResults.<field>", "ifItFails", "saveFailureAs.failed", "saveFailureAs.code", "ifStageEntersAgain",
    // Tell other systems
    "tell", "values.<key>",
  ],
  arrow: ["when", "when.button", "when.condition", "onlyWhen", "goTo", "goAsSoonAsTrue"],
  value: [],
  list: [],
  column: [],
  row: ["cells.<column>"],
  startsWhen: ["trigger", "onlyWhen", "button", "requester", "answers", "answers.<question>"],
  thingTold: ["words"],
} as const satisfies Record<ItemKind, readonly string[]>;

/** One reported part, as written in `LOCATION_PARTS` (placeholders in angle brackets). */
export type ReportedPart = (typeof LOCATION_PARTS)[ItemKind][number];

/**
 * A catalogue entry: `<connection>.<name>@<version>`, e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`.
 * The catalogue (contract part D: operations, data sources, triggers, event sinks, with their
 * fields) is owned by the platform; connections are set up by a platform admin outside the editor.
 * A workflow only references catalogue entries; it has no connections section of its own. An
 * entry's version never changes shape; a change is a new version. No connector name is built
 * into this format.
 */
export type CatalogueRef = `${string}.${string}@${number}`;

/**
 * A person or group in the Directory. `directoryId` is the directory's immutable object ID (never
 * an email or a name). `name` is a copy of the display name, kept so the draft reads well and
 * shows something if the directory is unreachable; the directory is authoritative.
 */
export interface DirectoryRef {
  directoryId: string;
  name: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 2. Expressions: anything that gives a value
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * One union usable wherever a value is needed (a slot). Three levels:
 *  (a) a reference to a value, possibly with steps into connected data, or a constant;
 *  (b) a "when ..." sentence (gives Yes/No);
 *  (c) a formula (the escape hatch).
 * The kind an expression gives is never stored; the checker works it out.
 */
export type Expression =
  | ValueReference
  | RequestReference
  | Constant
  | Sentence
  | Formula;

/**
 * The kinds of value. The kind is never stored on a value; it is worked out from what fills it
 * (and the catalogue's fields use the same kinds). A question's kind (`QuestionKind`) is one of
 * the first nine; the others only come from where a value is filled:
 *  - `choiceFromList`: a choice question answered from a list kept with the workflow; holds a row
 *    (`{ row }`), so steps can read the row's cells.
 *  - `choiceFromConnection`: a choice question answered from a catalogue data source; holds ONE
 *    value of two parts, `{ stored, label }`: what was stored, and the source's label for that item
 *    as recorded by the lookup made when the person answered (so the request page can show it
 *    later without asking the other system, even if the item is renamed or removed there).
 *    Conditions compare the `stored` part.
 *  - `people`: several people (e.g. a group's members after a `directory` step).
 *  - `list`, `fieldGroup`: a list of items, or a group of named fields, as an operation's result
 *    may give. Version 0 has no words for them in sentences; read them with a formula.
 * A task's "Button pressed" value is a `choice` whose choices are the task's buttons.
 * A value filled by `saveFailureAs.code` is a `choice` whose choices are the failure codes of the
 * operation (value = the code, label = the catalogue's label for it): the request holds the code,
 * a "when" compares by code (`{ failureCode }`), and a message or a text sent to another system
 * shows the label. If two actions save their failure code as the same value, its choices are the
 * codes of both; where one code has two labels, the first action in the document gives the label.
 */
export type ValueKind =
  | "text" | "longText" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "choice" | "multipleChoice" | "person" | "group"
  | "choiceFromList" | "choiceFromConnection" | "people" | "list" | "fieldGroup";

/**
 * "Title", "Primary domain's approvers", "Eng lead (if empty, use Primary domain's default lead)".
 * `steps` follow connected data from the value: a choice answered from a list gives a row, and a
 * `column` step reads a cell of that row; a `directory` step goes from a group to its people.
 */
export interface ValueReference {
  value: ValueId;
  steps?: Step[];
  /**
   * "If empty, use ...": used when this reference has nothing in it at that moment. "Empty" means
   * the value has nothing in it. A group that exists but has nobody in it is NOT empty: that case
   * is "nobody to ask", and the request goes to the people who look after stuck requests.
   */
  ifEmptyUse?: Expression;
}

/**
 * Things every request has: who started it ("Requester") and when ("Started on", a date).
 * For a request started by another system (a "Starts when" binding), the Requester is the
 * person the binding's `requester` names; when the binding has none, `{ request: "requester" }`
 * is empty, so its `ifEmptyUse` applies.
 */
export interface RequestReference {
  request: "requester" | "startedOn";
  steps?: Step[];
  ifEmptyUse?: Expression;
}


/**
 * One step into connected data.
 * - `column`: from a list row (a choice answered from a list) to that row's cell in the column.
 * - `directory: "members"`: from a group to the people in it. Inside a "when" (as is a `person.isIn`
 *   test on a group), it is a recorded read of the group's members, made just before the step that
 *   uses it, so it sees a group saved earlier in the same section. A condition on the start form
 *   cannot use it (a To do). Under Who is asked, "people in [group]" is the same as asking the
 *   group.
 * Who is asked: a task that may ask a group gets a recorded membership read beside the task. If that
 * read fails, those groups count as nobody to ask; a person asked directly still counts.
 * Later steps (e.g. "manager" of a person) would be new `directory` words; not in version 0.
 */
export type Step = { column: ColumnId } | { directory: "members" };

/** A typed literal. The key says the kind. */
export type Constant =
  | { text: string }
  | { number: number }
  | { yesNo: boolean }
  /** `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
  | { date: string }
  /** For "is on a [weekday]". */
  | { weekday: "monday" | "tuesday" | "wednesday" | "thursday" | "friday" | "saturday" | "sunday" }
  /** One typed-in choice of a question. */
  | { choice: ChoiceId }
  /** Several typed-in choices (a multiple-choice answer). */
  | { choices: ChoiceId[] }
  /** One row of a list (what a choice answered from a list holds). */
  | { row: RowId }
  /** A button (what a task's "Button pressed" value holds). */
  | { button: ButtonId }
  /** One failure code of a connection action, written as the catalogue declares it (kebab-case),
   *  e.g. `{ failureCode: "tests-failed" }`. What a value filled by `saveFailureAs.code` holds;
   *  valid only as the right side of a clause on such a value, and only for a code the action's
   *  operation declares. Written wherever a `button` constant may be written. */
  | { failureCode: string }
  | { person: DirectoryRef }
  | { group: DirectoryRef }
  /** Several people. */
  | { people: DirectoryRef[] }
  /** What a choice answered from a catalogue data source holds (kind `choiceFromConnection`).
   *  As the right side of a clause only `stored` is compared. */
  | { connectionChoice: { stored: string | number; label: string } };

/**
 * Text with value chips in it: notification messages, form text, a Jira summary. Strings are
 * shown as written; expressions are shown as their value at that moment.
 * Example: `["Your Jira issue for this change is ready: ", { "value": "v_jira_issue" }]`.
 */
export type Template = Array<string | Expression>;

/**
 * The escape hatch, for a "when ..." or a value. `formula` is text in the engine's formula
 * language (CEL), with chips written `{{<value id>}}`, `{{request.requester}}`,
 * `{{request.startedOn}}`, and, inside a "Starts when" binding only, `{{sent.<field>}}`. There is
 * no "today": the engine has no clock. Nothing else about its syntax belongs to this format.
 * `readsAs` is the required plain sentence shown everywhere instead of the formula (on the arrow,
 * in In words). (draft: `readsAs` may be empty.)
 */
export interface Formula {
  formula: string;
  readsAs: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 3. "When ..." sentences (the condition builder)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** A "when ...": a sentence from the builder, or a formula. Gives Yes/No. */
export type Condition = Sentence | Formula;

/**
 * Clauses joined by "and" (allOf) or "or" (anyOf). Flat: mixing "and" and "or" needs a formula.
 * An empty list is legal in a draft (the author has opened the builder but chosen nothing).
 */
export type Sentence = { allOf: Clause[] } | { anyOf: Clause[] };

export type Clause = WordsClause | PressedClause;

/**
 * `[left] [words] [right]`, e.g. "Risk is High", "Primary domain needs approval is No".
 * `right` is absent for words that need nothing after them (`WORDS_WITH_NOTHING_AFTER`), a list
 * for "is one of" words (`WORDS_WITH_A_LIST`), and one expression otherwise.
 * (draft: every part optional, the builder saves as the author goes.)
 */
export interface WordsClause {
  left?: Expression;
  words?: Words;
  right?: Expression | Expression[];
}

/**
 * "Approve is pressed" / "Security team presses Reject". Means: in this stage's current visit,
 * that button was pressed. Only legal in the stage that owns the button (its arrows, its
 * "After they respond" actions and their "Only when"). Elsewhere, read the task's
 * "Button pressed" value instead.
 */
export interface PressedClause {
  pressed: ButtonId;
}

/**
 * The words offered by the builder: a closed list per set of words, available at run time (the
 * condition builder and the engine both need it).
 *  - `yesNo` words are shown naturally, never as a double negative: "Domain needs no approval".
 *  - `date.isOnWeekday` takes a `{ weekday }` constant.
 *  - `person.isIn`: the person is a member of the group (or among the people) on the right.
 */
export const WORDS = {
  text: ["text.is", "text.isNot", "text.contains", "text.doesNotContain", "text.startsWith", "text.isFilled", "text.isEmpty"],
  number: ["number.is", "number.isNot", "number.isMoreThan", "number.isLessThan", "number.isAtLeast", "number.isAtMost", "number.isFilled", "number.isEmpty"],
  yesNo: ["yesNo.isYes", "yesNo.isNo", "yesNo.isFilled", "yesNo.isEmpty"],
  date: ["date.is", "date.isBefore", "date.isAfter", "date.isOnOrBefore", "date.isOnOrAfter", "date.isOnWeekday", "date.isFilled", "date.isEmpty"],
