  choice: ["choice.is", "choice.isNot", "choice.isOneOf", "choice.isNotOneOf", "choice.isFilled", "choice.isEmpty"],
  person: ["person.is", "person.isNot", "person.isOneOf", "person.isIn", "person.isNotIn", "person.isFilled", "person.isEmpty"],
  people: ["people.include", "people.doNotInclude", "people.areFilled", "people.areEmpty"],
  list: ["list.includes", "list.doesNotInclude", "list.includesAnyOf", "list.includesAllOf", "list.isFilled", "list.isEmpty"],
} as const;

export type WordSet = keyof typeof WORDS;
export type Words = (typeof WORDS)[WordSet][number];

/** Which set of words a kind of value is offered. `null`: none in version 0 (use a formula). */
export const WORDS_FOR_KIND: Record<ValueKind, WordSet | null> = {
  text: "text", longText: "text", number: "number", yesNo: "yesNo", date: "date",
  choice: "choice", choiceFromList: "choice", choiceFromConnection: "choice",
  multipleChoice: "list", person: "person", group: "people", people: "people",
  list: null, fieldGroup: null,
};

/** Words that take no `right`. */
export const WORDS_WITH_NOTHING_AFTER = [
  "text.isFilled", "text.isEmpty", "number.isFilled", "number.isEmpty", "yesNo.isYes", "yesNo.isNo", "yesNo.isFilled", "yesNo.isEmpty",
  "date.isFilled", "date.isEmpty", "choice.isFilled", "choice.isEmpty", "person.isFilled", "person.isEmpty",
  "people.areFilled", "people.areEmpty", "list.isFilled", "list.isEmpty",
] as const satisfies readonly Words[];
/** Words whose `right` is a list of expressions. Items of that list that are empty when the
 *  condition is checked are ignored. */
export const WORDS_WITH_A_LIST = [
  "choice.isOneOf", "choice.isNotOneOf", "person.isOneOf", "list.includesAnyOf", "list.includesAllOf",
] as const satisfies readonly Words[];

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 4. Workflow (root)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * The whole authored workflow: one draft (or one published version's source), as the editor
 * saves it. The workflow's name, its authors and "Stuck requests go to" are NOT here: they live
 * in the server's workflow record, so changing them is not an edit to any version.
 */
export interface AuthoredWorkflow {
  /** Version of this format. Stays 0 until the engine has compiled it once. */
  formatVersion: 0;
  /**
   * The document's own item ID: what workflow-level findings point at (`Location.item`). It is
   * NOT the server's workflow ID, which is opaque and server-generated.
   */
  id: WorkflowId;
  /** How a request starts. */
  start: Start;
  /** Every stage and ending. Array order has no meaning for running requests (the editor keeps
   *  the start stage first); arrows decide where requests go. */
  stages: Stage[];
  /** Status words and colours. Stages that show the same words share one status. */
  statuses: Status[];
  /** Things the workflow tells other systems happened ("Tell other systems"). See `ThingTold`. */
  thingsTold: ThingTold[];
  /** The value registry. See `Value`. */
  values: Value[];
  /** Lists kept with the workflow (the Domains list). Versioned with the workflow. */
  lists: List[];
  /** The request the editor uses for every sample it shows. Ignored by the compiler. */
  sampleRequest?: SampleRequest;
  /** Diagram positions. Absent means automatic layout (the normal case). Ignored by the compiler. */
  diagram?: Diagram;
  /**
   * Names of deleted things that are still referenced (an arrow to a deleted stage), so To do can
   * say "goes to Domain review (deleted)". Keyed by the old ID. Ignored by the compiler.
   */
  removedNames?: Record<string, string>;
}

/**
 * How a request starts. Always: a person submits the start stage's form (they become the
 * Requester). In addition, zero or more "Starts when" bindings let something outside start a
 * request by filling in that same form from what another system sent.
 */
export interface Start {
  by: "personSubmitsForm";
  /** The start stage. It must be a working stage with exactly one task. */
  stage: StageId;
  /** "Starts when ..." bindings. Empty when only people start requests. */
  startsWhen: StartsWhen[];
}

/**
 * "Starts when [a ticket is created in Helpdesk] ..."
 * When the catalogue trigger fires (and `onlyWhen` is true for what was sent), a request starts as if
 * the start form had been submitted with `answers`. Everything in a binding reads ONLY the fields
 * of what the other system sent, never workflow values (none exist yet); the types enforce this.
 */
export interface StartsWhen {
  /** Stable, like every other ID. */
  id: StartsWhenId;
  /** A catalogue trigger, e.g. `helpdesk.ticketCreated@1`. (draft: optional.) */
  trigger?: CatalogueRef;
  /** Narrows which of the things sent start a request. */
  onlyWhen?: SentCondition;
  /**
   * Which of the start form's buttons the binding presses. May be absent when the start task has
   * one button; with several, absent is a To do.
   */
  button?: ButtonId;
  /**
   * Names the Requester: a sent field of kind person, e.g. `{ sentField: "raisedBy" }`. The
   * request is still recorded as started by the connection; the Requester value is this person.
   * Absent: the request has no person as Requester, so `{ request: "requester" }` is empty and
   * `ifEmptyUse` applies.
   */
  requester?: SentExpression;
  /**
   * Answers for the start form's questions, keyed by question ID. Questions not listed stay empty.
   * The start form's "Needed to press" is checked against these answers: if it fails, no request
   * starts and the people who look after stuck requests are told.
   */
  answers: Partial<Record<QuestionId, SentExpression | SentTemplate>>;
}

/**
 * A field of what the other system sent. `sentField` is the field's id in the catalogue
 * trigger, dotted for nested fields (`reporter.email`).
 */
export interface SentFieldReference {
  sentField: string;
}
/** An expression inside a "Starts when" binding: fields of what was sent, constants, or a formula
 *  whose chips are written `{{sent.<field>}}`. */
export type SentExpression = SentFieldReference | Constant | Formula;
export type SentTemplate = Array<string | SentExpression>;
export type SentCondition = { allOf: SentClause[] } | { anyOf: SentClause[] } | Formula;
export interface SentClause {
  left?: SentExpression;
  words?: Words;
  right?: SentExpression | SentExpression[];
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 5. Stages, statuses and tasks
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** A box on the diagram: where a request sits. */
export type Stage = WorkingStage | EndingStage;

/**
 * The kind of stage. A kind is chosen when the stage is added; it pre-fills the stage and labels
 * it. It does not change which fields are legal, except that an ending has no anatomy.
 */
export type WorkingStageKind = "form" | "approval" | "work" | "automatic" | "blank";

/**
 * Every working stage has the same fixed anatomy, done in this order:
 *   whenThisStageStarts (actions, in order) → tasks → afterTheyRespond (actions, in order) → arrows.
 * Order rule: within one section, actions run in listed order and saves take effect in listed
 * order, so a later action, a later section, or an arrow sees an earlier save (and an earlier
 * action's saved results).
 * An Automatic stage has no tasks; the panel shows its `whenThisStageStarts` as "What it does".
 */
export interface WorkingStage {
  id: StageId;
  kind: WorkingStageKind;
  /** (draft: may be empty.) */
  name: string;
  /** The status people see while a request is here. (draft: optional.)
   *  The start stage normally has none: a request is never seen sitting there unless it is sent
   *  back, and then `ifSentBackStatus` is shown. Exception, raised by the check as a To do (not a
   *  format rule): a start stage with a connection action in "After they respond" needs a
   *  status, because a request can be seen sitting (or stuck) there. */
  status?: StatusId;
  /**
   * The status shown instead when the request arrived by an arrow that sends it back ("If sent
   * back: Needs changes"). Legal on any working stage. "Sent back" is never stored: an arrow sends
   * back when it goes to a stage that every request must already have passed through to reach the
   * arrow's own stage; the engine works this out.
   */
  ifSentBackStatus?: StatusId;
  /**
   * Done in order, before anyone is asked, every time the stage is entered. A new request begins
   * at the start stage's form, so the start stage's `whenThisStageStarts` runs only when a request
   * is sent back there.
   */
  whenThisStageStarts: Action[];
  /**
   * Who is asked, each with a form and buttons. Usually one; a short fixed list when several are
   * asked at the same time; none for an Automatic stage. All tasks open when the stage starts.
   */
  tasks: Task[];
  /** Done in order, once, when the stage finishes (after all tasks, or when an arrow marked
   *  `goAsSoonAsTrue` is taken). */
  afterTheyRespond: Action[];
  /** "Then go to". Checked from the top; the first one that fits is used. */
  arrows: Arrow[];
}

/** A box where a request finishes. Status and colour only. */
export interface EndingStage {
  id: StageId;
  kind: "ending";
  name: string;
  /** (draft: optional.) */
  status?: StatusId;
}

/** Status words and colour. Referenced by ID from stages, so two stages can share one. */
export interface Status {
  id: StatusId;
  /** "Waiting for approval". (draft: may be empty.) */
  words: string;
  colour: "grey" | "red" | "amber" | "green" | "blue" | "purple" | "teal" | "pink";
}

/** The part of a stage that asks people: who is asked, a form, buttons. */
export interface Task {
  id: TaskId;
  /**
   * The task's own name. Absent while the stage has one task. With several, the editor names each
   * task after who is asked ("Domain approvers"); set here only if the author renamed it.
   */
  name?: string;
  /**
   * Who is asked: an expression giving a person, a group, or several people. A fallback is
   * written on the reference (`ifEmptyUse`). For the start stage this is `{ request: "requester" }`
   * and only matters when a request is sent back there. (draft: optional — "Nobody is asked".)
   */
  whoIsAsked?: Expression;
  /**
   * How a group answers. Version 0 has one rule: "One answer is enough: the first person in the
   * group to answer decides." Later rules (everyone, at least N) would be new words here.
   */
  groupRule: "firstAnswerDecides";
  /** "The requester can't answer their own request" is this set to false (Approval: false). */
  requesterCanAnswer: boolean;
  form: Form;
  /** How a person finishes the task. Order is display order. */
  buttons: Button[];
  /**
   * The task's two extra answers, "Button pressed" (holds a `{ button }`) and "Answered by"
   * (a person). The value is created the first time the author uses it; absent means not saved.
   * When the task is cancelled by a `goAsSoonAsTrue` arrow, both are emptied for that visit; its
   * questions' values keep what they had.
   */
  savesButtonPressedAs?: ValueId;
  savesAnsweredByAs?: ValueId;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 6. Forms
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** The questions a task shows, on one or more pages. Form logic only shows or hides. */
export interface Form {
  pages: Page[];
}

export interface Page {
  id: PageId;
  title?: string;
  /** "Show when". When hidden, its questions stay empty. */
  showWhen?: Condition;
  items: FormItem[];
}

export type FormItem = Question | FormText;

/**
 * The kinds of question the author picks. The value it fills has the same kind, except a
 * `choice` whose choices come from a list (`choiceFromList`) or a catalogue data source
 * (`choiceFromConnection`); see `ValueKind`. A question whose choices are the people in a group
 * is a `person` question and fills a `person` value.
 */
export type QuestionKind = Extract<ValueKind, "text" | "longText" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "choice" | "multipleChoice" | "person" | "group">;

export interface Question {
  type: "question";
  id: QuestionId;
  /** (draft: may be empty.) */
  label: string;
  kind: QuestionKind;
  /** "Saved as [value]". Absent only in a broken draft (the editor creates the value with the question). */
  savedAs?: ValueId;
  /** For choice, multiple choice, person and group. (draft: optional.) */
  choices?: Choices;
  /** "Show when". When hidden, the question stays empty and is not needed to press any button. */
  showWhen?: Condition;
  /**
   * The "All" tick under "Needed to press": needed for every button of the task, including
   * buttons added later. See `Button.neededToPress` for the effective set.
   */
  neededForEveryButton?: boolean;
}

/** Text people can read but not change ("+ Add text"), with value chips in it. */
export interface FormText {
  type: "text";
  id: TextId;
  content: Template;
  showWhen?: Condition;
}

/**
 * Where a question's choices come from. Choices from the directory and from a connection are read
 * live while the form is shown, on the start form too; the answer is checked by a lookup when the
 * person answers, and for a connection the source's label is recorded with that lookup.
 */
export type Choices =
  /** Typed in by the author. */
  | { from: "typedIn"; choices: Choice[] }
  /** The rows of a list kept with the workflow; `shownColumn` is what people see. The answer is the row. */
  | { from: "list"; list: ListId; shownColumn?: ColumnId }
  /** The people in a group given by an expression (Lists and directory), e.g. the members of
   *  "Primary domain's engineering group". The answer is a person, so the value it fills has kind
   *  `person`, never `choice`. The editor offers this only on a question of kind `person`
   *  (changing the kind to text, number, choice and so on removes these choices; on a `group`
   *  question it is a To do); the fixtures do the same (`q_eng_lead`). */
  | { from: "directory"; peopleIn: Expression }
  /**
   * A catalogue data source, e.g. `servicecatalog.services@1`. `inputs` maps the source's input
   * fields to expressions; `labelField` is the item field people see, `storedField` the one
   * stored. The answer is one value of kind `choiceFromConnection`: `{ stored, label }`.
   */
  | { from: "source"; source?: CatalogueRef; inputs: Record<string, Expression | Template>; labelField?: string; storedField?: string }
  /** A formula that gives the list of choices. */
  | { from: "formula"; formula: Formula };

export interface Choice {
  id: ChoiceId;
  label: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 7. Buttons
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface Button {
  id: ButtonId;
  /** "Approve". (draft: may be empty.) */
  label: string;
  look: "primary" | "secondary" | "danger";
  /**
   * "Needed to press": questions that must be answered before this button can be pressed. The
   * effective set is this list plus every question of the task with `neededForEveryButton`.
   * A hidden question is never needed. The form editor shows the same fact on each question.
   */
  neededToPress: QuestionId[];
  /** "Also only when ...": one more "when ..." that must be true to press it. */
  enabledWhen?: Condition;
  /** Shown while it cannot be pressed. Absent: the editor reads back its needs and "when ...". */
  messageWhileDisabled?: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 8. Actions: things the workflow does by itself (and "Save a value")
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * An item in "When this stage starts" or "After they respond".
 * Every one may carry `onlyWhen`. There is no nesting.
 * Items run in listed order and saves take effect in listed order: a later item, and the arrows,
 * see what an earlier one saved.
 */
export type Action = SaveValue | Notify | UseConnection | TellOtherSystems;

interface ActionBase {
  id: ActionId;
  /** "Only when ...". For a save: when not true, the value keeps what it had. */
  onlyWhen?: Condition;
}

/** "Save [what] as [value]". */
export interface SaveValue extends ActionBase {
  type: "saveValue";
  /** (draft: optional.) */
  save?: Expression;
  /** (draft: optional.) */
  as?: ValueId;
}

/** "Notify [who]". The channel (email, Slack) is the platform's choice. If it can't be sent, the
 *  request carries on; there is no setting for that. */
export interface Notify extends ActionBase {
  type: "notify";
  /** A person, group or several people. (draft: optional.) */
  to?: Expression;
  /** Sent with the values as they were at that moment. */
  message: Template;
}

/**
 * Use a catalogue operation: "Create Jira issue", a look-up, "Wait for [system]".
 * Which sort it is (read: gives data / write: does something / await: asks the outside system to
 * do something and waits until it reports back, which may take long) is decided by the catalogue,
 * not by this format. The editor names the action after the operation.
 */
export interface UseConnection extends ActionBase {
  type: "useConnection";
  /** e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`. (draft: optional.) */
  operation?: CatalogueRef;
  /** Keyed by the operation's catalogue input field ids (e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`: `project`,
   *  `summary`, `assignee`, `description`), to expressions or templates. Fields the author has not
   *  filled are absent. */
  inputs: Record<string, Expression | Template>;
  /** Keyed by the operation's catalogue result field ids (e.g. `key`, `url`), to the values they
   *  are saved as. */
  saveResults: Record<string, ValueId>;
  /**
   * "If it fails". Applies to every connection action, look-ups included.
   * "stuck": the request is stuck here and the people in "Stuck requests go to" are told; they
   * can retry or close it. "carryOn": a failure is an ordinary result; later actions and the
   * arrows go on, and can test `saveFailureAs`.
   */
  ifItFails: "stuck" | "carryOn";
  /**
   * Only with "carryOn". `failed`: a Yes/No value, Yes when the operation failed and No when it
   * worked, so an arrow can say "When Deploy failed is Yes go to ...". `code`: a `choice` value
   * holding the failure code (one of the operation's catalogue failure codes; see `ValueKind`);
   * left as it was on success.
   */
  saveFailureAs?: { failed?: ValueId; code?: ValueId };
  /**
   * When the stage is entered again (after a send-back): "once" reuses the first result (one Jira
   * issue per request); "again" does it again. Absent: the catalogue entry's default.
   */
  ifStageEntersAgain?: "once" | "again";
}

/**
 * "Tell other systems": tells other systems something happened. Like Notify, it can never stop a
 * request. Who receives it is chosen outside the workflow by a platform admin.
 */
export interface TellOtherSystems extends ActionBase {
  type: "tellOtherSystems";
  /** Which thing told (an entry of `thingsTold`). Two actions may tell the same thing.
   *  (draft: optional.) */
  tell?: ToldId;
  /**
   * What the outside systems receive: field name to expression or template. The keys are what
   * the outside system receives, so renaming one is a visible change for it.
   */
  values: Record<string, Expression | Template>;
}

/**
 * Something the workflow tells other systems happened, e.g. "Change released". A registry like
 * statuses, so several actions can tell the same thing. Outside systems key on the `id`, so it
 * survives rewording `words`.
 */
export interface ThingTold {
  id: ToldId;
  /** The author's words for what happened. (draft: may be empty.) */
  words: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 9. Arrows ("Then go to")
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * One line under "Then go to": "When ... go to ...". Belongs to its source stage. An arrow carries
 * only a "when" and a destination: everything that happens lives in the stage's two action
 * sections, with "Only when".
 */
export interface Arrow {
  id: ArrowId;
  when: ArrowWhen;
  /** "+ only when ...": narrows a button arrow ("When Approve is pressed and Risk is High"). */
  onlyWhen?: Condition;
  /** The stage or ending it goes to. `null`: not chosen yet (amber To do). */
  goTo: StageId | null;
  /** "Words on the arrow". Absent: the editor uses the arrow's sentence ("Approve pressed"). */
  words?: string;
  /**
   * "Don't wait for the others" (stages with several tasks only): checked after every answer, and
   * taken as soon as it fits; tasks still open are cancelled. Default: checked once everyone
   * asked has answered.
   */
  goAsSoonAsTrue?: boolean;
}

export type ArrowWhen =
  /** "When [button] is pressed". */
  | { type: "buttonPressed"; button: ButtonId | null }
  /** A "when ..." that depends on answers. (draft: `condition` optional.) */
  | { type: "condition"; condition?: Condition }
  /** "In all other cases": the catch-all, last. */
  | { type: "inAllOtherCases" }
  /** "When done": an Automatic stage's arrow. */
  | { type: "whenDone" };

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 10. Values, lists, sample request, diagram
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * A named piece of data the workflow remembers. Never declared by the author: an entry exists
 * because something fills it. It is filled by
 *   - a question (`Question.savedAs`),
 *   - a save (`SaveValue.as`),
 *   - an action's result (`UseConnection.saveResults`, `UseConnection.saveFailureAs`),
 *   - a task's extra answers (`Task.savesButtonPressedAs`, `Task.savesAnsweredByAs`).
 * Its kind is not stored: it comes from what fills it. Two fillers of different kinds is a red
 * To do. If two places fill a value, the later one replaces the earlier. Within one stage, when two
 * tasks fill the same value, the task later in the document wins, not the later answer in time.
 *
 * "Used in N places" is derived, never stored: scan the document for references to the ID
 * (`{ "value": id }` in any expression or template, and `{{id}}` inside formula text), excluding
 * the filling positions above; N is the number of distinct items (question, text, button, action,
 * arrow, task, binding) containing one. "Filled in N places" is the count of filling positions.
 */
export interface Value {
  id: ValueId;
  name: string;
  description?: string;
}

/** A small table kept with the workflow, such as the Domains list. Versioned with the workflow. */
export interface List {
  id: ListId;
  name: string;
  columns: Column[];
  rows: Row[];
}

export interface Column {
  id: ColumnId;
  name: string;
  kind: "text" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "person" | "group";
}

export interface Row {
  id: RowId;
  /** Cells by column ID. An absent cell is "(not given)". */
  cells: Partial<Record<ColumnId, Constant>>;
}

/** The request the editor uses for samples (the last one used in Try it). */
export interface SampleRequest {
  /** Shown in the toolbar: "Sample: Rotate payment gateway API keys". */
  name: string;
  requester?: DirectoryRef;
  /** `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
  startedOn?: string;
  /** Sample answers by value ID. Values without one show no sample. */
  answers: Partial<Record<ValueId, Constant>>;
}

export interface Diagram {
  /** Positions per stage; stages without one are placed automatically. */
  positions: Partial<Record<StageId, { x: number; y: number }>>;
}
===\ncontract/authoring-api.md\n===
# Contract part B2: the authoring API (server)

Draft 3, engine owner, 2026-11-15. Replaces Draft 2. Pending the frontend owner's review and the product owner's review.
Revised 2026-11-15 after E-21 to E-26, and 2026-11-16 after E-27, E-28, E-31, E-32 and E-33.

The server's side of authoring: the workflows list, drafts, publishing, versions, each workflow's settings record, the catalogue and the server's core version. Checking, facts, formulas, form state, Try it and diff run in the browser on the core package (`core-api.md`); the server runs the same core again at save and at publish (E-3). Written against kernel spec v2.20, whose copy is in `engine/spec/`, and against decisions E-1 to E-33 (`docs/11-decisions-engine.md`). How codes are spelled: `core-api.md` section 1.1. Every shared type (`Result`, `ApiError`, `Finding`, `Ref`, `Caller`, `ServerWorkflowId`, `VersionNumber`, `CoreMeta`, `ParseProblem` ...) is defined in `core-api.md` (sections 2, 3, 4 and 13) and not repeated here.

## 1. Rules

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Each operation is a plain function taking the `Caller`, with a thin web-standard `Request -> Response` handler over it (E-11). The frontend's client omits `caller`; the host supplies it. | Mountable in the existing application later. |
| Paths are relative to `{base}`. The development host mounts this API and the runtime API at `/api/workflow/v1`, on one port. In the existing application: unknown: depends on the existing application. | |
| JSON bodies, UTF-8. A request body may be 64 KiB larger than the largest draft (1 MiB), so a draft that is too large gets the save's own `too-large` with the draft limit, not the body's (E-31). No `null` in any body, except inside an authored document, which keeps the nulls the authored format allows (`Arrow.goTo`, `ArrowWhen.button`) so an unfinished draft saves, and in the catalogue (operation 11), which writes `null` out as `catalogue.ts` says. Every response carries `Engine-Core-Version` and `Engine-Definition-Format` (`core-api.md` section 13). | Stale browser bundles are detected (E-3). |
| Success: the status in the table and the value as the body. Failure: the status of the first error's code (`core-api.md` section 2.6) and `{ "errors": ApiError[] }`. | One failure shape for every server call. |
| Paths carry no version of their own; the version is in `{base}`. | The only client ships with the server. Cheap to change. |

## 2. Who may do what

**Assumption, not decided by the product owner:** any signed-in user may create a workflow and becomes its first author. A workflow's authors may edit its draft, publish it and change its settings. Platform admins may do everything an author may, so a workflow whose authors have all left can be recovered.

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| List workflows, read a draft, list and read versions, read settings, read the catalogue | Any signed-in user |
| Create a workflow | Any signed-in user (assumption) |
| Save a draft, publish, save settings | The workflow's authors and platform admins (assumption) |

A user is an author if listed in `Settings.authors` or a member, looked up live, of a listed group. Every response that describes a workflow carries the caller's flags `may: { edit, publish, settings }`, so the frontend never works them out. Others get `forbidden` with `need: "author"`. If the directory cannot be reached, `may` is worked out from direct listing only, and a save, publish or settings save that needs a group to admit the caller is refused with `membership-unavailable`.

## 3. Resources

```ts
interface May { edit: boolean; publish: boolean; settings: boolean }

interface WorkflowSummary {
  id: ServerWorkflowId;
  name: string;
  description: string;                       // may be ""
  liveVersion?: VersionNumber;               // highest published version; absent: never published
  draft: { revision: number; savedAt: Timestamp; savedBy: Ref; changedSinceLive: boolean; todo: number; worthKnowing: number };
  triggers: { live: CatalogueRef[]; draft: CatalogueRef[] };   // the catalogue triggers its "Starts when" bindings use, document order, no repeats
  openRequests: number;                      // not closed, all versions
  stuckRequests: number;                     // stuck, for any reason (core-api.md section 8)
  may: May;
}

interface Draft {
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  revision: number;                          // 1 at creation; +1 on every save
  authored: AuthoredWorkflow;                // upgraded to the server core's authored format on read
  savedAt: Timestamp; savedBy: Ref;
  basedOnVersion?: VersionNumber;            // the live version when this revision was saved
  may: May;
}

interface SavedDraft { revision: number; savedAt: Timestamp; todo: number; worthKnowing: number }

interface PublishResult { version: VersionNumber; findings: Finding[] }   // findings: worthKnowing only

interface VersionSummary {
  version: VersionNumber;
  publishedAt: Timestamp; publishedBy: Ref;
  fromRevision: number;
  coreVersion: string; formatVersion: number;
  openRequests: number;                      // requests on this version not closed
}
interface Version extends VersionSummary {
  authored: AuthoredWorkflow;                // as published, not upgraded; the compiled definition stays on the server
}

interface Settings {
  name: string;
  description: string;                       // may be ""
  authors: Ref[];                            // at least one; users and groups
  stuckRequestsGoTo?: Ref[];                 // absent: the authors; never an empty list
}
interface SettingsRead extends Settings {    // what getSettings and saveSettings return
  changedBy: Ref;                            // who made the last change; the creator until the first save (E-23)
  changedAt: Timestamp;                      // when
}
```

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| The workflow ID is server-generated and never changes; name and description are settings. | The ID is recorded in `RequestStarted` for ever. |
| One draft per workflow, created with it, kept after publish. | The draft is "what I am working on"; versions are snapshots. |
| `todo`, `worthKnowing` are counted by the server's core at each save and stored with the draft. | The list needs them without running core over every draft. |
| `triggers.live` is read from the highest published version, `triggers.draft` from the draft. Whether a live binding is paused is `runtime-api.md` section 5.3. | The list can say "Starts when ..." without loading documents. |
| `stuckRequestsGoTo` absent follows the authors, resolved when read. An empty list is refused (`invalid-body`, problem `empty`). | Alerts must reach someone; a platform admin can always act. |
| Settings are not versioned and not history. A change applies at once to running requests: who may retry and close, who is told. | Spec: workflow admins live outside the published definition (E-14). |
| Every change to the settings is recorded with who and when, one `settings_log` row per save holding the record before and after (E-23). `SettingsRead.changedBy` and `changedAt` return the last. A body sent to `saveSettings` may carry `changedBy` and `changedAt`; they are ignored. | Who changed who is told, and who may retry and close, must be traceable. |
| Names need not be unique. A draft is at most 1 MiB. | Cheap to change. |

## 4. Two editors at once

Optimistic concurrency, no locks, no settings revision (F9: one author at a time). Each save names the revision it was based on. If that is not current, the save is refused with `stale-revision` and the current draft; nothing is merged. Settings are replaced whole; the last save wins. Locks, presence and merging are later and need no change here.

## 5. Operations

| # | Function | HTTP | Success |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `listWorkflows(caller): Result<WorkflowSummary[]>` | `GET {base}/workflows` | 200, newest draft first |
| 2 | `createWorkflow(caller, { name, description? }): Result<Draft>` | `POST {base}/workflows` | 201, `Location: {base}/workflows/{id}/draft` |
| 3 | `getDraft(caller, workflow): Result<Draft>` | `GET {base}/workflows/{id}/draft` | 200 |
| 4 | `saveDraft(caller, workflow, { baseRevision, authored }): Result<SavedDraft>` | `PUT {base}/workflows/{id}/draft` | 200 |
| 5 | `publish(caller, workflow, { revision, coreVersion }): Result<PublishResult>` | `POST {base}/workflows/{id}/versions` | 201, `Location: {base}/workflows/{id}/versions/{n}` |
| 6 | `listVersions(caller, workflow): Result<VersionSummary[]>` | `GET {base}/workflows/{id}/versions` | 200, newest first |
| 7 | `getVersion(caller, workflow, version): Result<Version>` | `GET {base}/workflows/{id}/versions/{n}` | 200, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` |
| 8 | `getSettings(caller, workflow): Result<SettingsRead>` | `GET {base}/workflows/{id}/settings` | 200 |
| 9 | `saveSettings(caller, workflow, settings: Settings): Result<SettingsRead>` | `PUT {base}/workflows/{id}/settings` | 200 |
| 10 | `getMeta(): Result<CoreMeta>` | `GET {base}/meta` | 200; no caller needed |
| 11 | `getCatalogue(caller): Result<Catalogue>` | `GET {base}/catalogue` | 200 |

Errors each operation can return (codes and params: `core-api.md` section 2.6). Every operation can also return `unauthenticated` (except `getMeta`), `invalid-body` and `internal`.

| # | Errors |
|---|---|
| 1 | none beyond the above |
| 2 | none beyond the above |
| 3 | `not-found` (`workflow`) |
| 4 | `not-found`, `forbidden`, `membership-unavailable`, `too-large`, `authored-format-unsupported`, `invalid-document`, `stale-revision` |
| 5 | `not-found`, `forbidden`, `membership-unavailable`, `core-version-mismatch`, `stale-revision`, `has-todo` |
| 6, 8 | `not-found` |
| 7 | `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`) |
| 9 | `not-found`, `forbidden`, `membership-unavailable`, `last-author` |
| 10, 11 | none beyond the above |

Behaviour:

2. **Create.** Generates the ID; stores the workflow with `authors: [caller.user]`, no `stuckRequestsGoTo`, the given name and description (`""` when absent), and a first `settings_log` row; stores draft revision 1 holding core's blank workflow (`blankWorkflow`, `core-api.md` section 14) at the current authored-format version (E-31). Authored IDs in the document are at most 40 characters (E-23; `core-api.md` section 3).
4. **Save.** In order: `stale-revision` if `baseRevision` is not current; `too-large`; `authored-format-unsupported` if `formatVersion` is outside what the server's core reads; `invalid-document` with the problems if `parse` fails. The check need not pass: a draft may be unfinished. Runs `check` to store the counts. One transaction with a lock on the workflow row.
5. **Publish.** One transaction with a lock on the workflow row: `core-version-mismatch` if `coreVersion` differs; `stale-revision` if `revision` is not current; upgrade, then `compile` with the server's catalogue in publish mode, with `workflow`, `version` and `compiler` filled (`core-api.md` section 12); any `todo` refuses with `has-todo` carrying the compiler's findings as it gives them, To dos and Worth knowing (E-31). The server then runs the kernel publish check with its catalogue, `checkDefinition(definition, catalogue)` (`core-api.md` section 14); a problem of severity `error` is a bug in core, answered `internal` with nothing written; a `warning` does not stop publishing (E-27). Inserts the version (highest + 1) with the compiled definition, schemas, origin map, the authored source, `from_revision`, `core_version`, `format_version`. Returns the version and the worth-knowing findings, which need no acknowledgement. The server's check is authoritative (E-3); if the catalogue changed since the author's check, the server's findings win. Publishing an unchanged draft makes a new version. The new version's bindings become the live ones (E-17); a binding keeps its paused state across versions, keyed by its `sw_` ID. Pausing and resuming a binding is the runtime API's (`runtime-api.md` section 5.3); this API has no binding operation (E-31).
7. **Read a version.** The authored source as published, not upgraded, so pages render a task from the version its request runs on (E-6). The runtime's `publishedSource` serves the same document to people who are not authors.
9. **Settings.** Replaces the whole record and writes one `settings_log` row with the caller and the time. `last-author` if `authors` is empty. The caller may remove themselves.
11. **Catalogue.** The server's current catalogue (`catalogue.ts`), every default written out, with `directoryConnection` naming the connection that is the directory and `notifyConnection` naming the connection that carries Notify (E-27). Both are always present, and the catalogue's version covers them. The editor treats it as data and hard-codes no connection (E-10). The catalogue is read from the server's configuration at start-up and changes only with a restart; every entry is `ready` (E-33). An entry of a `notSetUp` connection is a To do at publish (`catalogue.connectionNotSetUp`); of a `disabled` one, Worth knowing (`catalogue.connectionDisabled`).

## 6. What this needs in the engine's tables

The spec copy is read-only here; these go to `workflow-platform/engine` as a change request.

| Table | Change |
|---|---|
| `workflows` (new) | `id` (primary key), `name`, `description`, `created_by`, `created_at`. |
| `drafts` (new) | `workflow` (primary key), `revision`, `authored` jsonb, `saved_by`, `saved_at`, `based_on_version`, `todo`, `worth_knowing`. Working state, updated in place. |
| `definitions` | `workflow` holds the server workflow ID, not its name (E-23). Add `authored` (the authored source as published), `from_revision`, `core_version`, `format_version`. |
| `workflow_settings` | `authors` jsonb (users and groups); `stuck_requests_go_to` jsonb, the people who look after stuck requests, null or empty = the authors. It replaces the column `admins` (E-24); no column `admins` remains. |
| `settings_log` (new) | `workflow`, `at`, `by`, `before` jsonb (null at creation), `after` jsonb. One row per create, per settings save, and per pause or resume of a binding (E-23, E-33). Log. |
| `requests` | `client_token` and `client_args_hash`, unique per `(started_by, client_token)` (`runtime-api.md` section 3.3). |

## 7. Open points

1. **Who may author** is an assumption (section 2). The product owner decides; only who gets `forbidden` changes.
2. **Archiving a workflow** is not designed. It would be a flag that hides the workflow and refuses new starts, never a delete.
3. **Draft history.** Each save overwrites the draft. Keeping revisions is one more table and no API change.
4. **Which catalogue version a version was checked against** is not recorded; operation versions are pinned in the definition.
5. **Sign-in, the base path and the platform-admin entitlement:** unknown: depends on the existing application.
===\ncontract/catalogue.ts\n===
// Contract part D: the catalogue of connections.
// Draft 3, engine owner.
// Matches engine/design/integrations-shapes.md section 2 under decisions E-10, E-17, E-19, E-20,
// E-23, E-27, E-28 and E-32; contract/fixtures/catalogue.json follows it. Pending the frontend owner's review and the
// product owner's review.
//
// The catalogue is data. The editor hard-codes no connection and no entry (E-10). It is served by
// `GET {base}/catalogue` (authoring-api.md, operation 11) with every default written out, so a
// field below is never missing. Unlike the rest of the contract it holds `null` where this file
// says so, because it is the same document the server registers (integrations-shapes.md 2.9).
//
// Fixed: every field that the shape hash covers (`kind`, `sort`, `input`, `result`, `failureCodes`,
// `item`, `searchable`, `event`). Labels, descriptions, a field's `addressOf`, `supersededBy`,
// `onRepeat`, timeouts, `expectedWithinSeconds`, `await`, `cacheSeconds` and `sample` may change under
// one entry ID (E-20: the shape hash ignores labels; E-32: `addressOf` is display only). The
// catalogue's `version` covers all of them.
//
// The directory is a connection like any other. `directoryConnection` names it; it declares the
// operation `membersOf@1` (the recorded read behind a members step, an "is in group" test and the
// nobody-to-ask rule) and the data source `groupMembers@1` (directory choices, read live and looked
// up when the person acts) (integrations-shapes.md 2.7, 5.2, 5.5). A `membersOf@1` group item may carry the
// group's name. `notifyConnection` names the connection that carries Notify.

import type { ValueKind } from "./authored-format";

export type { ValueKind };

/** Any JSON value, as samples and items hold it. */
export type Json = string | number | boolean | null | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };
export type JsonObject = { [key: string]: Json };

/**
 * "<connection>.<name>@<version>", for example "jira.createIssue@1". Never names a second shape.
 *   connection: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$          (engine, system and platform are reserved)
 *   name:       ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}$         lowerCamelCase
 *   version:    ^[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$
 * The authored format names an entry with its `CatalogueRef`, which has this form.
 */
export type CatalogueId = string;

export interface Catalogue {
  /**
   * "cat1." + base64url(SHA-256(JCS({ connections, entries, directoryConnection, notifyConnection }))).
   * A check result names the version it used.
   */
  version: string;
  /**
   * The ID of the connection that is the directory: a platform setting (integrations-shapes.md 2.7,
   * 2.9). `compile` is pure (E-3) and learns it here; it names this connection in every membership
   * read and every directory choice. Always present.
   */
  directoryConnection: string;
  /**
   * The ID of the connection that carries Notify: the platform's messages and alerts. A platform
   * setting (integrations-shapes.md 2.7, 2.9). A workflow never names it; the platform sends every
   * notification through it. Always present. It must name a configured connection, or start-up fails.
   */
  notifyConnection: string;
  connections: Connection[];
  /** Every entry of every connection, defaults written out. */
  entries: CatalogueEntry[];
}

/**
 * A configured instance of a connector: one outside system the platform can reach. Set up by a
 * platform admin from configuration at start-up (E-19, E-20); never by an author.
 */
export interface Connection {
  id: string;                     // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$; never renamed, never reused
  label: string;                  // "Jira"
  description: string | null;
  /**
   * ready:    authors may use its entries.
   * notSetUp: listed, but unusable until a platform admin finishes it; an entry of it is a To do at publish.
   * disabled: a platform admin has disabled it in configuration. Every entry of it then behaves as
   *           a disabled entry, its inbound hook answers 503, and its subscriptions' deliveries
   *           fail and retry. An entry of it is Worth knowing at publish.
   * Connections are applied from configuration at start-up only (E-20).
   */
  status: "ready" | "notSetUp" | "disabled";
}

export type CatalogueEntry = Operation | DataSource | Trigger | EventSink;

interface EntryBase {
  id: CatalogueId;
  connection: string;             // Connection.id
  name: string;                   // "createIssue"
  version: number;                // 1
  kind: "operation" | "dataSource" | "trigger" | "eventSink";
  label: string;                  // "Create a Jira issue"
  description: string | null;
  /** A newer entry ID. Published workflows keep running on this one. */
  supersededBy: CatalogueId | null;
  /**
   * ready:    usable.
   * disabled: its shape changed under this ID, or it is no longer declared, so the server refused
   *           it at start-up (E-20: the entry, not its connection). Its calls wait, a data source
   *           answers source-unavailable, a trigger's events are dropped; Worth knowing at publish.
   * Filled by the server at registration, never by a connector.
   */
  status: "ready" | "disabled";
}

/** A field of an input, a result, an item or an event, in the editor's value kinds (E-17). */
export interface Field {
  id: string;                     // ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$; unique among its siblings; never starts with $
  label: string;
  /** A list kept with a workflow cannot come from outside, so never `choiceFromList`. */
  kind: Exclude<ValueKind, "choiceFromList">;
  /** false: the key may be absent. It is never null. */
  required: boolean;
  /** Exactly for `choice` and `multipleChoice`: the allowed values, unique. */
  choices?: { value: string; label: string }[];
  /** `list` only: the kind of each item. Exactly one of `itemKind` and `fields` for a list. */
  itemKind?: ValueKind;
  /** A list of objects, or a `fieldGroup`: its fields. */
  fields?: Field[];
  /**
   * A `text` field only: the ID of the sibling field whose web address this field holds, so a page can
   * show that field as a link (a Jira issue's `url` is the address of its `key`). Display only: not
   * covered by the shape hash (E-32).
   */
  addressOf?: string;
}

/** Something a workflow asks a connection to do or to tell it (door 3: a call). */
export interface Operation extends EntryBase {
  kind: "operation";
  /**
   * read:  gives data and changes nothing outside ("Look up").
   * write: does something outside and answers at once ("Do").
   * await: asks the outside system to do something and waits until it reports the result,
   *        which may take long ("Wait for"). The kernel sees it as a write call (E-17).
   */
  sort: "read" | "write" | "await";
  input: Field[];
  result: Field[];
  /** The failure codes it can report, kebab-case, unique. A failure is recorded as { code, message }. */
  failureCodes: { code: string; label: string }[];
  /**
   * The default for "when the stage is entered again" (a send-back), written out for every write
   * and await operation; null exactly for read.
   *   once:  the first result is reused and nothing is done twice (one Jira issue per request).
   *   again: it is done again on every entry.
   * The author may choose otherwise (`UseConnection.ifStageEntersAgain`). Publish writes the choice
   * explicitly, so a later change here changes only later publishes.
   */
  onRepeat: "once" | "again" | null;
  /** One delivery or one status question. Default 30. */
  timeoutSeconds: number;
  /**
   * A call with no result after this many seconds raises one call-overdue alert to the workflow
   * admins (E-17). At least `timeoutSeconds`. Default 900 for read and write; required for await.
   */
  expectedWithinSeconds: number;
  /** Non-null exactly when sort is "await". */
  await: null | {
    /** The outside system can call the engine's callback URL to say the job has moved on. A callback is a nudge, never a result (E-17). */
    callback: boolean;
    /** How often the engine asks for the job's status while the action waits. At least 10. */
    pollSeconds: number;
  };
  /** Used by Try it and by the editor's examples. Values follow core-api.md section 2.4. */
  sample: {
    input: JsonObject;            // fits `input`
    result: JsonObject;           // fits `result`
    failure: { code: string; message: string } | null;   // code is one of failureCodes
  };
}

/**
 * Data for a question's choices (door 5). The connector offers two things for every data source
 * (E-17):
 *   list: the items for the inputs, with an optional search text when `searchable`, paged;
 *         used when the form is shown (runtime-api.md section 3.4).
 *   get:  one item by the value of a field (the question's stored field) for the same inputs;
 *         used when the person acts, to check the answer and take the source's label (E-20).
 * `get` finds an item only if `list` with the same inputs would return it. Stored values are
 * stable identifiers.
 */
export interface DataSource extends EntryBase {
  kind: "dataSource";
  input: Field[];                 // arguments, for example a filter or a parent choice
  item: Field[];                  // the fields of one item; a question names its stored and label fields
  searchable: boolean;            // list accepts a search text
  /** How long a list result is cached. Default 60; 0 = never cached. `get` is never cached. */
  cacheSeconds: number;
  /** One list or one get. Default 10. */
  timeoutSeconds: number;
  sample: { input: JsonObject; items: JsonObject[] };
}

/** An outside event that can start a request (door 1, "Starts when"). */
export interface Trigger extends EntryBase {
  kind: "trigger";
  /** What a binding reads as sent.<field>. A person field holds `{ type: "user", id }`, resolved by the connector, or is absent. */
  event: Field[];
  sample: { event: JsonObject };
}

/** A subscriber that outbound events are sent to (door 7). Display only: shows the editor which systems receive them. */
export interface EventSink extends EntryBase {
  kind: "eventSink";
}

// Directory (people and groups). A reference is { type, id } with the directory's immutable object
// ID. This is the shape of a person or group everywhere in the contract (core-api.md 2.4), and
// differs from the authored format's own `DirectoryRef` ({ directoryId, name }).
export interface DirectoryRef { type: "user" | "group"; id: string }
export interface DirectoryEntry extends DirectoryRef {
  label: string;                  // display name
  detail?: string;                // for example an email address or a group description
}
export interface DirectoryApi {
  search(query: string, types: ("user" | "group")[]): Promise<DirectoryEntry[]>;
  lookup(refs: DirectoryRef[]): Promise<DirectoryEntry[]>;
  /**
   * For people pickers, samples and the form editor. The engine does its own lookups when a
   * request runs, and a question's directory choices come from the runtime's choices call.
   */
  membersOf(group: DirectoryRef): Promise<DirectoryEntry[]>;
}

/**
 * Proves the fixtures conform to AuthoredWorkflow.
 *
 * Layout (paths relative to contract/):
 *   authored-format.ts              the types
 *   fixtures/src/<name>.authored.ts the typed sources of the fixtures
 *   fixtures/<name>.authored.json   plain JSON, emitted from the sources (what the engine reads)
 *   check/                          this script and its package
 *
 * How: each source exports an object typed `AuthoredWorkflow`, so tsc type-checks it fully (an
 * imported .json would widen every string literal to `string` and could not be checked against
 * the unions). This script then checks each .json is byte-for-byte what its source produces, so
 * the JSON conforms too; that IDs are unique, follow the ID rule (pattern, no "__", known prefix)
 * and no reference points at a missing ID; and that fixtures/records.json (the stand-in for the
 * server's workflow records: name, description, "Stuck requests go to") has the right shape.
 *
 * Run inside contract/check:
 *   npm run check    type check only
 *   npm run verify   type check, then compare the JSON and check IDs and references
 *   npm run emit     type check, then rewrite the JSON from the sources
 */
// Minimal Node declarations, so the only devDependency is typescript.
declare const require: (m: string) => any;
declare const __dirname: string;
declare const process: { argv: string[]; exit(code: number): never };
declare const console: { log(s: string): void; error(s: string): void };
const fs = require("fs");
const path = require("path");

import { ID_PATTERN, ITEM_KINDS } from "../authored-format";
import type { Arrow, AuthoredWorkflow, Location, SampleRequest } from "../authored-format";
import { changeRequest } from "../fixtures/src/change-request.authored";
import { blank } from "../fixtures/src/blank.authored";
import { severalAtOnce } from "../fixtures/src/several-at-once.authored";
import { integratedSample } from "../fixtures/src/integrated-sample.authored";

const fixtures: Record<string, AuthoredWorkflow> = {
  "change-request.authored.json": changeRequest,
  "blank.authored.json": blank,
  "several-at-once.authored.json": severalAtOnce,
  "integrated-sample.authored.json": integratedSample,
};

// Small typed examples used in authored-format.md, checked here so the doc cannot drift.
export const docExamples: Arrow[] = [
  {
    // "When Approve is pressed and Risk is High go to Security review" (above the plain Approve arrow)
    id: "ar_da_approve_high_risk",
    when: { type: "buttonPressed", button: "btn_da_approve" },
    onlyWhen: { allOf: [{ left: { value: "v_risk" }, words: "choice.is", right: { choice: "ch_risk_high" } }] },
    goTo: "st_security_review",
  },
  {
    // The formula demo, labelled "Release is less than 3 days away"
    id: "ar_rf_rush",
    when: {
      type: "condition",
      condition: {
        formula: "{{v_planned_release_date}} < {{request.startedOn}} + days(3)",
        readsAs: "Planned release date is less than 3 days after the request was started",
      },
    },
    goTo: "st_domain_approval",
    words: "Release is less than 3 days away",
  },
  // An unfinished arrow: legal in a draft, an amber To do.
  { id: "ar_new", when: { type: "buttonPressed", button: "btn_rf_submit" }, goTo: null },
];

// Every question kind has a sample constant (multiple choice and several people included).
export const sampleConstants: SampleRequest["answers"] = {
  v_tags: { choices: ["ch_tag_security", "ch_tag_infra"] },
  v_reviewers: { people: [{ directoryId: "dir-user-mei-tanaka", name: "Mei Tanaka" }, { directoryId: "dir-user-diego-santos", name: "Diego Santos" }] },
  v_team: { group: { directoryId: "dir-group-payments-engineering", name: "Payments engineering" } },
  v_estimate: { number: 3 },
};

// Locations as findings would give them.
export const sampleLocations: Location[] = [
  { item: "wf_change_request" },
  { item: "tk_development", part: "whoIsAsked" },
  { item: "act_create_jira_issue", part: "inputs.summary" },
  { item: "act_notify_requester_rejected", part: "onlyWhen.0" },
];

// Anything that looks like an item ID: a known prefix, then "_". Used to find references.
const ID = new RegExp(`^(${Object.keys(ITEM_KINDS).join("|")})_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`);
const ID_RULE = new RegExp(ID_PATTERN);

/** The ID rule: the pattern, no "__", a known prefix. */
function idRuleProblems(name: string, id: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  if (!ID_RULE.test(id)) out.push(`${name}: id ${id} does not match ${ID_PATTERN}`);
  if (id.includes("__")) out.push(`${name}: id ${id} contains "__" (reserved for the compiler)`);
  if (!(id.split("_")[0] in ITEM_KINDS)) out.push(`${name}: id ${id} has no known prefix`);
  return out;
}

/** fixtures/records.json: the stand-in for the server's workflow records. Shape check only. */
function checkRecords(dir: string, names: string[]): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const file = path.join(dir, "records.json");
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return ["records.json: missing"];
  const records = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
  for (const n of names) {
    const r = records[n];
    if (!r) { out.push(`records.json: no record for ${n}`); continue; }
    if (typeof r.name !== "string" || !r.name) out.push(`records.json: ${n}.name must be a non-empty string`);
    if (r.description !== undefined && typeof r.description !== "string") out.push(`records.json: ${n}.description must be a string`);
    if (!Array.isArray(r.stuckRequestsGoTo)) out.push(`records.json: ${n}.stuckRequestsGoTo must be a list`);
    else for (const p of r.stuckRequestsGoTo)
      if (!p || (p.type !== "user" && p.type !== "group") || typeof p.id !== "string" || typeof p.label !== "string")
        out.push(`records.json: ${n}.stuckRequestsGoTo entries are { type: "user" | "group", id, label }`);
  }
  for (const k of Object.keys(records)) if (!names.includes(k)) out.push(`records.json: ${k} is not a fixture`);
  return out;
}

function checkReferences(name: string, wf: AuthoredWorkflow): string[] {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const defined = new Set<string>();
  const referenced = new Set<string>();
  const walk = (x: unknown, key?: string): void => {
    if (Array.isArray(x)) return x.forEach((y) => walk(y));
    if (x && typeof x === "object") {
      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(x)) {
        if (ID.test(k)) referenced.add(k); // Record keys (cells, answers, positions)
        if (k === "id" && typeof v === "string") {
          if (defined.has(v)) problems.push(`${name}: duplicate id ${v}`);
          problems.push(...idRuleProblems(name, v));
          defined.add(v);
        } else walk(v, k);
      }
      return;
    }
    if (typeof x === "string") {
      if (ID.test(x) && key !== "directoryId") referenced.add(x);
      for (const m of x.matchAll(/\{\{(v_[a-z0-9_]+)\}\}/g)) referenced.add(m[1]); // formula chips
    }
  };
  walk(wf);
  for (const r of referenced) if (!defined.has(r)) problems.push(`${name}: reference to unknown id ${r}`);
  return problems;
}

function main(): void {
  // Compiled to check/build/check/check.js; the JSON lives in contract/fixtures.
  const dir = path.resolve(__dirname, "..", "..", "..", "fixtures");
  const write = process.argv.includes("--write");
  const problems: string[] = [];
  for (const [file, wf] of Object.entries(fixtures)) {
    const json = JSON.stringify(wf, null, 2) + "\n";
    const target = path.join(dir, file);
    if (write) fs.writeFileSync(target, json, "utf8");
    else if (!fs.existsSync(target) || fs.readFileSync(target, "utf8") !== json) problems.push(`${file}: differs from its .ts source (run npm run emit)`);
    problems.push(...checkReferences(file, wf));
  }
  problems.push(...checkRecords(dir, Object.keys(fixtures).map((f) => f.replace(".authored.json", ""))));
  if (problems.length) {
    console.error(problems.join("\n"));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log(`${write ? "Wrote" : "Verified"} ${Object.keys(fixtures).length} fixtures: types conform, JSON matches, ids unique and follow the ID rule, no dangling references, records.json well formed.`);
}

main();
