# Contract part B1: the core package API

Draft 3, engine owner, 2026-11-15. Replaces Draft 2. Pending the frontend owner's review and the product owner's review.
Revised 2026-11-15 after E-21 to E-26, and 2026-11-16 after E-27 (the shapes as built), E-28, E-29, E-31 and E-32.

What the frontend calls in the browser from `engine/packages/core` (E-3, E-4), and the types that all three contract files share. The server runs the same functions at save, at publish and when a request runs. Written against kernel spec v2.20, whose copy is in `engine/spec/`, and against the final formats in `engine/design/definition-format.md` and `engine/design/event-payloads.md`, decisions E-1 to E-33 (`docs/11-decisions-engine.md`), the authored format version 0 (`authored-format.ts`) and the catalogue (`catalogue.ts`). `authoring-api.md` and `runtime-api.md` use the types defined here and define none of their own shared types. What changed in Drafts 2 and 3, and what the engine asks of the frontend: `CHANGES-draft2.md`.

Kernel terms (wait, outcome, transition, Set, activation, `decide`, `evolve`) appear only where this file says how a shape is built from history. None reaches a screen (E-7).

## 1. Rules

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Every function is synchronous, pure and deterministic: no I/O, no clock, no randomness. Every argument and every result is plain data. | One answer in the editor, in Try it and live (E-3). The frontend wraps core in its async interface and may run it in a Web Worker. |
| Nothing returns prose. A problem is a code, a `Location` in the authored format, and params (E-7). Text passed through: the author's `messageWhileDisabled` on a `check` refusal; the author's own words inside a rendered message; and, only to the people who look after stuck requests, engineers' text under one `admin` field (section 8) and the other system's failure text. | The frontend owns every sentence. |
| `params` is always present; `{}` when a code has none. | Frontend choice 3. |
| Every list of codes is open. A minor core version may add a code; a code's params never change meaning. | |
| Every function accepts an unfinished draft and never throws on one. Whether a value is an authored document at all is `parse`'s job. | Authors check and try drafts long before they are finished. |
| No result names a compiled element. Locations point into the authored workflow. | E-7. The origin map (section 12) translates. |
| Findings, facts and changes are in document order of their item, then by code. | Stable lists; tests can compare them. |
| No result holds `null`. An optional field with no value is omitted. Exceptions: an authored document returned whole (`parse`, `Draft.authored`) keeps the nulls the authored format allows (`Arrow.goTo`, `ArrowWhen.button`); the catalogue (`catalogue.ts`) and the inbound answer to other systems (`runtime-api.md` section 8) follow `engine/spec/integrations.md`, where `null` is written out. | Spec section 2: values are present or absent. A draft may be unfinished. |
| Target: `check` and `facts` on a 30-stage workflow under 50 ms in a current browser. | Runs on every edit. A target, not a guarantee; nothing has been measured. |

Order of delivery (E-15): `parse`; `check`, `facts`, `valuesInScope`; `formState`, `evaluate`, `evaluateSent`, `checkFormula`; `compile`; the test host and the story; `diff`.

### 1.1 How codes are spelled (E-17, E-20)

This is the one statement of the rule; the other contract files follow it.

| What | Spelling | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| A code that is recorded (history, the attempts log, log lines) or sent to an outside system | kebab-case | refusal and error codes (`not-found`, `choice-unknown`, `membership-unavailable`), `InvalidDataRule`, `ExpressionErrorKind`, stuck reasons (`action-failed`, `nobody-to-ask`), operation failure codes (`project-not-found`), log line kinds (`start-refused`, `call-outcome-unknown`) |
| A type discriminator that is recorded or sent | lowerCamelCase | `kind: "dataSource"`, `sort: "await"`, `by.type: "connection"`, `result: "notMatched"`, `BuiltInTold` |
| A code that passes only between core, the server and the frontend | the frontend's spelling | finding codes and their reasons (`item.partMissing`, `earlierArrowAlwaysFits`), parse problem codes, story entry codes (`task.opened`), change codes, built-in message codes (the keys of `contract/words/notifications.json`: `task.assigned`, `request.stuck`, `start.refused`, and `alert.<reason>` with the alert reason in kebab-case), `wait-not-open`'s `state` (`requestClosed`), `OpenAction.admin.state` (`inFlight`) |

## 2. Shared types

### 2.1 Imported from the other contract files

```ts
import type {
  AuthoredWorkflow, Location, ItemKind, ValueKind, Words, Expression, Template, Condition,
  SentExpression, SentTemplate, SentCondition, SampleRequest, CatalogueRef, Status,
  StageId, StatusId, TaskId, QuestionId, ButtonId, ActionId, ArrowId, ValueId, ListId, RowId,
  ColumnId, ChoiceId, StartsWhenId, ToldId,
} from "./authored-format";
import type { Catalogue, DirectoryRef } from "./catalogue";
```

`Location` is the authored format's `{ item, part? }`. No other location shape exists anywhere in the contract. `DirectoryRef` in this file is the catalogue's `{ type, id }`, not the authored format's `{ directoryId, name }` of the same name. At the package root the two are told apart by name (section 14): `DirectoryRef` is the authored format's and `CatalogueDirectoryRef` the catalogue's; this file's `Ref` is the catalogue's.

### 2.2 Basic types

```ts
type Json = string | number | boolean | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };   // never null
type Timestamp = string;        // RFC 3339, UTC, milliseconds: "2026-11-15T09:30:00.000Z"
type ItemId = string;           // any authored item ID: at most 40 characters, no "__" (E-23; section 3)
type Ref = DirectoryRef;        // { type: "user" | "group"; id }: id is the directory's immutable object ID
interface By { type: "user" | "connection" | "system"; id: string }   // who did something (E-17)
type ServerWorkflowId = string; // opaque, server-generated; not the document's own wf_ ID
type VersionNumber = number;    // a published version: 1, 2, ...
type RequestId = string;        // opaque to the page; matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ (E-23)
type ReadableId = string;       // decimal digits; display format: unknown: depends on the existing application
type TaskInstanceId = string;   // one instance of a task in one request: `t<seq>`, the seq of its WaitOpened; not the authored tk_ ID
type CallRef = string;          // Try it only: one call an action made: `<requestId>.c<seq>`, the seq of its WaitOpened
type Seq = number;              // position of an event in its request; a page's lastSeq detects a stale page
type OperationSort = "read" | "write" | "await";   // catalogue.ts Operation.sort
type Answers = Partial<Record<QuestionId, Json>>;  // section 2.4
type Values = Partial<Record<ValueId, Json>>;      // section 2.4; author values only (v_ keys)
interface ConnectionChoice { stored: string | number; label: string }   // the value of a choiceFromConnection

/** One choice offered for a question whose choices come from the directory or a data source (section 7.1). */
interface ChoiceOption {
  value: Json;      // exactly what the page sends as the answer: { stored, label } from a source, { type: "user", id } from the directory
  label: string;    // what the person sees; for a person, the directory's display name
}

interface Caller { user: string; platformAdmin: boolean }   // supplied by the host on every server call
```

- `By.id`: for `user`, the directory object ID; for `connection`, the connection ID; for `system`, `engine` or `platform`. Connection IDs `engine`, `system` and `platform` are reserved (E-17).
- `TaskInstanceId` and `CallRef` have these forms in Try it and on the server alike (E-27), so both hand out the same IDs. A page treats them as opaque.
- `Caller.user` is the signed-in person's directory object ID. How the host signs people in and checks the platform-admin entitlement: unknown: depends on the existing application.

### 2.3 Locations

`part` is the path from the item's own object to the field: field names and array indices joined by dots, never entering another item (an object with its own `id`). A clause in a sentence is its index (`onlyWhen.2`) and may continue into the clause (`onlyWhen.2.right`). A piece of a template is its index (`message.1`). A formula is reported at the part that holds the `Formula` object (`onlyWhen`, `choices.formula`, `inputs.summary`); a `FormulaRange` is into that object's `formula` text, and its sentence is `<part>.readsAs`. A key chosen by the catalogue or by the form is a segment (`inputs.summary`, `saveResults.key`, `answers.q_summary`, `values.ticket`).

The parts that findings, refusals, stuck states and story entries report, for authored format version 0. This list is complete for them; the frontend's word tables may key on it. `diff` is the exception: its `part.changed` may name any field of an item by the same path rule, including fields not listed here (`look`, `colour`, `words` on an arrow, `title`, `ifStageEntersAgain`) (section 11). The engine asks that this list replace the examples in `authored-format.ts` and `.md` (`CHANGES-draft2.md`, Asks to the frontend).

| Item | Parts reported |
|---|---|
| workflow (`wf_`) | `start.stage` |
| stage (`st_`) | `name`, `status`, `ifSentBackStatus`, `tasks`, `arrows`. Where a request is: `whenThisStageStarts`, `tasks`, `afterTheyRespond`, `arrows` |
| status (`stat_`) | `words` |
| task (`tk_`) | `whoIsAsked` (and deeper, e.g. `whoIsAsked.ifEmptyUse`), `requesterCanAnswer`, `buttons`, `savesButtonPressedAs`, `savesAnsweredByAs` |
| page (`pg_`) | `showWhen` |
| question (`q_`) | `label`, `savedAs`, `choices`, `choices.list`, `choices.shownColumn`, `choices.peopleIn`, `choices.source`, `choices.inputs`, `choices.inputs.<field>`, `choices.labelField`, `choices.storedField`, `choices.formula`, `showWhen` |
| text (`tx_`) | `content`, `showWhen` |
| button (`btn_`) | `label`, `neededToPress`, `enabledWhen` |
| action (`act_`) | `onlyWhen`. Save a value: `save`, `as`. Notify: `to`, `message`. Use a connection: `operation`, `inputs`, `inputs.<field>`, `saveResults.<field>`, `ifItFails`, `saveFailureAs.failed`, `saveFailureAs.code`. Tell other systems: `tell`, `values.<key>` |
| arrow (`ar_`) | `when`, `when.button`, `when.condition`, `onlyWhen`, `goTo`, `goAsSoonAsTrue` |
| list (`ls_`) | `rows` (E-27: a list with no rows that a question takes its choices from) |
| value (`v_`), choice (`ch_`), column (`col_`) | none: the item as a whole |
| row (`row_`) | `cells.<column>` |
| startsWhen (`sw_`) | `trigger`, `onlyWhen`, `button`, `requester`, `answers`, `answers.<question>` |
| thingTold (`told_`) | `words` |

### 2.4 Values and answers as JSON

A value is recorded in history in this form and kept for ever (`WaitCompleted.data`, `DataSet`, `RequestStarted.input.data`), so this table is fixed now. `Values`, `Answers`, `evaluate` results, story params, outbox entries, the values of `request.told@1` and the catalogue's samples all use it.

| Value kind | JSON | Authored constant | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text`, `longText` | string | `{ text }` | |
| `number` | number | `{ number }` | Always a CEL double (E-18), even `3`: the published definition's `types` block declares it, and `decide` reads JSON by it (E-23). An integer must lie within ±(2^53 − 1). |
| `yesNo` | boolean | `{ yesNo }` | |
| `date` | string `YYYY-MM-DD` | `{ date }` | A formula reads a date chip as a point in time: that date at 00:00 UTC (E-26, section 6.4). |
| `choice` | string: the `ChoiceId` | `{ choice }` | A task's "Button pressed" value is the `ButtonId` (`{ button }`). A value an action saves its failure code as (`saveFailureAs.code`) is the failure code (`{ failureCode }`); its choices are the operation's failure codes and their labels the catalogue's (E-29). |
| `multipleChoice` | array of `ChoiceId`, no duplicates, in the question's choice order | `{ choices }` | |
| `choiceFromList` | string: the `RowId` | `{ row }` | Cells are read from the list of the request's own version. |
| `choiceFromConnection` | `{ "stored": string or number, "label": string }` | `{ connectionChoice }` | `label` is the source's label, recorded when the person acted (E-17). Conditions compare `stored`. |
| `person` | `{ "type": "user", "id": string }` | `{ person }` | `id` is the authored `DirectoryRef.directoryId`. Names come from `directory.lookup`. A choice question whose choices are the people in a group gives a value of this kind (E-26). |
| `group` | `{ "type": "group", "id": string }` | `{ group }` | |
| `people` | array of `{ "type": "user", "id" }`, no duplicates | `{ people }` | |
| `list` | array; each item per the catalogue field's `itemKind` or `fields` | none | |
| `fieldGroup` | object keyed by catalogue field id | none | |

- **A person or group is always `{ type, id }`** (E-20): in data, answers, story params, outbox entries, `told` values, sent fields after the connector has read them, and catalogue samples. Never a bare ID string.
- **Empty is absent.** An empty answer or value is a missing key, never `""`, `[]` or `null`. A page sends no key for an empty question; `""` and `[]` are refused with `invalid-data` / `too-short`.
- **An empty value in a "when" clause** (a sentence clause of a condition) makes the clause not true, except "is empty" and the negative words (is not, does not contain, is not one of, is not in, do not include, does not include), which are true (E-22). In a list comparison (is one of, is not one of, includes any of, includes all of), an item of the list that is empty is ignored (E-24). It is never an error. A message (a Notify, a template) shows an empty value as nothing. A formula reads an empty value as absent: a plain read of it is the expression error `absent-value`, so a formula guards it with optional syntax or "If empty, use".
- **Requester** is a `person` value (absent when a system started the request and its binding names nobody, E-16). **Started on** is a `date`: the UTC date of the start.
- **A saved failure code** (E-29) is a `choice`: the request holds the code, a "when" compares by code (`{ failureCode }`), and "Tell other systems" sends the code. A message (a Notify part, given as text) and a text template sent to another system show the catalogue's label, which publish writes into the definition; a code with no label shows as the code. When two actions save their failure code as one value, its choices are the codes of both, and where one code has two labels the first action in document order gives it. A view or story shows the value as any choice value: the code.
- A weekday constant (`{ weekday }`) is only the right side of `date.isOnWeekday`; it is never a value.
- `Values` holds only author values (`v_` keys). Every other top-level data key belongs to the compiler (E-17) and is never returned.

```ts
/** The sample request's constants converted by the table above. A value whose kind is not known yet is left out. */
function sampleValues(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, sample: SampleRequest, catalogue?: Catalogue): SampleValues;
interface SampleValues { values: Values; requester?: Ref; startedOn?: string }
```

The catalogue gives the kind of a value saved from an operation's result (E-27). Without it, such a value has no known kind and is left out.

### 2.5 Coded records

```ts
/** One member per known code; `params` typed per code. */
type Coded<ParamsByCode, Base> =
  { [C in keyof ParamsByCode & string]: Base & { code: C; params: ParamsByCode[C] } }[keyof ParamsByCode & string];
```

The frontend's client adds its own member for a code it does not know (frontend choice 4). The engine sends codes as listed here and nothing else.

### 2.6 Results, errors and refusals

```ts
/** Every server call (authoring and runtime). `errors` is never empty; all entries come from one step. */
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: ApiError[] };

/** Every turn of a Try it request. `refusals` is never empty. */
type TurnResult<T extends object = {}> = ({ ok: true } & T) | { ok: false; refusals: Refusal[] };

interface ApiErrorBase {
  location?: Location;      // where in the authored workflow, when the problem is in it
  message?: string;         // only with `check`: the button's messageWhileDisabled, the author's own text
}
type ApiError = Coded<ApiErrorParams, ApiErrorBase>;
type Refusal = ApiError;    // one shape for Try it and the pages
```

`ApiErrorParams` maps each code to its params as in the table below. A code with no params has `params: {}`; in TypeScript that empty object may be typed either `{}` or `Record<string, never>` (core writes the second), and both mean exactly `{}`. Over HTTP a failure is `{ "errors": ApiError[] }` with the status below. A `503` is safe to repeat: nothing was written; `Retry-After: 2` is set. The inbound endpoint for other systems has its own bodies and codes (`runtime-api.md` section 8).

"Attempt" means a refusal of a start, an act or an admin turn that the engine writes to the attempts log (spec section 2). A "try again" refusal is never an attempt.

| Code | HTTP | Location | Params | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | | `{}` | No signed-in caller. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | | `{ need: "author" \| "devHost" }` | Not an author of this workflow (`authoring-api.md` section 2); `devHost`: switching person outside the development host. |
| `not-found` | 404 | | `{ what: "workflow" \| "version" \| "request" \| "task" \| "binding" \| "question" \| "refusedStart" \| "call" \| "path" }` | `what` names what was not found (E-28). `path`: the server, a path or method neither API has (E-31). `task`: also an act on a task the request never opened, or on an action's call (the kernel's `unknown-wait`). `call`: Try it only, a call `answerCall` does not hold or that is no longer pending (section 10.2). `refusedStart`: also a refused start whose sent body is no longer kept (`runtime-api.md` section 5.4). |
| `invalid-body` | 400 | | `{ field: string; problem: "missing" \| "type" \| "unknownField" \| "empty" \| "tooLong" \| "format" }` | The call does not have the documented shape. `field` is a JSON Pointer into the body, or for a query string the parameter's name (`status`, `cursor`). |
| `too-large` | 413 | | `{ limit: number }` | Body or draft over the limit, in bytes. |
| `busy` | 503 | | `{}` | The request's lock was not obtained in 5 s. |
| `internal` | 500 | | `{}` | Anything else. Detail in the server log only. |
| `invalid-document` | 422 | | `{ problems: ParseProblem[] }` | A saved draft fails `parse` (section 3). |
| `authored-format-unsupported` | 422 | | `{ version: number; min: number; max: number }` | |
| `stale-revision` | 409 | | `{ currentRevision: number; draft: Draft }` | `Draft`: `authoring-api.md` section 3; core exports it at the root (section 14, E-32). |
| `core-version-mismatch` | 409 | | `{ serverCoreVersion: string; serverFormatVersion: number }` | |
| `has-todo` | 422 | | `{ findings: Finding[] }` | Publish refused; the server's findings as `compile` gives them, To dos and Worth knowing (E-31). |
| `last-author` | 409 | | `{}` | Settings would leave no author. |
| `client-token-reused` | 409 | | `{ requestId: RequestId }` | Same start token, other arguments. |
| `unknown-button` | 422 | the task | `{ button: ButtonId }` | Not a button of this task in the request's version. |
| `wait-not-open` | 409 | the task | `{ state: "completed" \| "cancelled" \| "skipped" \| "requestClosed"; by?: By; button?: ButtonId }` | Kernel reason 1. A completed task is `completed` with `by` and `button`, also after the request closed (E-27); `requestClosed` is for any other task once the request is closed; `cancelled` and `skipped` for a task the request moved past while it is open. Mapped from the kernel's params (spec v2.19 section 2, E-28): `{state: "completed", by, outcome}` gives `completed` with `by` and `button` = `outcome`; `{state: "requestClosed"}` and `{state: "cancelled" \| "skipped"}` pass through. An attempt. |
| `membership-unavailable` | 503 | | `{}` | The directory could not be asked for the caller's groups (an act, an admin turn, an author check), or a directory read failed (`runtime-api.md` section 7). Try again; nothing changed; not an attempt (E-17). The lookup is made before the request is locked, after the unlocked check that the task is open, so an act on a task that is no longer open is answered `wait-not-open` instead (E-23). |
| `not-assignee` | 403 | the task, part `whoIsAsked` | `{}` | Kernel reason 2. An attempt. |
| `may` | 403 | the task, part `requesterCanAnswer` | `{}` | Kernel reason 3. An attempt. |
| `invalid-data` | 422 | the question; part `choices` with `not-a-choice`, `showWhen` with `hidden-answered`; the task when no question applies | `{ rule: InvalidDataRule }` | Kernel reason 4, and the question rules the compiler enforces as checks (section 7.2). An attempt. |
| `source-unavailable` | 503 | the question, part `choices` | `{}` | The data source could not be asked (the choices call, or the lookup when the person acts). Directory choices count: they are read through the directory connection's group-members source (E-20). Try again; nothing changed; not an attempt (E-17). |
| `choice-unknown` | 422 | the question, part `choices` | `{}` | An answer to a question whose choices come from the directory or a data source is not among them when the person acts: the source has no item with that stored value, or the person is not in the group now (E-20). An attempt. |
| `check` | 422 | the button, part `enabledWhen` | `{ button: ButtonId }` | Kernel reason 5: "Also only when" is not true. `message` is the button's `messageWhileDisabled` when set. An attempt. |
| `rule-error` | 422 | the item and part whose expression errored | `{ error: ExpressionErrorKind }` | A condition of the form could not be worked out. A CEL error is never false (spec section 3). An attempt. |
| `mapping-error` | 422 | the binding and part (`onlyWhen`, `requester`, `answers.<question>`) | `{ error: ExpressionErrorKind }` | A "Starts when" mapping could not be worked out; no request starts (E-17). |
| `unfinished` | none (Try it only) | the binding; the start task | `{}` | `startFrom` on a binding, or `start` when the start task, has a To do that stops a request from running (section 10.2). |
| `not-admin` | 403 | | `{}` | Not among "Stuck requests go to" nor a platform admin. An attempt. |
| `reason-required` | 422 | | `{}` | An attempt. |
| `stale` | 409 | | `{ lastSeq: Seq }` | The request moved since the page was read. |
| `request-closed` | 409 | | `{}` | Retry or close on a closed request. An attempt. |
| `not-stuck` | 409 | | `{}` | Retry on a request that is not stuck (E-20). An attempt. |
| `not-retryable` | 409 | | `{ reason: StuckReason }` | Retry on a request stuck with `nothing-fits` or `error` (or `unfinished` in Try it): only Close is offered for these (E-23). An attempt. |
| `requires-not-met` | 422 | the stage | `{ values: ValueId[] }` | Nothing in the first build produces it (E-33). |

```ts
type InvalidDataRule =
  | "required"          // a needed question is empty (unconditionally or by its Show when)
  | "wrong-kind" | "not-a-choice" | "too-long" | "too-short" | "out-of-range" | "bad-format"
  | "unknown-question"  // an answer for a question the form does not have; a field inside an answer that its schema does not have is wrong-kind
  | "hidden-answered";  // an answer for a question that is hidden with these answers
type ExpressionErrorKind =
  | "no-such-key" | "index-out-of-range" | "absent-value" | "wrong-kind" | "division-by-zero" | "overflow" | "other";
```

`not-a-choice` covers a typed-in choice or a list row that is not in the question's choices: the document holds them, so the outcome's schema refuses it. A choice from the directory or a data source that is not found is `choice-unknown`, which needs a live lookup (E-20).

## 3. `parse`

```ts
function parse(doc: unknown): ParseResult;

type ParseResult =
  | { ok: true; workflow: AuthoredWorkflow }
  | { ok: false; problems: ParseProblem[] };

type ParseProblem = Coded<ParseProblemParams, { location: Location }>;
interface ParseProblemParams {
  "parse.notAnObject":        { pointer: string };
  "parse.missingField":       { pointer: string; field: string };
  "parse.unknownField":       { pointer: string; field: string };
  "parse.wrongType":          { pointer: string; expected: string };   // "string", "array", "object", "number", "boolean"
  "parse.notAllowed":         { pointer: string; allowed: string[] };  // a closed word (kind, look, words, colour ...)
  "parse.badId":              { pointer: string; id: string };         // fails ID_PATTERN (at most 40 characters, E-23) or contains "__"
  "parse.wrongPrefix":        { pointer: string; id: string; expected: string };  // an ITEM_KINDS prefix
  "parse.duplicateId":        { pointer: string; id: string; other: string };     // `other`: pointer to the first
  "parse.unsupportedVersion": { pointer: string; version: number; min: number; max: number };
  "parse.badFormat":          { pointer: string; format: "catalogueRef" | "date" | "directoryId" | "failureCode" };   // E-26, E-27, E-29
}
```

- Checks the document against `authored-format.ts`: shapes, closed words, `ID_PATTERN`, no `__`, prefixes, unique IDs, `formatVersion`. `parse.badFormat` (E-26, E-27):
  - `format: "catalogueRef"`: a `CatalogueRef` that does not match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}@[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$`, which is `<connection>.<name>@<version>` with each part's rule from `catalogue.ts` (`CatalogueId`).
  - `format: "date"`: a date constant or a sample's `startedOn` that is not `YYYY-MM-DD` naming a real calendar day in the years 0001 to 9999 (`2026-02-29` and `0000-01-01` are refused).
  - `format: "directoryId"`: a person or group constant whose `directoryId` is not in the directory ID's form: 1 to 255 characters, none of them white space or a control character (`definition-format.md` section 6, `directory-object-id`). Every such constant counts, wherever it is written (a list cell, a clause, "Who is asked", Notify's "to", an input, a sample answer) and each person of a `people` constant (as built). An empty ID in a list cell is not a problem: it is a cell not given, as the compiler reads it; an empty ID anywhere else is. The sample request's Requester is not a constant and is not checked.
  - `format: "failureCode"`: a failure-code constant (`{ failureCode }`) whose text is not kebab-case, `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, the form of the catalogue's failure codes (E-29).
- **An authored ID is at most 40 characters** (E-23), so every compiled name (`<itemId>__<local>`, the stage prefix, the nobody-to-ask rule ID) fits the 64-character limit. `ID_PATTERN` in `authored-format.ts` is `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$`; a longer ID is `parse.badId`. It does **not** report anything a draft may leave unfinished (absent "(draft: optional)" fields, empty names, references to missing IDs): those are `check`'s.
- `location` is the nearest enclosing item with a valid ID, `part` the path from it; the workflow's `id` when there is none; `{ item: "" }` when the root has no valid `id`. `pointer` is the RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the document.
- The server runs `parse` on every save (`authoring-api.md`, `invalid-document`).

## 4. `check`

```ts
function check(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue): Finding[];

type Finding = Coded<FindingParams, {
  severity: "todo" | "worthKnowing";
  location: Location;
  debug?: { detail: string };   // only on compile.internal: engineers' text for logs, never shown. Never relied on.
}>;
interface FormulaRange { start: number; end: number }   // UTF-16 offsets into the formula text, end exclusive
```

Runs every check the server runs at publish plus the authoring checks below. A workflow may be published when no finding is `todo`. The last column says whether the To do stops a request from running in Try it (section 10.2).

| Code | Sev | Location | Params | Meaning | Stops Try it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item.partMissing` | todo | the item, the missing part | `{}` | A part needed to run is empty. Which parts: below. | Some parts: below |
| `item.brokenReference` | todo | the referring item and part | `{ target: ItemId }` | Refers to an ID that no longer exists (`removedNames` holds its old name). | Yes |
| `workflow.noStart` | todo | the workflow, part `start.stage` | `{}` | `start.stage` names no working stage. | Yes: no host |
| `start.notOneTask` | todo | the start stage, part `tasks` | `{ found: number }` | The start stage must have exactly one task. | Yes: no host |
| `start.needsStatus` | todo | the start stage, part `status` | `{ action: Location }` | E-16: a connection action in the start stage's "After they respond" and no `status`. `action`: the first such action. | No |
| `start.directoryInCondition` | todo | the condition part on the start form (page or question `showWhen`, text `showWhen`, button `enabledWhen`), with clause index | `{}` | A start-form condition uses a `directory` step, or a people word on a group: "is in" or "is not in" a group (E-26). A condition's directory read is a recorded read placed just before the step that uses it (E-23), and the start form is answered in the start turn, before any read can be recorded. | Yes |
| `startsWhen.neededNotFilled` | todo | the binding, part `answers` | `{ button: ButtonId; questions: QuestionId[] }` | E-17, E-20: the binding fills none of these questions, which the button it presses needs, whether or not they have a "Show when". | No: `startFrom` is refused with `invalid-data` / `required`, as live |
| `feature.notInThisBuild` | todo | the item using it | `{ feature: string }` | Reserved. Authored format 0 has nothing the first build leaves out (E-8). | Yes |
| `formula.syntax` | todo | the formula part | `FormulaRange` | Does not parse. | Yes |
| `formula.unknownName` | todo | the formula part | `FormulaRange & { name: string }` | A chip or name that names nothing. A name starting `cel1_` is reported here. | Yes |
| `formula.notInScope` | todo | the formula part | `FormulaRange & { name: string; declaredAt: Location }` | Names something this place cannot see. | Yes |

| `formula.argumentMismatch` | todo | the formula part | `FormulaRange & { function: string; expected: FormulaType[]; found: FormulaType[] }` | No form of the function or operator takes these. | Yes |
| `formula.kindMismatch` | todo | the formula part | `FormulaRange & { expected: ValueKind; found: FormulaType }` | The formula gives the wrong kind for its place. | Yes |
| `expression.kindMismatch` | todo | the slot | `{ expected: ValueKind[]; found: ValueKind }` | A value reference, constant, sentence or sent field gives the wrong kind for its slot: who is asked, notify to, a connection or source input, a binding's requester or answer, a clause's right side (`<part>.<n>.right`), a question's `choices.peopleIn` (E-26). | Yes |
| `clause.wordsDoNotFit` | todo | the clause (`<part>.<n>`) | `{ words: Words; kind: ValueKind }` | The words are not offered for the left side's kind (`WORDS_FOR_KIND`), or `right` does not match `WORDS_WITH_NOTHING_AFTER` / `WORDS_WITH_A_LIST`. | Yes |
| `clause.pressedOutsideStage` | todo | the clause; for an arrow, the arrow, part `when.button` | `{ button: ButtonId }` | "Is pressed" outside the stage that owns the button, or an arrow whose `when.button` is a button of another stage (E-26). An arrow that has this To do anywhere (at `when.button`, or a pressed clause in its `when.condition` or `onlyWhen`) gets no `arrow.neverUsed` beside it (E-27). | Yes |
| `value.kindConflict` | todo | the value | `{ kinds: { kind: ValueKind; at: Location }[] }` | Filled with different kinds in different places. | Yes |
| `value.neverFilled` | todo | the reading item and part | `Partial<FormulaRange> & { value: Location }` | No route fills it before this point. | No: the request meets the empty value as it would live |
| `value.mayBeEmpty` | todo | the reading item and part | `Partial<FormulaRange> & { value: Location; skippedVia: Location[] }` | Some route reaches this point without filling the value, the read has no "If empty, use", and an empty value here would stop or silently drop something (E-22). Raised only for these reads: who is asked (`whoIsAsked`), a notification's recipient (`to`), a directory group (a `members` step, "is in" a group, `choices.peopleIn`), and a needed connection input (`inputs.<field>` or `choices.inputs.<field>` of a required input). Nowhere else: a "when" clause treats an empty value as section 2.4 says, and a message shows it as nothing. `skippedVia`: one such route as stages, arrows and buttons in order. | No |
| `stage.buttonHasNowhereToGo` | todo | the button | `{ task: Location }` | One task: pressing this button fits no arrow. | No: stuck with `nothing-fits` |
| `stage.combinationHasNowhereToGo` | todo | the stage, part `arrows` | `{ combinations: { task: Location; button: Location }[][]; total: number }` | Several tasks: a combination of buttons, one per task, fits no arrow. The first ten; `total` counts all. | No |
| `arrow.otherCasesNotLast` | todo | the arrow, part `when` | `{}` | "In all other cases" is not the stage's last arrow, or there are two (E-18). | Yes |
| `action.failureHasNowhereToGo` | todo | the action, part `ifItFails` | `{ failed?: ValueId; code?: ValueId }` | "If it fails: carry on" and no arrow covers a failure. `failed`, `code`: the values the failure is saved as (A3). | No |
| `action.failureReadButStops` | todo | the reading part | `Partial<FormulaRange> & { action: Location }` | Something reads the action's failure values (a condition, a formula, a message, an input: any read anywhere in the workflow, E-26), but "If it fails" is "stuck", so they are never filled. | No |
| `catalogue.unknownEntry` | todo | the referring part (`operation`, `choices.source`, `trigger`) | `{ entry: CatalogueRef; expected: "operation" \| "dataSource" \| "trigger" }` | Not in the catalogue, or not an entry of that kind. | Yes: a broken reference |
| `catalogue.connectionNotSetUp` | todo | the referring part | `{ connection: string }` | The connection is `notSetUp`. | No: Try it fakes it |
| `catalogue.connectionDisabled` | worthKnowing | the referring part | `{ connection: string }` | The connection is `disabled`: calls wait, choices answer `source-unavailable`, its triggers start nothing, until a start-up with corrected configuration. | No |
| `catalogue.entryDisabled` | worthKnowing | the referring part | `{ entry: CatalogueRef }` | The entry is `disabled` because its shape changed under its ID (E-20): the same effects, for that entry only. | No |
| `catalogue.inputMissing` | todo | the item, part `inputs` or `choices.inputs` | `{ input: string }` | A required input field is not mapped. | No: the outbox shows the input missing |
| `catalogue.unknownField` | todo | `inputs.<field>`, `choices.inputs.<field>`, `saveResults.<field>`, `choices.labelField`, `choices.storedField`; on a binding, `requester`, `answers.<question>` and an `onlyWhen` clause (`onlyWhen.<n>.left`, `onlyWhen.<n>.right`) | `{ field: string }` | The entry has no such field. On a binding: a sent field it reads is not a field of the trigger's event (E-26). | Yes: a broken reference |
| `stage.noWayToEnd` | todo | the stage | `{}` | No route from it reaches an ending. | No |
| `loop.noTask` | todo | the arrow that closes the loop | `{ stages: Location[] }` | A loop passes no task or action opened inside it, so it would spin. | No: stuck with `error` after 50 moves |
| `action.resultSavedTwice` | todo | the action, part `saveResults.<field>` (the later field) | `{ value: ValueId; fields: string[] }` | Two results of one action are saved as the same value (E-23). | Yes |
| `question.choicesNotSupported` | todo | the question, part `choices` | `{ kind: ValueKind; from: "typedIn" \| "list" \| "source" \| "directory" }` | A choice source the compiler has no rule for: a `multipleChoice` or `group` question whose choices come from a data source or the directory; a `person` question with typed-in or list choices (E-23). | Yes |
| `arrow.otherCasesWithCondition` | todo | the arrow, part `onlyWhen` or `goAsSoonAsTrue` | `{}` | "In all other cases" with "+ only when" or "Don't wait for the others" (E-23). | Yes |
| `condition.noClauses` | todo | the condition part (`showWhen`, `enabledWhen`, `onlyWhen`, `when.condition`) | `{}` | A sentence with an empty "and" or "or" list (E-23), including an "only when" that is present with an empty list. Empty never means "always true" (E-25). An arrow's `when.condition` with no clauses stays `item.partMissing`. | Yes |
| `reference.stepsNotSupported` | todo | the part that holds the reference | `{ request: "requester" \| "startedOn" }` | Steps after "Requester" or "Started on" (E-23). | Yes |
| `template.kindNotJoinable` | todo | the template part (`inputs.<field>`, `values.<key>`, `answers.<question>`) with the piece index | `{ kind: ValueKind }` | A value of kind `multipleChoice`, `people`, `list` or `fieldGroup` inside a text template for a connection input, a Tell value or a binding answer: the compiler has no rule yet for rendering it as text, that is how each item renders and what separates them (E-23). | Yes |
| `startsWhen.showWhenReadsStartedOn` | todo | the binding, part `answers.<question>` | `{ question: QuestionId }` | The binding maps a question whose "Show when" reads "Started on", which the mapping cannot work out before the start (E-23). | For `startFrom` on that binding only: refused `unfinished`. `start` is not blocked |
| `group.readInSameStep` | todo | the reading part, with the clause index where it is a condition | `{ value: Location }` (the group value) | A `directory` step or an "is in" a group test over a group that the same tasks step fills, in that step's own Show when, "Also only when", lookup input, or early arrow ("Don't wait for the others"). The compiler has no rule for it (`compiler.md` 8.6, 14.3 item 9; E-26). Three limits (E-27): a question's "people in" group (`choices.peopleIn`) is not such a read, because it names the group and needs no recorded read; formulas are not judged; on the start form, Show when and "Also only when" are left to `start.directoryInCondition`, and only lookup inputs are reported here. | Yes |
| `startsWhen.buttonNotOnStart` | todo | the binding, part `button` | `{ button: ButtonId }` | The binding presses a button that is not a button of the start task (E-26). | For `startFrom` on that binding only: refused `unfinished` |
| `arrow.neverUsed` | todo | the arrow | `{ reason: "earlierArrowAlwaysFits" \| "conditionNeverTrue"; earlier?: Location; covering?: Location[] }` | Provably never used (E-25). With `earlierArrowAlwaysFits`, `covering` names every earlier arrow that is taken instead in some case (for each case, the first earlier arrow that surely fits it), in document order; together they cover the arrow (E-32). `earlier` is given only when one earlier arrow alone always fits. Neither is given with `conditionNeverTrue`. Raised only where that is provable: no finding does not mean usable. Not raised for an arrow whose `when` is not chosen yet (that arrow has `item.partMissing`), for an arrow out of an unreachable stage (`stage.unreachable` covers it), nor for an arrow that has `clause.pressedOutsideStage` anywhere: at `when.button`, or on a clause of its `when.condition` or `onlyWhen` (E-27). | No |
| `compile.internal` | todo | the workflow | `{}` | A bug in core. `debug.detail` is for logs, never shown. | Yes: no host |
| `stage.unreachable` | worthKnowing | the stage | `{}` | No route from the start reaches it. | No |
| `task.askedMayBeEmpty` | worthKnowing | the task, part `whoIsAsked` | `{ reason: "valueMayBeEmpty" \| "listMayBeEmpty"; value?: Location }` | Who is asked reads a list's cell through a column step, and a row that can reach the task leaves that cell "(not given)" (`listMayBeEmpty`; `value`: the value holding the row). A cell whose person or group has an empty `directoryId` is a cell not given (section 3). Raised only for that case (E-26), and only for the last link of an "If empty, use" chain that is read. The request would then be stuck with `nobody-to-ask` and the people who look after stuck requests are told. A group that may hold nobody is not reported: who is in it is known only at run time. An empty value there is the To do `value.mayBeEmpty` (E-22), so `valueMayBeEmpty` is no longer raised. | No |
| `action.repeatOnRead` | worthKnowing | the action (no part: `ifStageEntersAgain` is not a reported part, section 2.3) | `{}` | "When the stage is entered again" is set on a look-up. A read is made afresh on every entry, so the setting has no effect. | No |
| `requester.mayBeEmpty` | worthKnowing | the part that reads the Requester with no "If empty, use" (`whoIsAsked`, `to`) | `{ bindings: StartsWhenId[] }` | The workflow has bindings whose Requester may be empty, and this task asks, or this notification tells, the Requester. `bindings` lists each binding that names no Requester, and each binding whose Requester comes from something that may be empty (E-27). These sources count: a sent field the event may leave out, that is the field, or a field it sits in when it is a dotted field, is not required; and a formula one of whose sent-field chips may be left out by that rule (a formula is empty when a chip it reads is, `compiler.md` 8.4). A constant never counts. A sent field the trigger does not have is `catalogue.unknownField`'s and is not listed. The start task's `whoIsAsked` counts only when an arrow that can be taken from a reachable stage leads back to the start stage: it matters only when a request is sent back there (E-26, E-27). | No |
| `action.failureNotRead` | worthKnowing | the action, part `ifItFails` | `{ failed?: ValueId; code?: ValueId }` | "If it fails: carry on", and nothing reads the values the failure is saved as, or none is saved (E-27). Any read of either value anywhere in the workflow counts, a stage reached earlier included (it may be reached again on a send-back): an arrow, an "only when", an action, a message, a template or a condition. The request would carry on after a failure that nothing looks at. `failed`, `code`: the values the failure is saved as, when it is. | No |

`item.partMissing` is reported for: stage `name` (empty); task `whoIsAsked` (absent), `buttons` (empty); question `label` (empty), `savedAs` (absent), `choices` (absent on a `choice` or `multipleChoice` question, or typed-in with no choices: no answer could be given, E-32), `choices.source`, `choices.labelField`, `choices.storedField`; button `label`; Save a value `save`, `as`; Notify `to`; Use a connection `operation`; Tell other systems `tell`; arrow `goTo` (null), `when` (not chosen: absent or null), `when.button` (null), `when.condition` (absent or no clauses); a working stage's `arrows` (none); a clause's `left`, `words`, `right` (`<part>.<n>.left` ...); a formula's `readsAs` (empty); binding `trigger`, `button` (absent while the start task has several buttons); status and thing told `words` (empty); list `rows` (none, when a question takes its choices from that list: no answer could be given, E-27).

`choices.list` is not in this list: the format requires it on list choices, so a missing one is `parse.missingField` (E-26). An arrow whose "when" is not chosen yet (`when` absent or null, `when.button` null, or `when.condition` absent or with no clauses) is `item.partMissing`; an "only when" (`onlyWhen`, `showWhen`, `enabledWhen`) that is present with an empty list is `condition.noClauses`. An empty "when" or "only when" is never read as "always true" (E-25).

Template text is empty only when it is the empty string `''`; white space is not empty, as the compiler has it (E-26).

**Constants on the right of a clause.** A clause on a "Button pressed" value takes `button` constants, and a clause on a value an action saves its failure code as takes `failureCode` constants in the same places: one after the words of `WORDS_FOR_KIND.choice`, a list after the words of `WORDS_WITH_A_LIST` (E-29). Both values have the kind `choice`, so a `text` constant there is `expression.kindMismatch` (`expected: ["choice"]`, `found: "text"`), and a `failureCode` or `button` constant on a value of another kind is `expression.kindMismatch` with `found: "choice"`. A `button` constant naming another task's button, and a `failureCode` constant that is not one of the value's codes or is used on a choice value that is not a saved failure code, raise no finding yet: the clause is never true (section 16).

Of these, the ones that stop a request from running in Try it are: task `buttons` (nothing can answer it); Use a connection `operation` (no operation); arrow `goTo`, `when`, `when.button`, `when.condition` and a working stage's empty `arrows` (no destination); Save a value `save` and `as`; a clause's `left`, `words` and `right` (the condition cannot be built); binding `trigger` and `button`. Words and labels never do: stage `name`, question and button `label`, a formula's `readsAs`, status and thing told `words`. Nor do (E-28): task `whoIsAsked` (the request runs to the task, which asks nobody, and is stuck there with `nobody-to-ask`, as a published one would be); question `savedAs` (the answer is not kept); question `choices`, `choices.source`, `choices.labelField` and `choices.storedField`, and list `rows` (the tester sees a question nobody can answer properly: with no choices the answer is taken unchecked against its kind's schema with no lookup, and with typed-in choices that hold none, as with a list with no rows, no answer fits); Notify `to` and Tell other systems `tell` (neither can stop a request). `engine/design/compiler.md` section 13 gives what is compiled for each and says the same.

`action.repeatNotChosen` is withdrawn: the catalogue now writes `onRepeat` for every write and await operation (`catalogue.ts`), so the author always has a default.

The To dos marked E-23 above, and `group.readInSameStep` (E-26), are the constructs the compiler has no rule for (`engine/design/compiler.md`). Two constructs that compiler.md once asked core to report are not findings: a `members` step or "is in" a group over a value saved earlier in the same section, because the read is placed just before the step that uses it (E-23) (a group filled by the same tasks step is the To do `group.readInSameStep`); and a formula giving a timestamp where a date is needed, because the compiler applies `asDate` there (section 6.4).

## 5. `facts` and `valuesInScope`

```ts
function facts(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue): Facts;

interface Facts {
  stages: Partial<Record<StageId, StageFacts>>;
  arrows: Partial<Record<ArrowId, ArrowFacts>>;
  values: Partial<Record<ValueId, ValueFacts>>;
}
interface StageFacts { incoming: ArrowId[]; reachable: boolean }      // incoming in document order
type ArrowFacts =
  | { usable: true; sendsBack: boolean }                               // "not provably never"
  | { usable: false; reason: "earlierArrowAlwaysFits" | "conditionNeverTrue"; earlier?: Location; covering?: Location[]; sendsBack: boolean };   // earlier, covering: as arrow.neverUsed's (section 4)
interface ValueFacts {
  kind?: ValueKind | { conflict: { kind: ValueKind; at: Location }[] };   // absent: nothing that fills it says its kind yet
  filledAt: Location[];
  usedAt: Location[];
}

function valuesInScope(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue, at: Location): ValueInScope[];

interface ValueInScope {
  id: ValueId;
  name: string;
  kind?: ValueKind | { conflict: ValueKind[] };
  filledAt: Location[];
  usedAt: Location[];
  state: "never" | "mayBeEmpty" | "always";   // at `at`
  skippedVia?: Location[];                    // with mayBeEmpty: one route that reaches `at` without filling it
}
```

- `values` lists only the values in the workflow's value registry (E-26). A reference to an ID that is not there is `item.brokenReference`, not a fact.
- `arrows` judges each arrow as if its stage is reached (E-26), so an arrow out of an unreachable stage still has its `usable` and `sendsBack`. `check` reports `stage.unreachable` for the stage and no `arrow.neverUsed` for its arrows, so nothing is reported twice.
- `sendsBack`: the arrow's target is a stage every request must already have passed through to reach the arrow's source (the target dominates the source, E-14). Computed, never stored.
- `filledAt` lists every filler. Within one stage, when two tasks fill the same value, the later task in the document wins, not the later answer in time (E-23): both answers are written by one transition.
- `at` is the moment the located part is evaluated. An arrow's parts read the state before the arrow is taken, after the stage's after-response actions have run (E-22). The exception is an early arrow ("Don't wait for the others", `goAsSoonAsTrue`) taken while tasks are still open: it reads the values as they are after the tasks step, before the after-response actions (E-26). A stage's part reads the state when that section starts; actions in a section see earlier saves of the same section (authored format, rule 5). A question or page reads the state when the form is shown, plus the answers on the same form.
- Requester and Started on are not values; the frontend adds them to the picker itself.
- The catalogue is a parameter because a value filled from an action's result takes its kind from the operation's result fields.
- A value an action saves its failure code as has the kind `choice` (E-29), as a "Button pressed" value has.

## 6. Formulas and expressions

### 6.1 `checkFormula`

```ts
function checkFormula(
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue,
  at: Location,           // the part the formula belongs to: fixes its scope and the kind it must give
  formula: string,        // formula text with chips (authored format, Formula)
  sample?: SampleRequest,
): FormulaResult;

type FormulaResult =
  | { ok: true; kind: ValueKind; sample?: SampleResult }   // sample absent: none given, or it needs a directory lookup
  | { ok: false; error: FormulaError };

type FormulaError = Coded<
  Pick<FindingParams, "formula.syntax" | "formula.unknownName" | "formula.notInScope" | "formula.unknownFunction"
    | "formula.notInProfile" | "formula.argumentMismatch" | "formula.kindMismatch" | "value.neverFilled"
    | "value.mayBeEmpty" | "action.failureReadButStops">,
  FormulaRange>;
```

Checked as if it stood at `at` in place of what is there. Only the first error is returned: the library stops at the first.

How `kind` is read, as built (E-27):

- The formula's type is read as a value kind: text, number, yes/no, or a timestamp as `date` (the compiler applies `asDate`). An optional is read as its value.
- Where the place takes one of several kinds, `kind` is the first that fits.
- A type that is not a value kind (a whole number, a duration, `dyn`) is `formula.kindMismatch`. `expected` is the place's kind; where the place's kind is not known yet, it is `number` for a whole number (write `double()`), `date` for a duration, and `text` otherwise.
- A choices formula (`choices.formula`) must give a list. `kind` is the kind of its items (text, number, yes/no, date); any other type is `formula.kindMismatch` with `expected: "text"`.

### 6.2 `evaluate` (R3)

```ts
function evaluate(
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue,
  at: Location, what: Expression | Template,
  sample: SampleRequest, lookups?: KnownLookups,
): EvaluateResult;

type EvaluateResult =
  | { result: "value"; value: Json; kind?: ValueKind }
  | { result: "absent" }
  | { result: "error"; error: ExpressionErrorKind; params: { key?: string; index?: number } }
  | { result: "needsLookups"; lookups: NeededLookup[] };
type SampleResult = Exclude<EvaluateResult, { result: "needsLookups" }>;

interface NeededLookup { membersOf: Ref }                          // a group whose people are needed
interface KnownLookups { membersOf?: Partial<Record<string, Ref[]>> }   // group id -> its people
```

- Values come from `sampleValues(workflow, sample)`. A `pressed` clause is true when the sample's value for that task's `savesButtonPressedAs` is that button, otherwise false.
- A `Template` evaluates to `{ result: "value", value: MessagePart[] }` (section 10.3), never `absent`.
- A `directory` step or "is in" a group needs the group's people. Core does not read the directory (E-3): it returns `needsLookups`; the caller fetches them and calls again with `lookups`. Names are never resolved by core; the caller uses `directory.lookup` on the refs in the value.
- Same CEL environment as `decide` (E-18). An `error` is what would make a request stuck with reason `error` at that point. A Save a value whose result holds a key starting with `$` is `error` / `wrong-kind` at the `save` part, as the kernel faults that Set (E-27).
- A part the compiler has no rule for (an unfinished clause, an empty "and" or "or" list, a construct of `compiler.md` 14.3), and an expression that does not type-check, give `{ result: "error", error: "other", params: {} }`. Such a workflow cannot run, and `check` names the To do.

### 6.3 `evaluateSent` (a "Starts when" binding)

```ts
function evaluateSent(
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue,
  at: Location,                                         // a part of a binding
  what: SentExpression | SentTemplate | SentCondition,
  sent?: Record<string, Json>,                          // absent: the trigger's catalogue sample event
): SampleResult;
```

A binding reads only what the other system sent, so no lookup is ever needed. A binding with no `trigger` and no `sent` given reads every sent field as absent. A sent field of kind `person` is already a `{ type: "user", id }`: mapping an outside user to the directory is the connector's job (E-16).

### 6.4 The formula functions (profile `cel-1`)

```ts
const FORMULA_FUNCTIONS: readonly FormulaFunction[];
interface FormulaFunction {
  name: string;                                  // "size", "contains", "date", "+" ...
  style: "function" | "method" | "macro" | "operator";   // f(x), x.f(y), x.all(i, ...), a + b
  overloads: { receiver?: FormulaType; args: FormulaType[]; returns: FormulaType }[];
}
type FormulaType =
  | ValueKind                       // as the value's JSON reads in CEL: number is a double, a date chip is a timestamp, person is a map
  | "int"                           // a whole number: what size() gives, and a number literal written without a point
  | "timestamp" | "duration" | "map" | "any"
  | `listOf:${string}` | `optionalOf:${string}`;
```

`FORMULA_FUNCTIONS` is the content below, as data, and is versioned with the definition format: a change is a new profile. The profile's function list is written out and pinned in `engine/design/definition-format.md` section 5 (E-23); where the two differ, that file decides and this table follows. Words for each function are the frontend's; the meanings below are for the frontend's writers, not screen text.

Source: the engine's environment (`engine/packages/core/src/cel/`, wrapping `@marcbachmann/cel-js` 8.0.0) and the CEL trial (`engine/packages/core/test/cel/`). The trial exercised operators, comprehensions, optionals, `has`, `matches`, `timestamp`, `date`, `int`, durations, `lowerAscii` and `upperAscii`, and the time-zone refusal. The other functions are listed from the library's source and were not exercised.

Types as an author meets them: a `text` or `longText` value is text; a `number` value is a number (CEL double); a `yesNo` value is yes/no; a `date` chip (a date value, "Started on") reads as a point in time, a timestamp at 00:00 UTC of that date, because the compiler wraps it in `date()` (`compiler.md` 8.4, E-26), so a formula never writes `date({{v_due}})` (that is refused: `date` takes text); a `choice` is its `ch_` ID as text; a person or group is a map `{type, id}`; a `choiceFromConnection` is a map `{stored, label}`. A number literal written without a point (`2`) is a whole number (`int`); with one (`2.0`) it is a number.

**Operators**

| Operator | Takes | Gives | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!a` | yes/no | yes/no | Not. |
| `-a` | number or whole number | the same | The negative. |
| `a && b`, `a \|\| b` | yes/no | yes/no | And, or. An error on one side is ignored when the other side decides (`false && x` is false). |
| `c ? a : b` | yes/no, then two values of one type | that type | If `c`, then `a`, else `b`. |
| `a == b`, `a != b` | two values of one type | yes/no | Equal, not equal. Lists, maps and people compare by content. A number and a whole number never mix: write `2.0`. A person or group chip does not compare with a map literal (`{{request.requester}} == {'type': 'user', 'id': '…'}` is `formula.argumentMismatch`): compare two chips (E-27). |
| `a < b`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | two numbers or whole numbers (mixed allowed), two texts, two yes/no, two timestamps, two durations | yes/no | Order. Texts compare by code point. |
| `a + b` | two numbers; two whole numbers; two texts; two lists; two durations; a timestamp and a duration | the same; a timestamp | Adds; joins texts or lists; moves a timestamp later. The timestamp comes first: a duration plus a timestamp is refused (`formula.argumentMismatch`). |
| `a - b` | two numbers; two whole numbers; two durations; a timestamp and a duration; two timestamps | the same; a timestamp; a duration | Subtracts; moves a timestamp earlier; the time between two timestamps. |
| `a * b`, `a / b` | two numbers, or two whole numbers | the same | Multiplies, divides. A whole-number division drops the remainder; a whole number divided by 0 is an error; a number divided by 0 is infinite, and keeping it as a value is an `overflow` error. |
| `a % b` | two whole numbers | whole number | The remainder. By 0 is an error (`division-by-zero`). |
| `x in list` | a value and a list | yes/no | The list holds the value. |
| `k in m` | text and a map | yes/no | The map has the key. |
| `a[i]`, `m[k]`, `a.f` | list and whole number; map and key; map and field | the item | Item, key or field. Missing is an error (`index-out-of-range`, `no-such-key`). |
| `a.?f`, `m[?k]` | map and field or key | optional | The field or key if present, else absent. |

A number and a whole number never mix in `==`, `!=`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`: `{{v_amount}} + 1` is refused at check (`formula.argumentMismatch`); write `{{v_amount}} + 1.0` or `double(1)`.

**Functions**

| Name | Style | Takes | Gives | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | function `size(x)` and method `x.size()` | text, list or map | whole number | The number of characters (code points), items or keys. |
| `contains` | method | text, text | yes/no | The text contains the other. |
| `startsWith`, `endsWith` | method | text, text | yes/no | The text starts or ends with the other. |
| `matches` | method | text, pattern | yes/no | The RE2 pattern matches somewhere in the text. `(?i)` ignores case. No lookahead. A bad pattern is an error. |
| `lowerAscii`, `upperAscii` | method | text | text | Changes A to Z, or a to z, only; other letters are kept. |
| `trim` | method | text | text | Removes white space at both ends. |
| `indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` | method | text, text, optionally a whole-number start | whole number | Where the first or last occurrence begins; −1 when there is none. |
| `substring` | method | text, start, optionally end | text | The text from start up to, not including, end. Out of range is an error. |
| `split` | method | text, separator, optionally a whole-number limit | list of text | The pieces between separators. |
| `join` | method | list of text, optionally a separator | text | The texts joined. |
| `date` | function | text `YYYY-MM-DD` | timestamp | That date at 00:00 UTC. For a date written as text (`date('2026-01-01')`). A date chip is already a timestamp, so `date({{v_due}})` is refused at check (`formula.argumentMismatch`). A date that does not exist is an error. |
| `days` | function | whole number | duration | `days(n)` is a duration of n × 24 hours, so `{{v_due}} + days(3)` is three days later and stays at 00:00 UTC (E-23, E-26). A number with a point is refused at check (`formula.argumentMismatch`); write `days(int({{v_count}}))` for a number value. A duration beyond ±3,650,000 days is an error (`overflow`). |
| `asDate` | function | timestamp | date (text `YYYY-MM-DD`) | The UTC date of the timestamp: `asDate({{v_due}} + days(3))` is the date three days after `v_due` (E-23, E-26). The compiler applies it where a formula's result is used as a date (a Save a value to a date value, a date input), so an author need not write it. A timestamp outside the years 0001 to 9999 is an error (`other`). |
| `duration` | function | text such as `"72h"`, `"90m"`, `"1h30m"` | duration | A length of time. Units `h`, `m`, `s`, `ms`, `us`, `ns`. |
| `timestamp` | function | text, or a whole number | timestamp | Text: an RFC 3339 date and time with an offset (`2026-11-15T09:30:00Z`). Whole number: seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. Years 0001 to 9999. |
| `getFullYear`, `getMonth`, `getDate`, `getDayOfMonth`, `getDayOfWeek`, `getDayOfYear`, `getHours`, `getMinutes`, `getSeconds`, `getMilliseconds` | method | timestamp | whole number | A part of the time in UTC. `getMonth` counts from 0 (January is 0); `getDate` from 1; `getDayOfMonth` and `getDayOfYear` from 0; `getDayOfWeek` 0 is Sunday. |
| `getHours`, `getMinutes`, `getSeconds`, `getMilliseconds` | method | duration | whole number | The whole duration in that unit, rounded down. |
| `int` | function | number, text, timestamp or whole number | whole number | A number cut toward zero; text holding a whole number; a timestamp as seconds since 1970. Beyond the 64-bit range is an error. |
| `double` | function | whole number, text or number | number | The value as a number. |
| `string` | function | number, whole number, yes/no or text | text | The value as text. |
| `bool` | function | text | yes/no | `"true"`, `"True"`, `"TRUE"`, `"t"`, `"1"` are yes; `"false"`, `"False"`, `"FALSE"`, `"f"`, `"0"` are no; anything else is an error. |
| `has` | macro | a field, `has(x.f)` | yes/no | The field is present. On a field of a chip, `has({{v_x}}.f)`, `checkFormula` and the compiler both write an optional read of that field (E-27). It works where the chip's value has fields: a person, a group, a connection choice, a field group; on a chip whose value is text it is refused (E-28). The rewrite is a plain text match, so `has({{chip}}.f)` written inside a string literal is rewritten too. |
| `all`, `exists`, `exists_one` | macro on a list | a name and a condition, `x.all(i, i > 0)` | yes/no | Every item, at least one, or exactly one meets the condition. |
| `map` | macro on a list | a name and an expression, or a name, a condition and an expression | list | Each item turned into another; with a condition, only the items that meet it. |
| `filter` | macro on a list | a name and a condition | list | The items that meet the condition. |
| `optional.of`, `optional.none` | function | a value; nothing | optional | A present value; an absent one. A formula that gives `optional.none()` leaves its value empty. |
| `hasValue`, `value`, `or`, `orValue` | method | optional | yes/no; the value; optional; the value | Whether it is present; its value (an error when absent); itself if present, else the other optional; its value if present, else the other value. |
| `cel.bind` | macro | a name, a value, an expression | the expression's type | Names a value once for use inside the expression. |
| `dyn` | function | anything | any | Turns off kind checking for that value. |

Also accepted by the environment and not offered, because no authored value has these types: bytes and unsigned integers and their functions (`bytes()`, `uint()`, `size(bytes)`, `string(bytes)`), `null`, `type()`.

Indexes in `indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` and `substring` count UTF-16 units, while `size` counts code points; they differ only for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane. Kept as the library does it.

**Refused in `cel-1`**

| What | How it is refused |
|---|---|
| A time zone: any timestamp method given a time-zone argument (`getHours('Europe/Berlin')`) | `formula.notInProfile`, `rule: "timeZone"`. The environment refuses it (`time-zone-not-allowed`). |
| `\p` or `\P` in a pattern (E-20) | `formula.notInProfile`, `rule: "unicodeClass"`, when the formula is checked, for a pattern written as literal text (E-26). The environment refuses it (`unicode-class-not-allowed`). A pattern built at run time is refused when evaluated (expression error `other`). |
| A name or function starting `cel1_` (reserved for the environment's own functions) | `formula.unknownName` or `formula.unknownFunction`. |
| A duration plus a timestamp (`days(3) + {{v_due}}`) | `formula.argumentMismatch`; write the timestamp first. Also refused when evaluated. |
| `json()` on bytes | `formula.unknownFunction`. |
| A clock: there is no `now`, no "today" and no time zone | No such name exists. |
| Mixing a number and a whole number in arithmetic | `formula.argumentMismatch`. |
| Comprehensions with two names (`m.all(k, v, ...)`), the CEL extension libraries (math, strings, encoders) | `formula.unknownName` (the first name the environment does not know, such as `v` or `math`), `formula.unknownFunction` or `formula.syntax`, as the library first meets it (E-27). |
| A map literal with a key starting with `$` (`{'$x': 1}`) | `formula.notInProfile`, `rule: "reservedKey"` (E-27), at the first such key of the formula; as for every formula error, only that one is reported and the formula's kind is not checked. A key starting with `$` is reserved. A key built at run time is refused when the value is saved (expression error `wrong-kind`). |

A list or map literal may mix value types (E-20). A formula whose place needs a date may give a timestamp: the compiler applies `asDate` to it (E-23). A formula whose place needs any other value kind may not give a timestamp or a duration (`formula.kindMismatch`): neither is a value kind.

## 7. `formState` (R2)

```ts
function formState(
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow,
  catalogue: Catalogue,
  task: Location,               // { item: TaskId }; the start task for the start form
  answers: Answers,             // the form so far
  values: Values,               // the request's values; {} on the start form or in the form editor
  request?: { requester?: Ref; startedOn?: string },
  lookups?: KnownLookups,
): FormStateResult;

type FormStateResult =
  | { result: "state"; state: FormState }
  | { result: "needsLookups"; lookups: NeededLookup[] };

interface FormState {
  shown: ItemId[];                                     // pages, questions and texts shown; anything else is hidden
  choices: Partial<Record<QuestionId, Json[]>>;        // only for questions whose choices come from a formula
  buttons: FormButtonState[];                          // one per button, display order
  invalid?: Refusal[];                                 // the invalid-data refusals of the answers given, in form order; absent when none (E-27)
}
interface FormButtonState {
  button: ButtonId;
  available: boolean;           // missing is empty and there is no refusal
  missing: QuestionId[];        // needed questions that are shown and still empty
  refusal?: Refusal;            // the act's first refusal: `invalid-data`, `check` (Also only when ...) or `rule-error` (E-27)
}
```

`formState` validates and types the answers exactly as the compiled outcome schema of the button does, with the kernel's own validator: the form's conditions read each answer as `input` typed from that schema, so an answer whose schema is open (an item of a formula's choices with no value kind) reads as any value, not as text. What it calls available, the act's schema step and checks accept.

`invalid` lets the page mark each answer that would be refused, beside its question. A button's `refusal` is the one the act would give first: schema failures in form order (an answer to a question the form does not have comes after the questions' own failures), then the check step question by question (`runtime-api.md` section 4.3). A missing needed question is in `missing`, not in `refusal`.

The catalogue is a parameter because a question's kind and its source's fields come from it (E-20).

### 7.1 Rules

- Works with no request. While the form is open, a question's answer counts as its `savedAs` value, so a Show when on the same form sees it.
- A needed question is one in the button's effective set (`neededToPress` plus every question with `neededForEveryButton`) that is shown. A hidden question is never needed. The page sends no answer for a question that is not in `shown`.
- **Where choices come from.** Typed-in and list choices: the document. A formula: `FormState.choices`. The directory (`from: "directory"`) and a data source (`from: "source"`): the question-scoped choices call, `runtime.choices` (`runtime-api.md` section 3.4), or `TestHost.choices` in Try it. One call serves both, on the start form and on a task alike, and each answer is looked up again when the person acts (E-20): `choice-unknown` when it is not found; `source-unavailable` when the source, the directory's included, cannot be asked.
- **Lookups.** Where a condition of the form (a Show when, an "Also only when", a choices formula) uses a `directory` step or "is in" a group, `needsLookups` is returned and the caller calls again with `lookups`. On a task page they come from `TaskView.lookups`: the group members recorded by the read placed just before the task's step (E-20, E-23), which are what the act's checks read. On the start form a condition cannot use the directory (`start.directoryInCondition`), so no lookup is needed there. In Try it they come from `Fakes.groups`. In the form editor they come from `directory.membersOf`.
- A page or question Show when that cannot be worked out counts as shown; a choices formula that cannot be worked out gives no `choices` entry. In either case every button's `refusal` is that `rule-error`, located at the item and part, as the act would refuse. A page and its question combine as the act combines them: a Show when that is false wins over one that errors. A text's Show when (`tx_`) is not compiled (it only shapes what the page shows, `compiler.md` 5.3), so it never refuses a button.
- Who may press (`wait-not-open`, `not-assignee`, `may`) is not here; it is `ButtonState` (section 8). The act re-checks everything.
- `startedOn` on the start form is the page's own date; the request's is the server's at start.

### 7.2 How form rules reach a refusal

The compiler turns form rules into the outcome's schema, lookups and checks (E-6, E-14, E-20). The engine reports each failure as the rule the author wrote, at the place they wrote it:

| Authored rule | Refusal |
|---|---|
| A needed question is empty | `invalid-data` / `required`, location the question |
| An answer is not one of the typed-in choices or list rows | `invalid-data` / `not-a-choice`, location the question, part `choices` |
| A multiple choice out of the choices' order | `invalid-data` / `not-a-choice`, location the question, part `choices` |
| An empty multiple choice (`[]`) | `invalid-data` / `too-short`, location the question (E-27) |
| An answer from the directory or a data source is not found when the person acts | `choice-unknown`, location the question, part `choices` |
| The data source, or the directory for a directory choice, cannot be asked when the person acts | `source-unavailable`, location the question, part `choices` |
| An answer to a hidden question | `invalid-data` / `hidden-answered`, location the question (or its page), part `showWhen` |
| An answer of the wrong shape, a field inside it that its schema does not have included | `invalid-data` / `wrong-kind`, `too-long`, ..., location the question |
| "Also only when ..." is not true | `check`, location the button, part `enabledWhen`, `message` = `messageWhileDisabled` |
| A condition of the form errors | `rule-error`, location the item and part |

Kernel order is kept between steps (`runtime-api.md` section 4.3): the lookups are made before the request is locked, but every schema failure is reported before any lookup result is applied, and every lookup before any check; a rule the compiler enforces as a check is reported in the check step, still as `invalid-data` against its question.

An empty multiple choice and one out of order are refused by one compiled check, `<q>__choice` (`compiler.md` 5.4); `jsonschema-1` has no keyword for "at least one item" (E-27). The kernel's refusal names the check, so core's refusal mapping, which the server also uses, tells the two apart by the answer: `[]` is `too-short`, anything else `not-a-choice`.

## 8. Request views (shared by Try it and the runtime)

```ts
interface ButtonState {          // may the viewer press it now; viewer-level, before any answer
  button: ButtonId;
  available: boolean;            // refusals is empty
  refusals: Refusal[];           // in the order the engine checks: wait-not-open, membership-unavailable, not-assignee, may
}

interface OpenTask {
  requestId: RequestId;
  task: TaskInstanceId;
  location: Location;            // { item: TaskId }
  askedOf: Ref[];                // as recorded when the task opened; may be empty (the request is then stuck, nobody-to-ask)
  openedAt: Timestamp;
  buttonStates: ButtonState[];   // for the viewer (Try it: the person acted as)
}

interface OpenAction {
  location: Location;            // { item: ActionId }
  sort: OperationSort;
  openedAt: Timestamp;
  call?: CallRef;                // Try it only: to answer it with answerCall
  admin?: {                      // only for people who look after stuck requests; live only
    state: "queued" | "inFlight" | "accepted";   // accepted: an await whose outside job is running; else queued (E-33)
    attempts: number;
    lastAttemptAt?: Timestamp;
    lastError?: string;          // the other system's own text, or the engine's for a timeout
    expectedBy: Timestamp;       // openedAt + the operation's expectedWithinSeconds
    overdue: boolean;            // expectedBy has passed; nobody is told (E-33)
  };
}

/** Why a request cannot go on (E-19, E-20). One state, the same in the request view, the lists and the story. */
interface Stuck {
  reason: StuckReason;
  at: Timestamp;                 // when it became stuck
  location?: Location;           // what cannot go on (table below)
  admin?: StuckDetail;           // only for the people who look after stuck requests and platform admins
}
type StuckReason =
  | "action-failed"              // a call failed and was not carried on
  | "nobody-to-ask"              // an open task has nobody to ask
  | "nothing-fits"               // nothing is open and no arrow fits
  | "error"                      // something could not be worked out
  | "unfinished";                // Try it only: the request reached an unfinished part of the draft

/** Engineers' detail. Never shown as the page's own words; the page may show it as quoted detail. */
interface StuckDetail {
  fault?: string;                // the recorded fault code: "call-failed", "cel-error", "int-range", "key-invalid", "firing-limit"
  failureCode?: string;          // reason action-failed: the operation's failure code, from the fault's params (E-21, E-23)
  attempts?: number;             // reason action-failed: how many times the call was delivered, where known (E-21)
  error?: ExpressionErrorKind;   // reason error, when an expression failed
  key?: string;                  // the missing key, when it names something authored (a value ID, a catalogue field ID)
  index?: number;                // the list position, when it names something authored
  text?: string;                 // the engine's own error text: technical, may name engine things (E-27)
  outsideText?: string;          // reason action-failed: the other system's own failure text
}

interface RequestView {
  requestId: RequestId;
  readableId: ReadableId;
  workflow?: ServerWorkflowId;   // absent in Try it
  version?: VersionNumber;       // absent in Try it
  status?: Status;               // the authored Status (words, colour) of the version
  stage: Location;               // { item: StageId, part?: "whenThisStageStarts" | "tasks" | "afterTheyRespond" | "arrows" }
  closed?: { at: Timestamp; ending?: StageId; byAdmin: boolean };   // ending: the authored ending's stage ID; absent when an admin closed it
  startedBy: By;
  requester?: Ref;
  startedAt: Timestamp;
  updatedAt: Timestamp;
  lastSeq: Seq;
  values: Values;
  tasks: OpenTask[];
  actions: OpenAction[];
  stuck?: Stuck;                 // absent: not stuck
  story: StoryEntry[];           // oldest first
  viewer: { isAdmin: boolean };  // sees the admin fields; may close an open request, and retry one stuck with action-failed or nobody-to-ask
}
```

`Status` is the authored format's `Status`. The engine records the status ID; words and colour come from the version's source.

```ts
/** One published version as the readers need it: the definition with its origin map, the authored source it was compiled from, and the catalogue. */
interface PublishedVersion { definition: PublishedDefinition; source: AuthoredWorkflow; catalogue: Catalogue }

/** The request view, built from history only. `events`: the request's events from its start, in seq order. Throws when they hold no start. */
function requestView(published: PublishedVersion, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], options?: ViewOptions): RequestView;

interface ViewOptions {
  viewer?: { as?: Ref; isAdmin: boolean; groupsOf?: (user: string) => readonly string[] | undefined };   // groupsOf undefined: the directory could not be asked
  workflow?: ServerWorkflowId; version?: VersionNumber;   // live only
  why?: ReadonlyMap<number, readonly TraceEntry[]>;       // Try it: decide's trace per turn, for why.notFitting
  calls?: boolean;                                        // Try it: give each open action its CallRef
  unfinished?: readonly Unfinished[];                     // Try it: compile's unfinished parts (section 12)
  attempts?: (element: string) => number | undefined;     // how many times a call was delivered, for admin.attempts
  debug?: boolean;                                        // add each story entry's events
}
```

`PublishedDefinition`, `AnyEventRecord` and `TraceEntry` are the kernel entry's (`@workflow/core/kernel`, section 14); the server, which holds them, is the caller. The server's request page and Try it's `TestHost.request` build the view with this one function (E-27). At the root, `PublishedVersion` is exported under that name.

Every signed-in person sees that a request is stuck, its reason and its location; `admin` is filled only for the workflow's people who look after stuck requests and for platform admins (E-19, E-21). A request has at most one stuck state at a time.

The reason is worked out from history only, the first row that applies (E-23, E-33):

| Reason | Comes from | Location | `admin` | Retry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action-failed` | A `Faulted` with code `call-failed`, whatever added the call: an action whose "If it fails" is "stuck", or a compiler-added read such as a `members` step's.
