The fault's params carry the operation's failure code (E-23). | the action; for a compiler-added read, the item and part that read the group | `fault`, `failureCode`, `attempts`, `outsideText` | Offered |
| `error` | Any other `Faulted`: `cel-error`, `int-range`, `key-invalid` (an expression could not be worked out), `firing-limit` (more than 50 moves in one go), or a code added later. | the item and part the faulted element came from, through the origin map | `fault`, and `error`, `key`, `index`, `text` where they apply | Not offered |
| `nothing-fits` | Worked out, not recorded: the request is open, has no fault, and nothing is open (no task and no action), so no arrow fits. | the stage, part `arrows` | none | Not offered |
| `nobody-to-ask` | The match of the published definition's `nobodyToAsk` block (E-20, E-23; `engine/spec/integrations.md` section 11.5): an open task that nobody can answer (E-24). Who can answer is the people asked directly plus the recorded members of the groups asked (from the task's membership read `<task>__members`, opened beside the task), minus the Requester where the Requester may not answer; nobody-to-ask means that set is empty. A membership read that fails contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts. While the read has no result, a task that asks a group is not nobody-to-ask. Not a fault: the kernel keeps them apart (E-19). | the task, part `whoIsAsked` | none | Offered |
| `unfinished` | Try it only (section 10.2). Nobody is told: no `request.stuck` message and no `request.stuck@1` (section 10.3, E-32). | the unfinished stage | none | Not offered |

- `key` and `index` are given only when they name something authored; a key the compiler added is left out (E-7). `text` is the recorded fault's detail, passed through as it is. It is technical and may name engine things (a compiled ID, compiled expression text). It is for the people who look after stuck requests, and the page shows it behind a disclosure, never as the explanation (E-27).
- Every reader (the notifier, the publisher, the lists, the request view and the story) works the state out this way and no other. A stuck rule whose expression errors counts as no match for every reader, and the error is logged (E-23).
- A request stops being stuck when an admin turn retries it and it does not stop again, when it is closed, or, for `nobody-to-ask`, when the task is no longer open (an arrow marked "Don't wait for the others" moved the request on). For `nothing-fits`, when something is open again.
- Every reader compares the stuck state before and after each turn. A turn after which the request is stuck the same way (the same reason and location) gives no new story entry, message or event, and the stuck state keeps its `at`. A stuck state that changes, also while the request is faulted, gives a new `stuck` entry, sends `request.stuck` and publishes `request.stuck@1`, like any other change (E-27); Try it's `unfinished` gives the entry only (section 10.3).
- `request.stuck@1` and `request.unstuck@1` carry `{ reason, stage }` from the same rule, worked out once per turn (E-20), so every reader agrees. `stage`, there and in the `request.stuck` message, is always an authored stage ID: the authored stage the request is stuck in, found through the version's origin map by the compiler's conventions (E-27, E-28; `authoredStageOf` in the kernel entry, section 14). An engine stage whose origin has part `tasks` or `arrows` names its authored stage; from any other step (an action's steps, a directory read step) the authored stage is the first such stage along the transitions; an ending is its own stage; for Try it's unfinished step, whose origin is an arrow, it is the stage that arrow leaves. A hand-written definition with no origin map reports its own stage. Like every built-in event they carry IDs, status and reason only, never answers (E-22).

## 9. The story (R1)

```ts
type StoryEntry = Coded<StoryParams, {
  location?: Location;   // per code, below
  at: Timestamp;
  turn: number;          // entries caused by one input share it
  debug?: { events: unknown[] };   // only when asked: the events it was built from (engine/design/event-payloads.md). Never relied on.
}>;

interface StoryParams {
  /** Location: the start task. */
  "started": { by: By; button: ButtonId; answers: Answers; version?: VersionNumber; startsWhen?: StartsWhenId; requester?: Ref };
  /** Location: the task. */
  "task.opened": { task: TaskInstanceId; askedOf: Ref[] };
  "task.answered": { task: TaskInstanceId; by: By; button: ButtonId; answers: Answers; asMemberOf: Ref[] };
  "task.noLongerNeeded": { task: TaskInstanceId; because: "movedOn" | "closed" | "retried" };
  /** Location: the action. late: the result came after the request moved on. */
  "action.waiting": { sort: OperationSort };
  "action.done": { sort: OperationSort; result?: Record<string, Json>; late?: boolean };
  "action.failed": { sort: OperationSort; failureCode?: string; carriedOn: boolean; late?: boolean };
  /** Location: the Save a value action. to absent: emptied. */
  "value.saved": { value: ValueId; to?: Json };
  /** Location: the arrow taken. */
  "moved": { from: StageId; arrow: ArrowId; to: StageId; sentBack: boolean; why?: MoveWhy };
  /** Location: the stage entered. */
  "status.changed": { from?: StatusId; to?: StatusId };
  /** The entry's `at` and `location` equal the Stuck's. */
  "stuck": Stuck;
  /** Location: the authored stage the request is in, entered again. */
  "retried": { by: By; reason: string };
  /** No location. */
  "closed": { by: By; reason: string };       // closed by a person who looks after stuck requests
  /** Location: the ending. */
  "ended": { ending: StageId };
}

interface MoveWhy {
  taken: { arrow: ArrowId; reads: WhyRead[] };
  notFitting?: { arrow: ArrowId; reads: WhyRead[] }[];   // Try it only, in the order checked
}
interface WhyRead { of: ReadOf; value?: Json }           // value absent: empty
type ReadOf =
  | { value: ValueId; path?: (string | number)[] }       // a value; path into it (a field of a fieldGroup, a list index)
  | { request: "requester" | "startedOn" }
  | { pressed: TaskId }                                  // which button was pressed on the task in this visit
  | { list: ListId; row: RowId; column: ColumnId };      // a cell read through a column step
```

```ts
/** A request's story, from history only. The catalogue tells an await from a write (`action.waiting`, `sort`). */
function story(published: PublishedVersion, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], options?: StoryOptions): StoryEntry[];

interface StoryOptions {
  admin?: boolean;                                        // fill stuck.admin (the people who look after stuck requests)
  version?: VersionNumber;                                // live only: for the started entry
  why?: ReadonlyMap<number, readonly TraceEntry[]>;       // Try it: adds why.notFitting to every move
  unfinished?: readonly Unfinished[];                     // Try it, as in ViewOptions
  attempts?: (element: string) => number | undefined;     // as in ViewOptions
  debug?: boolean;                                        // add the events each entry was built from
}
```

`PublishedVersion` is section 8's. `RequestView.story` is this function's result for the same events.

How entries are built, from history only, through the origin map:

| Entry | From |
|---|---|
| `started` | `RequestStarted`, the start turn's root and first `StageEntered`, and the start task's `WaitOpened` and `WaitCompleted`: one entry. `startsWhen` from `trigger.id`. `requester` from the Requester start answer (E-17) or, for a person start, `by`. |
| `task.opened` | A person `WaitOpened`, except the start task in the start turn. |
| `task.answered` | A person `WaitCompleted`. `asMemberOf` from `evidence.memberOf`. |
| `task.noLongerNeeded` | A person `WaitCancelled` (`stage-exit`: `movedOn`; `request-closed`: `closed`), or `WaitSkipped` in a retry (`retried`). |
| `action.waiting` | A call `WaitOpened` of an `await` operation. Read and write calls show only their result. |
| `action.done`, `action.failed` | A call `WaitCompleted` `ok` / `failed`; `CallResultLate` with `late: true`. `carriedOn` from the action's "If it fails". |
| `value.saved` | A `DataSet` that came from a Save a value action, one entry per value. |
| `moved` | `TransitionFired`, `StageExited`, `StageEntered`, when the authored stage changes. Moves between the engine stages of one authored stage give no entry. `sentBack` as in `facts`. `why.taken.reads` from `TransitionFired.reads`. A list is a constant of the version, so its cells are not recorded reads: where the arrow's `when` or "+ only when" reads a cell through a column step, the cell (`{ list, row, column }`) of the row the value held follows that value's read, with its value in the version's list (E-32). `notFitting` from `decide`'s trace, which is not recorded (E-15), so live entries have no `notFitting`. |
| `status.changed` | A `StageEntered` whose status differs from the one shown before. |
| `stuck` | The turn after which the stuck state of section 8 is stuck and differs from before: a `Faulted`, nothing that fits, or the `nobodyToAsk` block's match, which begins when the task opens with nobody who can answer it or when its membership read completes and leaves nobody (section 8). A turn after which it is stuck the same way gives no entry (E-27). |
| `retried`, `closed` | `Overridden` with a re-entry, or with a close. |
| `ended` | `RequestClosed` with a stage. |

Every `moved` entry names its arrow. A retry re-enters the stage the request is in, so the authored stage does not change and no `moved` entry is made; a start is the `started` entry; a close moves nowhere. The "absent arrow: moved by a retry" case of Draft 2 could not occur and is removed.

`DataSet`s from answers, saved results, saved failures and a task's two extra answers fold into the entry of the input that caused them. A read in `TransitionFired.reads` that maps to nothing authored is left out of `why`. Notifications and things told are not history (E-9), so they are not in the story; Try it shows them in the outbox. The runtime returns the same shape (`runtime-api.md` section 6.3); `stuck.admin` is filled only for admins there too.

## 10. Try it: the test host

### 10.1 Creating one

```ts
function createTestHost(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue, fakes: Fakes): HostResult;

type HostResult =
  | { ok: true; host: TestHost; unfinished: Location[]; findings: Finding[] }
  | { ok: false; findings: Finding[] };      // the workflow-level To dos: workflow.noStart, start.notOneTask, compile.internal

interface Fakes {
  groups: Partial<Record<string, string[]>>;            // group id -> user ids: who is in each group during the test
  stuckRequestsGoTo: Ref[];                             // who may retry and close, and who is told
  calls?: Partial<Record<CatalogueRef, CallFake>>;      // default per operation: { mode: "sample" }
  sources?: Partial<Record<CatalogueRef, Record<string, Json>[]>>;   // data source items; default: the catalogue sample
  startAt: Timestamp;                                   // the time of the first turn; each later turn is 1 s later, unless a call gives its own (section 10.2)
}

type CallFake =
  | { mode: "sample" }                                  // answer at once with the catalogue sample result
  | { mode: "result"; data: Record<string, Json> }
  | { mode: "fail"; error: { code: string; message?: string } }   // code: one of the operation's failure codes
  | { mode: "hold" };                                   // stay waiting until answerCall
type CallAnswer =
  | { outcome: "ok"; data: Record<string, Json> }
  | { outcome: "failed"; error: { code: string; message?: string } };
```

A failed call is recorded as `{ code, message }` (E-23). An absent `message` is the catalogue sample's failure message when its code matches, else `""`.

How the fakes are read (E-27, as built):

- A group missing from `groups` is a group with nobody in it. A membership read lists it with no members and never fails with `group-not-found`.
- A data source keeps only the items whose fields equal the lookup's inputs, for each input field the item has. So an input `status: "active"` leaves out an item whose `status` is `retired`, and an input the items do not have filters nothing.
- Directory choices are labelled with the user ID, because the fakes hold no names. The page may look the names up with `directory.lookup`.

### 10.2 The host

```ts
interface TestHost {
  start(as: Ref, button: ButtonId, answers: Answers, at?: Timestamp): TurnResult<{ requestId: RequestId }>;
  startFrom(binding: StartsWhenId, sent: Record<string, Json>, at?: Timestamp): TurnResult<StartFromResult>;
  choices(args: ChoicesArgs): ChoicesPage;                      // runtime-api.md section 3.4
  openTasks(filter?: { requestId?: RequestId; askedOf?: Ref; as?: Ref }): OpenTask[];
  act(as: Ref, requestId: RequestId, task: TaskInstanceId, button: ButtonId, answers: Answers, at?: Timestamp): TurnResult;
  admin(as: Ref, requestId: RequestId, action: "retry" | "close", reason: string, at?: Timestamp): TurnResult;
  answerCall(call: CallRef, answer: CallAnswer, at?: Timestamp): TurnResult;
  setCallFake(operation: CatalogueRef, fake: CallFake): void;   // calls opened from now on
  outbox(requestId?: RequestId): OutboxEntry[];                 // oldest first
  request(requestId: RequestId, as?: Ref): RequestView | { ok: false; refusals: Refusal[] };   // story with why on every move; not-found for an unknown request
}

type StartFromResult = { started: true; requestId: RequestId } | { started: false; reason: "onlyWhenNotTrue" };
```

- **Time** (E-32). Each call that runs a turn may give its time, `at`: RFC 3339 with an offset (`Z` or `±hh:mm`) and up to nine fractional digits, of which six are kept, as the kernel's `at` has them. The turn, and the calls the host answers after it, run at that time, but never earlier than the request's previous event: an earlier time is taken as that event's. Without `at` a turn is 1 s after the host's last, as before. An `at` that is not RFC 3339 is refused with `invalid-body` `{ field: "/at", problem: "format" }`.
- **Same kernel.** Each input goes through core's turn function, the one the server runs in its transaction: validate, append, `decide`, stuck check. `decide`, `evolve`, the CEL environment, the schema validator, the `nobodyToAsk` matcher and the notification and told rules are the same code. Only I/O is replaced: memberships, membership reads (`membersOf@1`, the `<task>__members` read and the read of a `members` step inside a condition) and directory choices read `fakes.groups`, data sources read `fakes.sources`, calls are answered from `fakes.calls`, notifications and things told go to the outbox. Nothing leaves the browser (E-4).
- **Refusals** are the runtime's codes in the runtime's order (`runtime-api.md` section 4.3), so one renderer serves both. `membership-unavailable` and `source-unavailable` never occur: the fakes always answer.
- **Viewer.** `buttonStates` in `openTasks` and `request` are for `as`; without `as` they are `[]`. `viewer.isAdmin` is true when `as` is in `stuckRequestsGoTo`, and then `stuck.admin` is filled.
- **Calls.** After each turn the host answers every call opened in it, in declared order, each as its own turn, as the server's call job would. A `hold` call stays pending until `answerCall`. A result after the action's wait closed is recorded late and shown with `late: true`.
- **Unknown IDs** (E-27). `request` on a request the host does not hold answers `{ ok: false, refusals: [not-found] }` with `what: "request"`. `answerCall` on a call the host does not hold, or one no longer pending, answers `not-found` with `what: "call"` (E-28). `act` and `admin` answer `not-found` (`request`, `task`) as the runtime does; `act` on a task the request never opened, or on an action's call, is `not-found` with `what: "task"` (the kernel's `unknown-wait`, E-28).
- **A result that does not fit** its operation's result shape is refused by the call-result check (section 14) with `invalid-body` `{ field: "/data", problem: "type" }`; nothing is recorded and the call stays pending (E-27).
- **Choices.** `choices` takes the runtime's `ChoicesArgs` and returns its `ChoicesPage` (`runtime-api.md` section 3.4, the one statement of the shape, E-23). The host holds one draft, so for the start form `form` is any `{ workflow, version }` and both are ignored. It serves questions whose choices come from the directory or a data source, as the server does (E-20): for a source it works out the inputs from the stored form and the answers, lists `fakes.sources` (or the sample) and filters by `search` on the label; for the directory it works out the group from `peopleIn` and lists its people from `fakes.groups`. Any other question gives `{ choices: [] }`. `cursor` and `limit` page through the items as on the server. When the person acts, each such answer is looked up again in the same fakes; one not found is refused with `choice-unknown`, and the label recorded for a source answer is the item's.
- **`startFrom`** runs the binding as the inbound handler does: `onlyWhen`, then the mapping, then the start turn as the connection. A mapping error refuses with `mapping-error`; a failing start form with `invalid-data`, `choice-unknown`, `check` or `rule-error`; a refused start also puts one `start.refused` message, carrying all its refusals, to `stuckRequestsGoTo` in the outbox (E-16). Try it does not limit these to one an hour. A binding with a To do that stops a request from running is refused with `unfinished`; an ID that is not a binding of the draft with `not-found` (`binding`).
- **Unfinished drafts (E-20).** Try it treats a draft as unfinished only where a To do stops a request from running: the "Stops Try it" column of section 4 and the `item.partMissing` parts listed under it. In short: no destination, no operation, no button, a broken reference, a formula that does not parse or type-check, a kind conflict. Words and labels never block it. The part with such a To do (an arrow, an action, a task's step, a stage's arrows, a binding) compiles to the unfinished shapes of `engine/design/compiler.md` section 13 and is listed in `unfinished` (section 12); a request that gets there is stuck with reason `unfinished`. The start stage is the exception, because a start completes its task: an unfinished start stage keeps its task, so `start` works and the request is stuck with `unfinished` straight after the start turn; if the start task itself has such a To do, `start` is refused with `unfinished` (location: the task). Every other To do is left for the request to meet, so the tester sees what a request would do: an empty value that a formula reads without a guard makes the request stuck with `error` there; a button that fits no arrow makes it stuck with `nothing-fits`. No kernel rule is bent.
- **`why`** is `decide`'s trace for that turn: the arrows checked in order and what each read. Not recorded.
- **Admin actions** are the first build's two, retry and close, with the runtime's rules (`runtime-api.md` section 5.1): retry only for a request stuck with `action-failed` or `nobody-to-ask`; a request that is not stuck is refused `not-stuck`, one stuck with `nothing-fits`, `error` or `unfinished` is refused `not-retryable`; close for any open request (E-23). `as` must be in `stuckRequestsGoTo` (a group there counts its members in `fakes.groups`), else `not-admin`. A reason over 2000 characters after trimming is refused `invalid-body` `{ field: "/reason", problem: "tooLong" }`, as live.
- **State** is in memory for the life of the host. A changed draft needs a new host.

### 10.3 The outbox (R6, R9)

```ts
type OutboxEntry =
  | {                                   // done in other systems
      kind: "call"; call: CallRef; requestId: RequestId; at: Timestamp;
      action: Location; operation: CatalogueRef; sort: OperationSort;
      inputs: Record<string, Json>;     // input field id -> what would have been sent
      state: "pending" | "ok" | "failed" | "late";
      result?: Record<string, Json>; failure?: { code: string; message: string };
    }
  | {                                   // messages
      kind: "notification"; requestId?: RequestId; at: Timestamp;   // requestId absent for start.refused
      from: { action: Location } | BuiltInMessage;
      to: Ref[];                        // as written
      recipients: Ref[];                // groups expanded to people
      message?: MessagePart[];          // with from.action: the author's message as rendered
    }
  | {                                   // other systems told
      kind: "told"; requestId: RequestId; at: Timestamp;
      what: { tell: ToldId; action: Location } | { builtIn: BuiltInTold };
      values: Record<string, Json>;     // a Tell: each value as the request holds it; a built-in: IDs, status and reason only
    };

type MessagePart = string | { value?: Json; kind?: ValueKind };   // a chip: its value at that moment; absent value: empty, shown as nothing

type BuiltInMessage = { builtIn: Coded<BuiltInMessageParams, {}> };   // { builtIn: { code, params } }
interface BuiltInMessageParams {
  "task.assigned":    { stage: StageId; task: TaskId; askedOf: Ref[] };
  "request.stuck":    { stage: StageId; reason: StuckReason; location?: Location };
  "start.refused":    { binding: StartsWhenId; refusals: Refusal[] };
}
type BuiltInTold = "requestStarted" | "statusChanged" | "stuck" | "unstuck" | "ended";
```

- **The built-in messages the engine sends are `task.assigned` and `request.stuck`** (E-21, E-33). Their codes are the keys of `contract/words/notifications.json` (the frontend's words; the notifier sends from that file, E-14). Every other problem is a log line on the server (`engine/spec/integrations.md` section 14), and nobody is told.
- A built-in message carries its code and params, no words. The notifier fills the words' placeholders by these names: `{request}`, `{workflow}` (from the request and the workflow record), `{stage}`, `{task}`, `{askedOf}`; for `request.stuck`, `{reason}` and `{whatYouCanDo}` from the words file's `reasons.<reason>`. A placeholder names a param or one of these; a new one is agreed before the words use it.
- A request that becomes stuck sends `request.stuck` with its reason, for every reason a live request can have, `nobody-to-ask` included (E-21). It goes to the people who look after stuck requests. There is no separate message for nobody to ask. Try it's `unfinished` sends no `request.stuck` and is told to no other system (no `stuck`, and no `unstuck` when it ends), because a live request never has it (E-32); the story and the request view still show it.
- `task.assigned` goes to who is asked, less anyone who may not answer the task (the Requester where the Requester can't answer), by the rule that decides nobody-to-ask (E-32, E-33). puts no `task.assigned` there, and neither does Retry when it asks nobody again.
- A call entry's `action` is the call's origin: the action for a Use a connection, or the part that named the group for a membership read (the task's `whoIsAsked`) or a directory read step. A membership read or a directory read step makes no story entry, because it is not an action.
- A Notify's message is rendered with the values as they were at the event that set it off (E-14). An empty value is shown as nothing (E-22). People are references (`kind: "person"`, `"group"`, `"people"`); names come from `directory.lookup`. A saved failure code is a part of kind `text` holding the catalogue's label, because the authored source the page reads has no failure codes (E-29; section 2.4).
- **What is told** (E-22). A Tell other systems action sends each value as the request holds it (section 2.4): a choice from a connection as `{ stored, label }`, a person or group as `{ type, id }`, a typed-in choice as its `ch_` ID. An empty value leaves its name out.
- `BuiltInTold` is the outbound vocabulary of E-17: `request.started@1`, `request.statusChanged@1`, `request.stuck@1` and `request.unstuck@1` (both carrying `{ reason, stage }`, E-20), `request.ended@1` (carrying `stage`, the authored ending the request finished at, absent in the outbox when an admin closed it, E-32). They carry IDs, status and reason only, never answers (E-22). A Tell other systems action is `request.told@1`, carrying the thing told and the author's values. One type for every declaration; no type per thing told.
- No idempotency key is shown.

## 11. `diff`

```ts
function diff(before: AuthoredWorkflow, after: AuthoredWorkflow): Change[];

type Change = Coded<ChangeParams, { location: Location }>;   // in `after`; in `before` for item.removed
interface ChangeParams {
  "item.added":   { itemKind: ItemKind };
  "item.removed": { itemKind: ItemKind };
  "item.moved":   { itemKind: ItemKind; from: Location; to: Location };   // its parent, or the parent's field that holds it, changed
  "part.changed": { itemKind: ItemKind; before?: Json; after?: Json };    // before/after for small parts only
}
```

How changes are read, as built (E-28):

- Items are matched by ID. An item whose ID changed is a removal and an addition. The workflow is matched as the workflow, whatever its ID; a changed workflow ID is a `part.changed` at part `id`.
- Every added or removed item is listed on its own: removing a stage also lists its tasks, pages, questions, buttons and arrows as removed.
- A moved item is located by its parent and the field that holds it: `from` and `to` are `{ item: <parent ID>, part: <that field> }`, for example `{ item: "st_a", part: "whenThisStageStarts" }`. A move between two fields of the same parent is a move.
- A new order of items under one parent is one `part.changed` on the parent, at the field that holds them, with `before` and `after` the lists of their IDs. Adding, removing or moving one item alone does not report a change on its parent.
- A `part.changed` location's `part` follows the path rule of section 2.3 and may name any field of the item: the deepest reported part (section 2.3) that holds the change, otherwise the item's top-level field (`look`, `colour`, `title` ...); never a clause or template index. An object added or removed is compared field by field, so adding `saveFailureAs: { failed }` is a change at `saveFailureAs.failed`, not at `saveFailureAs`, and adding it with `failed` and `code` is two changes (E-32).
- `before` and `after` are given only for small parts: text, numbers, yes/no, and lists of them or of item IDs. An expression, a condition or a template with chips gets neither.
- `null` and absent are the same in every comparison, so `null` against absent is no change; `before` or `after` is absent where the part was absent or `null`.
- Order: by the item's place in `after`, then by code, then by the part's place in the reported parts. A removed item comes just before the next item of `before` that is still there.
- `diff` does not mark which changes can affect running requests; the Publish dialog does not need that in the first build.

`diagram`, `sampleRequest` and `removedNames` are ignored. How many requests still run on each version is a server read (`authoring-api.md`, `VersionSummary.openRequests`).

## 12. `compile` (the server's publish; Try it; the frontend need not call it)

```ts
function compile(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue, options?: CompileOptions): CompileResult;

interface CompileOptions {
  mode?: "publish" | "tryIt";   // default "publish"
  workflow?: string;            // the server's workflow ID (definition-format.md section 2); default "draft"
  version?: number;             // the version being published; default 1
  compiler?: string;            // the core version that compiles it; default "core"
}
type CompileResult =
  | { ok: true; published: Published; findings: Finding[]; unfinished: Unfinished[] }
  | { ok: false; findings: Finding[] };
interface Unfinished { location: Location; stage?: string }   // the blocking To do, and the engine stage a request that gets there is stuck in; no stage for a binding
```

- **Publish mode**: the server's publish. A draft with a `todo` is refused (`ok: false`, the findings). Otherwise the result passes the shape check and the kernel publish check (section 14); one that does not is `compile.internal`. `findings` holds the Worth knowing ones; `unfinished` is `[]`.
- **Try it mode**: any draft `parse` accepts. A part with a To do that stops a request (section 4) is compiled to the unfinished shapes of `engine/design/compiler.md` section 13 and listed in `unfinished`. `findings` holds every finding. `ok: false` only for a workflow-level To do (`workflow.noStart`, `start.notOneTask`) or `compile.internal`. The kernel publish check is not run.
- The server fills `workflow`, `version` and `compiler` at publish.

`compile` is in the root entry (E-27), because Try it compiles drafts in the browser: `createTestHost` calls it in Try it mode. The frontend need not call it itself. `Published` holds the definition (with its `types` block and, when not empty, its `triggers`, `events` and `nobodyToAsk` blocks), the schemas and the origin map, in the published definition format (`engine/design/definition-format.md`, E-18, E-23). The compiler emits kernel elements directly (E-19). The rules the frontend can rely on:

- One authored stage becomes a chain of engine stages; compiler-added names are `<itemId>__<local>` (E-14). Authored IDs never contain `__`. Stage names and the chain's shape are fixed in `engine/design/compiler.md` before anything is published (E-20).
- Value IDs are the data paths, button IDs the outcome IDs, task IDs the wait IDs, status IDs the status IDs (E-14). A rename changes nothing published.
- Every compiled element, and where needed each field of it, has an origin entry naming the authored item and part (E-18). An element's key is `<kind>:<ID>`; a single field's key is `<element key>#<JSON Pointer>` into the element (E-23). Every location in this contract comes from that map.
- Every task compiles to a person wait with role `obligation` (R8). Format 0 has no optional task.
- Each outcome carries `lookups`, one per answer from the directory or a data source: `{ property, connection, source, inputs, storedField, labelField, answer: "item" | "person" }` (E-20, E-23). The act-time lookup reads only the definition, never the authored form.
- **Nobody to ask** (E-23). The definition's `nobodyToAsk` block holds one rule per task. For every task whose who-is-asked may hold a group, a membership read `<task>__members` (a read call with `onFailure: outcome`) is opened beside the task in the task's own engine stage. A task whose who-is-asked can hold only people (by kind, through every "If empty, use") gets no read, and its rule names no read (`members: null`) (E-32). A formula there may give a group, so it counts as one that may. The tasks step leaves by an explicit condition that every task is answered, never by "otherwise", so the pending read cannot hold it; leaving the step cancels the read, which is dropped quietly, because a read cannot act outside (E-24). "People in [group]" under "Who is asked" asks the group itself; no separate directory read is made for it, so Retry for nobody-to-ask always reads the group again (E-24). Who can answer is section 8's. The built-in notification rules are `n_task` (`task.assigned`) and `n_stopped` on `Stuck` (`request.stuck`, with the reason) for every reason; Try it's outbox leaves out the `unfinished` one (section 10.3).
- A `members` step or an "is in" a group test inside a condition is a separate recorded read call in its own engine stage, placed just before the step that uses it (E-23), so it sees a group saved earlier in the same section.
- After-response actions run before the arrows are checked (E-22). If no arrow fits, they have already run and the request is stuck with `nothing-fits`.
- Within one stage, when two tasks fill the same value, the later task in the document wins (E-23).
- "When the stage is entered again" is written out explicitly, from the author's `ifStageEntersAgain` or the catalogue's `onRepeat` (E-14, R7). "Once" compiles to the explicit idempotency key `'once.' + request.id + '.' + <action ID>`, not `keyScope: request`, because a stage emitted twice would otherwise act twice; "again" compiles to `keyScope: activation` (E-23).

## 13. Versions

```ts
interface CoreMeta {
  coreVersion: string;                                   // semver of engine/packages/core
  definitionFormatVersion: number;
  authoredFormatVersions: { min: number; max: number };
}
const meta: CoreMeta;
function upgrade(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow): AuthoredWorkflow;   // to authoredFormatVersions.max; pure
```

- Every server response carries `Engine-Core-Version` and `Engine-Definition-Format` headers.
- The browser's `coreVersion` must equal the server's exactly. On a mismatch the editor marks its findings and Try it as possibly out of date and asks for a reload; saving still works; publishing is refused with `core-version-mismatch`. Cheap to relax.
- A draft is stored in its authored format and upgraded when read. `upgrade` is built; while there is one authored format it returns the document unchanged (E-31).

## 14. The package's two entries (E-26)

The package has two entries, because the contract surface and the kernel share names with different meanings (`Status`, `ValueKind`, `MessagePart`, `TurnResult`), so one root cannot hold both:

| Entry | Holds | Who imports it |
|---|---|---|
| `@workflow/core` | The contract surface: every function and type of this file (sections 2 to 13), `compile` included (E-27), with the authored-format types (`authored-format.ts`) and the catalogue types (`catalogue.ts`), as types only. | The frontend (only this one), the server |
| `@workflow/core/kernel` | The stored formats (the published definition, `engine/design/definition-format.md`, and the event types, `engine/design/event-payloads.md`), `decide`, `evolve`, the turn function (validate, `decide`, `evolve`, the stuck check, exported on its own so the server and the hosts run the same code), the `jsonschema-1` schema validator, the kernel publish check, the stuck state and the `nobodyToAsk` matcher, the notification and outbound-event matchers, the in-memory host, and the call-result check. | The server and the hosts |

The kernel entry's values, as built: the stored formats' `EVENT_TYPES`, `INPUT_EVENT_TYPES`, `VALUE_KINDS` and `validateDefinitionShape`; the schema validator `validateBySchema`, `checkSchemaProfile` and `SchemaProfileError`; the kernel `decide`, `evolve`, `EvolveError`, `emptyState`, `fold`, `lookupsToMake`, `lookupInputs`, `isWaitOpen`, `sameWait`, `turn` and `validateCallResult`; the publish check `checkDefinition`, `PUBLISH_CHECKS` (every code with its meaning) and `PUBLISH_WARNINGS` (the codes that do not stop publishing); the stuck state `stuckStateOf`, `nobodyToAsk` and `authoredStageOf` (the one mapper from an engine stage to the authored stage a stuck request is reported in, section 8); the matchers `matchNotifications`, `outboundEvents` and `outboundEventId`; and the in-memory host `createMemoryHost`. With them, the types of the stored formats and of each function.

**What the server shares with the views and the test host** (E-31, E-32). The server needs these too, so core exports them rather than the server copying them:

```ts
// The root, @workflow/core
function refusalOf(published: PublishedVersion, refusal: KernelRefusal, context?: RefusalContext): Refusal;   // a kernel refusal as section 2.6 reports it
interface RefusalContext { element?: string; button?: string; answers?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> }   // the person wait acted on, the button, the answers sent
function buttonStates(published: PublishedVersion, of: ButtonStatesOf, viewer: Viewer): ButtonState[];       // a viewer's button states, before any answer
type ButtonStatesOf = { form: "start"; at: string } | { form: "task"; events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]; task: TaskInstanceId };
interface Viewer { as?: Ref; isAdmin: boolean; groupsOf?: (user: string) => readonly string[] | undefined }
function blankWorkflow(options?: BlankOptions): AuthoredWorkflow;   // the blank workflow a new draft holds (authoring-api.md operation 2)
interface BlankOptions { id?: WorkflowId }                          // the document's own ID; default "wf_new"
function upgrade(workflow: AuthoredWorkflow): AuthoredWorkflow;     // section 13
// Draft: the type of authoring-api.md section 3, field for field; ApiErrorParams["stale-revision"].draft is a Draft

// The kernel entry, @workflow/core/kernel
function lookupInputs(
  def: PublishedDefinition, state: RequestState, element: string, outcome: string, property: string, data: JsonObject,
  request?: { id: string; by: By; at: string },
): { ok: true; inputs: JsonObject } | { ok: false; refusals: KernelRefusal[] } | undefined;   // a lookup's inputs before its answer is given
function isWaitOpen(state: RequestState, id: WaitId): boolean;
function sameWait(a: WaitId, b: WaitId): boolean;
```

`KernelRefusal`, `AnyEventRecord`, `PublishedDefinition`, `RequestState`, `WaitId`, `JsonObject` and the kernel's `By` are the kernel entry's. `ButtonStatesOf`'s `at` is the time a start would run at, in the events' form, because a `may` rule may read `request.at`. `lookupInputs` answers undefined when the outcome has no lookup for that property.

**Names at the root** (E-27). Where the contract files share a name, the root keeps one meaning for it and gives the other a new name:

| Name at the root | Is | The other meaning, renamed |
|---|---|---|
| `DirectoryRef` | the authored format's `{ directoryId, name }` | the catalogue's `{ type, id }` is `CatalogueDirectoryRef` (and `Ref` in this file) |
| `Json` | this file's (section 2.2), which never holds `null` | the catalogue's, which may, is `CatalogueJson` |
| `TurnResult` | this file's (section 2.6), a Try it turn's result | the kernel's turn function's result is `TurnResult` in `@workflow/core/kernel` only |
| `PublishedVersion` | section 8's `{ definition, source, catalogue }` | `Published` is `compile`'s published definition (section 12) |

The authored-format and catalogue types are exported as types only; the frontend takes their constants (`ITEM_KINDS`, `WORDS` ...) from its own copy of the contract files.

**The kernel publish check.**

```ts
function checkDefinition(definition: PublishedDefinition, catalogue?: object): PublishProblem[];   // [] when it may be published
const PUBLISH_CHECKS: { readonly [code in PublishCode]: string };   // each code with a one-line meaning, for developers
const PUBLISH_WARNINGS: ReadonlySet<PublishCode>;                  // the codes of severity "warning"; every other code is an error
interface PublishProblem {
  code: PublishCode;                  // kebab-case; the list is PUBLISH_CHECKS in the kernel entry
  severity: "error" | "warning";
  pointer: string;                    // RFC 6901 pointer into the definition
  params: { [name: string]: Json };
}
```

- `catalogue` is typed `object` in the kernel entry, because that entry takes nothing from the contract surface where the `Catalogue` type lives; the caller passes the contract's `Catalogue` (`catalogue.ts`).
- A definition may be published when no problem has severity `error`; a `warning` does not stop it (E-27). The one warning is spec section 6's write call that a root transition can interrupt, which format 1 cannot reach.
- The checks that need the catalogue (a lookup's entry and fields, `types.results` against the catalogue's entries, a membership read on the catalogue's `directoryConnection`, the bindings' triggers) run only when the catalogue is given. They are built with the server (E-27).
- **The call-result check.** A call result is checked against its operation's declared shape before the turn, by this one function, which both the server's call job and the in-memory host use. `decide` trusts its caller for that, as the spec says. A result holding a key that starts with `$` does not fit. It covers what the definition knows, the result's shape (E-27). That an await gave a job reference and that a failure code is one the operation declares are checked by the server, which has the catalogue.
- The stuck state, the `nobodyToAsk` matcher and the notification and outbound-event matchers are not for the frontend. The kernel entry's shapes may change between minor versions.

## 15. Notes on the decisions

- **Close for any open request; Retry only where it can help.** E-23 settles both: Close is offered for any open request, stuck or not, because a request whose outside job never reports back could otherwise never be ended (an open call never makes a request stuck, spec section 3); Retry is offered only for `action-failed` and `nobody-to-ask`.
- **E-7's "one piece of prose"** is narrower than the decisions around it: the other system's failure text and the engine's error text reach the people who look after stuck requests (under `admin`), and a rendered Notify message carries the author's words. None of them is engine prose written for a screen. This draft treats E-7 as "the engine writes no prose for a screen".
- **`connection`, not `connector`,** for a call wait's field and `by.type`. This contract uses `connection` (E-17), as kernel spec v2.20, whose copy is in `engine/spec/`, does.
- **A person value is `{ type, id }` (E-20).** The final formats (`engine/design/definition-format.md`, `engine/design/event-payloads.md`) and the samples in `contract/fixtures/catalogue.json` follow it; values are kept for ever.
- **The inbound answer's `check` carries `{ button }`,** as everywhere else (`runtime-api.md` section 8): a check ID is a compiled element, which E-7 keeps out of every report. `engine/spec/integrations.md` section 9.8 now says the same.

## 16. Open points

1. The origin map must resolve a field to an authored part, for `stuck` locations and `admin` detail (`runtime-api.md` section 10).
2. Test-host state cannot be saved or shared. Cheap to add as an export of each request's events.
3. Known limits, left as built (E-26, E-27): `check` on very large workflows with many tasks per stage and chained send-backs is above the 50 ms target (realistic 60-stage workflows take about 18 ms in Node; not yet measured in a browser); the root entry is about 139 KB gzipped. A value filled only by a formula has a kind in `check` and `facts`. A multiple choice whose choices come from a formula has the kind `multipleChoice`, with items of the formula's item kind; where the items have no value kind, the value has no kind and only the choice check guards the answer (E-28).
4. E-29 gives a `failureCode` constant that is not one of the value's codes, or that is used on another value, "the same finding as a button constant naming another task's button". No finding exists for that button constant: `check` accepts it and the clause is never true. Both wait for that finding's code to be chosen (section 4, "Constants on the right of a clause").

Settled by E-29, E-31 and E-32: a saved failure code is a choice (`{ failureCode }`); `upgrade` and the server's shared functions are at the root; `not-found` names a `path`; the test host takes a time per call; `arrow.neverUsed` names its `covering` arrows; typed-in choices with none are `item.partMissing`; `unfinished` is told to nobody; `request.ended@1` names the ending; the why of an arrow reads list cells; `diff` names the deepest part; `Draft` is core's.

Settled by E-28: `diff` is built, with the readings of section 11; `not-found` names a `call`; `wait-not-open`'s params from the kernel; a task with no "Who is asked", a missing choices and a list with no rows do not stop Try it; the authored stage of a stuck request (section 8); `has()` on a chip.

Settled since the last Draft 3 (E-27): the shapes of `compile`, `requestView`, `story` and `sampleValues` as built; `FormState.invalid`; the IDs `t<seq>` and `<request>.c<seq>`; the names at the root; `checkDefinition` with an optional catalogue and a severity per problem; `action.failureNotRead`; `formula.notInProfile` `reservedKey`; an empty multiple choice is `too-short`. Earlier: a formula can give a date (`asDate`, applied by the compiler, E-23); Retry is not offered for `nothing-fits` or `error` (E-23); `Faulted.error.params` carries `{ error, key?, index? }`, with `key` and `index` taken from the expression module's fields (E-26); `days(n)`, `asDate(t)` and the refusal of `\p` and `\P` are built (section 6.4); `arrow.neverUsed` is a To do and an empty "when" or "only when" is never "always true" (E-25).

/**
 * Asking several people at once (portfolio page 10, editor-model.md section 3 "Several tasks in
 * one stage"): the Change request demo with Domain approval given a second task, "Security
 * review", asked of the Security team at the same time. Everything else is the demo, reused.
 * Source of several-at-once.authored.json (emitted complete, not abbreviated).
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, WorkingStage } from "../../authored-format";
import { changeRequest } from "./change-request.authored";

const wf: AuthoredWorkflow = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(changeRequest));
wf.id = "wf_change_request_several";

const da = wf.stages.find((s) => s.id === "st_domain_approval") as WorkingStage;

// The first task now has a name of its own, after who is asked.
da.tasks[0].name = "Domain approvers";

// The second task, asked at the same time.
da.tasks.push({
  id: "tk_security_review",
  name: "Security team",
  whoIsAsked: { group: { directoryId: "dir-group-security-team", name: "Security team" } },
  groupRule: "firstAnswerDecides",
  requesterCanAnswer: false,
  form: {
    pages: [
      {
        id: "pg_security_review_1",
        items: [
          { type: "text", id: "tx_sec_the_request", content: [{ value: "v_title" }, "\n", { value: "v_description" }, "\nRisk: ", { value: "v_risk" }] },
          { type: "question", id: "q_security_notes", label: "Security notes", kind: "longText", savedAs: "v_security_notes" },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  buttons: [
    { id: "btn_sec_approve", label: "Approve", look: "primary", neededToPress: [] },
    { id: "btn_sec_reject", label: "Reject", look: "danger", neededToPress: ["q_security_notes"] },
  ],
  savesButtonPressedAs: "v_sec_button_pressed",
});

// Notify Requester when either task rejects.
da.afterTheyRespond = [
  {
    id: "act_notify_requester_rejected",
    type: "notify",
    to: { request: "requester" },
    message: ["Your change request was rejected"],
    onlyWhen: { anyOf: [{ pressed: "btn_da_reject" }, { pressed: "btn_sec_reject" }] },
  },
];

// Arrows, rewritten for two tasks. Checked from the top; the first one that fits is used.
da.arrows = [
  {
    // "When Domain approvers press Reject or Security team presses Reject go to Rejected"
    id: "ar_da_reject",
    when: { type: "condition", condition: { anyOf: [{ pressed: "btn_da_reject" }, { pressed: "btn_sec_reject" }] } },
    goTo: "st_rejected",
    goAsSoonAsTrue: true,
  },
  {
    // "When Domain approvers press Request changes go to Request form" (checked once both answered)
    id: "ar_da_request_changes",
    when: { type: "buttonPressed", button: "btn_da_request_changes" },
    goTo: "st_request_form",
  },
  // The editor asks for this, because the buttons can combine in many ways.
  { id: "ar_da_other", when: { type: "inAllOtherCases" }, goTo: "st_create_jira_issue" },
];

wf.values.push(
  { id: "v_security_notes", name: "Security notes" },
  { id: "v_sec_button_pressed", name: "Security review: button pressed" },
);
wf.sampleRequest!.answers.v_sec_button_pressed = { button: "btn_sec_approve" };

# What the frontend needs from the engine side

Draft 1, 2026-11-15, frontend session. This is the consumer's side of contract parts B, C and D (see `doc-plan.md`, section 5). It says what each screen must be able to ask. The Engine owner decides the shapes; names here are placeholders.

Words: *doc* is a draft in the authored workflow format (part A). A *location* is a path of authored-format IDs (stage, task, question, button, action, arrow) plus a field name. Nothing here refers to the compiled definition.

## Rules the frontend relies on

1. **Codes, not words.** Every check result, refusal and explanation is a code + location + parameters. The frontend owns every sentence a person reads.
2. **Locations are in the authored format.**
3. **Same answer in the editor, in Try it and live.** A condition, a check or a "who is asked" must give the same result in all three, because the author is promised that Try it shows what will happen.
4. **Fast enough to run on every edit.** The check and the facts below run after each change. In the browser this should feel instant; over a network it must tolerate being a few edits behind (results carry the revision they were computed for).
5. **A draft may be incomplete** and must still be checkable, explainable and (as far as it goes) tryable.

## B. Authoring

| The editor needs to | Call (placeholder) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| List workflows with their state | `listWorkflows()` | Per workflow: name, live version or none, draft changed when and by whom, number of To do items, open requests, stuck requests, what I may do. |
| Create a workflow | `createWorkflow(name)` | Returns the blank draft. |
| Open and save a draft | `getDraft(id)`, `saveDraft(id, doc, revision)` | Whole-document save with a revision; a stale save is refused with the newer doc. One author at a time in the first version. |
| Show To do and Worth knowing | `check(doc)` | Items: code, severity (to do / worth knowing), location, parameters, related locations. Whether Publish is allowed. |
| Fill the value picker and the Values tab | `facts(doc)` | For each value: its kind or a kind conflict, where it is filled, where it is used. For each point in the workflow (a stage's sections, an arrow, a question): which values exist there and whether each is always filled, may be empty (with the path that skips it), or is not filled yet. |
| Draw the diagram's marks | `facts(doc)` | For each stage: reached from, whether any request can reach it. For each arrow: whether it can ever be used, and whether an earlier arrow always wins. |
| Offer the right words in the condition builder | static | The closed list of value kinds and, per kind, the operators (words) a condition may use. Part of the contract, not a call. |
| Check a formula as it is typed | `checkFormula(doc, location, text, expectedKind)` | Kind it gives; errors as code + character range + parameters; its result for the sample request. |
| Show "for the sample: Payments" next to anything | `evaluate(doc, expression, sampleRequest)` | The value of any expression, including who-is-asked resolved to names, and steps into lists and the directory. |
| Try it | `startTry(doc, answers)` then the same calls as the runtime API on a test request | Extra: act as any person; for every move, why (which arrow was used, which earlier arrows did not fit and what they read); an outbox of what would have been sent (messages, calls to connections with their inputs, the faked results); run again with other answers. Nothing leaves the platform. Works on an incomplete draft until it reaches the unfinished part, then says where it stopped. |
| Publish | `publish(id, revision)` | Returns the version, or the To do items that block it. |
| Show what changed since the live version | `changes(id)` | Structured changes (stage added, arrow now goes to..., question removed) as codes; number of requests still running on each older version. |
| Know who may edit and publish | part of `listWorkflows`/`getDraft` | Flags only. |

## C. Runtime (the pages people who use a workflow see)

| The page needs to | Call (placeholder) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Show a start form | `startForm(workflowId)` | The version, the first stage's form in authored-form terms, and what a signed-in person may start. |
| Start a request | `startRequest(workflowId, version, button, answers)` | Returns the request, or refusals by question. |
| Show my tasks | `myTasks()` | Request, workflow, stage, task, since when. |
| Show a request | `getRequest(id)` | Status (id and label), workflow and version, where it is now, open tasks (who is asked as names, whether I may answer, the form with any earlier answers, each button enabled or not with the reason code), values a viewer may see, history as structured entries (who, which button, moved from and to, what was done), and if I look after stuck requests: why it is stuck. |
| Answer a task | `act(requestId, taskId, button, answers)` | Returns ok, or refusals by question. |
| Keep a form honest while typing | client-side if rule 3 can be met in the browser; otherwise `previewTask(requestId, taskId, answers)` | Which questions show, which buttons are enabled. |
| List requests | `listRequests(filter)` | By workflow, status, stuck, mine. |
| Unstick a request | `retry(requestId, reason)`, `close(requestId, reason)` | Only for the people in "Stuck requests go to" and platform admins. |
| Stay current | polling in the first version | After acting, and when the page regains focus. |

## D. Catalogue

| The editor needs to | Call (placeholder) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Offer actions, data and (once designed) starts and outbound events | `listConnections()` | Per connection: name, whether it is set up, and its operations. Per operation: id and version, what it is for (does something / gives data / starts or moves a request / tells another system), input fields (id, label, kind, required, allowed choices), result fields (id, label, kind), a sample result for Try it and for the editor's examples, and a plain failure code set. |
| Pick people and groups | `searchPeople(q)`, `searchGroups(q)`, `lookup(refs)` | References are `{type, id}`; the frontend needs display names, and members of a group for samples. |

## Open on the frontend side

- Whether the check, facts, formula check, evaluate and Try it run in the browser from a shared package, or behind calls. The frontend is written against an async interface either way.
- How a question's choices that come from a connection are fetched when a real person fills in the form (needs a runtime call that is not in the table yet).
