# Contract part C: the runtime API (server)

Draft 3, engine owner, 2026-11-15. Replaces Draft 2. Pending the frontend owner's review and the product owner's review.
Revised 2026-11-15 after E-21 to E-26, and 2026-11-16 after E-27, E-28, E-31 and E-33.

What the pages people use (start a request, my tasks, a task, a request's page, request lists, retry and close, refused starts) read and send, plus the development host's session and directory reads and the inbound endpoint for other systems (door 1). The frontend builds every page and owns every sentence. Written against kernel spec v2.20, whose copy is in `engine/spec/`, and against its data model and `integrations.md`, and decisions E-1 to E-33. Every shared type (`Result`, `ApiError`, `Refusal`, `Location`, `Ref`, `By`, `Caller`, `Answers`, `Values`, `ButtonState`, `OpenTask`, `RequestView`, `Stuck`, `StoryEntry`, `KnownLookups`, `ChoiceOption` ...) is defined in `core-api.md` (sections 2, 6.2, 8, 9 and 10) and not repeated here. Value JSON: `core-api.md` section 2.4. Error codes, HTTP statuses and params: `core-api.md` section 2.6. How codes are spelled: `core-api.md` section 1.1.

Not here: drafts, publish and settings (`authoring-api.md`); the check, form state and Try it (`core-api.md`, which runs Try it on the core's in-memory host with the same shapes and refusal codes).

## 1. Conventions

### 1.1 The interface

```ts
interface RuntimeApi {
  // 3. start
  listStartable(caller: Caller): Promise<Result<StartableWorkflow[]>>;
  startForm(caller: Caller, args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version?: VersionNumber }): Promise<Result<StartForm>>;
  start(caller: Caller, args: StartArgs): Promise<Result<StartResult>>;
  choices(caller: Caller, args: ChoicesArgs): Promise<Result<ChoicesPage>>;
  // 4. tasks
  myTasks(caller: Caller, args: PageArgs): Promise<Result<MyTasksPage>>;
  getTask(caller: Caller, args: { requestId: RequestId; task: TaskInstanceId }): Promise<Result<TaskView>>;
  act(caller: Caller, args: ActArgs): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  // 5. stuck requests, bindings and refused starts
  retry(caller: Caller, args: AdminArgs): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  close(caller: Caller, args: AdminArgs): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  listBindings(caller: Caller, args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId }): Promise<Result<BindingState[]>>;
  setBindingPaused(caller: Caller, args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; binding: StartsWhenId; paused: boolean }): Promise<Result<BindingChanged>>;
  listPausedDeliveries(caller: Caller, args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; binding: StartsWhenId }): Promise<Result<PausedDelivery[]>>;
  listRefusedStarts(caller: Caller, args: { workflow?: ServerWorkflowId } & PageArgs): Promise<Result<Page<RefusedStart>>>;
  retryRefusedStart(caller: Caller, args: { id: RefusedStartId }): Promise<Result<RetriedStart>>;
  // 6. reads
  publishedSource(caller: Caller, args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber }): Promise<Result<PublishedSource>>;
  listRequests(caller: Caller, args: RequestQuery): Promise<Result<Page<RequestRow>>>;
  getRequest(caller: Caller, args: GetRequestArgs): Promise<Result<RequestView>>;
}

interface PageArgs { cursor?: string; limit?: number }   // limit: default 50, at most 200; a larger limit is taken as 200 (E-31)
interface Page<T> { items: T[]; next?: string }           // next absent: the last page
```

- **Functions are the contract; HTTP is a transport.** The handler parses the request, asks the host for the `Caller`, calls the function and maps the `Result`. It adds no rule. The frontend's client omits `caller`. The same functions can be called in process from the existing application (E-11).
- **HTTP.** Paths are relative to `{base}` (development host: `/api/workflow/v1`; in the existing application: unknown: depends on the existing application). Success: the status in each operation's HTTP line, the value as the body. Failure: the first error's status and `{ "errors": ApiError[] }`. Every response carries `Engine-Core-Version` and `Engine-Definition-Format`. Request bodies: JSON, at most 256 KiB. A path or method that neither this API nor the authoring API has answers `404 not-found` with `what: "path"`, in the usual error body with the engine's headers (E-31).
- **No caller:** `401 unauthenticated`, from the handler, before any function runs. The engine trusts the host's `Caller` and records `by: { type: "user", id: caller.user }`. It never reads a user from a header or a body. Group memberships are looked up live where a rule needs them.
- **JSON.** No `null`, except in the inbound answer (section 8). Timestamps per `core-api.md` section 2.2. Every code list is open.

### 1.2 Words

| This file | Kernel spec | Authored format |
|---|---|---|
| task (instance) | person wait (instance) | task |
| button | outcome | button |
| action | call wait | action (`useConnection`) |
| arrow | transition | arrow |
| value | data path | value |
| stuck, with a reason | `Faulted`, the match of the `nobodyToAsk` block, or nothing that fits, worked out from the state (E-19, E-20, E-23, E-33) | stuck |
| people who look after stuck requests | workflow admins | "Stuck requests go to" (settings) |
| binding | trigger binding | "Starts when" |

## 2. Who may do what

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| Start any workflow with a published version; read every request, task and published source, including that a request is stuck and its reason; list requests; my tasks; choices | Any signed-in user (data model section 5, E-19). |
| Answer a task | A person among its recorded `askedOf`, directly or through a group they belong to now, for whom the task's rule allows it (`requesterCanAnswer`). |
| See the stuck detail (`Stuck.admin`, `OpenAction.admin`); retry a stuck request; close an open request; pause or resume a binding and list its paused deliveries; list refused starts and run one again | Platform admins and the workflow's people who look after stuck requests (`Settings.stuckRequestsGoTo`, absent: the authors), groups looked up live (E-19, E-21). Others: `not-admin` for the actions; the detail is left out; a refused-start list holds only the workflows the caller looks after. |

## 3. Start

### 3.1 Startable workflows

```ts
interface StartableWorkflow { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; name: string; highestVersion: VersionNumber }
```

`GET {base}/workflows/startable` -> `200 StartableWorkflow[]`, ordered by name. Every workflow with a published version. `name` is the settings name (`authoring-api.md`). Errors: none beyond the common ones.

### 3.2 The start form

```ts
interface StartForm {
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;          // send it back with start
  name: string;
  stage: StageId;                  // the start stage
  task: TaskId;                    // the start task
  buttonStates: ButtonState[];     // for the caller, before any answer
}
```

`GET {base}/workflows/{workflow}/start-form[?version=n]` -> `200 StartForm`. Absent `version`: the highest. Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`).

- The form, its buttons and its words come from `publishedSource` for that version (cached for ever). The page runs `core.formState(source, catalogue, { item: task }, answers, {}, { requester: me })`. A start-form condition cannot use the directory (`start.directoryInCondition` is a To do), so a published start form never answers `needsLookups`.
- Choices from the directory or a data source come from `choices` (3.4), as on a task.
- `buttonStates` holds only `may` refusals. Who is asked is not checked at start (spec section 2, Start).

### 3.3 Start a request

```ts
interface StartArgs {
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version?: VersionNumber;         // the version whose form was shown; absent: the highest
  button: ButtonId;
  answers: Answers;
  clientToken: string;             // 1 to 64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; made when the form is opened
}
interface StartResult {
  requestId: RequestId;
  readableId: ReadableId;
  version: VersionNumber;
  lastSeq: Seq;
  stopped: boolean;                // the request is stuck after the start turn, for any reason; the request exists
  replayed: boolean;               // this token had already started this request
}
```

`POST {base}/requests` body `StartArgs` -> `201 StartResult` (`200` when `replayed`).

- **Version.** Any published version can be started, so a publish while someone fills in the form rejects nothing.
- **Client token.** One `(starter, clientToken)` starts at most one request. The start turn writes the token and the hash of the arguments on the new request's row, in its own transaction. Same token and same arguments: the first request, `replayed: true`. Same token, other arguments (hash of the canonical JSON of `workflow`, `version` as sent, `button`, `answers`): `client-token-reused`. A refused start writes no request, so the person can fix the form and send again with the same token.
- **Requester.** The caller. An answer key that is not a question of the start form, `requester` included, is `invalid-data` / `unknown-question` (E-17: only a connection may supply the Requester).

Refusals, in this order; the first failing step decides; a list holds every failure of that step:

| # | Step | Codes | Attempt (logged) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shape | `invalid-body`, `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`), `unknown-button` | No |
| 2 | Client token | `client-token-reused` (or the replay) | No |
| 3 | Kernel reason 3 | `may`, `rule-error` | Yes |
| 4 | Kernel reason 4 | `invalid-data` (the outcome's schema) | Yes |
| 5 | Choice lookups (door 5, E-20) | `source-unavailable`; `choice-unknown` | `source-unavailable`: No. `choice-unknown`: Yes |
| 6 | Kernel reason 5 | `check`, `rule-error`, and `invalid-data` for form rules the compiler enforces as checks (`core-api.md` section 7.2) | Yes |

`wait-not-open`, `not-assignee` and the actor's membership lookup do not apply at start. The choice lookups are made before the start turn's transaction begins, and their results are applied at step 5 (E-23). A start turn that becomes stuck after it is accepted is not a refusal: the request exists, `stopped: true`.

### 3.4 Choices from the directory or a data source (door 5)

```ts
interface ChoicesArgs {
  form:
    | { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber }     // the start form
    | { requestId: RequestId; task: TaskInstanceId };            // a task
  question: QuestionId;
  answers: Answers;            // the form as filled so far
  search?: string;             // filters on the label; passed to a source only when it is searchable
  cursor?: string;
  limit?: number;              // default 50, at most 100; a larger limit is taken as 100 (E-31)
}
interface ChoicesPage { choices: ChoiceOption[]; next?: string }
```

`POST {base}/choices` body `ChoicesArgs` -> `200 ChoicesPage`.

This section is the one statement of the choices call's shape (E-23); `core-api.md` (`TestHost.choices`) and `engine/spec/integrations.md` section 11.2 cite it. One call for every question whose choices come from the directory (`from: "directory"`) or a data source (`from: "source"`), on the start form and on a task alike (E-20). The page names the question, never the source (E-17). The server reads the question from the stored version and works out what to list from it, the request's values (for a task; `{}` on the start form) and `answers`:

| Question's choices | What is listed | `ChoiceOption.value` | `label` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from: "source"` | The source's `list` with the question's `inputs`; an input whose expression is empty is left out; a required input left out gives `choices: []` | `{ stored, label }`, from the question's `storedField` and `labelField`; an item without either is dropped | the item's label |
| `from: "directory"` | The members now of the group `peopleIn` gives, read live through the group-members data source (`groupMembers@1`) of the connection the catalogue names as `directoryConnection` (`engine/spec/integrations.md` section 8.7) | `{ type: "user", id }` | the person's display name |

- Directory choices are a data source like any other (E-20): the same call, cache, lookup and refusals.
- Typed-in and list choices come from the document; formula choices from `core.formState` (`core-api.md` section 7).
- Not recorded. Lists are cached for the entry's `cacheSeconds`.
- Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`, `request`, `task`, `question`); `invalid-body` (`field: "/question"`, `problem: "format"`) when the question's choices come neither from the directory nor from a source; `wait-not-open` for a task that is not open; `source-unavailable` (503, try again).
- **When the person acts** (3.3 step 5, 4.3 step 10), each such answer is looked up again by its stored value with the same inputs (E-20): a source answer by `stored`, a directory answer by `id`. The label recorded for a source answer is the source's, whatever label the page sent; a person is recorded as `{ type: "user", id }` with no label. Not found: `choice-unknown`, an attempt. The source cannot be asked: `source-unavailable`; nothing changes and it is not an attempt. The page sends the `ChoiceOption.value` it was given.
- What was looked up and found is recorded in `WaitCompleted.evidence.lookups` (E-20).

## 4. Tasks

### 4.1 My tasks

```ts
interface MyTask {
  requestId: RequestId;
  readableId: ReadableId;
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;
  status?: Status;
  task: TaskInstanceId;
  location: Location;          // { item: TaskId }
  openedAt: Timestamp;
  via: Ref;                    // the caller, or the group through which they are asked
  mayAnswer: boolean;          // the task's rule for the caller; advisory
}
interface MyTasksPage extends Page<MyTask> { groupsUnavailable?: true }
```

`GET {base}/my-tasks?cursor=&limit=` -> `200 MyTasksPage`, oldest first.

- Open tasks whose recorded `askedOf` names the caller or a group they belong to now (spec section 7, action-item list). Only obligations are listed (person waits with role `obligation`, which every authored task compiles to): an option, which authored format 0 cannot make, would show on the request page only (spec section 7, E-31).
- A task the caller is asked but may not answer (their own request with "The requester can't answer") is not listed, as they are not told about it either (E-33). `mayAnswer` stays: it is false only when the task's rule could not be worked out for the caller (`rule-error`).
- The directory cannot be reached: tasks asking the caller directly only, and `groupsUnavailable: true`.

### 4.2 A task

```ts
interface TaskView {
  requestId: RequestId;
  readableId: ReadableId;
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;         // the version the request runs on; its form is that version's
  task: TaskInstanceId;
  authoredTask: TaskId;
  stage: StageId;
  state: "open" | "completed" | "cancelled" | "skipped";
  openedAt: Timestamp;
  askedOf: Ref[];                 // as recorded when it opened; may be empty
  values: Values;                 // the request's values now
  requester?: Ref;
  startedOn: string;              // YYYY-MM-DD
  lookups: KnownLookups;          // the group members recorded by the read placed just before this task's step; what the form's conditions read (E-20, E-23)
  completed?: { by: By; at: Timestamp; button: ButtonId; answers: Answers; asMemberOf: Ref[] };
  earlierAnswers?: Answers;       // answers to the same task the last time it was asked in this request
  buttonStates: ButtonState[];    // for the caller, before any answer
  lastSeq: Seq;
}
```

`GET {base}/requests/{requestId}/tasks/{task}` -> `200 TaskView`, `ETag` (9.3). Errors: `not-found` (`request`, `task`).

- Works for a task in any state, so old links open read-only.
- The form, buttons and words come from `publishedSource` for `version`. The page runs `core.formState(source, catalogue, { item: authoredTask }, answers, values, { requester, startedOn }, lookups)`. With `lookups` the form's conditions never need a directory call, and they read what the act's checks read. `lookups` is `{}` when the form has no condition that uses the directory.
- Choices from the directory or a data source come from `choices` (3.4); they are read live and checked when the person acts.
- `earlierAnswers` lets the form start from the last answers after a send-back. Earlier activations are invisible to conditions but are in history, and only the engine folds history.
- `buttonStates` hold the viewer-level refusals: `wait-not-open`, `membership-unavailable`, `not-assignee`, `may`. The caller's groups may be cached for 60 s for this only; the act always looks them up.

### 4.3 Act

```ts
interface ActArgs { requestId: RequestId; task: TaskInstanceId; button: ButtonId; answers: Answers }
interface TurnDone {
  requestId: RequestId;
  lastSeq: Seq;
  stopped: boolean;               // the request is stuck after this turn, for any reason (it may already have been; the answer is still recorded)
}
```

`POST {base}/requests/{requestId}/tasks/{task}/act` body `{ button, answers }` -> `200 TurnDone`.

One call is one turn (spec section 3). The steps run in this order (E-23). Steps 1 to 3 run without the request's lock; steps 4 to 11 run under it. The first failing step decides; a list holds every failure of that step:

| # | Step | Lock | Codes | Attempt (logged) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shape | No | `invalid-body`, `not-found` (`request`, `task`), `unknown-button` | No |
| 2 | Kernel reason 1, checked from an unlocked read of the request | No | `wait-not-open` (with how it ended) | Yes |
| 3 | The lookups (doors 4 and 5): the actor's groups, when the task's recorded `askedOf` holds a group; then, for each answer from the directory or a data source that fits the outcome's schema, a lookup by its stored value, with inputs worked out from the same unlocked read | No | none here: each result, or the failure to get it, is held for step 6 or step 10 | |
| 4 | Lock | Taken | `busy` (not obtained in 5 s) | No |
| 5 | Kernel reason 1 again | Held | `wait-not-open` (with how it ended) | Yes |
| 6 | The membership result | Held | `membership-unavailable` | No |
| 7 | Kernel reason 2 | Held | `not-assignee` | Yes |
| 8 | Kernel reason 3 | Held | `may`, `rule-error` | Yes |
| 9 | Kernel reason 4 | Held | `invalid-data` (the outcome's schema) | Yes |
| 10 | The choice lookup results (E-20) | Held | `source-unavailable`; `choice-unknown` | `source-unavailable`: No. `choice-unknown`: Yes |
| 11 | Kernel reason 5 | Held | `check`, `rule-error`, and `invalid-data` for form rules the compiler enforces as checks | Yes |

- **No outside call is made while a request is locked** (E-23). The lookups of step 3 are made after the unlocked check that the task is open, and the task is checked again under the lock (step 5). Their results are applied at their kernel step, so the refusal reported is still the first failing step in the kernel's order. A lookup failure changes nothing and writes nothing (E-17).
- An act on a task that is no longer open is answered `wait-not-open` at step 2 without any lookup, so it is answered so even while the directory or a source is down.
- The schema check of step 9 is pure; step 3 runs it on the unlocked read only to decide which answers to look up.
- What is recorded: the actor's groups as `WaitCompleted.evidence.memberOf`; each choice looked up in `evidence.lookups` (E-20); a source answer as `{ stored, label }` with the source's label in `WaitCompleted.data`. `decide` reads only what is recorded.
- `wait-not-open` carries `by` and `button` when the task was completed, so the page can tell "you already answered" from "someone else answered" or "it moved on". A double submit needs no token: the second call gets `wait-not-open` with the same `by`. A completed task says who completed it also after the request closed: `state: "completed"` wins over `requestClosed`, which is for any task not completed once the request is closed (E-27). The kernel gives `{state: "completed", by, outcome}`, and the server reports `outcome` as `button` (E-28).
- A task the request never opened is not one of its tasks: the shape step answers `not-found` (`task`). The kernel itself refuses an act on a wait the request never opened, or on a call wait, `unknown-wait`, not `wait-not-open` (spec v2.19, E-27, E-28); a caller of this API never sees that code (section 5.1).
- A stuck request still accepts the answer (spec section 3): `200` with `stopped: true`; it does not move until someone retries or closes it.

## 5. Stuck requests, bindings and refused starts

### 5.1 Retry and close

```ts
interface AdminArgs {
  requestId: RequestId;
  reason: string;                 // 1 to 2000 characters after trimming; recorded
  expectedLastSeq: Seq;           // the lastSeq of the page the person acted from
}
```

`POST {base}/requests/{requestId}/retry` and `POST {base}/requests/{requestId}/close`, body `{ reason, expectedLastSeq }` -> `200 TurnDone`.

Each is one admin turn (spec section 4), recorded as `Overridden { by, reason, actions }`. These are the only two admin actions (E-17, E-33).

| Operation | Offered for | Recorded actions | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| retry | A request stuck with `action-failed` or `nobody-to-ask` only (E-23). Not stuck: `not-stuck`. Stuck with `nothing-fits` or `error` (or `unfinished` in Try it): `not-retryable`. | `retry`: clears the fault, if any, and re-enters the active engine stage | Re-enters the engine stage that is stuck (E-19), per reason below. Then `decide` runs once. |
| close | Any open request, stuck or not (E-23) | `close` | Closed with no ending; open tasks cancelled; the stuck state ends. Outside jobs are not stopped; the results of writes and awaits are recorded late; reads are dropped (E-24). |

What Retry does, per reason:

| Reason | Retry | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `action-failed` | Offered | The failed action is tried again. Under "once" the call has the explicit key `'once.' + request.id + '.' + <action ID>`, so the connector is asked with the same key: a write whose key failed acts again, and an await starts a new job under that key. Under "again" (`keyScope: activation`) a new key is used. Actions of the authored stage before it are not repeated: only the engine stage where the request stopped is re-entered. This holds for every failed call, whatever added it, a directory read included (E-23). |
| `nobody-to-ask` | Offered | The task's engine stage is re-entered: the group is read again (`<task>__members`) and the stage's tasks are asked again, with who is asked worked out again from the request's values. "People in [group]" asks the group itself, so it is read again too (E-24). |
| `nothing-fits` | Not offered: Close only | Checking the same arrows over the same values gives the same result. |
| `error` | Not offered: Close only | After an error the request sits where its turn began, so running again repeats the same result, and could repeat an outside action that had already succeeded (E-23). |

Two limits of Retry (E-19):

- An empty value stays empty. Retry changes no value, so a request stuck on an empty value has Close as its only way out until values can be changed by hand.
- In a stage with several tasks, every task is asked again, including those already answered.

A call that is merely slow does not make a request stuck, so it cannot be retried: it is waited for, or the request is closed (E-20). This avoids starting a second outside job.

**Calls when a task or the request closes** (E-23, E-24). A write or await call that was sent at least once with no clear answer, whose wait then closes (by an arrow, a retry or a close), is kept and asked about, because it may have acted outside; each try writes a `call-outcome-unknown` log line, and nobody is told. Its eventual result is recorded late. A read call in that state, such as a task's membership read, is dropped quietly: no late result, because a read cannot act outside. A call never sent is dropped unsent.

Refusals, in order (E-31: who may act and the reason first, then `stale`, then the rest): `invalid-body`, `not-found` (`request`) (not logged); `membership-unavailable` when the caller's groups cannot be looked up and the caller is not a platform admin (not logged; the lookup is made before the lock, E-23); `busy` (not logged); `not-admin` (logged); `reason-required` (logged); `stale` with the current `lastSeq` (not logged); `request-closed` (logged); `not-stuck`, retry only (logged); `not-retryable`, retry only, with the reason (logged).

**The kernel refusal reasons E-26 named, and how a caller of this API meets each.** The server builds every kernel input itself, so most of them cannot reach a page:

| Kernel reason | What a caller sees |
|---|---|
| `unknown-outcome` | Never on its own: a button that is not the task's is refused `unknown-button` at the shape step, before the kernel runs. |
| `unknown-wait` | Never: a task that is not one of the request's, one the request never opened and an action's call included, is `not-found` (`task`) at the shape step. The kernel refuses an act on a wait the request never opened, or on a call wait, `unknown-wait`, before `wait-not-open` (E-27, E-28). |
| `already-started` | Never: the server makes a new request ID for every start, and a repeated start is the client token's replay (section 3.3). |
| `not-started` | Never: an act, retry or close on a request that does not exist is `not-found` (`request`). |
| `invalid-action` | Never: the server writes the actions, and `stale` catches a page that read an older stage. |

Where one of the "Never" rows happens anyway, it is a server bug: the call is answered `internal` and nothing is written.

### 5.2 Who is told

A live request has two built-in messages, `task.assigned` and `request.stuck` (E-21, E-33). `start.refused` exists only in Try it's outbox (`core-api.md` section 10.3); the server never sends it.

| Event | Message (`core-api.md` section 10.3) | To |
|---|---|---|
| A task opens | `task.assigned` | who is asked, less anyone who may not answer it (the Requester where the Requester can't answer) |
| A request becomes stuck, for any reason, `nobody-to-ask` included | `request.stuck`, with its `reason` | the people who look after stuck requests |

Words are in `contract/words/notifications.json`. Nothing else tells anyone: a refused start, an overdue or unknown call, and every other problem is a log line on the server (`engine/spec/integrations.md` section 14).

### 5.3 Bindings ("Starts when")

```ts
interface BindingState {
  binding: StartsWhenId;
  trigger: CatalogueRef;
  version: VersionNumber;         // the highest published version: only its bindings are live (E-17)
  paused: boolean;
  held: number;                   // always 0: a paused binding keeps no events (E-33)
  changedBy?: Ref;                // who last paused or resumed it; absent: never paused
  changedAt?: Timestamp;          // when
}
type BindingChanged = BindingState & {
  rerun?: number;                 // on a resume: always 0 (E-33)
  gone?: number;                  // on a resume: always 0 (E-33)
};
interface PausedDelivery {
  id: string;                     // opaque; names one delivery and one workflow
  binding: StartsWhenId;
  eventId: string;                // the sender's ID for the event
  at: Timestamp;                  // when the delivery was received
}
```

- `GET {base}/workflows/{workflow}/bindings` -> `200 BindingState[]`, document order; `[]` when the workflow has no published version. Any signed-in user. Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`).
- `PUT {base}/workflows/{workflow}/bindings/{binding}` body `{ paused }` -> `200 BindingChanged`; `rerun` and `gone` are present on a resume. Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`, `binding`), `not-admin`, `membership-unavailable`.
- `GET {base}/workflows/{workflow}/bindings/{binding}/paused-deliveries` -> `200 PausedDelivery[]`: always `[]`, since a paused binding keeps no events (E-33). Workflow admins and platform admins. Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`, `binding`), `not-admin`, `membership-unavailable`.
- Pausing needs no publish (E-17). The paused state is kept by binding ID, so it carries over to later versions that keep the binding. An event whose first matching binding is paused is a refused start with reason `paused`: the sender is answered `paused` at once (section 8) and is not expected to send it again; the event is listed with the other refused starts (5.4), and "run again" starts its request once the binding is resumed (while it is still paused, it is refused with `paused` again). A resume itself runs nothing again (E-33).
- Pausing and resuming is this API's only: the authoring API has no binding operations (E-31).
- Every pause and resume is recorded with who and when, one settings-log row each (E-23, E-33); `changedBy` and `changedAt` return the last.

### 5.4 Refused starts

```ts
type RefusedStartId = string;     // opaque; names one refused event and one workflow
interface RefusedStart {
  id: RefusedStartId;
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  startsWhen: StartsWhenId;       // the binding that matched
  at: Timestamp;                  // when the start was refused
  code: string;                   // the first problem: mapping-error, may, invalid-data, choice-unknown, check, rule-error; paused for a paused binding (location: the binding)
  params: { [key: string]: Json };   // as in core-api.md section 2.6 for that code
  location?: Location;            // the binding part, the question or the button, in the version that refused it
}
type RetriedStart =
  | { result: "started"; requestId: RequestId; readableId: ReadableId; binding: StartsWhenId; version: VersionNumber }
  | { result: "duplicate"; requestId: RequestId; readableId: ReadableId }
  | { result: "notMatched" }
  | { result: "paused"; binding: StartsWhenId }
  | { result: "refused"; binding: StartsWhenId; refusals: Refusal[] };
```

- `GET {base}/refused-starts?workflow=&cursor=&limit=` -> `200 Page<RefusedStart>`, newest first (E-21). The starts refused finally in the last 30 days and not run again since, not those answered "try again". Without `workflow`, the workflows the caller looks after; a platform admin sees every workflow. With `workflow`: `not-admin` when the caller does not look after it. Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`), `not-admin`, `membership-unavailable`.
- `POST {base}/refused-starts/{id}/retry` -> `200 RetriedStart`. Runs the start again for that workflow from the kept sent event, on the bindings of the workflow's live version at that moment, so the usual fix is to publish and then retry (E-21). The dedupe key still applies (`duplicate`). A start refused again is listed again. Who: as for the list. Errors: `not-found` (`refusedStart`), `not-admin`, `membership-unavailable`, `source-unavailable` and `busy` (503, try again; nothing was written).
- The sent event is kept, so a listed row can be run again while it is listed.

## 6. Reads

### 6.1 The published source

```ts
interface PublishedSource {
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;
  authored: AuthoredWorkflow;     // as published
  publishedAt: Timestamp;
  publishedBy: Ref;
}
```

`GET {base}/workflows/{workflow}/versions/{version}/source` -> `200 PublishedSource`, `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Errors: `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`).

The frontend turns every location into words with the version's own source, and renders every form from it (E-6). No read below repeats a label.

### 6.2 Request lists

```ts
interface RequestQuery extends PageArgs {
  workflow?: ServerWorkflowId;
  status?: StatusId[];            // needs workflow
  version?: VersionNumber;        // needs workflow
  state?: "open" | "closed";      // absent: both
  stuck?: boolean;
  startedBy?: string;             // a user's directory ID
  valueEquals?: { value: ValueId; equals: Json }[];   // needs workflow; all must hold; equality only; JSON per core 2.4
  include?: ValueId[];            // values to return per row, at most 10
  sort?: "readableId" | "startedAt" | "updatedAt";    // default readableId
  order?: "asc" | "desc";                             // default desc
}
interface RequestRow {
  requestId: RequestId;
  readableId: ReadableId;
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;
  status?: Status;
  stage: Location;                // { item: StageId, part? } as in RequestView
  startedBy: By;
  startedAt: Timestamp;
  updatedAt: Timestamp;
  closedAt?: Timestamp;
  stuck?: Stuck;                  // reason, at, location; never `admin` in a list
  values?: Values;                // only the included values
  lastSeq: Seq;
}
```

`GET {base}/requests?workflow=&status=a,b&version=&state=&stuck=true&startedBy=&value.<valueId>=<json>&include=a,b&sort=&order=&cursor=&limit=` -> `200 Page<RequestRow>`.

- `status` or `valueEquals` without `workflow`: `invalid-body`. Status IDs are per workflow. A person in `valueEquals` is `{ "type": "user", "id": ... }`.
- `stuck=true` gives the stuck list. Every row already shows its stuck state to everyone (E-19), so the filter is open to every signed-in user; showing the stuck list only to admins is the page's choice.
- Served by the `requests` projection's indexes: `(workflow, status)`, the partial index on the stuck state, `started_by`, GIN on `data` (`@>`), unique `readable_id`. Sorting by `startedAt` or `updatedAt` is unindexed at this scale. Text search, "involves me" and sorting by a value are not offered.

### 6.3 The request page

```ts
type GetRequestArgs = ({ requestId: RequestId } | { readableId: ReadableId }) & { debug?: boolean };
```

`GET {base}/requests/{requestId}` and `GET {base}/requests/by-number/{readableId}`, `?debug=true` optional -> `200 RequestView` (`core-api.md` section 8), `ETag` (9.3). Errors: `not-found` (`request`).

Built by folding the request's events, plus `pending_calls` for the admin fields. Live specifics:

- `values`: the data's top-level keys that are value IDs of the request's version.
- `tasks`: open tasks with `buttonStates` for the caller. `actions`: open actions; `admin` only for people who look after stuck requests. Its `state` is `queued` or `accepted` (an await whose outside job is running); the server never answers `inFlight`.
- `stuck`: the request's stuck state, worked out from the fault not yet cleared, the match of the `nobodyToAsk` block, or nothing that fits (`core-api.md` section 8). `stuck.admin` only for people who look after stuck requests, and only for two reasons: `action-failed` (`fault: "call-failed"`, and `failureCode` and `outsideText` when the other system gave them; in the thin build `attempts` is absent, because a failed call's tries are not kept once its result is recorded) and `error` (`fault`, and `error`, `key`, `index` and `text` when known). `nobody-to-ask` and `nothing-fits` have no `admin`, for anyone: their `location` is the whole detail. Retry is offered for `action-failed` and `nobody-to-ask` only; Close for any open request (5.1).
- `story`: built as `core-api.md` section 9 says. `moved.why` has `taken` only: the arrows that did not fit are not recorded (E-15). `stuck` entries carry `admin` only for admins. `debug` is filled only with `debug=true` and only for platform admins, because the events hold engineers' text and the other system's text.
- `viewer.isAdmin`: may the caller see the admin fields, retry and close.

## 7. Session and directory

```ts
interface Person { ref: Ref; label: string; platformAdmin: boolean }
```

| Function | HTTP | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `whoAmI(caller): Result<Person>` | `GET {base}/session` | |
| `signInAs(caller, person: Ref): Result<Person>` | `PUT {base}/session` body `{ person }` | Development host only; elsewhere `forbidden` with `need: "devHost"`. Only a person the directory knows: a group or an unknown person is `invalid-body` (`/person`, `format`), and the person signed in stays. |
| `people(caller): Result<Person[]>` | `GET {base}/session/people` | Development host: the people it offers; elsewhere `[]`. |
| `DirectoryApi.search` | `GET {base}/directory/search?q=&types=user,group&limit=` | `DirectoryEntry[]`, `limit` 1 to 50 |
| `DirectoryApi.lookup` | `POST {base}/directory/lookup` body `{ refs }` | `DirectoryEntry[]` |
| `DirectoryApi.membersOf` | `GET {base}/directory/groups/{id}/members` | `DirectoryEntry[]` |

Directory reads are live and recorded nowhere (E-9). They serve people pickers, names for display and the form editor's samples; a question's directory choices come from `choices` (3.4). A directory that cannot be reached answers `503 membership-unavailable`; `DirectoryApi` rejects. In the existing application the session and the directory: unknown: depends on the existing application.

## 8. The inbound endpoint (door 1)

Other systems hold this endpoint and its answers, so they are fixed exactly as `engine/spec/integrations.md` sections 9.6 to 9.8 give them. Fields may be added; none is removed or renamed. The frontend does not call it; Try it's `startFrom` gives the same outcome for one binding (`core-api.md` section 10.2).

`POST {hooks}/hooks/v1/events/{connection}`, one URL per connection. `{hooks}` is the engine's public base URL: the development host's own origin; in the existing application: unknown: depends on the existing application.

**Verification is the connector's job** (E-20). The connection's connector verifies the sender's own scheme, which must carry a signed timestamp; a real system signs its own way. The platform's own scheme, used by every mock system and by a later generic inbound webhook, is Standard Webhooks: `webhook-id` (the sender's message ID, which is the event ID), `webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds, refused more than 300 s from the engine's clock), `webhook-signature` (`v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>` over `id.timestamp.body`, with the connection's `inbound` secret), `content-type: application/json`. Body of the platform's scheme: `{ "type": "<trigger name>", "data": {...} }`.

Before any transaction, in this order:

| # | Check | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Body over 256 KiB (262144 bytes), by `Content-Length` or by stopping the read | `413 { "error": "too-large" }`, refused unread |
| 2 | No such connection, or its connector has no trigger entry | `404 { "error": "unknown-connection" }` |
| 3 | The connection is `notSetUp` or `disabled` | `503 { "error": "connection-unavailable" }`, `Retry-After: 300` |
| 4 | The connector's `verify` refuses | `401 { "error": "unauthenticated" }` |
| 5 | The connector's `parse`: cannot read the body; cannot resolve a person now; an event kind it does not map; an event that fails its trigger's schema | `400 { "error": "unparsable" }`; `503 { "error": "unavailable" }`, `Retry-After: 60`; `200` with `results: []`; `400 { "error": "event-invalid" }` |

Then each candidate workflow is processed in its own transaction (E-17), and the answer is:

| HTTP | Body | When | The sender should |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | `InboundAnswer` | Processed, whatever happened per workflow | Not retry |
| 400 | `{ "error": "unparsable" \| "event-invalid" }` | The body cannot be read, or fails the trigger's schema | Not retry; fix the sender |
| 401 | `{ "error": "unauthenticated" }` | Signature, timestamp or scheme refused | Fix its set-up |
| 404 | `{ "error": "unknown-connection" }` | | Fix its set-up |
| 413 | `{ "error": "too-large" }` | Over 256 KiB | Not retry |
| 503 | `{ "error": "connection-unavailable" \| "unavailable" }` | The connection is not ready or is disabled; the store, the directory or a data source cannot be reached; a start failed for an unexpected reason and was rolled back (E-20) | Retry after `Retry-After` |

```ts
interface InboundAnswer {                    // 200, content-type application/json
  eventId: string | null;                    // null only for an ignored delivery without an ID
  results: InboundResult[];                  // one per candidate workflow, in workflow ID order; [] when none
}

type InboundResult =
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "started";   binding: string; requestId: string; readableId: number }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "duplicate"; binding: string; requestId: string; readableId: number }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "notMatched" }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "paused";    binding: string }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "refused";   binding: string; problems: InboundProblem[] };

interface InboundProblem {
  code: "mapping-error" | "may" | "invalid-data" | "choice-unknown" | "check" | "rule-error" | (string & {});
  where: Location | null;                    // the binding part, the question, or the button
  params: { [key: string]: Json };           // as in core-api.md section 2.6 for the same code
}
```

- `workflow` is the server's workflow ID; `readableId` is a JSON number here, as `engine/spec/integrations.md` section 9.8 fixes it. For `duplicate`, `version` and `binding` are those that started the request. No expression error text and no check message leaves the platform.
- Candidates: every workflow whose highest published version has a binding on this connection for a parsed event. Per workflow, the bindings are checked in document order; the first whose `onlyWhen` is true decides. If it is paused the result is `paused`, decided before its mapping runs, and no later binding is tried; the event is kept and listed as a refused start with reason `paused` (5.4), so the sender need not send it again (E-33). At most one request per workflow (E-17).
- `duplicate`: the inbound log holds a started row for (connection, event ID, workflow), written in that start's transaction and kept for ever. A refused, paused or try-again result is no start, so a redelivery runs again.
- `refused` is final: a mapping error, or a start refused with `may`, `invalid-data`, `choice-unknown`, `check` or `rule-error`. It leaves no request, writes one inbound-log row and a `start-refused` log line (nobody is told, 5.2), and is listed for 30 days, from where it can be run again (5.4).
- **Try again.** When any workflow's start could not be made now (`source-unavailable`, or any other failure inside that start: an exception, a lost store connection, a lock not obtained; each is rolled back), the whole answer is `503 { "error": "unavailable" }`, `Retry-After: 60`. The workflows that did start answer `duplicate` on the sender's retry. The 400, 401, 404 and 413 answers are final and write an `inbound-refused` log line; nobody is told (E-33).
- Try it's `startFrom`: `started: true` is `started`, `started: false` is `notMatched`, refusals are `refused`.

## 9. Paging and consistency

### 9.1 Read-your-writes

A turn appends events and updates the read tables in one transaction. `start`, `act`, `retry` and `close` answer after the commit, and the first build reads from the primary only, so any later read sees the turn. Replicas: unknown: depends on the existing application. A call's result and notifications arrive in later turns; a page that has just acted shows the request waiting on the action until a later read.

### 9.2 Paging

Keyset cursors over `(sort key, request ID)`; `next` is opaque. Each page is its own read. A cursor from another query is `invalid-body`. The story is not paged.

### 9.3 Staying current

Polling in the first build. `getRequest` and `getTask` answer `ETag: W/"<lastSeq>.<coreVersion>"` and `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`; a poll with `If-None-Match` gets `304` when nothing was recorded. Viewer-level fields (`buttonStates`, `viewer.isAdmin`, `mayAnswer`, the `admin` fields) depend on live memberships and settings that the ETag does not cover; they are advisory, and every act and admin turn checks again.

## 10. What this needs from the engine design

What this contract needed from the design, all now in kernel spec v2.20 and its data model (E-2).

| Need | Where | Kept for ever? |
|---|---|---|
| `Faulted.error.params` carries `{ error, key?, index? }` with `error` one of `ExpressionErrorKind` | spec section 5 | Yes |
| The origin map resolves an element and a field to an authored item and part; a check to the form rule it enforces | definition format | Yes, while a request runs on the version |
| A person value is `{ type, id }` in schemas and data (E-20; the definition-format note's user field changes) | definition format | Yes |
| `by.type` and the call wait field are `connection` (E-17) | spec sections 2, 5 | Yes |
| An outcome carries `lookups`, each `{ property, connection, source, inputs, storedField, labelField, answer: "item" \| "person" }`; `WaitCompleted.evidence` gains `lookups`; the refusal `choice-unknown` (E-20, E-23) | spec section 2, definition format | Yes |
| The `nobodyToAsk` block and the membership read `<task>__members` opened beside each task that may ask a group, which every reader uses (E-20, E-23) | definition format, spec v2.16 | Yes |
| The `types` block, by which `decide` reads JSON numbers (E-23) | definition format | Yes |
| The client token and the hash of its arguments on the request's row, unique per `(started_by, client_token)` | data model, `requests` | No |
| Inbound dedupe key `(connection, event_id, workflow) -> request_id`, a started row of the inbound log | data model, kept record (E-17) | Yes |
| Paused bindings; who paused or resumed and when, in the settings log (E-23, E-33) | data model, configuration and log | No |
| Refused starts listed for 30 days with their sent event (E-21) | data model, the inbound log | No |

## 11. Decisions in this draft

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| C-1 | Functions on one interface with a handler over them; the host supplies the `Caller`. | E-11. |
| C-2 | A task instance has its own opaque ID. | A stale page must be refused (`wait-not-open`). |
| C-3 | No labels and no forms in reads; the page reads the version's source once. | Immutable and cacheable; words are the frontend's (F5). |
| C-4 | Start deduplication by the client token on the request's row; same token, other arguments is `client-token-reused`. | Event shapes are fixed; deduplication is working state. |
| C-5 | Act needs no token. | The task instance is the key. |
| C-6 | A refusal list holds every failure of the first failing step. | The page shows all problems at once; the kernel's order holds between steps. |
| C-7 | An expression error in a form rule refuses with `rule-error`. | A CEL error is never false; nothing is written. |
| C-8 | Retry = clear the fault if any + re-enter the active engine stage, only for a request stuck with `action-failed` or `nobody-to-ask`; Close for any open request. Both need `expectedLastSeq`. | E-19, E-20, E-23. Repeats only what running again can help; a slow call is never retried. |
| C-9 | Choices are asked for by question, for the directory and for data sources alike, on every form; each answer is looked up again when the person acts. | E-17, E-20. |
| C-10 | Outside lookups (memberships, choices) happen before the lock, after an unlocked check that the task is open; the task is checked again under the lock; each result is reported at its step. | E-23. No outside call under the lock; the kernel's order is kept. |
| C-11 | My tasks leaves out a task the caller may not answer and still carries `mayAnswer`; a failed group lookup gives a partial list with a flag. | A person who may not answer a task is not told about it (E-33), so the list does not offer it either. |
| C-12 | Reads go to the primary; polling with an ETag on `lastSeq`. | Read-your-writes with no extra machinery. |
| C-13 | An event's first matching binding decides, paused or not; a paused one refuses the event. | Pausing one binding never sends events to another. |
| C-14 | An inbound delivery with any try-again result answers `503 unavailable`; started workflows answer `duplicate` on the retry. | `engine/spec/integrations.md` section 9.7; the sender's retry is the only way the event is processed again. |

## 12. Open points

Depends on the existing application:

1. The request ID's storage type and the readable ID's display format. Both are strings here, except the inbound answer's `readableId`, a number.
2. How the host signs people in, supplies the `Caller`, checks the platform-admin entitlement and guards against cross-site requests.
3. Where the handlers are mounted (`{base}`, `{hooks}`), and whether reads may go to a replica.
4. The directory's group-membership API, its limits and failure modes, which decide how often `membership-unavailable` and `groupsUnavailable` occur.
5. Which page URL a notification links to; the API serves both request IDs.
6. How the real Helpdesk signs its deliveries.

Depends on the product owner:

7. Whether every signed-in user should see answers, action results and the whole story of every request. The first build follows the data model and E-19: yes.

Engine:

8. A choice lookup's inputs are worked out from the unlocked read of the request (4.3 step 3). If another turn changes a value those inputs read between that read and the lock, the answer was looked up with the earlier inputs. Whether to compare the inputs again under the lock is not decided.
===\ncontract/words/README.md\n===
# Words

`notifications.json` holds the words of the platform's built-in messages and alerts. The frontend owner holds the pen: plain words, full sentences, sentence case, "you" for the reader, no blame, no exclamation marks. The engine's notifier and alert sender send from this file and never write their own wording. Parameters are named, written `{name}`, and filled by the sender.

## Keys

| Key | Sent to | Params |
|---|---|---|
| `task.assigned` | The people asked | `askedOf`, `request`, `workflow`, `stage` |
| `request.stuck` | People who look after stuck requests | `request`, `workflow`, `stage`, `reason`, `whatYouCanDo` |
| `start.refused` | People who look after stuck requests | `workflow`, `startsWhen`, `code` |
| `alert.call-overdue` | People who look after stuck requests | `workflow`, `entry`, `connection` |
| `alert.job-left-running` | People who look after stuck requests | `request`, `workflow`, `stage`, `action` |
| `alert.rule-failed` | People who look after stuck requests | `workflow`, `version`, `action` |
| `alert.call-outcome-unknown` | People who look after stuck requests | `request`, `workflow`, `action`, `connection` |
| `alert.publish-failed` | Platform admins | `request`, `workflow` |
| `alert.inbound-refused` | Platform admins | `connection`, `code` |
| `alert.delivery-stuck` | Platform admins | `connection` |
| `alert.directory-unavailable` | Platform admins | `connection` |
| `alert.source-unavailable` | Platform admins | `entry`, `connection` |
| `alert.catalogue-rejected` | Platform admins | `entry`, `connection` |
| `alert.subscription-failing` | Platform admins | `subscription` |

Two blocks are not messages but fill a param:

- `reasons`: keyed by the engine's stuck reason (`action-failed`, `nobody-to-ask`, `nothing-fits`, `error`, and `unfinished`, which exists only in Try it: it is never sent as a message, only shown when a test request reaches a part of the draft that is not finished; there is nothing to retry or close, so its `whatYouCanDo` says to finish that part and try again). Each has two parts that read as one message: `clause` fills `{reason}` in `request.stuck` and completes "is stuck at {stage}: ..."; `whatYouCanDo` fills `{whatYouCanDo}` and says what the reader can do. Retry is offered only where running again can help: for `action-failed` (it tries the action again) and `nobody-to-ask` (it reads the group again and asks again), and the part also names Close. For `nothing-fits` and `error` only Close is offered: the part says so, why trying again would not help, and to tell the people who built the workflow.
- `refusedBecause`: fills `{code}` in `start.refused`, keyed by the refusal code (`mapping-error`, `may`, `invalid-data`, `choice-unknown`, `check`, `rule-error`). The engine fills `{code}` from the first refusal's code.

The alerts table in `engine/design/integrations-shapes.md` section 8 has two more reasons with no `alert.` entry here: `start-refused` is sent as `start.refused`, and `notification` is sent as the built-in messages above (a task with nobody to ask is `request.stuck` with reason `nobody-to-ask`; there is no separate message for it).

Messages to people who look after stuck requests use the author's words only (connection, "Starts when", "Tell other systems", request, stage). Messages to platform admins may use the engine design's technical terms.

## What fills each param

| Param | Filled with |
|---|---|
| `workflow` | The workflow's name, from the server's workflow record |
| `request` | The request's title, or its readable number when it has no title |
| `stage` | The stage's name |
| `askedOf` | The name of the person or group asked |
| `action` | The action's name as the editor shows it ("Create Jira issue", "Notify Requester") |
| `startsWhen` | The connection's label of what starts it, e.g. "Helpdesk: a ticket is tagged" |
| `connection` | The connection's label |
| `entry` | The catalogue entry's label and ID (in `alert.call-overdue`: the operation the calls use) |
| `subscription` | The subscription's name |
| `version` | The workflow's version number |
| `reason` | The `clause` of the `reasons` entry for the stuck reason |
| `whatYouCanDo` | The `whatYouCanDo` of the same `reasons` entry |
| `code` | In `start.refused`: the `refusedBecause` entry. In `alert.inbound-refused`: the hook's error code as is (`unauthenticated`, `unparsable`, ...) |
===\ncontract/words/notifications.json\n===
{
  "task.assigned": {
    "subject": "You have something to do on {request}",
    "body": "{askedOf}: the request {request} in {workflow} is now at {stage} and needs your answer. Open it to see what is asked."
  },
  "request.stuck": {
    "subject": "{request} is stuck at {stage}",
    "body": "The request {request} in {workflow} is stuck at {stage}: {reason}. {whatYouCanDo} You can do this from the request's page. You are told because you look after stuck requests in {workflow}."
  },
  "start.refused": {
    "subject": "A request in {workflow} could not be started",
    "body": "{startsWhen} tried to start a request in {workflow}, but the request could not be started: {code}. No request was started. It is kept in the list of refused starts for 30 days, where you can run it again once the cause is put right. Check the workflow's \"Starts when\" and what the other system sends, and ask whoever looks after the connection if it is on their side. You are told because you look after stuck requests in {workflow}."
  },
  "alert.call-overdue": {
    "subject": "Requests in {workflow} are waiting longer than expected for {entry}",
    "body": "Some requests in {workflow} have been waiting for {entry} on connection {connection} for longer than it usually takes. They are not stuck: each carries on as soon as its answer arrives. Look at the other system to see why it is slow; the requests go on by themselves as soon as it answers. If a request should not go on, you can close it from its page. You get at most one of these per workflow and action each hour. You are told because you look after stuck requests in {workflow}."
  },
  "alert.job-left-running": {
    "subject": "Work started by {action} is still running after {request} moved on",
    "body": "{action} asked another system to do some work for the request {request} in {workflow}. The request has since left {stage}, but the other system reports that the work is still running. Nothing in the request waits for it any more, so its result will not be used. If the work should not finish, stop it in the other system. You are told because you look after stuck requests in {workflow}."
  },
  "alert.rule-failed": {
    "subject": "{action} could not be sent in {workflow}",
    "body": "In version {version} of {workflow}, {action} could not work out what to send, so nothing was sent for it. This usually means a value it uses has nothing in it or does not fit. Requests carry on as before. To fix it, change {action} in the draft and publish a new version. You are told because you look after stuck requests in {workflow}."
  },
  "alert.publish-failed": {
    "subject": "Outbound events for {request} have been held for 15 minutes",
    "body": "The publisher job for the request {request} in {workflow} has kept failing for 15 minutes, so that request's outbound events (Tell other systems) are held and retried; other requests publish on, and the request itself is not affected. Look at the publisher's errors for this request and fix the cause; the held events are sent in order once it succeeds."
  },
  "alert.call-outcome-unknown": {
    "subject": "It is not clear whether {action} was done for {request}",
    "body": "For the request {request} in {workflow}, {action} asked another system, through connection {connection}, to do something. The request has since moved on, and it never became clear whether the other system did it. Look in the other system to see whether it was done, and put it right by hand if needed. You are told because you look after stuck requests in {workflow}."
  },
  "alert.inbound-refused": {
    "subject": "Inbound delivery refused for connection {connection}",
    "body": "A delivery to the inbound hook of connection {connection} was refused with {code} (HTTP 400, 401, 404 or 413). Nothing was started or recorded from it. If this keeps happening, check the connection's inbound secret and URL, and what the sender posts. You get at most one of these per connection and code each hour."
  },
  "alert.delivery-stuck": {
    "subject": "A delivery from {connection} has not been processed for 15 minutes",
    "body": "A trigger delivery from connection {connection} was received but is still not answered 15 minutes later. The reconciler keeps trying it, so requests it should start may be late rather than lost. Check that the store, the directory and any data sources the start needs can be reached."
  },
  "alert.directory-unavailable": {
    "subject": "The directory could not be reached",
    "body": "A membership lookup failed when someone acted, or connection {connection} could not resolve a person while reading a delivery. Until the directory is back, people may be unable to act on tasks and some starts are retried. Check the directory service. You get at most one of these per connection each hour."
  },
  "alert.source-unavailable": {
    "subject": "Data source {entry} on {connection} could not be reached",
    "body": "The data source {entry} on connection {connection} failed to list or get items. Questions that take their choices from it cannot be answered for now, and starts that need it are retried. Check the connection and the outside system. You get at most one of these per connection each hour."
  },
  "alert.catalogue-rejected": {
    "subject": "Catalogue entry {entry} on {connection} was rejected and is disabled",
    "body": "The catalogue entry {entry} on connection {connection} changed its shape, is missing, or failed registration. The entry has been disabled so that no workflow runs against a shape it was not checked with; calls to it are held. Fix the connector or register a new entry version, then enable the entry again."
  },
  "alert.subscription-failing": {
    "subject": "Deliveries to subscription {subscription} have failed for 15 minutes",
    "body": "Outbound events to subscription {subscription} have been failing for 15 minutes. They are kept and retried, so nothing is lost yet, but the receiver is falling behind. Check the receiver's endpoint and credentials."
  },
  "reasons": {
    "action-failed": {
      "clause": "one of its actions did not work",
      "whatYouCanDo": "Once you have put right what made it fail, you can retry the request, which tries the action again, or close it if it is no longer needed."
    },
    "nobody-to-ask": {
      "clause": "there is nobody to ask",
      "whatYouCanDo": "Nobody can be chosen by hand in this version. Put the person or group right outside the request, for example by adding people to the group in the directory, then retry the request: it reads the group again and asks again. Or close the request if it is no longer needed."
    },
    "nothing-fits": {
      "clause": "none of the arrows out of the stage fits this request",
      "whatYouCanDo": "The request can only be closed: trying again would read the arrows out of this stage the same way and find none again. Tell the people who built the workflow, so that the next request does not get stuck the same way."
    },
    "error": {
      "clause": "something went wrong that the platform could not handle",
      "whatYouCanDo": "The request can only be closed: trying again would make the same thing go wrong again. Tell the people who built the workflow, so that the next request does not get stuck the same way."
    },
    "unfinished": {
      "clause": "it reached a part of the workflow that is not finished yet, such as an arrow with no stage chosen, an action with nothing chosen, or nobody chosen in Who is asked",
      "whatYouCanDo": "This is a test request, so there is nothing to retry. Finish that part of the workflow, then try it again with a new test request."
    }
  },
  "refusedBecause": {
    "mapping-error": "the start form's answers could not be worked out from what the other system sent",
    "may": "the workflow does not let this start a request",
    "invalid-data": "an answer worked out from what was sent does not fit its question",
    "choice-unknown": "an answer is not one of the choices its question offers",
    "check": "the start form's rules were not met, for example a question needed to press its button was empty",
    "rule-error": "one of the start form's rules, such as a Show when or an Also only when, could not be worked out from the answers it was given"
  }
}

# Technical design: what the documents and diagrams must convey

Owner: Frontend owner. Agreed with the Engine owner on 2026-11-15, with their additions (two views per door and a ledger in document 5; diagrams D4b, D7b, D10a, D10b). This is the table of contents of `docs/`.

## 1. Who reads this, and what they need

| Reader | What they need to come away with |
|---|---|
| Product owner and leadership | The parts of the platform, who owns each, what is built first, and how customers' workflows relate to the platform we build. |
| Engineers who build and maintain it | Boundaries, contracts, data flow, lifecycles, failure handling. Enough to change one part without reading the others. |
| People who connect other systems | Every way data and control cross the platform's edge, in both directions, and what a connection must promise. |
| The two build sessions | The interface between frontend and engine, exact enough to build against separately. |

## 2. The six things the set must make clear

Every document and diagram exists to land one of these. If it lands none, it is cut.

1. **We build a platform; customers build workflows.** The platform is an authoring tool, an engine, and a set of doors to other systems. "Change request" is an example and never appears in the platform's code.
2. **A workflow exists in three forms.** What the author edits (a draft), what the engine runs (a published, immutable version), and what happened (a request's history). One pipeline connects them: edit, check, publish, run, record, show.
3. **Everything crosses the platform's edge through a small number of doors.** Upstream and downstream, data and control (triggers and events). Each door has a rule for what is recorded, what is retried, and what happens when it fails.
4. **The editor's words map one-to-one onto the engine's concepts.** Stage, task, button, arrow, value, action, To do, stuck, Try it: each has exactly one engine counterpart and one field in the contract.
5. **The frontend and the engine meet at one contract.** The authored workflow format, the authoring API, the runtime API, and the catalogue of connections.
6. **What is in the first build, what is held as a shape, and what is later.**

## 3. The documents

Owner means who holds the pen. The other session reviews.

## 5. The contract, in four parts

This is the interface the two sessions build against. It is the main thing to agree first.

| Part | What it is | Proposed pen |
|---|---|---|
| A. Authored workflow format | The draft as data, in the editor's terms: stages and their kinds, tasks, who is asked, forms, buttons, actions, arrows and their conditions, values, lists, the sample request, diagram positions. It is compiled to a published definition. | Frontend drafts from the editor model (`workflow/spec/editor-model.md`); Engine makes it compilable and owns the compiler |
| B. Authoring API | Drafts, check (To do and Worth knowing as codes with locations), values in scope at a point (kind, where filled, may be empty), formula check and sample result, Try it, publish, versions and what changed. | Engine; Frontend states what each screen needs |
| C. Runtime API | Start a request, act on a task, admin retry and close; reads for lists, the request page, action items and history. | Engine |
| D. Catalogue | The connections available to an author: actions, data sources, things that can start or move a request, events sent out; each with versioned input and output shapes and a sample. Also the directory search. | Engine |

Two rules proposed for the contract:

- **The engine reports in codes, the frontend chooses the words.** A check result is a code, a location in the authored format, and parameters. The editor turns it into "To do" text. Engine terms never reach the screen.
- **Locations are in the authored format, never in the compiled definition.** An author is always shown their own workflow.

## 6. Form

- Sources are Markdown with Mermaid diagrams, one file per document, in `docs/`. Each file's header names its owner.
- A small script builds them into one self-contained page for reading.
- A diagram that needs a screenshot uses the mockups.

# Start here

Owner: Frontend owner.

Answers: What is this system, in one picture, and where do I read next?

This is the technical design of a no-code workflow platform. On it, people who do not write code build **workflows**: a form someone fills in, the people who must approve or do the work, and what happens in other systems along the way. Each time someone uses a workflow, that is a **request**. This page gives the whole system in one picture, the six things the design must make clear, and where to read next.

## The system in one picture

We build three parts: the **editor and pages** people use in the browser, the **engine** that runs requests and keeps their history, and the **connections** through which data and control cross to other systems. Around them are the people who use the platform, the existing application it lives in, and other systems.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph people["People, by role"]
    author["Workflow author<br/>builds and publishes"]
    requester["Requester<br/>starts a request"]
    asked["Person asked<br/>answers a task"]
    keeper["Looks after<br/>stuck requests"]
    padmin["Platform admin<br/>sets up connections"]
  end

  subgraph platform["The platform: the three parts we build"]
    ui["1. Editor and pages<br/>in the browser"]
    engine["2. Engine<br/>runs requests, keeps history"]
    conn["3. Connections<br/>the doors to other systems"]
  end

  subgraph app["The existing application"]
    signin["Sign-in"]
    dir["Directory<br/>people and groups"]
    mail["Email and Slack"]
  end

  outside["Other systems<br/>samples: Helpdesk, Service catalog,<br/>Jira, Deploy pipeline, Reporting"]

  author --> ui
  requester --> ui
  asked --> ui
  keeper --> ui
  padmin --> conn
  ui <-->|"one contract"| engine
  ui -.-|"who is signed in"| signin
  engine <--> conn
  conn <--> dir
  conn --> mail
  conn <--> outside

  classDef ours fill:#e4e6fc,stroke:#4f46e5,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1c2030
  classDef existing fill:#f4f5f7,stroke:#a0a6b1,color:#1c2030
  classDef other fill:#ffffff,stroke:#a0a6b1,color:#1c2030
  class ui,engine,conn ours
  class signin,dir,mail existing
  class outside other
```

*D1. The platform and everything around it: who uses it, what we build, what the existing application supplies, and which other systems it reaches*

Read the picture from top to bottom. People only ever use the editor and pages. The editor and pages talk to the engine through one contract. The engine reaches everything outside the platform through connections, never directly. Document 1 ([Context](01-context.md)) draws the same picture with every line labelled.

## Six things to know

1. **We build a platform; customers build workflows.** The platform is the editor, the engine and the connections. A customer's workflow is data that an author builds in the editor and publishes without a deployment. "Change request", used as the example everywhere, is sample data; the platform's code never names it.
2. **A workflow exists in three forms**: the draft an author edits, the published version the engine runs, and the history of each request. One pipeline connects them: edit, check, publish, run, record, show. See the next section.
3. **Everything crosses the platform's edge through a small number of doors.** There are seven: a request starts, a person acts, the workflow calls another system, the directory says who is in a group, a question gets its choices, a message is sent, and other systems are told what happened. Each door has a rule for what is recorded, what is retried and what happens when it fails. Nothing gets in any other way. Document 5 ([Integrations](05-integrations.md)) covers each door.
4. **The editor's words map one-to-one onto the engine's concepts.** Stage, task, button, arrow, value, action, To do, stuck, Try it: each has one engine counterpart and one field in the saved workflow. Document 4 ([Word map](04-word-map.md)) is the table.
5. **The frontend and the engine meet at one contract** of four parts: the authored workflow format (the saved draft), the authoring API (check, try, publish), the runtime API (start, act, read), and the catalogue of connections. It lives in the repository's `contract/` folder; document 6 ([The contract](06-the-contract.md)) explains it.
6. **Each feature is in the first build, held as a shape, or later.** "First build" is what this repository builds and runs. "Shape only" means the recorded history can already hold it but nothing produces it yet. "Later" means designed enough not to block it, not built. Examples of later: deadlines and reminders (the engine has no clock), and another system nudging a request that did not ask it.

## Three forms of a workflow

- **Draft.** What the author edits in the editor, saved continuously. It may be unfinished; the editor's To do list says what is missing.
- **Published version.** Publishing checks the draft and compiles it into a definition the engine runs. A version never changes; the next publish makes a new one.
- **Request history.** Every request runs on the version it started on, and the engine records everything that happens to it, in order, for good.
- The pages and Try it show a request by reading that history back, in the author's words.
- Document 3 ([The life of a workflow](03-life-of-a-workflow.md)) follows one workflow through all three forms, with diagrams [D4](#fig-d4) and [D5](#fig-d5).
