# Building the reading page

This folder builds every `docs/NN-*.md` into one page, `docs/site/index.html`. The page is self-contained: open it straight from the file system, with no network and no server. The built page is committed, so people can open it without building.

## How to build

Node is needed (LTS). Chrome must be installed; the build uses the system Chrome and never downloads a browser.

```sh
cd docs/build
PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 npm install   # once (PowerShell: $env:PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD = '1'; npm install)
npm run build        # writes docs/site/index.html
npm run check        # the same checks, writes nothing
```

The build looks for Chrome (or Chromium) where Windows, macOS and Linux usually install it (`chrome-path.mjs`); if yours is elsewhere, set `CHROME_PATH` to its executable.

Other scripts:

- `npm run annotate` redraws `docs/assets/d6-stage-annotated.png` (diagram D6 in the word map) from `docs/assets/01-editor-default.png`, a copy of the mockup screenshot `workflow/mockups/shots/01-editor__default.png`. The callout positions are in `annotate-d6.mjs`; its numbers must match the legend in `04-word-map.md`.
- `node shoot.mjs <out dir> [css selector ...]` takes screenshots of the built page (the top, then each selector), for checking how it looks.

### What fails the build, and what only warns

Fails (exit code 1):

- A Mermaid block that does not render. The message names the file, the line and the diagram.
- A broken in-page link: a link to a heading, or to a document, that does not exist.
- An image under `docs/` that does not exist.

Warns:

- A diagram id (D1, D4b ...) in the doc plan's diagram table that no document draws yet.
- A link to a numbered document, or to a diagram, that has not been written yet.
- A link to a file outside `docs/` that does not exist.

## Conventions for authors

**Files.** One document per file, named `NN-name.md` in `docs/`. The page orders them by number: `00-start-here.md` first, then 01, 02 ..., the `11-decisions-*.md` files, and `00-doc-plan.md` last under the title "About this document set".

**The top of a document.**

```markdown
# Title

Owner: Frontend owner.

Answers: The question from the doc plan.
```

The `Owner:` and `Answers:` lines are shown as the document's header. The table of contents lists each document and its `##` headings.

**Links.**

- To another document: `[Integrations](05-integrations.md)`.
- To a heading in another document: `[the ledger](05-integrations.md#the-ledger)`. The anchor is the heading in lower case, punctuation removed, spaces as hyphens.
- To a heading in the same document: `[below](#the-ledger)`.
- To a diagram, wherever it is drawn: `[D4b](#fig-d4b)`.
- To a file elsewhere in the repository: `../contract/authored-format.md`. It stays a relative link from the built page.

**Diagrams.** Write Mermaid in a fenced block marked `mermaid`. It is drawn to SVG when the page is built, in one theme set in `build.mjs` (taken from the mockup kit), so do not set colours or themes in the diagram unless a colour means something (then use `classDef`). Put the caption on the line right after the block, in italics, starting with the diagram's number from the doc plan:

```markdown
*D7. The integration map: upstream and downstream, data and control*
```

The caption becomes the figure's caption and an entry in the "List of diagrams" at the end of the page. A caption may also follow an image or a table (for a diagram that is a matrix); the two become one figure.

Keep a diagram narrow enough to read: about 1000 pixels at its natural size. A wider one is never shrunk below 80%; it scrolls sideways instead, and the reader can use "Open larger".

**Images.** Put them in `docs/assets/` and link them as `assets/name.png`, in Markdown or in an `<img>` tag. They are inlined into the page.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `build.mjs` | The build and the checks |
| `page.css`, `page.js` | The page's look (tokens from the mockup kit) and its small optional script: highlighting the current section, "Open larger" |
| `annotate-d6.mjs` | Draws the D6 callouts |
| `shoot.mjs` | Screenshots of the built page |

// Draws numbered callouts over the editor mockup screenshot for diagram D6
// (docs/04-word-map.md). Input:  docs/assets/01-editor-default.png (a copy of

import fs from 'node:fs';

// [number, box x, y, w, h, badge x, badge y]  (pixels of the 1440x900 screenshot)

  [8, 1056, 638, 368, 40, 1236, 666],   // group rule
  [9, 1060, 684, 362, 216, 1398, 706],  // depends on the Domains list

  `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="7" fill="none" stroke="${NOTE}" stroke-width="2.2"/>`).join('');

  await browser.close();
}
===\ndocs/build/build.mjs\n===
// Builds every docs/NN-*.md into one self-contained page: docs/site/index.html.
//   node build.mjs           build and write the page
//   node build.mjs --check   build in memory, report problems, write nothing
// Fails (exit 1) on: a Mermaid block that does not render, a broken in-page link.
// Warns on: a diagram id in the doc plan's table that no document draws, a link
// to a file outside docs/ that does not exist.
// See README.md for the conventions authors follow.

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';
import { chromePath } from './chrome-path.mjs';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const DOCS = path.resolve(HERE, '..');
const OUT_DIR = path.join(DOCS, 'site');
const OUT = path.join(OUT_DIR, 'index.html');
const CHECK_ONLY = process.argv.includes('--check');
const CHROME = chromePath();

const DOC_PLAN = '00-doc-plan.md';
const START = '00-start-here.md';
const TITLE_OVERRIDES = { [DOC_PLAN]: 'About this document set' };
const CAPTION_RE = /^\*(D\d+[a-z]?)\.\s+(.+?)\*$/;

// One Mermaid theme for every diagram, from the mockup kit's tokens (kit.css).
const MERMAID_CONFIG = {
  startOnLoad: false,
  securityLevel: 'loose',
  theme: 'base',
  fontFamily: '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif',
  themeVariables: {
    fontFamily: '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif',
    fontSize: '15px',
    background: '#ffffff',
    primaryColor: '#f1f2fe',
    primaryBorderColor: '#a5abef',
    primaryTextColor: '#1c2030',
    secondaryColor: '#f4f5f7',
    secondaryBorderColor: '#c9cdd4',
    secondaryTextColor: '#1c2030',
    tertiaryColor: '#fafbfc',
    tertiaryBorderColor: '#d5d8de',
    tertiaryTextColor: '#1c2030',
    lineColor: '#79808d',
    textColor: '#1c2030',
    mainBkg: '#f1f2fe',
    nodeBorder: '#a5abef',
    clusterBkg: '#fafbfc',
    clusterBorder: '#d5d8de',
    titleColor: '#1c2030',
    edgeLabelBackground: '#ffffff',
    noteBkgColor: '#fdf3e3',
    noteBorderColor: '#e8c48f',
    noteTextColor: '#8a4b06',
    actorBkg: '#f1f2fe',
    actorBorder: '#a5abef',
    actorTextColor: '#1c2030',
    actorLineColor: '#c9cdd4',
    signalColor: '#464d5e',
    signalTextColor: '#1c2030',
    labelBoxBkgColor: '#f4f5f7',
    labelBoxBorderColor: '#c9cdd4',
    labelTextColor: '#1c2030',
    loopTextColor: '#464d5e',
    activationBkgColor: '#e4e6fc',
    activationBorderColor: '#a5abef',
    sequenceNumberColor: '#ffffff',
  },
  flowchart: { curve: 'basis', padding: 12, nodeSpacing: 40, rankSpacing: 50, htmlLabels: true },
  sequence: { useMaxWidth: true, mirrorActors: false, actorMargin: 40, messageFontSize: 13, noteFontSize: 13 },
  state: { useMaxWidth: true },
};

// ---------- collect documents ----------

function orderDocs(files) {
  const num = (f) => parseInt(f.slice(0, 2), 10);
  const decisions = files.filter((f) => /^11-decisions-/.test(f)).sort();
  const rest = files.filter((f) => f !== START && f !== DOC_PLAN && !decisions.includes(f));
  rest.sort((a, b) => num(a) - num(b) || a.localeCompare(b));
  const before = rest.filter((f) => num(f) <= 11);
  const after = rest.filter((f) => num(f) > 11);
  const out = [];
  if (files.includes(START)) out.push(START);
  out.push(...before, ...decisions, ...after);
  if (files.includes(DOC_PLAN)) out.push(DOC_PLAN);
  return out;
}

const files = orderDocs(fs.readdirSync(DOCS).filter((f) => /^\d\d-.+\.md$/.test(f)));
if (!files.length) fail('No docs/NN-*.md files found.');

// ---------- helpers ----------

const slug = (s) =>
  s.toLowerCase().trim()
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')
    .replace(/[`*_~"'“”‘’()[\]{}:;,.!?/\\|<>@#$%^&+=]/g, '')
    .replace(/\s+/g, '-')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
const base = (f) => f.replace(/\.md$/, '');
const docAnchor = (f) => `doc-${base(f)}`;
const headAnchor = (f, h) => `${base(f)}--${h}`;
const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;').replace(/"/g, '&quot;');

const errors = [];
const warnings = [];
function fail(msg) { console.error(`ERROR: ${msg}`); process.exit(1); }

const mimeOf = (p) => ({ '.png': 'image/png', '.jpg': 'image/jpeg', '.jpeg': 'image/jpeg', '.gif': 'image/gif', '.svg': 'image/svg+xml', '.webp': 'image/webp' })[path.extname(p).toLowerCase()];
function dataUri(rel, where) {
  const p = path.resolve(DOCS, rel);
  if (!fs.existsSync(p)) { errors.push(`${where}: image not found: ${rel}`); return rel; }
  return `data:${mimeOf(p) || 'application/octet-stream'};base64,${fs.readFileSync(p).toString('base64')}`;
}

// ---------- markdown ----------

const md = new MarkdownIt({ html: true, linkify: false, typographer: false });

// Per-document state used by the renderer rules.
let cur = null;
const globalFigIds = new Set();

// Heading ids: h1 = doc anchor; others = <doc>--<slug>, unique per doc.
md.core.ruler.push('anchors_captions_meta', (state) => {
  const t = state.tokens;
  for (let i = 0; i < t.length; i++) {
    const tok = t[i];
    if (tok.type === 'heading_open') {
      const text = t[i + 1].content;
      const level = Number(tok.tag.slice(1));
      let id;
      if (level === 1 && !cur.h1) {
        id = docAnchor(cur.file);
        cur.h1 = text;
      } else {
        let s = slug(text) || 'section';
        let n = s, k = 2;
        while (cur.slugs.has(n)) n = `${s}-${k++}`;
        cur.slugs.add(n);
        id = headAnchor(cur.file, n);
        if (level === 2) cur.h2.push({ id, text });
      }
      tok.attrSet('id', id);
      cur.ids.add(id);
    }
    // "Owner:" / "Answers:" lines near the top become the document's meta block.
    if (tok.type === 'paragraph_open' && i < 12) {
      const c = t[i + 1].content;
      if (/^Owner:/.test(c)) tok.attrJoin('class', 'doc-meta doc-owner');
      if (/^Answers:/.test(c)) tok.attrJoin('class', 'doc-meta doc-answers');
    }
    // "*D7. Title*" paragraph: a figure caption.
    if (tok.type === 'paragraph_open' && t[i + 1] && t[i + 2]?.type === 'paragraph_close') {
      const m = CAPTION_RE.exec(t[i + 1].content.trim());
      if (m) {
        const [, did, title] = m;
        // The first drawing of a diagram gets "fig-d7"; a later one (another
        // document drawing it again) gets "fig-d7-2", so ids stay unique.
        let id = `fig-${did.toLowerCase()}`;
        for (let k = 2; globalFigIds.has(id); k++) id = `fig-${did.toLowerCase()}-${k}`;
        globalFigIds.add(id);
        const prev = t[i - 1];
        const caption = { did, title, id, file: cur.file };
        if (cur.figIds.has(did)) warnings.push(`${cur.file}: diagram ${did} is captioned twice in this document`);
        cur.figIds.add(did);
        cur.ids.add(id);
        cur.captions.push(caption);
        if (prev && prev.type === 'fence' && prev.info.trim() === 'mermaid') {
          prev.meta = { ...(prev.meta || {}), caption };
          tok.hidden = true; t[i + 1].hidden = true; t[i + 2].hidden = true;
          t[i + 1].children = [];
        } else {
          tok.attrSet('id', id);
          tok.attrJoin('class', 'figure-caption standalone');
          t[i + 1].children = [];
          t[i + 1].content = '';
          tok.meta = { caption };
        }
      }
    }
  }
});

const defaultParagraphOpen = md.renderer.rules.paragraph_open || ((tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => self.renderToken(tokens, idx, opts));
md.renderer.rules.paragraph_open = (tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => {
  const tok = tokens[idx];
  if (tok.hidden) return '';
  if (tok.meta?.caption) {
    const c = tok.meta.caption;
    return `<p id="${c.id}" class="figure-caption standalone"><span class="fig-id">${esc(c.did)}.</span> ${md.renderInline(c.title)}`;
  }
  return defaultParagraphOpen(tokens, idx, opts, env, self);
};
const defaultParagraphClose = md.renderer.rules.paragraph_close || ((tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => self.renderToken(tokens, idx, opts));
md.renderer.rules.paragraph_close = (tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => (tokens[idx].hidden ? '' : defaultParagraphClose(tokens, idx, opts, env, self));

// Mermaid fences become placeholders; rendered to SVG later in one browser session.
const defaultFence = md.renderer.rules.fence;
md.renderer.rules.fence = (tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => {
  const tok = tokens[idx];
  if (tok.info.trim() === 'mermaid') {
    const n = diagrams.length;
    const line = (tok.map?.[0] ?? 0) + 1;
    diagrams.push({ n, file: cur.file, line, code: tok.content, caption: tok.meta?.caption });
    return `<!--MERMAID:${n}-->`;
  }
  return defaultFence(tokens, idx, opts, env, self);
};

// Tables scroll sideways inside a wrapper rather than breaking the page.
md.renderer.rules.table_open = () => '<div class="table-wrap"><table>';
md.renderer.rules.table_close = () => '</table></div>';

// Links: other docs and in-doc anchors become in-page anchors.
const defaultLinkOpen = md.renderer.rules.link_open || ((tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => self.renderToken(tokens, idx, opts));
md.renderer.rules.link_open = (tokens, idx, opts, env, self) => {
  const tok = tokens[idx];
  const href = tok.attrGet('href') || '';
  tok.attrSet('href', rewriteHref(href, cur.file));
  if (/^https?:/.test(href)) tok.attrSet('rel', 'noopener');
  return defaultLinkOpen(tokens, idx, opts, env, self);
};
md.renderer.rules.image = (tokens, idx) => {
  const tok = tokens[idx];
  const src = tok.attrGet('src') || '';
  const alt = tok.content || '';
  const resolved = /^(data:|https?:)/.test(src) ? src : dataUri(src, cur.file);
  return `<img src="${resolved}" alt="${esc(alt)}">`;
};

function rewriteHref(href, file) {
  if (/^(https?:|mailto:|data:)/.test(href)) return href;
  if (/^#fig-d\d+[a-z]?$/i.test(href)) {
    // A diagram, wherever it is drawn: "#fig-d4b".
    const target = href.slice(1).toLowerCase();
    cur.links.push({ from: file, href, target, figure: true });
    return `#${target}`;
  }
  if (href.startsWith('#')) {
    const frag = href.slice(1);
    const target = headAnchor(file, frag);
    cur.links.push({ from: file, href, target });
    return `#${target}`;
  }
  const [p, frag] = href.split('#');
  const name = path.basename(p);
  const inDocs = path.resolve(DOCS, path.dirname(file), p);
  if (path.dirname(inDocs) === DOCS && /^\d\d-.+\.md$/.test(name)) {
    const target = frag ? headAnchor(name, frag) : docAnchor(name);
    cur.links.push({ from: file, href, target, doc: name });
    return `#${target}`;
  }
  // A file elsewhere in the repo: link relative to docs/site/.
  if (!fs.existsSync(inDocs)) warnings.push(`${file}: link to a file that does not exist: ${href}`);
  return path.relative(OUT_DIR, inDocs).split(path.sep).join('/') + (frag ? `#${frag}` : '');
}

// ---------- render documents ----------

const diagrams = [];
const docs = [];
for (const file of files) {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(path.join(DOCS, file), 'utf8');
  cur = { file, h1: null, h2: [], slugs: new Set(), ids: new Set(), links: [], captions: [], figIds: new Set() };
  let html = md.render(src);
  // Images in raw HTML blocks: src="assets/..." -> data URI.
  html = html.replace(/(<img\b[^>]*?\bsrc=")(?!data:|https?:)([^"]+)(")/g, (_, a, s, b) => a + dataUri(s, file) + b);
  // An image paragraph followed by its caption becomes one figure, so a link
  // to the diagram lands on the picture, not under it.
  html = html.replace(/(?:<p>\s*)?(<img\b[^>]*>)\s*(?:<\/p>)?\s*<p id="(fig-[^"]+)" class="figure-caption standalone">([\s\S]*?)<\/p>/g,
    (_, img, id, cap) => `<figure class="image" id="${id}">${img}<figcaption class="figure-caption">${cap}</figcaption></figure>`);
  // A table followed by its caption (a matrix diagram) becomes one figure too.
  const tableCaption = /<\/table><\/div>\s*<p id="(fig-[^"]+)" class="figure-caption standalone">([\s\S]*?)<\/p>/;
  for (let m; (m = tableCaption.exec(html));) {
    const [whole, id, cap] = m;
    const start = html.lastIndexOf('<div class="table-wrap">', m.index);
    html = html.slice(0, start) + `<figure class="matrix" id="${id}">` + html.slice(start, m.index) +
      `</table></div><figcaption class="figure-caption">${cap}</figcaption></figure>` + html.slice(m.index + whole.length);
  }
  if (!cur.h1) warnings.push(`${file}: no "# Title" line`);
  docs.push({ ...cur, html, title: TITLE_OVERRIDES[file] || cur.h1 || base(file), originalTitle: cur.h1 });
}

// ---------- links ----------

const allIds = new Set(docs.flatMap((d) => [...d.ids]));
for (const d of docs) {
  for (const l of d.links) {
    if (!allIds.has(l.target)) {
      if (l.figure) {
        warnings.push(`${l.from}: links to diagram ${'D' + l.href.slice(6)}, which no document draws yet`);
      } else if (l.doc && !files.includes(l.doc)) {
        // A document that has not been written yet: not broken, but say so.
        warnings.push(`${l.from}: links to ${l.href}, which does not exist yet`);
      } else {
        errors.push(`${l.from}: broken link ${l.href} (no anchor #${l.target})`);
      }
    }
  }
}

// ---------- mermaid ----------

async function renderMermaid() {
  if (!diagrams.length) return [];
  if (!fs.existsSync(CHROME)) fail(`Chrome not found at ${CHROME}. Set CHROME_PATH.`);
  const browser = await chromium.launch({ executablePath: CHROME, headless: true });
  try {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1400, height: 1000 } });
    await page.setContent('<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"></head><body style="font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif"></body></html>');
    await page.addScriptTag({ path: path.join(HERE, 'node_modules', 'mermaid', 'dist', 'mermaid.min.js') });
    await page.evaluate((cfg) => window.mermaid.initialize(cfg), MERMAID_CONFIG);
    const out = [];
    for (const d of diagrams) {
      const res = await page.evaluate(async ({ id, code }) => {
        try {
          const { svg } = await window.mermaid.render(id, code);
          return { svg };
        } catch (e) {
          document.querySelectorAll(`#d${id}, #${id}`).forEach((n) => n.remove());
          return { error: String(e && e.message ? e.message : e) };
        }
      }, { id: `mmd-${d.n}`, code: d.code });
      if (res.error) errors.push(`${d.file}, Mermaid block at line ${d.line}${d.caption ? ` (${d.caption.did})` : ''}: ${res.error.split('\n')[0]}`);
      out.push(res);
    }
    return out;
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
  }
}

const rendered = await renderMermaid();
for (const doc of docs) {
  doc.html = doc.html.replace(/<!--MERMAID:(\d+)-->/g, (_, n) => {
    const d = diagrams[Number(n)];
    const r = rendered[Number(n)] || {};
    const cap = d.caption;
    // Never shrink a diagram below 80% of its natural size: scroll sideways instead.
    const svg = r.svg
      ? r.svg.replace(/style="max-width: ([\d.]+)px;"/, (m, w) => `style="max-width: ${Math.ceil(w)}px; min-width: ${Math.round(w * 0.8)}px;"`)
      : `<pre class="diagram-error">Diagram failed to render.</pre>`;
    return `<figure class="diagram"${cap ? ` id="${cap.id}"` : ''}><div class="diagram-body">${svg}</div>${cap ? `<figcaption class="figure-caption"><span class="fig-id">${esc(cap.did)}.</span> ${md.renderInline(cap.title)}</figcaption>` : ''}</figure>`;
  });
}

// ---------- diagram ids from the doc plan ----------

const captions = docs.flatMap((d) => d.captions.map((c) => ({ ...c, docTitle: d.title })));
const plan = docs.find((d) => d.file === DOC_PLAN);
if (plan) {
  const planSrc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(DOCS, DOC_PLAN), 'utf8');
  const planned = [...planSrc.matchAll(/^\|\s*(D\d+[a-z]?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+)\|/gm)].map((m) => ({ id: m[1], title: m[2].trim() }));
  const drawn = new Set(captions.map((c) => c.did));
  const missing = planned.filter((p) => !drawn.has(p.id));
  if (missing.length) {
    warnings.push(`Diagrams in the doc plan that no document draws yet (${missing.length} of ${planned.length}):\n` +
      missing.map((m) => `    ${m.id}  ${m.title}`).join('\n'));
  }
  const unplanned = captions.filter((c) => !planned.some((p) => p.id === c.did));
  for (const u of unplanned) warnings.push(`${u.file}: caption ${u.did} is not in the doc plan's diagram table`);
}

// ---------- page ----------

const css = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'page.css'), 'utf8').replace(/^﻿/, '');
const js = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'page.js'), 'utf8').replace(/^﻿/, '');
const builtOn = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

const toc = docs.map((d) => `
      <li class="toc-doc"><a href="#${docAnchor(d.file)}">${esc(d.title)}</a>${d.h2.length ? `
        <ul>${d.h2.map((h) => `<li><a href="#${h.id}">${md.renderInline(h.text).replace(/<\/?a[^>]*>/g, '')}</a></li>`).join('')}</ul>` : ''}</li>`).join('');

const listOfDiagrams = captions.length ? `
  <section class="doc" id="list-of-diagrams">
    <h1>List of diagrams</h1>
    <div class="table-wrap"><table>
      <thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Diagram</th><th>In</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${captions.map((c) => `<tr><td><a href="#${c.id}">${esc(c.did)}</a></td><td>${md.renderInline(c.title)}</td><td class="nowrap"><a href="#${docAnchor(c.file)}">${esc(c.docTitle)}</a></td></tr>`).join('')}</tbody>
    </table></div>
  </section>` : '';

const body = docs.map((d) => {
  let html = d.html;
  if (TITLE_OVERRIDES[d.file] && d.originalTitle) {
    html = html.replace(/(<h1[^>]*>)([\s\S]*?)(<\/h1>)/, `$1${esc(TITLE_OVERRIDES[d.file])}$3<p class="doc-subtitle">${esc(d.originalTitle)}</p>`);
  }
  return `<section class="doc" data-file="${esc(d.file)}">${html}</section>`;
}).join('\n');

const page = `<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Workflow platform: technical design</title>
<style>${css}</style>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip" href="#content">Skip to the text</a>
<nav class="toc" aria-label="Contents">
  <div class="toc-head">
    <div class="toc-title">Workflow platform</div>
    <div class="toc-sub">Technical design · built ${builtOn}</div>
  </div>
  <ul>${toc}
      ${captions.length ? '<li class="toc-doc"><a href="#list-of-diagrams">List of diagrams</a></li>' : ''}
  </ul>
</nav>
<main id="content">
${body}
${listOfDiagrams}
</main>
<script>${js}</script>
</body>
</html>
`;

// ---------- report ----------

const uniqueWarnings = [...new Set(warnings)];
warnings.length = 0; warnings.push(...uniqueWarnings);
for (const w of warnings) console.warn(`warning: ${w}`);
for (const e of errors) console.error(`ERROR: ${e}`);
console.log(`${docs.length} documents, ${diagrams.length} diagrams (${captions.length} captioned), ${errors.length} errors, ${warnings.length} warnings.`);
if (errors.length) process.exit(1);
if (!CHECK_ONLY) {
  fs.mkdirSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(OUT, page);
  console.log(`Wrote ${path.relative(path.resolve(DOCS, '..'), OUT)} (${Math.round(page.length / 1024)} KB).`);
}
===\ndocs/build/chrome-path.mjs\n===
// Where the system Chrome (or Chromium) is, so the docs build never downloads a browser.
// CHROME_PATH wins; otherwise the usual install places on Windows, macOS and Linux are tried in order.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

function candidates() {
  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    const roots = [process.env.PROGRAMFILES, process.env['PROGRAMFILES(X86)'], process.env.LOCALAPPDATA].filter(Boolean);
    return roots.map((root) => path.join(root, 'Google', 'Chrome', 'Application', 'chrome.exe'));
  }
  if (process.platform === 'darwin') {
    return [
      '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome',
      '/Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium',
    ];
  }
  return ['/usr/bin/google-chrome', '/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable', '/usr/bin/chromium', '/usr/bin/chromium-browser', '/snap/bin/chromium'];
}

/** The Chrome executable to launch: CHROME_PATH, else the first usual place that exists, else the first usual place (so the error names it). */
export function chromePath() {
  if (process.env.CHROME_PATH) return process.env.CHROME_PATH;
  const all = candidates();
  return all.find((p) => fs.existsSync(p)) ?? all[0];
}

===\ndocs/build/page.js\n===
// Optional behaviour. The page reads fine without it.
(function () {
  // 1. Highlight the current document and section in the contents.
  document.querySelector('.toc').classList.add('js');
  var links = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.toc a[href^="#"]'));
  var byId = {};
  links.forEach(function (a) { byId[a.getAttribute('href').slice(1)] = a; });
  var heads = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('main h1[id], main h2[id], #list-of-diagrams'))
    .filter(function (h) { return byId[h.id]; });
  var active = [];
  function update() {
    var y = window.scrollY + 80, curDoc = null, curSec = null;
    for (var i = 0; i < heads.length; i++) {
      var h = heads[i];
      if (h.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY > y) break;
      if (h.tagName === 'H2') curSec = h; else { curDoc = h; curSec = null; }
    }
    active.forEach(function (a) { a.classList.remove('active'); });
    active = [];
    var openDoc = curDoc && byId[curDoc.id] ? byId[curDoc.id].parentNode : null;
    document.querySelectorAll('.toc-doc.open').forEach(function (li) { if (li !== openDoc) li.classList.remove('open'); });
    if (openDoc) openDoc.classList.add('open');
    [curDoc, curSec].forEach(function (h) {
      if (h && byId[h.id]) { byId[h.id].classList.add('active'); active.push(byId[h.id]); }
    });
    if (active.length) {
      var last = active[active.length - 1], toc = document.querySelector('.toc');
      var r = last.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (r.top < 60 || r.bottom > window.innerHeight - 20) toc.scrollTop += r.top - window.innerHeight / 3;
    }
  }
  var pending = false;
  window.addEventListener('scroll', function () {
    if (!pending) { pending = true; requestAnimationFrame(function () { pending = false; update(); }); }
  }, { passive: true });
  update();

  // 2. "Open larger" for each diagram.
  function close(fig, btn) {
    fig.classList.remove('large'); document.body.classList.remove('has-large'); btn.textContent = 'Open larger';
  }
  document.querySelectorAll('figure.diagram, figure.image').forEach(function (fig) {
    var btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.type = 'button'; btn.className = 'diagram-toggle'; btn.textContent = 'Open larger';
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
      if (fig.classList.contains('large')) { close(fig, btn); return; }
      fig.classList.add('large'); document.body.classList.add('has-large'); btn.textContent = 'Close';
    });
    fig.insertBefore(btn, fig.firstChild);
  });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
    var fig = document.querySelector('figure.large');
    if (fig) close(fig, fig.querySelector('.diagram-toggle'));
  });
})();
===\ndocs/build/shoot.mjs\n===
// Screenshots of the built page, for checking how it looks.
//   node shoot.mjs <out dir> [selector ...]
// Always shoots the top of the page; each selector shoots the first match
// scrolled into view (e.g. "#fig-d1", "#doc-04-word-map table").

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';
import { chromePath } from './chrome-path.mjs';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const PAGE = path.resolve(HERE, '..', 'site', 'index.html');
const CHROME = chromePath();
const [outDir = path.join(HERE, 'shots'), ...selectors] = process.argv.slice(2);
fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

const browser = await chromium.launch({ executablePath: CHROME, headless: true });
try {
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } });
  await page.goto(pathToFileURL(PAGE).href);
  await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(outDir, 'top.png') });
  console.log(path.join(outDir, 'top.png'));
  for (const [i, sel] of selectors.entries()) {
    const el = page.locator(sel).first();
    await el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await page.evaluate((s) => { const n = document.querySelector(s); if (n) window.scrollTo(0, n.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY - 20); }, sel);
    await page.waitForTimeout(150);
    const file = path.join(outDir, `${String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${sel.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/gi, '_').replace(/^_|_$/g, '')}.png`);
    await page.screenshot({ path: file });
    console.log(file);
  }
} finally {
  await browser.close();
}

<section class="doc" data-file="00-start-here.md"><h1 id="doc-00-start-here">Start here</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Frontend owner.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: What is this system, in one picture, and where do I read next?</p>
<p>This is the technical design of a no-code workflow platform. On it, people who do not write code build <strong>workflows</strong>: a form someone fills in, the people who must approve or do the work, and what happens in other systems along the way. Each time someone uses a workflow, that is a <strong>request</strong>. This page gives the whole system in one picture, the six things the design must make clear, and where to read next.</p>
<h2 id="00-start-here--the-system-in-one-picture">The system in one picture</h2>
<p>We build three parts: the <strong>editor and pages</strong> people use in the browser, the <strong>engine</strong> that runs requests and keeps their history, and the <strong>connections</strong> through which data and control cross to other systems. Around them are the people who use the platform, the existing application it lives in, and other systems.</p>

<p>Read the picture from top to bottom. People only ever use the editor and pages. The editor and pages talk to the engine through one contract. The engine reaches everything outside the platform through connections, never directly. Document 1 (<a href="#doc-01-context">Context</a>) draws the same picture with every line labelled.</p>
<h2 id="00-start-here--six-things-to-know">Six things to know</h2>
<ol>
<li><strong>We build a platform; customers build workflows.</strong> The platform is the editor, the engine and the connections. A customer's workflow is data that an author builds in the editor and publishes without a deployment. &quot;Change request&quot;, used as the example everywhere, is sample data; the platform's code never names it.</li>
<li><strong>A workflow exists in three forms</strong>: the draft an author edits, the published version the engine runs, and the history of each request. One pipeline connects them: edit, check, publish, run, record, show. See the next section.</li>
<li><strong>Everything crosses the platform's edge through a small number of doors.</strong> There are seven: a request starts, a person acts, the workflow calls another system, the directory says who is in a group, a question gets its choices, a message is sent, and other systems are told what happened. Each door has a rule for what is recorded, what is retried and what happens when it fails. Nothing gets in any other way. Document 5 (<a href="#doc-05-integrations">Integrations</a>) covers each door.</li>
<li><strong>The editor's words map one-to-one onto the engine's concepts.</strong> Stage, task, button, arrow, value, action, To do, stuck, Try it: each has one engine counterpart and one field in the saved workflow. Document 4 (<a href="#doc-04-word-map">Word map</a>) is the table.</li>
<li><strong>The frontend and the engine meet at one contract</strong> of four parts: the authored workflow format (the saved draft), the authoring API (check, try, publish), the runtime API (start, act, read), and the catalogue of connections. It lives in the repository's <code>contract/</code> folder; document 6 (<a href="#doc-06-the-contract">The contract</a>) explains it.</li>
<li><strong>Each feature is in the first build, held as a shape, or later.</strong> &quot;First build&quot; is what this repository builds and runs. &quot;Shape only&quot; means the recorded history can already hold it but nothing produces it yet. &quot;Later&quot; means designed enough not to block it, not built. Examples of later: deadlines and reminders (the engine has no clock), and another system nudging a request that did not ask it.</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="00-start-here--three-forms-of-a-workflow">Three forms of a workflow</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Draft.</strong> What the author edits in the editor, saved continuously. It may be unfinished; the editor's To do list says what is missing.</li>
<li><strong>Published version.</strong> Publishing checks the draft and compiles it into a definition the engine runs. A version never changes; the next publish makes a new one.</li>
<li><strong>Request history.</strong> Every request runs on the version it started on, and the engine records everything that happens to it, in order, for good.</li>
<li>The pages and Try it show a request by reading that history back, in the author's words.</li>
<li>Document 3 (<a href="#doc-03-life-of-a-workflow">The life of a workflow</a>) follows one workflow through all three forms, with diagrams <a href="#fig-d4">D4</a> and <a href="#fig-d5">D5</a>.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="00-start-here--what-exists-today-and-how-to-see-it">What exists today, and how to see it</h2>
<p>Document 10 (Build plan and status), which the two leads will write, says what runs today and how to run it. Until it exists:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The editor's design</strong> is a set of clickable mockups, outside this repository, in the <code>workflow</code> folder beside it: <code>../workflow/mockups/index.html</code> (relative to this repo's root). Its rules and words are in <code>../workflow/spec/editor-model.md</code>.</li>
<li><strong>The contract</strong> is in <code>contract/</code>: the authored format with sample workflows in <code>contract/fixtures/</code>, the core, authoring and runtime APIs, and the catalogue of connections. Document 6 (<a href="#doc-06-the-contract">The contract</a>) explains it.</li>
<li><strong>The engine</strong> follows kernel spec v2.20, kept in the <code>workflow-platform</code> repository, with a copy in <code>engine/spec/</code>. Its core package, which decides everything a request does, is built: 1899 tests pass. The server's store and its authoring and runtime APIs are built too, with 237 tests passing; its workers, its endpoints for other systems, the mock systems and its development host are not yet, so nothing can run against the server.</li>
<li><strong>The frontend</strong> is built: every screen of the editor and of the pages people use. It runs on the engine's core in the browser, and a stand-in plays the server until the real one can be run. Document 8 (<a href="#doc-08-frontend-design">Frontend design</a>) says what is not built yet.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>To see it running:</strong> in <code>frontend/</code>, run <code>npm install</code> once, then <code>npm run dev</code>, and open <code>http://localhost:5173</code>. Pages have hash addresses, such as <code>#/tasks</code>. It opens on the workflows list, with three sample workflows, Change request among them. The footer has &quot;Reset sample data&quot;, which starts the samples again.</p>
<h2 id="00-start-here--ten-words-to-know-first">Ten words to know first</h2>
<p>The editor's word is what people see on screen. The engine's word is what engineers and the engine's documents use. Document 4 has the full list.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What it means</th>
<th>Engine word</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Workflow</strong></td>
<td>What an author builds. Edited as a <strong>draft</strong>; each publish makes a new <strong>version</strong> that never changes.</td>
<td>Definition (one per published version)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Request</strong></td>
<td>One use of a workflow, from the start form to an ending.</td>
<td>Request, with its history of events</td>

<td>Stage. One authored stage becomes a short chain of engine stages.</td>

<tr>
<td><strong>Task</strong></td>
<td>The part of a stage that asks people: who is asked, a form, buttons.</td>
<td>Person wait</td>
</tr>

<td>Outcome</td>

<td>Transition</td>

<td>Data path in the request's data</td>

<td>Connection (a configured connector) and its catalogue entries</td>

<tr>
<td><strong>Stuck</strong></td>

The people who look after stuck requests are told. They can close it; where running again can help (a failed action, nobody to ask) they can also retry it.</td>
<td><code>stuck { reason, at }</code>; inside the kernel, a fault or a person wait with nobody asked</td>

<section class="doc" data-file="01-context.md"><h1 id="doc-01-context">Context</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Frontend owner (draws); the Engine owner supplies the facts.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: Who and what does the platform touch?</p>
<p>The platform touches two kinds of thing: <strong>people</strong>, who only ever use its screens, and <strong>other systems</strong>, which it reaches only through a fixed set of doors. This document names every person by role and every other system in the first build, and says what crosses between them and the platform, in which direction, and who starts it.</p>
<p>Two terms first. A <strong>door</strong> is one of the seven ways data or control can cross the platform's edge (decision E-9 in <a href="#doc-11-decisions-engine">Decisions: engine</a>); nothing crosses any other way. A <strong>connection</strong> is another system the platform is linked to, set up once by an administrator; a workflow uses what a connection offers but never sees how it is set up.</p>
<h2 id="01-context--the-platform-and-the-systems-around-it">The platform and the systems around it</h2>
<p>Things that come in are on the left; things that go out are on the right. A solid line is control: it starts a request, answers one, or makes something happen in another system. A dotted line is data. Data that comes in is recorded and can still decide what happens next: a looked-up value is read by arrows, and the read of a group's members decides whether anybody can answer a task. The numbers are the doors.</p>

<p>In a real deployment, sign-in, the directory, and email and Slack come from the existing application the platform lives in. The first build has real connectors for the directory, Jira, and email and Slack. On the development and test hosts, every system on this picture except sign-in is a small mock server with real HTTP in and out, so the wiring is real and each can be inspected (E-12). Document 5 (<a href="#doc-05-integrations">Integrations</a>) gives each door's rules: what is recorded, what is retried, and what failure does.</p>
<h2 id="01-context--who-does-what">Who does what</h2>
<p>Six roles use the platform. One person can hold several; for example, the author of a workflow usually also looks after its stuck requests. Every signed-in person can open any request's page in the first build, and sees there whether it is stuck and why; the Stuck requests list, the technical detail, and Retry and Close are only for the people who look after stuck requests and for platform admins.</p>

<p>One line each: what crosses, in which direction, and who starts it. &quot;Engine&quot; means the engine starts the exchange; it always records what comes back before it acts on it.</p>

<td>7</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Two rules hold for all of them. <strong>Nothing outside moves a request unless the workflow asked it to</strong>: another system can start a request, or answer a request that asked it something, and nothing else. <strong>A message, or telling other systems what happened, never holds a request up</strong>: of everything that crosses the edge, only two things can leave a request stuck: an action that uses a connection and fails where its author chose &quot;stuck&quot;, and a read of a group's members that finds nobody able to answer a task, or that fails.</p>
<h2 id="01-context--we-build-the-platform-customers-build-workflows">We build the platform; customers build workflows</h2>
<p>The platform is the editor and pages, the engine and the connections. A customer's workflow is data: an author builds it in the editor and publishes it without anyone deploying code. So:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>&quot;Change request&quot; is sample data.</strong> It is the example in every mockup and diagram, and it lives in <code>contract/fixtures/</code> as a test workflow. Platform code never names it, nor any of its stages, values or buttons.</li>
<li><strong>The sample systems are sample data too.</strong> Helpdesk, Service catalog, Jira, Deploy pipeline and Reporting appear to the editor and the engine only as catalogue entries such as <code>jira.createIssue@1</code>. The editor lists whatever the catalogue offers and hard-codes no system (E-10).</li>
<li><strong>What is ours, and what is the customer's.</strong> Ours: the editor, the pages, the engine, the connectors and the catalogue. The customer's: their workflows, their Domains-list-style tables inside those workflows, and the choice of who looks after stuck requests.</li>
</ul>
</section>
<section class="doc" data-file="02-the-parts.md"><h1 id="doc-02-the-parts">The parts</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Engine owner.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: What runs where, and who owns it?</p>
<p>Two teams build the platform. The <strong>frontend team</strong> owns the editor and the pages people use in the browser. The <strong>engine team</strong> owns everything on the server, plus one package of engine code, <strong>core</strong>, that also runs in the browser. The <strong>existing application</strong> the platform will live in supplies three things: sign-in, the directory of people and groups, and the message service that sends email and Slack. This document shows where each part runs, who owns it, what it depends on, and where state is kept. Core and the server are built: they run in the engine packages' own tests and on the development host, against in-memory mock systems, and the frontend runs on core. Nothing runs yet inside the existing application.</p>
<p>Terms used below. A <strong>turn</strong> is how the engine handles one input (a start, a button pressed, a connection's result, an admin's retry or close): one database transaction that records the input and everything that follows from it. A <strong>job</strong> is background work a turn queues in its own transaction and a worker runs after the turn commits. A <strong>connector</strong> is code that talks to one kind of outside system; a <strong>connection</strong> is one configured instance of it, written in the deployment's configuration by a platform admin.</p>

supply?</figcaption></figure>
<p>The owner is written in each box as well as shown by colour: green is the frontend's, blue the engine's, grey and dashed the existing application's, white the outside systems. The outside systems shown are the mock systems of the first build (E-12); a real deployment connects whatever its platform admins set up.</p>
<p>The pages never reach Postgres, a job or an outside system: they call the two APIs over HTTP and core in the browser. The engine never reaches an outside system except through a connector, the directory and the message service included. How the server side is split into processes, and where the job workers run, is not designed. The APIs are plain functions with thin web-standard <code>Request -&gt; Response</code> handlers, so they can be mounted in the existing Next.js application later (E-11); where they are mounted is unknown: depends on the existing application.</p>
<h2 id="02-the-parts--each-part">Each part</h2>
<p>&quot;First build*&quot; marks a part built, in its thinnest form, beyond the MVP's requirements, at the product owner's request (E-9, E-33).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Part</th>
<th>What it does</th>
<th>Owner</th>
<th>Depends on</th>
<th>Build</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tr>
<td>Editor</td>
<td>The diagram, &quot;In words&quot;, forms, values, To do, Try it, Publish, settings</td>
<td>Frontend</td>
<td>core, authoring API, the catalogue</td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Pages</td>
<td>Start a request, My tasks, a task, the request page, request lists, Stuck requests with Retry and Close</td>
<td>Frontend</td>

<td>First build</td>
</tr>

<td>core package</td>
<td>The authored-format types, <code>parse</code>, <code>check</code>, <code>facts</code>, <code>formState</code>, <code>evaluate</code>, <code>compile</code>, <code>story</code>, <code>diff</code>, the turn function with <code>decide</code> and <code>evolve</code>, the expression environment, the Try it host (E-3, E-15)</td>
<td>Engine</td>
<td>The expression library, <code>@marcbachmann/cel-js</code> 8.0.0, and nothing else</td>
<td>First build. Built, with tests, except <code>diff</code> and <code>upgrade</code> (E-27).</td>

<td>The workflows list, drafts, publish, versions, workflow settings, the catalogue, the server's core version (<code>contract/authoring-api.md</code>)</td>
<td>Engine</td>
<td>core, Postgres, the directory (authors listed as groups)</td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Runtime API</td>
<td>Start, choices, My tasks, act, retry, close, pausing a binding, listing and retrying refused starts, reads for lists and the request page, sign-in and directory reads for pages (<code>contract/runtime-api.md</code>)</td>
<td>Engine</td>
<td>core, Postgres, the directory (memberships when a person acts, looked up before the request is locked), data sources (choices and their look-up, likewise)</td>
<td>First build</td>

<td>Engine</td>

<td>First build*</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>Engine</td>

<td>First build</td>

<tr>

<td>Engine</td>
<td>core's rule matching, the directory (groups expanded when sending), the message service, the words file <code>contract/words/notifications.json</code></td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Publisher</td>
<td>One job per turn: works out the turn's public events and posts each, in the request's order, to every address in the configuration, at least once</td>
<td>Engine</td>
<td>core, Postgres</td>
<td>First build*</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Connectors and connections</td>
<td>Code for one kind of system, and its configured connections with their settings and the names of their secrets, read from the deployment's configuration at start-up and held in memory with the catalogue. A snapshot test fails the build when an entry's shape changes under its version</td>
<td>Engine builds; a platform admin writes the configuration</td>
<td>The outside system</td>
<td>First build: connectors for the directory, Jira, and email and Slack, and the mock connectors for development and tests. The interfaces of the existing application's directory and message service: unknown: depends on the existing application.</td>

<td>Engine</td>

stop-opacity="1"></stop></linearGradient></svg></div><figcaption class="figure-caption"><span class="fig-id">D3b.</span> Which package may use which?</figcaption></figure>
<ul>
<li><strong>core</strong> (<code>engine/packages/core</code>) is pure TypeScript with no I/O and no Node-only or browser-only API, so it runs in a browser and on the server (E-3). Every function is synchronous and deterministic: no I/O, no clock, no randomness (<code>contract/core-api.md</code> section 1).</li>
<li><strong>server</strong> (<code>engine/packages/server</code>) holds the Postgres store, the turn transaction, the jobs, the connectors, the inbound hook and the HTTP API. It imports core. It is the authority: at publish it runs the check and the compile again and stores its own result (E-3).</li>
</ul>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Rule</th>
<th>How it is held</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>core imports no Node built-in and uses no Node or browser API.</td>
<td>ESLint, a boundaries test in core, and core's TypeScript settings (<code>types: []</code>, <code>lib: [&quot;ES2022&quot;]</code>) (<code>engine/README-dev.md</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Only core's <code>src/cel/environment.ts</code> imports the expression library; everything else goes through that wrapper (E-18).</td>
<td>The same two checks</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Platform code never imports the server's <code>src/mock</code>; the hosts register the mock connectors, and production registers none of them.</td>
<td><code>engine/design/mock-systems.md</code> section 1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Platform code never names a customer workflow or a connector; both are data.</td>
<td>Root <code>README.md</code>; E-10</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The frontend uses core as a package and reaches the server only through the authoring and runtime APIs.</td>
<td>E-3; the contract</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>How the frontend consumes core.</strong> The frontend depends on core by a local path (<code>&quot;@workflow/core&quot;: &quot;file:../engine/packages/core&quot;</code>). It can use core's TypeScript source through the export condition <code>workflow-source</code>, or the built <code>dist</code> after core is built (<code>engine/README-dev.md</code>); the frontend uses the source. The frontend wraps core's synchronous functions in its own asynchronous interface and may run them in a Web Worker. Every server response names the core version it runs; the browser's must match it exactly, or the editor marks its findings as possibly out of date and publish is refused (<code>contract/core-api.md</code> section 13). core has two entries (E-26). <code>@workflow/core</code> is the contract surface, with the authored-format and catalogue types; the frontend imports only this one. <code>@workflow/core/kernel</code> holds the stored formats, <code>decide</code>, <code>evolve</code>, the turn function, the schema validator, the kernel publish check, the in-memory host and the call-result check, for the server and the hosts; its shapes may change between minor versions. One root cannot hold both, because the two share names with different meanings (<code>Status</code>, <code>ValueKind</code>, <code>MessagePart</code>) (<code>contract/core-api.md</code> section 14).</p>
<h2 id="02-the-parts--where-state-lives">Where state lives</h2>
<p>For engineers only: every table and what it can be rebuilt from.</p>
<p>Twelve tables (data model). Two are the source of truth: <code>events</code> and <code>definitions</code>. They are never updated and never deleted. Connections, secrets and the catalogue are configuration held in memory, not tables.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Store</th>
<th>Holds</th>
<th>Kind</th>
<th>Rebuildable from</th>
<th>Kept</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>events</code></td>
<td>Every request's history</td>
<td>History, source of truth</td>
<td>Nothing: everything else is worked out from it</td>
<td>For ever</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>definitions</code></td>
<td>Each published version, keyed by the workflow's ID (not its name) and the version: the compiled definition with its <code>types</code> block and origin map, form schemas, the authored source, the draft revision it came from, the core and authored-format versions that compiled it, the catalogue version, who published it</td>
<td>History, source of truth</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>For ever</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>workflows</code></td>
<td>The server's workflow ID, name, description, who created it</td>
<td>Configuration</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>For ever; archiving is not designed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>drafts</code></td>
<td>One draft per workflow, its revision and its To do counts</td>
<td>Working copy, replaced on each save</td>
<td>Nothing; earlier revisions are not kept</td>
<td>Until the next save</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>workflow_settings</code></td>
<td><code>authors</code>, <code>stuck_requests_go_to</code>, paused bindings</td>
<td>Configuration, not versioned</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>For ever</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>settings_log</code></td>
<td>Each change to a workflow's settings, a pause or resume of a binding included, with who and when</td>
<td>Log</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>For ever</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>requests</code>, <code>open_waits</code></td>
<td>One row per request (status, stuck state, values, a person's start token) for lists; the open tasks and calls, for My tasks</td>
<td>Read tables</td>
<td><code>events</code>, by replay, except the start token</td>
<td>Rebuilt at will</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>pending_calls</code></td>
<td>Calls opened and not yet answered: attempts, the outside job's reference</td>
<td>Working state</td>
<td>Partly: rows for open calls from <code>WaitOpened</code></td>
<td>Until the result is recorded</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>jobs</code></td>
<td>Call, notify and publish jobs</td>
<td>Working state</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>Until done</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>attempts_log</code>, <code>inbound_log</code></td>
<td>Refused attempts; every event received on the inbound hook, with its result or code and the event, the start dedupe included</td>
<td>Logs</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>Not deleted in the first build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Browser memory</td>
<td>Try it's test requests</td>
<td>Test state</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
<td>While the page is open</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><ul>
<li><strong>A read table reads events only</strong>: never another read table, never the live version, never the clock. So it can be rebuilt for one request or for all, and a new one can be added later and filled for every existing request (data model section 4).</li>
<li><strong>Outbound payloads are not stored.</strong> They are worked out from <code>events</code> when a turn's events are posted.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="02-the-parts--the-development-host">The development host</h2>
<p>For engineers only: how the engine runs before it lives in the existing application.</p>
<p>The development host is the server itself, on PGlite, with the in-memory mock connectors, a seeded directory and the development sign-in. One command starts it, and it serves both APIs on one port (E-33; <code>engine/design/mock-systems.md</code>).</p>

<p>Try it does not use the development host or the mocks: it runs in the browser on core's in-memory host and answers from the catalogue's samples (E-4).</p>
<h2 id="02-the-parts--browser-parts">Browser parts</h2>
<p>The browser runs the editor, the pages people use, and engine code for everything the editor works out on each edit. It holds no state of its own beyond the open page: drafts, versions and requests are on the server, and Try it's test requests live in the page's memory. Document 8, <a href="#doc-08-frontend-design">Frontend design</a>, gives the detail: its modules (D21), what happens on one edit (D22), and what each screen asks of the contract (D23).</p>

<section class="doc" data-file="03-life-of-a-workflow.md"><h1 id="doc-03-life-of-a-workflow">The life of a workflow</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Engine owner.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: How does a draft become a running request and a history?</p>
<p>A workflow exists in three forms. The author edits a <strong>draft</strong>. Publishing turns the draft into a <strong>published version</strong> (the engine calls it a definition), which the engine runs and which never changes. Each use of a version is a <strong>request</strong>, and everything that happens to it is recorded, in order and for good, as its <strong>history</strong>. This document follows one workflow through the three forms, says which code does each step and where it runs, and marks what is in the first build, what is held as a shape only, and what is later. It describes a design; nothing in it has run.</p>
<p>Four engine words are used below. An <strong>input</strong> is one thing that comes into a request: a start, a button pressed, a connection's result, an admin's retry or close. A <strong>turn</strong> is how the engine handles one input: in one database transaction it records the input and every consequence. <strong><code>decide</code></strong> is the engine function that works out those consequences; <strong><code>evolve</code></strong> is the function that rebuilds a request's state by reading its recorded history back.</p>
<h2 id="03-life-of-a-workflow--three-forms-and-the-steps-between">Three forms and the steps between</h2>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Form</th>
<th>What it is</th>
<th>Where it is kept</th>
<th>Can it change?</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Draft</td>
<td>The workflow in the authored format (<code>contract/authored-format.md</code>): stages, tasks, forms, buttons, actions, arrows, values, lists, in the editor's words. It may be unfinished.</td>
<td>On the server, one per workflow, with a revision number.</td>
<td>Yes. Every save replaces it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Published version</td>
<td>The compiled definition (engine stages, waits, transitions, rules, and a <code>types</code> block with the type of every data path, constant and operation result), the form schemas, the origin map (which authored item each compiled part came from), and the authored source it was compiled from.</td>
<td>On the server, one row per version (<code>definitions</code>).</td>
<td>Never. The next publish makes a new version.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Request history</td>
<td>The events recorded for one request, in order.</td>
<td>On the server (<code>events</code>).</td>
<td>Only by adding events at the end.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

class="fig-id">D4.</span> What are the three forms of a workflow, and which steps lead from one to the next?</figcaption></figure><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Step</th>
<th>What happens</th>
<th>Code</th>
<th>Runs in</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Edit</td>
<td>The editor changes the draft and saves it. The server refuses a save based on an old revision (<code>stale-revision</code>) and a document that is not in the authored format (<code>invalid-document</code>). An unfinished draft saves.</td>
<td>Editor (frontend); authoring API with core's <code>parse</code> and <code>check</code> (engine)</td>
<td>Browser; server at each save</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Check</td>
<td>core's <code>check</code> returns findings. A <strong>To do</strong> stops publishing; a <strong>Worth knowing</strong> does not. Each finding is a code, a location in the draft, and parameters. <code>facts</code> adds which arrows send back and which values can be read where.</td>
<td>core</td>
<td>Browser, on every edit. Server, at every save (to store the counts) and at publish (authoritative).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Try</td>
<td>A test request runs on the draft in the editor, with every connection pretended. See <a href="#03-life-of-a-workflow--try-it">Try it</a>.</td>
<td>core's test host</td>
<td>Browser only</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Publish</td>
<td>The server upgrades the draft to its own core's authored format, checks and compiles it with the catalogue it holds, refuses on any To do, and stores the new version.</td>
<td>Authoring API, core's <code>compile</code></td>
<td>Server. It is the authority (E-3).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Start</td>
<td>A person submits the start form, or an event from another system fits a &quot;Starts when&quot; binding. The start turn records <code>RequestStarted</code>, naming the workflow and the version.</td>
<td>Runtime API or the inbound hook; core's turn function inside a server transaction</td>
<td>Server</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Act</td>
<td>A person presses a button, a connection's result comes back, or an admin retries or closes. Each is one input and one turn.</td>
<td>Runtime API, the inbound hook, the call's job; core's turn function</td>
<td>Server</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Record</td>
<td>In one transaction the turn validates the input, appends it and every consequence <code>decide</code> works out, updates the tables that lists read with the stuck state worked out after it, and queues the jobs that send calls, messages and events.</td>
<td>core (<code>decide</code>) inside the server's transaction</td>
<td>Server and Postgres</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Show</td>
<td>Lists, My tasks, the request page and its story are worked out from the history and named through the version's origin map. The page turns codes into words using that version's authored source.</td>
<td>Server reads, with core's <code>story</code>; pages (frontend)</td>
<td>Server, then browser</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>The same core package runs in the browser and on the server (E-3). It has no I/O and no clock, so what the browser's check and Try it say is what the server will say. What the browser computes is still only a preview: at publish the server runs <code>check</code> and <code>compile</code> again and stores only its own result. Every server response carries the core version it runs (<code>Engine-Core-Version</code>). If the browser's version differs, the editor marks its findings and Try it as possibly out of date, saving still works, and publishing is refused with <code>core-version-mismatch</code> (<code>contract/core-api.md</code> section 13).</p>
<h2 id="03-life-of-a-workflow--what-the-compiler-does-to-one-stage">What the compiler does to one stage</h2>
<p>An author sees one stage. The engine runs a short chain of <strong>engine stages</strong> made from it, in a fixed order: the actions of &quot;When this stage starts&quot;, the tasks, the actions of &quot;After they respond&quot;, and a <strong>routing step</strong> that holds the arrows. A task that may ask a group has a membership read beside it, in the tasks step itself. A <code>members</code> step, or an &quot;is in group&quot; test inside a condition, is a separate recorded read in its own engine stage, placed just before the step that uses it, so it sees a group saved earlier in the same stage. A step the stage does not need is left out; the routing step is always there (<code>engine/design/compiler.md</code> section 2; E-23). The Domain approval stage of the change request becomes three engine stages:</p>

class="fig-id">D4b.</span> What does one authored stage become in the published version, and how is each piece tied back to it?</figcaption></figure>
<ul>
<li><strong>IDs carry through.</strong> The task ID is the wait's ID, each button ID an outcome ID, each arrow ID a transition ID, each value ID a data path, each status ID the status ID. Names the compiler adds are <code>&lt;authored item ID&gt;__&lt;local name&gt;</code>; authored IDs never contain a double underscore, so the two can never clash. An authored ID is at most 40 characters, so every compiled name fits the 64-character limit. A rename changes nothing published (E-14, E-23).</li>
<li><strong>One status for the whole chain.</strong> Every step carries the stage's status, so people see &quot;Waiting for approval&quot; from the tasks step to the routing step. Moves between the engine stages of one authored stage make no entry in the story.</li>
<li><strong>The membership read beside the task.</strong> &quot;Who is asked&quot; here is a group, so the compiler opens a read of the group's members, <code>tk_domain_approval__members</code> (<code>membersOf@1</code> on the directory connection, <code>onFailure: outcome</code>), in the task's own engine stage, together with the task. The task is open and visible at once; the read only tells, from history, whether anybody can answer it. The published version's <code>nobodyToAsk</code> block names the task and its read. Who can answer is the people asked directly plus the recorded members of the groups asked, less the Requester where the Requester may not answer. When that set is empty the request is stuck with <code>nobody-to-ask</code>, shown at the task's &quot;Who is asked&quot;. A read that fails contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts (E-23, E-24; <code>engine/spec/integrations.md</code> section 11.5). &quot;People in [group]&quot; under &quot;Who is asked&quot; is the same as asking the group: it gets this read and no other, so Retry for nobody-to-ask always reads the group again (E-24).</li>
<li><strong>The tasks step leaves when every task is answered.</strong> Its exit, <code>st_domain_approval__answered</code>, is an explicit condition that every task is answered, never &quot;in all other cases&quot;, so a membership read still pending can never hold up an answered task. Leaving the step cancels the read; its result, if it comes, is recorded late (E-23).</li>
<li><strong>Two tasks that fill the same value.</strong> Within one stage, the later task in the document wins, whichever answered later (E-23).</li>
<li><strong>&quot;After they respond&quot; runs before the arrows are checked</strong> (E-22). If no arrow fits, those actions have already run and the request is stuck with <code>nothing-fits</code>.</li>
<li><strong>A second copy</strong> of the chain, with every step name ending in <code>Back</code>, is made when an arrow sends requests back to a stage and that stage shows another status then, or is the start stage. In the change request only the Request form has one, <code>st_request_form__tasksBack</code>, whose status is &quot;Needs changes&quot;.</li>
<li>The compiler emits the kernel's elements directly (E-19).</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>The origin map.</strong> The published version stores, for every compiled element and, where needed, each field of it, the authored item and part it came from (E-18). Everything the engine reports reaches the author through this map; nothing names a compiled element (E-7). An element is keyed by its kind and ID, such as <code>wait:st_domain_approval__tasks.tk_domain_approval</code>; a single field of it by <code>&lt;element key&gt;#&lt;JSON Pointer&gt;</code>, such as <code>wait:st_domain_approval__tasks.tk_domain_approval#/assignees</code>. For the stage above (<code>engine/design/compiler.md</code> sections 12 and 15.4):</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Compiled element</th>

</table></div><p>Why it is built this way: stage, wait and transition IDs are recorded in histories for ever, and a later compiler may lay the chain out differently for later publishes (compiler section 1.5). Because every reader goes through the origin map of the request's own version, no reader depends on the shape of an ID, and an author is always shown their own stage, task, button or arrow.</p>
<h2 id="03-life-of-a-workflow--what-publish-checks">What publish checks</h2>
<p>Both layers of checks are in core.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Layer</th>
<th>What it checks</th>
<th>When it runs</th>
<th>What comes of it</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>core's <code>check</code></td>
<td>What the author can fix: a part needed to run is missing (nobody asked, an arrow that goes nowhere); a broken reference; a formula that does not parse or gives the wrong kind; a button, or a combination of buttons, that fits no arrow; a value that may be empty where an empty value stops or silently drops something (who is asked, a notification's recipient, a directory group, a needed connection input; <code>value.mayBeEmpty</code>); a stage with no way to an ending; a loop with no task; a catalogue entry that does not exist or whose connection is not set up; a &quot;Starts when&quot; binding that leaves a needed question unanswered; any construct the compiler has no rule for, such as two results of one action saved as the same value, or a binding mapping whose question's &quot;Show when&quot; reads &quot;Started on&quot; (the list is in <code>engine/design/compiler.md</code>). The full list: <code>contract/core-api.md</code> section 4.</td>
<td>Browser on every edit; server at every save and at publish</td>
<td>Findings, To do or Worth knowing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The kernel's publish checks (spec section 6)</td>
<td>The compiled definition: every expression type-checks, data is read only where it is set, every stage can reach a final stage, every cycle passes a wait, every write call has a key scope or an explicit key, every data path, constant and operation result has a declared type, and the blocks for bindings, things told and nobody-to-ask are well formed.</td>
<td>Server, at publish only, on the compiler's result</td>
<td>Core's check is designed so that all of them hold (compiler section 14). If one fails, that is a bug in core; the finding for a bug in core is <code>compile.internal</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Publishing is refused, and nothing is stored, when the browser's core version differs from the server's (<code>core-version-mismatch</code>), when the draft changed after the revision the author published (<code>stale-revision</code>), or when any finding is a To do (<code>has-todo</code>, carrying the server's findings). Worth knowing never stops it. If the catalogue changed since the author's last check, the server's findings win (<code>contract/authoring-api.md</code> section 5).</p>
<p><strong>How a problem reaches the right spot.</strong> Every finding carries a <code>Location</code>: the ID of an item in the draft (a stage, task, question, button, action, arrow, binding) and the part of it (<code>whoIsAsked</code>, <code>goTo</code>, <code>onlyWhen.2</code>, <code>inputs.summary</code>). The editor shows the To do on that item, at that part, in its own words; the engine sends codes and never sentences (E-7). For example, if Domain approval's Request changes button had no arrow, <code>check</code> would return <code>stage.buttonHasNowhereToGo</code> located at the button <code>btn_da_request_changes</code>, with its task as a parameter. Problems found while a request runs use the same <code>Location</code>, through the origin map: a refused press, a stuck request, an entry in the story. Document 6 (The contract) draws the edit loop as D14.</p>

class="label" style="" transform="translate(-99.421875, -22.5)"><rect></rect><foreignObject width="198.84375" height="45"><div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" style="display: table-cell;
