xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" style="display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;"><span class="nodeLabel "><p>A start form shown from version 2<br/>and sent after version 3 was published</p></span></div></foreignObject></g></g></g></g></g><defs><filter id="mmd-8-drop-shadow" height="130%" width="130%"><feDropShadow dx="4" dy="4" stdDeviation="0" flood-opacity="0.06" flood-color="#000000"></feDropShadow></filter></defs><defs><filter id="mmd-8-drop-shadow-small" height="150%" width="150%"><feDropShadow dx="2" dy="2" stdDeviation="0" flood-opacity="0.06" flood-color="#000000"></feDropShadow></filter></defs><linearGradient id="mmd-8-gradient" gradientUnits="objectBoundingBox" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%"><stop offset="0%" stop-color="#a5abef" stop-opacity="1"></stop><stop offset="100%" stop-color="#c9cdd4" stop-opacity="1"></stop></linearGradient></svg></div><figcaption class="figure-caption"><span class="fig-id">D5.</span> Which version does each request run on while the workflow keeps changing?</figcaption></figure>
<ul>
<li><strong>A version never changes, and a request never changes version.</strong> <code>decide</code> reads only the request's own version; the version is read from the request's events, never assumed (spec section 8; data model section 2).</li>
<li><strong>A start names the version whose start form was shown.</strong> Any published version can be started, so a publish while someone is filling in the form refuses nothing. A start that names no version uses the highest (architecture section 4; <code>contract/runtime-api.md</code> section 3.3).</li>
<li><strong>Only the highest version's &quot;Starts when&quot; bindings are live.</strong> A binding keeps its paused state across versions, by its ID (E-17; <code>contract/authoring-api.md</code> section 5).</li>
<li><strong>Old versions keep running.</strong> The engine must run a version for as long as a request on it is open. So the definition format, its expression profile (<code>cel-1</code>) and its form-schema validator are fixed per format, publish writes every default out, and an operation version such as <code>jira.createIssue@1</code> never changes shape (spec section 7). <code>listVersions</code> shows how many requests are still open on each version.</li>
<li><strong>The draft is kept after publish</strong> and stays the author's working copy. It records the live version it was based on. Publishing an unchanged draft still makes a new version. core's <code>diff</code> lists what changed between two authored documents.</li>
</ul>
<p>Some things about a workflow are settings, kept outside every version:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Setting</th>
<th>Kept in</th>
<th>Why it is not versioned</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Name, description</td>
<td>The server's workflow record</td>
<td>Renaming a workflow is not an edit to any version (authored format).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Authors</td>
<td>Workflow settings</td>
<td>They decide who may edit and publish, not how a request runs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>&quot;Stuck requests go to&quot; (the engine's workflow admins)</td>
<td>Workflow settings</td>
<td>A change must apply at once to every running request on every version: who is told, who may retry and close (E-14; data model section 2).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Paused bindings</td>
<td>Workflow settings</td>
<td>A workflow admin pauses a binding without publishing (E-17).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Connections, their secrets, the addresses that receive outbound events</td>
<td>The deployment's configuration, read at start-up</td>
<td>They belong to the platform. An author uses what the catalogue offers and never sets these (E-10, E-17, E-19).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>A change to a workflow's settings, each pause or resume of a binding included, is recorded with who made it and when (<code>settings_log</code>) (E-23).</p>
<h2 id="03-life-of-a-workflow--try-it">Try it</h2>
<p>Try it runs test requests on the draft inside the editor, with no server state (E-4). core's <code>createTestHost(draft, catalogue, fakes)</code> compiles the draft in Try it mode and returns a host held in browser memory. Each input goes through the same turn function the server runs: validate, append, <code>decide</code>, then the stuck state worked out. <code>decide</code>, <code>evolve</code>, the expression environment, the schema validator, the nobody-to-ask rule and the rules for messages and things told are the same code as on the server. Only I/O is replaced (<code>contract/core-api.md</code> section 10):</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>On the server</th>
<th>In Try it</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Group memberships and choices from the directory</td>
<td><code>fakes.groups</code>: who is in each group during the test</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Choices from a connection</td>
<td><code>fakes.sources</code>, else the catalogue's sample items</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A connection action (&quot;Look up&quot;, Create Jira issue, &quot;Wait for&quot;)</td>
<td>Per operation: the catalogue's sample result, a chosen result, a failure code, or hold until the author answers it</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Email and Slack, &quot;Tell other systems&quot;</td>
<td>The test outbox</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The clock</td>
<td><code>startAt</code>, then one second later per turn</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>&quot;Stuck requests go to&quot;</td>
<td><code>fakes.stuckRequestsGoTo</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>What Try it shows</th>
<th>What it does not show</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Where a request goes and why: every arrow checked, in order, with what it read, including the arrows that did not fit. A live request records only the arrow taken.</td>
<td>Any real connection. Nothing leaves the browser, and the mock systems are not used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Refusals, with the runtime's codes in the runtime's order.</td>
<td>A directory or data source that cannot be reached: <code>membership-unavailable</code> and <code>source-unavailable</code> never occur.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Stuck, with its reason; Retry for <code>action-failed</code> and <code>nobody-to-ask</code>, and Close.</td>
<td>A call that times out or answers &quot;don't know&quot;: the fakes offer a sample, a result, a failure, or hold. Sending again and status questions belong to the server's call jobs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What would be sent: each call's inputs, each message with its recipients, each thing told with its values.</td>
<td>Outbound event envelopes and posting them to other systems.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>A start from a &quot;Starts when&quot; binding, given what the other system would send (<code>startFrom</code>).</td>
<td>The inbound hook's own checks: signatures, body size, parsing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>An unfinished draft. A request that reaches a part whose To do stops it from running is stuck with reason <code>unfinished</code>. Words and labels never stop it (E-20). Nor does a task with nobody asked, which the request reaches and is stuck at with <code>nobody-to-ask</code>, nor a question with no choices or choices from a list with no rows, which the tester sees and cannot answer properly (E-28).</td>
<td>Anything kept: test requests last while the page is open, and a changed draft needs a new host. Saving or sharing them is not designed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>A test run on the server is later; it can be added without changing the contract (E-4).</p>
<h2 id="03-life-of-a-workflow--a-requests-history-is-the-source-of-truth">A request's history is the source of truth</h2>
<p>In each turn the engine records the input and every consequence <code>decide</code> worked out, as events, in the order they happened. Nothing is changed or removed afterwards.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>What is recorded</th>
<th>Events</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>What came in</td>
<td><code>RequestStarted</code> (who started it, or which connection and binding; the <code>workflow</code> and the version; the start answers). <code>WaitCompleted</code> (the button and answers, who pressed it, the groups that let them, each choice as looked up; or a connection's result). <code>CallResultLate</code> (a result that arrived after the request moved on). <code>Overridden</code> (an admin's retry or close, with who and why).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What the engine decided</td>
<td><code>TransitionFired</code> (the arrow, and every value its condition read), <code>StageEntered</code> (with the status shown), <code>StageExited</code>, <code>WaitOpened</code> (who is asked, as worked out then; or the connection, operation, arguments and idempotency key), <code>WaitCancelled</code>, <code>WaitSkipped</code>, <code>DataSet</code> (values saved; removing a value that is not there records nothing, so a person's start records no empty &quot;remove&quot; for the Requester, E-24), <code>Faulted</code>, <code>RequestClosed</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>On every event</td>
<td>The request, its position <code>seq</code>, the time <code>at</code> (the only clock the engine has), the <code>turn</code>, the event's schema version, the engine build</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Outside data enters only as recorded results: a connection's result, the group lookup when a person acts, the look-up of an answer chosen from a data source. <code>decide</code> never reads live data (E-9).</p>
<p>Not in the history: messages sent, events told to other systems (worked out from history and posted, not stored), refused attempts (a log), <code>decide</code>'s note of the arrows that did not fit, and what pages read live (people search, choices while a form is open, display names).</p>

xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" style="display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;"><span class="nodeLabel "><p>Event publisher<br/>payload worked out at each send</p></span></div></foreignObject></g></g></g></g></g><defs><filter id="mmd-9-drop-shadow" height="130%" width="130%"><feDropShadow dx="4" dy="4" stdDeviation="0" flood-opacity="0.06" flood-color="#000000"></feDropShadow></filter></defs><linearGradient id="mmd-9-gradient" gradientUnits="objectBoundingBox" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%"><stop class="fig-id">D4c.</span> What is worked out from a request's history, and by whom?</figcaption></figure>
<ul>
<li><strong>Replaying never re-runs workflow logic.</strong> <code>evolve</code> folds events into state. It never evaluates an expression and never reads a definition, because <code>decide</code> spelled out every consequence as events when it happened. The cost: a bug in <code>decide</code> is recorded as fact. It is repaired by an admin turn, never by rewriting history (architecture section 3).</li>
<li><strong>The tables lists read can be rebuilt.</strong> <code>requests</code> and <code>open_waits</code> are updated in each turn's transaction. Deleting a request's rows and replaying its events gives the same rows. A new list or report is a new table filled the same way, for every existing request (data model section 4).</li>
<li><strong>Readers speak the author's words.</strong> The request page and the story fold the request's events and name every element through the origin map of the request's own version; the page renders words and forms from that version's authored source (E-6, E-7). Try it and live requests use the same <code>story</code> function.</li>
<li><strong>Messages and things told read the past.</strong> Their values are the request's data folded up to the event that set them off, not the data when the job runs (E-14, E-17). Neither can stop or move a request.</li>
</ul>

<section class="doc" data-file="04-word-map.md"><h1 id="doc-04-word-map">Word map</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Frontend owner; the Engine owner checks.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: What does each editor word mean in the engine and in the contract?</p>
<p>Every word an author sees in the editor has exactly one meaning in the saved workflow and one in the engine. This document is that mapping. Read a row from left to right: what the author means by the word, where the editor saves it, what the engine turns it into or checks it with, and where it is recorded when a request runs.</p>
<p>Four terms used in the columns:</p>
<ul>
<li>The <strong>authored format</strong> is the workflow as the editor saves it: a JSON document in the editor's own words (<code>contract/authored-format.md</code>). Field names below are its fields.</li>
<li>The <strong>compiler</strong> turns a published draft into a <strong>definition</strong>, the form the engine runs. It lives in the engine's shared core, which also runs in the browser.</li>
<li>The <strong>history</strong> is the list of events the engine records for each request, in order, for good. Event names below (<code>StageEntered</code>, <code>DataSet</code> ...) are its entries. Nothing is ever changed in it, only added.</li>
<li>A <strong>projection</strong> is a table rebuilt from the history for fast reading, such as the list of requests.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="04-word-map--the-words-one-row-each">The words, one row each</h2>
<h3 id="04-word-map--workflow-versions-and-requests">Workflow, versions and requests</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What the author means</th>
<th>Authored field</th>
<th>Engine concept</th>
<th>Recorded at run time</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Workflow</strong></td>
<td>What I build.</td>
<td>The document's root: <code>id</code>, <code>formatVersion</code>, and everything below. Its name, description and &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot; live in the server's workflow record, not in the document.</td>
<td>A definition per published version.</td>
<td>Each request names its definition version in <code>RequestStarted</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Draft</strong> (&quot;Draft (not live)&quot;)</td>
<td>The version I am changing. Saved as I type.</td>
<td>The whole document, stored with a revision number. It may be unfinished.</td>
<td>Not run. Checked on every edit.</td>
<td>Not at run time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Version</strong> (&quot;Version 3 is live&quot;)</td>
<td>What people use now. It never changes.</td>
<td>The authored document, stored beside its compiled definition.</td>
<td>A published definition. A request stays on the version it started on.</td>
<td>The <code>definitions</code> table.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Publish</strong></td>
<td>Make my draft the live version.</td>
<td>None: an operation of the authoring API on the draft.</td>
<td>The server runs the check and the compiler again, refuses while anything is To do, and stores the definition, the form schemas and the origin map (which compiled part came from which authored item).</td>
<td>A new row in <code>definitions</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Request</strong></td>
<td>One use of my workflow, from start form to ending.</td>
<td>Not in the document.</td>
<td>A request: its history of events.</td>
<td>The history (<code>events</code>), and the <code>requests</code> projection.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h3 id="04-word-map--stages">Stages</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What the author means</th>
<th>Authored field</th>
<th>Engine concept</th>
<th>Recorded at run time</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Stage</strong></td>
<td>A box on the diagram where a request sits.</td>
<td><code>stages[]</code></td>
<td>A chain of engine stages: actions on arrival, the tasks, actions after they respond, then a routing step that holds the arrows (E-14; see <a href="#fig-d4b">D4b</a>). Engine IDs are made from the stage's ID, so renaming changes nothing.</td>
<td><code>StageEntered</code> and <code>StageExited</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Kind</strong> (of stage): Form, Approval, Work, Automatic, Blank</td>
<td>What sort of stage this is. It pre-fills the stage.</td>
<td><code>kind</code></td>
<td>Nothing of its own. A kind changes no rule; an Automatic stage is simply one with no tasks. The compiler emits the engine's elements directly; it does not use the spec's Approval and Task composites.</td>
<td>Not recorded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Ending</strong></td>
<td>A box where a request finishes.</td>
<td>A stage with <code>kind: &quot;ending&quot;</code>: name and status only.</td>
<td>A final stage.</td>
<td><code>StageEntered</code>, then <code>RequestClosed</code> naming the ending.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Status</strong></td>
<td>The words and colour people see for where a request is.</td>
<td><code>statuses[]</code>, and a stage's <code>status</code> and <code>ifSentBackStatus</code>.</td>
<td>A stage's status, <code>{ id, label }</code>. Pages key on the status ID, never on the stage.</td>
<td>Inside <code>StageEntered</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>When this stage starts</strong> / <strong>After they respond</strong></td>
<td>Things done in order, before anyone is asked / once, when the stage finishes.</td>
<td><code>whenThisStageStarts[]</code> / <code>afterTheyRespond[]</code></td>
<td>The first and third links of the stage's chain.</td>
<td>The entries of each action (below).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h3 id="04-word-map--tasks-and-forms">Tasks and forms</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What the author means</th>
<th>Authored field</th>
<th>Engine concept</th>
<th>Recorded at run time</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Task</strong></td>
<td>The part of a stage that asks people.</td>
<td><code>tasks[]</code></td>
<td>A person wait that must be answered (an obligation).</td>
<td><code>WaitOpened</code>, <code>WaitCompleted</code>, or <code>WaitCancelled</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Who is asked</strong></td>
<td>The person or group the task goes to.</td>
<td><code>whoIsAsked</code>, with <code>ifEmptyUse</code>; <code>groupRule: &quot;firstAnswerDecides&quot;</code>; <code>requesterCanAnswer</code>.</td>
<td>The wait's assignees, worked out when it opens. &quot;The requester can't answer&quot; is a rule on who may act. Whether someone is in the group is checked when they act. When a task may ask a group, the compiler adds a recorded read of the group's members beside the task, in the task's own step; it decides only whether anybody is able to answer, and a read that fails counts as nobody to ask.</td>
<td>Assignees in <code>WaitOpened</code> (groups are not expanded). The membership read, as a call's result. The person's group membership, looked up when they act, as evidence in <code>WaitCompleted</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Form</strong></td>
<td>The questions a task shows.</td>
<td><code>form.pages[]</code></td>
<td>A JSON Schema and a set of checks for each button (E-6).</td>
<td>The answers in <code>WaitCompleted</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Page</strong> (of a form)</td>
<td>One page of questions.</td>
<td><code>pages[]</code>, with <code>title</code> and <code>showWhen</code>.</td>
<td>Part of the conditional checks.</td>
<td>Not separately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Question</strong></td>
<td>One item on a form.</td>
<td><code>items[]</code> with <code>type: &quot;question&quot;</code>: <code>label</code>, <code>kind</code>, <code>savedAs</code>, <code>choices</code>, <code>showWhen</code>.</td>
<td>A field of the answers, keyed by the question's ID; then copied to its value.</td>
<td><code>WaitCompleted</code>, then <code>DataSet</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Choices from</strong> (a connection)</td>
<td>A question whose choices come from another system each time the form opens.</td>
<td><code>choices</code> with <code>from: &quot;source&quot;</code> and a catalogue <code>source</code>.</td>
<td>A catalogue data source (door 5). While the form is shown, the page asks the engine and the engine reads the source. When the person presses, the chosen item is looked up again. The author is told that only the answer is kept, so a later change in the other system does not change a request's answer.</td>
<td>The answer, <code>{ stored, label }</code>, with the source's label at the moment of pressing, and the lookup as evidence in <code>WaitCompleted</code>. The list is never recorded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Button</strong></td>
<td>How a person finishes a task.</td>
<td><code>buttons[]</code></td>

</tr>
<tr>

<tr>

<td>Writes of the outcome and the actor to values.</td>
<td><code>DataSet</code>.</td>
</tr>

<td>A transition into a stage entered before. Re-entry gives fresh tasks. A stage with an &quot;If sent back&quot; status is compiled twice, once per way in.</td>

</table></div><h3 id="04-word-map--actions-and-connections">Actions and connections</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What the author means</th>
<th>Authored field</th>
<th>Engine concept</th>
<th>Recorded at run time</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Action</strong></td>
<td>Something the workflow does by itself.</td>
<td>An entry of <code>whenThisStageStarts[]</code> or <code>afterTheyRespond[]</code>, with <code>type</code> and an optional <code>onlyWhen</code>.</td>
<td>By type, below. Actions run in listed order.</td>
<td>By type, below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Save a value</strong></td>
<td>&quot;Save [what] as [value]&quot;.</td>
<td><code>type: &quot;saveValue&quot;</code>: <code>save</code>, <code>as</code>.</td>
<td>A Set: a write to the request's data, placed on the transition out of the step that holds the action.</td>
<td><code>DataSet</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Notify</strong></td>
<td>Send a message to a person or group.</td>
<td><code>type: &quot;notify&quot;</code>: <code>to</code>, <code>message</code>.</td>
<td>A notification rule in the published version, matched on the recorded entry into the step that holds the action. The notifier sends it with the values as they were at that moment. It never stops a request.</td>
<td>Nothing of its own in the history. What was sent is kept in <code>notifications_sent</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Tell other systems</strong></td>
<td>Announce that something happened (&quot;Change released&quot;) to every system that listens.</td>
<td><code>type: &quot;tellOtherSystems&quot;</code>: <code>tell</code> (an entry of <code>thingsTold</code>), <code>values</code>.</td>
<td>Like Notify, a rule in the published version (an <code>events</code> block beside the notification rules), matched on the recorded entry into the step that holds the action. The event publisher builds the outbound message from that entry, with the values as they were then, and delivers it to listening systems (door 7) as one type, <code>request.told</code>, carrying the thing told as <code>{ id, words }</code> and the named values. Each value goes out exactly as the request holds it: a choice from a connection with its stored value and its label, a person as a directory reference. The built-in tellings (started, status changed, stuck, no longer stuck, ended) carry IDs, status and reason only, never answers. It never stops a request.</td>
<td>Nothing of its own: the stage entry it is matched on is the record.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Connection</strong></td>
<td>Another system the platform is linked to, set up by an administrator.</td>
<td>Never named directly: only catalogue IDs such as <code>jira.createIssue@1</code> in <code>operation</code>, <code>trigger</code> or <code>source</code>.</td>
<td>A connection: a configured instance of a connector (the code for one kind of system). The catalogue lists what it offers, in four sorts (next four rows).</td>
<td>The connection and operation, in <code>WaitOpened</code> of the call.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Gives data</strong>: <strong>Look up</strong></td>
<td>Read something from another system and save it as values.</td>
<td><code>type: &quot;useConnection&quot;</code> with a read operation; <code>saveResults</code>.</td>
<td>A call wait of sort read.</td>
<td>Arguments in <code>WaitOpened</code>; the result in <code>WaitCompleted</code>; the saved values in <code>DataSet</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Does something</strong> (e.g. Create Jira issue)</td>
<td>Have another system do something; the request moves on when it is done.</td>
<td><code>useConnection</code> with a write operation; <code>inputs</code>, <code>saveResults</code>, <code>ifStageEntersAgain</code>.</td>
<td>A call wait of sort write, sent with an idempotency key (a key that lets the other system ignore a repeat). &quot;Once&quot; (<code>keyScope: request</code>) keeps the key for the whole request; &quot;again&quot; (<code>keyScope: activation</code>) makes a new one each time the stage is entered. The catalogue gives the default, shown and editable on the action; it is a To do only when the catalogue gives none and the author chose none.</td>
<td>As for Look up, plus the key. A result that arrives after the request moved on: <code>CallResultLate</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Does something and waits</strong>: <strong>Wait for</strong></td>
<td>Ask another system to do something and keep the request here until it reports back.</td>
<td><code>useConnection</code> with an await operation.</td>
<td>An ordinary call wait; &quot;waits&quot; is a property of the catalogue entry (sort await). The engine asks the other system to start a job, then takes a result only by asking for the job's status; a callback from the other system only brings that question forward.</td>
<td>As for Look up: an ordinary action call.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Can start a request</strong>: <strong>Starts when</strong></td>
<td>Another system's event starts a request, as if the start form were filled in.</td>
<td><code>start.startsWhen[]</code>: <code>trigger</code>, <code>onlyWhen</code>, <code>answers</code>, <code>button</code>, <code>requester</code>.</td>
<td>A trigger binding: the event's fields are mapped onto the start form, and its button is pressed.</td>
<td><code>RequestStarted</code>, naming the trigger; the starter is the connection.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>If it fails</strong></td>
<td>What happens when an action that uses a connection fails.</td>
<td><code>ifItFails</code>: <code>&quot;stuck&quot;</code> or <code>&quot;carryOn&quot;</code>, with <code>saveFailureAs</code>.</td>
<td>The call's <code>onFailure</code>: <code>fault</code> (the request stops) or <code>outcome</code> (the failure is an ordinary result an arrow can test).</td>
<td>The failed result in <code>WaitCompleted</code>; then either <code>Faulted</code> (stuck), or the failure saved as values by <code>DataSet</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Pretended</strong> (Try it)</td>
<td>What a connection would have done, shown instead of doing it.</td>
<td>None.</td>
<td>The test host's fakes: answer with the catalogue's sample, a chosen result, a failure, or hold until the author answers.</td>
<td>Only in the Test outbox.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h3 id="04-word-map--values-and-conditions">Values and conditions</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What the author means</th>
<th>Authored field</th>
<th>Engine concept</th>
<th>Recorded at run time</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Value</strong></td>
<td>A named piece of data the workflow remembers.</td>
<td><code>values[]</code> holds only <code>id</code> and <code>name</code>. A value is filled by <code>savedAs</code>, <code>as</code>, <code>saveResults</code>, <code>saveFailureAs</code>, <code>savesButtonPressedAs</code> or <code>savesAnsweredByAs</code>.</td>
<td>A data path in the request's data; its first segment is the value's ID. A value is present or absent, never null. Within one stage, when two tasks fill the same value, the later task in the document wins, not the later answer in time.</td>
<td><code>DataSet</code>; the current values in the <code>requests</code> projection.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Kind</strong> (of value)</td>
<td>What sort of value: text, number, Yes/No, date, person ...</td>
<td>Never stored: it comes from what fills the value.</td>
<td>A type in the formula language, and a JSON Schema fragment.</td>
<td>Not recorded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>List</strong> (the Domains list)</td>
<td>A small table kept with the workflow.</td>
<td><code>lists[]</code>: <code>columns</code>, <code>rows</code>.</td>
<td>Constants compiled into the published version.</td>
<td>Not per request. A list choice records the chosen row.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>If empty, use</strong></td>
<td>What to use when a value has nothing in it.</td>
<td><code>ifEmptyUse</code> on a reference.</td>
<td>A fallback in the compiled expression.</td>
<td>What was read, where the expression is recorded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>When ...</strong> (a sentence)</td>
<td>The condition built from chips: &quot;Risk is High&quot;.</td>
<td>A sentence: <code>allOf</code> or <code>anyOf</code> clauses.</td>
<td>An expression in the formula language (CEL).</td>
<td>What it read, in <code>TransitionFired</code> or the check's evidence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Formula</strong></td>
<td>The typed way to say a &quot;when ...&quot; or a value.</td>
<td><code>{ formula, readsAs }</code>; <code>readsAs</code> is the plain sentence shown instead.</td>
<td>A CEL expression.</td>
<td>What it read. An error that cannot be evaluated faults the request.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h3 id="04-word-map--checking-trying-and-when-things-go-wrong">Checking, trying, and when things go wrong</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Editor word</th>
<th>What the author means</th>
<th>Authored field</th>
<th>Engine concept</th>
<th>Recorded at run time</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>To do</strong></td>
<td>Must be done before publishing.</td>
<td>Not stored: worked out from the draft.</td>
<td>A finding of the check with severity <code>todo</code>: a code, a location in the authored format, and parameters. Publishing is refused while any exists.</td>
<td>Not at run time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Worth knowing</strong></td>
<td>Good to know; does not stop publishing.</td>
<td>Not stored.</td>
<td>A finding with severity <code>worthKnowing</code>.</td>
<td>Not at run time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Try it</strong></td>
<td>Run a test request inside the editor.</td>
<td>None.</td>
<td>The test host: the same engine core, run in the browser, with every connection pretended and a test outbox (E-4).</td>
<td>Nowhere: held in memory while the page is open.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Sample request</strong></td>
<td>The request the editor uses for every sample.</td>
<td><code>sampleRequest</code></td>
<td>Ignored by the compiler. Used for formula samples and Try it.</td>
<td>Not at run time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Stuck</strong></td>
<td>A request that cannot move until someone acts.</td>
<td>None on the stage.</td>
<td>One state, <code>stuck { reason, at }</code>, the same in the history, the request view and lists. Reasons: <code>action-failed</code>, <code>nobody-to-ask</code> (nobody was asked, or the group's recorded membership read finds nobody able to answer, or that read failed), <code>nothing-fits</code> (no arrow fits), <code>error</code>. Inside, the kernel keeps its own distinction: a failure is a fault, while nobody to ask is an open task that nobody can answer, which the engine reports as stuck. Retry and Close are admin turns. Retry is offered only for <code>action-failed</code> and <code>nobody-to-ask</code>; Close for any open request (see below the table).</td>
<td><code>Faulted</code> for a failure; the one stuck message, <code>request.stuck</code>, with the reason, to the people who look after stuck requests; <code>Overridden</code> for a retry or close; <code>RequestClosed</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Stuck requests go to</strong></td>
<td>Who is told about stuck requests and may close them, or retry them where that can help.</td>
<td>Not in the document: only in the workflow's settings record.</td>
<td>The workflow's admins, a setting outside the published definition. A change applies at once to running requests.</td>
<td>The <code>workflow_settings</code> table.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Retry and Close, by reason.</strong> Retry is offered only where running again can help. <code>action-failed</code>: the action is tried again. <code>nobody-to-ask</code>: who is asked is worked out again, the group's members are read again, and the stage's tasks are asked again. For <code>nothing-fits</code> and <code>error</code> only Close is offered: running again would read the same values and go wrong the same way, so the fix is in the workflow, for the next request. Close is offered for any open request, stuck or not. Two limits in the first build: if nobody is asked because a value is empty, Retry reads the same empty value, so Close is the only way out; and in a stage with several tasks, Retry asks all of them again. If the cause was an empty group and someone is then added to it, that person can simply answer, and the request stops being stuck when the task is answered.</p>
<p>Everyone signed in can open a request's page and see that it is stuck, and why. The Stuck requests list, the technical detail, and Retry and Close are for the people who look after stuck requests and for platform admins.</p>

<td>An Automatic stage, Create Jira issue, which saves the new issue as Jira issue</td>
<td><code>kind: &quot;automatic&quot;</code>; <code>whenThisStageStarts: [useConnection jira.createIssue@1]</code>; <code>saveResults: { key: &quot;v_jira_issue&quot; }</code></td>
<td>A call wait of sort write, then a data write (<code>DataSet</code>), then the &quot;When done&quot; transition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>17</td>
<td>An ending, Rejected</td>
<td><code>kind: &quot;ending&quot;</code></td>
<td>A final stage; <code>RequestClosed</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Below the visible part, the panel goes on with the task's <strong>Form</strong> (a summary with Edit form), its <strong>Buttons</strong> and what each needs, <strong>After they respond</strong>, and <strong>Then go to</strong> (the arrows). They map as in the tables above.</p>
<h2 id="04-word-map--one-authored-stage-becomes-a-chain-of-engine-steps">One authored stage becomes a chain of engine steps</h2>
<p>An author sees one stage; the engine runs a short chain of stages made from it: actions on arrival, the tasks, actions after they respond, then a routing step that holds the arrows. Where a task may ask a group, a read of the group's members sits beside the task, in the task's own step. Diagram <a href="#fig-d4b">D4b</a> in document 3 (<a href="#doc-03-life-of-a-workflow">The life of a workflow</a>) draws it, with the origin map that lets the engine report every problem back at the author's own stage.</p>
<h2 id="04-word-map--words-the-engine-has-that-the-editor-never-shows">Words the engine has that the editor never shows</h2>
<p>The engine's words stay in the engine and its documents. An engineer reading the history will meet them; an author never does. Each has an editor word a person sees instead.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Engine word</th>
<th>What it is</th>
<th>What a person sees instead</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Wait</strong></td>

<section class="doc" data-file="05-integrations.md"><h1 id="doc-05-integrations">Integrations</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Engine owner.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: How do data and events get in and out of the platform, upstream and downstream, and how is each way set up and wired?</p>
<p>This chapter covers everything that crosses the platform's edge: another system starting a request, a person's answer, a look-up, an action in another system, a message to people, and an event sent to other systems. For each it says who sets it up and where the settings are kept, what happens at run time, what the engine records, and what happens when something fails.</p>
<p>It describes a design. The first build shows every door working in its thinnest form, against mock systems; the fuller designs are kept for later (E-33, <a href="#05-integrations--reserved-for-later">Reserved for later</a>). The sources are the engine decisions in <a href="#doc-11-decisions-engine">Decisions: engine</a> (E-9 to E-33), kernel spec v2.20 and its <code>integrations.md</code> (whose copy is in <code>engine/spec/</code>), the server's side in <a href="../../engine/design/integrations-shapes.md">integrations-shapes.md</a>, the mock systems in <a href="../../engine/design/mock-systems.md">mock-systems.md</a>, the worked sample in <a href="../../engine/design/integrated-sample.md">integrated-sample.md</a>, and the catalogue <a href="../../contract/fixtures/catalogue.json">catalogue.json</a>. Field-level shapes stay in those files; this chapter names them.</p>
<p><strong>How to read it.</strong> The sections up to &quot;One request through every door&quot; are for every reader. Each door then has a table at a glance and one worked example. A part that is for connection builders or engineers says so; the product owner can skip it. Names in code type, such as <code>WaitCompleted</code> or <code>pending_calls</code>, are the engine's records, tables and codes, for engineers.</p>
<p><strong>Build status.</strong></p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Mark</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>First build</td>
<td>Part of what this repository builds first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>First build *</td>
<td>Built in its thinnest form because the product owner asked to see every kind of integration working against mock systems. Beyond <code>requirements/mvp.md</code> (E-9, E-33).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Later</td>
<td>Designed enough not to block it; not built.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h2 id="05-integrations--words-used-here">Words used here</h2>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Word</th>
<th>What it is</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Request history</td>
<td>Everything the engine records for one request, in order, never changed. Arrows, checks and conditions read only this.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Door</td>
<td>One of the seven ways data or control crosses the platform's edge (E-9).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Turn</td>
<td>One input to a request and everything the engine records for it at once: a start, a button pressed, a result from another system, an admin's Retry or Close.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Connection</td>
<td>Another system the platform is linked to, such as Jira. A platform admin writes each one in the deployment's configuration. Authors use what it offers and never see how it is reached. The code that talks to the other system is a <strong>connector</strong>, written by a <strong>connection builder</strong>, an engineer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What a connection offers</td>
<td>In the editor's words: <strong>Gives data</strong> (a question's choices, &quot;From a connection&quot;, or a &quot;Look up&quot; action), <strong>Does something</strong> (an action named after what it does, such as &quot;Create issue&quot;), <strong>Does something and waits</strong> (a &quot;Wait for&quot; action, such as &quot;Run the pipeline and wait&quot;), and <strong>Can start a request</strong> (&quot;Also start it from another system&quot; on the start stage). Each thing offered has a fixed version, such as <code>jira.createIssue@1</code>. The action &quot;Tell other systems&quot; needs no connection.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The compiler</td>
<td>The part of the engine that turns the author's draft into the published version that requests run on. It adds a few things the author does not, such as the read below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The people who look after stuck requests</td>
<td>The people and groups in the workflow's &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot; setting; when it is not set, the authors. They are told when a request is stuck and can retry or close it. The engine calls them <strong>workflow admins</strong>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Platform admins</td>
<td>Holders of the existing application's platform-admin entitlement. They write the connections and the addresses that receive outbound events.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Stuck</td>
<td>A request that cannot move until someone acts. There are four reasons; see <a href="#05-integrations--when-a-request-is-stuck">When a request is stuck</a>. A request that is only waiting for a slow system is not stuck.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The key</td>
<td>Every call to another system carries a key, so the other system can recognise a repeat of the same call and not act twice. A call that gets no answer is sent again with the same key. When the request comes back to the stage, either the key is kept for the whole request (<strong>&quot;once&quot;</strong>: the other system returns its earlier result) or each entry gets a new key (<strong>&quot;again&quot;</strong>: it acts again). What a connection offers sets the default; the editor states it on the action. A &quot;Look up&quot; always reads again.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Accepted</td>
<td>The answer a system gives when asked to do something it will finish later (a &quot;Wait for&quot;): it has started a job, here is the job's reference, such as <code>run-5001</code>. Nothing is recorded yet; the engine asks about the job until it ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The read the compiler adds</td>
<td>For every task that may ask a group, the engine reads the group's members when the task opens, beside the task, and records the answer, so history shows whether anybody can answer the task. The task can be answered while the read is still pending. It is a read call (door 3); this chapter describes it under door 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Log line</td>
<td>A structured line the server writes for engineers. Problems that tell nobody, such as a refused start or a slow call, are log lines.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h2 id="05-integrations--the-idea-in-one-page">The idea in one page</h2>
<p>Data and control cross the platform's edge through seven doors. Nothing enters a request's history any other way (E-9).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>#</th>
<th>Door</th>
<th>What the author sees</th>
<th>What crosses</th>
<th>Build</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Start</td>
<td>The start form; &quot;Also start it from another system&quot;, which adds a &quot;Starts when&quot; card</td>
<td>A person submits the start form, or another system's event is mapped onto it</td>
<td>Person: first build. Another system: first build *</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>Act</td>
<td>A task's form and buttons</td>
<td>A person's answers and the button they pressed</td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td>Call</td>
<td>&quot;Look up&quot;, an action that does something such as &quot;Create issue&quot;, &quot;Wait for&quot;, each added from a stage's &quot;+ Add&quot; menu</td>
<td>The engine asks another system; the result comes back and is recorded</td>
<td>Look up, Does something: first build. Wait for: first build *</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>Membership</td>
<td>A task whose &quot;Who is asked&quot; shows a group</td>
<td>Who is in the group, read when the task opens; which groups a person is in, when they press a button</td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>Choices</td>
<td>A question whose &quot;Choices&quot; are &quot;From a connection&quot; or &quot;People from the directory&quot;</td>
<td>The list while the form is open; the chosen item, looked up again when the person presses</td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>Notification</td>
<td>&quot;Notify&quot;; the built-in messages</td>
<td>Messages to people through email and Slack</td>
<td>First build</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7</td>
<td>Event out</td>
<td>&quot;Tell other systems&quot;; the built-in events</td>
<td>Public events posted to the addresses a platform admin lists</td>
<td>First build *</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Pages also read live data that is recorded nowhere: people search, choices while a form is open, names for display. Those reads are not doors. What they return reaches history only through door 2 or door 5.</p>

<h3 id="05-integrations--three-rules-that-never-bend">Three rules that never bend</h3>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Rule</th>
<th>What it means in the engine</th>
<th>What follows for an author</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Nothing outside moves a request unless the workflow asked.</strong></td>
<td>Another system can start a request (door 1) or answer a call the engine made (door 3). Nothing else reaches a running request.</td>
<td>To wait for another system, use a &quot;Wait for&quot; action: the engine asks about the job until it ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>No clock.</strong></td>
<td><code>decide</code>, the kernel function that works out what a turn does, never reads the time. Each event carries the time it was recorded. Jobs use a clock for retries and polls, never to move a request.</td>
<td>No deadlines, reminders, timers or scheduled starts in the first build. A formula has no &quot;today&quot;; it can read the day the request started.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Outside data is recorded when it arrives.</strong></td>
<td>A call's result, a membership lookup and a choice lookup are written into history in the turn that uses them. <code>decide</code> never reads live data, and replay never calls out.</td>
<td>Arrows and checks see a value as it was when it was looked up. The label of a chosen item is the source's label at the moment the person pressed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>A notification or an outbound event never stops or holds up a request. A door can make a request stuck in two ways only: an action that uses a connection fails and its &quot;If it fails&quot; is &quot;stuck&quot; (door 3), or a task is open that nobody can answer (doors 2 and 4). History is append-only: what went wrong is put right by a Retry or Close, recorded as a new event.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--when-a-request-is-stuck">When a request is stuck</h2>
<p>Everyone who can see a request sees that it is stuck and the reason. The detail, and the buttons Retry and Close, are for the people who look after stuck requests and the platform admins (E-19, E-23). Stuck is worked out from the request's state after each turn, never recorded (E-33).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Reason</th>
<th>What it means</th>
<th>What can be done</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Action failed (<code>action-failed</code>)</td>
<td>An action that uses a connection failed clearly, and its &quot;If it fails&quot; is &quot;stuck&quot;. The detail gives the failure code the connection returned.</td>
<td>Retry: the action is tried again. Close.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Nobody to ask (<code>nobody-to-ask</code>)</td>
<td>A task is open and nobody can answer it: the people asked directly plus the recorded members of the groups asked, less the Requester where the Requester may not answer. A group whose read failed counts as no one (E-24).</td>
<td>Retry: the groups are read again and the stage's tasks asked again. Close.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Nothing fits (<code>nothing-fits</code>)</td>
<td>Nothing is open and no arrow out of the stage fits.</td>
<td>Close only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Error (<code>error</code>)</td>
<td>Something in the workflow could not be worked out, such as a formula, or one turn took more than 50 arrows.</td>
<td>Close only: running again would repeat the same result.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Who is told.</strong> When a request becomes stuck, for any reason, the people who look after stuck requests get the built-in message <code>request.stuck</code> with the reason, and systems listening to outbound events get <code>request.stuck@1</code>. That is the one alert in the first build. Everything else that goes wrong at the edge (a refused start, a slow or unclear call, a directory or data source that cannot be reached, a rule that cannot be worked out) is a log line on the server, and nobody is told (E-33).</p>
<p>Close is offered for any open request, stuck or not. A request that is only waiting for a slow call is not stuck and cannot be retried; it is waited for or closed (E-20).</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--one-request-through-every-door">One request through every door</h2>
<p>The running example is the integrated sample workflow, &quot;Service change&quot; (<code>contract/fixtures/integrated-sample.authored.json</code>), run against the in-memory mock systems. Its stages:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Request form</strong>, the start stage. A Helpdesk ticket of category &quot;Service change&quot; also starts it.</li>
<li><strong>Find service owner</strong>: &quot;Look up a service&quot; in the Service catalog, saving the owner and tier as values.</li>
<li><strong>Approve change</strong>, for Tier 3 services only: the Platform team approves. Not on the path below.</li>
<li><strong>Deploy</strong>: &quot;Wait for&quot; the Deploy pipeline; then &quot;Tell other systems&quot; &quot;Change deployed&quot; if it succeeded.</li>
<li><strong>Fix deployment</strong>, if the deploy failed: &quot;Create Jira issue&quot;, &quot;Notify&quot; the owner (or the Platform team when there is none), then a task with the buttons Mark fixed and Deploy again.</li>
<li><strong>Deployed</strong>, the ending.</li>
</ul>
<p>Priya raises a Helpdesk ticket for Ledger, a service with no owner, so the Platform team (Sam and Mei) is asked to fix the failed deploy. The full walk is <a href="../../engine/design/integrated-sample.md">integrated-sample.md</a> section 3.</p>

<p>Ledger has no owner, so Fix deployment asks the Platform team; the compiler adds the read of its members, so history shows whether anybody can answer. On this path Reporting receives every event in order, the request sends 4 messages and nobody is alerted. &quot;Deploy again&quot; sends the request back to Deploy with a new key, so the pipeline starts a new run. The Tell is published only on the pass that succeeded.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--what-a-connection-is-and-who-sets-one-up">What a connection is, and who sets one up</h2>
<p>A connection joins three things: connector code written by an engineer, a configuration entry written by a platform admin, and the catalogue entries that tell the editor what the connection offers. Authors use what it offers and never see how a connection is reached (E-10, E-19).</p>

connection made of, and who adds one and how?</figcaption></figure><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Who</th>
<th>Does</th>
<th>Kept in</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Connection builder</td>
<td>Writes a connector and the catalogue entries for what it offers. Production and the development host register different sets; platform code names none.</td>
<td>Repository code</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Platform admin</td>
<td>Writes each connection: its ID, which connector, a label, its settings, whether it is ready, and where its secret is. Names which connection is the directory and which carries messages. Lists the addresses that receive outbound events.</td>
<td>The deployment's configuration, read at start-up only. No table and no screen (E-33).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Workflow author</td>
<td>Uses what connections offer in actions, questions' choices and &quot;Starts when&quot; cards. Chooses &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot;.</td>
<td>The draft, then the published version; the workflow's settings, each change recorded with who and when (<code>settings_log</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The people who look after stuck requests</td>
<td>Pause or Resume a &quot;Starts when&quot; card; see refused starts and &quot;Run again&quot; one.</td>
<td>The workflow's settings; the inbound log</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>A connection that is not set up is listed to authors but cannot be used: using it is a To do at publish. A disabled one holds its calls, and its address for incoming events answers &quot;try again later&quot;. <strong>Try it</strong> pretends every connection from the samples its catalogue entries carry, in the browser; nothing reaches another system (E-4).</p>
<p>For engineers: the connection ID matches <code>^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$</code> and is never renamed; <code>directoryConnection</code> and <code>notifyConnection</code> are platform settings in the same configuration. An entry's shape (its fields, ignoring labels) never changes under one version; a new shape is a new version (<code>createIssue@2</code>). A snapshot test over every declared entry fails the build when a shape changes under its ID. The catalogue's version is worked out at start-up.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--door-1-a-request-starts">Door 1: a request starts</h2>
<p>A request starts when a person submits the start form, or when another system's event fits one of the workflow's &quot;Starts when&quot; cards. The event's fields fill in the start form, and the request goes on as if a person had pressed Submit.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>The author adds a &quot;Starts when&quot; card to the start stage: what starts it, &quot;Only when&quot;, and &quot;Fill in the form from the ticket&quot;, the Requester being one row. A connection builder writes the trigger entry and the connector's <code>verify</code> and <code>parse</code>; a platform admin writes the connection and gives the other system its address and secret.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>One address per connection, <code>{hooks}/hooks/v1/events/{connection}</code>. The event is handled while the sender waits: checked, mapped, and the request started in one transaction per workflow. The sender gets a synchronous answer with one result per workflow: <code>started</code>, <code>duplicate</code>, <code>notMatched</code>, <code>paused</code> or <code>refused</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td><code>RequestStarted</code>, by the connection, with the binding and the sender's event ID as its trigger. Every event received is one row of the inbound log, with its result or its code.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The same event twice</td>
<td>Starts nothing: the answer is <code>duplicate</code> with the first request.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Paused</td>
<td>The people who look after stuck requests can Pause a card. An event it would take is refused with <code>paused</code> and not kept; the other system must send it again after Resume.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>A final refusal (a mapping that fails, or the start form's rules) leaves no request and is listed on the Stuck requests page for 30 days, where &quot;Run again&quot; runs it on the live version, usually after a publish. A sending refused at the door (unreadable, too big, a bad signature, an unknown connection) is answered with a code. If the platform cannot reach a system it needs, it answers 503 and the sender sends again. Each of these is a log line; nobody is told.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Worked example.</strong> A Helpdesk ticket arrives, and then the same ticket again after a lost answer.</p>

fill: none;"></line><text x="360" y="597" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" alignment-baseline="middle" class="messageText" dy="1em" style="font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, Roboto, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, Arial, sans-serif; fill: none;"></line></svg></div><figcaption class="figure-caption"><span class="fig-id">D10a.</span> What happens when a Helpdesk ticket arrives, and when the same ticket arrives twice?</figcaption></figure>
<p>The starter is the connection. The Requester the card names is a start answer that only a connection may supply; a person who sends it is refused. &quot;The requester can't answer their own request&quot; compares the person acting with that Requester. For engineers: a person's start is <code>POST {base}/requests</code> with a client token made when the form opened; one token starts at most one request.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--door-2-a-person-acts">Door 2: a person acts</h2>
<p>A person answers a task: fills in its form and presses a button.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>The author: the task's form, buttons, &quot;Who is asked&quot;, &quot;The requester can't answer their own request&quot;.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>The lookups a press needs (the person's groups, door 4; the chosen items, door 5) are made before the request is locked, after a check that the task is open; the task is checked again under the lock. The press is then checked in order: still open, the person's groups, among those asked, the task's rule, the answers fit the form, the chosen items, the button's checks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td><code>WaitCompleted</code>: the button, the answers, who acted, and evidence (the groups they belong to among those asked, what each check read, each item looked up). A refused press is written to the attempts log.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>Refused with its code; nothing changes in history. A second press of the same task is refused <code>wait-not-open</code>, naming who answered. A lookup that cannot be made is refused &quot;try again&quot;.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Worked example.</strong> Mei presses Deploy again on Fix deployment: her groups are looked up (Platform team), the press is recorded with them as evidence, and the arrow back to Deploy is taken. Diagram <a href="#fig-d9">D9</a>, under door 4, draws it.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--door-3-the-workflow-calls-another-system">Door 3: the workflow calls another system</h2>
<p>An action that uses a connection: &quot;Look up&quot; reads data and saves it under &quot;Save the results as&quot;; an action that does something makes another system act, such as &quot;Create issue&quot;; &quot;Wait for&quot; asks another system to do something and keeps the request in the stage until it reports the result. The sort is set by what the connection offers (E-10).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>A connection builder writes the entry and the connector's <code>call</code> (and <code>status</code>, for &quot;Wait for&quot;); a platform admin writes the connection; the author adds the action from the &quot;+ Add&quot; menu and sets its inputs, &quot;Save the results as&quot; and &quot;If it fails&quot;.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>The turn that enters the stage records the call (connection, operation, arguments, key) and creates one job for it. The job sends the call with the recorded key. An answer becomes a new turn. No answer, or an unclear one, means the job runs again later with the same key, without limit. A &quot;Wait for&quot; is answered &quot;accepted&quot; with a job reference, and the same job asks for the job's status every poll interval until it ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td><code>WaitOpened</code> when the stage is entered; <code>WaitCompleted</code> (<code>ok</code>, or <code>failed</code> with the failure code) when the result arrives; <code>CallResultLate</code> for a result after the stage was left, which no arrow reads. &quot;Accepted&quot;, the job reference and polls are not recorded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>A clear failure follows &quot;If it fails&quot;: stuck (<code>action-failed</code>), or &quot;Carry on, saving the problem as&quot; values an arrow can test. No answer is never a failure and never stuck. A slow call is waited for; past the time the connection says to expect, the server writes a log line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Leaving the stage</td>
<td>Tells the other system nothing. A call never sent, and a &quot;Look up&quot;, are dropped. An action sent with no clear answer is kept and asked again until it answers, and its result is recorded late.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Retry and Close</td>
<td>Retry, only for a request stuck with <code>action-failed</code> or <code>nobody-to-ask</code>, re-enters the stuck step: under &quot;once&quot; the same key is sent, so the other system returns the earlier result or acts again if that key failed; under &quot;again&quot; a new key is used. Close closes every open task and call; outside jobs are not stopped.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Worked example: Does something, no answer, a failure, Retry.</strong></p>

<p>An answer counts only if it names the job the call holds, so a result about an earlier run never completes the wait of a later one.</p>
<p><strong>The documented exception.</strong> The other system must honour the key. The sample's Jira create does not: it creates without looking for an earlier issue, so if Jira creates the issue and the answer is lost, the next try creates a second one; an admin closes the extra by hand (spec <code>integrations.md</code> section 3). The mock shows this, unfixed.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--door-4-the-directory-says-who-can-answer">Door 4: the directory says who can answer</h2>
<p>Who is in a group. It is read when a task asked of a group opens (the read the compiler adds), to tell whether anybody can answer it; and when a person presses a button on such a task, to check which groups they are in now.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>A platform admin names the directory connection. The author picks the group in &quot;Who is asked&quot;.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>The membership read opens with the task, so the task is visible at once and a slow directory delays nobody; its result decides &quot;nobody to ask&quot;, never who may press. At a press, the person's groups are looked up before the lock.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td>The read's result, as a call result; at a press, the groups among those asked that the person belongs to, as evidence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>The read fails: its groups count as no one; if nobody else can answer, the request is stuck <code>nobody-to-ask</code> and Retry reads the group again. The directory cannot be reached at a press: refused <code>membership-unavailable</code> (&quot;try again&quot;), nothing written, a log line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Who is told about a task</td>
<td>The people asked, less anyone who may not answer it (the Requester where the Requester can't answer).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

<p>The membership read is a snapshot: a person added to the group after it can still answer, while the request shows &quot;nobody to ask&quot; until they do.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--door-5-choices-from-another-system">Door 5: choices from another system</h2>
<p>A question whose choices come from a connection's data source (&quot;From a connection&quot;) or from the members of a directory group (&quot;People from the directory&quot;). The list is read live while the form is open; the chosen item is looked up again when the person presses, so the label recorded comes from the source and not from the browser (E-17, E-20).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>A connection builder writes a data source with list and get; the author sets the question's choices: the source, its filters, the stored and label fields, or the group.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>The page asks for choices by question, never by source (<code>POST {base}/choices</code>); lists are cached for a minute. When the person presses, each answer is looked up again by its stored value with the same inputs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td>The answer as <code>{stored, label}</code> with the source's label; a person as <code>{type: &quot;user&quot;, id}</code>; the lookup as evidence. The list is never recorded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>The list cannot be read: no choices shown. The item is not found: refused <code>choice-unknown</code>. The source cannot be asked at a press: refused <code>source-unavailable</code> (&quot;try again&quot;), nothing written, a log line.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Worked example.</strong></p>

<h2 id="05-integrations--door-6-notifications">Door 6: notifications</h2>
<p>Messages to people. The author's &quot;Notify&quot; sends a message, with values in it, to a person or group, optionally &quot;only when&quot;. The built-in messages are <code>task.assigned</code> (a task opens) and <code>request.stuck</code> with its reason.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>The author writes Notify actions. The words of the built-in messages are the frontend's. Which connection carries messages is a platform setting, <code>notifyConnection</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>One job per turn whose events could match a rule. It reads the request's values as they were at the event, not later; expands groups when sending; leaves out anyone a task's rule says may not answer it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td>Nothing in history.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>The job runs again; a crash can send a message twice. A rule that cannot be worked out sends nothing and writes a log line. It never holds the request.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Worked example.</strong> When Fix deployment is entered, its Notify sends &quot;The deploy of Rotate Ledger database credentials failed with code The tests failed. Fix issue: OPS-101.&quot; to Sam and Mei (the owner is empty, so the Platform team), and <code>task.assigned</code> tells them about the task. Diagram <a href="#fig-d11">D11</a> draws the notifier beside the publisher.</p>
<h2 id="05-integrations--door-7-events-out">Door 7: events out</h2>
<p>Other systems learn what happened to requests, without asking. Every request publishes the built-in events; the author's &quot;Tell other systems&quot; adds <code>request.told@1</code>.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Who sets it up</td>
<td>The author adds &quot;Tell other systems&quot;: &quot;What happened&quot;, &quot;With these values&quot;, &quot;Only when&quot;. A platform admin lists the addresses that receive events; authors never choose who listens.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>At run time</td>
<td>One job per turn. Each event of the turn is posted, in the request's order, to every address in the configuration, signed, one event per POST, at least once.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What is recorded</td>
<td>Nothing. Each event's <code>id</code> is its request, the event's number and the rule, so a repeat has the same <code>id</code> and subscribers dedupe on it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>When it fails</td>
<td>An address that does not answer 2xx fails the job, which runs again later and posts the turn's events again; that request's later events wait. It never holds the request.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Published when</th>
<th><code>data</code></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>request.started@1</code></td>
<td>The request starts</td>
<td><code>startedBy</code>, <code>trigger</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>request.statusChanged@1</code></td>
<td>The status after the turn differs from before it</td>
<td><code>from</code>, <code>to</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>request.stuck@1</code></td>
<td>The request becomes stuck, or stuck another way</td>
<td><code>reason</code>, <code>stage</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>request.unstuck@1</code></td>
<td>It was stuck and is not</td>
<td><code>reason</code>, <code>stage</code>, <code>by</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>request.ended@1</code></td>
<td>The request closes</td>
<td><code>status</code>, <code>stage</code>, <code>closedBy</code>, <code>by</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>request.told@1</code></td>
<td>A &quot;Tell other systems&quot; is reached and its &quot;Only when&quot; is true</td>
<td><code>told: {id, words}</code>, <code>values</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Worked example.</strong></p>
<figure class="diagram" id="fig-d11"><div class="diagram-body"><svg id="mmd-19" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="max-width: 1743px; min-width: 1394px;" viewBox="-213 -10 1742.5 <h2 id="05-integrations--what-other-systems-must-promise-and-what-the-platform-promises-them">What other systems must promise, and what the platform promises them</h2>
<p>For connection builders and engineers.</p>
<p><strong>A connector and its system must promise:</strong> every answer fits the entry's fields; a timeout or &quot;don't know&quot; is <code>unknown</code>, never <code>failed</code>; a Look up has no outside effect; an action honours the key (for a key that succeeded, return that result; for a key that failed, act again); a &quot;Wait for&quot; starts at most one job per key and names the job in every answer; a data source's get finds only what its list would return; a trigger's event ID is the same on every redelivery, and a signed timestamp more than 300 s away is refused.</p>
<p><strong>The platform promises:</strong> one call is always sent with the same key, at least once; one event starts at most one request per workflow, for ever, and the answer says per workflow what became of it, with codes and authored locations; an outbound event is posted at least once, in its request's order, with the same <code>id</code> on every send and <code>time</code> when it happened.</p>

<p>Not built in the first build, with each item's full design archived: held events and re-runs for a paused card, signing-key rotation, callbacks from a &quot;Wait for&quot; job, the reconciler and call log, outbound positions with a pull feed, subscriptions and delivery logs, a catalogue registry with shape hashes, connections and secrets in the database, the alert kinds, and mock systems as HTTP servers. <p>The list, how each would be added and which kept convention makes that cheap is <code>workflow-platform/research/reserved-for-later.md</code>, section &quot;Integrations&quot;; the archived designs are in <code>workflow-platform/research/later/integrations-full/</code>.</p>
