<p>As of 2026-11-16, everything below is committed. Every screen of the editor and of the pages people use is built, on the engine's core; the server they talk to is still the stand-in.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Folder</th>
<th>What is in it</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>app</code></td>
<td>The route table (hash routes) for every screen; the editor's top bar and the app frame; the Glossary; a page showing every primitive (<code>/ui-reference</code>); the model slots filled; the services provided to every screen. The development host also has the controls listed below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ui</code></td>
<td>Tokens from the mockup kit, and 21 primitives: icon, button, icon button, field, text input, text area, select, checkbox, date field, external link, popover, dialog, menu, tabs, tooltip, chip, mark, card, empty state, callout, page. The overlays, menus and tabs are built on Radix.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>words</code></td>
<td>The shared vocabulary and one file per feature, including the words for every finding, refusal, story entry and change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>contract</code></td>
<td>The authored format, the catalogue types and the sample workflows, imported from the repository's <code>contract/</code> folder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>model</code></td>
<td>The store with undo and redo (up to 200 steps), the revision and the save state; about a hundred named commands in thirteen groups; the derivations; <code>describe</code>, which says any part of a workflow in the author's words; and the editor session, which opens a workflow, checks it after each pause in typing, autosaves it with its revision, and publishes it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>services</code></td>
<td>The interface; the engine's core behind it; and the stand-in for the server (see &quot;How the frontend uses the engine's core&quot;).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>features/*</code></td>
<td>Every screen. The workflows list. The editor's Diagram, In words and Values tabs, the stage panel, Settings, To do and Worth knowing, and Publish with what changed since the live version. The form editor, with one form view that Try it and the pages people use show too. The value picker, the &quot;when&quot; builder and the formula editor. Actions: Look up, Wait for, an action that does something, Notify, Save a value and Tell other systems. The Connections page, and &quot;Also starts from another system&quot; on the start stage, with Pause and Resume. Try it, with the story, &quot;So far&quot; and the Test outbox. The pages people use: start a request, My tasks, the requests list (with the stuck requests and the starts that were refused), and a request's page.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p><strong>Controls on the development host only:</strong> a switcher to act as another person, &quot;Reset sample data&quot;, &quot;Pretend [connection] sent this now&quot; to start a request from another system, and the version of the engine's core in the footer.</p>
<p><strong>Not built yet:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>A way to see the history of a workflow's versions.</li>
<li>Anything about time that an author sets, such as deadlines or reminders: the engine has no clock.</li>
<li>Signing in: the development host offers the person switcher instead.</li>
<li>A control to pretend that another system answered a &quot;Wait for&quot; on a live request: such a request waits.</li>
<li>The real server behind the authoring and runtime APIs. The engine owner has built its store and both APIs, but not yet its workers, its endpoints for other systems, the mock systems or its development host, so the frontend cannot run against it. Until then the stand-in plays the server.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Known defects</strong> from the last check of the running app: the times shown for a live request's later actions are wrong, because they come from the test host's clock, which moves one second per move rather than with real time; and a few wordings need fixing. The frontend's decisions are U-1 to U-22 in <a href="#doc-11-decisions-frontend">Decisions: frontend</a>.</p>
</section>
<section class="doc" data-file="09-people-and-permissions.md"><h1 id="doc-09-people-and-permissions">People and permissions</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Engine owner.</p>
<p class="doc-meta doc-answers">Answers: Who may author, publish, act and administer, and where is that enforced?</p>
<p>The platform does not sign anyone in. The existing application tells the engine who is signed in on every call, and the engine decides what that person may do from three things: the workflow's settings, what a request recorded, and the directory, asked at the moment of acting. This document names each role, gives one matrix of who may do what, and says where each rule is checked and what is kept as evidence. Sources: decisions E-14, E-16, E-17, E-19 to E-24; the authoring API and runtime API (section 2 of each); integrations section 6 of the kernel package v2.20; <code>engine/spec/integrations.md</code> sections 9.4, 11.1 and 11.5; decision E-33; the data model. Nothing here has run.</p>
<h2 id="09-people-and-permissions--the-roles">The roles</h2>
<p>One person can hold several roles: the author of a workflow is usually also one of the people who look after its stuck requests.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Role</th>
<th>Who holds it</th>
<th>How the engine knows</th>
<th>Recorded as</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Workflow author</strong></td>
<td>The people and groups listed as authors in the workflow's settings. Whoever creates a workflow is its first author.</td>
<td>The settings record; group membership looked up live.</td>
<td><code>drafts.saved_by</code>; <code>definitions.published_by</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Requester</strong></td>
<td>The person who started the request. After a start by another system, the person its &quot;Starts when&quot; names from what was sent; if it names nobody, there is no Requester.</td>
<td>The recorded start answer that names the Requester, when present; else the starter, when the starter is a person.</td>
<td><code>RequestStarted.by</code>, or the start answer <code>requester</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Person asked</strong></td>
<td>Whoever a task's &quot;Who is asked&quot; gives when the task opens: people, and groups whose members are not listed. &quot;People in [group]&quot; asks the group.</td>
<td>Recorded when the task opens.</td>
<td><code>WaitOpened.assignees</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Workflow admin</strong></td>
<td>The people and groups in &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot;, a workflow setting; when it is not set, the authors. The engine calls them the workflow's admins.</td>
<td>The settings record, read when an admin acts and when the stuck message is sent; group membership looked up live. Not versioned: a change applies at once to running requests.</td>
<td><code>Overridden.by</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Platform admin</strong></td>
<td>Holders of the existing application's platform-admin entitlement.</td>
<td>Unknown: depends on the existing application.</td>
<td><code>Overridden.by</code> and the other <code>by</code> and <code>created_by</code> columns</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Connection builder</strong></td>
<td>An engineer who writes connector code (the code for one kind of system) and its catalogue entries. The code ships with a deployment (E-19).</td>
<td>Not at run time: there is no such role in the running platform.</td>
<td>Nothing at run time</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Two things act that are not people. Each is written <code>{type, id}</code> wherever the engine records who did something:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Actor</th>
<th>Written as</th>
<th>What it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>A connection</strong></td>
<td><code>{type: &quot;connection&quot;, id: &quot;&lt;connection ID&gt;&quot;}</code>, for example <code>helpdesk</code></td>
<td>Starts a request through a live &quot;Starts when&quot;; returns a call's result. It is never asked a task and never an admin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>The system</strong></td>
<td><code>{type: &quot;system&quot;, id: &quot;engine&quot;}</code></td>
<td>Acts for the engine itself.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>The connection IDs <code>engine</code>, <code>system</code> and <code>platform</code> are reserved, so no connection can pass for the engine (E-17).</p>
<h2 id="09-people-and-permissions--who-may-do-what">Who may do what</h2>
<p>&quot;Where it is checked&quot; names one of: <strong>the API</strong> (the authoring or runtime API, before any turn; it also turns away a call with no signed-in person, <code>401</code>); <strong>the engine at act time</strong> (inside the turn, under the request's lock, in the kernel's refusal order; the directory and data-source lookups it needs are made just before the lock, so no outside call is made while a request is locked); <strong>the hook</strong> (the inbound endpoint for other systems, before any transaction). &quot;Assumed&quot; marks a rule the product owner has not decided.</p>
<figure class="matrix" id="fig-d24"><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Action</th>
<th>Who may</th>
<th>Where it is checked</th>
<th>Evidence recorded</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Create a workflow</td>
<td>Any signed-in person, who becomes its first author. Assumed.</td>
<td>API</td>
<td><code>workflows.created_by</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Edit a draft</td>
<td>The workflow's authors and platform admins. Assumed.</td>
<td>API: others get <code>forbidden</code></td>
<td><code>drafts.saved_by</code>, <code>saved_at</code>, overwritten on every save</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Use a connection's entries in a workflow</td>
<td>Every author may use every entry of a ready connection.</td>
<td>Publish: an entry of a connection that is not set up is a To do</td>
<td>The published version names each operation, source and trigger</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Publish</td>
<td>The workflow's authors and platform admins. Assumed.</td>
<td>API, then the server runs the check and the compiler again; any To do refuses (<code>has-todo</code>)</td>
<td><code>definitions.published_by</code>, <code>published_at</code>; the version is immutable</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Change settings: name, authors, &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot;</td>
<td>The workflow's authors and platform admins. Assumed.</td>
<td>API: an empty author list is refused (<code>last-author</code>), and so is an empty &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot;</td>
<td><code>settings_log</code>: each change, with who made it and when. Settings are not versioned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Start a request, as a person</td>
<td>Any signed-in person, if the start task's rules allow it (its rule on who may answer, its questions, its checks). Who is asked by the start task is not checked at start.</td>
<td>API, then the engine at act time</td>
<td><code>RequestStarted.by</code>; the start task's <code>WaitCompleted.evidence</code>; a refusal in <code>attempts_log</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Start a request, as another system</td>
<td>A connection whose event fits a live, unpaused &quot;Starts when&quot; of the workflow's highest published version</td>
<td>The hook (the connector verifies the sender's signature), the binding's mapping, then the engine at act time as for a person</td>
<td><code>RequestStarted.by</code> (the connection) and <code>trigger</code>; one <code>inbound_log</code> row per event and workflow, a final refusal included, and a <code>start-refused</code> log line</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Answer a task</td>
<td>A person among those recorded as asked, directly or through a group they belong to now, whom the task's rule allows (for example &quot;The requester can't answer&quot;)</td>
<td>The engine at act time</td>
<td><code>WaitCompleted.by</code>; <code>evidence.memberOf</code> (the asked groups they belong to), what each check read, each choice looked up; a refusal in <code>attempts_log</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>See a request: its values, tasks, story, that it is stuck and the reason</td>
<td>Any signed-in person (E-19)</td>
<td>API</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>See why it is stuck in detail: for <code>action-failed</code>, the operation's failure code and the number of delivery attempts</td>
<td>Workflow admins and platform admins; the engineers' detail (the internal error behind an error, for debugging) platform admins only</td>
<td>API, at read time, groups looked up live; others do not receive the fields</td>
<td>Nothing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Retry, Close</td>
<td>Workflow admins and platform admins, also on their own requests. A reason is required. Retry only for a request stuck with <code>action-failed</code> or <code>nobody-to-ask</code>; Close for any open request (E-23).</td>
<td>The engine, when the admin turn is submitted: others are refused <code>not-admin</code>; Retry on a request that is not stuck is refused <code>not-stuck</code>, on one stuck with <code>nothing-fits</code> or <code>error</code> <code>not-retryable</code></td>
<td><code>Overridden {by, reason, actions}</code>; a <code>not-admin</code> refusal in <code>attempts_log</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Pause or resume a &quot;Starts when&quot; (a paused one refuses events); list the starts refused in the last 30 days and run one again (on the live version's bindings at that moment)</td>
<td>The workflow's admins and platform admins</td>
<td>API: others get <code>not-admin</code></td>
<td><code>workflow_settings.paused_bindings</code>; each pause or resume, with who and when, in <code>settings_log</code>; a run again is an <code>inbound_log</code> row with <code>by</code> and <code>retry_of</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Set up a connection</td>
<td>A platform admin, in the deployment's configuration; read at start-up only (E-19, E-33). No screen and no API.</td>
<td>Outside the engine: whoever may change the deployment's configuration. Unknown: depends on the existing application.</td>
<td>Not recorded by the engine</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Name the addresses that receive outbound events</td>
<td>A platform admin, in the deployment's configuration (E-17, E-33). Authors never choose who listens.</td>
<td>Outside the engine</td>
<td>Not recorded by the engine</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><figcaption class="figure-caption"><span class="fig-id">D24.</span> Who may do what, where it is checked, and what is recorded</figcaption></figure>

<h2 id="09-people-and-permissions--who-is-asked-and-who-may-act">Who is asked, and who may act</h2>
<p><strong>Recorded when the task opens.</strong> When a stage is entered the engine works out each task's &quot;Who is asked&quot; and records the result in <code>WaitOpened.assignees</code> as user and group references, with groups not expanded. A reference that is neither a user nor a group, such as a connection, is dropped and not recorded (E-17). The list may be empty: the task still opens, nobody can answer it, and the request is stuck with <code>nobody-to-ask</code>.</p>
<p>&quot;People in [group]&quot; under &quot;Who is asked&quot; is the same as asking the group: the group is recorded as asked, and no separate directory read is made for it (E-24).</p>
<p>For a task that may ask a group, the compiler adds a read of the group's members through the directory connection beside the task, in the task's own engine stage: a call wait <code>&lt;task&gt;__members</code> on <code>membersOf@1</code> with <code>onFailure: outcome</code>, opened with the task and recorded like any call. No arrow reads it. It exists so that &quot;nobody can answer&quot; is decided from history. <strong>Who can answer a task</strong> is the people asked directly plus the recorded members of the groups asked, less the Requester where the Requester may not answer. Nobody-to-ask means that set is empty: the task matches its rule in the published version's <code>nobodyToAsk</code> block (integrations section 11.5). A read that fails contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts (E-24). Retry for nobody-to-ask therefore always reads the group again. The tasks step leaves by an explicit condition that every task is answered, so a pending read never holds up an answered task; leaving the step cancels the read (E-23).</p>
<p><strong>Checked live when the person acts.</strong> The lookups the act needs, the person's groups and each answer chosen from a list, are made before the request is locked, after an unlocked check that the task is open. The task is checked again under the lock, and no outside call is made while the request is locked (E-23). So an act on a task that is no longer open is answered <code>wait-not-open</code> even while the directory is down. The engine checks, in order:</p>
<ol>
<li>The task is still open (<code>wait-not-open</code>, with who answered it, if anyone).</li>
<li>If a group is among those asked, the directory is asked which groups the person is in now, within 5 s (<code>membership-unavailable</code> if it cannot answer).</li>
<li>The person is asked directly or is in an asked group (<code>not-assignee</code>).</li>
<li>The task's rule allows them (<code>may</code>).</li>
<li>The answers fit the button's questions (<code>invalid-data</code>), each answer from a list in another system or the directory is looked up again by its stored value (<code>source-unavailable</code>, <code>choice-unknown</code>), and the checks pass (<code>check</code>).</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Recorded as evidence.</strong> The answer's <code>WaitCompleted</code> keeps who answered, the asked groups they belonged to at that moment, what each check read, and each item looked up. A refused attempt changes nothing in history and is kept in <code>attempts_log</code> for 90 days.</p>
<p>What the pages show follows the same rules but is advisory: My tasks lists open tasks whose recorded asked names the person or a group they are in now, less a task the person is asked but may not answer; whether each button can be pressed on a task page may be worked out from group memberships cached for 60 s. The act always checks again. The message <code>task.assigned</code> goes to everyone asked, with groups expanded when it is sent, less anyone who may not answer the task, such as a Requester who can't answer (E-33).</p>
<p><strong>The Requester exclusion.</strong> &quot;The requester can't answer their own request&quot; compiles to the task's <code>may</code>: the person acting must not be the Requester (<code>engine/spec/integrations.md</code> section 9.4).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>How the request started</th>
<th>Who the Requester is</th>
<th>Who is excluded</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>A person submitted the start form</td>
<td>That person</td>
<td>That person</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Another system started it, and its &quot;Starts when&quot; names a person from what was sent (E-16)</td>
<td>That person, recorded as the start answer <code>requester</code>. The connector maps the outside user to a directory reference.</td>
<td>That person, though the request's starter is the connection. This is what stops a ticket's reporter from approving their own ticket.</td>

</table></div><p>Only a connection may supply <code>requester</code>. A person who sends it, at the start or on a start form the request was sent back to, is refused <code>invalid-data</code> (<code>unknown-question</code>), enforced by a check the compiler adds to the start task. The nobody-to-ask rule leaves the Requester out in the same way.</p>
<p><strong>When the directory cannot be reached.</strong></p>

<td>Its job is retried by the queue.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h2 id="09-people-and-permissions--assumed-and-depending-on-the-existing-application">Assumed, and depending on the existing application</h2>
<p><strong>Assumed, not decided by the product owner:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Who may author.</strong> Any signed-in person may create a workflow and becomes its first author; a workflow's authors may edit its draft, publish it and change its settings; platform admins may do all of that, so a workflow whose authors have all left can be recovered (authoring API section 2). If the product owner decides otherwise, only who is refused <code>forbidden</code> changes.</li>
<li><strong>Every signed-in person sees every request,</strong> including its answers, call results and story (E-19; data model section 5). Restricting who may view a request is later. It needs no change to history: a new projection over <code>RequestStarted.by</code>, <code>WaitOpened.assignees</code> and <code>WaitCompleted.by</code>, with group membership resolved when asked.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Depends on the existing application:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Sign-in.</strong> How the signed-in person reaches the engine's API, how the host supplies the caller, and how cross-site requests are guarded: unknown: depends on the existing application. The engine trusts the caller the host supplies and never reads a user from a header or a body. The development host has its own sign-in, where a person is picked from a list; it is refused elsewhere.</li>
<li><strong>The platform-admin entitlement.</strong> How it is checked: unknown: depends on the existing application.</li>
<li><strong>The directory's API,</strong> its limits and its failure modes, which decide how often <code>membership-unavailable</code> occurs; the pattern of a directory object ID: unknown: depends on the existing application.</li>
<li><strong>Who may change the deployment's configuration and its secret store,</strong> which is who can set up a connection: unknown: depends on the existing application.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="09-people-and-permissions--personal-data">Personal data</h2>
<p><strong>Where it can be.</strong> Answers, values, call arguments and results, and free text written by people or by other systems (an admin's reason, an outside system's error message, an expression error that quotes data).</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Holds request data</th>
<th>Holds no request data by design</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>events</code> (history), <code>requests.data</code></td>
<td><code>definitions</code>, settings, the configuration</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>pending_calls.args</code>, until the result is recorded</td>
<td>The server's log lines: IDs and codes only, never arguments, results or an outside system's message</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inbound_log.sent</code>, what another system sent</td>
<td>Outbound events: no payload is stored</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>attempts_log.input</code>, what a refused attempt sent</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Outside the engine, messages sent by email and Slack, and values a workflow tells other systems, are held by their receivers. Whether the user IDs recorded for who acted, who was asked and which asked groups a person was in count as personal data is open (spec section 9).</p>
<p>Erasing personal data is not in the first build (E-33). Which values are personal, and when they are erased, is for the product owner.</p>
<p><strong>What the first build already does:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Outbound event payloads are not stored. They are worked out from history when a turn's events are posted.</li>
<li>The built-in public events carry IDs, statuses and reasons only, never answers. Only &quot;Tell other systems&quot; sends values, and only the ones its author chose (E-22).</li>
<li>There is no file storage, so no attachments.</li>
</ul>
</section>
<section class="doc" data-file="11-decisions-engine.md"><h1 id="doc-11-decisions-engine">Decisions: engine owner</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Engine owner session. Every entry was decided by the engine owner under the product owner's delegation of 2026-11-15 and is <strong>pending the product owner's review</strong>. An entry says what was decided and why, in a few lines. Detail lives in the document it points to.</p>
<p>Terms: &quot;first build&quot; is what this repo builds and runs. &quot;Shape only&quot; means history and tables can hold it and replay handles it, but nothing produces it. &quot;Later&quot; means designed enough not to block it, not built.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-1-one-repo-four-folders-2026-11-15">E-1. One repo, four folders (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p><code>workflow-system</code>, with <code>docs/</code>, <code>contract/</code>, <code>engine/</code>, <code>frontend/</code>. Ownership and commit rules are in the root <code>README.md</code>. Agreed with the frontend owner.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-2-the-kernel-spec-stays-where-it-is-this-repo-holds-a-copy">E-2. The kernel spec stays where it is; this repo holds a copy</h2>
<p><code>engine/spec/</code> is a read-only copy of the engine design package (kernel spec v2.17 at the last refresh; <code>engine/spec/SOURCE.md</code> names the commit). Spec changes are made in <code>workflow-platform/engine</code> (version bump, decision log) and copied again. Reason: one source, and that repo's rules about the spec keep applying.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-3-two-engine-packages-a-pure-core-and-a-server">E-3. Two engine packages: a pure core and a server</h2>
<ul>
<li><code>engine/packages/core</code>: pure TypeScript with no I/O and no Node-only API, so it runs in a browser and on the server. It holds the authored-format types, the compiler (authored format to published definition), the checks, the kernel (<code>decide</code>, <code>evolve</code>), the CEL environment, and an in-memory host that runs a request with faked connections.</li>
<li><code>engine/packages/server</code>: Postgres store, the turn transaction, workers (dispatcher, reconciler, notifier, event publisher), connectors, inbound hooks, the HTTP API.</li>
<li>The server is the authority. At publish it runs the check and the compile again and stores its own result. What the browser computes is a preview.</li>
<li>The frontend depends on <code>core</code> as a local package. The API reports the core version it runs, so a stale browser bundle is detected.</li>
</ul>
<p>Reason: <code>decide</code> and <code>evolve</code> are pure by design, and the check and the compile have no need of I/O. One implementation gives the editor instant checks and a Try it that behaves exactly like the engine.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-4-try-it-runs-in-the-browser-on-the-cores-in-memory-host">E-4. Try it runs in the browser, on the core's in-memory host</h2>
<p>No server state for test runs in the first build. Connections are faked from the samples in the catalogue; sends go to a test outbox held in memory. Reason: simplest thing that is exact. A server-side test run can be added later without changing the contract.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-5-everything-server-side-is-the-engines">E-5. Everything server-side is the engine's</h2>
<p>Drafts, published versions (the authored source is stored beside the compiled definition), workflow settings, connections, trigger deliveries, event subscriptions, the catalogue.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-6-forms">E-6. Forms</h2>
<p>The authored format carries a form in the editor's terms. The compiler derives the JSON Schema and the per-outcome checks. The frontend owns the renderer. A published version keeps the authored form so a task can be rendered from the version its request runs on.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-7-reporting-rule">E-7. Reporting rule</h2>
<p>The engine reports a problem as a code, a location in the authored format, and parameters. It never reports a location in the compiled definition; the published definition's origin map (spec section 7) is what makes that possible at run time. The one piece of prose the engine passes through is a check's <code>message</code>, which is the author's own text.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-8-scope-the-build-follows">E-8. Scope the build follows</h2>
<p>The editor model of 2026-11-14 (<code>workflow/mvp-scope.md</code>), pending the product owner's review of the five overturned 2026-11-13 decisions. So: several tasks in one stage (a static list), send-back arrows, actions inside a stage, an in-workflow list, &quot;If empty, use&quot;, per-button &quot;Needed to press&quot; are built. &quot;Everyone in a group must answer&quot; (<code>foreach</code>) stays shape only.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-9-integrations-seven-doors-and-nothing-enters-a-requests-history-any-other-way">E-9. Integrations: seven doors, and nothing enters a request's history any other way</h2>
<p>The product owner asked on 2026-11-15 for upstream and downstream integrations to be designed and shown working against mock systems. Items marked * go beyond <code>requirements/mvp.md</code> for that reason; each is cheap to cut.</p>

</table></div><p>Rules that follow from the kernel and are not relaxed:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>No unsolicited input to a running request.</strong> An outside event can start a request (door 1) or answer a call the engine made (door 3). It cannot poke a request any other way. &quot;Wait for system X&quot; is an await call: the engine asks, so it can also check on it. An unsolicited &quot;message wait&quot; is later; the spec reserves nothing for it, because wait kinds are an open list.</li>
<li><strong>No clock.</strong> Timers, deadlines, reminders and scheduled starts are later. Timer waits are reserved in the spec.</li>
<li><strong>Outside data is recorded when it arrives.</strong> <code>decide</code> never reads live data.</li>
<li><strong>A notification or an outbound event can never stop a request.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Pages also read live data that is recorded nowhere</strong> (people search, choices while a form is open, names for display). Those reads are not doors: nothing they return enters history except through door 2 or door 5.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-10-the-catalogue-is-fixed-by-us-in-the-first-build-and-is-data-to-the-editor">E-10. The catalogue is fixed by us in the first build, and is data to the editor</h2>
<p>A connector is code. A connection is a configured instance of a connector (address, credentials, defaults), set up by a platform admin, not by an author. The catalogue lists what an author can use: operations (read, write, await), data sources for choices, triggers, and event sinks, each versioned, with input and output schemas and a sample. The editor must treat the catalogue as data and hard-code no connector. Later, a customer-defined connection (generic HTTP call, generic inbound webhook) produces the same catalogue entries, so neither the editor nor the engine changes.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-11-development-stack-for-the-engine">E-11. Development stack for the engine</h2>
<p>Node LTS, TypeScript, npm, Vitest. The store targets Postgres; tests and the dev host run on PGlite (Postgres compiled to WebAssembly, in process), with real Postgres through Docker required for the cases that test concurrency (PGlite serves one connection, so it cannot show two transactions racing). The API is plain functions with thin web-standard <code>Request -&gt; Response</code> handlers over them, so it can be mounted in the existing Next.js application later. All cheap to change.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-12-the-mock-outside-systems">E-12. The mock outside systems</h2>
<p>Each is a small in-process server with real HTTP in and out, so the wiring is real, and each can be inspected. Platform code names none of them; they are catalogue entries.</p>

</table></div><h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-14-how-the-authored-format-contract-part-a-v0-compiles">E-14. How the authored format (contract part A, v0) compiles</h2>
<p>Answers given to the frontend owner on 2026-11-15. The format is <code>contract/authored-format.ts</code>; the frontend holds the pen.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>One authored stage becomes a chain of engine stages:</strong> arrival actions, the tasks, the after-response actions in listed order, then a routing step that holds the arrows. Compiler-added names are <code>&lt;itemId&gt;__&lt;local&gt;</code>; authored IDs never contain a double underscore.</li>
<li><strong>IDs carry through.</strong> Value IDs are the data paths, button IDs the outcome IDs, task IDs the wait IDs, status IDs the status IDs. A rename changes nothing published.</li>
<li><strong>A status that depends on how a stage was entered</strong> (&quot;If sent back&quot;) is compiled by emitting the stage twice. An arrow sends back when its target is a stage every request must already have passed through to reach the arrow's source (the target dominates the source). Core computes it; it is not stored.</li>
<li><strong>The start stage:</strong> a new request begins at the form. The start stage's arrival actions run only when a request is sent back there.</li>
<li><strong>Workflow name, description, authors and &quot;Stuck requests go to&quot; are settings,</strong> outside the document and not versioned.</li>
<li><strong>The directory inside a workflow:</strong> a <code>members</code> step or an &quot;is in group&quot; test is a recorded read call made when the request enters the section that uses it. Directory choices on a task use that recorded list and are checked when the person acts. The start form is the exception: read live, not checked.</li>
<li><strong>Notifications, and things told to other systems, read the request's values as they were at the triggering event,</strong> folded from history. This needs a small spec change (the notifier's context gains <code>data</code> as of the event); it goes into the next spec version with the integrations changes.</li>
<li><strong>A task cancelled by an early arrow</strong> has its &quot;Button pressed&quot; and &quot;Answered by&quot; values emptied for that visit; its questions' values keep what they had.</li>
<li><strong>A request started by an outside system</strong> has the connection as its starter. As a person the Requester is empty, so &quot;If empty, use&quot; applies. Naming a person from the event as the Requester is later.</li>
<li><strong>A hidden question</strong> must arrive with no answer and is never needed; compiled as conditional checks.</li>
<li><strong>The catalogue gives the default for &quot;when the stage is entered again&quot;</strong> (<code>once</code> or <code>again</code>); publish writes it explicitly.</li>
<li><strong>Words belong to the frontend,</strong> including the three built-in notification messages, which the notifier sends from a data file under <code>contract/</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-16-three-more-answers-on-triggers-and-failures-2026-11-15">E-16. Three more answers on triggers and failures (2026-11-15)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>A trigger binding may name the Requester</strong> from a sent field of kind person. This replaces the &quot;later&quot; in E-14. The request is still recorded as started by the connection; the Requester is carried as one more start answer that only a connection may supply, so the kernel does not change. Mapping an outside user to a directory reference is the connector's job.</li>
<li><strong>An inbound delivery is handled while the sender waits,</strong> and the response says per binding: started, did not fit, refused (with codes), or already started. So the sending system can show a refusal. The workflow admins are told too.</li>
<li><strong>A failed read can be carried on like any other call.</strong> The editor offers the same &quot;If it fails&quot; choice on every connection action.</li>
<li><strong>A start stage that has a connection action after its form needs a status,</strong> because the request can be seen sitting there (or stuck there). Core raises a To do.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-17-the-integrations-design-settled-after-the-design-round-2026-11-15">E-17. The integrations design, settled after the design round (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p>Three independent designs and two reviews were written (<code>engine/notes/integrations/</code>, deleted after E-33; git keeps them). These are the choices made between them. The exact shapes are in <code>engine/design/integrations-shapes.md</code>; the explanation with diagrams is <code>docs/05-integrations.md</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Names kept forever</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>A call wait names its <strong>connection</strong> (the field was <code>connector</code>), and <code>by.type</code> for a non-person is <code>connection</code> (was <code>connector</code>). A connector is code and is never recorded; the versioned operation (<code>createIssue@1</code>) is the contract. Connection IDs <code>engine</code>, <code>system</code> and <code>platform</code> are reserved.</li>
<li><code>RequestStarted.trigger</code> is null when a person starts a request. For a start by an outside event it is <code>{kind: &quot;event&quot;, id, connection, event, eventId}</code>: the binding, the connection, the catalogue trigger with its version, and the sender's ID for the occurrence. Other kinds (a schedule) stay reserved.</li>
<li><code>StageExited</code> and <code>TransitionFired</code> name their stage. A person <code>WaitOpened</code> records the <code>foreach</code> item. Both are cheap now and impossible later.</li>
<li>Enum values: codes (refusal reasons, causes, error codes) are kebab-case; type discriminators are lowerCamelCase.</li>
<li>A data key or schema property may not start with <code>$</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Door 1: a request started by an outside event</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Bindings are published with the version, in a <code>triggers</code> block that <code>decide</code> never reads. Only the highest published version's bindings are live. A workflow admin can pause a binding without publishing.</li>
<li>The mapping is CEL over <code>sent</code> (what the other system sent) and the workflow's lists. It runs before the turn, so a mapping error refuses the start; it never faults a request.</li>
<li>The starter is the connection. The Requester named by a binding is a start answer, <code>requester</code>, that only a connection may supply; a person who sends it is refused. Authored value IDs start with <code>v_</code>; every other top-level data key belongs to the compiler.</li>
<li>A reference that is not a user or a group is dropped when a person wait opens, so &quot;nobody to ask&quot; alerts the workflow admins. The compiler also filters them out.</li>
<li>One event starts at most one request per workflow: the first matching binding. The dedupe key is (connection, event ID, workflow), written in the start turn's transaction and kept for ever without the body.</li>
<li>The delivery is handled while the sender waits, one transaction per start. The answer says per workflow: started, did not match, refused (with codes), duplicate, or paused. A disabled connection answers 503 so the sender retries.</li>
<li>Inbound requests are signed (Standard Webhooks: HMAC with a timestamp). A refused inbound request alerts the platform admins, at most once an hour per connection and reason. Bodies over 256 KiB are refused unread.</li>
<li>A binding that cannot fill a question its button needs is a To do at publish.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Door 3: await</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The kernel sees an await as a write call. &quot;Await&quot; is a property of the catalogue operation. The connector may answer <code>accepted</code> with the outside job's reference; the pending call then waits.</li>
<li><strong>A callback is a nudge, not a result.</strong> The callback URL carries a token signed by the engine that names the request, connection, operation and key. On a valid callback the engine asks the connector for the job's status and records that answer. So every await operation must answer a status question by key and job reference, a forged or stale callback can record nothing, and there is one path by which a result arrives.</li>
<li>A result is tied to its outside job: it is recorded only for the call whose job reference it carries.</li>
<li>The reconciler also asks on a schedule. Any call, of any sort, that has no result after the time its operation says to expect raises one alert to the workflow admins. Workers may read the clock; the kernel still does not.</li>
<li>Leaving the stage does not stop the outside job. Its eventual result is recorded as a late result.</li>
<li>Whether a wait already has a result is read from history, never from working tables.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Door 5: choices</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The page asks for a question's choices by naming the question, not the data source. The server works out the source's inputs from the stored form and the answers so far.</li>
<li>When the person acts, the engine looks the answer up in the source by its stored value, as it looks up group membership. An unknown item is refused. The label recorded is the source's, not the browser's. If the source cannot be reached the act is refused with &quot;try again&quot;. This replaces &quot;only the answer is recorded, unchecked&quot; in E-9: a label that approvers read as fact must not come from the browser.</li>
<li>A data source must therefore offer two things: list (with search) and get by stored value.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Door 4: membership</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>If the directory cannot be reached when a person acts, the act is refused with &quot;try again&quot; and nothing changes.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Door 7: outbound events</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 with a <code>position</code> extension: a gap-free number, sent as a decimal string, that orders every event the platform publishes.</li>
<li>Six event types: <code>request.started@1</code>, <code>request.statusChanged@1</code> (status before and after a turn, compared once per turn), <code>request.stuck@1</code>, <code>request.unstuck@1</code>, <code>request.ended@1</code>, and <code>request.told@1</code> for what an author declares. <code>request.erased@1</code> is reserved.</li>
<li><strong>Everything an author declares is one type, <code>request.told@1</code>,</strong> carrying the thing told (<code>{id, words}</code>, like a status) and the author's named values. No type per declaration and no schema versions to manage in the first build.</li>
<li>What an author declares lives in an <code>events</code> block beside <code>notifications</code>. Its values, and a notification's, read the request's data as it was at the event that set them off.</li>
<li>Payloads are not stored. They are worked out from history at each send, so an erasure reaches later sends. Only the erasure marker may differ between two sends of one event.</li>
<li>Subscriptions are set up by a platform admin. Authors never pick who listens. Delivery is one event per POST, signed, in order, at least once, retried without limit; a subscriber that is down blocks only itself, and the platform admins are alerted after 15 minutes. There is also a pull feed by position.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Catalogue</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>A connector declares its operations in value kinds (<code>Field[]</code>), the editor's vocabulary; the engine derives JSON Schema from them. One vocabulary for authors, connectors, and later customer-defined connections.</li>
<li>A changed shape under an existing <code>name@version</code> disables that connection and alerts the platform admins. It does not stop the server.</li>
<li>Secrets sit behind a small store interface. The first build keeps them encrypted in Postgres.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Alerts</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Every alert is a row in <code>platform_alerts</code> before anything is sent, so alerts survive the message service being down.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Left out of the first build on purpose:</strong> batching and rewinding of outbound events, a &quot;send again&quot; button for calls, a connection test button, rotation of the callback signing key, telling an outside job to stop, a third admin action (&quot;clear only&quot;), and naming a Requester who is not in what the event sent.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-18-formats-and-the-expression-library-2026-11-15">E-18. Formats and the expression library (2026-11-15)</h2>
<ul>
<li>The JSON of a published definition and of every event is in <code>engine/design/</code>. A number from a form or a formula is always a CEL double; integers stay within the range JSON carries exactly.</li>
<li>What a condition read is recorded as the value at the end of each path it selected, or &quot;absent&quot;.</li>
<li>The origin map names, for each compiled element and where needed each field of it, the authored item and part it came from. A fault's field pointer is for engineers; what an author sees comes from the origin map.</li>
<li>A stage has at most one &quot;in all other cases&quot; transition, and it is last.</li>
<li>The CEL library is <code>@marcbachmann/cel-js</code>, pinned to an exact version and wrapped by an engine-owned environment that replaces its regular expressions, timestamp parsing and date reading. It is the only pure JavaScript library found that both type-checks with source positions and supports optional values. A hands-on trial comes before any kernel code depends on it.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-19-stuck-the-compiler-and-composites-and-who-sets-up-a-connection-2026-11-15">E-19. Stuck, the compiler and composites, and who sets up a connection (2026-11-15)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>&quot;Stuck&quot; is one state outside the kernel:</strong> <code>stuck {reason, at}</code> with reasons <code>actionFailed</code>, <code>nobodyToAsk</code>, <code>nothingFits</code>, <code>error</code>. It is the same in a request's story, the request view and the lists. The kernel keeps its own distinction (a fault of kind error or stuck; nobody-to-ask is not a fault and is worked out from the recorded task and membership read).</li>
<li><strong>Retry</strong> re-enters the step that is stuck: a failed action is tried again; for nobody-to-ask, who is asked is read again and the stage's tasks are opened afresh. Known limits: an empty value stays empty, so Close is the only way out until values can be changed by hand; in a stage with several tasks every task is asked again.</li>
<li><strong>Who sees what:</strong> every signed-in person sees every request, including that it is stuck and the reason code. The stuck list, the error detail, and Retry and Close are for the workflow admins and platform admins.</li>
<li><strong>The compiler emits kernel elements directly.</strong> It does not use the spec's Approval and Task composites; those remain for hand-written definitions. The origin map ties each element to its authored item.</li>
<li><strong>A connection is set up by a platform admin, by configuration,</strong> with its secret in the secret store. No screen in the first build. A connection builder is an engineer who writes connector code that ships with a deployment.</li>
<li><code>jira.createIssue@1</code> returns <code>key</code> and <code>url</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-20-calls-made-after-the-second-design-round-2026-11-15">E-20. Calls made after the second design round (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p>The reviews of <code>engine/design/integrations-shapes.md</code>, of the contract Draft 2 and of the expression-library trial returned these judgment calls. Where one changes an earlier decision, it says so.</p>
<p><strong>Kept forever</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>A person or group in a request's data is always <code>{type, id}</code>,</strong> the kernel's reference form, never a bare ID string.</li>
<li><strong>Stuck reasons are kebab-case:</strong> <code>action-failed</code>, <code>nobody-to-ask</code>, <code>nothing-fits</code>, <code>error</code>. This corrects the spelling in E-19. E-17's casing rule covers what is recorded or sent to outside systems; codes that only pass between core and the frontend (finding codes and their reasons) keep the frontend's spelling.</li>
<li><strong><code>request.stuck@1</code> and <code>request.unstuck@1</code> carry E-19's stuck state,</strong> <code>{reason, stage}</code>, worked out once per turn, so a request that has nobody to ask is published as stuck like any other.</li>
<li><strong>Nobody-to-ask is decided by a rule the compiler emits</strong> over recorded events (the task's recorded assignees and, for a group, a recorded membership read). Every reader, the notifier, the publisher, the lists and the story, uses that rule's match, so they agree.</li>
<li><strong>An outcome carries <code>lookups</code></strong> in the published definition: for each answer that names an item of a data source, the source, its inputs, and the stored and label fields. The act-time check reads only the definition, never the authored form. <code>WaitCompleted.evidence</code> gains <code>lookups</code>, listing what was looked up and found.</li>
<li><strong>What a condition read</strong> is recorded as every path the expression selects from the request (data, waits, request, actor, input), in the order they appear, each with its value or &quot;absent&quot;. Constants are not recorded: they are in the definition.</li>
<li><strong>The catalogue's shape hash ignores labels,</strong> so correcting a label does not count as a changed shape.</li>
<li><strong>The compiler's stage names and chain shape</strong> are designed in <code>engine/design/compiler.md</code> before anything is published, because stage IDs are recorded for ever.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Changed from earlier decisions</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Directory choices are a data source like any other</strong> (replaces the recorded-list rule in E-14). Wherever a question's choices come from the directory or from a connection, the list is read live when the form is shown and the answer is checked by a lookup when the person acts, on the start form too. A <code>members</code> step and an &quot;is in group&quot; test inside a condition still compile to a recorded read.</li>
<li><strong>A changed shape disables that catalogue entry,</strong> not its whole connection (narrows E-17).</li>
<li><strong>Inbound signatures are the connector's job</strong> (corrects E-17): a real system signs its own way. Standard Webhooks is the platform's own scheme, used by the mock systems and for everything the platform sends.</li>
<li><strong>The spec's composites are left unchanged.</strong> The compiler does not use them (E-19), so the Requester rule lives in the compiler only.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Behaviour</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Retry is offered only for a stuck request. A call that is merely slow is waited for or the request is closed; this avoids starting a second outside job.</li>
<li>A binding that leaves a needed question unmapped is a To do whether or not that question has a &quot;Show when&quot;. The compiler wraps a mapping in its question's &quot;Show when&quot;, so a hidden question arrives empty.</li>
<li>A trigger delivery that fails for an unexpected reason is rolled back and answered &quot;try again&quot;; only final refusals alert the workflow admins.</li>
<li>A paused binding's deliveries are listed and are run again when it is resumed, for up to 30 days.</li>
<li>Overdue-call alerts are grouped per workflow, connection, operation and hour. A job left running with no call waiting for it raises its own alert. A publisher job that keeps failing blocks only its own request's events and raises an alert after 15 minutes.</li>
<li>A callback that arrives before its call is marked accepted is remembered. A callback writes a log row only when it moved the next status question.</li>
<li>Connections are applied from configuration at start-up only; there is no save path in the first build.</li>
<li>Try it treats a draft as unfinished only where a To do stops a request from running. Words and labels never block it.</li>
<li><code>formState</code> takes the catalogue. An internal compile error carries its detail under a <code>debug</code> field, the same exception shape the story uses.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Expression profile <code>cel-1</code></strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The trial passed (36 tests) with <code>@marcbachmann/cel-js</code> 8.0.0 behind the engine's wrapper. The profile lists everything the wrapper changes, not only the three items in E-18.</li>
<li>Map literals may mix value types. A pattern may not use <code>\p</code> or <code>\P</code> (Unicode tables differ between JavaScript engines).</li>
<li>Reading, comparing or testing the erasure marker never fails; a typed operation on it is an expression error. The spec's sentence is narrowed to say so.</li>
<li>A recorded expression error carries the engine's own code, not the library's.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-21-refused-starts-and-one-message-for-stuck-2026-11-15">E-21. Refused starts, and one message for stuck (2026-11-15)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>One stuck state means one built-in message:</strong> <code>request.stuck</code> with its reason. The separate &quot;nobody could be asked&quot; message is dropped. The built-in messages are <code>task.assigned</code>, <code>request.stuck</code>, <code>start.refused</code>, and one per alert reason.</li>
<li><strong>Refused starts are listed</strong> for the workflow admins and platform admins, for 30 days: <code>listRefusedStarts</code>. A refused start can be run again (<code>retryRefusedStart</code>) while the sent body is kept; it uses the live version's bindings at that moment, so the usual fix is to publish and then retry.</li>
<li><strong>The stuck detail for a failed action</strong> carries the operation's failure code and the number of delivery attempts. It is admin-only.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-22-empty-values-what-is-told-and-editing-shared-type-files-2026-11-15">E-22. Empty values, what is told, and editing shared type files (2026-11-15)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>An empty value in a &quot;when&quot; clause</strong> makes the clause not true, except &quot;is empty&quot; and the negative words (is not, does not contain, is not one of, is not in, do not include, does not include), which are true. A message shows an empty value as nothing. Core flags &quot;may be empty&quot; only where an empty value stops or silently drops something: who is asked, a notification's recipient, a directory group, a needed connection input.</li>
<li><strong>&quot;Tell other systems&quot; sends each value as the request holds it:</strong> a choice from a connection as <code>{stored, label}</code>, a person as <code>{type, id}</code>. The built-in events carry IDs, status and reason only, never answers.</li>
<li><strong>After-response actions run before the arrows are checked.</strong> If no arrow fits, they have already run and the request is stuck with <code>nothing-fits</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Type-affecting edits to <code>contract/*.ts</code> are made in one commit, with a line to the frontend owner first,</strong> because the frontend's build type-checks those files from the working tree.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-23-calls-made-after-the-third-design-round-2026-11-15">E-23. Calls made after the third design round (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p>The compiler design, the v2.16 spec edit, the final formats and the documents were written in parallel and disagreed in places. These calls settle the disagreements. Where one changes an earlier decision, it says so.</p>
<p><strong>Nobody-to-ask and the membership read (two designs existed; this is the one kept)</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The design in <code>engine/design/integrations-shapes.md</code> section 5.5 and kernel spec v2.16 is kept: a <code>nobodyToAsk</code> block in the published definition, a membership read opened <strong>beside</strong> the task in the task's own engine stage (<code>&lt;task&gt;__members</code>), and one built-in stuck rule on <code>Stuck</code> for every reason. <code>engine/design/compiler.md</code> moves to it.</li>
<li>Reason: the task is open and visible at once, a slow directory does not delay asking, and Retry re-enters one engine stage and so reads the group again without any extra rule.</li>
<li>Because that read is a call in the tasks step, the step's exit is an explicit &quot;every task is answered&quot; condition, not <code>otherwise</code>. An unanswered directory can therefore never hold up an answered task; leaving the step cancels the read.</li>
<li>A failed membership read counts as nobody to ask. A stuck rule whose expression errors counts as no match for every reader, and the error is logged.</li>
<li>A <code>members</code> step or an &quot;is in group&quot; test inside a condition is a separate recorded read placed just before the step that uses it (not at the start of the section), so it sees a group saved earlier in the same section.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Kept for ever</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>&quot;Once&quot; compiles to an explicit idempotency key,</strong> <code>'once.' + request.id + '.' + &lt;action ID&gt;</code>, not <code>keyScope: request</code>. A stage with a second status is emitted twice, and the kernel's derived key includes the stage, so the two copies would otherwise act twice. Request IDs are limited to 64 characters of <code>[A-Za-z0-9_-]</code>. This corrects E-14.</li>
<li><strong>A published definition carries a <code>types</code> block</strong> (the type of every data path, constant and operation result). <code>decide</code> uses it to read JSON numbers correctly: a number is a double, an integer an int. Without it E-18's rule cannot hold.</li>
<li><strong><code>RequestStarted</code> names its <code>workflow</code></strong> (the spec said &quot;definition&quot;). A failed call's data is <code>{code, message}</code>, and a fault from a failed call copies the code into the fault's parameters.</li>
<li><strong>The profile <code>cel-1</code> gains <code>days(n)</code> and a date conversion,</strong> and its function list is written out and pinned, not left as &quot;whatever the library registers&quot;.</li>
<li><strong>Authored IDs are at most 40 characters,</strong> so every compiled name fits the 64-character limit.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Changed from earlier decisions</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The spec's composites and the demo workflow follow the same rules as compiled workflows</strong> (replaces &quot;composites are left unchanged&quot; in E-20): people and groups are <code>{type, id}</code> in the demo's data, results and cases, and the composites use the <code>nobodyToAsk</code> block and the single stuck rule. Nothing is published, so the composites stay at version 1. What stays true from E-20: the compiler does not use composites.</li>
<li><strong>Retry is offered only where running again can help</strong> (narrows E-19): for <code>action-failed</code> (the action is tried again) and <code>nobody-to-ask</code> (the group is read again and the tasks are asked again). For <code>nothing-fits</code> and <code>error</code> only Close is offered: both would repeat the same result, and after an error the request sits where its turn began, so a retry could repeat an outside action that had already succeeded.</li>
<li><strong>Close is offered for any open request,</strong> stuck or not.</li>
<li><strong>Every fault from a failed call is <code>action-failed</code>,</strong> whatever added the call. Readers decide the reason from the fault's code.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Behaviour</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The lookups made when a person acts (membership, choices) happen before the request is locked, after an unlocked check that the task is still open; the task is checked again under the lock. No outside call is made while a request is locked.</li>
<li>A call that was sent at least once with no clear answer and whose task then closes is not dropped: it is kept, asked about, and raises one alert, because it may have acted outside. Only a call never sent is dropped.</li>
<li>Changes to a workflow's settings and to a binding's paused state are recorded with who and when.</li>
<li>The data model gains the authoring tables (workflows, drafts, the extra columns on published versions and settings) and <code>start_tokens</code>.</li>
<li>The kernel folder may cite <code>integrations.md</code> for blocks that <code>decide</code> never reads; the package README says so.</li>
<li>Within one stage, when two tasks fill the same value, the later one in the document wins, not the later one in time.</li>
<li>Core raises a To do for the constructs the compiler has no rule for (listed in <code>engine/design/compiler.md</code>), including two results of one action saved as the same value.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-24-corrections-after-the-consistency-pass-2026-11-15">E-24. Corrections after the consistency pass (2026-11-15)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Who can answer a task</strong> is the people asked directly plus the recorded members of the groups asked, minus the Requester where the Requester may not answer. Nobody-to-ask means that set is empty. A membership read that fails contributes nobody <strong>from its groups</strong>; a person asked directly still counts. This corrects the wording in E-23, which read as if any failed read made the whole task nobody-to-ask.</li>
<li><strong>&quot;People in [group]&quot; under &quot;Who is asked&quot; is the same as asking the group.</strong> No separate directory read is made for it, so Retry for nobody-to-ask always reads the group again.</li>
<li><strong>In a list comparison (&quot;is one of&quot;, &quot;includes any of&quot;), empty items are ignored.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Removing a value that is not there records nothing.</strong> A person's start therefore records no empty &quot;remove&quot; for the Requester.</li>
<li><strong>The &quot;may have acted outside&quot; alert (<code>call-outcome-unknown</code>) is for actions only.</strong> A read that was sent with no clear answer and whose task then closes is dropped quietly: a read cannot act outside. The alert goes to the workflow admins.</li>
<li><strong>The integrated sample's cases are asserted on what a person or an outside system can see:</strong> inputs, refusals, the story, alerts, messages and published events. The exact list of engine events for each case is produced by the built compiler and engine and reviewed once, then kept as the expected output. The hand-written event lists in the sample are illustrations and are not renumbered by hand.</li>
<li><code>workflow_settings.admins</code> is replaced by <code>stuck_requests_go_to</code>; empty means the authors.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-25-two-checker-rules-from-the-frontends-verifiers-2026-11-16">E-25. Two checker rules from the frontend's verifiers (2026-11-16)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>An arrow that can never be used is a To do</strong> (it was &quot;worth knowing&quot;), raised only where that is provable. It is not raised for an arrow whose &quot;when&quot; is not chosen yet; that arrow already has its own To do.</li>
<li><strong>An empty &quot;when&quot; or &quot;only when&quot; means &quot;not decided&quot;,</strong> never &quot;always true&quot;. Core raises a To do for it.</li>
<li>To apply in <code>contract/core-api.md</code> and in core's checker after the first code wave lands.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-26-calls-made-after-the-first-code-wave-2026-11-15">E-26. Calls made after the first code wave (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p>The first code wave built the kernel, the expression profile, and parse, facts and check, and ran the spec's cases (R1 to R10 and D1 to D12 pass). Its engineers and reviewers reported places where the design was silent or two documents disagreed. These are the calls. Those marked <strong>spec</strong> change the kernel spec (v2.17).</p>
<p>Kernel:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>A stuck flag ends when the request moves (spec).</strong> <code>Faulted{kind: stuck}</code> is cleared by any later turn in which a transition fires, by any admin turn, and by the request closing. The stuck check then runs at the end of that turn as before, so a request that still has nothing open is flagged again. <code>evolve</code> treats exactly the kind <code>stuck</code> as this flag; every other kind stays until an admin clears it. Before this, the flag stayed after the request had moved on.</li>
<li><strong>A wait's opening expressions may not read a wait of the same stage (spec, publish check).</strong> The waits of a stage open in declared order, so a sibling is not there yet.</li>
<li><strong><code>root.initial</code> declares no <code>requires</code> (spec, publish check).</strong></li>
<li><strong>Keys starting with <code>$</code> (spec).</strong> A Set whose value holds such a key faults the turn, unless the key is part of a whole erasure marker, which is a copy of an erased value. A map literal in a published expression may not have such a key (publish check). A call result holding one is a result that does not fit its declared shape.</li>
<li><strong>An expression that gives null is an error (spec).</strong> The engine never writes null.</li>
<li><strong>Order rules the spec left open (spec, one line each):</strong> every ordinary transition, the root's then the stage's, is tried before any <code>otherwise</code>; a close cancels the stage's open waits before the root's; setting a path below a value that is not an object replaces that value; removing below one changes nothing; a closed request keeps the stages it closed in, and a reopen empties them first.</li>
<li><strong>A failed call that arrives while the request is already faulted raises its own fault.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Call results are checked before the turn, by one function in core</strong> that both the server's dispatcher and the in-memory host use. <code>decide</code> trusts its caller for that, as the spec says.</li>
<li><strong>Names for cases the spec gave no code:</strong> refusals <code>unknown-outcome</code> (after <code>wait-not-open</code>), <code>unknown-wait</code>, <code>already-started</code>, <code>not-started</code>, <code>action-not-built</code>, <code>invalid-action</code>, <code>requires-not-met</code>; fault codes <code>set-overlap</code>, <code>requires-not-met</code>, <code>unknown-stage</code> (a publish check makes each unreachable). A clear of a fault with no re-entry and no close in the same turn is refused <code>action-not-built</code> in the first build.</li>
<li><strong>The spec's replay cases are corrected:</strong> R5 writes its action in full; R6 and R7 list their actions.</li>
</ul>
<p>Formats and expressions:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>jsonschema-1</code> refuses a leap second,</strong> as <code>cel-1</code> does. Its failures map to the refusal rules as built: <code>enum</code> to <code>not-a-choice</code>; <code>const</code> and <code>uniqueItems</code> to <code>wrong-kind</code>; an integer beyond 2^53-1 to <code>out-of-range</code>. A <code>type</code> may be a list of types; <code>&quot;null&quot;</code> is never a type; a subschema may be <code>true</code> or <code>false</code>.</li>
<li><strong>A directory object ID</strong> is 1 to 255 characters with no white space and no control character, until a real directory says otherwise.</li>
<li><strong>A wait's data is typed as the merge of its outcomes' shapes;</strong> a field whose type differs between outcomes is untyped.</li>
<li><strong>A timestamp outside the years 0001 to 9999 is an error</strong> wherever it leaves an expression.</li>
<li><strong>The expression module reports an error's key and index as fields,</strong> not only as text, and tells a <code>days()</code> overflow from an integer leaving its range.</li>
<li><strong>A literal <code>\p</code> or <code>\P</code> pattern is refused when the formula is checked,</strong> not only at publish.</li>
</ul>
<p>The package:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>@workflow/core</code> exports the contract's surface,</strong> with the authored-format and catalogue types. <strong><code>@workflow/core/kernel</code> exports the stored formats, <code>decide</code>, <code>evolve</code>, the turn function, the schema validator and the in-memory host.</strong> The two sets share names with different meanings (<code>Status</code>, <code>ValueKind</code>, <code>MessagePart</code>), so one root cannot hold both. The frontend imports only the first.</li>
<li><strong>The turn function is exported on its own</strong> (validate, decide, evolve, stuck check), so the server and the hosts run the same code.</li>
</ul>
<p>The checker and the facts (all in <code>contract/core-api.md</code>):</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>An early arrow</strong> (&quot;Don't wait for the others&quot;) taken while tasks are still open reads the values as they are after the tasks step, before the after-response actions. Any other arrow reads them after those actions.</li>
<li><strong>A date value in a formula reads as a point in time</strong> (midnight UTC), as the compiler has it: <code>{{v_due}} + days(3)</code>, and <code>asDate(...)</code> to save a date. The contract's examples that wrap the chip in <code>date()</code> are corrected.</li>
<li><strong>A choice question whose choices are people in a group gives a person.</strong> The value's kind is <code>person</code>. The authored format's comment says <code>choice</code>; the frontend owner is asked to correct it.</li>
<li><strong>Three new To dos:</strong> <code>group.readInSameStep</code> (a directory step or &quot;is in group&quot; over a group that the same tasks step fills, read by that step's own Show when, &quot;Also only when&quot;, lookup input or early arrow; the compiler has no rule, compiler.md 14.3 item 9); <code>startsWhen.buttonNotOnStart</code> (a binding presses a button that is not the start task's); <code>parse.badFormat</code> (a catalogue reference or a date that is not in its form).</li>
<li><strong><code>clause.pressedOutsideStage</code> also covers an arrow whose &quot;when&quot; names another stage's button.</strong></li>
<li><strong><code>catalogue.unknownField</code> also covers a binding's sent field.</strong></li>
<li><strong><code>requester.mayBeEmpty</code> is not raised for the start task when no arrow leads back to the start.</strong></li>
<li><strong><code>facts.values</code> lists only the values in the registry. <code>facts.arrows</code> judges an arrow as if its stage is reached,</strong> so an arrow out of an unreachable stage is not reported twice.</li>
<li><strong>When a task's own question and its &quot;save which button was pressed&quot; fill the same value, the question's answer is kept.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Template text is empty only when it is the empty string,</strong> as the compiler has it; white space is not empty.</li>
<li><strong><code>choices.list</code> is no longer a &quot;part missing&quot; case:</strong> the format requires it.</li>
<li>The other readings the checker's engineers took where the table was loose are accepted and written into the table: <code>task.askedMayBeEmpty</code> is raised only for a list cell left &quot;(not given)&quot; by a row that can reach the task; <code>expression.kindMismatch</code> also covers a clause's right side and <code>choices.peopleIn</code>; <code>action.failureReadButStops</code> covers any read; <code>start.directoryInCondition</code> covers the people words on a group.</li>
</ul>
<p>Left as built, known limits: the kinds of values filled only by a formula are unknown to the checker until <code>checkFormula</code> feeds the facts; the checker's speed on very large workflows with many tasks per stage and chained send-backs is above the 50 ms target (realistic 60-stage workflows take about 18 ms in Node; not yet measured in a browser).</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-27-calls-made-after-the-second-code-wave-2026-11-16">E-27. Calls made after the second code wave (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>The second code wave built the compiler, the kernel publish check, the formula and form functions, the notification and outbound-event matchers, and the test host with the request view and story. Compiled workflows agreed with an independent reading of the authored format over more than 900 generated runs. These are the calls on what its engineers and reviewers left open. Those marked <strong>spec</strong> change the kernel spec (v2.18).</p>
<p>Kernel and spec:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>A turn that ends in an error fault also clears the stuck flag (spec).</strong> A request is never flagged stuck and faulted at once.</li>
<li><strong>A lookup's inputs may read <code>request</code> (spec),</strong> so &quot;the Requester&quot; and &quot;Started on&quot; work there.</li>
<li><strong>A notification rule on a wait opening sends nothing when that wait is no longer open at the end of the turn (spec).</strong></li>
<li><strong>The publish check's readings are written into the spec (spec, one sentence each):</strong> which paths count as present for a read and for <code>requires</code>; how a stage's transitions cover its waits' outcomes; what breaks a cycle; which forms guard a read of a wait's data; a rule's <code>on.element</code> names an existing element.</li>
<li><strong>A Set holding a <code>$</code> key faults with <code>cel-error</code>, error <code>wrong-kind</code>, detail <code>reserved-key</code>.</strong></li>
<li><strong>An act on a wait the request never opened is refused <code>unknown-wait</code>,</strong> as v2.17 already says; the code follows.</li>
<li><strong><code>wait-not-open</code> on a completed wait says who completed it, also after the request closed.</strong></li>
<li><strong>The spec's cases define <code>faulted</code> once (spec):</strong> false, <code>stuck</code> or <code>error</code>.</li>
<li><strong>A stuck state that changes while the request is faulted publishes and notifies</strong> like any other change of the stuck state. The same stuck state after a turn gives no new story entry, message or event; the contract's sentence that said otherwise is deleted.</li>
<li><strong>The stuck state and the nobody-to-ask rule move into the kernel folder, and a stuck request's stage is reported as the authored stage,</strong> found through the definition's origin map. A hand-written definition with no origin map reports its own stage.</li>
<li><strong>The call-result check in core covers what the definition knows</strong> (the result's shape). That an await gave a job reference and that a failure code is one the operation declares are checked by the server, which has the catalogue.</li>
<li><strong>The kernel publish check takes the catalogue as an optional second argument</strong> for the checks that need it; they are built with the server. A publish problem carries a severity.</li>
<li><strong>Correction to E-26:</strong> in <code>jsonschema-1</code> a boolean subschema is allowed only under <code>additionalProperties</code> and <code>items</code>. A field inside an answer that the schema does not have is <code>wrong-kind</code>; <code>unknown-question</code> is only for an answer to a question the form does not have.</li>
</ul>
<p>Compiler:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Several questions on one form saved as the same value: the last answered one is kept,</strong> and the value is removed only when all of them are empty. This matches what the form shows and the pattern of alternate pages.</li>
<li><strong>References and connection choices written as constants are <code>dyn({...})</code> in compiled expressions, and a person or group schema types its <code>const</code>.</strong> A formula cannot compare a person with a map literal; it compares two chips.</li>
<li><strong><code>has()</code> on a field of a chip compiles to an optional read.</strong></li>
<li><strong>An empty multiple choice is refused by the same compiled check as a choice out of order;</strong> the refusal mapping in core, which the server also uses, reports it as <code>too-short</code>. <code>jsonschema-1</code> gains no keyword.</li>
<li><strong>Output order is by the catalogue's field order and, for told values, by name,</strong> so compiled output does not depend on the key order of a stored draft.</li>
<li><strong>One module owns the form's outcome schemas;</strong> <code>formState</code> and the compiler both use it. The publish check and <code>decide</code> share one expression environment.</li>
<li>The remaining differences between the built compiler and the worked examples in <code>compiler.md</code> are corrected in the document: a stage with no tasks still runs its after-response actions; the Requester chip; parentheses; list-choice text by the column's kind.</li>
</ul>
<p>Contract (<code>contract/core-api.md</code>), all as built:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>sampleValues</code> takes the catalogue; <code>compile</code> takes options (publish or Try it) and returns what is unfinished; <code>story</code> and <code>requestView</code> have signatures, taking the published version (definition, source, catalogue) and the events; a task instance is <code>t&lt;seq&gt;</code> and a call <code>&lt;request&gt;.c&lt;seq&gt;</code>.</li>
<li><code>FormState</code> has <code>invalid</code>, the refusals per answer; a button's refusal may be <code>invalid-data</code>.</li>
<li><code>TestHost.request</code> on an unknown request answers <code>not-found</code>; <code>answerCall</code> on an unknown call answers <code>not-found</code>; a result that does not fit leaves the call pending.</li>
<li>At the root, <code>DirectoryRef</code> and <code>Json</code> are the authored format's and the contract's; the catalogue's are <code>CatalogueDirectoryRef</code> and <code>CatalogueJson</code>.</li>
<li><code>compile</code> stays in the root entry: Try it compiles drafts in the browser.</li>
<li>A formula with a map-literal key starting with <code>$</code> is <code>formula.notInProfile</code>, rule <code>reservedKey</code>.</li>
<li>A stuck request's detail text is technical and may name engine things; it is for the people who look after stuck requests, behind a disclosure.</li>
</ul>
<p>Checker, including seven points from the frontend's verifiers:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>New &quot;worth knowing&quot; <code>action.failureNotRead</code>:</strong> an action carries on after a failure and nothing reads the saved failure values, or none is saved. Located at the action, part <code>ifItFails</code>.</li>
<li><strong><code>requester.mayBeEmpty</code> also lists bindings whose Requester comes from something that may be empty</strong> with no &quot;If empty, use&quot;.</li>
<li><code>clause.pressedOutsideStage</code> on an arrow is located at <code>when.button</code>, and <code>arrow.neverUsed</code> is not raised beside it. <code>requester.mayBeEmpty</code> counts only arrows that can be taken from a reachable stage. A date constant must be a real calendar day in the years 0001 to 9999. A directory ID in a list cell that is not in the ID's form is <code>parse.badFormat</code>. A question whose choices come from a list with no rows is <code>item.partMissing</code> on the list's rows.</li>
<li><code>group.readInSameStep</code> does not cover a question's &quot;people in&quot; group (it names the group and needs no recorded read) or formulas; on the start form, conditions stay with <code>start.directoryInCondition</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Catalogue:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>notifyConnection</code> beside <code>directoryConnection</code>:</strong> the connection that carries Notify. Always present, covered by the catalogue version.</li>
<li>The mock catalogue's words lose engine terms, its samples carry a name beside every ID, and the pretended Jira issue is <code>CHG-101</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Known limits, left: the integrated sample's cases that need the server (inbound events, the dispatcher, callbacks, deliveries, a second version, alerts) are not run yet; <code>diff</code> and <code>upgrade</code> are not built; the root entry is 136 KB gzipped.</p>
