<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-28-small-calls-after-the-fix-wave-2026-11-16">E-28. Small calls after the fix wave (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>The fix wave applied E-27 (spec v2.18, <code>diff</code>, the catalogue changes). What it left open, decided here; the first three change the kernel spec (v2.19).</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>A lookup's inputs do not read <code>request.id</code></strong> (publish check). On the start form no request exists when the choices are listed, so the page and the act would disagree. <code>request.by</code> and <code>request.at</code> are fine: on the start form they are the caller and the time of the call.</li>
<li><strong>A recipient expression that gives nothing, or not a list, is a rule error:</strong> nothing is sent and the workflow's admins get the rule-error alert, as for any other failing rule.</li>
<li><strong>The spec's integrations document carries <code>notifyConnection</code>, the catalogue version formula that covers it, and the directory's optional group name.</strong> <code>notifyConnection</code> must name a configured connection, or start-up fails. Demo case D7's act on a wait the request never opened expects <code>unknown-wait</code>.</li>
<li><strong><code>wait-not-open</code> carries</strong> <code>{state: &quot;completed&quot;, by, outcome}</code>, <code>{state: &quot;requestClosed&quot;}</code>, or <code>{state: &quot;cancelled&quot; | &quot;skipped&quot;}</code>. An act on a call wait is <code>unknown-wait</code>.</li>
<li><strong>The authored stage of an engine stage</strong> is found from the origin map by the compiler's conventions: a stage origin with part <code>tasks</code> or <code>arrows</code> names the authored stage; from any other step, follow the transitions to the first such stage. For Try it's &quot;unfinished&quot; step, whose origin is an arrow, it is the stage that arrow leaves.</li>
<li><strong><code>diff</code> as built:</strong> every added or removed item is listed on its own; a moved item is located by its parent and the field that holds it; a new order of items under one parent is one change on the parent; before and after are given only for small parts (text, numbers, yes/no, and lists of them or of IDs); an item whose ID changed is a removal and an addition; null and absent are the same. It does not mark which changes can affect running requests; the Publish dialog does not need that in the first build.</li>
<li><strong>A task with no &quot;Who is asked&quot; does not stop Try it:</strong> the request runs to that task and is stuck there with nobody to ask. A missing choices or a list with no rows does not stop it either; the tester sees a question nobody can answer.</li>
<li><strong><code>not-found</code> names what was not found:</strong> <code>task</code>, <code>request</code> or <code>call</code>.</li>
<li><strong>A multiple choice whose choices come from a formula</strong> has the kind multiple choice with items of the formula's item kind; where the items have no value kind, the value has no kind and only the choice check guards the answer.</li>
<li><strong><code>has()</code> on a chip</strong> works where the chip's value has fields (a person, a group, a connection choice, a field group) and is refused on text.</li>
<li><strong>The mock directory's group item gains an optional name.</strong> This changed that entry's shape under its ID; harmless here because nothing is deployed, and the rule that a changed shape disables an entry stays.</li>
<li>The long generated tests get a longer time limit; they are slow only when several suites run at once.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-29-a-saved-failure-code-is-a-choice-2026-11-16">E-29. A saved failure code is a choice (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>Asked by the frontend owner: an action's &quot;what went wrong&quot; value held the bare failure code, so a message to a person would have shown <code>tests-failed</code>.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The value an action saves its failure code as has the kind choice.</strong> Its choices are the operation's failure codes from the catalogue: the value is the code, the label is the catalogue's label. Failure codes are part of an entry's shape and cannot change under one entry ID; labels can, and publish writes the labels it saw into the definition, as for typed-in choices.</li>
<li><strong>The request holds the code.</strong> A &quot;when&quot; compares by code. A message, and a text template sent to another system, show the label. &quot;Tell other systems&quot; sends the code.</li>
<li><strong>Two actions saving their failure code as one value:</strong> the choices are the union; where one code has two labels, the first action in document order gives it.</li>
<li><strong>The authored format gains the constant <code>{ failureCode }</code></strong> (the frontend's file), compared with such a value the way a button constant is compared with &quot;Button pressed&quot;. A failure-code constant that is not one of the value's codes, or is used against another value, gets the same finding as a button constant naming another task's button. No new finding code.</li>
<li><strong>Also fixed with it:</strong> a Notify whose &quot;To&quot; is a formula giving people passed the checker but could not be compiled.</li>
<li>To be built from the frontend's commit that adds the constant.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-30-the-servers-plumbing-2026-11-16">E-30. The server's plumbing (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>Cheap choices, each easy to change later, made so the server can be built. None of them is visible to an author or kept in history.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Database access is plain SQL behind one small interface</strong> (query, transaction), with two adapters: PGlite for tests and the dev host, node-postgres for a real Postgres. No ORM. The schema is numbered SQL files applied in order by a small runner.</li>
<li><strong>Jobs are a table of the engine's own,</strong> written in the turn's transaction and taken by polling workers with <code>FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED</code>. No queue library in the first build: the two candidates need a real Postgres, and the dev host runs on PGlite. This replaces &quot;Graphile Worker or pg-boss; not chosen&quot;.</li>
<li><strong>HTTP handlers are functions from a request to a response</strong> (Hono, pinned), so tests and the dev host call them without a socket.</li>
<li><strong>Who is calling</strong> comes from one adapter. The dev host reads a development-only header; the real sign-in is the existing application's and is not known yet.</li>
<li><strong>Folders of <code>@workflow/server</code>:</strong> <code>store</code> (schema, events, the tables read from them), <code>turn</code> (the turn transaction around core's turn function), <code>api</code> (authoring and runtime), <code>workers</code> (dispatcher, reconciler, notifier, publisher), <code>connectors</code>, <code>hooks</code>, <code>mock</code> (the mock systems), <code>dev-host</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Order of building:</strong> the store and the turn transaction; the two APIs with every outside system behind the connector interface; then the workers, hooks, mock systems and dev host; then the integrated sample's server cases.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-31-calls-after-the-servers-first-wave-2026-11-16">E-31. Calls after the server's first wave (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>The store, the turn transaction and the two APIs are built on PGlite and reviewed. What that wave left open:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Pausing and resuming a &quot;Starts when&quot; belongs to the runtime API only.</strong> It was built twice; the copy in the authoring API is deleted. On a resume, &quot;gone&quot; counts the deliveries held since that binding's last pause that are older than 30 days, so an old delivery is counted once.</li>
<li><strong>Rebuilding a request's read tables takes the same lock as a turn,</strong> in one transaction, and updates the rows in place.</li>
<li><strong>An unknown path or method answers <code>not-found</code></strong> (<code>what: &quot;path&quot;</code>) in the usual error body, with the engine's headers.</li>
<li><strong>The settings log and the pause log refuse updates and deletes,</strong> like the events.</li>
<li><strong>The runtime API serves only versions published through the authoring API.</strong> A hand-written definition has no authored source; it is for the kernel's tests.</li>
<li><strong>Readers use the current catalogue.</strong> A version records which catalogue version it was compiled against, for diagnosis only.</li>
<li><strong>The request list reads the authored stage and the listed stuck state from the read table,</strong> which gains those two columns, instead of folding every request's events.</li>
<li><strong>Core exports what the server had to copy:</strong> the refusal mapping, a viewer's button states (also for the start form), a lookup's inputs, &quot;is this wait open&quot;, the blank workflow, and <code>upgrade</code> (which changes nothing while there is one format).</li>
<li><strong>An admin action's refusals come in the documented order:</strong> not an admin and reason missing first, then stale, then the rest (closed, not stuck, not retryable).</li>
<li><strong>A request body may be 64 KiB larger than the largest draft,</strong> so the draft's own size refusal is the one a client sees.</li>
<li>As built and accepted: a refused attempt's log row carries the refusals in its input; publish answers <code>has-todo</code> with the findings as the compiler gives them; a turn that appends nothing enqueues no publisher job; the turn's time is the server's clock, never earlier than the request's previous event; request IDs are random UUIDs and readable numbers start at 1 until the existing application's highest number is known.</li>
<li><strong>To carry into the design package's data model at its next version:</strong> the jobs table, the catalogue-version column, the append-only triggers, and the wording on what a read table may read (its own request's version).</li>
<li><strong>Not run yet:</strong> the six concurrency tests that need a real Postgres. No Docker daemon was running.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-32-the-frontends-list-after-it-swapped-to-core-2026-11-16">E-32. The frontend's list after it swapped to core (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>The frontend now runs on core: its own checker, interpreter, story and outbox are deleted. It sent one list of what it met. Decided:</p>
<p>Built now, with E-29:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The test host takes a time for each call,</strong> never earlier than the request's previous event. Before, every turn was stamped one second after the last.</li>
<li><strong><code>arrow.neverUsed</code> names every earlier arrow that together covers the arrow</strong> (<code>covering</code>), not only a single one.</li>
<li><strong>A typed-in choice question with no choices is a &quot;part missing&quot; To do,</strong> like a list with no rows.</li>
<li><strong>Try it's &quot;unfinished&quot; stop sends no stuck message.</strong> It is not a stuck reason a live request can have.</li>
<li><strong>The compiler makes no membership read for a task that can ask no group</strong> (who is asked is only people).</li>
<li><strong>A catalogue field can say it is the web address of a sibling field</strong> (<code>addressOf</code>), so &quot;CHG-101&quot; can be shown as a link without guessing. Display only; not part of the entry's shape.</li>
<li><strong>The &quot;ended&quot; event carries the ending stage,</strong> as the integrations document says. The &quot;why&quot; of an arrow includes a list-cell read. <code>diff</code> names the deepest reported part (<code>saveFailureAs.failed</code>). The <code>Draft</code> type is in core. Core compiles with unused locals and parameters refused.</li>
</ul>
<p>Accepted, built after the usage reset:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>A person who may not answer a task is not told about it and does not see it in &quot;My tasks&quot;</strong> (the Requester, where the Requester can't answer their own request), also when they are in a group that is asked. The rule that decides nobody-to-ask decides this too.</li>
<li><strong>A button whose arrows all carry &quot;+ only when&quot; on a value is a To do</strong> (<code>stage.buttonHasNowhereToGo</code>), unless the conditions are plainly complementary or the stage has &quot;In all other cases&quot;. Today the request would be stuck with nothing that fits.</li>
<li><strong>A formula that compares a choice with a text that is none of its choices is a finding,</strong> and a choice is written in a formula as a chip the editor inserts. The chip's form is to be designed.</li>
<li><strong>A question's &quot;Show when&quot; reads only earlier questions of its form;</strong> <code>valuesInScope</code> will say so. To be confirmed against what the compiler does.</li>
<li><strong>A clause whose constant names a choice, a button or a failure code that its value can never hold is a To do.</strong> No finding exists for it today, also not for a button constant naming another task's button, which E-29 assumed; the clause is simply never true. It needs a new finding code and words.</li>
<li><strong><code>buttonStates</code> takes a time the way the test host does:</strong> any RFC 3339 time, and a malformed one is refused, not thrown. Today it throws unless the time has six fractional digits.</li>
<li><strong>To carry into the design package at its next version,</strong> with the data-model points of E-31: the &quot;ended&quot; event's stage in the integrations document.</li>
</ul>
<p>Not done, because the server's dev host replaces the need: events in and out of the test host, a host on a published version, request IDs chosen by the caller, changing who looks after stuck requests on a running host, and the Try it-only parts of the view. Switching a question's choices from the directory to a list gives several changes in <code>diff</code>, one per part; that is intended.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-33-paring-the-design-down-2026-11-16">E-33. Paring the design down (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>A review for overengineering (five critics, each answered by a defender, and two independent baselines) found the core sound and the edges about two to three times heavier than two engineers can keep. <strong>Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16:</strong> pare the reserved kernel concepts and the integrations down; keep an example of each kind of integration shown working, not fully implemented; reserve the rest in documents. The details below are the engine owner's, pending review. This entry replaces the order of building in E-30 and the &quot;accepted, built after the reset&quot; list of E-32 where they differ.</p>
<p>The rule from now on: <strong>a stored shape is reserved only when adding it later would change the meaning or the form of something already written.</strong> An optional field, a new event type, a new action or a new table is added in the release that builds it.</p>
<p>Kernel (kernel spec v2.20):</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Removed from the spec's rules, the stored formats, the code and the cases,</strong> and listed in the reserved page: <code>foreach</code> waits; root waits and root transitions; child requests; trigger kinds other than an outside event; the break-glass field; the admin actions skip, set data, disable a transition, reopen and jump to another stage, with the reopened event; <code>requires</code> and waived; composites; <code>keyScope: request</code>; the erasure marker and every reader's tolerance of it (the ban on keys starting with <code>$</code> stays, one line).</li>
<li><strong>Kept as they are, because they are written today or fix an ID:</strong> the event envelope; element and wait-instance IDs with their activation; the active stages as a set; typed <code>by</code>; patch-based data sets; open enums; an admin turn as a list of actions, now with two: retry (clear the fault and re-enter the stage) and close.</li>
<li><strong>Stuck is worked out, not recorded.</strong> No stuck event. A request is stuck with nothing that fits when it is open, has no error fault, and has no open obligation and no open call: one function of the state. A fault is only ever an error. A rule on &quot;stuck&quot; still means the stuck state after the turn differs from before it.</li>
<li><strong>A derived idempotency key is readable text</strong> made of the request and the wait instance; the hand-written SHA-256 goes. An outbound event's ID is the request, the event's number and the rule.</li>
<li><strong>The demo definition is rewritten without the removed constructs;</strong> its cases change only where an ID or key changes.</li>
<li><strong>Deliberately kept:</strong> event sourcing; the two formats and the compiler; the reads recorded on a fired transition (the story's &quot;why&quot; uses them); nobody-to-ask; the expression profile; the schema validator; the publish check, less the rules for what is removed.</li>
</ul>
<p>Integrations, each door shown working in its thinnest form:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Start by an outside event:</strong> one endpoint per connection, the binding's mapping, a synchronous answer. Every event received is one row of one table, accepted with its request or refused with its code; the same event twice starts nothing. A paused binding refuses events; it does not hold them. An event refused because of a pause is a refused start like any other, with the reason <code>paused</code>: the sender is answered at once, per workflow, in the usual way for a refused start and is not expected to send again; the event is listed with the other refused starts and &quot;run again&quot; starts its request once the binding is resumed (while it is still paused, &quot;run again&quot; is refused with <code>paused</code> again). So a pause loses nothing a person cannot recover. The refused-starts list and &quot;run again&quot; read that table. No signing-key rotation, no held deliveries.</li>
<li><strong>Calls:</strong> one job per call. Sent with the recorded key; an answer becomes the result turn; no answer means the job runs again later with the same key. A &quot;wait for&quot; call is answered &quot;accepted&quot; with a job reference, and the same job asks for its status every poll interval. No callback endpoint, no tokens, no separate reconciler, no call log table.</li>
<li><strong>Notifications:</strong> one job per turn that could match a rule, sent through the connection that carries Notify. A crash can send a message twice. A person who may not answer a task is not told about it.</li>
<li><strong>Outbound events:</strong> one job per turn. Each event is posted, in the request's order, to every subscriber address in the configuration, at least once. No positions, no subscriptions or deliveries tables, no feed.</li>
<li><strong>The catalogue and the connections come from configuration at start-up</strong> and live in memory. No tables for connections, secrets or catalogue entries, and no shape-hash registry: a snapshot test fails the build when an entry's shape changes under its ID. The catalogue version stays.</li>
<li><strong>Alerts:</strong> the stuck message only. Rule errors and platform problems are structured log lines.</li>
<li><strong>Tables, from 26 to about 11:</strong> events, definitions, workflows, drafts, workflow settings, requests, open waits, pending calls, jobs, the attempts log and the inbound log. A start's client token is a column on the request. Nothing is deployed, so the schema files are edited in place.</li>
<li><strong>Seven mock systems, one per kind of example, in memory,</strong> each with at most two switches (fail the next call; be down). No mock HTTP servers and no control API beyond the development calls the runtime contract already has. Added on 2026-11-16 at the frontend's request: a small development-only control surface on the dev host (the switches, what each mock received, making the helpdesk send), so a failed action, Retry and what was really sent can be shown from the browser.</li>
<li><strong>The dev host is the server itself</strong> on PGlite with the mock connectors, a seeded directory and the development sign-in, started by one command and serving both APIs on one port.</li>
<li><strong>The HTTP contract's shapes do not change for the frontend.</strong> Where behaviour is thinner (a resume re-runs nothing; the paused-deliveries list is empty), the contract says so.</li>
</ul>
<p>Documents and process:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The full designs of what is no longer built are archived, not lost:</strong> <code>workflow-platform/research/later/</code>, with one page, <code>workflow-platform/research/reserved-for-later.md</code>, that lists each reserved item, how it would be added, and which kept convention makes that cheap.</li>
<li>The spec copy in this repo is made by a script, and a test fails when it is stale. The process rules are otherwise unchanged in this round.</li>
<li><strong>On hold:</strong> the three new checks accepted in E-32 (a button whose arrows all carry a condition; a formula comparing a choice with text; a constant a value can never hold) and the &quot;Show when reads only earlier questions&quot; rule. They add checker weight; they come back only if a real workflow needs them.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-15-core-functions-the-frontend-asked-for">E-15. Core functions the frontend asked for</h2>
<p>Accepted: <code>story</code> (a request's history as codes with authored locations, same shape from the runtime API), <code>formState</code> (which questions show, which buttons are available and what they still need, with or without a request), <code>evaluate</code> for any authored expression (returns &quot;needs these lookups&quot; where the directory is involved; core stays pure), <code>facts</code> (per stage, arrow and value, including which arrows send back), and a test host that can start from a trigger binding. <code>decide</code> returns a trace beside its events for &quot;why did it go there&quot;; the trace is not recorded.</p>
<p>Order of delivery: parse; check and facts; formState, evaluate, checkFormula; compile; test host and story; diff.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-engine--e-13-two-sample-workflows">E-13. Two sample workflows</h2>
<ol>
<li><code>change-request-demo</code>, as specified, with faked Jira, directory and notifier. This is the first joint milestone.</li>
<li>An integrated variant that goes through every door in E-9 with the mock systems in E-12. This is what the integration diagrams use as their running example.</li>
</ol>
</section>
<section class="doc" data-file="11-decisions-frontend.md"><h1 id="doc-11-decisions-frontend">Decisions: frontend owner</h1>
<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Frontend owner session. Every entry was decided by the frontend owner under the product owner's delegation of 2026-11-15 and is <strong>pending the product owner's review</strong>. Each says what was decided and why in a few lines; detail lives in the document it points to. The frontend's build decisions F1 to F10 are in <code>08-frontend-design.md</code> and are not repeated here.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-1-what-the-design-set-must-convey-comes-first-2026-11-15">U-1. What the design set must convey comes first (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p><code>00-doc-plan.md</code>: six messages, twelve documents with an owner each, and the diagrams. A document or diagram that lands none of the six messages is cut. Agreed with the Engine owner, who added the set-up and run-time views per door, a ledger, and four diagrams.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-2-the-contract-has-four-parts">U-2. The contract has four parts</h2>
<p>A. the authored workflow format; B. the authoring API; C. the runtime API; D. the catalogue of connections. The frontend drafts A from the editor model; the engine owns B, C and D and the compiler from A to a published definition. Two rules: the engine reports in codes with a location and parameters, and the frontend chooses every word a person reads; locations are always in the authored format.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-3-the-authored-format-speaks-the-editors-language">U-3. The authored format speaks the editor's language</h2>
<p>Field names are the words on screen (stage, task, button, arrow, value, action, list). Everything addressable has a stable ID separate from its name, so a rename changes one place. A draft may be incomplete; completeness is the check's job, not the format's. Reason: one vocabulary from screen to saved document keeps the word map (document 4) one-to-one, and an author is always shown their own workflow.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-4-the-frontend-is-built-against-the-engines-shared-core-behind-one-interface">U-4. The frontend is built against the engine's shared core, behind one interface</h2>
<p>The engine owner offered one pure package (compile, check, values in scope, formula check, the kernel, an in-memory host for Try it) that runs in the browser (their E-3, E-4). The frontend calls it through one async interface and uses a small stand-in until it arrives. Reason: instant checks, and a Try it that behaves exactly as the engine will.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-5-everything-that-happens-lives-in-a-stage-an-arrow-carries-only-a-condition-and-a-destination">U-5. Everything that happens lives in a stage; an arrow carries only a condition and a destination</h2>
<p>&quot;Save a value&quot;, &quot;Notify&quot; and &quot;Tell other systems&quot; are actions in a stage's two action sections, each with an optional &quot;only when&quot;. The engine places them where they belong when it compiles. Reason: the fixed stage anatomy was the most stable result of the mockup rounds; putting effects on arrows would give authors a second place to look.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-6-how-connections-appear-to-an-author">U-6. How connections appear to an author</h2>
<ul>
<li>A <strong>connection</strong> is another system the platform is linked to. It is set up by an administrator outside the editor; authors see a read-only Connections list.</li>
<li>What a connection offers is shown in four sorts, in the author's words: <strong>gives data</strong> (&quot;Choices from&quot; on a question; a &quot;Look up&quot; action), <strong>does something</strong> (an action), <strong>does something and waits</strong> (a &quot;Wait for&quot; action), <strong>can start a request</strong> (&quot;Starts when&quot;).</li>
<li><strong>&quot;Tell other systems&quot;</strong> is an action that announces something happened. Listening systems are always told when a request starts, changes status, gets stuck or ends.</li>
<li>The words connector, integration, API, webhook, trigger, event, payload never appear on screen.</li>
<li>The editor hard-codes no system: menus, the Connections page and &quot;Starts when&quot; are filled from the catalogue (the engine's E-10).</li>
</ul>
<p>Reason: the product owner named upstream and downstream connections as the unclear part. Four sorts answer &quot;what can I use this system for&quot; without teaching the engine's seven doors.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-7-mockup-first-then-build">U-7. Mockup first, then build</h2>
<p>New author-facing design (connections) is drawn as a mockup page in <code>workflow/mockups</code> and written into <code>workflow/spec/editor-model.md</code> before it is built, the same order as the rest of the editor. The mockups stay the UX reference.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-8-nodejs-was-installed-on-this-machine">U-8. Node.js was installed on this machine</h2>
<p>Node LTS 26.13.1 through scoop, at user level (<code>scoop uninstall nodejs-lts</code> removes it). The machine had no JavaScript runtime and both sessions need one.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-9-scope-the-frontend-builds">U-9. Scope the frontend builds</h2>
<p>The editor model of 2026-11-14 plus connections (U-6). The five 2026-11-13 decisions it overturned are still pending the product owner's review; nothing in the build makes any of them expensive to reverse except the interactive diagram.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-10-what-the-engine-reports-the-editor-says-in-its-own-words-2026-11-15">U-10. What the engine reports, the editor says in its own words (2026-11-15)</h2>
<p>Every finding, refusal, stuck reason and notification arrives as a code with a location and parameters. The editor holds the words (<code>frontend/src/words</code>, and <code>contract/words/notifications.json</code> for messages the engine sends). Reason: one voice for the author, and a wording change never needs an engine change.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-11-one-stuck-state-and-what-an-admin-can-do-about-it">U-11. One stuck state, and what an admin can do about it</h2>
<p>A request is &quot;stuck&quot; for one of four reasons. &quot;Retry&quot; is offered only when an action failed or there was nobody to ask; &quot;Close&quot; is offered always. Refused starts (another system tried to start a request and it was refused) are a second section of the Stuck requests page, each with &quot;Run again&quot; for 30 days. Reason: Retry on a request where no arrow fits would do the same thing again; a refused start is the same kind of &quot;something needs a person&quot; and should not need a second page.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-12-pause-and-resume-sit-on-the-starts-when-card-of-the-live-version">U-12. Pause and Resume sit on the &quot;Starts when&quot; card of the live version</h2>
<p>Pausing stops another system from starting requests of this workflow; what arrives meanwhile is kept and listed. It is a switch on what is live, not part of the draft, so it is not published and not undone by Undo.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-13-small-rules-of-the-main-screen">U-13. Small rules of the main screen</h2>
<ul>
<li>The stage panel is 480px wide and can be dragged between 400 and 640.</li>
<li>A new blank stage arrives with one empty task, because a stage with nothing to do is never what the author wants next.</li>
<li>&quot;Worth knowing (n)&quot; shows in the top bar only when n is above zero.</li>
<li>A draft equal to the live version shows the badge &quot;Published&quot; and &quot;Version n is live&quot;; &quot;Publish&quot; is greyed with the reason in its tooltip.</li>
<li>A new ending's status is named after the ending, in a neutral colour.</li>
<li>At 1440 wide the top bar is one row: the full name (up to 28 characters), the word &quot;Glossary&quot;, and the save state always visible.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-14-if-it-fails-carry-on-asks-two-optional-things">U-14. &quot;If it fails: Carry on&quot; asks two optional things</h2>
<p>Whether it failed (a Yes/No value) and what went wrong (a text value), each saved only if the author names a value. They match the two things the engine can record. &quot;If the stage starts again&quot; is shown only when the connection gives no default for it. Reason: most authors never need either; the two rows appear exactly where the choice exists.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-15-the-editor-does-not-offer-what-the-engine-cannot-run">U-15. The editor does not offer what the engine cannot run</h2>
<p>The condition builder leaves out directory steps and &quot;is in [group]&quot; on the start form; the form editor does not offer multiple-choice or group questions with choices from a connection or the directory, nor typed-in choices on a person question. A document that holds one anyway (imported, or made before the rule) gets a To do in plain words. Reason: a To do the author could never have avoided reads as the editor's mistake.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-16-an-empty-when-is-not-decided-and-an-arrow-that-can-never-be-used-is-a-to-do">U-16. An empty &quot;when&quot; is &quot;not decided&quot;, and an arrow that can never be used is a To do</h2>
<p>Asked of the engine owner and accepted (their E-25). Try it stops at a &quot;when&quot; that is not decided and says so. Reason: an empty condition silently meaning &quot;always&quot; hid unfinished work; an unusable arrow is a mistake in the workflow, not a tip.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-17-development-only-controls">U-17. Development-only controls</h2>
<p>Two controls exist only in a development build and are marked as such: a person switcher (to act as another person on request pages), and &quot;Pretend <connection> sent this now&quot; on the Starts-when card, which sends the connection's sample so a request can be watched starting from outside. Reason: the product owner asked to see upstream connections working before any real system is linked. Neither ships.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-18-the-task-page-makes-two-calls">U-18. The task page makes two calls</h2>
<p>It reads the task, then the published form it belongs to. Kept as two calls: the form is the same for every task of that version and is cached, the task is not.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-19-the-slow-system-notice-stays-on-a-look-up-and-a-wait-for">U-19. The slow-system notice stays on a Look up and a Wait for</h2>
<p>A verifier read the editor model's &quot;no clock in the first version&quot; as forbidding &quot;If Deploy pipeline has not reported back after 30 minutes, ... is told; the request is not stuck.&quot; Ruling: it stays, with its time from the connection, because it is true and it is the one thing an author most needs to know about a slow system. &quot;No clock&quot; is about deadlines an author sets. The verb is &quot;is told&quot;, never &quot;is alerted&quot;.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-20-the-form-editor-keeps-the-editors-top-bar">U-20. The form editor keeps the editor's top bar</h2>
<p>The mockup of the form editor has one bar; the build has the editor's top bar and the form's own bar under it. Ruling: keep both, so Undo, To do, Try it and the save state stay in reach while editing a form. The form's bar no longer repeats the trail: it reads &quot;Back to diagram&quot;, &quot;Form for: <stage>&quot;, who fills it in, &quot;Switch form&quot;, Preview, Done.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-21-in-words-only-stage-names-are-links">U-21. In words: only stage names are links</h2>
<p>A sentence is plain text; a stage's name opens that stage on the diagram. Reason: a sentence cut into several links gave keyboard and screen-reader users links named &quot;.&quot; and &quot;The&quot;.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-22-one-sentence-each-kept-in-the-model">U-22. One sentence each, kept in the model</h2>
<p>Who is told about a stuck request, what happens when another system fails or cannot be reached, a request's title, the name of a &quot;Starts when&quot;, and a stored value put into words each come from one function in the model, used by the editor, Try it and the live pages. Reason: the verifiers found the same fact worded two or three ways, once falsely (In words said an unreachable system makes a request stuck; it does not).</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-23-the-frontend-has-no-engine-of-its-own-2026-11-16">U-23. The frontend has no engine of its own (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>The stand-in's checker, interpreter, story and outbox were deleted once the engine owner's core package could be linked. The editor, Try it and the live pages now ask the engine's own code for every answer; only <code>src/services</code> may import it. What is left of the stand-in plays the server (drafts, versions, lists, who is signed in) and pretends the other systems, until the engine's dev host exists. A finding or change kind the engine adds without words in the frontend fails the frontend's build. Reason: two implementations of the rules would drift, and Try it must behave exactly as the engine will (U-4).</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-24-what-went-wrong-is-a-choice-not-a-code">U-24. What went wrong is a choice, not a code</h2>
<p>The value an action saves as &quot;what went wrong&quot; is a choice among the failures the connection says it can report. People read the connection's words for it (&quot;The tests failed&quot;) in messages, on the request page and in a &quot;when&quot;; other systems are sent the code. Asked of the engine owner and accepted (their E-29), with a new constant in the workflow format. Reason: a verifier found a code about to be put into messages to people.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-25-asks-of-the-engine-after-driving-the-editor-on-it">U-25. Asks of the engine after driving the editor on it</h2>
<p>Twenty-two items went to the engine owner as one list (their E-32). Accepted and built: a time on each move of a test request, the arrows that together make another arrow unusable, a To do for a choice question with no choices, where a request ended in what other systems are told. Accepted for after the usage reset: a person who may not answer a task is not told about it; a To do for a button that goes nowhere in some cases; a readable way to write a choice in a formula; a &quot;Show when&quot; reads only the questions above it. Not built, by agreement: running live requests on the test host, because the engine's dev host replaces it.</p>
<h2 id="11-decisions-frontend--u-26-a-paused-starts-when-refuses-and-the-refusal-can-be-run-again-2026-11-16">U-26. A paused &quot;Starts when&quot; refuses, and the refusal can be run again (2026-11-16)</h2>
<p>The engine's paring round (their E-33) no longer keeps what another system sends while a &quot;Starts when&quot; is paused. Asked of the engine owner and accepted: such a start is listed under &quot;Starts that were refused&quot; with the reason &quot;it was paused&quot; and &quot;Run again&quot;, like any other refused start, so a pause loses nothing a person cannot recover. The other system is told the start was refused; nothing is sent again by itself. This replaces U-12's &quot;what arrives meanwhile is kept and listed&quot;. The screens change when the frontend moves onto the engine's dev host; until then the stand-in still keeps deliveries.</p>
</section>

<p class="doc-meta doc-owner">Owner: Frontend owner. Agreed with the Engine owner on 2026-11-15, with their additions (two views per door and a ledger in document 5; diagrams D4b, D7b, D10a, D10b). This is the table of contents of <code>docs/</code>.</p>
<h2 id="00-doc-plan--1-who-reads-this-and-what-they-need">1. Who reads this, and what they need</h2>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Reader</th>
<th>What they need to come away with</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Product owner and leadership</td>
<td>The parts of the platform, who owns each, what is built first, and how customers' workflows relate to the platform we build.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Engineers who build and maintain it</td>
<td>Boundaries, contracts, data flow, lifecycles, failure handling. Enough to change one part without reading the others.</td>
</tr>

</tr>

<td>The interface between frontend and engine, exact enough to build against separately.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><h2 id="00-doc-plan--2-the-six-things-the-set-must-make-clear">2. The six things the set must make clear</h2>
<p>Every document and diagram exists to land one of these. If it lands none, it is cut.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>We build a platform; customers build workflows.</strong> The platform is an authoring tool, an engine, and a set of doors to other systems. &quot;Change request&quot; is an example and never appears in the platform's code.</li>
<li><strong>A workflow exists in three forms.</strong> What the author edits (a draft), what the engine runs (a published, immutable version), and what happened (a request's history). One pipeline connects them: edit, check, publish, run, record, show.</li>
<li><strong>Everything crosses the platform's edge through a small number of doors.</strong> Upstream and downstream, data and control (triggers and events). Each door has a rule for what is recorded, what is retried, and what happens when it fails.</li>
<li><strong>The editor's words map one-to-one onto the engine's concepts.</strong> Stage, task, button, arrow, value, action, To do, stuck, Try it: each has exactly one engine counterpart and one field in the contract.</li>
<li><strong>The frontend and the engine meet at one contract.</strong> The authored workflow format, the authoring API, the runtime API, and the catalogue of connections.</li>
<li><strong>What is in the first build, what is held as a shape, and what is later.</strong></li>
</ol>

</table></div><h2 id="00-doc-plan--5-the-contract-in-four-parts">5. The contract, in four parts</h2>
<p>This is the interface the two sessions build against. It is the main thing to agree first.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead>
<tr>
<th>Part</th>
<th>What it is</th>
<th>Proposed pen</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>A. Authored workflow format</td>
<td>The draft as data, in the editor's terms: stages and their kinds, tasks, who is asked, forms, buttons, actions, arrows and their conditions, values, lists, the sample request, diagram positions. It is compiled to a published definition.</td>
<td>Frontend drafts from the editor model (<code>workflow/spec/editor-model.md</code>); Engine makes it compilable and owns the compiler</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>B. Authoring API</td>
<td>Drafts, check (To do and Worth knowing as codes with locations), values in scope at a point (kind, where filled, may be empty), formula check and sample result, Try it, publish, versions and what changed.</td>
<td>Engine; Frontend states what each screen needs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>C. Runtime API</td>
<td>Start a request, act on a task, admin retry and close; reads for lists, the request page, action items and history.</td>
<td>Engine</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>D. Catalogue</td>
<td>The connections available to an author: actions, data sources, things that can start or move a request, events sent out; each with versioned input and output shapes and a sample. Also the directory search.</td>
<td>Engine</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Two rules proposed for the contract:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>The engine reports in codes, the frontend chooses the words.</strong> A check result is a code, a location in the authored format, and parameters. The editor turns it into &quot;To do&quot; text. Engine terms never reach the screen.</li>
<li><strong>Locations are in the authored format, never in the compiled definition.</strong> An author is always shown their own workflow.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="00-doc-plan--6-form">6. Form</h2>
<ul>
<li>Sources are Markdown with Mermaid diagrams, one file per document, in <code>docs/</code>. Each file's header names its owner.</li>
<li>A small script builds them into one self-contained page for reading.</li>
<li>A diagram that needs a screenshot uses the mockups.</li>
</ul>
</section>

<script>// Optional behaviour. The page reads fine without it.
(function () {
  // 1. Highlight the current document and section in the contents.
  document.querySelector('.toc').classList.add('js');
  var links = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.toc a[href^="#"]'));
  var byId = {};
  links.forEach(function (a) { byId[a.getAttribute('href').slice(1)] = a; });
  var heads = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('main h1[id], main h2[id], #list-of-diagrams'))
    .filter(function (h) { return byId[h.id]; });
  var active = [];
  function update() {
    var y = window.scrollY + 80, curDoc = null, curSec = null;
    for (var i = 0; i < heads.length; i++) {
      var h = heads[i];
      if (h.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY > y) break;
      if (h.tagName === 'H2') curSec = h; else { curDoc = h; curSec = null; }
    }
    active.forEach(function (a) { a.classList.remove('active'); });
    active = [];
    var openDoc = curDoc && byId[curDoc.id] ? byId[curDoc.id].parentNode : null;
    document.querySelectorAll('.toc-doc.open').forEach(function (li) { if (li !== openDoc) li.classList.remove('open'); });
    if (openDoc) openDoc.classList.add('open');
    [curDoc, curSec].forEach(function (h) {
      if (h && byId[h.id]) { byId[h.id].classList.add('active'); active.push(byId[h.id]); }
    });
    if (active.length) {
      var last = active[active.length - 1], toc = document.querySelector('.toc');
      var r = last.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (r.top < 60 || r.bottom > window.innerHeight - 20) toc.scrollTop += r.top - window.innerHeight / 3;
    }
  }
  var pending = false;
  window.addEventListener('scroll', function () {
    if (!pending) { pending = true; requestAnimationFrame(function () { pending = false; update(); }); }
  }, { passive: true });
  update();

  // 2. "Open larger" for each diagram.
  function close(fig, btn) {
    fig.classList.remove('large'); document.body.classList.remove('has-large'); btn.textContent = 'Open larger';
  }
  document.querySelectorAll('figure.diagram, figure.image').forEach(function (fig) {
    var btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.type = 'button'; btn.className = 'diagram-toggle'; btn.textContent = 'Open larger';
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
      if (fig.classList.contains('large')) { close(fig, btn); return; }
      fig.classList.add('large'); document.body.classList.add('has-large'); btn.textContent = 'Close';
    });
    fig.insertBefore(btn, fig.firstChild);
  });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
    var fig = document.querySelector('figure.large');
    if (fig) close(fig, fig.querySelector('.diagram-toggle'));
  });
})();

# The dev host

The engine's server running on your machine, for the frontend: both APIs (`contract/authoring-api.md`, `contract/runtime-api.md`) and the inbound hook on one port, a database in memory, and seven mock systems in place of the real ones. Requests run for real: calls, messages and outbound events go through the worker loop to the mocks.

## Start it

Node 24 or later. From `engine/`, once: `npm install`. Then:

```powershell
npm run dev-host                     # nothing published
npm run dev-host -- --seed           # publishes the three sample workflows
npm run dev-host -- --seed --port 9000 --data ./dev-data
```

It prints its address: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` by default (`http://localhost:8787` works too). The APIs are at `{address}/api/workflow/v1`, the hook at `{address}/hooks/v1/events/{connection}`. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

- `--seed` publishes `change-request`, `several-at-once` and `integrated-sample` (the files in `contract/fixtures`) as version 1, authored by Sam Carter, with the settings in `contract/fixtures/records.json`. A workflow already there is left alone.
- `--data <directory>` keeps the database in that directory across restarts. Without it, every start is empty.
- Any `http://localhost:<port>` or `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` origin may call it (CORS), so the frontend's dev server can call it directly.

## Signing in

There are no passwords. One person is signed in on the host; at start that is Sam Carter.

- `PUT /api/workflow/v1/session` with `{ "person": { "type": "user", "id": "dir-user-priya-raman" } }` signs in as someone else, for every later call.
- `GET /api/workflow/v1/session/people` lists the people to choose from; `GET /api/workflow/v1/session` says who is signed in.
- A single call can act as someone else with the header `x-dev-user: <directory ID>` (and `x-dev-platform-admin: true` or `false`). Tests and scripts use this.
- Only a person of the directory below can be signed in. `PUT /session` with a group or an unknown ID answers `400 invalid-body` (`field: "/person"`, `problem: "format"`) and changes nothing; `x-dev-user` naming one answers `401 unauthenticated`.

## People and groups

Every ID is `dir-user-<name>` or `dir-group-<name>`; emails are `first.last@example.test`.

| Person | ID | In |
|---|---|---|
| Priya Raman | `dir-user-priya-raman` | |

| Mei Tanaka | `dir-user-mei-tanaka` | Payments engineering |
| Mei Lin | `dir-user-mei-lin` | Platform team; owner of Docs site |
| Sam Carter | `dir-user-sam-carter` | Platform team; author of the samples |

Groups: `dir-group-payments-approvers`, `-payments-engineering`, `-identity-approvers`, `-identity-engineering`, `-data-platform-approvers`, `-data-platform-engineering`, `-internal-tools-engineering`, `-security-team`, `-platform-team`.

Who looks after stuck requests: Sam Carter for the two change-request samples; the Platform team for `integrated-sample`.

## The mock systems

The catalogue the host serves is exactly `contract/fixtures/catalogue.json`, version included.

| Connection | What it does | Switches |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | The people and groups above; group members as choices; "is in group" and membership reads | down |
| `servicecatalog` | Services: Payments API (Tier 1, owner Diego), Ledger (Tier 2, no owner), Docs site (Tier 3, owner Mei Lin), Old billing (retired). A list for choices and a "look up a service" read | fail next (`service-not-found`), down |
| `helpdesk` | Sends a new ticket to the hook; starts `integrated-sample` | none |
| `jira` | Creates issues `OPS-101`, `CHG-101` ... | fail next (`permission-denied`), down |
| `deploy` | A deploy that runs: accepted, "running" at the first status question, done at the second (the worker asks every 60 s) | fail next (the run ends `tests-failed`), down |
| `messages` | Keeps every message the platform sends | down |
| `reporting` | Keeps every outbound event | down |

"Fail next" makes the next call fail clearly, and switches itself off after that call; "down" makes every call go unanswered until switched back, so the worker tries again later. Set them from the browser (next section), or as fields on the mocks from code that starts the host itself:

```js
// node --conditions=workflow-source my-script.mjs, from engine/
import { startDevHost } from "./packages/server/src/dev-host/host.ts";
const host = await startDevHost({ seed: true });
host.mocks.jira.failNext = true;   // the next issue fails: the request is stuck, Retry sends it again
```

## Controlling the mocks from the browser

A small development-only control surface, served by the dev host only, under `{address}/dev` (not under the API base). JSON in and out, the same CORS as the rest, no sign-in. A refusal answers `{ "error": "<one line>" }`. The examples use the default address.

**1. The mocks and their switches.** `GET /dev/mocks`: every mock in catalogue order, with only the switches it has and their values now.

```powershell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/dev/mocks
```

```ts
{ mocks: { connection: string; label: string; switches: { failNext?: boolean; down?: boolean } }[] }
// { "mocks": [ { "connection": "directory", "label": "Directory", "switches": { "down": false } },
//              { "connection": "servicecatalog", "label": "Service catalog", "switches": { "failNext": false, "down": false } },
//              { "connection": "helpdesk", "label": "Helpdesk", "switches": {} }, ... ] }
```

**2. Set a switch.** `PUT /dev/mocks/{connection}` with body `{ failNext?: boolean, down?: boolean }`: `200` with that mock's entry as in 1. `failNext: true` makes the next call fail and switches itself off after it; `down` stays until set `false`.

```powershell
curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8787/dev/mocks/jira -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"failNext":true}'
# {"connection":"jira","label":"Jira","switches":{"failNext":true,"down":false}}
```

| Answer | When |
|---|---|
| `404 { "error": "no mock system nowhere" }` | No such connection |
| `400 { "error": "messages has no switch failNext" }` | A switch that mock does not have |
| `400 { "error": "down must be true or false" }` | A value that is not a boolean |
| `400 { "error": "unknown key slow: the switches are failNext and down" }` | Any other key |
| `400 { "error": "the body is not JSON" }`, `"the body is not a JSON object"` | |

A refused body changes nothing.

**3. What a mock received.** `GET /dev/mocks/{connection}/received[?request=<request ID>]`: `{ items: [...] }`, oldest first, everything that mock was sent since the host started (each mock keeps its newest 1,000), only that request's when `request` is given. Unknown connection: `404`.

```powershell
curl "http://127.0.0.1:8787/dev/mocks/jira/received?request=<request ID>"
```

The items, by connection:

```ts
// messages: each message the notifier sent, one per person.
{
  at: string;            // when it was sent (ISO)
  request: string;       // the request ID
  rule: string;          // the notification rule, or the platform's built-in code
  to: string;            // the person's directory ID
  message: { words: string } | { parts: ({ text: string } | { kind: string; value?: unknown })[] };   // exactly as sent
}

// reporting: each outbound event body exactly as posted (request.started@1, request.statusChanged@1 ...);
// filtered by its `subject`, the request ID.

// jira, deploy, servicecatalog, directory: each call received.
{
  at: string;                    // when it was answered (ISO)
  request: string | null;        // the request whose call it is
  operation: string;             // "createIssue@1", "runPipeline@1", "serviceDetails@1", "membersOf@1"
  kind: "call" | "status";       // "status": an await's status question (the deploy pipeline)
  key: string;                   // the idempotency key it was sent with
  input: object;                 // the call's input as sent; for a status question { jobRef }
  answer:
    | { answer: "ok"; data: object; jobRef?: string }
    | { answer: "failed"; code: string; message: string; jobRef?: string }
    | { answer: "accepted"; jobRef: string }
    | { answer: "running"; jobRef: string }      // status questions only
    | { answer: "none"; detail: string };        // no answer: the mock is down
}

// helpdesk: nothing; items is [].
```

The directory lists its recorded reads (`membersOf@1`, the read behind a members step and an "is in group" test), not the live reads behind pickers and checks; the service catalog lists its `serviceDetails@1` calls, not its choice lists.

**4. Make the helpdesk send.** `POST /dev/mocks/helpdesk/send` with body `{ key?, title?, description?, category?, priority?, service?, reporter?, url? }`, one key per field of the trigger's event in `contract/fixtures/catalogue.json` (`helpdesk.ticketCreated@1`), all text: sends the event to this host's own hook, signed as the script signs it, and answers `200 { status, answer }`, the hook's HTTP status and its JSON answer. A field not given is the sample ticket's:

| Key | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `HD-2291` | The same key twice is the same event. |
| `title` | `Raise payment API rate limit` | |
| `description` | `Checkout is throttled at peak.` | |
| `category` | `Service change` | Only this starts `integrated-sample`. |
| `priority` | `high` | The catalogue's choices: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`; anything else is sent as given, for the hook to refuse. |
| `service` | `svc-payments-api` | A service ID; sent with the seeded service's name, or the ID. |
| `reporter` | `priya.raman@example.test` | An email; the directory's person with it becomes the Requester. |
| `url` | `http://helpdesk.mock.test/tickets/{key}` | |

A field that is not text: `400 { "error": "<key> must be text" }`. Any other key: `400 { "error": "unknown key <key>: the fields are key, title, description, category, priority, service, reporter, url" }`.

```powershell
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/dev/mocks/helpdesk/send -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"key":"HD-2292","service":"svc-docs-site"}'
# {"status":200,"answer":{"eventId":"HD-2292.created","results":[{"workflow":"integrated-sample","version":1,"result":"started","binding":"sw_helpdesk_ticket","requestId":"...","readableId":3}]}}
```

The same key again answers `result: "duplicate"` and starts nothing.

A failed action and Retry, from the browser: `PUT /dev/mocks/jira {"failNext":true}`; run a change request to its Jira step (Marcus approves); the request is stuck; `GET /dev/mocks/jira/received?request=...` shows the failed call and its key; Retry; the same list shows a second call with the same key, answered `ok`, and the request moves on.

## Making the helpdesk send an event

With the host running, from `engine/`:

```powershell
node packages/server/scripts/helpdesk-event.mjs --key HD-2292 --service svc-docs-site
```

Options: `--port`, and one per field of the event, as in the table above: `--key` (the same key twice is the same event: the second starts nothing), `--title`, `--description`, `--category` (only "Service change" starts `integrated-sample`), `--priority`, `--service` (a service ID), `--reporter` (an email; becomes the Requester), `--url`. It prints the hook's answer. An unknown service is refused and then listed under refused starts, from where it can be run again. `POST /dev/mocks/helpdesk/send` does the same through the same function.

## Seeing what was sent

`GET /dev/mocks/{connection}/received` lists it (above). Messages and outbound events stay in the mocks' memory; the host also prints a line for each on its output, among its other log lines:

```
{"at":"...","kind":"mock-message-sent","request":"<request ID>","rule":"n_task","detail":"dir-user-marcus-lee"}
{"at":"...","kind":"mock-event-received","request":"<request ID>","detail":"request.statusChanged@1"}
```

Other log lines: `start-refused` and `inbound-refused` from the hook, `call-attempt` per call sent, `rule-error`, `job-failed`.

## Resetting

Stop the host and start it again. Without `--data` everything is gone; with it, delete the directory.

## Checking it works

`node packages/server/scripts/dev-host-smoke.mjs` starts the host with `--seed`, runs a change request to its end as Priya, Marcus and Diego over HTTP, prints the story and exits 0.
===\nengine/README-dev.md\n===
# Engine: development

The engine's code is an npm workspace rooted at `engine/`. The repo root has no `package.json` and must not get one (root `README.md`).

| Package | Path | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `@workflow/core` | `packages/core` | Pure TypeScript, ESM, no I/O, no Node-only API (decision E-3). Two entries (E-26): `@workflow/core`, the contract surface (parse, check, facts, formulas, `formState`, `diff`, `compile`, Try it's test host, the request views and the story), and `@workflow/core/kernel`, the stored formats, the kernel, the publish check, the stuck state, the rule matchers and the in-memory host. |
| `@workflow/server` | `packages/server` | The engine's server (E-3, E-30, E-33): the store on Postgres (PGlite in tests and on the dev host), the turn transaction around core's turn function, the configuration and connectors, the worker loop, the inbound hook, the authoring and runtime APIs over HTTP, the seven mock systems and the development host. `scripts/smoke.mjs` runs core from plain Node. |

The stored formats and the compiler design are in `design/`. `spec/` is a read-only copy of the kernel spec package (`workflow-platform/engine`), made by `npm run sync-spec` (`scripts/sync-spec.mjs`); `packages/core/test/spec-copy.test.ts` fails when it is stale and is skipped when the source repo is not on disk.

## What core holds

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/index.ts` | The entry `@workflow/core`: what `contract/core-api.md` names that exists (sections 2 to 13), every name exported explicitly. Values (22): `parse`, `check`, `facts`, `valuesInScope`, `sampleValues`, `checkFormula`, `evaluate`, `evaluateSent`, `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS`, `formState`, `requestView`, `story`, `createTestHost`, `diff`, `compile`, `coreVersion`, `meta`, `CEL_PROFILE`, `upgrade`, and what the server shares with the views and the test host (E-31): `refusalOf` (a kernel refusal as the contract reports it), `buttonStates` (a viewer's button states on a task or the start form) and `blankWorkflow`. Types: the shared types of section 2 (`Json`, `Ref`, `By`, `Refusal`, `TurnResult`, `Result` ...), each function's result types, `FindingCode`, the request view, story, test host and outbox types, `PublishedVersion`, `Change` and `ChangeParams`, and every type of `contract/authored-format.ts` and `contract/catalogue.ts`. `diff` (section 11) is built, in `src/authored/diff/`; `upgrade` (section 13) returns the document unchanged while there is one authored format. `Draft` (`authoring-api.md` section 3) is core's, the type of the `stale-revision` refusal's draft; the server's authoring API uses it. |
| `src/kernel-entry.ts` | The entry `@workflow/core/kernel` (29 values): the stored formats (definition and events), `validateDefinitionShape`, the `jsonschema-1` validator, `decide`, `evolve`, `fold`, `turn`, `validateCallResult`, `lookupsToMake`, `lookupInputs` (a lookup's inputs before its answer is given), `isWaitOpen`, `sameWait`, `checkDefinition` (the kernel publish check) with `PUBLISH_CHECKS` and `PUBLISH_WARNINGS` (empty: no check is a warning today), the stuck state (`stuckStateOf`, `nobodyToAsk`, `authoredStageOf`), `matchNotifications`, `outboundEvents`, `outboundEventId`, `mapBinding` (a "Starts when" binding's start from what was sent), and the in-memory host. For the server and the hosts; never the frontend. |
| `src/authored/` | The authored format (contract part A) and everything the contract surface does with it: `parse/`, `check/` (the findings of core-api.md section 4), `facts/`, `formula/` (`checkFormula`, chips, value kinds as CEL types), `evaluate/` (`sampleValues`, `evaluate`, `evaluateSent`), `form/` (`formState`), `diff/`, `compile/` (the compiler), `host/` (Try it's test host and outbox), `view/` (request views; `reading.ts` turns engine elements into authored locations through the origin map), `story/`, `index-doc.ts` (the one walk over a document the rest reads), `blank.ts` (the blank workflow) and `upgrade.ts`. `contract/` holds copies of `contract/authored-format.ts` and `catalogue.ts`, made by `scripts/sync-contract.mjs`; never edit them by hand. |
| `src/cel/` | The CEL environment of profile `cel-1` (E-18, E-23), wrapping `@marcbachmann/cel-js` and `@bufbuild/re2`; what a condition reads; JSON to CEL; `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS` as data. |
| `src/format/` | The stored formats as types: the published definition (format 1) and the events (`design/definition-format.md`, `design/event-payloads.md`), and `validateDefinitionShape`. |
| `src/schema/` | The JSON Schema validator of profile `jsonschema-1` that `decide` checks outcome data with. Written here, not a library. |
| `src/kernel/` | `evolve` and the request state; `decide/`, the turn's events from a definition, a state, an input and what the caller looked up (kernel spec sections 2 to 5); `turn.ts`, the turn on its own (validate, decide, evolve); `call-result.ts`, the call-result check; `decide/environment.ts`, the one CEL environment `decide` and the publish check share; `publish/`, the kernel publish check; `stuck/`, the stuck state every reader works out from the request state (nothing records it), the nobody-to-ask matcher, and `authoredStageOf`, the one mapper from an engine stage to the authored stage a stuck request is reported in; `notify/`, the notification and outbound-event matchers. |
| `src/host/` | The in-memory host (`createMemoryHost`): runs requests on a published definition with fixtures for the directory and data sources, keeps an attempts log, and works out the stuck state once per turn with `src/kernel/stuck/`. Used by the spec's cases; Try it uses `src/authored/host/`, so the root's bundle leaves this out. |
| `scripts/` | `sync-contract.mjs`: copies the contract's TypeScript files into `src/authored/contract/`. |
| `test/` | Vitest, one folder per source folder. `kernel/cases/` translates the spec's case files (`spec/workflows/change-request-demo/test-cases.yaml`, `spec/kernel/replay-only.yaml`); `host/change-request-demo.test.ts` runs the demo's acceptance cases through the host. `library/` measures the CEL library itself. `boundaries.test.ts` and `public-api.test.ts` guard the package's edges; `cel/t29-bundle-size.test.ts` bundles both entries for the browser; `spec-copy.test.ts` checks that `engine/spec` equals its source. |

## What the server holds

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/store/` | `db.ts`: one small interface (query, transaction) with a PGlite and a node-postgres adapter. `schema/`: the numbered SQL files (`001` to `005`, 12 tables) that `migrate.ts` applies in order; `events`, `definitions`, `settings_log` and `inbound_log` refuse UPDATE and DELETE by trigger. `events.ts`, `definitions.ts`, `lock.ts`, `projections.ts` (the `requests` and `open_waits` read tables), `pending-calls.ts`, `jobs.ts`, `attempts.ts`, `authoring.ts`. |
| `src/turn/` | The turn transaction (data model section 1): lookups before the lock, then in one transaction the lock, core's `turn`, the events, the read tables, the pending calls and the jobs; a binding's start also writes its `inbound_log` row, whose unique index is the dedupe. |
| `src/config/` | The configuration read at start-up (`engine/design/integrations-shapes.md`): connections, connectors, secrets from the environment, subscribers; the catalogue built from them; the structured log. |
| `src/connectors/` | The connector interface (directory, data sources, operations, Notify, triggers), the lookups a turn makes through it, and the in-memory connectors the tests use. |
| `src/workers/` | One worker loop over `jobs`: the call, notify and publish jobs. |
| `src/hooks/` | The inbound endpoint `POST /hooks/v1/events/{connection}` (runtime-api.md section 8) and running a refused start again. Core's `mapBinding` runs the binding. |
| `src/api/` | `authoring/` (authoring-api.md) and `runtime/` (runtime-api.md, bindings and refused starts included): each a set of plain functions and Hono routes over them, called without a socket. `shared/`: the error body and headers, body reading, the catalogue registry, who looks after a workflow. `caller.ts`: the development caller adapter. An unknown path or method answers `not-found` (`path`). |
| `src/mock/` | The seven mock systems of `engine/design/mock-systems.md`, in memory, their connectors and seed configuration (the catalogue they declare is `contract/fixtures/catalogue.json`), and the dev host's `--seed`. The only folder that names outside systems and fixtures. |
| `src/dev-host/` | The development host: the server on PGlite with the mocks, both APIs and the hook on one port, the worker running. How to use it: `engine/DEV-HOST.md`. |
| `scripts/` | `smoke.mjs` (core from plain Node), `dev-host-smoke.mjs` (the dev host with `--seed`, the change-request sample run to its ending over HTTP as three people), `helpdesk-event.mjs` (the mock helpdesk sends a ticket to a running dev host), `copy-schema.mjs` (the build's). |
| `test/` | Vitest, one folder per source folder, on PGlite: each test file starts its own in-memory PGlite with the schema applied (`test/helpers.ts`). `review/` holds the cross-cutting checks. `dev-host/` starts the dev host on a free port and drives each door over real HTTP. The `*.pg.test.ts` files need a real Postgres and are skipped without `DATABASE_URL`. `boundaries.test.ts`: the server's source names no customer workflow (`src/mock` excepted) and takes core only through its two entries. |

The dev host: `npm run dev-host` from `engine/` (add `-- --seed` for the sample workflows); `node packages/server/scripts/dev-host-smoke.mjs` checks it end to end.

## Tooling

Node 24 or later and npm 11, on `PATH`; checked with Node 26.13.1 and npm 11.20.0.

All versions are pinned exactly (`--save-exact`); `package-lock.json` holds the integrity hashes. The CEL library is `@marcbachmann/cel-js` 8.0.0 (decision E-18). Changing it is a new CEL profile and a new definition format, never an in-place upgrade.

## Install, test, build

Run every command in `engine/`. Never run npm in the repo root.

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `npm install` |
| Test (all packages) | `npm test` |
| Test one file | `npx vitest run packages/core/test/cel/trial.test.ts` |
| Show the trial's measurements (T27, T29, T30) | `npx vitest run packages/core/test --silent=false` |
| Type-check | `npm run typecheck` |
| Lint | `npm run lint` |
| Build to `dist/` | `npm run build` (core first, then server) |
| Copy the contract's TypeScript files into core | `npm run sync-contract -w @workflow/core` |
| Copy the kernel spec package into `spec/` | `npm run sync-spec` |
| The server's real-Postgres tests | `$env:DATABASE_URL = "postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/db"; npx vitest run --project server` |

The server's tests run on PGlite (Postgres compiled to WebAssembly, in memory), so they need no database. Three files, `packages/server/test/turn/concurrency.pg.test.ts`, `test/api/runtime/concurrency.pg.test.ts` and `test/api/authoring/concurrency.pg.test.ts`, race two connections on one request, which PGlite (one connection) cannot show; they are skipped unless `DATABASE_URL` names a Postgres the tests may use. Each run creates a schema of its own there and drops it after.

On 2026-11-16, on kernel spec v2.20, from clean (`dist/` removed): typecheck, lint and build were clean. Core's tests: 102 files, 1878 tests, all passed. The server's tests: 32 files, 281 tests, 273 passed, 8 skipped (the three `*.pg.test.ts` files). No test is marked `it.fails`. Both smoke runs (`dist` and source) ended at `st_released`, and so did the dev host smoke run.

Core's tests have a 60-second limit each (`testTimeout` in `packages/core/vitest.config.ts`), not Vitest's 5 seconds: the generated tests (random walks, mutation suites) run slower when several suites share a loaded machine. A test that needs longer still gives its own limit.

npm 11 does not run `esbuild`'s install script unless it is approved (`npm install-scripts approve esbuild`). It is not needed: the platform binary arrives as an optional dependency, and the tests that bundle with esbuild pass without it.

## Rules the tooling enforces

- Core imports no Node built-in and uses no Node-only global. ESLint (`no-restricted-imports`, `no-restricted-globals`) and `packages/core/test/boundaries.test.ts` both check it. Core's `tsconfig.json` has `"types": []` and `"lib": ["ES2022"]`, so a Node or DOM API does not type-check either.
- Only `packages/core/src/cel/environment.ts` imports the CEL library. Same two checks. Tests under `packages/core/test/library/` import it on purpose: they measure the library itself.
- No source file names a customer workflow, its systems or a fixture (`change request`, `Jira`, a fixture's name): `boundaries.test.ts`. The copies in `src/authored/contract/` are exempt; their comments give examples.
- The two entries are separate: neither imports the other, the kernel entry takes nothing from `src/authored/`, and both import only from inside core (`boundaries.test.ts`).
- Layers: `src/kernel/` imports nothing from `src/authored/` or `src/host/`, and `src/authored/` nothing from `src/host/` (`boundaries.test.ts`).
- ESLint gives `.mjs` scripts Node's globals (`console`, `process`, `URL` ...), so a script needs no `/* global */` comment. `test/cel/t29-bundle-size.test.ts` bundles each entry for the browser with esbuild, holds it to a gzip budget, and checks that the root holds the kernel but not the in-memory host, and the kernel entry nothing authored.
- Core uses only TypeScript syntax that can be erased (`erasableSyntaxOnly`), so Node can run its source directly.
- Core compiles with `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` (its three tsconfig files), so a consumer of its source with those flags on compiles it too: `boundaries.test.ts` checks the settings.
- The copies in `src/authored/contract/` equal the contract's files: `test/authored/contract-sync.test.ts`. After the contract changes, run `npm run sync-contract -w @workflow/core`.
- `spec/` equals `workflow-platform/engine` with LF endings, file for file, and `spec/SOURCE.md` names the spec's version: `packages/core/test/spec-copy.test.ts`. After the spec changes, run `npm run sync-spec`.
- Each entry exports exactly its listed values, and the two share none: `test/public-api.test.ts`. Its type checks (run by `npm run typecheck`) pin the root's function signatures and result shapes to `contract/core-api.md`. Tests of internal parts import the folder's own `index.ts`, never an entry.

## How another package consumes core

Import only `@workflow/core` and `@workflow/core/kernel`; deep imports are not exported. Each entry is a conditional export:

```json
".":        { "workflow-source": "./src/index.ts",        "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",        "default": "./dist/index.js" },
"./kernel": { "workflow-source": "./src/kernel-entry.ts", "types": "./dist/kernel-entry.d.ts", "default": "./dist/kernel-entry.js" }
```

The two entries share type names with different meanings (`Status`, `ValueKind`, `MessagePart`, `TurnResult`): the root's are the contract's, the kernel's are the stored formats'. A module that needs both imports one as a namespace (`import * as kernel from "@workflow/core/kernel"`).

- **As TypeScript source** (no build step): the consumer resolves with the `workflow-source` condition. The server does this for type-checking and tests: `customConditions: ["workflow-source"]` in `tsconfig.base.json`, and `resolve.conditions` / `ssr.resolve.conditions` in `packages/server/vitest.config.ts`.
- **As built JavaScript**: run `npm run build -w @workflow/core`. A consumer without the condition gets `dist/`. `@workflow/server`'s build (`customConditions: []`) compiles against core's `dist`.
- **Plain Node**, either way: `node packages/server/scripts/smoke.mjs` (from `dist`) and `node --conditions=workflow-source packages/server/scripts/smoke.mjs` (from source) import both entries, then parse, check and compile `contract/fixtures/change-request.authored.json`, run the kernel's publish check on the result, and run a request through `createTestHost` from the start form to `st_released`, using only the root for the request.

### The frontend

The frontend imports only `@workflow/core`: functions, their result types, and the authored-format and catalogue types (`AuthoredWorkflow`, `Location`, `Catalogue` ...), which the root re-exports as types. Constants (`ID_PATTERN`, `WORDS` ...) are not re-exported; the frontend takes them from its own copy of the contract. Three names differ from the contract files':

- `DirectoryRef` is the authored format's `{ directoryId, name }`; the catalogue's `{ type, id }` is `CatalogueDirectoryRef`, the same shape as `Ref`.
- `Json` is core-api.md's, which never holds `null`; the catalogue's, which may, is `CatalogueJson`.
- `Published` is what `compile` returns (the stored definition); the request views and the story take a `PublishedVersion`, that definition with its authored source and catalogue.

The root's browser bundle holds the kernel, because Try it runs requests in the browser, and the CEL library; tree-shaking leaves out the in-memory host. Sizes on 2026-11-16, kernel spec v2.20 (esbuild, minified, ES2022): root 442,758 bytes, 137,074 gzip (core's own code 310,221, `@marcbachmann/cel-js` 82,612, `@bufbuild/re2` 49,556); kernel entry 239,360 bytes, 74,145 gzip (core's own code 106,761). Budgets in `t29-bundle-size.test.ts`: 160,000 and 90,000 bytes gzip.

How the frontend links core (as `frontend/package.json`, `vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json` do):

1. `"@workflow/core": "file:../engine/packages/core"` in `frontend/package.json`. npm links the folder; core's own dependencies resolve from `engine/node_modules`, so run `npm install` in `engine/` first.
2. For source: Vite `resolve.conditions: ["workflow-source", ...defaultClientConditions]` (from `vite`), and TypeScript `"customConditions": ["workflow-source"]` with `"allowImportingTsExtensions": true` (core's source imports `./x.ts`). Vite's dev server may also need `server.fs.allow` to include `../engine`.
3. For `dist` instead: no settings; build core first.

The API reports the core version it runs (`coreVersion`, also `meta.coreVersion`), so a stale browser bundle can be detected (E-3).

# The compiler: authored format 0 to the published definition

Owner: engine owner. Status: design, 2026-11-15, pending the product owner's review; revised 2026-11-16 after E-27, E-28, E-29, E-32 and E-33. The compiler is built in core (`engine/packages/core/src/authored/compile/`). Where the built compiler and the worked examples here differed, E-27 settled each point and this file says what is built.

Against: kernel spec v2.20 (its copy is in `engine/spec/`); `engine/design/integrations-shapes.md` (cited as "shapes"); the published definition format 1 (`engine/design/definition-format.md`, cited as "format") and the event payloads (`engine/design/event-payloads.md`, cited as "event-payloads"); decisions E-1 to E-33 (`docs/11-decisions-engine.md`; where this file and a decision differ, the decision holds); the authored format 0 (`contract/authored-format.ts`, `.md`); `contract/core-api.md` Draft 3 (cited as "core"); `contract/runtime-api.md`; profile `cel-1` as wrapped in `engine/packages/core/src/cel/` and tried in `engine/packages/core/test/cel/`.

E-20 requires the stage names and chain shape to be fixed here before anything is published, because stage, wait and transition IDs and data paths are recorded in history for ever. This revision applies E-21 to E-23: nobody-to-ask follows shapes 5.5 (a `nobodyToAsk` block and a membership read beside the task), the tasks step leaves by an explicit condition, each directory read sits just before the step that uses it, and Retry is offered only for `action-failed` and `nobody-to-ask`. It also applies E-24: who can answer a task (10.4), "people in [group]" asks the group (4.2), empty items in a list comparison are ignored (8.3), a cancelled read is dropped quietly (10.4). Sections 1 to 16 answer the sixteen points of the brief in order. Section 17 lists the choices made, most expensive first; section 18 lists flaws found in decisions and in other files; section 19 lists what other files must change; section 20 is the adversarial review of this file and what E-23 settled.

Terms: kernel terms (stage, wait, outcome, check, transition, Set, activation, `decide`, rule) for engine things; authored terms (stage, task, question, button, action, arrow, value, list) for authored things. "Engine stage" always means a kernel stage; "stage" alone means an authored stage. "Step" is one engine stage of a chain.

## 0. What `compile` is

`compile(workflow, catalogue, options)` (core section 12) is pure. It reads one `AuthoredWorkflow` and the catalogue (which names the directory connection, `directoryConnection`), and returns the published definition (format 1, with the v2.16 names: `connection`, `triggers`, `events`, `nobodyToAsk`, `send.message`), the pinned schemas, the origin map, and the declared types, with the list of unfinished parts (section 13). `options` gives the mode (below) and the server's `workflow` (its own workflow ID), `version` and `compiler` (the core version), which default to `draft`, 1 and `core`.

Output order does not depend on the key order of a stored draft, which `jsonb` does not keep (E-27). Call arguments and lookup inputs follow the catalogue's input field order; the Sets of an action's results follow the catalogue's result field order; Tell values are sorted by name. Everything else follows the document's arrays. Object key order is never relied on, but positional origins such as `#/set/<n>/expr` follow this order. The compiler emits kernel elements directly; `composites` is always `[]` (E-19; E-23 keeps it).
