The declared types are the definition's `types` block (format 3.12; E-23): the type of every data path, constant and operation result. `decide` uses it when it turns JSON into CEL values, so a schema `number` is a CEL double and an `integer` an int. Section 3.4 gives what the compiler writes.

Two modes:

| Mode | Used by | Input | On a To do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publish | The server at publish (E-3) | A draft with no `todo` finding | Never reached: publish is refused with `has-todo` first |
| Try it | `createTestHost` (core section 10) | Any draft that `parse` accepts | Emits the unfinished shapes of section 13 and lists their locations |

Only publish mode runs the kernel publish checks (spec section 6) on the result.

## 1. Naming

### 1.1 The rule

Every engine ID the compiler adds is `<authored item ID>__<local name>`: one authored ID, a double underscore, one local name from the table in 1.2. Authored IDs never contain `__` (format rule 2), so the authored item is everything before the first `__`, and no two items can produce the same name. Local names are lowerCamelCase words that match `^[a-z][A-Za-z]*$`.

Authored IDs that carry through unchanged (E-14):

| Authored ID | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Ending `st_` | The final engine stage's ID |
| Task `tk_` | The person wait's local ID, in each copy of the tasks step |
| Action `act_` (connection action) | The call wait's local ID in the action's step |
| Button `btn_` | The outcome ID |
| Arrow `ar_` | The routing step's transition ID |
| Value `v_` | The top-level data path |
| Status `stat_` | The status ID |
| List `ls_` | The constant's name |
| Starts-when binding `sw_` | The `triggers` entry ID |
| Action `act_` (Notify) | The notification rule ID |
| Action `act_` (Tell other systems) | The `events` rule ID |
| Question `q_` | The property name in the outcome's data and schema, and in a binding's `data` |

A working stage's own ID is never an engine stage ID: every step of its chain has a local name. Reason: a step's ID then means one role for ever, and adding or removing a section adds or removes steps without renaming any other.

Length: format section 2 caps a Name at 64 characters. The longest local names are 15 characters (`groupsTasksBack`, `groupsRouteBack`), so every authored ID must be at most 47 characters. E-23 limits authored IDs to 40 characters and `parse` refuses a longer one, so every compiled Name is at most 57 characters. A nobody-to-ask rule ID (`<S>__tasksBack.<T>__nobody`) is two such Names joined by a dot, which format section 2 allows. Editor IDs are about 9 characters; the longest fixture ID is 29 (`act_notify_requester_rejected`).

### 1.2 Every local name

| Kind | Name | Attached to | What it is | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Engine stage | `tasks`, `tasksBack` | stage | The tasks step, normal and sent-back copy | 2, 7 |
| Engine stage | `route`, `routeBack` | stage | The routing step | 2, 6 |
| Engine stage | `groupsTasks`, `groupsTasksBack` | stage | The directory read just before the tasks step | 8.6 |
| Engine stage | `groupsRoute`, `groupsRouteBack` | stage | The directory read just before the routing step | 8.6 |
| Engine stage | `groups`, `groupsBack` | action | The directory read just before the action's first step | 8.6 |
| Engine stage | `run`, `runBack` | action | The action's own step | 2, 11 |
| Engine stage | `gate`, `gateBack` | connection action with `onlyWhen` | Decides whether the call is made | 2, 11 |
| Engine stage | `unfinished` | arrow | Try it only: where an unfinished arrow leads | 13 |
| Wait | `members` | task that may ask a group | The membership read beside the task, in the tasks step (E-23; shapes 5.5) | 10.4 |
| Wait | `read` | stage or action | A directory read step's call wait | 8.6 |
| Transition | `answered` | stage | Tasks step: every task answered (an explicit condition, never `otherwise`) | 2.3, 4 |
| Transition | `early` | arrow | Tasks step: a "Don't wait for the others" arrow fits | 6 |
| Transition | `readOk` | stage or action | Directory read step: the read answered | 8.6 |
| Transition | `save`, `skip` | action | Save step: save, or "Only when" not true | 2 |
| Transition | `next` | action | Notify or Tell step: move on | 2 |
| Transition | `ok`, `failed` | action | Connection step: the call's two outcomes | 11 |
| Transition | `go`, `skip` | action | Gate step: make the call, or not | 11 |
| Data path | `pressed` | task | The button pressed on the task in this visit | 3 |
| Data path | `early` | stage | The "Don't wait for the others" arrow chosen in this visit | 3, 6 |
| Data path | `groups` | stage | The last recorded directory read step of this visit | 3, 8.6 |
| Check | `hidden` | question | A hidden question must arrive empty | 5 |
| Check | `needed` | question | A needed question with a Show when | 5 |
| Check | `choice` | question | Formula choices; a multiple choice not empty and in order | 5 |
| Check | `also` | button | "Also only when" | 4 |
| Check | `requester` | start task | Only a connection may supply the Requester | 10 |

Not of the form above, and fixed here:

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `requester` | Data path: the Requester (E-17; shapes 1.5) |
| `<full wait ID>__nobody` | A `nobodyToAsk` rule ID (format section 2), one per emitted person wait: `st_domain_approval__tasks.tk_domain_approval__nobody` (section 10.4) |
| `n_task`, `n_stopped` | The two built-in notification rules (section 10.3) |
| `<tk>.<btn>@1` | Schema reference: schema ID `<task ID>.<button ID>`, version always 1 (section 5) |

### 1.3 What is positional

| Positional (meaningful only inside one element of one version) | Not positional |
|---|---|
| The order of stages, waits, outcomes, checks, transitions, sets and rules in their arrays | Every ID in section 1.2 and every carried-through ID |
| Array indices in a field pointer (`/set/2/expr`, `/send/message/parts/1/value`) and in field origin keys (section 12) | Data paths |
| | Schema property names (question IDs) |

The origin map is stored with the version, so a positional field pointer is always read against the definition that wrote it.

### 1.4 What an edit changes

| Author's edit | Engine IDs and paths |
|---|---|
| Renames anything (stage, task, question, button, value, status words, told words, labels) | No ID or path changes. Status labels, told words, choice labels in rendered templates and Notify text change in the next version's definition. |
| Reorders stages | No change. Declared order of `root.stages` follows; behaviour does not depend on it. |
| Reorders arrows, actions, questions, pages, tasks | No ID changes. Transition order, chain order, set order and check order follow, which is the intended change of behaviour. |
| Inserts an action, task, question, arrow or stage | New IDs only. Four insertions add compiler names to existing items: the first pressed clause on a task adds `<tk>__pressed`; a "Who is asked" that can give a group adds `<tk>__members` and fills the `members` field of the task's nobody-to-ask rules; the first directory step or "is in group" test read by a step adds that step's read step (`S__groupsTasks`, `S__groupsRoute` or `A__groups`) and `<st>__groups`; an arrow that makes another stage send back (dominance, section 7) adds a `…Back` chain and moves an arrow's target to it. |
| Deletes an item | Its IDs vanish and are never reused (format rule 2). |
| Sets or clears `ifSentBackStatus` | Adds or removes the `…Back` chain. |
| Adds or clears "Only when" on a connection action | Adds or removes its `gate` step. |

### 1.5 Why a later compiler version can change the chain

- A request runs on its own definition version for its whole life (spec section 2; format rule "immutable"). `decide` reads only that version; `evolve` reads no definition.
- Every reader that names a step to a person (story, request view, lists, stuck state, outbound `where`) goes through that version's origin map (E-7, E-18), never through the shape of an ID. The stuck reason and Retry read the fault and the `nobodyToAsk` block (section 12.4), not ID shapes.
- Nothing outside the platform holds an engine stage, wait or transition ID: outbound events carry status IDs and authored locations (shapes 7.2), callback tokens carry connection, op and key (shapes 4.5), and inbound answers carry binding IDs. A derived idempotency key contains the element (spec section 2), and the compiler emits derived keys only with `keyScope: activation`, which makes a new key on every entry anyway; "once" uses an explicit key built from the action ID (section 11.3), which no chain change touches.
- The definition records the core version that compiled it (`compiler`).

So a new compiler version may add, merge or rename steps for later publishes. Requests on older versions keep their steps. The one feature that would map steps across versions, moving a request to another version (spec section 8), is reserved and carries its own stage mapping.

## 2. One authored stage as a chain

### 2.1 The steps, in order

For a working stage `S`, one copy (section 7 gives the second):

| # | Step | Engine stage ID | Present when | Waits | Transitions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Each arrival action, in listed order | `A__groups` (if any), `A__gate` (if any), `A__run` | Always, one per action; `A__groups` when the action uses a directory step or an "is in group" test (8.6) | See 2.2 and 8.6 | See 2.2 and 8.6 |
| 2 | Directory read for the tasks step | `S__groupsTasks` | A Show when, "Also only when", lookup input or early arrow of the stage uses a directory step or an "is in group" test (8.6); never for "Who is asked", where "people in [group]" asks the group (4.2) | `S__read` | `S__readOk` |
| 3 | Tasks step | `S__tasks` | The stage has tasks | per task, in listed order: its membership read `<tk>__members` when it may ask a group (10.4), then its person wait | `<ar>__early` per early arrow, then `S__answered` |
| 4 | Each after-response action, in listed order | `A__groups`, `A__gate`, `A__run` | One per action, as step 1 | See 2.2 and 8.6 | See 2.2 and 8.6 |
| 5 | Directory read for the arrows | `S__groupsRoute` | An arrow's condition or "+ only when" uses a directory step or an "is in group" test | `S__read` | `S__readOk` |
| 6 | Routing step | `S__route` | Always | none | one per arrow, in arrow order |

A step that is absent is skipped: each step's transitions go to the next present step. The entry of the chain is its first present step. The routing step is always present, even when one arrow could ride on the previous step's transition: arrow transitions then always live in `S__route` and the story always finds them there. Cost: one stage entry, one exit and one firing per visit (cheap).

A stage with no tasks (an Automatic stage) has steps 1, 4, 5, 6: its "After they respond" actions, which the format allows there, still run, before the arrows (authored format rule 5; E-27). An ending is one final stage (section 9). The start stage's normal copy has no arrival actions and no read before the tasks step (section 7.4).

After-response actions run before the arrows are checked (E-22). When no arrow fits, they have already run, and the request is stuck with `nothing-fits` in `S__route`. An early arrow (6.4) is the one arrow chosen before them; the request still runs them before it leaves the stage.

Every step of a copy carries that copy's status (section 7.2), so passing from step to step never changes what people see, and `request.statusChanged@1` fires only when the authored stage changes.

### 2.2 Where each kind of action lives

| Action | Its step `A__run` | "Only when" | Listed order |
|---|---|---|---|
| Save a value | No waits. `A__save`: `when` = Only when (or `true`), `set [{path: [<as>], expr: N(<kind>, O(<save>))}]`, to the next step. `A__skip` (only with Only when): `otherwise`, no set, to the next step. | `A__save` fires only when true; `A__skip` writes nothing, so the value keeps what it had and no `DataSet` is recorded. | The Set is on the transition out of the save's own step; the next step is entered after it, so a later item reads it. |
| Notify | No waits. `A__next`: `when: true`, to the next step. Plus one notification rule (section 10.2) on this step's `StageEntered`. | The rule's `when`. | The rule reads `data` as of its `StageEntered` (shapes 6.2), which follows the `DataSet` of every earlier step. |
| Tell other systems | No waits. `A__next` as Notify. Plus one `events` rule (section 10.5) on this step's `StageEntered`. | The rule's `when`. | As Notify. |
| Use a connection: read, write, await | One call wait `A` (section 11). `A__ok`, and `A__failed` with "carry on". | A gate step `A__gate` before `A__run`: `A__go` (`when` = Only when, to `A__run`), `A__skip` (`otherwise`, to the step after `A__run`). Entering a stage opens its waits, so the decision must be made before the call's step is entered. | The call's results are saved by `A__ok`, before the next step is entered. |

`N(…)` is the empty-value rule of section 3.3. An action's directory read `A__groups` (8.6), when it has one, comes before its gate, so the gate's "Only when" can read it.

Each action costs one firing (two for a gated connection action). A turn may fire at most 50 transitions (spec section 3), so a stretch of more than about 45 actions with no call or task between them faults with `firing-limit`. Known limit; core could warn (cheap).

### 2.3 The tasks step

One person wait per task (section 4), each preceded by its membership read `<tk>__members` when the task may ask a group (section 10.4). Its transitions, in declared order:

1. One `<ar>__early` per arrow with `goAsSoonAsTrue`, in arrow order, only when the stage has two or more tasks (section 6.4).
2. `S__answered`: `otherwise: false`, `when: ALL(S)`. It carries every answer into data (section 4.6) and goes to the next step.

`ALL(S)` reads the person waits only:

| Tasks of `S`, in listed order | `ALL(S)` |
|---|---|
| One task `T` | `waits.T.status == 'completed'` |
| `T1` … `Tn` | `waits.T1.status == 'completed' && … && waits.Tn.status == 'completed'` |

The step never leaves by `otherwise` (E-23). The kernel's `otherwise` also needs every call of the stage completed (spec section 2), so a pending membership read would hold an answered task while the directory is slow or down. `ALL(S)` does not read the reads, so the step leaves as soon as every task is answered, and leaving it cancels any read still open (spec section 2: leaving a stage cancels its open waits; 10.4 says what happens to the call).

An early arrow fits beside `ALL(S)` without competing with it: each `<ar>__early` is declared before `S__answered` and requires some task still open (6.4), so when the last answer arrives only `S__answered` can be true, and the arrows are then checked in the routing step. While a task is open, `ALL(S)` is false and only an early transition can fire.

Coverage (spec section 6): the step has no `otherwise`, so its transitions must cover every combination of its waits' outcomes. A combination gives every wait of the step an outcome, so every person wait is completed in it and `ALL(S)` is true, whatever the buttons and whatever each membership read's outcome. The reads have `onFailure: outcome`, so their `ok` and `failed` both count, and `S__answered` covers both. Coverage of button combinations by arrows is core's check (section 14).

### 2.4 The routing step

One transition per arrow, ID = the arrow's ID, in arrow order; "In all other cases" is the `otherwise` transition and is last (E-18). Section 6 gives each `when`. Every transition also removes the visit-scoped data paths of section 3.2.

## 3. Data layout

### 3.1 Top-level paths

Every top-level data key is a path of one segment. Authored values are `v_…` (E-17). Every other key belongs to the compiler and is listed here. No key starts with `$` (K11).

| Path | Kind (JSON, core 2.4) | Set by | Removed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_…` | The value's kind | Question answers (`S__answered`, `<ar>__early`), saves (`A__save`), results and failure saves (`A__ok`, `A__failed`), the two extra answers (`S__answered`, `<ar>__early`) | An expression that gives `optional.none()` in one of those Sets: an empty answer, an empty saved result, a cancelled task's extra answers |
| `requester` | `{type: "user", id}` | `S__answered` of the start stage, both copies (section 10.1) | Never |
| `<tk>__pressed` | string: a `ButtonId` | `S__answered` and `<ar>__early` of the task's stage: the button, or none for a task not completed | Every routing-step transition of the task's stage |
| `<st>__early` | string: an `ArrowId` | `<ar>__early` | Every routing-step transition of the stage |
| `<st>__groups` | list of `{id: {type: "group", id}, members: [{type: "user", id}]}`: the `groups` result of `membersOf@1`, as recorded | The `readOk` transition of each directory read step of the stage, `S__groupsTasks`, `S__groupsRoute` or `A__groups` (each replaces it) | Every routing-step transition of the stage |

`<tk>__pressed` is emitted only for a task with a pressed clause read after the tasks step (an after-response "Only when" or an arrow); `<st>__early` only for a stage with an early arrow; `<st>__groups` only for a stage with a directory read step. Emitting them only when read keeps history free of keys nothing reads (cheap either way). A membership read `<tk>__members` writes no data: the readers of nobody-to-ask read its recorded result (10.4).

What is carried from the tasks step to the routing step: the answers (as `v_…` values), each task's pressed button (`<tk>__pressed`), and the early arrow chosen (`<st>__early`). Who answered is carried only as the author's "Answered by" value; no arrow or condition reads the answerer of this visit except through it.

Why the visit-scoped keys are removed on leaving: the next visit sets `<tk>__pressed` and `<st>__groups` again before anything reads them, and `S__answered` removes `<st>__early` (4.6), so a key left by a visit that did not reach the routing step (a retry) is never read; removal on leaving keeps compiler keys out of the request's data between visits, where a notification or a Tell reading `data` might otherwise see a stale value. The removal is a Set entry with `expr: optional.none()` on each routing transition (removing an absent path does nothing).

### 3.2 Visit-scoped keys

`<tk>__pressed`, `<st>__early` and `<st>__groups` are visit-scoped: set inside one visit of the authored stage and removed when the request leaves it. `requester` and `v_…` are request-scoped.

### 3.3 The empty-value rule `N`

Empty is absent (core 2.4): data never holds `""`, `[]` or `null`. Answers already satisfy it (section 5: `minLength`, and the `<q>__choice` check that refuses an empty multiple choice). Every other write goes through `N(kind, e)`, where `e` is an optional:

| Kind | `N(kind, e)` |
|---|---|
| `text`, `longText` | `e.orValue('') == '' ? optional.none() : e` |
| `multipleChoice`, `people`, `list` | `e.hasValue() && size(e.value()) > 0 ? e : optional.none()` |
| any other | `e` |

### 3.4 The `types` block

The compiler writes `types` (format 3.12; E-23), and `decide` reads JSON into CEL by it (format 5.4): a schema `number` is a double, even for `3`, and an `integer` an int. The publish check type-checks every expression against the same declarations.

| Part | Entry | Schema |
|---|---|---|
| `types.data` | Each authored value `v_…` | The kind schema of 5.1 for the value's kind: the same schema as the question that fills it, or for a saved result the catalogue field's derived schema (shapes 2.3). A number is `{"type": "number"}`, never `integer`. |
| `types.data` | `requester` | The person schema of 5.1 |
| `types.data` | `<tk>__pressed`, `<st>__early` | `{"type": "string"}` |
| `types.data` | `<st>__groups` | The schema of the `groups` result field of `membersOf@1` |
| `types.constants` | Each list `ls_x` | `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": <ROW>}`, where `<ROW>` is `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {<column ID>: <the cell schema of the column's kind>, …}}` with no `required`, because a cell may be "(not given)". The cell schema is the kind schema of 5.1, except text, which is a plain `{"type": "string"}`, so a list may hold any text the author typed, an empty cell included (15.3). So a list reads as a map of row ID to a row object, and a cell's type is its column's. |
| `types.results` | Each `connection` and `op` a call wait names, membership reads included | The schema derived from the catalogue entry's `result` fields (shapes 2.3) |

A reference is `{type, id}` everywhere: in data, in list cells, in results and in literals the compiler writes. The person and group schemas of 5.1 type their `type` property as a string with a `const` (`{"type": "string", "const": "user"}`), so a recorded reference, `request.by` and `actor` have one CEL type, and `REQ`'s `.or()` and `actor == REQ.value()` type-check (E-27). A reference or connection-choice literal is written `dyn({'type': 'group', 'id': '…'})` (8.2): `cel-1` does not type-check `==`, `.or()` or list `+` between a bare map literal and a reference typed by these schemas, and `dyn()` compares by value (E-27).

## 4. Tasks

### 4.1 The person wait

Each task `T` of stage `S` becomes, in each copy of the tasks step:

```
T: person { role: obligation,
            assignees: ASK(T),
            may: MAY(T),
            outcomes: [ { id: <btn>, schema: T.<btn>@1, checks: CHECKS(T, btn), lookups: LOOKUPS(T) } per button, in button order ] }
```

Every task is an obligation (core section 12). `groupRule: "firstAnswerDecides"` is the kernel's own behaviour for one wait with a group among its assignees: the first person to complete it decides. Nothing is emitted for it. A task that may ask a group also gets its membership read `T__members`, declared just before `T` in the same step, and every task gets a nobody-to-ask rule (section 10.4).

### 4.2 Who is asked: `ASK(T)`

`whoIsAsked` is an expression of kind `person`, `group` or `people` (core's `expression.kindMismatch` ensures it). With `O(e)`, the optional form of an expression (section 8):

| Kind of `whoIsAsked` | `ASK(T)` |
|---|---|
| `person` or `group` | `(O(e).hasValue() ? [O(e).value()].filter(r, r.type == 'user' \|\| r.type == 'group') : [])` |
| `people` | `O(e).orValue([]).filter(r, r.type == 'user' \|\| r.type == 'group')` |
| a formula giving one person or group (a map), as core's check accepts it | as `person` |
| a formula giving a list of them | `O(e).orValue([]).filter(r, r.type == 'user' \|\| r.type == 'group')` (when it cannot be empty, `F(f)` with the same filter) |
| absent (Try it only) | `[]` |

`ASK(T)` is always parenthesized, so `ASK(T).filter(…)` (10.4) applies to the whole list.

- A person: a value, a constant `{person}`, a list cell of kind person, the Requester.
- A group: a value, a constant `{group}`, a list cell of kind group.
- Several: a `{people}` constant, a value of kind `people`.
- A formula (E-29): its type says only `map` or `list`, so it is read as one reference or a list of them, and it may give a group. The same rule compiles a Notify's `to` (10.2).
- "People in [group]", an expression whose last step is `{directory: "members"}`: the group itself (E-24). `ASK(T)` drops that step and compiles the rest as of kind `group`, so the group is asked and its membership read `T__members` (10.4) records who is in it. No directory read step is made for it (8.6).
- "If empty, use": `O(ref).or(O(fallback))` (section 8.2). A fallback of another kind is allowed when the kinds are person and group; the wait then asks one person or one group. A group that exists and has nobody in it is not empty (format), so `or` does not apply to it.
- Non-person references: the `filter` drops any reference whose `type` is neither `user` nor `group` (E-17). The kernel also drops them at open (K5); the filter makes the recorded list right without relying on that.

Invariant used by section 10.4: a compiled `ASK(T)` gives `[]`, one or more users, or exactly one group, except from a formula, which may give any list of users and groups. No authored kind gives a mix. "Who is asked" may give a group when it is a group constant, a group value, a list cell of kind group, "people in [group]" (which asks the group), a formula, or has one of these in its "If empty, use". When it can give only people (a person, people, the Requester, through every "If empty, use"), the task gets no membership read and its nobody-to-ask rule has `members: null` (10.4, E-32).

### 4.3 The Requester exclusion: `MAY(T)`

| Task | `MAY(T)` |
|---|---|
| `requesterCanAnswer: true` | `true` |
| `requesterCanAnswer: false` | `!(REQ.hasValue() && actor == REQ.value())`, with `REQ` the Requester of section 8.1 |
| The start task, normal copy | `true` (section 7.4) |

`REQ` reads the data path `requester` of section 10.1 first, so this holds after a connection start that names a Requester and after one that names nobody (then nobody is excluded). The membership lookup at act time decides group membership; `may` only excludes the Requester.

### 4.4 Several tasks in one stage

Every task is a wait of the one tasks step, opened together on entry (spec section 2: entering a stage opens all its waits), with the membership reads of those that may ask a group. `S__answered` fires once all tasks are completed (`ALL(S)`, 2.3), whatever the reads are doing. Early arrows are section 6.4.

### 4.5 Buttons, checks and "Also only when"

Each button is an outcome; its schema is section 5. `CHECKS(T, btn)` is, in this order:

1. `<tk>__requester` on the start task's outcomes, when the start schema has `requester` (section 10.1).
2. For each question of the task's form, in form order: `<q>__hidden`, `<q>__needed`, `<q>__choice`, each where section 5 says.
3. `<btn>__also` when the button has `enabledWhen`:
   ```
   { id: <btn>__also, when: C_check(enabledWhen), message: <messageWhileDisabled, or ""> }
   ```
   `C_check` compiles a condition in the check context (section 8.1). The message is the author's text (E-7); `""` when absent, and the frontend reads back the needs and the condition.

### 4.6 Answers into data, and the two extra answers

`S__answered` and every `<ar>__early` carry the same Set list, in this order: authored values in document order of their first filler, then `<tk>__pressed` keys, then, in a stage with an early arrow, `<st>__early`: `optional.of('<ar>')` on `<ar>__early`, `optional.none()` on `S__answered`. Spec section 2: every expression reads the state before the transition.

Question `q` of task `T` saved as `v`, with `T`'s buttons `b1 … bn`:

```
W(T, q, v) = waits.T.outcome == 'b1' ? waits.T.data.?q
           : waits.T.outcome == 'b2' ? waits.T.data.?q
           …
           : waits.T.outcome == 'bn' ? waits.T.data.?q
           : data.?v
```

- Each read of `waits.T.data` sits in the true branch of a test of one outcome, which is the `.data` guard of spec section 6 (section 14.2 states the reading).
- A completed task writes its answer; an answer left empty, or a hidden question, removes the value ("hidden means empty").
- A task not completed (cancelled by an early arrow) has `outcome == ""`, so the value keeps what it had (E-14).
- **Several questions of one task's form saved as the same value** (E-27): the last answered one in form order is kept, and the value is removed only when all of them are empty. This is what the form shows (core 7.1) and the pattern of alternate pages, where only one page's question is shown. Within each outcome's branch the questions' reads are joined with `.or`, the later question first: `waits.T.outcome == 'b1' ? waits.T.data.?q2.or(waits.T.data.?q1) : …`. The form's checks read the same value the same way, `input.?q2.or(input.?q1)` (5.2), so a check and the saved data agree. A hidden question arrives empty (5.2), so it never hides an answered one.
- Two fillers of one value in one tasks step otherwise (two tasks, or a question and an extra answer below, or two tasks' extra answers) would be two overlapping Sets, which spec section 6 forbids. They are merged into one entry: the later filler in document order wraps the earlier, replacing its fall-through: `W(T2, q2, W(T1, q1, data.?v))`. When two completed tasks fill the same value, the later one in the document wins, not the later one in time (E-23): both are written by one transition, and CEL cannot read when a wait completed. For an extra answer the fall-through is its `optional.none()` branch, so when it is merged after another filler, a task not completed leaves the earlier filler's result instead of emptying the value; alone, it empties the value as below. Example: both tasks of a stage save "Answered by" as `v_by`: `waits.T2.status == 'completed' ? optional.of(waits.T2.by) : (waits.T1.status == 'completed' ? optional.of(waits.T1.by) : optional.none())`.
- **Within one task, its own questions win over its "save which button was pressed" and "save who answered"** for the same value (E-26), whatever their order, even when all the questions are empty. The questions wrap the extra answer: `W(T, q, P)`, with `P` the extra answer's expression (with several questions, their merged read of the bullet above). So a completed task writes the questions' answer (all of them empty removes the value), and only a task not completed falls through to `P`, which leaves the value empty.

The extra answers of task `T`:

| Authored | Set |
|---|---|
| `savesButtonPressedAs: v` | `{path: [v], expr: waits.T.status == 'completed' ? optional.of(waits.T.outcome) : optional.none()}` |
| `savesAnsweredByAs: v` | `{path: [v], expr: waits.T.status == 'completed' ? optional.of(waits.T.by) : optional.none()}` |
| (compiler) pressed clause read later | `{path: [T__pressed], expr: <same as Button pressed>}` |

`outcome`, `status` and `by` need no guard (spec section 2). The "Button pressed" value holds the `ButtonId` string; "Answered by" holds `{type: "user", id}`.

### 4.7 A task cancelled by an early arrow

When `<ar>__early` fires, the tasks still open are cancelled by the stage exit (`WaitCancelled` after `DataSet` in the turn's event order). Their two extra answers and their `<tk>__pressed` are removed for the visit (`status != 'completed'`), and their questions' values keep what they had (`W` falls through to `data.?v`). This is E-14 exactly.

## 5. Forms

### 5.1 The schema per outcome

One module of core owns the outcome schemas; `formState` (core 7) and the compiler both use it, so the form and the published definition refuse the same answers (E-27).

One schema per button, ID `<tk>.<btn>`, version 1. A schema reference has meaning only inside its own definition version; nothing compares schemas across versions, so a fixed version 1 is the simplest choice (cheap). Both copies of a tasks step use the same schemas. Dialect `jsonschema-1` (format section 6); no `$` keyword or property.

```json
{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [ <needed questions of this button that have no Show when, on a page with no Show when> ],
  "properties": { "<q_id>": <kind schema>, … every question of the task, all pages, form order;
                  "requester": <person schema>  (start task only, section 10.1) } }
```

"Needed" is the button's effective set: its `neededToPress` plus every question with `neededForEveryButton` (format).

Kind schemas (core 2.4 for the JSON; E-20 for references):

| Question | Answer kind | Schema |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | text | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":1000}` |
| `longText` | longText | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":20000}` |
| `number` | number | `{"type":"number"}` |
| `yesNo` | yesNo | `{"type":"boolean"}` |
| `date` | date | `{"type":"string","format":"date"}` |
| `choice`, typed in | choice | `{"type":"string","enum":[<ch_ IDs in choice order>]}` |
| `multipleChoice`, typed in | multipleChoice | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","enum":[…]},"uniqueItems":true}` |
| `choice` from a list | choiceFromList | `{"type":"string","enum":[<row_ IDs in row order>]}` |
| `multipleChoice` from a list | multipleChoice of rows | as typed in, with row IDs |
| `choice` from a data source | choiceFromConnection | `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"required":["stored","label"],"properties":{"stored":<schema of the source's stored field>,"label":{"type":"string"}}}` |
| `person` (any choices, or none) | person | `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"required":["type","id"],"properties":{"type":{"type":"string","const":"user"},"id":{"type":"string","format":"directory-object-id"}}}` |
| `group` | group | as person, with `"const":"group"` |
| `choice` from a formula | the formula's item kind (text, number, yesNo, or date for a timestamp) | the item schema: text `{"type":"string"}`, number `{"type":"number"}`, yes/no `{"type":"boolean"}`; a date item and an item with no value kind `{}` |
| `multipleChoice` from a formula | multipleChoice, with items of the formula's item kind (E-28) | `{"type":"array","items":<the item schema as for a choice>,"uniqueItems":true}` |

As built (E-27): `jsonschema-1` has no `minimum`, `maximum` or `minItems` (format section 6), and gains none. A number needs no bounds in its schema: the validator refuses an integer beyond +/-(2^53 - 1) whatever the schema. That a multiple choice holds at least one item is the `<q>__choice` check (5.4). `const` in the person and group schemas is typed (`"type":"string"`), so their CEL type matches `request.by` and `actor` (3.4). A choice question from a list with no rows gets a schema no answer satisfies (`jsonschema-1` refuses an empty `enum`); core reports that list's `rows` as `item.partMissing`.

A choice from a formula (E-28): where the formula's items have no value kind (a list of maps, or of `dyn`), the value has no kind and its item schema is `{}`, so only the `<q>__choice` check (5.4) guards the answer against the choices the formula gives. A date item also gets `{}`: the formula gives timestamps and the answer is checked by `<q>__choice` alone, while the value's kind is date (multiple choice: a list of dates).

Maximum lengths are cheap choices. A choice outside a typed-in or list enum fails the schema and is reported `invalid-data` / `not-a-choice` (core 7.2).

### 5.2 Pages, Show when and hidden questions

A question `q` on page `p` is visible when `V(q) = C_check(p.showWhen) && C_check(q.showWhen)`, each absent part being `true`. If either part exists:

```
{ id: q__hidden, when: V(q) || !has(input.q), message: "" }                 every outcome
{ id: q__needed, when: !V(q) || has(input.q), message: "" }                 outcomes whose effective set has q
```

A needed question with a Show when is not in `required`; `q__needed` enforces it while visible, so "a hidden question is never needed" (format). A hidden question must arrive empty and is never needed (E-14), compiled as conditional checks.

`C_check` reads the form's own answers as the values they are saved as (core 7.1): a value filled by a question of this task's form reads `input.?q` (several such questions: the later one in form order first, `input.?q2.or(input.?q1)`); every other value reads data (section 8.1). Answers given by another task of the same stage in this visit are not yet values (they become values at `S__answered`), as on the page.

### 5.3 Read-only text

A `FormText` compiles to nothing. Its content and Show when are rendered by the page from the version's stored authored form (E-6). It has no answer, so no schema property and no check.

### 5.4 Choices

| `choices.from` | Schema | Check | Lookup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `typedIn` | enum of `ch_` IDs | `q__choice` for `multipleChoice` only: `!has(input.q) \|\| size(input.q) > 0 && [<ch IDs in order>].filter(c, c in input.q) == input.q` (not empty, and in the recorded order, core 2.4) | none |
| `list` | enum of `row_` IDs | as typed in, for `multipleChoice` | none |
| `directory` (`peopleIn`) | person | none | One lookup: the directory's data source (below) |
| `source` | connection choice | none | One lookup |
| `formula` | the item schema of 5.1 (`{}` for a date item or an item with no value kind) | `q__choice`: `!has(input.q) \|\| F.exists(c, c == input.q)`; multiple: `!has(input.q) \|\| size(input.q) > 0 && input.q.all(x, F.exists(c, c == x))`, with `F` the formula in the check context (`F.orValue([])` when the formula can be empty) | none |

One check covers both an empty multiple choice and one out of order (E-27). The kernel's refusal names the check, so core's refusal mapping, which the server also uses, reports `[]` as `invalid-data` / `too-short` and any other failure as `not-a-choice` (core 7.2, 12.3).

E-20 makes directory choices a data source like any other: read live when the form is shown, checked by a lookup when the person acts, on the start form too. The outcome's `lookups` (E-20) carries what the act-time check needs, read only from the definition:

The shape is format 3.3's `Lookup` (shapes 5.2), always written, `[]` when none:

```ts
interface Lookup {
  property: string;                    // the question ID: the outcome data property
  connection: string;                  // e.g. "servicecatalog"; for directory choices, the directory connection
  source: string;                      // "<name>@<version>" of a data source entry
  inputs: { [field: string]: Cel };    // check context (section 8.1); optional.none() leaves the input out
  storedField: string;
  labelField: string;                  // shown on the form; for a person answer nothing but the Ref is recorded
  answer: "item" | "person";           // item: {stored, label}, label replaced by the source's; person: {type: "user", id: <stored>}
}
```

`LOOKUPS(T)` lists one entry per question of `T` whose choices come from `directory` or `source`, in form order, on every outcome of `T` (the property exists on every outcome's schema). For `directory`: `connection` is the catalogue's `directoryConnection`, `source` its group-members data source `groupMembers@1` (the entry `directory.groupMembers@1` in `contract/fixtures/catalogue.json`) with input `group` = `O(peopleIn)`, `storedField: "id"`, `labelField: "name"`, `answer: "person"`. For `source`: the authored `source` split into connection and `name@version`, `inputs` from the authored inputs (an `Expression` through `O`, a `Template` through section 8.4), `storedField`, `labelField`, `answer: "item"`.

Shapes 5.3 defines the act-time `get`; for a person answer the engine calls `get(source, inputs, storedField, answer.id)` and keeps the answer as given when found. Refusals are unchanged: `choice-unknown`, `source-unavailable`. The page's choices call is `getChoices` in `contract/runtime-api.md`; it names the question, and the server finds this lookup. A lookup's origin is a field key, `outcome:<wait>/<btn>#/lookups/<n>` (12.2).

## 6. Arrows

### 6.1 The condition of an arrow, `A(ar)`

Compiled in the route context (section 8.1), where a pressed clause reads `<tk>__pressed`:

| `when` | `A(ar)` |
|---|---|
| `buttonPressed` on `btn` of task `T` | `data.?T__pressed.orValue('') == 'btn'` |
| `condition` | `C(condition)` |
| `inAllOtherCases` | the transition is `otherwise: true`, `when: null` |
| `whenDone` | `true` |
| with "+ only when" | `(<the above>) && (C(onlyWhen))` |

### 6.2 The routing step

In a stage with no early arrow, the transition for arrow `ar` is:

```
ar: when A(ar)  set REMOVE(S)  -> TARGET(ar)
```

`REMOVE(S)` is one `{path: [k], expr: optional.none()}` per visit-scoped key of the stage (section 3.2), in the order `<tk>__pressed` (task order), `<st>__early`, `<st>__groups`. `TARGET(ar)` is section 7.3.

In a stage with early arrows (section 6.4), the chosen early arrow must win whatever the order:

```
ar (an early arrow):  when data.?S__early.orValue('') == 'ar' || (!has(data.S__early) && (A(ar)))
ar (any other arrow): when !has(data.S__early) && (A(ar))
"In all other cases": otherwise (fires only when no other transition is enabled; when S__early is set, its arrow is)
```

`A(ar)` is in parentheses unless it is a simple term, so an `||` inside it cannot bind with the `&&` before it (E-27).

### 6.3 Coverage and arrows that can never be used

- The routing step has no waits, so the kernel's coverage rule (spec section 6) has one empty combination and is met by any transition (section 14.2 states the reading). The tasks step is covered by `S__answered` (2.3).
- Coverage of every combination of buttons, one per task, is core's check (`stage.buttonHasNowhereToGo`, `stage.combinationHasNowhereToGo`, both To do). A published workflow therefore has an arrow for every combination; a condition-only routing step can still find nothing that fits, and the kernel's stuck check flags it (`nothing-fits`, E-19).
- An arrow that can never be used compiles like any other. Core reports it as a To do (`arrow.neverUsed`, E-25), only where that is provable; it does not stop Try it. The kernel has no check against a transition that never fires.

### 6.4 "Don't wait for the others"

Only in a stage with two or more tasks. In the tasks step, before `S__answered`, one transition per early arrow, in arrow order:

```
ar__early: when (waits.T1.status == 'completed' || … || waits.Tn.status == 'completed')
             && (waits.T1.status == 'open' || … || waits.Tn.status == 'open')
             && A_tasks(ar)
           set [ <the Set list of 4.6, ending with {path: [S__early], expr: optional.of('ar')}> ]
           -> <the step after the tasks step>
```

- "Checked after every answer": transitions are level-triggered at the end of every turn (spec section 2); the first clause stops the arrow firing in the turn that opens the tasks, before anyone has answered.
- "Taken as soon as it fits": the second clause hands the last answer to `S__answered`, so that when everyone has answered the arrows are checked from the top in the routing step, as for any other arrow.
- "Cancels the open tasks": leaving the tasks step cancels the waits still open (spec section 2), and 4.7 applies.
- `A_tasks` is `A` in the tasks context: a pressed clause reads `waits.T.outcome == 'btn'`, and a value filled in this tasks step reads its Set expression (`W`, section 4.6), so the arrow sees the answers given so far exactly as the routing step would.
- "Its destination must survive the after-response actions": the arrow is chosen here and recorded in `S__early`; the after-response actions run; the routing step takes the recorded arrow whatever the actions saved (6.2). It is not re-evaluated.

### 6.5 The pressed clause

| Where | Compiles to |
|---|---|
| Tasks step (early arrows) | `waits.T.outcome == 'btn'` |
| After-response actions' "Only when", arrows | `data.?T__pressed.orValue('') == 'btn'` |
| Anywhere else | Not legal (core's `clause.pressedOutsideStage`) |

## 7. Send-backs and the second status

### 7.1 What "sends back" means

An arrow from `S` to `T` sends back when `T` dominates `S` in the authored stage graph: every route from the start stage to `S` passes through `T` (E-14). Nodes are the working stages and endings; edges are the arrows with a `goTo`; the root is `start.stage`. `T == S` dominates, so an arrow to its own stage sends back. An arrow out of a stage no route reaches does not send back. The compiler uses core's `facts` function (`sendsBack`), so the editor and the compiled definition agree. The start stage dominates every reachable stage, so every arrow into it sends back.

### 7.2 Two copies

A stage gets a second copy, the sent-back chain, when some arrow sends back to it and either it has an `ifSentBackStatus` that differs from its `status`, or it is the start stage. An absent `ifSentBackStatus` means "show the usual status" (format: it is the status shown *instead*), so it never makes a second copy by itself; 15.7's Deploy relies on this. The second copy is the whole chain with every engine stage's local name suffixed `Back` (`tasksBack`, `routeBack`, `groupsTasksBack`, `groupsRouteBack`, `groupsBack`, `runBack`, `gateBack`); wait, transition and check local IDs are the same in both copies. Each copy's person waits get their own nobody-to-ask rules, because a rule ID carries the stage (10.4).

| Copy | Status of every step |
|---|---|
| Normal | `status`, or `null` |
| Sent back | `ifSentBackStatus`, else `status`, else `null` |

A request that arrives by a sending-back arrow stays in the second copy until it leaves the authored stage: every transition of a copy targets the next step of the same copy. So "Needs changes" stays on screen through the arrival actions, the tasks and the after-response actions.

### 7.3 Which arrows target which copy

`TARGET(ar)` is:

| Arrow | Target |
|---|---|
| To an ending | The ending |
| Sends back, and the target has a second copy | The entry of the target's sent-back chain |
| Anything else | The entry of the target's normal chain |

The routing steps of both copies of `S` carry the same transitions with the same targets.

### 7.4 The start stage

- `root.initial` is the start stage's normal tasks step, `<start>__tasks`; `start` names its one wait, `<start>__tasks.<tk>` (spec section 2: a person wait of `root.initial`). Core's `start.notOneTask` ensures there is exactly one task.
- The normal chain of the start stage has no arrival actions and no directory read before the tasks: a new request begins at the form (E-14), and the start turn enters `root.initial` directly.
- The sent-back chain has all steps, so the arrival actions run only when a request is sent back (E-14). Its tasks step's wait is an ordinary person wait (it is not `start`), with `MAY` from `requesterCanAnswer`. The normal copy's `may` is `true`: the starter is the Requester by definition.
- Status: the normal chain carries `status` (normally none). A start stage with a connection action in "After they respond" needs one (E-16); core's `start.needsStatus` makes it a To do, and the compiler puts it on every step of the normal chain, so the request is seen (or stuck) there with that status.
- The start wait's assignees are evaluated and recorded in the start turn but not checked (spec section 2). Its nobody-to-ask rule (10.4) cannot match in the start turn: the match is for open waits at the end of a turn (shapes 5.5), and the start wait is completed by then. If the start task may ask a group, its membership read is opened and cancelled in the start turn, never sent, and dropped (spec section 2).

## 8. Expressions

### 8.1 Contexts

| Context | Where | A value `v` reads as | Requester | Pressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| data | Arrival actions, after-response actions, routing step, gates, call args, directory reads, rules | `data.?v` | `REQ` | `data.?T__pressed.orValue('') == 'btn'` (after-response and arrows only) |
| tasks | `assignees`, early transitions, the Sets of the tasks step | `data.?v`, except a value filled in this tasks step reads its Set expression (`W`) in early transitions | `REQ` | `waits.T.outcome == 'btn'` |
| check | `may`, checks, lookup inputs | `input.?q` for a value filled by this task's form (several questions: the later one first, `.or`, 4.6); else `data.?v` | Start task: `RQ0` (below); else `REQ` | not legal |
| sent | A binding's `when` and `data` | not legal (format: a binding reads only `sent`) | not legal | not legal |

`REQ`, the Requester (shapes 3.4): `data.?requester.or(request.by.type == 'user' ? optional.of(request.by) : optional.none())`. It is the Requester shapes 5.5's nobody-to-ask match uses. The fallback to `request.by` gives the Requester of a person's start, which records no `requester` (10.1); it also covers the start turn before `S__answered` and a start turn whose firings faulted and were rolled back.

`RQ0`, the Requester on the start form, where a connection may supply it in the same act: `input.?requester.or(REQ)`, without `input.?requester` when the start schema has no `requester`.

A lookup's inputs read `request` (the Requester's `request.by`, "Started on"'s `request.at`): spec v2.18 declares `request` in a lookup's scope (E-27; format section 4). They never read `request.id`, which spec v2.19 refuses at publish (E-28, 14.2): on the start form the choices are listed before a request exists.

### 8.2 Each expression form: `O(e)`, an optional

Every reference is read through optional syntax, so the spec section 6 path check passes without any presence analysis: a path that may be absent is read only through `.?` or `has()`.

| Form | `O(e)` |
|---|---|
| `{value: v}` | per context (8.1) |
| `{value: v, steps: [{column: c}]}`, `v` a list choice of list `L` | `(O(v).hasValue() ? L[O(v).value()].?c : optional.none())` |
| `{value: g, steps: [{directory: "members"}]}` | `(O(g).hasValue() ? optional.of(data.?S__groups.orValue([]).filter(e, e.id == O(g).value())[0].members) : optional.none())`, reading the read made just before this step (8.6) |
| `{request: "requester"}` | per context (8.1) |
| `{request: "startedOn"}` | `optional.of(asDate(timestamp(request.at)))`: the start day, `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC |
| `ifEmptyUse: f` on either reference | `O(<reference without ifEmptyUse>).or(O(f))` |
| Constant | `optional.of(<literal>)`, literals below |
| Sentence | `optional.of(C(sentence))` |
| Formula | `(P(f) ? optional.of(F(f)) : optional.none())`, with `asDate` applied where the result is used as a date (8.4) |

Steps apply left to right; a `members` step after a `column` step reads the group in the cell. A column step on a row ID that is not in the version's list is an expression error (`no-such-key`); it cannot happen for a list choice answered in that version, because the schema's enum is that version's rows.

Literals:

| Constant | CEL |
|---|---|
| `{text}`, `{date}`, `{choice}`, `{row}`, `{button}`, `{failureCode}` | a single-quoted string; `\`, `'` and control characters escaped |
| `{number}` | a double literal: an integral number gets `.0` (`3.0`) |
| `{yesNo}` | `true` / `false` |
| `{choices}` | `['ch_a', 'ch_b']` in the question's choice order |
| `{person}`, `{group}` | `dyn({'type': 'user', 'id': '<directoryId>'})`, `dyn({'type': 'group', 'id': '<directoryId>'})` (E-20, E-27; format answer 2) |
| `{people}` | a list of person literals |
| `{connectionChoice}` | `dyn({'stored': <string or double>, 'label': '<label>'})` (E-27) |

A reference or connection-choice literal is wrapped in `dyn()` (E-27): `cel-1` does not type-check `==`, `.or()` or list `+` between a bare map literal and a value typed by the person, group or connection-choice schema, and `dyn()` lets them compare by value (3.4).
| `{weekday}` | only as the right side of `date.isOnWeekday`: an integer 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday), CEL's `getDayOfWeek` numbering |

### 8.3 The condition builder: `C(sentence)`

A `Condition` that is a `Formula` compiles to `P(f) && (F(f))` (8.4); `C` below is for a `Sentence`. `allOf` joins clauses with `&&`, `anyOf` with `||`, each clause in parentheses; a list of one clause is that clause. Below, `L = O(left)`, `R = O(right)`, `Ri` the i-th expression of a list right side, `L?` stands for `L.hasValue()` and `L!` for `L.value()`.

An empty value makes a clause not true (E-22), except the empty words (`isEmpty`, `areEmpty`) and the negative words (is not, does not contain, is not one of, is not in, do not include, does not include), which are true. So every positive word tests each side it reads, and each negative word is `!` of its positive word. In a list comparison (is one of, is not one of, includes any of, includes all of), an item of the right side that is empty is ignored (E-24): "is one of" and "includes any of" are not true when every item is empty, and "includes all of" is then true when the left side has a value.

| Words | CEL |
|---|---|
| `text.is` / `text.isNot` | `L? && R? && L! == R!` / `!(…)` |
| `text.contains` / `text.doesNotContain` | `L? && R? && L!.contains(R!)` / `!(…)` |
| `text.startsWith` | `L? && R? && L!.startsWith(R!)` |
| `text.isFilled` / `text.isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `number.is` / `isNot` / `isMoreThan` / `isLessThan` / `isAtLeast` / `isAtMost` | `L? && R? && L! == R!` (`!(…)`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`) |
| `number.isFilled` / `isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `yesNo.isYes` / `yesNo.isNo` | `L.orValue(false)` / `!L.orValue(true)` |
| `yesNo.isFilled` / `isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `date.is` / `isBefore` / `isAfter` / `isOnOrBefore` / `isOnOrAfter` | `L? && R? && L! == R!` (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`): a `YYYY-MM-DD` string compares as the date |
| `date.isOnWeekday` | `L? && date(L!).getDayOfWeek() == <n>` |
| `date.isFilled` / `isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `choice.is` / `isNot` | `L? && R? && L! == R!` / `!(…)`; for a connection choice `L!.stored == R!.stored` (format: conditions compare `stored`) |
| `choice.isOneOf` / `isNotOneOf` | `L? && ((R1? && L! == R1!) \|\| … \|\| (Rn? && L! == Rn!))` / `!(…)` (`.stored` as above) |
| `choice.isFilled` / `isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `person.is` / `isNot` | `L? && R? && L! == R!` / `!(…)` |
| `person.isOneOf` | `L? && ((R1? && L! == R1!) \|\| … \|\| (Rn? && L! == Rn!))` |
| `person.isIn` / `isNotIn`, right a group | `L? && R? && data.?S__groups.orValue([]).exists(e, e.id == R! && e.members.exists(m, m == L!))` / `!(…)`, reading the read just before this step (8.6) |
| `person.isIn` / `isNotIn`, right people | `L? && R? && R!.exists(m, m == L!)` / `!(…)` |
| `person.isFilled` / `isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `people.include` / `doNotInclude`, left a group | `L? && R? && data.?S__groups.orValue([]).exists(e, e.id == L! && e.members.exists(m, m == R!))` / `!(…)` |
| `people.include` / `doNotInclude`, left people | `L? && R? && L!.exists(m, m == R!)` / `!(…)` |
| `people.areFilled` / `areEmpty`, left a group | `L? && data.?S__groups.orValue([]).exists(e, e.id == L! && size(e.members) > 0)` / `!(…)` |
| `people.areFilled` / `areEmpty`, left people | `L? && size(L!) > 0` / `!(…)` |
| `list.includes` / `doesNotInclude` | `L? && R? && R! in L!` / `!(…)` |
| `list.includesAnyOf` | `L? && ((R1? && R1! in L!) \|\| … \|\| (Rn? && Rn! in L!))` |
| `list.includesAllOf` | `L? && (!R1? \|\| R1! in L!) && … && (!Rn? \|\| Rn! in L!)` |
| `list.isFilled` / `isEmpty` | `L?` / `!L?` |
| `{pressed: btn}` | section 6.5 |

`O(left)` and `O(right)` are written out at each use; a long reference appears more than once in the CEL text. `TransitionFired.reads` lists each path once (E-20), so the repetition costs text only.

Functions the compiler writes: `date`, `timestamp`, `asDate`, `getDayOfWeek()` with no time-zone argument, `string(double)`, `size`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `in`, `dyn` (8.2), the macros `exists`, `all` and `filter`, and the optional methods. Each must be in `cel-1`'s written-out function list (format section 5; E-23). `getDayOfWeek()`, `string(double)` and the optional methods `or`, `hasValue` and `value` were not exercised in the trial (format section 12).

### 8.4 Formulas and templates

Formula `F(formula)`: the text is CEL of profile `cel-1`; each chip is replaced, everything else is kept byte for byte. Ranges of check errors are mapped back to the authored text, as the wrapper already does for its renames.

| Chip | Replaced by (data context; the other contexts substitute as in 8.1) |
|---|---|
| `{{v_x}}`, `v_x` of kind date | `date(data.?v_x.value())` |
| `{{v_x}}`, any other kind | `data.?v_x.value()` |
| `{{request.requester}}` | `REQ.value()` (8.1); `RQ0.value()` on the start form (E-27) |
| `{{request.startedOn}}` | `date(asDate(timestamp(request.at)))`: 00:00 UTC of the start day |
| `{{sent.a.b}}` (binding only) | `sent.?a.?b.value()` |

An empty chip. `P(f)` is the guard of formula `f`: the conjunction, in chip order, of the presence test of each chip's read in its context (`data.?v_x.hasValue()`, `input.?q.hasValue()`, `REQ.hasValue()`, `sent.?a.?b.hasValue()`); `true`, and left out, when `f` has no chip that can be empty. A formula used as a condition compiles to `P(f) && (F(f))`, so an empty value makes it not true, as for a sentence clause (E-22). A formula used as a value (a Save, a call or lookup input, a Tell value, a Notify part, a binding answer) compiles to `P(f) ? optional.of(F(f)) : optional.none()`, so it is empty when a value it reads is empty. Inside the guard, `.?v_x.value()` cannot fail, and it still passes the publish path check. Core flags "may be empty" only where an empty value stops or silently drops something (E-22): who is asked, a notification's recipient, a directory group, a needed connection input. A formula feeding a needed connection input is therefore flagged there; nowhere else does an empty chip fault a request.

A formula's result is written to data for a Save a value, and passed on as a call or lookup input or a Tell value. Its kind is core's (`checkFormula`). A date chip is a timestamp. Where a formula's result is used as a date (a Save into a date value, a date call input, a date Tell value, the other side of a date clause) and its type is a timestamp, the compiler applies `asDate`: `asDate(F(f))` is the `YYYY-MM-DD` string of that timestamp in UTC (E-23). `days(n)` turns an int into a duration, so the authored format's example `{{v}} < {{request.startedOn}} + days(3)` is `cel-1`.

`has()` on a field of a chip, `has({{v_x}}.f)`, compiles to an optional read of that field, `O.?f.hasValue()` with `O` the chip's optional read (`data.?v_x.?f.hasValue()`) (E-27). Written literally it would be `has(<read>.value().f)`, which the library refuses as a `has()` argument. `checkFormula` makes the same rewrite, so the two type the same text. It works where the chip's value has fields (a person, a group, a connection choice, a field group); on a chip whose value is text it is refused (E-28).

Four points the rules above leave open, as built (E-27):

1. A clause whose list right side is empty (`right: []`) has no rule; core reports it as `item.partMissing` (`<part>.<n>.right`).
2. A formula whose result is itself an optional stays an optional: `(P(f) ? (F(f)) : optional.none())`, never `optional.of(<an optional>)`. A result of `optional.none()` leaves the value empty.
3. A chip used twice is tested once in `P(f)`.
4. `asDate` is applied to any formula value whose type is a timestamp, not only in date places: check (`formula.kindMismatch`) already refuses a timestamp anywhere a date is not taken.

Template, three targets:

| Target | Compiles to |
|---|---|
| Notify message | `parts` (section 10.2): `{text}` for a string, `{value: O(e), kind}` for an expression. The notifier renders by kind, names included, and an empty value as nothing. |
| Tell value, call input, binding answer | One CEL string: the pieces joined with `+`, a string as a literal, an expression through `TXT(e)` below. |
| Form text | Nothing (5.3). |

`TXT(e)` by the expression's kind: text, long text, date: `O(e).orValue('')`; number: `O(e).hasValue() ? string(O(e).value()) : ''`; yes/no: `O(e).hasValue() ? (O(e).value() ? 'Yes' : 'No') : ''`; choice: `O(e).hasValue() ? {<ch>: '<label>', …}[O(e).value()] : ''`, the map holding the question's choices or the task's buttons; a saved failure code (E-29): `O(e).hasValue() ? {'<code>': '<label>', …}[?O(e).value()].orValue(O(e).value()) : ''`, the map holding the failure codes of every action that saves its code as the value, with the catalogue's labels at publish (the first action in document order gives a label two actions disagree on), and a code the map does not hold shown as the code; a constant `{choice}` or `{button}` is its label, `{failureCode}` its code; list choice: the shown column's cell rendered by `TXT` of the column's kind (E-27), with `L[O(e).value()].?<shownColumn>` as the cell's optional, inside `O(e).hasValue() ? … : ''`; for a text column that is `O(e).hasValue() ? L[O(e).value()].?<shownColumn>.orValue('') : ''` (the row ID when no shown column); connection choice: `O(e).hasValue() ? O(e).value().label : ''`; person, group: `O(e).hasValue() ? O(e).value().id : ''`. A person renders as its directory ID because `decide` reads no live data; names are the notifier's. Multiple choice, people, list and field group have no text rule yet (how each item renders, and the separator), so such a template is a To do (14.3). An empty value renders as nothing (E-22). `Yes`/`No` and `string(double)` formatting are cheap choices; `string(double)` was not in the trial.

Several of these rules are ternaries, so when a template has more than one piece, each expression piece that is not a simple term (a read with method calls after it, such as `data.?v.orValue('')`) is written in parentheses before the pieces are joined with `+` (E-27): `'Helpdesk ' + (O(e).hasValue() ? string(O(e).value()) : '')`. Without them `'a' + x ? y : ''` would parse as `('a' + x) ? y : ''`. A template of one piece is written bare. A plain value that nothing fills renders as empty text.

### 8.5 "If empty, use", lists and absent values

- "If empty, use" is `.or()` on optionals (8.2): it applies only when the value is absent, never to a group with nobody in it.
- A list step is a constant lookup: `ls_x[<row ID>].?<column>` gives an optional, so a cell "(not given)" is empty and "If empty, use" applies.
- Every value is read through `.?` (references) or `.?…value()` under the guard `P(f)` (formula chips). No compiled expression reads a path the kernel could find absent without optional syntax.

### 8.6 Directory steps: the recorded read

A `members` step, a `person.isIn` / `isNotIn` against a group, and the `people` words on a group need a group's members, and `decide` reads no live data. The exception is "people in [group]" under "Who is asked" and in a Notify's `to`: it names the group itself and needs no read here (4.2, 10.2; E-24). Each step that uses one is preceded by its own recorded read call, in its own engine stage, placed just before it (E-23). So the read sees a group saved earlier in the same section, by an earlier action or by the tasks step. Two other directory uses are not here: the membership read for nobody to ask sits beside its task (10.4), and directory choices are a data source (5.4).

| Step that uses one | Uses one when | Read step `X` | Read wait | Read transition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| An action `A` (arrival or after-response) | Its "Only when", an input, `save` or a told value (not `to`, which compiles like `ASK`, 10.2) | `A__groups`, before `A__gate` or `A__run` | `A__read` | `A__readOk` |
| Tasks step | A Show when, "Also only when" or lookup input of the stage's forms uses one, or an early arrow does. Not "Who is asked": "people in [group]" there asks the group (4.2, E-24) | `S__groupsTasks` | `S__read` | `S__readOk` |
| Routing step | An arrow's condition or "+ only when" | `S__groupsRoute` | `S__read` | `S__readOk` |

The read step, in each copy, with `I` the item it is attached to (`A` or `S`):

```
X:   status: <copy's status>
  waits:
    I__read: call { connection: <directoryConnection>, op: membersOf@1, effect: read, onFailure: fault,
                    keyScope: activation, idempotencyKey: null,
                    args: { groups: <GROUPS> } }
  transitions:
    I__readOk: when waits.I__read.outcome == 'ok'
               set [ { path: [S__groups], expr: optional.of(waits.I__read.data.groups) } ]  -> <the step it serves>
```

`<GROUPS>` is the list of every group the served step names, each as `(O(g).hasValue() ? [O(g).value()] : [])`, joined with `+`. It is evaluated over data as the read step is entered. Duplicates are harmless. Every read step of a stage writes the stage's one key `<st>__groups`, replacing the last; each step reads the read made just before it.

- When the list is empty at run time, the read is still made, with `groups: []`. Gating it would need one more step per read; cheap to add later.
- Failure: the directory clearly refuses (`group-not-found`): `onFailure: fault`, so the request faults at `X.I__read` with `call-failed` and the operation's failure code in the fault's params; its origin is the part that named the group (section 12). Reason `action-failed`, as for every fault from a failed call (E-23; 12.4). Retry re-enters `X`, so the group is read again. The directory unreachable: the call stays pending (a connector never reports "don't know" as failed), and the `call-overdue` alert reaches the workflow admins after the operation's `expectedWithinSeconds` (shapes 4.7).
- A group answered on a form and read by the same form's Show when, "Also only when" or lookup input, or by an early arrow of that tasks step, cannot be read: the read is made before the tasks step opens. Core makes it the To do `group.readInSameStep` (14.3, E-26). It does not cover a question's "people in" group (`choices.peopleIn`), which names the group and needs no recorded read, nor formulas; on the start form, conditions stay with `start.directoryInCondition` (E-27).

## 9. Lists, statuses, endings

- **Lists** become constants named by the list ID: `ls_x: { <row ID>: { <column ID>: <cell JSON> } }`. Cells use core 2.4's JSON (a person cell is `{type: "user", id}`); a cell "(not given)" is an absent key. Every list is emitted, used or not. Its column kinds give its `types.constants` entry (3.4). Versioned with the definition, as the format says.
- **Statuses**: every authored status, in authored order, as `{id, label: <words>, color: <colour>}`. `StageEntered.status` records `{id, label}`, so the words at the request's version are what history keeps.
- **Endings**: `{id: <st>, final: true, status: <status or null>, waits: [], transitions: []}`. One copy only. `RequestClosed.stage` names the authored ending.

## 10. Bindings, things told, notifications

### 10.1 The Requester and the start task

E-16, E-17, E-20 and shapes 3.4, with the Requester as a reference (E-20):

- When some binding names a `requester`, every start outcome's schema gains the property `requester` (person schema), and every start outcome gains, first, the check

  ```
  { id: <start task>__requester, when: actor.type == 'connection' || !has(input.requester), message: "" }
  ```

- The start stage's `S__answered`, in both copies, sets, last among the authored values (shapes 3.4):

  ```
  { path: [requester], expr: (waits.T.outcome == 'b1' ? waits.T.data.?requester : … : optional.none())
                               .or(data.?requester) }
  ```

  without the first part when no binding names a Requester (then the expression is `data.?requester`). A connection's start sets the named person, or nothing. A person's start sets nothing: `REQ` falls back to `request.by` (8.1). A person who resubmits on the sent-back copy cannot change it: the check refuses a person's `requester`, so the Set keeps the value.
- `{request: "requester"}` is `REQ` (8.1) everywhere except the start task's checks, where it is `RQ0`, so "Notify Requester", "asked of the Requester" and "can't answer their own request" hold for connection starts. With nobody named it is empty, and "If empty, use" applies (E-14).

### 10.2 Notify

One notification rule per Notify action, ID = the action ID:

```
{ id: <act>,
  on:   { event: "StageEntered", element: <act>__run }        // one copy
        { event: "StageEntered", element: null }               // two copies: when starts with event.stage in ['<act>__run', '<act>__runBack']
  when: C(onlyWhen), or "true"
  send: { message: { parts: [ {text: "…"} | {value: O(e), kind: <kind>} … ] },
          to: [ { type: "expr", expr: ASK-like list of the `to` expression } ] } }
```

`to` compiles like `ASK` (4.2): a person, a group, several, the Requester, a formula giving one or a list of them (E-29); "people in [group]" names the group, which the notifier expands when it sends, so `to` needs no directory read step. A part's `value` may give `optional.none()`, which the notifier renders as nothing (E-22). A part that reads a saved failure code is `{value: O(e).hasValue() ? optional.of(<its label, as TXT gives it>) : optional.none(), kind: "text"}`: the label, because the authored source a page renders a choice from holds no failure codes (E-29). Context: `data` as of the `StageEntered` (shapes 6.2), so earlier saves are seen and later ones are not (E-14).

### 10.3 The built-in notifications

Two built-in rules, after the authored rules (format 3.6):

| Rule | `on` | `when` | `send` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_task` | `{event: "WaitOpened", element: null}` | `event.kind == 'person' && event.role == 'obligation'` | `{message: {words: "task.assigned"}, to: [{type: "expr", expr: "event.assignees"}]}` |
| `n_stopped` | `{event: "Stuck", element: null}` | `true` | `{message: {words: "request.stuck"}, to: [{type: "workflowAdmins"}]}` |

`n_stopped` fires for every stuck reason, `nobody-to-ask` included; the notifier fills the reason from `event.reason` (E-21). There is no `n_noAssignee`, no `task.nobodyToAsk` message and no rule field for a stuck reason. `n_task` does not fire for a membership read: its `event.kind` is `call`. `start.refused` is not a rule: the inbound handler raises it (shapes 3.7). Known limit of `n_task`: a group is expanded by the notifier when it sends, so a Requester who is in an asked group and may not answer is told too. A per-task rule reading the recorded members would fix it (cheap, later).

### 10.4 Nobody to ask (E-23; shapes 5.5)

**The membership read.** For every task `T` whose "Who is asked" may give a group (4.2), and no other (a task asked only people, by kind, gets none, E-32), each copy of its tasks step declares, just before `T`'s person wait, the call wait

```
T__members: call { connection: <directoryConnection>, op: membersOf@1, effect: read, onFailure: outcome,
                   keyScope: activation, idempotencyKey: null,
                   args: { groups: ASK(T).filter(r, r.type == 'group') } }
```

- It is opened with the task, so the task is open and visible at once and a slow directory does not delay asking (E-23). It is made even when `ASK(T)` gives no group this time (`groups: []`).
- No transition reads it, and `ALL(S)` does not wait for it (2.3). When the step is left first, the read is cancelled and dropped quietly, sent or not: a read cannot act outside, so it is not kept and raises no `call-outcome-unknown` alert (E-24; shapes 4.8).
- `failed` (the directory refuses, `group-not-found`) is an outcome, not a fault, so the request does not fault. A failed read contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts (E-24).
- The directory unreachable: the read stays pending, the task stays open and can be answered (the act-time membership lookup is a separate thing, shapes 5.1), and `call-overdue` reaches the workflow admins after `expectedWithinSeconds`.

**The rule.** The `nobodyToAsk` block (format 3.9) has one rule per person wait the compiler emits, both copies included, in stage then wait order:

```
{ id: "<S__tasks>.<T>__nobody",
  wait: "<S__tasks>.<T>",
  members: "<S__tasks>.<T>__members", or null when "Who is asked" can never give a group,
  excludeRequester: <true when requesterCanAnswer is false> }
```

with `S__tasksBack` in place of `S__tasks` for the sent-back copy. The rule holds no CEL and no message. The match is shapes 5.5's (E-24): an open obligation matches when nobody can answer it. Who can answer is the people asked directly (the users among its recorded assignees) plus the recorded members of the groups asked (as listed by the read in the same activation), minus the Requester when `excludeRequester` (the Requester as `REQ`, 8.1). A read whose result is `failed` contributes nobody from its groups; a person asked directly still counts. While the read has no result, a wait that asks a group does not match. So a task asked only of the Requester, who may not answer, matches with or without a read.

- It reads only recorded events: the task's recorded assignees and the read's recorded `WaitCompleted`. The match is recorded nowhere; the notifier, the publisher, the `requests` projection and core's story each work it out the same way, so they agree (E-20).
- The stuck reason `nobody-to-ask` is the match (12.4). `n_stopped` sends `request.stuck` with that reason; the publisher publishes `request.stuck@1` and, when the wait closes or Retry re-reads, `request.unstuck@1`.
- No match for a wait completed in the turn that opened it: the match is for open waits at the end of a turn.
- Retry re-enters the tasks step, so the group is read again (12.4).

### 10.5 Tell other systems

One `events` rule per Tell action (shapes 7.3), ID = the action ID:

```
{ id: <act>, on: <as Notify>, when: C(onlyWhen) or "true",
  told: { id: <told ID>, words: <its words at this version> },
  values: { <name>: <O(e), or the template string as optional.of(…)> } }
```

A value that gives `optional.none()` leaves its name out (shapes 7.4). Each value is sent as the request holds it (E-22), the data's own JSON (core 2.4): a choice from a connection as `{stored, label}`, a person as `{type, id}`, a typed-in choice as its choice ID, a saved failure code as the code (E-29). A template value is the string of 8.4. `told.id` must be a `thingsTold` entry (core's `item.brokenReference`). The built-in outbound events carry IDs, status and reason only; the compiler emits nothing for them.

### 10.6 Starts when: the `triggers` block

One entry per binding, in `startsWhen` order (shapes 3.1):

```
{ id: <sw>, connection: <trigger's connection>, event: "<name>@<version>",
  when: CS(onlyWhen) or "true",
  outcome: <button>, or the start task's one button when absent,
  data: { <q>: WRAP(q, OS(answer)) per answered question, requester: OS(requester) when given } }
```

- Sent context (8.1): `OS({sentField: "a.b"})` is `sent.?a.?b`; a constant is `optional.of(<literal>)`; a formula is `(P(f) ? optional.of(F(f)) : optional.none())` with `{{sent.…}}` chips (8.4); a `SentTemplate` is `optional.of(<string>)` with absent fields as `''`. `CS` is `C` over sent fields, with the same words. A sent field of kind person is already `{type: "user", id}` (core 6.3).
- `WRAP(q, e)` (E-20): when `q` or its page has a Show when, `V_sent(q) ? e : optional.none()`, where `V_sent` is the Show when with each value filled by a start-form question replaced by that question's mapping (with several start-form questions saved as one value, their mappings merged as 4.6 merges their answers, the later question in form order first: `later.or(earlier)`; a question the binding does not map counts as `optional.none()`), the Requester by the binding's requester mapping, and every other value as `optional.none()` (no request exists yet). A mapping whose question's Show when reads "Started on" has no rule: the binding has no request time. Core makes it a To do (E-23; 14.3).
- A binding with a To do is left out in Try it mode (core: `startFrom` refuses `unfinished`).

## 11. Connection actions

### 11.1 The call wait

Action `A` in its step `A__run` (and `A__runBack`):

```
A: call { connection: <operation's connection>, op: "<name>@<version>",
          args: { <field>: O(e) or optional.of(<template string>) … per filled input },
          effect: <read for sort read; write for write and await>,
          onFailure: <fault for "stuck"; outcome for "carryOn">,
          keyScope, idempotencyKey: <11.3> }
```

An argument whose expression gives `optional.none()` is left out (K8). An await is a write call to the kernel (shapes 4.1); the recorded op names the catalogue entry, so history says it was an await.

### 11.2 Results and failures

```
A__ok:     when waits.A.outcome == 'ok'
           set [ { path: [<v>], expr: N(<kind>, waits.A.data.?<field>) } per saveResults entry, in field order,
                 { path: [<failed v>], expr: optional.of(false) } with saveFailureAs.failed ]
           -> <next step>
A__failed: when waits.A.outcome == 'failed'                                  (carryOn only)
           set [ { path: [<failed v>], expr: optional.of(true) } with saveFailureAs.failed,
                 { path: [<code v>], expr: optional.of(waits.A.data.code) } with saveFailureAs.code ]
           -> <next step>
```

- A result field that is absent (not `required`) removes the value, so a look-up that finds no owner empties "Service owner" rather than keeping an old one.
- The value `saveFailureAs.code` fills has the kind `choice` (E-29): its choices are the failure codes of the operation (of each operation, when several actions save their code as it), its labels the catalogue's, written into the definition where a template or message shows it (8.4, 10.2). It is declared `{"type": "string"}` in `types.data`, as a "Button pressed" value is. A "when" compares it with a `{failureCode}` literal, the code.
- On failure the saved results keep what they had; on success the failure code keeps what it had (format).
- With "stuck", `failed` is not an outcome the stage may read (spec section 6); the request faults with `call-failed` at `A__run.A`, the operation's failure code copied into the fault's params (E-23), the request is stuck with `action-failed`, and Retry re-enters `A__run` (12.4). A failed call's data is `{code, message}`.
- Each read of `waits.A.data` is guarded by its transition's `when`.

### 11.3 Key scope

| Sort | "When the stage is entered again" (authored, else the catalogue's `onRepeat`) | Written |
|---|---|---|
| read | (ignored) | `keyScope: "activation"`, `idempotencyKey: null` |
| write, await | `again` | `keyScope: "activation"`, `idempotencyKey: null` |
| write, await | `once` | `keyScope: null`, `idempotencyKey: "'once.' + request.id + '.<act ID>'"` |

The explicit key is the same in both copies and on every re-entry, which is "once per request" (E-23). A request ID matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (E-23), so a key is at most 5 + 64 + 1 + 40 = 110 characters (the limit is 255) and needs no escaping.

A read always has `activation` (format 3.3); `ifStageEntersAgain` on a read has no effect, and core says so (`action.repeatOnRead`, Worth knowing).

The default is written out (E-14): a missing authored choice is replaced by the catalogue's `onRepeat` at compile time, so a later change of the catalogue default changes only later publishes (shapes 2.6).

### 11.4 Each action as its own engine stage

A call opens when its step is entered and the request waits there until the result arrives; the step's status is what people see while it waits, and a fault names `A__run.A`. Two calls in one step would run in parallel and break the listed order. So every connection action has its own step, as every other action does (2.2).

## 12. The origin map

### 12.1 Shape

Format 3.11's `origins` map, with these rules for compiled authored workflows:

- `item` is a one-element array holding the authored item ID; the workflow's own `wf_` ID for workflow-level elements. `part` is the authored `Location.part`, or `null` for the item as a whole. So `{item: [i], part: p}` reads as the `Location {item: i, part: p}`.
- Element keys as format 3.11, including `trigger:<sw>`, `event:<act>` and `nobody:<rule ID>`.
- Field keys (E-18): `<element key>#<JSON Pointer into the element>`, for every field holding CEL whose origin differs from its element's. The pointer is exactly what `Faulted.error.field` carries (event-payloads, `Faulted`), so a fault resolves to a field origin first and to its element's otherwise. A lookup's origin is such a field key, `outcome:…#/lookups/<n>` (E-23).

### 12.2 Every element and field

| Element (key) | Origin | Field keys |
|---|---|---|
| `stage:root` | `[wf]`, null | |
| `stage:S__tasks(Back)` | `[S]`, `tasks` | |
| `stage:S__route(Back)` | `[S]`, `arrows` | |
| `stage:S__groupsTasks(Back)`, `stage:S__groupsRoute(Back)` | `[S]`, `tasks` / `arrows` | |
