| `stage:A__groups(Back)`, `stage:A__run(Back)`, `stage:A__gate(Back)` | `[A]`, null | |
| `stage:<ending>` | `[ending]`, null | |
| `stage:ar__unfinished` (Try it) | `[ar]`, the part with the To do | |
| `wait:S__tasks.T` | `[T]`, null | `#/assignees` → `[T]`, `whoIsAsked`; `#/may` → `[T]`, `requesterCanAnswer` |
| `wait:A__run.A` | `[A]`, null | `#/args/<f>` → `[A]`, `inputs.<f>`; `#/idempotencyKey` → `[A]`, `ifStageEntersAgain`, also when the author left it absent and the catalogue's `onRepeat` applies: the origin then names where the author would set it (E-27) |
| `wait:S__tasks.T__members` | `[T]`, `whoIsAsked` | |
| `wait:S__groupsTasks.S__read`, `wait:S__groupsRoute.S__read` | `[S]`, `tasks` / `arrows` | `#/args/groups` → the one part that names the groups (a clause; a lookup input; never `whoIsAsked`, 4.2); the stage's part when several do |
| `wait:A__groups.A__read` | `[A]`, null | `#/args/groups` → the one part that names the groups (`[A]`, `onlyWhen`, `inputs.<f>`, `to`, `save`, `values.<name>`); `[A]`, null when several do |
| `outcome:S__tasks.T/btn` | `[btn]`, null | `#/lookups/<n>` and `#/lookups/<n>/inputs/<f>` → `[q]`, `choices` / `choices.inputs.<f>` (directory: `choices.peopleIn`) |
| `check:…/btn/q__hidden` | `[q]`, `showWhen` (`[pg]`, `showWhen` when only the page has one) | none: `#/when` has the element's origin, and format 3.11 writes a field key only where it differs |
| `check:…/btn/q__needed` | `[q]`, null | |
| `check:…/btn/q__choice` | `[q]`, `choices` | `#/when` → `[q]`, `choices.formula` for formula choices |
| `check:…/btn/btn__also` | `[btn]`, `enabledWhen` | |
| `check:…/btn/T__requester` | `[T]`, null | |
| `transition:S__tasks.S__answered` | `[S]`, `tasks` | `#/set/<n>/expr` → the filler: `[q]`, `savedAs`; `[T]`, `savesButtonPressedAs` / `savesAnsweredByAs`; `[T]`, null for `__pressed`; `[start task]`, null for `requester`; for a merged Set (4.6), no field key: it has the element's origin, the stage's `tasks` part |
| `transition:S__tasks.ar__early` | `[ar]`, `goAsSoonAsTrue` | `#/when` → `[ar]`, `when`; `#/set/<n>/expr` as above |
| `transition:S__route.ar` | `[ar]`, null | `#/when` → `[ar]`, `when.condition` when only the condition contributes, `onlyWhen` when only that does, else `[ar]`, null |
| `transition:S__groupsTasks.S__readOk`, `transition:S__groupsRoute.S__readOk` | `[S]`, `tasks` / `arrows` | |
| `transition:A__groups.A__readOk` | `[A]`, null | |
| `transition:A__run.A__save` / `A__skip` | `[A]`, null | `#/when` → `[A]`, `onlyWhen`; `#/set/0/expr` → `[A]`, `save` |
| `transition:A__run.A__next` | `[A]`, null | |
| `transition:A__run.A__ok` / `A__failed` | `[A]`, null | `#/set/<n>/expr` → `[A]`, `saveResults.<f>` / `saveFailureAs.failed` / `saveFailureAs.code` |
| `transition:A__gate.A__go` / `A__skip` | `[A]`, `onlyWhen` | |
| `rule:<act>` (Notify) | `[A]`, null | `#/when` → `onlyWhen`; `#/send/to/0/expr` → `to`; `#/send/message/parts/<n>/value` → `message.<i>` (the template piece) |
| `nobody:S__tasks.T__nobody` (and `S__tasksBack`) | `[T]`, `whoIsAsked` | |
| `rule:n_task`, `rule:n_stopped` | `[wf]`, null | |
| `trigger:<sw>` | `[sw]`, null | `#/when` → `onlyWhen`; `#/data/<q>` → `answers.<q>`; `#/data/requester` → `requester` |
| `event:<act>` (Tell) | `[A]`, null | `#/when` → `onlyWhen`; `#/values/<name>` → `values.<name>` |

Schemas need no origin: a property is a question ID, and `requester` maps to the start task.

### 12.3 Everything the engine can raise, and its Location

| Raised | Recorded or returned as | Location from |
|---|---|---|
| Expression error in a transition (`when` or a Set), an assignee list, `may`, call args, an explicit key | `Faulted {kind: error, element, error: {code: cel-error \| int-range \| key-invalid, field}}` | The field origin, else the element's. `params.key` names a value ID or catalogue field when one is involved. |
| A call failed with "stuck" | `Faulted {kind: error, element: A__run.A, error: {code: call-failed, field: null, params: {code: <the operation's failure code>}}}` | `[A]`, null. Reason `action-failed`. |
| A directory read step's read failed | `Faulted {kind: error, element: X.I__read, error: {code: call-failed, field: null, params: {code}}}` | The read's `#/args/groups` origin. Reason `action-failed` (E-23: whatever added the call). |
| A membership read `T__members` failed | Its `WaitCompleted {outcome: failed}`; no fault | Its groups contribute nobody to who can answer; a person asked directly still counts (10.4) |
| A cancelled write or await that was sent with no clear answer | `call-outcome-unknown` alert to the workflow admins (E-23, E-24). A read is dropped quietly. | The call wait's origin |
| More than 50 firings | `Faulted {error, element: <the transition>, code: firing-limit}` | That transition's origin |
| Nothing fits | `Faulted {kind: stuck, element: null}` | The active stage's origin: `[S]`, `arrows` (a routing step) or the step's own. Reason `nothing-fits`. |
| Nobody to ask | The match of the wait's `nobodyToAsk` rule (10.4) | `nobody:` origin: `[T]`, `whoIsAsked`. Reason `nobody-to-ask`. |
| Refusal `wait-not-open` | attempts log | `[T]` (the wait) |
| `membership-unavailable` | not an attempt | none (core) |
| `not-assignee` | attempts log | `#/assignees`: `[T]`, `whoIsAsked` |
| `may` | attempts log | `#/may`: `[T]`, `requesterCanAnswer` |
| `invalid-data` (schema) | attempts log | `[q]` from the property name, a field inside the answer that its schema does not have included (`wrong-kind`, E-27); `requester` and a property the schema does not have → `[T]` |
| `source-unavailable`, `choice-unknown` | not an attempt / attempts log | `#/lookups/<n>`: `[q]`, `choices` |
| `check` | attempts log | The check's origin. The local name gives the report (core 7.2): `hidden` → `invalid-data`/`hidden-answered`; `needed` → `invalid-data`/`required`; `choice` → `invalid-data`/`too-short` for an empty multiple choice, else `invalid-data`/`not-a-choice` (E-27); `requester` → `invalid-data`/`unknown-question` (runtime-api 3.1); `also` → `check` with the message |
| A check's `when` errors | refusal `rule-error` | The check's `#/when` origin |
| A binding: `mapping-error` | inbound answer, alert | `trigger:<sw>` field origin; an error in a `WRAP` stays at `#/data/<q>` |
| A binding: `may`, `invalid-data`, `choice-unknown`, `check` | inbound answer, alert | As for a person's act, on the start outcome |
| A rule expression error (notifier, publisher) | `rule_errors`, `rule-failed` alert | The rule's field origin |
| `unfinished` (Try it) | stuck in a stage listed by compile | The listed Location (section 13) |
| Findings | `check` (core) | Located in the authored workflow by core; no origin needed |

Every element has an origin entry (format section 9, a publish check), so every row above resolves.

### 12.4 The stuck reason, and Retry per reason

Every reader reads the stuck reason from the fault and the `nobodyToAsk` block (shapes 5.5; E-23), never from the shape of an ID. The stage a stuck request is reported in (`Stuck`, `request.stuck@1`, `request.unstuck@1`) is the authored stage, found through the origin map by this section's conventions (E-27, E-28; `authoredStageOf` in core's kernel entry), from the definition alone: an engine stage whose origin has part `tasks` or `arrows` (`[S]`, `tasks` or `arrows`, 12.2) names the authored stage `S`; an ending's origin names the ending itself; from any other step (an action's `A__groups`, `A__run` or `A__gate`, whose origin `[A]`, null names the action), it is the first such stage along the transitions, which is the stage the action is in, because a compiled stage is left only through its own routing step. For Try it's unfinished step `ar__unfinished`, whose origin is the arrow, it is the stage that arrow leaves. A definition with no origin map reports its own stage. The stuck state and the nobody-to-ask rule are in the kernel folder of core (E-27). Retry and Close are `contract/runtime-api.md`'s; what they do to this design:

| Recorded state | Reason | Retry |
|---|---|---|
| A `Faulted` not cleared, `kind: error`, `code: call-failed`: any call, an action's or a directory read step's | `action-failed` | Offered. `Overridden {actions: [retry]}` clears the fault and re-enters the active stage, the stage of `Faulted.element`: `A__run(Back)` for an action, `A__groups(Back)`, `S__groupsTasks(Back)` or `S__groupsRoute(Back)` for a directory read step. The re-entry opens the call again: `once` keeps its explicit key, so the connector returns the first result or tries the failed key again; `again` and a read get a new activation key. |
| A `Faulted` not cleared, `kind: error`, any other code (`cel-error`, `int-range`, `key-invalid`, `firing-limit`) | `error` | Not offered; Retry is refused with `not-retryable`. Only Close. After an error the request sits where its turn began, so a retry could repeat an outside action that had already succeeded (E-23). |
| Open, no fault, no open obligation and no open call | `nothing-fits` | Not offered; refused with `not-retryable`. Only Close. The same data would give the same result. |
| An open obligation matches its `nobodyToAsk` rule | `nobody-to-ask` | Offered. `Overridden {actions: [retry]}` re-enters the active stage, which is the tasks step `S__tasks(Back)`. |
| None | not stuck | Refused with `not-stuck`. Close is offered for any open request. |

Re-entering the tasks step reads the group again. The retry skips the step's open waits and enters `S__tasks` afresh: a new activation, so every task's wait opens again with `ASK(T)` evaluated over the current data, and each `T__members` opens again with a new activation key, so the directory is asked again. The rule matches only against the read of the wait's own activation, so the old read no longer counts. Until the new read is recorded, a wait with a group among its assignees does not match: the request is not stuck, and `request.unstuck@1` is published. If the new read also leaves nobody, the wait matches again, the request is stuck with `nobody-to-ask` again, and `n_stopped` tells the admins again. No step other than the tasks step is re-entered, so no arrival action runs again.

Known limits, as E-19 states them: an empty "Who is asked" stays empty, so Close is the only way out until values can be changed by hand; in a stage with several tasks every task is asked again, answered ones included. A task asked of "people in [group]" asks the group itself (4.2), so Retry reads that group again too (E-24).

## 13. Try it on an unfinished draft (E-20)

Try it treats a part as unfinished only where a To do stops a request from running (E-20). Words, labels, names, status words, `readsAs`, and anything that only shapes what people see never block. The rule: a To do blocks when the compiler cannot produce the element (a missing destination, operation, condition or filler; a broken reference; an expression that does not type-check; an unknown catalogue entry; a required input unmapped). Then:

| Part with a blocking To do | Emitted | A request that gets there |
|---|---|---|
| An arrow with `goTo: null` | Its transition with its real `when`, to `ar__unfinished` (a stage with no waits and no transitions, the source copy's status) | Takes the arrow if it fits, then is stuck, reported in the stage the arrow leaves (12.4) |
| An arrow whose `when` or "+ only when" is unfinished | Its transition at its place with `when: true`, to `ar__unfinished` | Stuck there, unless an earlier arrow fits |
| An action (Save a value, Use a connection) | Its step `A__run` with no waits and no transitions; no gate | Stuck on entering it |
| A Notify with no `to`, a Tell with no `tell` | The step as usual; the rule left out | Runs on: neither can ever stop a request (format) |
| A task (no buttons, a broken button condition) | The tasks step with no waits and no transitions | Stuck on entering it |
| A question without `savedAs` | The question as usual; no Set for it | Its answer is not kept |
| A question whose choices cannot be offered (no `choices`, no `source`, `labelField` or `storedField`, a list with no rows) | The question's property typed by its kind's schema of 5.1 with no enum and no lookup; with a list with no rows, a schema no answer satisfies. Not unfinished (E-28) | The answer is taken unchecked against the choices, or cannot be given; the tester sees a question nobody can answer properly |
| A task with no "Who is asked" | `assignees: []`; not unfinished (E-28) | Runs to the task and is stuck there with `nobody-to-ask`, as a published one would |
| A stage with no arrows | The routing step with no transitions | Stuck there |
| The start task | Its tasks step `<start>__tasks` (`root.initial`) with no waits, listed as unfinished there | `start` is refused with `unfinished` (core 10.2) |
| A binding | Left out of `triggers` | `startFrom` is refused with `unfinished` |

Which To dos block is core section 4's "Stops Try it" column and the `item.partMissing` parts listed under it; this table and that column say the same (E-27, E-28). A task stops Try it only for no buttons or a broken button condition; a missing "Who is asked", a missing choices and a list with no rows do not.

The kernel's stuck check flags a request in such a stage (`Faulted {kind: stuck}`), and Try it reports it with cause `unfinished` because compile returns `unfinished: {location: Location, stage?: string}[]` naming each such engine stage (no `stage` for a binding). No kernel rule is bent. Try it mode does not run the kernel publish checks (an unfinished draft fails "every stage can reach a final stage" by design). This refines core 10.2, which made a whole stage unfinished.

Try it emits the `nobodyToAsk` block and the membership reads as publish does, and works out the stuck state as every reader does (12.4). Its membership reads and directory read steps are answered by the in-memory host's faked directory (E-4).

## 14. Checks the compiler relies on, and the publish checks it meets

### 14.1 What core's check (or `parse`) has made true

| Assumed | Ensured by | Why the compiler needs it |
|---|---|---|
| IDs match the pattern, have no `__`, carry the right prefix, are unique | `parse` | Names in section 1 are unique and split unambiguously |
| Every authored ID is at most 40 characters | `parse` (E-23) | Names fit 64 characters |
| `start.stage` is a working stage with exactly one task | `workflow.noStart`, `start.notOneTask` | `root.initial` and `start` exist |
| Every reference points at an existing item | `item.brokenReference` | Every name compiled exists |
| Every part needed to run is present | `item.partMissing` | Section 13 handles the rest in Try it |
| Each value has one kind | `value.kindConflict` | One declared CEL type per path; merged Sets (4.6) type-check |
| Words fit their kinds; `right` has the right shape; slots get the right kind | `clause.wordsDoNotFit`, `expression.kindMismatch` | Section 8.3 is defined for the kind; `ASK` gets person, group or people |
| Formulas parse, name known things in scope, use known functions, give the right kind | `formula.*` | `F` type-checks |
| Pressed clauses only in the owning stage's after-response "Only when" and arrows | `clause.pressedOutsideStage` | `<tk>__pressed` and `waits.T` are in scope where read |
| At most one "In all other cases", last | `arrow.otherCasesNotLast` | At most one `otherwise` per routing step, last (E-18, K4) |
| Every button or combination of buttons fits an arrow | `stage.buttonHasNowhereToGo`, `stage.combinationHasNowhereToGo` | A routing step reached from a tasks step finds an arrow |
| A carried-on failure has an arrow; a stopped one is not read | `action.failureHasNowhereToGo`, `action.failureReadButStops` | `A__failed` exists exactly when failure values may be read |
| A write or await has a key scope | The catalogue writes `onRepeat` for every write and await (`catalogue.ts`); `action.repeatNotChosen` is withdrawn (core section 4) | 11.3 always has a value |
| Every person or group constant, a list cell's included, has a directory ID in the ID's form; an empty ID in a list cell is a cell not given | `parse.badFormat`, `format: "directoryId"` (E-27; core section 3) | Every constant fits its `types.constants` entry (`constant-does-not-fit`) and every reference literal fits the person or group schema |
| A choice question from a list takes it from a list with rows | `item.partMissing` on the list's `rows` (E-27) | An `enum` is never empty (5.1) |
| Catalogue entries exist, are of the right kind, their fields exist, required inputs are mapped, connections are set up | `catalogue.*` | Call waits, lookups and triggers name real entries |
| No directory step in a start-form condition | `start.directoryInCondition` | No read is needed in the start turn |
| A start stage with a connection action after its form has a status | `start.needsStatus` | 7.4 |
| Bindings fill the needed questions and are well-typed | `startsWhen.neededNotFilled`, shapes 3.11 | 10.6 |
| Every stage reaches an ending | `stage.noWayToEnd` | Spec: every stage can reach a final stage |
| Every loop passes a task or an action opened inside it | `loop.noTask` | Spec: every cycle passes a condition on a wait opened inside it |
| None of the constructs of 14.3 is in the draft | A core To do for each (E-23) | The compiler has no rule for them |

The compiler does not rely on `value.mayBeEmpty` for kernel validity: every read uses optional syntax (8.5). E-22 limits that finding to who is asked, a notification's recipient, a directory group and a needed connection input; every other empty value is handled by the rules of 3.3, 8.3 and 8.4.

### 14.3 Constructs with no compile rule

Core raises a To do for each (E-23). None occurs in the four fixtures. In publish mode a construct check does not catch becomes `compile.internal`; in Try it it is listed as unfinished (section 13).

| # | Construct | Core's To do | Why there is no rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Two results of one action saved as the same value (`saveResults: {key: v_x, url: v_x}`) | `action.resultSavedTwice` | Two Sets on one path in `A__ok` (spec section 6 forbids it); no order between result fields says which wins |
| 2 | A binding mapping for a question whose Show when (or its page's) reads "Started on" | `startsWhen.showWhenReadsStartedOn` | The mapping runs before the request exists, so `WRAP` (10.6) has no start time |
| 3 | A `multipleChoice` or `group` question with choices `from: "source"` or `"directory"` | `question.choicesNotSupported` | A lookup answers one item or one person (5.4) |
| 4 | A `person` question with choices `from: "typedIn"` or `"list"` | `question.choicesNotSupported` | A person answer is a directory reference, checked by a lookup |
| 5 | `inAllOtherCases` with "+ only when", or with `goAsSoonAsTrue` | `arrow.otherCasesWithCondition` | `otherwise` takes no condition, and an early arrow needs one (6.4) |
| 6 | An empty `allOf` or `anyOf` | `condition.noClauses` (`item.partMissing` for an arrow's `when.condition`) | No clause to compile; true or false would be a guess |
| 7 | `steps` on a `RequestReference` | `reference.stepsNotSupported` | 8.2 defines steps on a value only |
| 8 | Multiple choice, people, a list or a field group in a template (a call input, a Tell value, a binding answer) | `template.kindNotJoinable` | No rule for rendering a list or a group as text (8.4) |
| 9 | A directory step or an "is in group" test, in a task's Show when, "Also only when" or lookup input, or in an early arrow, over a group filled in the same tasks step. Not a question's "people in" group, which needs no read; formulas are not judged; on the start form, conditions are `start.directoryInCondition`'s (E-27) | `group.readInSameStep` (E-26) | The read is made before the tasks step opens (8.6) |

### 14.2 Kernel publish checks (spec v2.20 section 6, format section 9, shapes) and how each is met

The codes are the kernel publish check's (`PUBLISH_CHECKS` in core's kernel entry; core section 14). Spec section 6 states the readings this table once asked for (E-27): which paths count as present for a read, how a stage's transitions cover its waits' outcomes, what breaks a cycle, and which forms guard a read of a wait's data. The checks that need the catalogue run only when `checkDefinition` is given it (core section 14).

| Check | Codes | Met by |
|---|---|---|
| Every CEL expression type-checks | `expression-invalid`, `expression-wrong-type`, `set-type-mismatch` | The `types` block of 3.4; the catalogue's derived types for inputs and sent fields; core's kind checks (14.1). The publish check and `decide` type an expression in one shared environment, so what publish accepts runs (E-27). |
| Wait reads in scope | `wait-out-of-scope` | `waits.T` is read only in its own tasks step (early transitions, `S__answered`); `waits.T__members` by no expression; `waits.A` only in `A__run`; `waits.I__read` only in its read step. |
| `.data` reads guarded | `wait-data-unguarded` | `W` (4.6): each read in the true branch of a one-outcome test; `A__ok`, `A__failed`, `I__readOk`: guarded by the transition's `when`. `waits.T__members.data` is never read. The guard forms spec v2.19 accepts include a test that the wait's outcome equals one outcome, under `&&` beside the read or as the condition of `?:` for its true branch. |
| Paths read only where set, or through `has()` or optional syntax | `data-path-maybe-absent` | Every read is `.?` (8.5) or `has()` |
| Sets in one transition do not overlap | `set-overlap` | One entry per path: merged fillers (4.6); visit-scoped keys distinct |
| `start` names a person wait of `root.initial` | `start-not-person-wait-of-initial`, `initial-unknown` | 7.4 |
| Every write has `keyScope` or `idempotencyKey`; exactly one is non-null; a read has `activation` | `read-key-scope` (exactly one non-null: the shape check) | 11.3 |
| Coverage of outcome combinations, or `otherwise` | `outcomes-not-covered` | Tasks step: no `otherwise`; `S__answered`'s `ALL(S)` is true in every combination, because a combination completes every wait, and it does not read the membership reads, whose `ok` and `failed` both count (2.3). Call steps: `ok` (fault) or `ok` and `failed` (outcome). Directory read steps: `I__readOk` covers `ok`, the only outcome with `onFailure: fault`. Steps with no waits: one empty combination, covered by any transition. |
| A call's `failed` counts, and is read, only with `onFailure: outcome` | `failed-not-handled` | `A__failed` exists only for carry on; a membership read has `onFailure: outcome` and its `failed` is read by no expression |
| Every stage can reach a final stage | `stage-cannot-end` | `stage.noWayToEnd`; every compiler step lies on its chain toward the routing step |
| Every cycle passes a condition on a wait opened inside it | `cycle-without-wait` | `loop.noTask`; a compiled cycle passes a tasks step (`S__answered` and every early transition test the task waits opened there) or a call step (`ok` tests the call). Not met when the loop's only connection action has "Only when": its gate's `A__skip` is an edge around the call step, so the transition graph has a cycle with no wait. `loop.noTask` counts a connection action only when it has no "Only when". |
| At most one `otherwise`, last | `otherwise-twice`, `otherwise-not-last` | Tasks step: none; routing step: "In all other cases" last; save and gate steps: `skip` last |
| No `$` in paths or schema properties | `path-segment-invalid`, `schema-property-invalid` | Paths and properties are authored IDs, `requester`, and section 1.2 names |
| No map literal with a key starting with `$` (E-26) | `map-key-dollar` | The compiler writes map literals only with authored IDs, catalogue field IDs and its own keys (`type`, `id`, `stored`, `label`) as keys. A formula's map literal is the author's: core refuses a `$` key there as `formula.notInProfile`, rule `reservedKey` (E-27) |
| A wait's opening expressions read no wait of the same stage (E-26) | `opening-reads-sibling-wait` | `assignees` and `args` read `data`, `request` and constants only; a group read is made in its own read step before the step that uses it (8.6), and a membership read `T__members` reads `data`, not `waits.T` |
| IDs match their patterns; no wait ID a `.`-prefix of another | `id-invalid`, `id-duplicate`, `wait-id-prefix` | No compiled stage, wait or transition ID contains a dot, so `T` and `T__members` are not prefixes of each other; a nobody-to-ask rule ID is two Names joined by a dot (format section 2); lengths by 14.1 |
| Every transition target is a stage; every status is declared | `transition-target-unknown`, `status-unknown` | Section 7.3; section 9 |
| Every outcome schema exists and every schema is used | `schema-unknown`, `schema-unused`, `schema-ref-mismatch` | One schema per button, `<tk>.<btn>@1` |
| Every element has exactly one origin | `origin-missing`, `origin-unknown-element`, `origin-field-not-cel` | Section 12.2, nobody-to-ask rules included |
| Every Set path, constant and call op has a `types` entry, and no other entry exists | `types-data-missing`, `types-data-unused`, `types-constant-missing`, `types-constant-unused`, `constant-does-not-fit`, `types-result-missing`, `types-result-unused` | 3.4 |
| Schemas use only `jsonschema-1` | `schema-not-in-profile` | 5.1 as built: no `minimum`, `maximum` or `minItems` |
| `nobodyToAsk`: `wait` names a person wait; `members` is null or a `membersOf@1` read call (`onFailure: outcome`) in the wait's stage, on the catalogue's directory connection when the catalogue is given; at most one rule per wait (format section 9) | `nobody-wait-not-person`, `nobody-wait-twice`, `nobody-members-invalid` | 10.4: one rule per emitted person wait; `members` names `T__members` in the wait's own stage |
| A stage that holds a membership read has no `otherwise` transition (format section 9) | `nobody-members-with-otherwise` | The tasks step leaves by `S__answered`, never `otherwise` (2.3) |
| Final stages have no waits or transitions | `final-stage-not-empty` | Section 9 |
| Rules: `on.event` is a recorded event type or `Stuck`; `on.element` only where allowed, and naming an element of the definition of a kind its event type can name (spec v2.19, format 3.6); `{words}` keys known | `rule-event-unknown`, `rule-element-not-allowed`, `rule-element-unknown`, `words-unknown` | 10.2, 10.3, 10.5: `n_task` and `n_stopped` name no element; a Notify's or a Tell's rule is on `StageEntered` and names the action's own engine stage, or no element when the action runs in two copies |
| Triggers and events blocks pass shapes 3.11 and 7.5 | `binding-button-missing`, `binding-answer-invalid`, `binding-answer-missing` | 10.5, 10.6 |
| Lookups name a property of their outcome's schema; `answer: "person"` only on the person schema | `lookup-property-unknown`, `lookup-person-not-person-schema` | 5.4 |
| A lookup's inputs do not read `request.id`, nor the whole `request` (E-28, spec v2.19) | `lookup-reads-request-id` | An input reads `request.by` for "the Requester" and `request.at` for "Started on" (8.2), never `request.id`: no authored reference names the request's ID |
## 15. Worked example: `contract/fixtures/change-request.authored.json`

### 15.1 Facts the compiler computes

- Dominance (root `st_request_form`): `st_domain_approval` is dominated by `st_request_form`; `st_create_jira_issue` by `st_request_form`; `st_development` by `st_request_form` and `st_create_jira_issue`. The one arrow that sends back is `ar_da_request_changes` (to the start stage).
- Second copies: `st_request_form` only (start stage, sent back to). `st_domain_approval`, `st_create_jira_issue`, `st_development` have none.
- Tasks that may ask a group: `tk_domain_approval` only (`whoIsAsked` is a list cell of kind group), so it gets the membership read `tk_domain_approval__members`. `tk_request_form` asks the Requester; `tk_development` asks a person value, else a list cell of kind person. `q_eng_lead`'s directory choices are a lookup (E-20). No `members` step and no "is in group" test, so no directory read step.
- Pressed clauses read after a tasks step: `btn_da_reject` (Notify's Only when), every button arrow. So `tk_domain_approval__pressed` and `tk_development__pressed`. No early arrows.
- No binding, so no `requester` property or check; no Tell. No formula.
- None of the constructs of 14.3.

### 15.2 Abbreviations

Each stands for its text exactly; the published definition holds the expansion (15.6 shows it for the first stage).

```
PD(c)    = (data.?v_primary_domain.hasValue() ? ls_domains[data.?v_primary_domain.value()].?c : optional.none())
REQ      = data.?requester.or(request.by.type == 'user' ? optional.of(request.by) : optional.none())
LIST(x)  = (x.hasValue() ? [x.value()].filter(r, r.type == 'user' || r.type == 'group') : [])
LEAD     = data.?v_eng_lead.or(PD(col_default_lead))
W1(q, v) = waits.tk_request_form.outcome == 'btn_rf_submit' ? waits.tk_request_form.data.?q : data.?v
W3(q, v) = waits.tk_domain_approval.outcome == 'btn_da_approve' ? waits.tk_domain_approval.data.?q
         : waits.tk_domain_approval.outcome == 'btn_da_reject' ? waits.tk_domain_approval.data.?q
         : waits.tk_domain_approval.outcome == 'btn_da_request_changes' ? waits.tk_domain_approval.data.?q
         : data.?v
WD(q, v) = waits.tk_development.outcome == 'btn_dev_mark_released' ? waits.tk_development.data.?q : data.?v
DONE(T)  = waits.T.status == 'completed' ? optional.of(waits.T.outcome) : optional.none()
BY(T)    = waits.T.status == 'completed' ? optional.of(waits.T.by) : optional.none()
NONE     = optional.none()
```

Schema abbreviations (5.1), used in `types` and `schemas`:

```
TEXT     = {"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":1000}
LONG     = {"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":20000}
DATE     = {"type":"string","format":"date"}
STR      = {"type":"string"}
YESNO    = {"type":"boolean"}
PERSON   = {"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"required":["type","id"],
            "properties":{"type":{"type":"string","const":"user"},"id":{"type":"string","format":"directory-object-id"}}}
GROUP    = PERSON with "const":"group"
ROWS     = {"type":"string","enum":["row_payments","row_identity","row_data_platform","row_internal_tools"]}
RISK     = {"type":"string","enum":["ch_risk_low","ch_risk_medium","ch_risk_high"]}
```

### 15.3 The definition

```
start: st_request_form__tasks.tk_request_form
constants: ls_domains
  ls_domains:
    row_payments:       { col_domain: 'Payments', col_needs_approval: true,
                          col_approvers: {type: group, id: dir-group-payments-approvers},
                          col_engineering_group: {type: group, id: dir-group-payments-engineering},
                          col_default_lead: {type: user, id: dir-user-diego-santos} }
    row_identity:       { col_domain: 'Identity', col_needs_approval: true,
                          col_approvers: {type: group, id: dir-group-identity-approvers},
```

`triggers` and `events` are absent: the fixture has no binding and nothing told.

Rule order: authored rules in document order of their actions, then `n_task` and `n_stopped` (format 3.1). `nobodyToAsk` follows the order of `root.stages`.

### 15.4 Data paths and origins of the example

| Path | Set by (transition) | Removed by |
|---|---|---|
| `requester` | `st_request_form__answered` in both copies (here always `optional.none()`: no binding names a Requester, so a person's start sets nothing) | never |
| `v_title`, `v_description`, `v_primary_domain`, `v_planned_release_date`, `v_risk` | `st_request_form__answered` in both copies | an empty answer (only `v_description` can be empty) |
| `v_eng_lead`, `v_reason` | `st_domain_approval__tasks.st_domain_approval__answered` | an empty answer |
| `v_da_button_pressed`, `v_da_answered_by` | the same | never (the one task always completes) |
| `tk_domain_approval__pressed` | the same | each `st_domain_approval__route` transition |
| `v_jira_issue` | `act_create_jira_issue__run.act_create_jira_issue__ok` | an empty key |
| `v_release_notes` | `st_development__tasks.st_development__answered` | an empty answer |
| `tk_development__pressed` | the same | `st_development__route.ar_dev_released` |

The membership read `tk_domain_approval__members` writes no data; its recorded result is what `st_domain_approval__tasks.tk_domain_approval__nobody` reads.

What the turns look like (no case written here): the start turn fires `st_request_form__answered` and one route transition (two firings) and stops at the domain approval task, with its membership read open beside it, or at the Jira call. An approval answer fires `st_domain_approval__answered`, `act_notify_requester_rejected__next` and an arrow (three firings); leaving the tasks step cancels the membership read if it is still open. A domain whose approvers group is empty, or holds only the Requester, leaves the task open with nobody to ask once the read answers: the request is stuck with `nobody-to-ask`, `n_stopped` tells the workflow admins, and Retry re-enters `st_domain_approval__tasks`, which reads the group again (12.4). "Request changes" lands the request in `st_request_form__tasksBack` with status "Needs changes", and `n_task` tells the Requester.

### 15.5 Kernel publish checks on the example

First checked by hand against spec v2.16 section 6 and format section 9. Core's compiler now compiles this fixture in publish mode, which runs the kernel publish check of 14.2 on the result, and it passes. The checks spec v2.17 adds (E-26: no sibling wait read when a wait opens, no `$` key in a map literal) hold for every compiled definition (14.2).

| Check | On this definition |
|---|---|
| Expressions type-check | Against the `types` block above, the five schemas and `types.results`. Not run. |
| Wait reads in scope | Each `waits.X` is read only in its own stage: `tk_request_form` in both `st_request_form` tasks steps, `tk_domain_approval` in `st_domain_approval__tasks`, `act_create_jira_issue` in its step, `tk_development` in its step. `tk_domain_approval__members` is read by no expression. |
| `.data` guarded | `W1`, `W3`, `WD`: each `.data` read is in the true branch of a one-outcome test. `act_create_jira_issue__ok` reads `.data` under `outcome == 'ok'`. |
| Paths read only where set, or optionally | Every data read is `data.?…`. |
| Sets do not overlap | One entry per path in every transition. |
| `start` | `st_request_form__tasks.tk_request_form`, a person wait of `root.initial`. |
| Keys | `act_create_jira_issue`: `keyScope: null`, explicit key. `tk_domain_approval__members`: a read with `keyScope: activation`. |
| Coverage | `st_request_form__tasks(Back)`: one wait, one outcome; `ALL` is true for it. `st_domain_approval__tasks`: waits `tk_domain_approval__members` (`ok`, `failed`: both count, `onFailure: outcome`) and `tk_domain_approval` (three buttons), six combinations; in each, `tk_domain_approval` is completed, so `st_domain_approval__answered` is true. The read with two outcomes needs no transition of its own. `act_create_jira_issue__run`: `ok` only counts (`onFailure: fault`); `__ok` covers it. `st_development__tasks`: one wait, one outcome. Steps with no waits (the two Notify steps and four routing steps): one empty combination, met by any transition under spec v2.18's reading (14.2); that every button reaches an arrow is core's check (14.1). |
| `failed` read only with `onFailure: outcome` | No expression reads a `failed` outcome. |
| Every stage reaches a final stage | Every chain leads to `st_released` or `st_rejected`. |
| Every cycle passes a condition on a wait opened in it | The one cycle, `st_request_form__tasksBack` → `…routeBack` → `st_domain_approval__tasks` → `act_notify_requester_rejected__run` → `st_domain_approval__route` → `st_request_form__tasksBack`, passes `st_domain_approval__answered` (on `tk_domain_approval`, opened in the cycle) and `st_request_form__answered` (on the `tasksBack` wait). The branch through `ar_rf_no_approval` leaves the cycle at the Jira call. |
| One `otherwise`, last | Only the two `ar_rf_other` transitions, each last. |
| IDs | No stage, wait or transition ID contains a dot; `tk_domain_approval` is no `.`-prefix of `tk_domain_approval__members`; the longest Name is `act_notify_requester_rejected__next` (35). |
| Origins | Every element in 15.4 has one element key. |
| `types` | Every Set path, the constant and both ops have an entry. |
| `nobodyToAsk` | Four rules, one per person wait; the one `members` names `membersOf@1` on `directory`, the catalogue's `directoryConnection`. |
| Final stages | As section 9 and 14.2. |

### 15.7 The integrated sample: where it differs in kind

`contract/fixtures/integrated-sample.authored.json` now has the binding fill `q_service` (ask A1 of `integrated-sample.md`), so it has no To do that blocks publish. What the compiler emits for each kind of thing the change-request example lacks:

| Kind | What the compiler emits |
|---|---|
| Binding | `triggers: [{ id: "sw_helpdesk_ticket", connection: "helpdesk", event: "ticketCreated@1", when: "sent.?category.hasValue() && sent.?category.value() == 'Service change'", outcome: "btn_rf_submit", data: { "q_summary": "sent.?title", "q_service": "sent.?service", "q_helpdesk_ticket": "optional.of('Helpdesk ' + sent.?key.orValue(''))", "requester": "sent.?reporter" } }]`, the constant side's presence test folded away. No question has a Show when, so nothing is wrapped. |
| Requester | The start schema gains `requester` (person); every start outcome gains `tk_request_form__requester` first; `st_request_form__answered`, in both copies, sets `requester` from `(waits.tk_request_form.outcome == 'btn_rf_submit' ? waits.tk_request_form.data.?requester : optional.none()).or(data.?requester)`. The binding's start is recorded `by` the connection. |
| Needed for every button | `q_summary` is in `required` of `btn_rf_submit` (with `q_service` from `neededToPress`). |
| Lookups | `btn_rf_submit` carries `lookups: [{ property: "q_service", connection: "servicecatalog", source: "services@1", inputs: { status: "optional.of('active')" }, storedField: "id", labelField: "name", answer: "item" }]`; `q_service`'s schema is the connection-choice object with `stored: {"type":"string"}`. |
| Read action | `act_look_up_service__run` with call `act_look_up_service` (`servicecatalog`, `serviceDetails@1`, `read`, `onFailure: fault`, `keyScope: activation`, args `serviceId: data.?v_service`); `act_look_up_service__ok` sets, in the catalogue's result field order (`tier` before `owner`, E-27), `v_service_tier` through `N(text, …)` and `v_service_owner = waits.act_look_up_service.data.?owner` (a person; absent removes it). A failure faults with `call-failed` (`params.code: service-not-found`): stuck with `action-failed`, and Retry re-enters `act_look_up_service__run`. |
| Write action, "once" | `act_open_fix_issue__run` with call `act_open_fix_issue` (`jira`, `createIssue@1`, `effect: write`, `onFailure: fault`, `keyScope: null`, `idempotencyKey: "'once.' + request.id + '.act_open_fix_issue'"` from the catalogue's `onRepeat: once`); `description` is the template `'Deploy failed with code ' + (data.?v_deploy_failure_code.hasValue() ? {'tests-failed': 'The tests failed', 'deploy-failed': 'The deployment failed', 'rolled-back': 'The deployment was rolled back', 'service-not-found': 'The pipeline does not know the service'}[?data.?v_deploy_failure_code.value()].orValue(data.?v_deploy_failure_code.value()) : '')`: the saved failure code is a choice whose label is shown (8.4, E-29). `act_open_fix_issue__ok` saves `key` and `url` to two different values, so 14.3 item 1 does not apply. |
| Await action | `act_run_pipeline__run` with call `act_run_pipeline` (`deploy`, `runPipeline@1`, `effect: write`, `onFailure: outcome`, `keyScope: activation` from the catalogue's `onRepeat: again`, `idempotencyKey: null`, args `service: data.?v_service`, `reference: data.?v_helpdesk_ticket`). `act_run_pipeline__ok` sets `v_run_link` and `v_deploy_failed = optional.of(false)`; `act_run_pipeline__failed` sets `v_deploy_failed = optional.of(true)` and `v_deploy_failure_code = optional.of(waits.act_run_pipeline.data.code)`. `ar_fix_again` sends back to Deploy (Deploy dominates Fix deployment); Deploy has no `ifSentBackStatus`, so no second copy: the arrow targets `act_run_pipeline__run` and the new activation gives a new key. |
| Tell | Step `act_send_change_deployed__run` (`act_send_change_deployed__next`, `when: true`); `events: [{ id: "act_send_change_deployed", on: { event: "StageEntered", element: "act_send_change_deployed__run" }, when: "!data.?v_deploy_failed.orValue(true)", told: { id: "told_change_deployed", words: "Change deployed" }, values: { runLink: "data.?v_run_link", service: "data.?v_service", summary: "data.?v_summary" } }]`, the values sorted by name (E-27). `service` is sent as the request holds it, `{stored, label}` (E-22). |
| Group fallback | `tk_fix_deployment` asks `v_service_owner`, else the Platform team group, so `st_fix_deployment__tasks` declares `tk_fix_deployment__members` before `tk_fix_deployment`, with `groups: LIST(data.?v_service_owner.or(optional.of(dyn({'type': 'group', 'id': 'dir-group-platform-team'})))).filter(r, r.type == 'group')`, which is `[]` when an owner exists. The group literal is in `dyn()` (8.2, E-27). Its rule: `{id: "st_fix_deployment__tasks.tk_fix_deployment__nobody", wait: "st_fix_deployment__tasks.tk_fix_deployment", members: "st_fix_deployment__tasks.tk_fix_deployment__members", excludeRequester: false}`. |
| A group with the Requester excluded | `st_approve__tasks` declares `tk_approve__members` (`groups: [dyn({'type': 'group', 'id': 'dir-group-platform-team'})]`, the `LIST` of a constant) before `tk_approve`; its rule has `excludeRequester: true`. `ar_approve_back` sends back to the start stage, whose second copy is entered. |
| Routing on a saved failure | `st_deploy__route`: `ar_dep_failed: when data.?v_deploy_failed.orValue(false)`; `ar_dep_other: otherwise`. |

If `integrated-sample.md` still uses placeholders or older names, under this design its stage IDs are the chain names (`act_look_up_service` → `act_look_up_service__run`, and so on), its call waits are named by the action ID rather than `call`, its two tasks that may ask a group have membership reads beside them and rules in a `nobodyToAsk` block, and the Jira action has `idempotencyKey: "'once.' + request.id + '.act_open_fix_issue'"` instead of `keyScope: request`, which changes the keys asserted in its cases (section 19, item 4).

## 16. What is not compiled in format 0, and why

| Authored | Why not |
|---|---|
| `sampleRequest`, `diagram`, `removedNames` | Editor only (format). |
| Workflow name, description, authors, "Stuck requests go to" | Not in the document (E-14). |
| Stage `name`, `kind`; task `name`; page `title`; question `label`; button `label`, `look`; value `name`, `description`; list, column and choice names; arrow `words`; formula `readsAs` | What people see. The page reads them from the version's stored authored source (E-6). Choice labels and a list's shown column appear only inside a rendered call-input or Tell template (8.4). |
| `FormText` (content and Show when) | Rendered by the page; it has no answer (5.3). |
| `groupRule` | Version 0 has one rule, which is the kernel's single-wait behaviour (4.1). |
| `Start.by`, `formatVersion` | One value each in format 0; `parse` checks them. |
| `goAsSoonAsTrue` on a stage with one task | Means nothing there (6.4). |
| `ifStageEntersAgain` on a read | A read has a fresh key on every entry (11.3). |

## 17. Choices made here, most expensive first

| # | Choice | Cost class | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every working-stage step is `<item>__<local>`; a working stage's own ID is never an engine stage ID; endings keep theirs | Recorded for ever | One ID, one role; inserting a section renames nothing |
| 2 | The local names of 1.2, including `Back` suffixes for the second copy | Recorded for ever | Short, one token, fit 64 characters |
| 3 | Wait IDs: task ID, action ID, `<tk>__members`, `<item>__read`; transition IDs: arrow ID in the routing step, local names elsewhere | Recorded for ever | Carry authored meaning; no positions |
| 4 | Compiler data keys `requester`, `<tk>__pressed`, `<st>__early`, `<st>__groups`, their JSON and lifetimes | Recorded for ever | The minimum carried between steps |
| 5 | `once` compiles to an explicit key `'once.' + request.id + '.<act>'` | Sent to outside systems | E-23; the same key in both copies of the step |
| 6 | The `nobodyToAsk` block, one rule per emitted person wait, IDs `<full wait ID>__nobody`; a membership read `<tk>__members` beside each task that may ask a group | Format 1 shape; IDs recorded | E-23 (shapes 5.5): one match all readers use; the task opens at once |
| 7 | The tasks step leaves by `S__answered` with `ALL(S)`, never `otherwise`, with per-outcome ternaries | Definition shape per version | E-23: a pending read cannot hold an answered task; no transition explosion with several tasks |
| 8 | The `types` block as 3.4 writes it | Format 1 content, read by `decide` | E-23: numbers read as declared |
| 9 | Outcome field `lookups` with `answer: item \| person` | Format 1 shape | E-20, E-23 |
| 10 | Check IDs by local name, and the reporting of each (12.3) | Recorded in evidence and attempts | One rule maps a check to the refusal the author wrote |
| 11 | Field origin keys `<element key>#<pointer>` and `item: [id]` | Format 1 content | E-18 field level; matches `Faulted.error.field` |
| 12 | Early arrows: tasks-step `__early` plus the recorded choice in `<st>__early` | Recorded | The destination survives the after-response actions |
| 13 | A directory read step just before each step that uses a directory step or an "is in group" test, writing the stage's one `<st>__groups` | Recorded | E-23 placement |
| 14 | Authored IDs at most 40 characters | `parse` rule | E-23; names fit 64 characters |
| 15 | Schema references `<tk>.<btn>@1`, always version 1 | Recorded in `WaitOpened` | Meaningful only within a version |
| 16 | Notify and Tell rules with `element: null` and a stage list when the action has two copies | Definition per version | One rule ID per action |
| 17 | Routing step always present; every action its own step | Definition per version (cheap) | Simplest; uniform story |
| 18 | Visit-scoped keys removed on leaving the stage | Recorded (cheap) | No stale compiler keys between visits |
| 19 | A formula guarded by its chips, `P(f)`: empty means not true, or an empty result (8.4) | Definition per version (cheap) | E-22; an empty value never faults a request |
| 20 | In a list comparison, an item of the right side that is empty is ignored (8.3) | Definition per version (cheap) | E-24 |
| 21 | The merged fall-through for extra answers keeps an earlier filler when the later task was cancelled (4.6); a merged Set has the stage's `tasks` origin; an unknown property's `invalid-data` is at the task (12) | Cheap | E-14's "emptied for that visit" read as "this task contributes nothing"; no single filler to name |
| 22 | Text 1000 and long text 20000 characters; `Yes`/`No` and directory IDs in rendered templates; an empty `membersOf` call when no group is asked | Cheap | Simplest; change freely |
| 23 | `n_task` kept as the default, telling a Requester in an asked group | Cheap | A per-task rule can replace it later |

## 18. Flaws found

In the decisions (each followed as written):

1. **E-18/E-20's field-level origin** stops at a field: an arrow whose `when` and "+ only when" both contribute is reported at the arrow, not at the clause. A source range in `Faulted.error.params` would refine it; not proposed now (cheap later as an added parameter).
2. Settled by E-24: "people in [group]" under "Who is asked" asks the group itself (4.2), so no read step is made for it and Retry for nobody-to-ask always reads the group again through `T__members` (12.4).
3. Settled by E-24: `call-outcome-unknown` is for a write or await only. A membership read sent with no clear answer whose task then closes is dropped quietly (10.4).
4. Settled by E-24: in a list comparison, empty items are ignored (8.3).
5. Settled by E-24: the Requester is subtracted from the people asked directly too, whether or not there is a membership read (10.4), so a task asked only of the Requester, who may not answer, is nobody-to-ask.

In other files:

6. A list kind in a template is a To do (14.3 item 8) because no rule yet says how each item renders as text and what separates them. `cel-1` has `join` (`engine/design/definition-format.md` section 5.3), so this is a rendering choice for the frontend and core to agree, not a profile gap.
7. Core 10.2 makes a whole stage unfinished; E-20 narrows Try it to parts that stop a request. Section 13 replaces core 10.2's rule.
8. Core 2.4 says a multiple-choice answer is in choice order; nothing enforced it. `<q>__choice` now does (5.4).

## 19. What other files must change

Each row is what that file must say for this design to hold; another session may already have made the change.

| # | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `engine/design/definition-format.md` | Section 10's `nobodyToAsk` example names the membership read beside the task (`"members": "st_approve__tasks.tk_approve__members"`), not a read step; section 12 items 2, 5 and 6 are settled by E-23. The written-out `cel-1` function list (section 5) includes everything 8.3 and 8.4 write: `date`, `timestamp`, `asDate`, `days`, `getDayOfWeek()` without a time zone, `string(double)`, `size`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `in`, the macros and the optional methods. |
| 2 | `engine/design/integrations-shapes.md` | 5.5: the rule ID example uses the chain names (`st_fix_deployment__tasks.tk_fix_deployment__nobody`); the tasks step leaves by an explicit all-answered condition; a stuck rule's expression error counts as no match; the match is E-24's who-can-answer set, with the Requester subtracted from the people asked directly too and a failed read contributing nobody from its groups. 4.8: Retry only for `action-failed` and `nobody-to-ask`, `not-retryable` otherwise; a sent write or await with no clear answer whose wait closes is kept and alerted (`call-outcome-unknown`); a read is dropped quietly (E-24). 5.2: lookup origins are `outcome:…#/lookups/<n>`, not `lookup:…`. 6.1 and section 8: no `n_noAssignee`, no `task.nobodyToAsk`; `n_stopped` on `Stuck` for every reason; section 8 adds `call-outcome-unknown`. |

The wrapper is unchanged. |
| 6 | Kernel publish check (spec section 6), as implemented in core | Closed: spec v2.18 section 6 states the readings (E-27), and core's check accepts a `.data` read in the true branch of `?:` on a one-outcome test, treats coverage of a stage with no waits as met by any transition, and completes every wait in a coverage combination (2.3). |

| 8 | `contract/authored-format.ts` (the frontend's pen) | ID rule: at most 40 characters (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$`), E-23. |
| 9 | `contract/runtime-api.md` | `retry`: refused with `not-retryable` for `nothing-fits` and `error`; for `nobody-to-ask` the re-entry is the tasks step, which reads the group again (12.4). |

## 20. Review

An adversarial review of this file, 2026-11-15, against `contract/authored-format.ts`, the four fixtures, kernel spec v2.15 with shapes section 10, and E-14, E-16, E-19, E-20, E-21. Nothing was run. The file was then revised for E-21 to E-23; 20.2 lists what E-23 settled. Where a row of 20.1 names a mechanism E-23 replaced, the note says so.

### 20.2 Settled by E-23

The review's judgment calls that the decisions now settle, and where this file applies each:

1. `decide` needs declared types: the `types` block (3.4).
2. Nobody-to-ask had two designs: shapes 5.5's is kept, the `nobodyToAsk` block and a membership read beside the task, with `n_stopped` on `Stuck` for every reason (10.3, 10.4). The review's objection to it, that `otherwise` waits for the read, is met by the explicit exit `ALL(S)` (2.3). This file's earlier recommendation, a read step before the task, is withdrawn.
3. Where Retry re-enters: the stage of the faulted call for `action-failed`, the tasks step for `nobody-to-ask`; no Retry for `nothing-fits` or `error` (12.4). The gap once listed as 18 item 2 is closed by E-24.
4. The reason for a failed directory read: `action-failed`, as for every fault from a failed call (8.6, 12.3).
5. Two results of one action saved as one value: a To do (14.3 item 1).
6. Constructs with no compile rule: a To do each (14.3).
7. Two tasks filling one value: the later in the document wins (4.6).
8. A stuck rule whose expression errors counts as no match for every reader, and is logged. The `nobodyToAsk` block holds no expression; `n_stopped`'s `when` is `true`.
9. A binding mapping whose question's Show when reads "Started on": a To do (10.6, 14.3 item 2).
10. `Lookup.answer` and lookup origins: the field stays, `labelField` is always a field name, and origins are `outcome:…#/lookups/<n>` (5.4, 12.1).
11. Read placement: just before the step that uses it (8.6), which also removes the stale-group flaw of E-14.
12. "Once" as an explicit key and the request ID pattern (11.3); authored IDs at most 40 characters (1.1); `days` and `asDate` in `cel-1` (8.4).

Coverage found nothing else missing: every `WORDS` entry has a row in 8.3; every `LOCATION_PARTS` entry the origin map uses exists; change-request compiles as 15.3 shows; several-at-once needs C2 only if two tasks share a value (it does not); integrated-sample compiles as 15.7 shows; blank compiles to `st_request_form__tasks`, `st_request_form__route` and `st_done`, with no second copy. For 15.3, each kernel publish check holds as 15.5 states, given the readings of section 19 item 6. None of this was run at the time of the review; since E-27 the built compiler and publish check run it (15.5).
