# Published definition: JSON format 1

Owner: engine owner. Status: final shape for format 1, 2026-11-15, pending the product owner's review (decisions E-17, E-18, E-20 to E-28 in `docs/11-decisions-engine.md`). Against kernel spec v2.20 (its copy is in `engine/spec/`; its `integrations.md` is cited as "integrations") and `engine/design/compiler.md` (cited as "compiler"). Where compiler and this file differ on a shape, this file and E-23 hold; where E-26, E-27 or E-28 differs from either, the later decision holds. Core (`engine/packages/core`) implements profile `cel-1` (section 5) and the `jsonschema-1` validator (section 6), with tests. The example was parsed and its CEL expressions type-checked with that wrapper; no server has published or run a definition of this format yet.

**These shapes are kept for ever once the first request runs.** A published definition is immutable and is read by `decide` for as long as any request on it is open. After the first request starts on format 1, no field of this file may be removed, renamed, retyped or given a new meaning; a change that `decide` would see is a new format number.

Event payloads are in `event-payloads.md`, next to this file. The demo workflow in this format is `examples/change-request-demo.definition.json`.

## 1. Rules for the whole document

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Publish writes every field of section 3 explicitly, with its default when nothing was given. The only fields that may be absent are the three optional blocks `triggers`, `events` and `nobodyToAsk`, which are absent when empty. | Spec section 7: `decide` has no defaults of its own, so a later change of a default changes only later publishes. |
| Every ordered collection is a JSON array in declared order: stages, waits, outcomes, checks, lookups, transitions, a transition's sets, statuses, notification rules, recipients, message parts, trigger bindings, event rules, nobody-to-ask rules. Object key order is never relied on. | Spec section 2; `jsonb` does not keep key order. |
| `null` appears only in the fields this file marks nullable. Constants, `types` and schemas never hold `null`. | Spec section 2, Values: the engine never writes null. |
| No key anywhere in the document starts with `$`. Pinned schemas therefore carry no `$schema`, `$id`, `$ref` or `$defs`; the dialect is fixed by `runtime.validator`. | L11; spec section 2, Values: the prefix is reserved. |
| A CEL expression is a JSON string holding its source text, read under the profile named by `runtime.cel`. | Simplest; the profile parses it at publish and at run time. |
| The document is immutable once published. A change is a new `version`. | Spec section 7; `definitions` rows are never updated. |
| `format` is `1`. Anything `decide` reads that changes meaning or shape needs a new format number. A top-level block that `decide` never reads may be added as an optional key without a new format number. | The format and its CEL profile are a long-lived contract (spec section 7). |
| Codes are kebab-case; type discriminators and enum values that name a kind of thing are lowerCamelCase. | L3; spec section 5. |

## 2. Identifiers

IDs are recorded in events, in outbound event IDs and in kept tables. They are expensive. `Name` is `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`.

| ID | Pattern | Unique within | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow ID | `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$`. The server's ID, not the authored document's `wf_` ID. Who assigns it: the server, at the workflow's creation. | the platform | `change-request-demo` |
| Request ID | `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (E-23). Not in the definition; `request.id` in CEL and `requestId` in events (`event-payloads.md` section 3.1). | the platform | `req-1001` |
| Authored ID | At most 40 characters (E-23); `parse` refuses a longer one. Contains no `__`. | its authored document | `tk_domain_approval` |
| Version | integer, 1 to 2147483647 | its workflow | `1` |
| Stage ID | a Name. `root` is the root stage; no child stage may use it. Contains no `.`. | the definition | `Pending`, `st_domain_approval__tasks` |
| Local ID (wait, transition) | one or more Names joined by `.` | its stage; waits and transitions share one namespace, because `Faulted.element` and `DataSet.element` name either by the same full ID. No wait ID visible in a CEL scope (its stage's and the root's) equals another or is a `.`-prefix of another, because a dotted ID is nested field access in `waits`. | `primary.decision`, `tk_review` |
| Full element ID | `<stage ID>.<local ID>`; split at the first `.` | the definition | `Pending.primary.decision` |
| Outcome ID | a Name | its wait | `approve`, `btn_da_approve` |
| Check ID | a Name | its outcome | `tk_request_form__requester` |
| Status ID | a Name | the definition | `pendingApproval`, `stat_released` |
| Constant name | a Name that is not a CEL keyword (`true`, `false`, `null`, `in`, `as`, `break`, `const`, `continue`, `else`, `for`, `function`, `if`, `import`, `let`, `loop`, `package`, `namespace`, `return`, `var`, `void`, `while`), not a CEL type name (`int`, `uint`, `double`, `bool`, `string`, `bytes`, `list`, `map`, `null_type`, `type`, `dyn`, `timestamp`, `duration`), not one of `data`, `request`, `actor`, `input`, `waits`, `item`, `event`, `sent`, `now`, `optional`, `cel`, `google`, and does not start with `cel1_` | the definition | `approverGroup`, `ls_domains` |
| Data key and path segment | a Name | its object | `v_title`, `requester`, `tk_review__pressed` |
| Schema property name | a Name | its schema object | `q_title`, `engLead` |
| Schema reference | `<schema ID>@<version>`; schema ID is Names joined by `.`; version an integer from 1 | the definition | `changeForm@1`, `tk_request_form.btn_rf_submit@1` |
| Connection ID | `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$`; `engine`, `system` and `platform` are reserved (Integrations 7.1) | the platform | `jira` |
| Operation, data source, trigger event | `<name>@<version>`; name `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}$`, version `^[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$` (Integrations 7.2). Stored apart from the connection; the definition never stores `<connection>.<name>@<version>`. | its connection | `createIssue@1`, `ticketCreated@1` |
| Notification rule ID | one or more Names joined by `.`. A default rule or an authored Notify is one Name (`n_task`, `act_notify_lead`). | the `notifications` block | `n_stopped` |
| Trigger binding ID | a Name: the authored `StartsWhen` ID | the `triggers` block | `sw_helpdesk_ticket` |
| Event rule ID | a Name: the authored action ID | the `events` block | `act_send_change_deployed` |
| Nobody-to-ask rule ID | `<full element ID of the person wait>__nobody` | the `nobodyToAsk` block | `st_review__tasks.tk_review__nobody` |
| Told ID | a Name: the authored `ThingTold` ID | the definition | `told_change_deployed` |
| Told value name | a Name | its event rule | `runLink` |

Compiler-added names are `<authored item ID>__<local name>` (compiler 1.1). Authored IDs never contain `__`, so everything before the first `__` is the authored item. Every compiled name fits the 64-character `Name` because an authored ID is at most 40 characters (E-23). The membership read of a task is the call wait `<task ID>__members` in the task's own engine stage (section 3.9).

## 3. Fields

"Written" says whether publish writes the field in every definition. "Always" means it is written with its default when nothing was given.

### 3.1 Top level

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | `1` | Format number. | Always |
| `workflow` | Workflow ID | The `definitions.workflow` key (L1). | Always |
| `version` | integer | The `definitions.version` key. | Always |
| `compiler` | string | The `core` version that compiled or expanded it (E-3). Diagnostic; nothing branches on it. | Always |
| `runtime` | Runtime | The pinned profiles (section 3.14). | Always |
| `start` | full element ID | The start wait: a person wait of `root.initial`. | Always |
| `root` | RootStage | The root stage and every child stage. | Always |
| `statuses` | Status[] | May be empty. | Always |
| `notifications` | NotificationRule[] | Authored rules in document order, then the default rules. | Always |
| `constants` | map of constant name to Json | Fixed at publish; readable in CEL by name. May be `{}`. | Always |
| `types` | DeclaredTypes | The declared types `decide` uses to read JSON into CEL (section 3.12). | Always |
| `schemas` | map of schema reference to PinnedSchema | Every schema an outcome names, and no other. | Always |
| `origins` | map of origin key to Origin | Section 3.11. | Always |
| `triggers` | TriggerBinding[] | Section 3.7. `decide` never reads it. | Only when non-empty |
| `events` | EventRule[] | Section 3.8. `decide` never reads it. | Only when non-empty |
| `nobodyToAsk` | NobodyToAskRule[] | Section 3.9. `decide` never reads it. | Only when non-empty |

### 3.2 Stages

| Field | Type | Root | Child | Written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | Stage ID | `"root"` | the stage ID | Always |
| `initial` | Stage ID | the child stage a request starts in | not present | Always on the root |
| `stages` | ChildStage[] | the child stages | not present: one level of children | Always on the root |
| `final` | boolean | not present: the root is never final | `true` closes the request on entry. Default `false`. | Always on a child |
| `status` | status ID, nullable | not present | the stage's status, or `null` | Always on a child |
| `waits` | Wait[] | not present | declared order | Always on a child |
| `transitions` | Transition[] | not present | declared order | Always on a child |

A `Path` is an array of data keys, one per segment: `["engLead"]`, `["form", "title"]`. A final stage has `waits: []` and `transitions: []`.

### 3.3 Waits

Every wait:

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | local ID | | Always |
| `kind` | `"person"` or `"call"` | Discriminator. | Always |

**Person wait** (`kind: "person"`):

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | `"obligation"` or `"option"` | | `"obligation"` | Always |
| `assignees` | CEL | A list of `{type, id}` references, evaluated when the wait opens. A reference whose `type` is not `user` or `group` is dropped then and not recorded. | none: the author or compiler gives it | Always |
| `may` | CEL | Boolean, evaluated at act time. | `"true"` | Always |
| `outcomes` | Outcome[] | At least one. | | Always |

**Outcome**:

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | outcome ID | | | Always |
| `schema` | schema reference | The schema the submitted data must satisfy. | | Always |
| `checks` | Check[] | Run in order after the schema and the lookups. | `[]` | Always |
| `lookups` | Lookup[] | One per answer that names an item of a data source, in form order (E-20, Integrations 11.2). | `[]` | Always |

**Check**:

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | check ID | Recorded in evidence and in a `check` refusal. | Always |
| `when` | CEL | Boolean; the outcome is accepted only if it is `true`. An error refuses with `rule-error`; it is never `false`. | Always |
| `message` | string | The author's own text, passed through on refusal (E-7). `""` for a compiler-added check; the frontend words it by check ID and location. | Always |

**Lookup** (Integrations 11.2):

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `property` | Name | The outcome's data property whose answer is looked up: the question ID. | Always |
| `connection` | connection ID | | Always |
| `source` | `<name>@<version>` | A data-source entry of that connection. | Always |
| `inputs` | map of input field ID to CEL | Over `input`, `data` and the constants. An expression may give an optional; `optional.none()` leaves that input out. `{}` when the source takes none. | Always |
| `storedField` | Name | The item field compared with the answer. | Always |
| `labelField` | Name | The item field shown as the label. | Always |
| `answer` | `"item"` or `"person"` | `item`: the answer is `{stored, label}`, compared by `stored`, and the item's `labelField` value is recorded as `label`. `person`: the answer is a user `Ref`, compared by its `id` with `storedField`; nothing but the `Ref` is recorded (directory choices). | Always |

**Call wait** (`kind: "call"`):

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default | Written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connection` | connection ID | A configured instance of connector code (L2). The connector is never recorded. | | Always |
| `op` | `<name>@<version>` | An operation entry of that connection. Its arguments and result shape never change. | | Always |
| `args` | map of argument name to CEL | One expression per argument, evaluated when the wait opens. An argument whose expression gives `optional.none()` is left out of the call (L13). | `{}` | Always |
| `effect` | `"read"` or `"write"` | The compiler writes `write` for an operation of sort `write` or `await` (Integrations 10.1). | | Always |
| `onFailure` | `"fault"` or `"outcome"` | | `"fault"` | Always |
| `keyScope` | `"activation"`, nullable | The idempotency key is derived (`event-payloads.md` section 3.4). A read is always `"activation"`. A write is `"activation"`, or `null` when `idempotencyKey` is given. | read: `"activation"`; write: none, it must be given | Always |
| `idempotencyKey` | CEL, nullable | An explicit key: a string of 1 to 255 characters, or the turn faults with `key-invalid`. Exactly one of `keyScope` and `idempotencyKey` is non-null. | `null` | Always |

A call wait has no `role`: it counts like an obligation in `otherwise` and in the stuck check. Its outcomes are always `ok` and `failed` and are not listed. `ok` data has the shape `types.results[connection][op]`; `failed` data is `{code, message}`, `code` one of the operation's catalogue failure codes (E-23).

What the compiler writes for the key (E-23):

| Call | `keyScope` | `idempotencyKey` |
|---|---|---|
| A read | `"activation"` | `null` |
| A write or await, "when the stage is entered again": `again` | `"activation"` | `null` |
| A write or await, `once` | `null` | `"'once.' + request.id + '.<action ID>'"`, the action ID as a literal: `'once.' + request.id + '.act_create_jira_issue'` |

"Once" is an explicit key because a stage with a second status is emitted twice: the explicit key is the same in both copies. A request ID of at most 64 characters and an action ID of at most 40 keep it within 110 characters.

### 3.4 Transitions

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | local ID | | Always |
| `otherwise` | boolean | The built-in `otherwise` condition. Default `false`. A stage has at most one, and it is last (L14). | Always |
| `when` | CEL, nullable | The condition. `null` exactly when `otherwise` is `true`. | Always |
| `set` | SetEntry[] | Default `[]`. | Always |
| `to` | Stage ID | Target stage. A self-target exits and re-enters. | Always |

SetEntry: `{path: Path, expr: CEL}`, both always written. The expression may give an optional; `optional.none()` removes the path, and removing a path that is absent records nothing (E-24; `event-payloads.md` section 5.11). Two paths in one transition's sets do not overlap.

### 3.5 Statuses

`{id, label, color}`, all always written. `label` is the words at this version. `color` is one of `grey`, `red`, `amber`, `green`, `blue`, `purple`, `teal`, `pink` (the authored format's colours); an open set, cheap to change.

### 3.6 Notification rules

Integrations 12.1, as amended by E-21.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | notification rule ID | With `(requestId, seq)`, the notifier's dedupe key. | Always |
| `on.event` | string | A recorded event type, or `"Stuck"`. | Always |
| `on.element` | string, nullable | Narrows the match to one element. Matched against `wait.element` (`WaitOpened`, `WaitCompleted`, `WaitCancelled`, `WaitSkipped`, `CallResultLate`), `element` (`Faulted`, `DataSet`), `stage` (`StageEntered`, `StageExited`, `RequestClosed`), or `<stage>.<transition>` (`TransitionFired`). Must be `null` for `RequestStarted`, `Overridden` and `Stuck`. When not null it names an element of the definition of a kind its event type can name (publish check, section 9): any wait for `WaitOpened`, `WaitCompleted`, `WaitCancelled` and `WaitSkipped`; a call wait for `CallResultLate`; a wait or a transition for `Faulted` and `DataSet` (they share one namespace, section 2); a stage, the root included, for `StageEntered` and `StageExited`; a final stage for `RequestClosed`; a transition, as `<stage>.<transition>`, for `TransitionFired`. Default `null`. | Always |
| `when` | CEL | Boolean over the rule context (section 4). Default `"true"`. | Always |
| `send.message` | Message | `{words}` or `{parts}`. | Always |
| `send.to` | Recipient[] | At least one. | Always |

Message:

| Variant | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `{words}` | `words`: string | A key of the platform's words file (`contract/words/notifications.json`, the frontend's). Format 1 uses `task.assigned` and `request.stuck` (E-21). The notifier fills the placeholders from the event, the request and the version's authored source. |
| `{parts}` | `parts`: MessagePart[] | An authored Notify message, in order. A part is `{text}` (the author's literal text) or `{value: CEL, kind: ValueKind}` (a chip; `kind` written by the compiler). A `value` that gives `optional.none()` renders as empty. |

Recipient: `{type: "expr", expr: CEL}`, a list of `{type, id}` references over the rule context; or `{type: "workflowAdmins"}`, the per-workflow setting, resolved when the notifier sends. A reference that is not a user or a group is skipped. An `expr` that gives nothing (`optional.none()`) or a value that is not a list is a rule error (Integrations 12.3, 6.4; spec v2.19, E-28): nothing is sent for that rule and a rule-error log line is written.

`Stuck` is not a recorded event type. A rule `on: {event: "Stuck", element: null}` matches a turn after which the request's stuck state (Integrations 11.5) is stuck and differs from the state before the turn. Its `event` is `{reason, stage}`: `reason` one of `action-failed`, `nobody-to-ask`, `nothing-fits`, `error` (an open set); `stage` the authored stage (Integrations 11.5 table). A rule on `WaitOpened` sends nothing when that wait is no longer open at the end of the turn: completed, cancelled or skipped in the same turn (E-27, spec v2.18); that rule is the notifier's, not a field.

The reason is worked out from the state after the turn, the first that applies (E-23, Integrations 11.5):

| Recorded state | `reason` |
|---|---|
| A `Faulted` not cleared, `kind: "error"`, `error.code: "call-failed"`, whatever added the call | `action-failed` |
| A `Faulted` not cleared, `kind: "error"`, any other code | `error` |
| An open obligation matches its rule in the `nobodyToAsk` block (section 3.9) | `nobody-to-ask` |
| The request is open, has no fault, and has no open obligation and no open call | `nothing-fits` |

The default rules of format 1, one built-in rule per event and none per reason (E-21, E-23). The compiler writes them, and so does the demo (E-23):

| ID | `on` | `when` | `send` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_task` | `{event: "WaitOpened", element: null}` | `event.kind == 'person' && event.role == 'obligation'` | `{message: {words: "task.assigned"}, to: [{type: "expr", expr: "event.assignees"}]}` |
| `n_stopped` | `{event: "Stuck", element: null}` | `true` | `{message: {words: "request.stuck"}, to: [{type: "workflowAdmins"}]}` |

`n_stopped` fires for every reason and the notifier fills `{reason}` in `request.stuck`. A rule has no `stuckReason` field; there is no `n_noAssignee` and no `task.nobodyToAsk` message (E-21, E-23): nobody-to-ask is a stuck reason, worked out from the `nobodyToAsk` block, and `n_stopped` sends it.

### 3.7 Trigger bindings: `triggers`

Integrations 9.1. Declared order is the authored `startsWhen` order. Only the bindings of a workflow's highest published version are live.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | binding ID | The authored `StartsWhen` ID. Recorded as `RequestStarted.trigger.id`. | Always |
| `connection` | connection ID | | Always |
| `event` | `<name>@<version>` | A trigger entry of that connection. | Always |
| `when` | CEL | Boolean over `sent` and the constants. `"true"` when the binding has no "Only when". | Always |
| `outcome` | outcome ID | The start wait's outcome the binding presses. | Always |
| `data` | map of property name to CEL | The start outcome's data, over `sent` and the constants. A key is a property of the outcome's schema; `requester` is the Requester when the binding names one. An expression may give an optional; `optional.none()` leaves the key absent. A question with a Show when is wrapped in it (E-20). | Always |

The mapping runs before the turn, outside `decide`. An error refuses the start with `mapping-error`; it never faults a request.

### 3.8 Event rules: `events`

Integrations 13.3. What the workflow tells other systems, published as `request.told@1`.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | event rule ID | The authored action ID. | Always |
| `on` | `{event, element}` | As a notification rule's `on`. The compiler writes `StageEntered` of the chain stage that holds the action. | Always |
| `when` | CEL | Boolean over the rule context. `"true"` when the action has no "Only when". | Always |
| `told` | `{id, words}` | The `ThingTold` ID and its words at this version. | Always |
| `values` | map of told value name to CEL | The authored values, keyed by the names outside systems receive. `optional.none()` leaves the name out. `{}` when none. | Always |

### 3.9 Nobody-to-ask rules: `nobodyToAsk`

Integrations 11.5 and spec v2.17 section 6; the design kept by E-23. One rule per person wait the compiler emits (one per task), in stage then task order. `decide` never reads it; the notifier, the publisher, the `requests` projection and the story read it, so they agree (E-20).

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | nobody-to-ask rule ID | | Always |
| `wait` | full element ID | The person wait it judges. | Always |
| `members` | full element ID, nullable | The membership read: a call wait in the same stage as `wait`, whose recorded `membersOf@1` result lists the members of the wait's groups. `null` when who is asked is never a group. | Always |
| `excludeRequester` | boolean | `true` when the Requester may not answer. | Always |

A person wait that no rule names is judged as if by a rule with `members: null` and `excludeRequester: false`. The match itself is Integrations 11.5's (E-24): the wait matches when nobody can answer it. Who can answer is the people asked directly (the users among the recorded assignees) plus the recorded members of the groups asked (from the membership read's result), minus the Requester when `excludeRequester`; nobody to ask means that set is empty. While a group's members are unknown (the read has no result, or `members` is null), a wait that asks that group does not match. It reads only recorded events. The read that counts is the one in the same activation as the wait, because both are waits of one engine stage.

- **A failed read contributes nobody from its groups;** a person asked directly still counts (E-24). Retry re-enters the stage, which reads the group again and asks the stage's tasks again.
- **A rule whose evaluation errors counts as no match for every reader,** and the error is logged in `rule_errors` (E-23). A format 1 rule holds no CEL; the clause covers a fault in working out the match.

**The membership read the compiler emits** (Integrations 11.5, E-23). For every task whose who-is-asked may resolve to a group, the task's engine stage (the tasks step) declares, before the person wait, a call wait:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `<task ID>__members` |
| `connection` | the catalogue's `directoryConnection` |
| `op` | `membersOf@1` |
| `args` | `{groups: "(<the task's assignees expression>).filter(r, r.type == 'group')"}`, which gives `[]` when the assignees hold no group; the read is opened all the same |
| `effect`, `onFailure` | `"read"`, `"outcome"` |
| `keyScope`, `idempotencyKey` | `"activation"`, `null` |

It is opened with the task, so the task is open and visible at once. No transition reads it. Because a call wait counts like an obligation in `otherwise`, the tasks step's normal exit (`<stage>__answered`) has an explicit `when` that every task's wait is completed (`waits.<task>.status == 'completed'` for each, joined with `&&`), never `otherwise: true`, so a pending read cannot hold up an answered task. Early arrows keep their own conditions. Leaving the step cancels the read (`WaitCancelled`, cause `stage-exit`); the read is then dropped quietly, sent or not, so no `CallResultLate` is recorded for it and no alert is raised (E-24).

"People in [group]" under who is asked compiles to asking the group itself, so it is covered by this read and makes no read of its own (E-24). A `members` step or an "is in group" test inside a condition is not this read: it compiles to a separate recorded `membersOf@1` call in its own engine stage, placed just before the step that uses it (E-23). The `nobodyToAsk` block never names it.

### 3.11 The origin map: `origins`

Compiler 12.1. `origins` maps an origin key to an Origin. Every element has exactly one element key. A field key exists for a field holding CEL whose origin differs from its element's (L7, E-18).

| Origin key | For |
|---|---|
| `stage:<stage ID>` | a stage, the root included |
| `wait:<full element ID>` | a wait |
| `outcome:<full wait ID>/<outcome ID>` | a person wait's outcome |
| `check:<full wait ID>/<outcome ID>/<check ID>` | a check |
| `transition:<full element ID>` | a transition |
| `rule:<notification rule ID>` | a notification rule |
| `trigger:<binding ID>` | a trigger binding |
| `event:<event rule ID>` | an event rule |
| `nobody:<nobody-to-ask rule ID>` | a nobody-to-ask rule |
| `<element key>#<JSON Pointer>` | a field of that element: `wait:A__run.A#/args/summary`, `outcome:S__tasks.T/btn#/lookups/0/inputs/group`, `transition:S__tasks.S__answered#/set/2/expr`, `rule:act_x#/send/message/parts/1/value` |

The pointer is RFC 6901 into the element's own JSON object, exactly what `Faulted.error.field` carries, so a fault resolves to its field's origin first and to its element's otherwise. Array indices in a pointer are positional and meaningful only in this version.

Origin:

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | string[] | A compiled definition: one authored item ID, or the workflow's `wf_` ID for workflow-level elements, so `{item: [i], part: p}` reads as the authored `Location {item: i, part: p}`. A hand-written definition: the path of names in its notation; `[]` is the workflow. | Always |
| `part` | string, nullable | A compiled definition: the authored `Location.part` (`contract/authored-format.ts` `LOCATION_PARTS`). `null` for the item as a whole. | Always |

What the author is shown comes from this map; a fault's field pointer is for engineers (L7, E-7).

**The authored stage of an engine stage** (E-27, E-28; spec v2.19 `integrations.md` 11.5), which a stuck request is reported in, is read from this map alone, by the compiler's conventions (compiler 12): an engine stage whose `stage:` origin has part `tasks` or `arrows` names its authored stage (the origin's item); an engine stage whose origin item is its own ID (an ending, or a hand-written stage) is its own authored stage; from any other step, follow the transitions, breadth first, to the first such stage, which in a compiled definition is the stage the step belongs to. For Try it's unfinished step, whose origin item is an arrow, it is the stage that arrow leaves. A definition with no origin map reports the engine stage itself. Core's `authoredStageOf` is the one implementation.

### 3.12 Declared types: `types`

Decided by E-23. A published definition carries the type of every data path, every constant and every operation result. After `JSON.parse`, `3` and `3.0` cannot be told apart, so the declared type must travel with the definition, or E-18's rule (a number is always a double) cannot hold. `types` holds every type `decide` needs that `schemas` does not.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `types.data` | map of data key to JsonSchema | One entry per top-level data key a Set of this definition can write, and no other. Its schema types every path below that key. | Always; `{}` when no Set writes |
| `types.constants` | map of constant name to JsonSchema | One entry per key of `constants`, and no other. | Always; `{}` when there are none |
| `types.results` | map of connection ID to map of `<name>@<version>` to JsonSchema | The `ok` result of every operation a call wait names, and no other: the catalogue entry's `result` fields mapped by Integrations 8.3. | Always; `{}` when there is no call wait |

The schemas here are `jsonschema-1` schemas (section 6), used for typing only; nothing is validated against `types`.

**Who writes it, and when.** Publish writes it: the server's compile (E-3) derives `types.data` from the value kinds of the authored values (the Integrations 8.3 mapping, as for `schemas`), `types.constants` from the authored lists and constants, and `types.results` from the catalogue entries the workflow uses, as they are at that publish. Core's preview compile derives the same. A hand-written definition (the demo) carries it as written, and publish checks it (section 9). It never changes after publish: an operation version's shape never changes (Integrations 8.6).

**How `decide` uses it.** Whenever `decide` turns a JSON value into a CEL value (the data document, a constant, a recorded result, submitted input), the wrapper reads the value by its declared type (section 5.4): a schema `number` is a CEL `double`, even `3`; a schema `integer` is an `int`; an `object` with `properties` an object type; and so on down the schema. The declarations are taken from:

| CEL name | Declared by |
|---|---|
| `data.<key>` | `types.data[<key>]` |
| a constant | `types.constants[<name>]` |
| `waits.<call>.data` | the merge of its two outcomes' shapes: `types.results[<connection>][<op>]` for `ok` and `{code: string, message: string}` for `failed` |
| `waits.<person>.data` | the merge of its outcomes' pinned schemas in `schemas` |
| `input` | the outcome's pinned schema in `schemas` |

**A wait's data is typed as the merge of its outcomes' shapes** (E-26). A field that is declared in one outcome only keeps that outcome's type. A field whose type differs between outcomes is untyped (`dyn`). The type does not depend on a guard on the outcome, because the check environment cannot see one.
| `request`, `actor`, `waits.<id>` fields, `event` | section 4 |

A path that no declaration covers (a property a schema does not declare, a position inside `event`'s data) reads as `dyn`: a JSON integer within +/-(2^53 - 1) is an `int`, any other number a `double`. The check environment declares the same types, so an expression that mixes them is refused at publish, not at run time.

### 3.13 Pinned schemas: `schemas`

`schemas` maps a schema reference to `{id, version, schema}`, all always written. `schema` is the JSON Schema itself, in full, so the definition depends on no other store. The compiler derives it from the authored form (E-6) by the mapping of Integrations 8.3, with `additionalProperties: false`. A person is a user `Ref` (`{type: "user", id}`), a group a group `Ref`, never a bare ID (E-20). A compiled schema ID is `<task ID>.<button ID>` and its version is always 1 (compiler 1.2): it is meaningful only within one definition version.

### 3.14 Runtime pins

| Field | Type | Format 1 value | Written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runtime.cel` | string | `"cel-1"` (section 5) | Always |
| `runtime.validator` | string | `"jsonschema-1"` (section 6) | Always |

The spec fixes both per definition format, so in format 1 these fields hold only these values. They are written so a reader of a stored document sees the pins without knowing the format table. A profile is immutable; a behaviour change in either is a new profile and a new format.

## 4. CEL contexts, per field

Scope is lexical (spec section 2): `waits` holds the waits of the declaring stage and the root, in their current activation, named by local ID.

| Field | Evaluated | Variables | Result type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Person `assignees` | when the wait opens | `data`, `request`, `waits`, constants | list of `{type, id}` |
| Person `may` | at act time | `data`, `request`, `actor`, `waits`, constants | bool |
| Check `when` | at act time, after the lookups | `data`, `request`, `actor`, `waits`, `input`, constants | bool |
| Lookup `inputs` | when choices are listed, and at act time | `input`, `data`, `request`, constants (`request` since spec v2.18, E-27, so the Requester and "Started on" work there; never `request.id`, spec v2.19, E-28) | the input field's type, or optional |
| Call `args`, `idempotencyKey` | when the wait opens | `data`, `request`, `waits`, constants | the argument's type or optional; string |
| Transition `when`, Set `expr` | at the end of every turn | `data`, `request`, `waits`, constants | bool; the path's type or optional |
| Notification `when`, recipient `expr`, part `value` | by the notifier, after the turn commits | `event`, `request`, `data`, constants | bool; list of `{type, id}`; any |
| Event rule `when`, `values` | by the publisher | `event`, `request`, `data`, constants | bool; any |
| Binding `when`, `data` | before the start turn | `sent`, constants | bool; the property's type or optional |

| Variable | Shape |
|---|---|
| `data` | The request's data document, typed by `types.data`. In rules: folded up to and including the matched event (Integrations 12.2). |
| `request` | `{id: string, by: {type: string, id: string}, at: string}`. `by` is the starter; `at` is the `RequestStarted` time as recorded (read it with `timestamp()`). |
| `actor` | `{type: string, id: string}` |
| `input` | The submitted data, typed by the outcome's schema; after the lookups, a source answer's `label` is the source's. |
| `waits.<local ID>` | `{status, outcome, by, data}`: `status` one of `open`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `skipped`; `outcome` `""` unless completed; `by` `{type: "", id: ""}` until completed. `data` may be read only under a guard on that wait's outcome; it is typed as the merge of the outcomes' shapes (section 3.12): the outcomes' schemas for a person wait, `types.results` for `ok` and `{code, message}` for `failed` for a call wait. |
| `event` | The matched event's payload (`event-payloads.md`), or `{reason, stage}` for `Stuck`, with `stage` the authored stage (section 12, item 7). Every number in a payload's own fields is an `int`. A data position inside it (`data`, `input.data`, `args`, `patch[].value`, `reads[].value`) is read as `dyn`: rules that need typed values read `data` instead. A nullable field holding `null` is CEL `null`. |
| `sent` | The trigger entry's event fields, typed by Integrations 8.3. |
| Each constant | By name, typed by `types.constants`. |

## 5. Profile `cel-1`

The CEL profile of format 1. It is what is pinned; the library is its implementation. A change to any item below, including a library version, is a new profile and a new definition format. The rules are implemented in `engine/packages/core/src/cel/` and are tried by `engine/packages/core/test/cel/` (E-20).

### 5.1 Implementation pinned

| Package | Version | Integrity |
|---|---|---|
| `@marcbachmann/cel-js` | 8.0.0, exact | `sha512-oaTrAziGr3zDLFiMt/yLU3nZuRMawyWQB5X1a0I7s9eGy3JYzX9l8ZXXHyMd64nzbeVFZTewuUShwsZQdK6UCA==` |
| `@bufbuild/re2` | 0.6.2, exact | `sha512-/J0aKLB8jZSRe8P5h988GGA15pX/QTBcYvmUzvSdqSJlandchxDxbvykJf1RUpR4bgAEM3eobH8rarINw74bCQ==` |

The wrapper is the only code that imports the library. It keeps two library environments: a check environment that declares every variable with its type, and an evaluation environment that declares every variable `dyn` and types the values itself (section 5.4).

### 5.2 Library options, written out

| Option | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `enableOptionalTypes` | `true` | |
| `homogeneousAggregateLiterals` | `false` | A list or map literal may mix value types (E-20). |
| `unlistedVariablesAreDyn` | `false` | An undeclared name is a check error. |
| `limits.maxAstNodes` | 100000 | |
| `limits.maxDepth` | 250 | |
| `limits.maxListElements` | 1000 | |
| `limits.maxMapEntries` | 1000 | |
| `limits.maxCallArguments` | 32 | |

### 5.3 The language

| Area | cel-1 |
|---|---|
| Syntax | CEL as the pinned library parses it. |
| Macros | `has`, `all`, `exists`, `exists_one`, `map`, `filter`, `cel.bind`. |
| Optionals | `.?`, `[?]`, `optional.of`, `optional.none`, `orValue`, `or`, `hasValue`, `value`. |
| Equality | `==` and `!=` take two operands of one type, objects included, compared by value (the wrapper registers equality for object types). `int`, `uint` and `double` are never mixed in equality or arithmetic: `1 == 1.0` and `x * 2` with `x` a `double` are check errors; write `2.0`. Ordering (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) may compare `int`, `uint` and `double` with each other. |
| Functions and operators | Exactly those of the pinned list below (E-23). Nothing else the library may register is in `cel-1`. |
| Time | No clock, no `now` (spec section 2). UTC only. Timestamps hold milliseconds. |
| Purity | Synchronous; no I/O, no randomness. A function that returns a Promise is an error (`async-not-allowed`). |

**The pinned list.** Source: the library's own registrations (`lib/functions.js`, `overloads.js`, `macros.js`, `optional.js` of 8.0.0) and the wrapper (`src/cel/environment.ts`, `functions.ts`). Every row was called through the wrapper; the rows the wrapper adds or replaces have tests in `engine/packages/core/test/`. "Library" means the library's behaviour is kept; "replaced" means the wrapper's.

Operators:

| Operator | Overloads | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `!a` | `bool` → `bool` | |
| `-a` | `int` → `int`; `double` → `double` | No negation of `uint` or `duration`. |
| `a && b`, `a \|\| b` | `bool`, `bool` → `bool` | An error on one side is absorbed when the other side decides, in either order. |
| `c ? a : b` | `bool`, `T`, `T` → `T` | |
| `a + b` | `int`, `uint`, `double`, `string`, `bytes`, `list<V>`, `duration` with itself → the same; `timestamp + duration` → `timestamp` | `duration + timestamp` is refused (below). |
| `a - b` | `int`, `uint`, `double`, `duration` with itself → the same; `timestamp - duration` → `timestamp`; `timestamp - timestamp` → `duration` | |
| `a * b`, `a / b` | `int`, `uint`, `double` with itself → the same | `int` division truncates; `int` or `uint` by zero is `division-by-zero`; `int` beyond int64 is `numeric-overflow`. A `double` by zero is infinite and fails as `double-not-finite` when it leaves CEL. No `duration * int`: use `days(n)`. |
| `a % b` | `int`, `uint` with itself → the same | By zero: `modulo-by-zero`. |
| `a == b`, `a != b` | `bool`, `string`, `int`, `uint`, `double`, `bytes`, `null`, `type`, `timestamp`, `duration`, `list<V>`, `map<K, V>` and each object type, with itself → `bool` | No equality of two optionals. |
| `a < b`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | `bool`, `string`, `int`, `uint`, `double`, `timestamp`, `duration` with itself; `int`, `uint`, `double` with each other → `bool` | Strings by code point. |
| `x in l`, `k in m` | `V in list<V>`; `K in map<K, V>` → `bool` | |
| `a.f`, `a[i]`, `m[k]` | object or map field; list and `int`; map and key | Missing is `no-such-key` or `index-out-of-bounds`. |
| `a.?f`, `a[?k]` | optional selection and index → `optional<T>` | |

Functions, macros and names:

| Name | Overloads | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `has(a.f)` | → `bool` | library macro |
| `l.all(x, p)`, `l.exists(x, p)`, `l.exists_one(x, p)` | list or map (its keys), a name, a `bool` → `bool` | library macros; one iteration name only |
| `l.map(x, e)`, `l.map(x, p, e)`, `l.filter(x, p)` | list or map (its keys) → `list` | library macros |
| `cel.bind(x, v, e)` | → the type of `e` | library macro |
| `optional.of(v)`, `optional.none()` | → `optional<T>` | library |
| `o.hasValue()`, `o.value()`, `o.or(o2)`, `o.orValue(v)` | on `optional<T>` → `bool`, `T`, `optional<T>`, `T` | library; `value()` of none is `optional-value-missing` |
| `size(x)`, `x.size()` | `string` (code points), `bytes`, `list`, `map` → `int` | library |
| `s.contains(t)`, `s.startsWith(t)`, `s.endsWith(t)` | `string`, `string` → `bool` | library |
| `s.matches(p)` | `string`, `string` → `bool` | replaced: RE2 (`@bufbuild/re2`), true if the pattern matches any substring; no lookaround or backreference (`invalid-regular-expression`); `(?i)` works; linear time |
| `s.lowerAscii()`, `s.upperAscii()` | `string` → `string` | replaced: change only `A`-`Z` and `a`-`z` |
| `s.trim()` | `string` → `string` | library |
| `s.indexOf(t)`, `s.indexOf(t, i)`, `s.lastIndexOf(t)`, `s.lastIndexOf(t, i)` | → `int`; `-1` when absent | library; positions count UTF-16 units |
| `s.substring(i)`, `s.substring(i, j)` | → `string` | library; out of range is `index-out-of-bounds` |
| `s.split(sep)`, `s.split(sep, n)` | → `list<string>` | library |
| `l.join()`, `l.join(sep)` | `list<string>` → `string` | library |
| `bool(x)` | `bool`; `string` (`true`, `True`, `TRUE`, `t`, `1`, and the same for false) → `bool` | library |
| `int(x)` | `int`, `double`, `string`, `uint`, `timestamp` → `int` | replaced: `int(double)` truncates toward zero and refuses NaN, infinity and values outside int64; `int(string)` takes a signed decimal within int64; `int(uint)` within int64; `int(timestamp)` is Unix seconds, floored |
| `uint(x)` | `uint`, `int`, `double`, `string` → `uint` | library |
| `double(x)` | `double`, `int`, `uint`, `string` → `double` | library |
| `string(x)` | `string`, `bool`, `int`, `uint`, `double`, `bytes` → `string` | library; no `string(timestamp)`: use `asDate` |
| `bytes(x)` | `string`, `bytes` → `bytes` | library; a `bytes` value cannot leave CEL (`not-json`) |
| `b.hex()`, `b.base64()`, `b.string()`, `b.at(i)` | on `bytes` → `string`, `string`, `string`, `int` | library |
| `dyn(x)` | → `dyn` | library |
| `type(x)` and the type names `int`, `uint`, `double`, `bool`, `string`, `bytes`, `list`, `map`, `null_type`, `type`, `google.protobuf.Timestamp`, `google.protobuf.Duration` | → `type` | library; a `type` value cannot leave CEL (`not-json`) |
| `timestamp(x)` | `string`, `int`, `timestamp` → `timestamp` | replaced: a string is RFC 3339 `date-time` only, with a mandatory offset (`Z` or `+hh:mm`), years 0001 to 9999, no leap second, fractions beyond milliseconds truncated, anything else `invalid-timestamp`; an `int` is Unix seconds within years 0001 to 9999 |
| `date(s)` | `string` → `timestamp` | added: a `YYYY-MM-DD` string as 00:00 UTC; a malformed or non-existent date is `invalid-date` |
| `duration(s)` | `string` → `duration` | library: Go-style, units `h`, `m`, `s`, `ms`, `us`, `ns` (`"72h"`, `"1h30m"`) |
| `days(n)` | `int` → `duration` | added (E-23): `n` × 86,400 seconds; beyond +/-3,650,000 days is an `overflow` error with detail `days-out-of-range`, apart from an `int` leaving its range (section 5.7, E-26) |
| `asDate(t)` | `timestamp` → `string` | added (E-23): the UTC date of `t` as `YYYY-MM-DD`; a timestamp outside years 0001 to 9999 is `invalid-timestamp`. The compiler applies it wherever a formula's result is used as a date value, so `asDate(date(data.v_due) + days(3))` fills a date. |
| `t.getFullYear()`, `t.getMonth()` (from 0), `t.getDate()` (from 1), `t.getDayOfMonth()` (from 0), `t.getDayOfWeek()` (0 is Sunday), `t.getHours()`, `t.getMinutes()`, `t.getSeconds()`, `t.getMilliseconds()` | `timestamp` → `int`, in UTC | library, without the time-zone argument |
| `t.getDayOfYear()` | `timestamp` → `int`, from 0, in UTC | replaced: the library's counts in the host's time zone (`date('2026-03-29').getDayOfYear()` gave 86 under `TZ=America/New_York` and 87 under `TZ=Europe/Berlin`), so the wrapper counts in UTC |
| `d.getHours()`, `d.getMinutes()`, `d.getSeconds()`, `d.getMilliseconds()` | `duration` → `int`: the whole duration in that unit, rounded down | library |
| `optional`, `cel`, `google` | names reserved by the library | library |

Refused:

| What | When | Code |
|---|---|---|
| An identifier or function name starting with `cel1_` (reserved for the wrapper) | check | `unknown-variable`, `unknown-function` |
| A timestamp getter with a time-zone argument (`getHours('Europe/Berlin')`, and likewise `getDate`, `getDayOfMonth`, `getDayOfWeek`, `getDayOfYear`, `getFullYear`, `getMilliseconds`, `getMinutes`, `getMonth`, `getSeconds`) | check | `time-zone-not-allowed` |
| `duration + timestamp`. The library registers it with the result typed `duration` while the value is a timestamp. Write `timestamp + duration`. Also refused at run time, where a `dyn` operand can hide it. | check; run time | `no-such-overload` |
| `b.json()` on `bytes`. It reads JSON numbers with no declared type and can give `null`. | check | `unknown-function` |
| A literal pattern using `\p` or `\P`. Refused when the formula is checked, not only at publish (E-26). | check, and so publish (spec section 6) | `unicode-class-not-allowed` |
| A non-literal pattern using `\p` or `\P` | run time | expression error `unicode-class-not-allowed`, kind `other` (spec section 6) |
| An undeclared variable | check | the library's code, kebab-case |
| Mixing `int`, `uint` and `double` in arithmetic or equality | check | the library's code, kebab-case |
| A comprehension with two iteration names; the CEL extension libraries (math, strings, encoders) | check | the library's code, kebab-case |

### 5.4 JSON into CEL

By the declared type (section 3.12, section 4):

| Declared | JSON value | CEL value |
|---|---|---|
| `string` | string | `string` |
| `boolean` | boolean | `bool` |
| `integer` | an integer within +/-(2^53 - 1) | `int`; outside the range: error `int-out-of-range` |
| `number` | any number | `double`, even `3` (L4) |
| `array` | array | `list`, items by `items` |
| `object` with `properties` | object | an object type; a property may be absent; an undeclared property is `dyn` |
| `object` without `properties` | object | `map(string, V)`, `V` from `additionalProperties` |
| none (`dyn`) | number | `int` if an integer within +/-(2^53 - 1), else `double` |
| any | `null` | `null`; occurs only in a nullable event field under `event` |

A JSON value that does not fit its declared type is error `context-type-mismatch` (kind `wrong-kind`).

### 5.5 CEL into JSON

| CEL value | JSON |
|---|---|
| `int`, `uint` | a number; outside +/-(2^53 - 1): error `int-out-of-range` |
| `double` | a number; NaN or infinity: error `double-not-finite` |
| `string`, `bool`, `list` | as is |
| `map`, object | an object; a key that is not a string is error `not-json` |
| `timestamp` | RFC 3339 with milliseconds and `Z`: `2026-11-15T09:30:00.000Z`; outside the years 0001 to 9999: error `invalid-timestamp` (E-26) |
| `null`, at the top or anywhere inside a list or map | error `null-value`, kind `wrong-kind`: the engine never writes `null` (E-26, spec v2.17). The expression module reports it for every value that leaves an expression, so no caller looks for one |
| `duration` | `"<seconds>s"` |
| `optional` at the top | its value, or absent for `optional.none()` |
| `optional` inside a list or map | error `not-json` |

### 5.7 Errors

An evaluation error is reported as an `ExpressionErrorKind` (`contract/core-api.md`) plus a specific kebab-case `detail`. The library's own code is never recorded (E-20).

| Detail | Kind |
|---|---|
| `no-such-key` | `no-such-key` |
| `index-out-of-bounds` | `index-out-of-range` |
| `optional-value-missing` | `absent-value` |
| `no-matching-overload`, `no-such-overload`, `field-type-mismatch`, `variable-type-mismatch`, `list-item-type-mismatch`, `cannot-index-type`, `context-type-mismatch`, `null-value` (a `null` leaving an expression, 5.5), `reserved-key` (a Set whose value holds a key starting with `$`, `event-payloads.md` 5.11) | `wrong-kind` |
| `division-by-zero`, `modulo-by-zero` | `division-by-zero` |
| `numeric-overflow`, `int-out-of-range`, `double-not-finite`, `days-out-of-range` (a `days()` beyond +/-3,650,000 days) | `overflow` |
| anything else (`invalid-date`, `invalid-timestamp`, `invalid-regular-expression`, `invalid-int`, `not-json`, `unicode-class-not-allowed`, `async-not-allowed`) | `other` |

A CEL error is never treated as `false` (spec section 3).

- **Key and index as fields** (E-26). For `no-such-key` and `index-out-of-range` the expression module reports the missing key and the list position as fields of the error, not only in its text. A `cel-error` fault takes `params.key` and `params.index` from these fields (`event-payloads.md`).
- **A `days()` overflow is told apart from an `int` leaving its range** (E-26): both are kind `overflow`; the detail is `days-out-of-range` for the one and `int-out-of-range` for the other.
- **An expression that gives `null` is an error** (E-26, spec v2.17): detail `null-value`, kind `wrong-kind`, for a `null` at the top or anywhere inside the value. The engine never writes `null`.
- **A timestamp outside the years 0001 to 9999 is an error** wherever it leaves an expression (E-26): into data, a call argument, a key or a rule's value.

### 5.8 Reads

What a condition read (E-20, L12) is recorded on `TransitionFired.reads` and on each check in `WaitCompleted.evidence`:

- Every path the expression selects from the request, rooted at `data`, `waits`, `request`, `actor` or `input`. Constants are not recorded: they are in the definition.
- A path is a maximal selection chain: field selections, and indexes whose key is a literal or is itself a request path (resolved to its value). Any other index ends the path at its receiver. A chain on a comprehension variable is cut back to the range it iterates.
- The value recorded is the value at the end of the path, whatever its type (a whole list or map included), or `absent`.
- Order: by the position in the source where each path begins; each path once. A path is listed even where evaluation short-circuits before it.
- A literal list index is a number segment: `["waits", "leads", "data", "groups", 0, "members", 0]`. A dotted wait ID is nested: `["waits", "primary", "decision", "outcome"]`.

## 6. Profile `jsonschema-1`

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Dialect | JSON Schema 2020-12 semantics. No `$schema` key is written (section 1). |
| Keywords allowed | `type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `uniqueItems`, `enum`, `const`, `format`, `minLength`, `maxLength`. Any other keyword is a publish error. |
| `type` | One type name, or a non-empty list of distinct type names (E-26). The names are `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`. `"null"` is never a type: a value is present or absent (section 1). |
| Subschemas | `additionalProperties` and `items` may be a schema, `true` or `false` (E-26). Only there: a property's schema under `properties`, and the schema at the top, are objects, never `true` or `false` (E-27). `items: false` refuses any item; `additionalProperties: false` refuses any undeclared property. |
| `enum`, `const` | Hold no `null` and no key starting with `$`. `enum` is non-empty, its members distinct. |
| Changes to data | None: no type coercion, no removal of unknown properties, no defaults applied. |
| Formats asserted | `date`: `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date. `date-time`: RFC 3339 with an offset; a leap second (`:60`) is refused, as `cel-1`'s `timestamp()` refuses it (E-26). `directory-object-id`: the directory's immutable object ID: 1 to 255 characters, none of them white space or a control character, until a real directory says otherwise (E-26). Any other format is a publish error. |
| Numbers | A number with no fractional part outside +/-(2^53 - 1) is refused, whatever its schema. |
| Lengths | `minLength` and `maxLength` count Unicode code points. |
| `uniqueItems` | Compares JSON values by value; object key order does not matter. |
| Refusal | One `invalid-data` refusal naming each failing property; the rule names are `InvalidDataRule` of `contract/core-api.md`. |

How each failure maps to a rule (E-26), as built:

| Failure | `InvalidDataRule` |
|---|---|
| `required` | `required` |
| `type`, `const`, `uniqueItems`, `items: false`, a key starting with `$`, a number that is not finite | `wrong-kind` |
| An undeclared property under `additionalProperties: false`: at the top of the answers (a question the form does not have) | `unknown-question` |
| The same inside an answer (a field the answer's schema does not have, such as `extra` in `{stored, label, extra}`) | `wrong-kind` (E-27) |
| `enum` | `not-a-choice` |
| `format` | `bad-format` |
| `minLength`, `maxLength` | `too-short`, `too-long` |
| An integer beyond +/-(2^53 - 1) | `out-of-range` |

The validator is written in core (`engine/packages/core/src/schema/`), not taken from a library: the profile is pinned for good per definition format, and it must run in a browser without code generation.

## 7. Storage in `definitions`

The data model's `definitions` columns hold the document with no change of content:

| Column | Holds |
|---|---|
| `document` | `format`, `workflow`, `version`, `compiler`, `runtime`, `start`, `root`, `statuses`, `notifications`, `constants`, `types`, `origins`, and `triggers`, `events`, `nobodyToAsk` when present |
| `schemas` | `schemas` |
| `authored`, `from_revision`, `core_version`, `format_version` | The authoring columns (E-23): the authored source, the draft revision it was published from, the `core` version that compiled it, and the format number. Not part of this format. |

`definitions.workflow` holds the workflow ID, as the document's `workflow` does, not its name. Reassembled, the two columns `document` and `schemas` give exactly the document of section 8. The split is cheap to change.

## 8. TypeScript

```ts
/** JSON with no null. Constants, types, schemas and parameters use it. */
export type Json = string | number | boolean | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };
/** CEL source text, profile cel-1. */
export type Cel = string;
export type WorkflowId = string;   // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$
export type StageId = string;      // Name; "root" for the root stage
export type LocalId = string;      // Names joined by "."
export type FullId = string;       // `${StageId}.${LocalId}`
export type SchemaRef = string;    // `${schemaId}@${version}`
export type ConnectionId = string; // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$
export type EntryRef = string;     // `${name}@${version}`, without the connection
export type Path = string[];
export type JsonSchema = { [keyword: string]: Json };   // profile jsonschema-1

export interface PublishedDefinition {
  format: 1;
  workflow: WorkflowId;
  version: number;
  compiler: string;
  runtime: Runtime;
  start: FullId;
  root: RootStage;
  statuses: Status[];
  notifications: NotificationRule[];
  constants: { [name: string]: Json };
  types: DeclaredTypes;
  schemas: { [ref: SchemaRef]: PinnedSchema };
  origins: { [originKey: string]: Origin };
  triggers?: TriggerBinding[];       // absent when empty; decide never reads it
  events?: EventRule[];              // absent when empty; decide never reads it
  nobodyToAsk?: NobodyToAskRule[];   // absent when empty; decide never reads it
}

export interface Runtime {
  cel: "cel-1";
  validator: "jsonschema-1";
}

export interface RootStage {
  id: "root";
  initial: StageId;
  stages: ChildStage[];
}

export interface ChildStage {
  id: StageId;
  final: boolean;
  status: string | null;             // a status ID
  waits: Wait[];
  transitions: Transition[];
}

export type Wait = PersonWait | CallWait;

export interface PersonWait {
  id: LocalId;
  kind: "person";
  role: "obligation" | "option";
  assignees: Cel;                    // -> list<{type, id}>
  may: Cel;                          // -> bool
  outcomes: Outcome[];
}

export interface Outcome {
  id: string;
  schema: SchemaRef;
  checks: Check[];
  lookups: Lookup[];
}

export interface Check {
  id: string;
  when: Cel;                         // -> bool; true means the check passes
  message: string;
}

export interface Lookup {
  property: string;
  connection: ConnectionId;
  source: EntryRef;                  // a dataSource entry
  inputs: { [field: string]: Cel };  // over input, data, constants
  storedField: string;
  labelField: string;
  answer: "item" | "person";
}

export interface CallWait {
  id: LocalId;
  kind: "call";
  connection: ConnectionId;
  op: EntryRef;                      // an operation entry
  args: { [name: string]: Cel };
  effect: "read" | "write";
  onFailure: "fault" | "outcome";
  keyScope: "activation" | null;
  idempotencyKey: Cel | null;
}

export interface Transition {
  id: LocalId;
  otherwise: boolean;
  when: Cel | null;                  // null exactly when otherwise is true
  set: SetEntry[];
  to: StageId;
}

export interface SetEntry {
  path: Path;
  expr: Cel;
}

export interface Status {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  color: "grey" | "red" | "amber" | "green" | "blue" | "purple" | "teal" | "pink" | (string & {});
}

export interface NotificationRule {
  id: string;
  on: RuleOn;
  when: Cel;
  send: { message: Message; to: Recipient[] };
}

export interface RuleOn {
  event: string;                     // a recorded event type, or "Stuck"
  element: string | null;
}

export type Message =
  | { words: string }                // a key of contract/words/notifications.json
  | { parts: MessagePart[] };

export type MessagePart =
  | { text: string }
  | { value: Cel; kind: ValueKind };

/** contract/authored-format.ts ValueKind. */
export type ValueKind =
  | "text" | "longText" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "choice" | "multipleChoice" | "person" | "group"
  | "choiceFromList" | "choiceFromConnection" | "people" | "list" | "fieldGroup";

export type Recipient =
  | { type: "expr"; expr: Cel }
  | { type: "workflowAdmins" };

export interface TriggerBinding {
  id: string;                        // sw_...
  connection: ConnectionId;
  event: EntryRef;                   // a trigger entry
  when: Cel;                         // over sent and constants
  outcome: string;                   // an outcome of the start wait
  data: { [property: string]: Cel }; // over sent and constants; "requester" names the Requester
}

export interface EventRule {
  id: string;                        // act_...
  on: RuleOn;
  when: Cel;
  told: { id: string; words: string };
  values: { [name: string]: Cel };
}

export interface NobodyToAskRule {
  id: string;                        // `${waitFullId}__nobody`
  wait: FullId;
  members: FullId | null;
  excludeRequester: boolean;
}

export interface Origin {
  item: string[];
  part: string | null;
}

export interface DeclaredTypes {
  data: { [key: string]: JsonSchema };
  constants: { [name: string]: JsonSchema };
  results: { [connection: ConnectionId]: { [op: EntryRef]: JsonSchema } };
}

export interface PinnedSchema {
  id: string;
  version: number;
  schema: JsonSchema;
}
```

## 9. Publish checks this format adds

Beyond spec section 6, Integrations 9.11 (bindings) and Integrations 13.3 (event rules). Spec v2.19 section 6 writes out the readings of its own checks, one sentence each (E-27): which paths count as present for a read, how a stage's transitions cover its waits' outcomes, what breaks a cycle, which forms guard a read of a wait's data, and that a rule's `on.element` names an existing element.

The check is core's `checkDefinition(definition, catalogue?)` (`contract/core-api.md` section 14). Each problem carries a code, a pointer, params and a severity, `error` or `warning`; a definition may be published when no problem is an `error`. The checks below marked "with the catalogue" run only when the catalogue is given, and are built with the server (E-27).

- Every ID matches its pattern in section 2 and is unique where section 2 says, including the rule that no wait ID visible in a CEL scope is a `.`-prefix of another.
- No key in the document starts with `$`; every data key, path segment and schema property name is a Name.
- Every outcome's `schema` is a key of `schemas`; every key of `schemas` is used.
- Every element (stage, wait, outcome, check, transition, notification rule, binding, event rule, nobody-to-ask rule) has exactly one element key in `origins`; every element key names an element; every field key's pointer resolves to a field holding CEL of that element, or to a lookup (`#/lookups/<n>`, the one field key that names an object, section 10).
- `types` (section 3.12): every top-level path a Set writes has a `types.data` entry and every entry is written by some Set; every constant has a `types.constants` entry that its value fits, and no other entry exists; every call wait's `connection` and `op` have a `types.results` entry, and no other entry exists. With the catalogue: each `types.results` entry equals the schema derived from the catalogue entry. Every CEL field type-checks against these declarations.
- A call has exactly one of `keyScope` and `idempotencyKey` non-null; a read has `keyScope: "activation"`.
- A stage has at most one `otherwise` transition, and it is last.
- A final stage has no waits and no transitions.
- A wait's opening expressions (`assignees`, `args`, `idempotencyKey`) read no wait of the same stage: the waits of a stage open in declared order, so a sibling is not there yet (E-26, spec v2.17).
- A map literal in any CEL field has no key starting with `$` (E-26, spec v2.17).
- The kernel publish check makes the fault codes `set-overlap` and `unknown-stage` unreachable (`event-payloads.md`; E-26): no two Set paths of one transition overlap (section 3.4), and every transition target is a stage of the definition. `decide` still records each code if it ever meets the case.
- `on.element` is non-null only on the event types listed in section 3.6 (`rule-element-not-allowed`), and then names an element of the definition of a kind its event type can name, as section 3.6 lists them (`rule-element-unknown`; spec v2.18, E-27); `on.event` is a recorded event type or `Stuck` (`rule-event-unknown`).
- Every `{words}` key is a key of the platform's words file of the core version that publishes.
- Lookups: `property` is a property of the outcome's schema; `inputs` type-check and do not read `request.id`, nor the whole `request` (`lookup-reads-request-id`; spec v2.19, E-28: on the start form the choices are listed before a request exists); `answer: "person"` only when the property's schema is the person schema. With the catalogue: `connection` and `source` name a `dataSource` entry; every required input of the entry is mapped; `storedField` and `labelField` are fields of the entry's `item`.
- `nobodyToAsk`: `wait` names a person wait; `members` is `null` or names a call wait in the same stage as `wait`, with op `membersOf@1`, `effect: "read"` and `onFailure: "outcome"` (with the catalogue: on the catalogue's `directoryConnection`); at most one rule per wait. A stage that holds such a membership read has no `otherwise` transition (section 3.9).
- `types` and `schemas` use only the keywords and formats of `jsonschema-1`.
- A wait `kind` other than `person` and `call` is refused.

## 10. The blocks the demo does not use

The demo (`examples/change-request-demo.definition.json`) has no binding, no event rule, no lookup and no authored Notify. These fragments are adapted from `engine/design/integrated-sample.md` section 2 and compiler 15.3, with compiler's stage names; they show each block in format 1. Each fragment parses as JSON; the CEL of the tasks-step fragment was type-checked under `dyn` with the wrapper; nothing else in them was run.

A lookup on the start outcome:

```json
{ "id": "btn_rf_submit", "schema": "tk_request_form.btn_rf_submit@1",
  "checks": [ { "id": "tk_request_form__requester",
                "when": "actor.type == 'connection' || !has(input.requester)", "message": "" } ],
  "lookups": [ { "property": "q_service", "connection": "servicecatalog", "source": "services@1",
                 "inputs": { "status": "optional.of('active')" },
                 "storedField": "id", "labelField": "name", "answer": "item" } ] }
```

A trigger binding, an event rule, an authored Notify and a nobody-to-ask rule:

```json
{
  "triggers": [
    { "id": "sw_helpdesk_ticket", "connection": "helpdesk", "event": "ticketCreated@1",
      "when": "sent.category == 'Service change'", "outcome": "btn_rf_submit",
```

The tasks step that rule judges, with the membership read beside the task and the explicit exit (section 3.9; the other outcomes and the transition's sets are left out here):

```json
  "waits": [

      "may": "actor != request.by",
      "outcomes": [ { "id": "btn_approve", "schema": "tk_approve.btn_approve@1", "checks": [], "lookups": [] } ] } ],
  "transitions": [
    { "id": "st_approve__answered", "otherwise": false, "when": "waits.tk_approve.status == 'completed'",
      "set": [], "to": "st_approve__route" } ] }
```
