/** What `compile` returns (contract/core-api.md section 12; compiler.md sections 0 and 13). */
import type { PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { Finding } from "../check/findings.ts";
import type { Location } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";

/** The published definition, with its types block, schemas and origin map (definition-format.md). */
export type Published = PublishedDefinition;

/**
 * A part Try it cannot run (compiler.md 13): where the blocking To do is, and the engine stage a request
 * that gets there is stuck in. `stage` is absent for a binding, which is left out of `triggers`.
 */
export interface Unfinished {
  location: Location;
  stage?: string;
}

/**
 * `publish`: the server's publish. A draft with a To do is refused, and the result passes the kernel publish
 * checks. `tryIt`: any draft `parse` accepts; a part with a To do that stops a request is compiled to the
 * unfinished shapes of compiler.md 13 and listed in `unfinished`.
 */
export type CompileMode = "publish" | "tryIt";

export interface CompileOptions {
  mode?: CompileMode;
  /** The server's workflow ID (definition-format.md section 2). Default `draft`. */
  workflow?: string;
  /** The version being published. Default 1. */
  version?: number;
  /** The core version that compiles it. Default `core`. */
  compiler?: string;
}

export type CompileResult =
  /** `findings` holds Worth knowing only in publish mode, and every finding in Try it mode. */
  | { ok: true; published: Published; findings: Finding[]; unfinished: Unfinished[] }
  /** At least one To do (publish mode), a workflow-level To do (Try it mode), or `compile.internal`. */
  | { ok: false; findings: Finding[] };
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/contract/authored-format.ts\n===
// COPY of contract/authored-format.ts, made by engine/packages/core/scripts/sync-contract.mjs. Do not edit:
// change contract/authored-format.ts and run the script again. test/authored/contract-sync.test.ts checks it.
/**
 * Authored workflow format, version 0 (draft for review).
 *
 * The JSON document the workflow editor saves as a draft and the engine's compiler turns into a
 * published definition. Field names use the editor's words only (see spec/editor-model.md).
 *
 * Reading guide, top to bottom:
 *   1. IDs                      6. Forms (pages, questions, text)
 *   2. Expressions              7. Buttons
 *   3. "When ..." sentences     8. Actions
 *   4. Workflow (root)          9. Arrows
 *   5. Stages and tasks        10. Values, lists, sample request, diagram
 *
 * Drafts may be unfinished. Every field marked "(draft: optional)" may be missing while the author
 * is still working; the checker reports it under To do. The format never rejects an unfinished
 * draft; it only rejects things that are malformed (wrong shape).
 */

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 1. IDs
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Every addressable thing has a stable ID, generated once by the editor and never reused, even
 * after the thing is deleted. Names and labels are separate and renamable; every reference is by
 * ID, so a rename changes one place.
 *
 * The prefix is part of the ID and says what sort of thing it names (so a stage ID can never be
 * used where a value ID is expected; see `ITEM_KINDS`). After the prefix the ID is opaque.
 *
 * ID rule (the compiler turns IDs into formula identifiers and element names):
 *  - every ID matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$` (`ID_PATTERN`): it starts with a letter and
 *    is at most 40 characters long, so every name the compiler builds from it fits in 64;
 *  - no ID contains a double underscore `__` (reserved for names the compiler adds);
 *  - IDs the editor generates are `<prefix>_<base36>`, e.g. `st_8f3k2q`. Fixtures use readable
 *    ones that follow the same rule, e.g. `st_domain_approval`.
 *
 * A reference may point at an ID that no longer exists (an arrow to a deleted stage). That is
 * legal in a draft and is a red To do.
 */
export type WorkflowId = `wf_${string}`;
export type StageId = `st_${string}`;
export type StatusId = `stat_${string}`;
export type TaskId = `tk_${string}`;
export type PageId = `pg_${string}`;
export type QuestionId = `q_${string}`;
/** Read-only text on a form ("+ Add text"). */
export type TextId = `tx_${string}`;
/** A typed-in choice of a choice or multiple-choice question. */
export type ChoiceId = `ch_${string}`;
export type ButtonId = `btn_${string}`;
export type ActionId = `act_${string}`;
export type ArrowId = `ar_${string}`;
export type ValueId = `v_${string}`;
export type ListId = `ls_${string}`;
export type ColumnId = `col_${string}`;
export type RowId = `row_${string}`;
/** A "Starts when" binding on the start block. */
export type StartsWhenId = `sw_${string}`;
/** An entry of `thingsTold`: something the workflow tells other systems happened. */
export type ToldId = `told_${string}`;

/** Each ID prefix and the kind of item it names. Data only. */
export const ITEM_KINDS = {
  wf: "workflow",
  st: "stage",
  stat: "status",
  tk: "task",
  pg: "page",
  q: "question",
  tx: "text",
  ch: "choice",
  btn: "button",
  act: "action",
  ar: "arrow",
  v: "value",
  ls: "list",
  col: "column",
  row: "row",
  sw: "startsWhen",
  told: "thingTold",
} as const;
export type ItemKind = (typeof ITEM_KINDS)[keyof typeof ITEM_KINDS];

/** The pattern every ID matches: a letter, then letters, digits or `_`, at most 40 characters in
 *  all (and none contains `__`). */
export const ID_PATTERN = "^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,39}$";

/**
 * A place in the document, used by findings (To do, Worth knowing), refusals, problems, story
 * entries and the compiler's origin table. `item` is an item's ID (the workflow's own `id` for
 * workflow-level findings). `part` is absent for the item as a whole; otherwise it is the path
 * from the item's own object to the field: the authored field names, joined by dots, never
 * entering another item (an object with its own `id`). Array positions and pieces are numeric
 * segments counted from 0: `onlyWhen.2` is the third clause of the item's "Only when" and may
 * continue into it (`onlyWhen.2.right`); `message.1` is the second piece of a template. A key
 * chosen by the catalogue or by the form is a segment (`inputs.summary`, `saveResults.key`,
 * `answers.q_summary`, `values.ticket`). A formula is reported at the part that holds the
 * `Formula` object, and its sentence at `<part>.readsAs`.
 * The parts reported are listed, complete, in `LOCATION_PARTS`.
 */
export interface Location {
  item: string;
  part?: string;
}

/**
 * Every `Location.part` that findings, refusals, problems and story entries report, per kind of
 * item, for format version 0 (the engine's list, contract `core-api.md` section 2.3). Word tables
 * may key on it. A segment in angle brackets stands for a key chosen by the catalogue or the form
 * (`<field>`, `<key>`, `<column>`, `<question>`). A listed part may be followed by deeper segments
 * by the path rule on `Location` (a clause or template index, `readsAs`, `whoIsAsked.ifEmptyUse`).
 * A diff's "changed" part may name any field of an item by the same rule, including fields not
 * listed here. Items with an empty list are reported only as a whole. A stage's
 * `whenThisStageStarts`, `tasks`, `afterTheyRespond` and `arrows` also say where a request is.
 */
export const LOCATION_PARTS = {
  workflow: ["start.stage"],
  stage: ["name", "status", "ifSentBackStatus", "whenThisStageStarts", "tasks", "afterTheyRespond", "arrows"],
  status: ["words"],
  task: ["whoIsAsked", "whoIsAsked.ifEmptyUse", "requesterCanAnswer", "buttons", "savesButtonPressedAs", "savesAnsweredByAs"],
  page: ["showWhen"],
  question: [
    "label", "savedAs", "choices", "choices.list", "choices.shownColumn", "choices.peopleIn", "choices.source",
    "choices.inputs", "choices.inputs.<field>", "choices.labelField", "choices.storedField", "choices.formula", "showWhen",
  ],
  text: ["content", "showWhen"],
  choice: [],
  button: ["label", "neededToPress", "enabledWhen"],
  action: [
    "onlyWhen",
    // Save a value
    "save", "as",
    // Notify
    "to", "message",
    // Use a connection
    "operation", "inputs", "inputs.<field>", "saveResults.<field>", "ifItFails", "saveFailureAs.failed", "saveFailureAs.code", "ifStageEntersAgain",
    // Tell other systems
    "tell", "values.<key>",
  ],
  arrow: ["when", "when.button", "when.condition", "onlyWhen", "goTo", "goAsSoonAsTrue"],
  value: [],
  list: [],
  column: [],
  row: ["cells.<column>"],
  startsWhen: ["trigger", "onlyWhen", "button", "requester", "answers", "answers.<question>"],
  thingTold: ["words"],
} as const satisfies Record<ItemKind, readonly string[]>;

/** One reported part, as written in `LOCATION_PARTS` (placeholders in angle brackets). */
export type ReportedPart = (typeof LOCATION_PARTS)[ItemKind][number];

/**
 * A catalogue entry: `<connection>.<name>@<version>`, e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`.
 * The catalogue (contract part D: operations, data sources, triggers, event sinks, with their
 * fields) is owned by the platform; connections are set up by a platform admin outside the editor.
 * A workflow only references catalogue entries; it has no connections section of its own. An
 * entry's version never changes shape; a change is a new version. No connector name is built
 * into this format.
 */
export type CatalogueRef = `${string}.${string}@${number}`;

/**
 * A person or group in the Directory. `directoryId` is the directory's immutable object ID (never
 * an email or a name). `name` is a copy of the display name, kept so the draft reads well and
 * shows something if the directory is unreachable; the directory is authoritative.
 */
export interface DirectoryRef {
  directoryId: string;
  name: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 2. Expressions: anything that gives a value
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * One union usable wherever a value is needed (a slot). Three levels:
 *  (a) a reference to a value, possibly with steps into connected data, or a constant;
 *  (b) a "when ..." sentence (gives Yes/No);
 *  (c) a formula (the escape hatch).
 * The kind an expression gives is never stored; the checker works it out.
 */
export type Expression =
  | ValueReference
  | RequestReference
  | Constant
  | Sentence
  | Formula;

/**
 * The kinds of value. The kind is never stored on a value; it is worked out from what fills it
 * (and the catalogue's fields use the same kinds). A question's kind (`QuestionKind`) is one of
 * the first nine; the others only come from where a value is filled:
 *  - `choiceFromList`: a choice question answered from a list kept with the workflow; holds a row
 *    (`{ row }`), so steps can read the row's cells.
 *  - `choiceFromConnection`: a choice question answered from a catalogue data source; holds ONE
 *    value of two parts, `{ stored, label }`: what was stored, and the source's label for that item
 *    as recorded by the lookup made when the person answered (so the request page can show it
 *    later without asking the other system, even if the item is renamed or removed there).
 *    Conditions compare the `stored` part.
 *  - `people`: several people (e.g. a group's members after a `directory` step).
 *  - `list`, `fieldGroup`: a list of items, or a group of named fields, as an operation's result
 *    may give. Version 0 has no words for them in sentences; read them with a formula.
 * A task's "Button pressed" value is a `choice` whose choices are the task's buttons.
 * A value filled by `saveFailureAs.code` is a `choice` whose choices are the failure codes of the
 * operation (value = the code, label = the catalogue's label for it): the request holds the code,
 * a "when" compares by code (`{ failureCode }`), and a message or a text sent to another system
 * shows the label. If two actions save their failure code as the same value, its choices are the
 * codes of both; where one code has two labels, the first action in the document gives the label.
 */
export type ValueKind =
  | "text" | "longText" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "choice" | "multipleChoice" | "person" | "group"
  | "choiceFromList" | "choiceFromConnection" | "people" | "list" | "fieldGroup";

/**
 * "Title", "Primary domain's approvers", "Eng lead (if empty, use Primary domain's default lead)".
 * `steps` follow connected data from the value: a choice answered from a list gives a row, and a
 * `column` step reads a cell of that row; a `directory` step goes from a group to its people.
 */
export interface ValueReference {
  value: ValueId;
  steps?: Step[];
  /**
   * "If empty, use ...": used when this reference has nothing in it at that moment. "Empty" means
   * the value has nothing in it. A group that exists but has nobody in it is NOT empty: that case
   * is "nobody to ask", and the request goes to the people who look after stuck requests.
   */
  ifEmptyUse?: Expression;
}

/**
 * Things every request has: who started it ("Requester") and when ("Started on", a date).
 * For a request started by another system (a "Starts when" binding), the Requester is the
 * person the binding's `requester` names; when the binding has none, `{ request: "requester" }`
 * is empty, so its `ifEmptyUse` applies.
 */
export interface RequestReference {
  request: "requester" | "startedOn";
  steps?: Step[];
  ifEmptyUse?: Expression;
}


/**
 * One step into connected data.
 * - `column`: from a list row (a choice answered from a list) to that row's cell in the column.
 * - `directory: "members"`: from a group to the people in it. Inside a "when" (as is a `person.isIn`
 *   test on a group), it is a recorded read of the group's members, made just before the step that
 *   uses it, so it sees a group saved earlier in the same section. A condition on the start form
 *   cannot use it (a To do). Under Who is asked, "people in [group]" is the same as asking the
 *   group.
 * Who is asked: a task that may ask a group gets a recorded membership read beside the task. If that
 * read fails, those groups count as nobody to ask; a person asked directly still counts.
 * Later steps (e.g. "manager" of a person) would be new `directory` words; not in version 0.
 */
export type Step = { column: ColumnId } | { directory: "members" };

/** A typed literal. The key says the kind. */
export type Constant =
  | { text: string }
  | { number: number }
  | { yesNo: boolean }
  /** `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
  | { date: string }
  /** For "is on a [weekday]". */
  | { weekday: "monday" | "tuesday" | "wednesday" | "thursday" | "friday" | "saturday" | "sunday" }
  /** One typed-in choice of a question. */
  | { choice: ChoiceId }
  /** Several typed-in choices (a multiple-choice answer). */
  | { choices: ChoiceId[] }
  /** One row of a list (what a choice answered from a list holds). */
  | { row: RowId }
  /** A button (what a task's "Button pressed" value holds). */
  | { button: ButtonId }
  /** One failure code of a connection action, written as the catalogue declares it (kebab-case),
   *  e.g. `{ failureCode: "tests-failed" }`. What a value filled by `saveFailureAs.code` holds;
   *  valid only as the right side of a clause on such a value, and only for a code the action's
   *  operation declares. Written wherever a `button` constant may be written. */
  | { failureCode: string }
  | { person: DirectoryRef }
  | { group: DirectoryRef }
  /** Several people. */
  | { people: DirectoryRef[] }
  /** What a choice answered from a catalogue data source holds (kind `choiceFromConnection`).
   *  As the right side of a clause only `stored` is compared. */
  | { connectionChoice: { stored: string | number; label: string } };

/**
 * Text with value chips in it: notification messages, form text, a Jira summary. Strings are
 * shown as written; expressions are shown as their value at that moment.
 * Example: `["Your Jira issue for this change is ready: ", { "value": "v_jira_issue" }]`.
 */
export type Template = Array<string | Expression>;

/**
 * The escape hatch, for a "when ..." or a value. `formula` is text in the engine's formula
 * language (CEL), with chips written `{{<value id>}}`, `{{request.requester}}`,
 * `{{request.startedOn}}`, and, inside a "Starts when" binding only, `{{sent.<field>}}`. There is
 * no "today": the engine has no clock. Nothing else about its syntax belongs to this format.
 * `readsAs` is the required plain sentence shown everywhere instead of the formula (on the arrow,
 * in In words). (draft: `readsAs` may be empty.)
 */
export interface Formula {
  formula: string;
  readsAs: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 3. "When ..." sentences (the condition builder)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** A "when ...": a sentence from the builder, or a formula. Gives Yes/No. */
export type Condition = Sentence | Formula;

/**
 * Clauses joined by "and" (allOf) or "or" (anyOf). Flat: mixing "and" and "or" needs a formula.
 * An empty list is legal in a draft (the author has opened the builder but chosen nothing).
 */
export type Sentence = { allOf: Clause[] } | { anyOf: Clause[] };

export type Clause = WordsClause | PressedClause;

/**
 * `[left] [words] [right]`, e.g. "Risk is High", "Primary domain needs approval is No".
 * `right` is absent for words that need nothing after them (`WORDS_WITH_NOTHING_AFTER`), a list
 * for "is one of" words (`WORDS_WITH_A_LIST`), and one expression otherwise.
 * (draft: every part optional, the builder saves as the author goes.)
 */
export interface WordsClause {
  left?: Expression;
  words?: Words;
  right?: Expression | Expression[];
}

/**
 * "Approve is pressed" / "Security team presses Reject". Means: in this stage's current visit,
 * that button was pressed. Only legal in the stage that owns the button (its arrows, its
 * "After they respond" actions and their "Only when"). Elsewhere, read the task's
 * "Button pressed" value instead.
 */
export interface PressedClause {
  pressed: ButtonId;
}

/**
 * The words offered by the builder: a closed list per set of words, available at run time (the
 * condition builder and the engine both need it).
 *  - `yesNo` words are shown naturally, never as a double negative: "Domain needs no approval".
 *  - `date.isOnWeekday` takes a `{ weekday }` constant.
 *  - `person.isIn`: the person is a member of the group (or among the people) on the right.
 */
export const WORDS = {
  text: ["text.is", "text.isNot", "text.contains", "text.doesNotContain", "text.startsWith", "text.isFilled", "text.isEmpty"],
  number: ["number.is", "number.isNot", "number.isMoreThan", "number.isLessThan", "number.isAtLeast", "number.isAtMost", "number.isFilled", "number.isEmpty"],
  yesNo: ["yesNo.isYes", "yesNo.isNo", "yesNo.isFilled", "yesNo.isEmpty"],
  date: ["date.is", "date.isBefore", "date.isAfter", "date.isOnOrBefore", "date.isOnOrAfter", "date.isOnWeekday", "date.isFilled", "date.isEmpty"],
  choice: ["choice.is", "choice.isNot", "choice.isOneOf", "choice.isNotOneOf", "choice.isFilled", "choice.isEmpty"],
  person: ["person.is", "person.isNot", "person.isOneOf", "person.isIn", "person.isNotIn", "person.isFilled", "person.isEmpty"],
  people: ["people.include", "people.doNotInclude", "people.areFilled", "people.areEmpty"],
  list: ["list.includes", "list.doesNotInclude", "list.includesAnyOf", "list.includesAllOf", "list.isFilled", "list.isEmpty"],
} as const;

export type WordSet = keyof typeof WORDS;
export type Words = (typeof WORDS)[WordSet][number];

/** Which set of words a kind of value is offered. `null`: none in version 0 (use a formula). */
export const WORDS_FOR_KIND: Record<ValueKind, WordSet | null> = {
  text: "text", longText: "text", number: "number", yesNo: "yesNo", date: "date",
  choice: "choice", choiceFromList: "choice", choiceFromConnection: "choice",
  multipleChoice: "list", person: "person", group: "people", people: "people",
  list: null, fieldGroup: null,
};

/** Words that take no `right`. */
export const WORDS_WITH_NOTHING_AFTER = [
  "text.isFilled", "text.isEmpty", "number.isFilled", "number.isEmpty", "yesNo.isYes", "yesNo.isNo", "yesNo.isFilled", "yesNo.isEmpty",
  "date.isFilled", "date.isEmpty", "choice.isFilled", "choice.isEmpty", "person.isFilled", "person.isEmpty",
  "people.areFilled", "people.areEmpty", "list.isFilled", "list.isEmpty",
] as const satisfies readonly Words[];
/** Words whose `right` is a list of expressions. Items of that list that are empty when the
 *  condition is checked are ignored. */
export const WORDS_WITH_A_LIST = [
  "choice.isOneOf", "choice.isNotOneOf", "person.isOneOf", "list.includesAnyOf", "list.includesAllOf",
] as const satisfies readonly Words[];

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 4. Workflow (root)
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * The whole authored workflow: one draft (or one published version's source), as the editor
 * saves it. The workflow's name, its authors and "Stuck requests go to" are NOT here: they live
 * in the server's workflow record, so changing them is not an edit to any version.
 */
export interface AuthoredWorkflow {
  /** Version of this format. Stays 0 until the engine has compiled it once. */
  formatVersion: 0;
  /**
   * The document's own item ID: what workflow-level findings point at (`Location.item`). It is
   * NOT the server's workflow ID, which is opaque and server-generated.
   */
  id: WorkflowId;
  /** How a request starts. */
  start: Start;
  /** Every stage and ending. Array order has no meaning for running requests (the editor keeps
   *  the start stage first); arrows decide where requests go. */
  stages: Stage[];
  /** Status words and colours. Stages that show the same words share one status. */
  statuses: Status[];
  /** Things the workflow tells other systems happened ("Tell other systems"). See `ThingTold`. */
  thingsTold: ThingTold[];
  /** The value registry. See `Value`. */
  values: Value[];
  /** Lists kept with the workflow (the Domains list). Versioned with the workflow. */
  lists: List[];
  /** The request the editor uses for every sample it shows. Ignored by the compiler. */
  sampleRequest?: SampleRequest;
  /** Diagram positions. Absent means automatic layout (the normal case). Ignored by the compiler. */
  diagram?: Diagram;
  /**
   * Names of deleted things that are still referenced (an arrow to a deleted stage), so To do can
   * say "goes to Domain review (deleted)". Keyed by the old ID. Ignored by the compiler.
   */
  removedNames?: Record<string, string>;
}

/**
 * How a request starts. Always: a person submits the start stage's form (they become the
 * Requester). In addition, zero or more "Starts when" bindings let something outside start a
 * request by filling in that same form from what another system sent.
 */
export interface Start {
  by: "personSubmitsForm";
  /** The start stage. It must be a working stage with exactly one task. */
  stage: StageId;
  /** "Starts when ..." bindings. Empty when only people start requests. */
  startsWhen: StartsWhen[];
}

/**
 * "Starts when [a ticket is created in Helpdesk] ..."
 * When the catalogue trigger fires (and `onlyWhen` is true for what was sent), a request starts as if
 * the start form had been submitted with `answers`. Everything in a binding reads ONLY the fields
 * of what the other system sent, never workflow values (none exist yet); the types enforce this.
 */
export interface StartsWhen {
  /** Stable, like every other ID. */
  id: StartsWhenId;
  /** A catalogue trigger, e.g. `helpdesk.ticketCreated@1`. (draft: optional.) */
  trigger?: CatalogueRef;
  /** Narrows which of the things sent start a request. */
  onlyWhen?: SentCondition;
  /**
   * Which of the start form's buttons the binding presses. May be absent when the start task has
   * one button; with several, absent is a To do.
   */
  button?: ButtonId;
  /**
   * Names the Requester: a sent field of kind person, e.g. `{ sentField: "raisedBy" }`. The
   * request is still recorded as started by the connection; the Requester value is this person.
   * Absent: the request has no person as Requester, so `{ request: "requester" }` is empty and
   * `ifEmptyUse` applies.
   */
  requester?: SentExpression;
  /**
   * Answers for the start form's questions, keyed by question ID. Questions not listed stay empty.
   * The start form's "Needed to press" is checked against these answers: if it fails, no request
   * starts and the people who look after stuck requests are told.
   */
  answers: Partial<Record<QuestionId, SentExpression | SentTemplate>>;
}

/**
 * A field of what the other system sent. `sentField` is the field's id in the catalogue
 * trigger, dotted for nested fields (`reporter.email`).
 */
export interface SentFieldReference {
  sentField: string;
}
/** An expression inside a "Starts when" binding: fields of what was sent, constants, or a formula
 *  whose chips are written `{{sent.<field>}}`. */
export type SentExpression = SentFieldReference | Constant | Formula;
export type SentTemplate = Array<string | SentExpression>;
export type SentCondition = { allOf: SentClause[] } | { anyOf: SentClause[] } | Formula;
export interface SentClause {
  left?: SentExpression;
  words?: Words;
  right?: SentExpression | SentExpression[];
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 5. Stages, statuses and tasks
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** A box on the diagram: where a request sits. */
export type Stage = WorkingStage | EndingStage;

/**
 * The kind of stage. A kind is chosen when the stage is added; it pre-fills the stage and labels
 * it. It does not change which fields are legal, except that an ending has no anatomy.
 */
export type WorkingStageKind = "form" | "approval" | "work" | "automatic" | "blank";

/**
 * Every working stage has the same fixed anatomy, done in this order:
 *   whenThisStageStarts (actions, in order) → tasks → afterTheyRespond (actions, in order) → arrows.
 * Order rule: within one section, actions run in listed order and saves take effect in listed
 * order, so a later action, a later section, or an arrow sees an earlier save (and an earlier
 * action's saved results).
 * An Automatic stage has no tasks; the panel shows its `whenThisStageStarts` as "What it does".
 */
export interface WorkingStage {
  id: StageId;
  kind: WorkingStageKind;
  /** (draft: may be empty.) */
  name: string;
  /** The status people see while a request is here. (draft: optional.)
   *  The start stage normally has none: a request is never seen sitting there unless it is sent
   *  back, and then `ifSentBackStatus` is shown. Exception, raised by the check as a To do (not a
   *  format rule): a start stage with a connection action in "After they respond" needs a
   *  status, because a request can be seen sitting (or stuck) there. */
  status?: StatusId;
  /**
   * The status shown instead when the request arrived by an arrow that sends it back ("If sent
   * back: Needs changes"). Legal on any working stage. "Sent back" is never stored: an arrow sends
   * back when it goes to a stage that every request must already have passed through to reach the
   * arrow's own stage; the engine works this out.
   */
  ifSentBackStatus?: StatusId;
  /**
   * Done in order, before anyone is asked, every time the stage is entered. A new request begins
   * at the start stage's form, so the start stage's `whenThisStageStarts` runs only when a request
   * is sent back there.
   */
  whenThisStageStarts: Action[];
  /**
   * Who is asked, each with a form and buttons. Usually one; a short fixed list when several are
   * asked at the same time; none for an Automatic stage. All tasks open when the stage starts.
   */
  tasks: Task[];
  /** Done in order, once, when the stage finishes (after all tasks, or when an arrow marked
   *  `goAsSoonAsTrue` is taken). */
  afterTheyRespond: Action[];
  /** "Then go to". Checked from the top; the first one that fits is used. */
  arrows: Arrow[];
}

/** A box where a request finishes. Status and colour only. */
export interface EndingStage {
  id: StageId;
  kind: "ending";
  name: string;
  /** (draft: optional.) */
  status?: StatusId;
}

/** Status words and colour. Referenced by ID from stages, so two stages can share one. */
export interface Status {
  id: StatusId;
  /** "Waiting for approval". (draft: may be empty.) */
  words: string;
  colour: "grey" | "red" | "amber" | "green" | "blue" | "purple" | "teal" | "pink";
}

/** The part of a stage that asks people: who is asked, a form, buttons. */
export interface Task {
  id: TaskId;
  /**
   * The task's own name. Absent while the stage has one task. With several, the editor names each
   * task after who is asked ("Domain approvers"); set here only if the author renamed it.
   */
  name?: string;
  /**
   * Who is asked: an expression giving a person, a group, or several people. A fallback is
   * written on the reference (`ifEmptyUse`). For the start stage this is `{ request: "requester" }`
   * and only matters when a request is sent back there. (draft: optional — "Nobody is asked".)
   */
  whoIsAsked?: Expression;
  /**
   * How a group answers. Version 0 has one rule: "One answer is enough: the first person in the
   * group to answer decides." Later rules (everyone, at least N) would be new words here.
   */
  groupRule: "firstAnswerDecides";
  /** "The requester can't answer their own request" is this set to false (Approval: false). */
  requesterCanAnswer: boolean;
  form: Form;
  /** How a person finishes the task. Order is display order. */
  buttons: Button[];
  /**
   * The task's two extra answers, "Button pressed" (holds a `{ button }`) and "Answered by"
   * (a person). The value is created the first time the author uses it; absent means not saved.
   * When the task is cancelled by a `goAsSoonAsTrue` arrow, both are emptied for that visit; its
   * questions' values keep what they had.
   */
  savesButtonPressedAs?: ValueId;
  savesAnsweredByAs?: ValueId;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 6. Forms
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** The questions a task shows, on one or more pages. Form logic only shows or hides. */
export interface Form {
  pages: Page[];
}

export interface Page {
  id: PageId;
  title?: string;
  /** "Show when". When hidden, its questions stay empty. */
  showWhen?: Condition;
  items: FormItem[];
}

export type FormItem = Question | FormText;

/**
 * The kinds of question the author picks. The value it fills has the same kind, except a
 * `choice` whose choices come from a list (`choiceFromList`) or a catalogue data source
 * (`choiceFromConnection`); see `ValueKind`. A question whose choices are the people in a group
 * is a `person` question and fills a `person` value.
 */
export type QuestionKind = Extract<ValueKind, "text" | "longText" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "choice" | "multipleChoice" | "person" | "group">;

export interface Question {
  type: "question";
  id: QuestionId;
  /** (draft: may be empty.) */
  label: string;
  kind: QuestionKind;
  /** "Saved as [value]". Absent only in a broken draft (the editor creates the value with the question). */
  savedAs?: ValueId;
  /** For choice, multiple choice, person and group. (draft: optional.) */
  choices?: Choices;
  /** "Show when". When hidden, the question stays empty and is not needed to press any button. */
  showWhen?: Condition;
  /**
   * The "All" tick under "Needed to press": needed for every button of the task, including
   * buttons added later. See `Button.neededToPress` for the effective set.
   */
  neededForEveryButton?: boolean;
}

/** Text people can read but not change ("+ Add text"), with value chips in it. */
export interface FormText {
  type: "text";
  id: TextId;
  content: Template;
  showWhen?: Condition;
}

/**
 * Where a question's choices come from. Choices from the directory and from a connection are read
 * live while the form is shown, on the start form too; the answer is checked by a lookup when the
 * person answers, and for a connection the source's label is recorded with that lookup.
 */
export type Choices =
  /** Typed in by the author. */
  | { from: "typedIn"; choices: Choice[] }
  /** The rows of a list kept with the workflow; `shownColumn` is what people see. The answer is the row. */
  | { from: "list"; list: ListId; shownColumn?: ColumnId }
  /** The people in a group given by an expression (Lists and directory), e.g. the members of
   *  "Primary domain's engineering group". The answer is a person, so the value it fills has kind
   *  `person`, never `choice`. The editor offers this only on a question of kind `person`
   *  (changing the kind to text, number, choice and so on removes these choices; on a `group`
   *  question it is a To do); the fixtures do the same (`q_eng_lead`). */
  | { from: "directory"; peopleIn: Expression }
  /**
   * A catalogue data source, e.g. `servicecatalog.services@1`. `inputs` maps the source's input
   * fields to expressions; `labelField` is the item field people see, `storedField` the one
   * stored. The answer is one value of kind `choiceFromConnection`: `{ stored, label }`.
   */
  | { from: "source"; source?: CatalogueRef; inputs: Record<string, Expression | Template>; labelField?: string; storedField?: string }
  /** A formula that gives the list of choices. */
  | { from: "formula"; formula: Formula };

export interface Choice {
  id: ChoiceId;
  label: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 7. Buttons
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface Button {
  id: ButtonId;
  /** "Approve". (draft: may be empty.) */
  label: string;
  look: "primary" | "secondary" | "danger";
  /**
   * "Needed to press": questions that must be answered before this button can be pressed. The
   * effective set is this list plus every question of the task with `neededForEveryButton`.
   * A hidden question is never needed. The form editor shows the same fact on each question.
   */
  neededToPress: QuestionId[];
  /** "Also only when ...": one more "when ..." that must be true to press it. */
  enabledWhen?: Condition;
  /** Shown while it cannot be pressed. Absent: the editor reads back its needs and "when ...". */
  messageWhileDisabled?: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 8. Actions: things the workflow does by itself (and "Save a value")
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * An item in "When this stage starts" or "After they respond".
 * Every one may carry `onlyWhen`. There is no nesting.
 * Items run in listed order and saves take effect in listed order: a later item, and the arrows,
 * see what an earlier one saved.
 */
export type Action = SaveValue | Notify | UseConnection | TellOtherSystems;

interface ActionBase {
  id: ActionId;
  /** "Only when ...". For a save: when not true, the value keeps what it had. */
  onlyWhen?: Condition;
}

/** "Save [what] as [value]". */
export interface SaveValue extends ActionBase {
  type: "saveValue";
  /** (draft: optional.) */
  save?: Expression;
  /** (draft: optional.) */
  as?: ValueId;
}

/** "Notify [who]". The channel (email, Slack) is the platform's choice. If it can't be sent, the
 *  request carries on; there is no setting for that. */
export interface Notify extends ActionBase {
  type: "notify";
  /** A person, group or several people. (draft: optional.) */
  to?: Expression;
  /** Sent with the values as they were at that moment. */
  message: Template;
}

/**
 * Use a catalogue operation: "Create Jira issue", a look-up, "Wait for [system]".
 * Which sort it is (read: gives data / write: does something / await: asks the outside system to
 * do something and waits until it reports back, which may take long) is decided by the catalogue,
 * not by this format. The editor names the action after the operation.
 */
export interface UseConnection extends ActionBase {
  type: "useConnection";
  /** e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`. (draft: optional.) */
  operation?: CatalogueRef;
  /** Keyed by the operation's catalogue input field ids (e.g. `jira.createIssue@1`: `project`,
   *  `summary`, `assignee`, `description`), to expressions or templates. Fields the author has not
   *  filled are absent. */
  inputs: Record<string, Expression | Template>;
  /** Keyed by the operation's catalogue result field ids (e.g. `key`, `url`), to the values they
   *  are saved as. */
  saveResults: Record<string, ValueId>;
  /**
   * "If it fails". Applies to every connection action, look-ups included.
   * "stuck": the request is stuck here and the people in "Stuck requests go to" are told; they
   * can retry or close it. "carryOn": a failure is an ordinary result; later actions and the
   * arrows go on, and can test `saveFailureAs`.
   */
  ifItFails: "stuck" | "carryOn";
  /**
   * Only with "carryOn". `failed`: a Yes/No value, Yes when the operation failed and No when it
   * worked, so an arrow can say "When Deploy failed is Yes go to ...". `code`: a `choice` value
   * holding the failure code (one of the operation's catalogue failure codes; see `ValueKind`);
   * left as it was on success.
   */
  saveFailureAs?: { failed?: ValueId; code?: ValueId };
  /**
   * When the stage is entered again (after a send-back): "once" reuses the first result (one Jira
   * issue per request); "again" does it again. Absent: the catalogue entry's default.
   */
  ifStageEntersAgain?: "once" | "again";
}

/**
 * "Tell other systems": tells other systems something happened. Like Notify, it can never stop a
 * request. Who receives it is chosen outside the workflow by a platform admin.
 */
export interface TellOtherSystems extends ActionBase {
  type: "tellOtherSystems";
  /** Which thing told (an entry of `thingsTold`). Two actions may tell the same thing.
   *  (draft: optional.) */
  tell?: ToldId;
  /**
   * What the outside systems receive: field name to expression or template. The keys are what
   * the outside system receives, so renaming one is a visible change for it.
   */
  values: Record<string, Expression | Template>;
}

/**
 * Something the workflow tells other systems happened, e.g. "Change released". A registry like
 * statuses, so several actions can tell the same thing. Outside systems key on the `id`, so it
 * survives rewording `words`.
 */
export interface ThingTold {
  id: ToldId;
  /** The author's words for what happened. (draft: may be empty.) */
  words: string;
}

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 9. Arrows ("Then go to")
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * One line under "Then go to": "When ... go to ...". Belongs to its source stage. An arrow carries
 * only a "when" and a destination: everything that happens lives in the stage's two action
 * sections, with "Only when".
 */
export interface Arrow {
  id: ArrowId;
  when: ArrowWhen;
  /** "+ only when ...": narrows a button arrow ("When Approve is pressed and Risk is High"). */
  onlyWhen?: Condition;
  /** The stage or ending it goes to. `null`: not chosen yet (amber To do). */
  goTo: StageId | null;
  /** "Words on the arrow". Absent: the editor uses the arrow's sentence ("Approve pressed"). */
  words?: string;
  /**
   * "Don't wait for the others" (stages with several tasks only): checked after every answer, and
   * taken as soon as it fits; tasks still open are cancelled. Default: checked once everyone
   * asked has answered.
   */
  goAsSoonAsTrue?: boolean;
}

export type ArrowWhen =
  /** "When [button] is pressed". */
  | { type: "buttonPressed"; button: ButtonId | null }
  /** A "when ..." that depends on answers. (draft: `condition` optional.) */
  | { type: "condition"; condition?: Condition }
  /** "In all other cases": the catch-all, last. */
  | { type: "inAllOtherCases" }
  /** "When done": an Automatic stage's arrow. */
  | { type: "whenDone" };

// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 10. Values, lists, sample request, diagram
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * A named piece of data the workflow remembers. Never declared by the author: an entry exists
 * because something fills it. It is filled by
 *   - a question (`Question.savedAs`),
 *   - a save (`SaveValue.as`),
 *   - an action's result (`UseConnection.saveResults`, `UseConnection.saveFailureAs`),
 *   - a task's extra answers (`Task.savesButtonPressedAs`, `Task.savesAnsweredByAs`).
 * Its kind is not stored: it comes from what fills it. Two fillers of different kinds is a red
 * To do. If two places fill a value, the later one replaces the earlier. Within one stage, when two
 * tasks fill the same value, the task later in the document wins, not the later answer in time.
 *
 * "Used in N places" is derived, never stored: scan the document for references to the ID
 * (`{ "value": id }` in any expression or template, and `{{id}}` inside formula text), excluding
 * the filling positions above; N is the number of distinct items (question, text, button, action,
 * arrow, task, binding) containing one. "Filled in N places" is the count of filling positions.
 */
export interface Value {
  id: ValueId;
  name: string;
  description?: string;
}

/** A small table kept with the workflow, such as the Domains list. Versioned with the workflow. */
export interface List {
  id: ListId;
  name: string;
  columns: Column[];
  rows: Row[];
}

export interface Column {
  id: ColumnId;
  name: string;
  kind: "text" | "number" | "yesNo" | "date" | "person" | "group";
}

export interface Row {
  id: RowId;
  /** Cells by column ID. An absent cell is "(not given)". */
  cells: Partial<Record<ColumnId, Constant>>;
}

/** The request the editor uses for samples (the last one used in Try it). */
export interface SampleRequest {
  /** Shown in the toolbar: "Sample: Rotate payment gateway API keys". */
  name: string;
  requester?: DirectoryRef;
  /** `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
  startedOn?: string;
  /** Sample answers by value ID. Values without one show no sample. */
  answers: Partial<Record<ValueId, Constant>>;
}

export interface Diagram {
  /** Positions per stage; stages without one are placed automatically. */
  positions: Partial<Record<StageId, { x: number; y: number }>>;
}

// COPY of contract/catalogue.ts, made by engine/packages/core/scripts/sync-contract.mjs. Do not edit:
// change contract/catalogue.ts and run the script again. test/authored/contract-sync.test.ts checks it.
// Contract part D: the catalogue of connections.
// Draft 3, engine owner.
// Matches engine/design/integrations-shapes.md section 2 under decisions E-10, E-17, E-19, E-20,
// E-23, E-27, E-28 and E-32; contract/fixtures/catalogue.json follows it. Pending the frontend owner's review and the
// product owner's review.
//
// The catalogue is data. The editor hard-codes no connection and no entry (E-10). It is served by
// `GET {base}/catalogue` (authoring-api.md, operation 11) with every default written out, so a
// field below is never missing. Unlike the rest of the contract it holds `null` where this file
// says so, because it is the same document the server registers (integrations-shapes.md 2.9).
//
// Fixed: every field that the shape hash covers (`kind`, `sort`, `input`, `result`, `failureCodes`,
// `item`, `searchable`, `event`). Labels, descriptions, a field's `addressOf`, `supersededBy`,
// `onRepeat`, timeouts, `expectedWithinSeconds`, `await`, `cacheSeconds` and `sample` may change under
// one entry ID (E-20: the shape hash ignores labels; E-32: `addressOf` is display only). The
// catalogue's `version` covers all of them.
//
// The directory is a connection like any other. `directoryConnection` names it; it declares the
// operation `membersOf@1` (the recorded read behind a members step, an "is in group" test and the
// nobody-to-ask rule) and the data source `groupMembers@1` (directory choices, read live and looked
// up when the person acts) (integrations-shapes.md 2.7, 5.2, 5.5). A `membersOf@1` group item may carry the
// group's name. `notifyConnection` names the connection that carries Notify.

import type { ValueKind } from "./authored-format";

export type { ValueKind };

/** Any JSON value, as samples and items hold it. */
export type Json = string | number | boolean | null | Json[] | { [key: string]: Json };
export type JsonObject = { [key: string]: Json };

/**
 * "<connection>.<name>@<version>", for example "jira.createIssue@1". Never names a second shape.
 *   connection: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$          (engine, system and platform are reserved)
 *   name:       ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}$         lowerCamelCase
 *   version:    ^[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$
 * The authored format names an entry with its `CatalogueRef`, which has this form.
 */
export type CatalogueId = string;

export interface Catalogue {
  /**
   * "cat1." + base64url(SHA-256(JCS({ connections, entries, directoryConnection, notifyConnection }))).
   * A check result names the version it used.
   */
  version: string;
  /**
   * The ID of the connection that is the directory: a platform setting (integrations-shapes.md 2.7,
   * 2.9). `compile` is pure (E-3) and learns it here; it names this connection in every membership
   * read and every directory choice. Always present.
   */
  directoryConnection: string;
  /**
   * The ID of the connection that carries Notify: the platform's messages and alerts. A platform
   * setting (integrations-shapes.md 2.7, 2.9). A workflow never names it; the platform sends every
   * notification through it. Always present. It must name a configured connection, or start-up fails.
   */
  notifyConnection: string;
  connections: Connection[];
  /** Every entry of every connection, defaults written out. */
  entries: CatalogueEntry[];
}

/**
 * A configured instance of a connector: one outside system the platform can reach. Set up by a
 * platform admin from configuration at start-up (E-19, E-20); never by an author.
 */
export interface Connection {
  id: string;                     // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$; never renamed, never reused
  label: string;                  // "Jira"
  description: string | null;
  /**
   * ready:    authors may use its entries.
   * notSetUp: listed, but unusable until a platform admin finishes it; an entry of it is a To do at publish.
   * disabled: a platform admin has disabled it in configuration. Every entry of it then behaves as
   *           a disabled entry, its inbound hook answers 503, and its subscriptions' deliveries
   *           fail and retry. An entry of it is Worth knowing at publish.
   * Connections are applied from configuration at start-up only (E-20).
   */
  status: "ready" | "notSetUp" | "disabled";
}

export type CatalogueEntry = Operation | DataSource | Trigger | EventSink;

interface EntryBase {
  id: CatalogueId;
  connection: string;             // Connection.id
  name: string;                   // "createIssue"
  version: number;                // 1
  kind: "operation" | "dataSource" | "trigger" | "eventSink";
  label: string;                  // "Create a Jira issue"
  description: string | null;
  /** A newer entry ID. Published workflows keep running on this one. */
  supersededBy: CatalogueId | null;
  /**
   * ready:    usable.
   * disabled: its shape changed under this ID, or it is no longer declared, so the server refused
   *           it at start-up (E-20: the entry, not its connection). Its calls wait, a data source
   *           answers source-unavailable, a trigger's events are dropped; Worth knowing at publish.
   * Filled by the server at registration, never by a connector.
   */
  status: "ready" | "disabled";
}

/** A field of an input, a result, an item or an event, in the editor's value kinds (E-17). */
export interface Field {
  id: string;                     // ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$; unique among its siblings; never starts with $
  label: string;
  /** A list kept with a workflow cannot come from outside, so never `choiceFromList`. */
  kind: Exclude<ValueKind, "choiceFromList">;
  /** false: the key may be absent. It is never null. */
  required: boolean;
  /** Exactly for `choice` and `multipleChoice`: the allowed values, unique. */
  choices?: { value: string; label: string }[];
  /** `list` only: the kind of each item. Exactly one of `itemKind` and `fields` for a list. */
  itemKind?: ValueKind;
  /** A list of objects, or a `fieldGroup`: its fields. */
  fields?: Field[];
  /**
   * A `text` field only: the ID of the sibling field whose web address this field holds, so a page can
   * show that field as a link (a Jira issue's `url` is the address of its `key`). Display only: not
   * covered by the shape hash (E-32).
   */
  addressOf?: string;
}

/** Something a workflow asks a connection to do or to tell it (door 3: a call). */
export interface Operation extends EntryBase {
  kind: "operation";
  /**
   * read:  gives data and changes nothing outside ("Look up").
   * write: does something outside and answers at once ("Do").
   * await: asks the outside system to do something and waits until it reports the result,
   *        which may take long ("Wait for"). The kernel sees it as a write call (E-17).
   */
  sort: "read" | "write" | "await";
  input: Field[];
  result: Field[];
  /** The failure codes it can report, kebab-case, unique. A failure is recorded as { code, message }. */
  failureCodes: { code: string; label: string }[];
  /**
   * The default for "when the stage is entered again" (a send-back), written out for every write
   * and await operation; null exactly for read.
   *   once:  the first result is reused and nothing is done twice (one Jira issue per request).
   *   again: it is done again on every entry.
   * The author may choose otherwise (`UseConnection.ifStageEntersAgain`). Publish writes the choice
   * explicitly, so a later change here changes only later publishes.
   */
  onRepeat: "once" | "again" | null;
  /** One delivery or one status question. Default 30. */
  timeoutSeconds: number;
  /**
   * A call with no result after this many seconds raises one call-overdue alert to the workflow
   * admins (E-17). At least `timeoutSeconds`. Default 900 for read and write; required for await.
   */
  expectedWithinSeconds: number;
  /** Non-null exactly when sort is "await". */
  await: null | {
    /** The outside system can call the engine's callback URL to say the job has moved on. A callback is a nudge, never a result (E-17). */
    callback: boolean;
    /** How often the engine asks for the job's status while the action waits. At least 10. */
    pollSeconds: number;
  };
  /** Used by Try it and by the editor's examples. Values follow core-api.md section 2.4. */
  sample: {
    input: JsonObject;            // fits `input`
    result: JsonObject;           // fits `result`
    failure: { code: string; message: string } | null;   // code is one of failureCodes
  };
}

/**
 * Data for a question's choices (door 5). The connector offers two things for every data source
 * (E-17):
 *   list: the items for the inputs, with an optional search text when `searchable`, paged;
 *         used when the form is shown (runtime-api.md section 3.4).
 *   get:  one item by the value of a field (the question's stored field) for the same inputs;
 *         used when the person acts, to check the answer and take the source's label (E-20).
 * `get` finds an item only if `list` with the same inputs would return it. Stored values are
 * stable identifiers.
 */
export interface DataSource extends EntryBase {
  kind: "dataSource";
  input: Field[];                 // arguments, for example a filter or a parent choice
  item: Field[];                  // the fields of one item; a question names its stored and label fields
  searchable: boolean;            // list accepts a search text
  /** How long a list result is cached. Default 60; 0 = never cached. `get` is never cached. */
  cacheSeconds: number;
  /** One list or one get. Default 10. */
  timeoutSeconds: number;
  sample: { input: JsonObject; items: JsonObject[] };
}

/** An outside event that can start a request (door 1, "Starts when"). */
export interface Trigger extends EntryBase {
  kind: "trigger";
  /** What a binding reads as sent.<field>. A person field holds `{ type: "user", id }`, resolved by the connector, or is absent. */
  event: Field[];
  sample: { event: JsonObject };
}

/** A subscriber that outbound events are sent to (door 7). Display only: shows the editor which systems receive them. */

  kind: "eventSink";
}

===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/diff/diff.ts\n===
/**
 * `diff` (contract/core-api.md section 11): what changed between two authored workflows, for the
 * Publish dialog. Items are matched by ID, so a renamed item is one `part.changed`. Every item is
 * reported on its own: removing a stage also reports its tasks, buttons and arrows as removed.
 *
 * The rules where section 11 is silent:
 *  - A changed part is named by the longest reported part of `LOCATION_PARTS` that holds the change,
 *    otherwise by the item's top-level field (`look`, `colour`, `title` ...). An object added or removed
 *    is compared field by field, so adding `saveFailureAs` with `failed` is a change at `saveFailureAs.failed`.
 *  - An item moved when its parent changed, or the field of the parent that holds it (an action from
 *    "When this stage starts" to "After they respond"). `from` and `to` are the parent and that field.
 *  - A new order of items inside one field is a `part.changed` on the parent, at that field's part.
 *  - `before` and `after` are given only when small: a string, number or yes/no, or a list of them.
 *    An item inside a part is shown as its ID.
 *  - `null` and absent are the same.
 *  - The workflow is matched as the workflow, whatever its ID.
 *  - Order: by the item's place in `after`, then by code, then by part. A removed item comes just
 *    before the next item of `before` that is still there.
 * Pure and deterministic; never throws, on any two values.
 */
import { LOCATION_PARTS, type AuthoredWorkflow, type ItemKind, type Location } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Json } from "../evaluate/types.ts";
import { indexDocument } from "../index-doc.ts";
import type { Change } from "./types.ts";

type Obj = Record<string, unknown>;
const isObject = (x: unknown): x is Obj => typeof x === "object" && x !== null && !Array.isArray(x);

/** Fields of the workflow that `diff` ignores (section 11). */
const IGNORED = new Set(["diagram", "sampleRequest", "removedNames"]);

/** An item inside another item's content, standing for that item. */
class ChildRef {
  readonly id: string;
  constructor(id: string) {
    this.id = id;
  }
}

/** One item of one document. */
interface Entry {
  id: string;
  kind: ItemKind;
  /** Document order (the index's); the workflow is -1. */
  order: number;
  /** The parent's ID; `null` for the workflow's own items and for the workflow. */
  parent: string | null;
  /** The path from the parent's object to the field that holds the item (`tasks`, `form.pages`). */
  field: string;
  /** Position inside that field. */
  position: number;
  /** The item's own content: child items as `ChildRef`, no `id` (except the workflow's), no null. */
  content: unknown;
}

interface Side {
  root: Entry;
  /** Every item but the workflow, by ID. */
  items: Map<string, Entry>;
}

function read(doc: unknown): Side {
  const index = indexDocument(doc as AuthoredWorkflow);
  const rootId = isObject(doc) && typeof doc["id"] === "string" ? doc["id"] : "";
  const items = new Map<string, Entry>();

  const asChild = (node: unknown, parent: string | null, field: string, position: number): ChildRef | undefined => {
    if (!isObject(node) || typeof node["id"] !== "string") return undefined;
    const id = node["id"];
    const known = index.byId.get(id);
    if (known === undefined || id === rootId || items.has(id)) return undefined;
    const entry: Entry = { id, kind: known.kind, order: known.order, parent, field, position, content: undefined };
    items.set(id, entry);
    entry.content = contentOf(node, id, [], true);
    return new ChildRef(id);
  };

  const contentOf = (node: unknown, owner: string | null, path: readonly string[], dropId: boolean): unknown => {
    if (Array.isArray(node)) {
      const field = path.join(".");
      return node.map((x, i) => asChild(x, owner, field, i) ?? contentOf(x, owner, [...path, String(i)], false));
    }
    if (!isObject(node)) return node;
    const out: Obj = {};
    for (const key of Object.keys(node).sort()) {
      const value = node[key];
      if (value === null || value === undefined) continue;
      if (dropId && key === "id") continue;
      if (owner === null && path.length === 0 && IGNORED.has(key)) continue;
      out[key] = asChild(value, owner, [...path, key].join("."), 0) ?? contentOf(value, owner, [...path, key], false);
    }
    return out;
  };

  const root: Entry = { id: rootId, kind: "workflow", order: -1, parent: null, field: "", position: 0, content: undefined };
  root.content = contentOf(doc, null, [], false);
  return { root, items };
}

// Parts

const PATTERNS: Partial<Record<ItemKind, string[][]>> = Object.fromEntries(
  Object.entries(LOCATION_PARTS).map(([kind, parts]) => [kind, parts.map((p) => p.split("."))]),
);
const matches = (pattern: readonly string[], path: readonly string[]): boolean =>
  pattern.length <= path.length && pattern.every((s, i) => s.startsWith("<") || s === path[i]);

/** The part that names a change at `path`: the longest reported part holding it, else the top-level field. */
function partOf(kind: ItemKind, path: readonly string[]): string | undefined {
  if (path.length === 0) return undefined;
  let best: readonly string[] | undefined;
  for (const pattern of PATTERNS[kind] ?? []) if (matches(pattern, path) && (!best || pattern.length > best.length)) best = pattern;
  return path.slice(0, best ? best.length : 1).join(".");
}

/** Where a part comes in an item's list of changes: the order of `LOCATION_PARTS`, then the others. */
function partRank(kind: ItemKind, part: string | undefined): number {
  if (part === undefined) return -1;
  const path = part.split(".");
  const i = (PATTERNS[kind] ?? []).findIndex((p) => p.length === path.length && matches(p, path));
  return i < 0 ? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER : i;
}

// Content

/** Paths where two contents differ. Child items are left out of lists: they are compared on their own. */
function differences(a: unknown, b: unknown, path: readonly string[], out: string[][]): void {
  if (a instanceof ChildRef || b instanceof ChildRef) {
    if (!(a instanceof ChildRef && b instanceof ChildRef && a.id === b.id)) out.push([...path]);
    return;
  }
  if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) {
    const xa = a.filter((x) => !(x instanceof ChildRef));
    const xb = b.filter((x) => !(x instanceof ChildRef));
    if (xa.length !== xb.length) out.push([...path]);
    else xa.forEach((x, i) => differences(x, xb[i], [...path, String(i)], out));
    return;
  }
  // An object added or removed is compared field by field, so the change is named by the deepest reported part
  // that holds it (`saveFailureAs.failed`, not `saveFailureAs`).
  const one = (x: unknown, y: unknown): boolean => isObject(x) && Object.keys(x).length > 0 && (isObject(y) || y === undefined);
  if ((isObject(a) && isObject(b)) || one(a, b) || one(b, a)) {
    const keys = [...new Set([...Object.keys(isObject(a) ? a : {}), ...Object.keys(isObject(b) ? b : {})])].sort();
    for (const key of keys) differences(isObject(a) ? a[key] : undefined, isObject(b) ? b[key] : undefined, [...path, key], out);
    return;
  }
  if (a !== b) out.push([...path]);
}

/** The part's value when it is small (a string, number or yes/no, or a list of them); child items as their IDs. */
function small(content: unknown, part: string | undefined): Json | undefined {
  let node = content;
  for (const key of part === undefined ? [] : part.split(".")) node = isObject(node) ? node[key] : undefined;
  const scalar = (x: unknown): string | number | boolean | undefined =>
    x instanceof ChildRef ? x.id : typeof x === "string" || typeof x === "boolean" || (typeof x === "number" && Number.isFinite(x)) ? x : undefined;
  if (!Array.isArray(node)) return scalar(node);
  const list = node.map(scalar);
  return list.every((x) => x !== undefined) ? (list as Json[]) : undefined;
}

// The changes

interface Sorted {
  change: Change;
  /** Document order: the item's place in `after`, or for a removed item the place of the item before it. */
  key: [number, number, number, number, number, string];
}

const CODES = ["item.added", "item.moved", "item.removed", "part.changed"];

export function diff(before: AuthoredWorkflow, after: AuthoredWorkflow): Change[] {
  const b = read(before);
  const a = read(after);
  const out: Sorted[] = [];
  const at = (entry: Entry): Location => ({ item: entry.id });
  const push = (change: Change, primary: number, tier: number, secondary: number, kind: ItemKind, part?: string): void => {
    out.push({ change, key: [primary, tier, secondary, CODES.indexOf(change.code), partRank(kind, part), part ?? ""] });
  };

  const matched = (id: string): [Entry, Entry] | undefined => {
    const x = b.items.get(id);
    const y = a.items.get(id);
    return x && y && x.kind === y.kind ? [x, y] : undefined;
  };
  const parentLocation = (side: Side, entry: Entry): Location => {
    const parent = entry.parent === null ? side.root.id : entry.parent;
    return entry.field ? { item: parent, part: entry.field } : { item: parent };
  };

  // Changed parts: content, then a new order of items inside one field.
  const changedParts = new Map<string | null, Set<string | undefined>>();
  const note = (id: string | null, part: string | undefined): void => {
    const parts = changedParts.get(id) ?? new Set<string | undefined>();
    parts.add(part);
    changedParts.set(id, parts);
  };
  const compare = (x: Entry, y: Entry, id: string | null): void => {
    const paths: string[][] = [];
    differences(x.content, y.content, [], paths);
    for (const path of paths) note(id, partOf(y.kind, path));
  };
  compare(b.root, a.root, null);
  for (const id of a.items.keys()) {
    const pair = matched(id);
    if (pair) compare(pair[0], pair[1], id);
  }
  const groups = (side: Side): Map<string, Entry[]> => {
    const out = new Map<string, Entry[]>();
    for (const entry of side.items.values()) {
      const key = JSON.stringify([entry.parent, entry.field]);
      out.set(key, [...(out.get(key) ?? []), entry]);
    }
    for (const list of out.values()) list.sort((p, q) => p.position - q.position);
    return out;
  };
  const beforeGroups = groups(b);
  for (const [key, afterList] of groups(a)) {
    const beforeList = beforeGroups.get(key) ?? [];
    const parent = afterList[0]?.parent ?? null;
    if (parent !== null && !matched(parent)) continue;
    const inBefore = new Set(beforeList.map((e) => e.id));
    const inAfter = new Set(afterList.map((e) => e.id));
    const order1 = beforeList.filter((e) => inAfter.has(e.id)).map((e) => e.id);
    const order2 = afterList.filter((e) => inBefore.has(e.id)).map((e) => e.id);
    if (order1.join("\u0000") !== order2.join("\u0000")) {
      const kind = parent === null ? "workflow" : (a.items.get(parent)?.kind ?? "workflow");
      note(parent, partOf(kind, (afterList[0]?.field ?? "").split(".")));
    }
  }
  const reportParts = (x: Entry, y: Entry, id: string | null): void => {
    for (const part of changedParts.get(id) ?? []) {
      const params: { itemKind: ItemKind; before?: Json; after?: Json } = { itemKind: y.kind };
      const was = small(x.content, part);
      const is = small(y.content, part);
      if (was !== undefined) params.before = was;
      if (is !== undefined) params.after = is;
      const location: Location = part === undefined ? at(y) : { item: y.id, part };
      push({ code: "part.changed", location, params }, y.order, 0, 0, y.kind, part);
    }
  };

  reportParts(b.root, a.root, null);
  for (const [id, y] of a.items) {
    const pair = matched(id);
    if (!pair) {
      push({ code: "item.added", location: at(y), params: { itemKind: y.kind } }, y.order, 0, 0, y.kind);
      continue;
    }
    const x = pair[0];
    if (x.parent !== y.parent || x.field !== y.field)
      push(
        { code: "item.moved", location: at(y), params: { itemKind: y.kind, from: parentLocation(b, x), to: parentLocation(a, y) } },
        y.order, 0, 0, y.kind,
      );
    reportParts(x, y, id);
  }

  // A removed item comes just before the next item of `before` that is still there.
  let anchor = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
  for (const x of [...b.items.values()].sort((p, q) => q.order - p.order)) {
    const pair = matched(x.id);
    if (pair) anchor = pair[1].order;
    else push({ code: "item.removed", location: at(x), params: { itemKind: x.kind } }, anchor, -1, x.order, x.kind);
  }

  out.sort((p, q) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      const d = (p.key[i] as number) - (q.key[i] as number);
      if (d !== 0) return d;
    }
    return p.key[5] < q.key[5] ? -1 : p.key[5] > q.key[5] ? 1 : 0;
  });
  return out.map((s) => s.change);
}

/** What `diff` returns (contract/core-api.md section 11). */
import type { ItemKind, Location } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Coded } from "../coded.ts";
import type { Json } from "../evaluate/types.ts";

export interface ChangeParams {
  "item.added": { itemKind: ItemKind };
  "item.removed": { itemKind: ItemKind };
  /** Its parent, or the field of the parent that holds it, changed. `from` and `to` name the parent and that field. */
  "item.moved": { itemKind: ItemKind; from: Location; to: Location };
  /** `before` and `after` are given only for small parts, and are absent where the part was absent or `null`. */
  "part.changed": { itemKind: ItemKind; before?: Json; after?: Json };
}

/** The location is in `after`; for `item.removed` it is in `before`. */
export type Change = Coded<ChangeParams, { location: Location }>;
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/evaluate/constants.ts\n===
/**
 * An authored constant as the JSON a value of a given kind holds (core-api.md 2.4). Used for the
 * sample request's answers and for list cells. A constant that does not fit the kind, or that is
 * empty, gives nothing: empty is absent.
 */
import { isDate } from "../../schema/formats.ts";
import type { ValueKind } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Json } from "./types.ts";

type Obj = Record<string, unknown>;
const isObject = (x: unknown): x is Obj => typeof x === "object" && x !== null && !Array.isArray(x);
const isString = (x: unknown): x is string => typeof x === "string";

function refOf(type: "user" | "group", x: unknown): Json | undefined {
  return isObject(x) && isString(x["directoryId"]) && x["directoryId"] !== "" ? { type, id: x["directoryId"] } : undefined;
}

/** Each item once, in `order` where it is known, the others after them in the order given. */
function ordered(ids: readonly string[], order: readonly string[] | undefined): string[] {
  const distinct = [...new Set(ids)];
  if (!order) return distinct;
  const at = (id: string) => {
    const i = order.indexOf(id);
    return i < 0 ? order.length : i;
  };
  return distinct.map((id, i) => ({ id, i })).sort((a, b) => at(a.id) - at(b.id) || a.i - b.i).map((x) => x.id);
}

/**
 * The JSON of constant `c` for a value of `kind`, or undefined. `order` is the choice order of a
 * multiple choice: its answer lists the chosen IDs in that order.
 */
export function constantJson(c: unknown, kind: ValueKind | undefined, order?: readonly string[]): Json | undefined {
  if (!isObject(c)) return undefined;
  switch (kind) {
    case "text":
    case "longText":
      return isString(c["text"]) && c["text"] !== "" ? c["text"] : undefined;
    case "number": {
      const n = c["number"];
      if (typeof n !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(n)) return undefined;
      return Number.isInteger(n) && !Number.isSafeInteger(n) ? undefined : n;
    }
    case "yesNo":
      return typeof c["yesNo"] === "boolean" ? c["yesNo"] : undefined;
    case "date":
      return isString(c["date"]) && isDate(c["date"]) ? c["date"] : undefined;
    case "choice":
      if (isString(c["choice"])) return c["choice"];
      if (isString(c["failureCode"])) return c["failureCode"];
      return isString(c["button"]) ? c["button"] : undefined;
    case "multipleChoice": {
      const ids = c["choices"];
      if (!Array.isArray(ids) || ids.length === 0 || !ids.every(isString)) return undefined;
      return ordered(ids, order);
    }
    case "choiceFromList":
      return isString(c["row"]) ? c["row"] : undefined;
    case "choiceFromConnection": {
      const cc = c["connectionChoice"];
      if (!isObject(cc) || !isString(cc["label"])) return undefined;
      const stored = cc["stored"];
      if (isString(stored) || (typeof stored === "number" && Number.isFinite(stored))) return { stored, label: cc["label"] };
      return undefined;
    }
    case "person":
      return refOf("user", c["person"]);
    case "group":
      return refOf("group", c["group"]);
    case "people": {
      const list = c["people"];
      if (!Array.isArray(list) || list.length === 0) return undefined;
      const refs = list.map((p) => refOf("user", p));
      if (refs.some((r) => r === undefined)) return undefined;
      const seen = new Set<string>();
      return (refs as { type: string; id: string }[]).filter((r) => !seen.has(r.id) && (seen.add(r.id), true));
    }
    default:
      return undefined;
  }
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/evaluate/evaluate-sent.ts\n===
/**
 * `evaluateSent` (core-api.md 6.3): a part of a "Starts when" binding worked out over what the other
 * system sent, or over the trigger's catalogue sample. A binding reads only what was sent, so no
 * lookup is ever needed. It compiles in the compiler's `sent` place (compiler.md 10.6) and runs in
 * the engine's CEL environment, as the trigger's `when` and `data` do.
 */
import { t, type CelType, type JsonValue } from "../../cel/types.ts";
import { compileCondition, compileExpression, compileTextTemplate, type SentPlace } from "../compile/expr/index.ts";
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Location, SentCondition, SentExpression, SentTemplate, ValueKind } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Catalogue, Field } from "../contract/catalogue.ts";
import { CONDITION_PARTS } from "./evaluate.ts";
import { docSetup, environmentFor, isObject, isString, run, sentType, withKind } from "./setup.ts";
import type { Json, SampleResult } from "./types.ts";

const OTHER: SampleResult = { result: "error", error: "other", params: {} };

/** Every sent field by its dotted ID, with its kind. */
function fieldKinds(fields: readonly Field[], prefix = "", out: Record<string, ValueKind> = {}): Record<string, ValueKind> {
  for (const f of fields) {
    if (!isObject(f) || !isString(f.id)) continue;
    const id = `${prefix}${f.id}`;
    out[id] = f.kind;
    if (Array.isArray(f.fields) && f.kind !== "list") fieldKinds(f.fields, `${id}.`, out);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The catalogue's JSON writes null out (integrations-shapes.md); a value never holds it, so null is absent. */
function withoutNulls(x: unknown): Json | undefined {
  if (x === null || x === undefined) return undefined;
  if (Array.isArray(x)) return x.map(withoutNulls).filter((v): v is Json => v !== undefined);
  if (isObject(x)) {
    const out: Record<string, Json> = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(x)) {
      const j = withoutNulls(v);
      if (j !== undefined) out[k] = j;
    }
    return out;
  }
  return typeof x === "string" || typeof x === "number" || typeof x === "boolean" ? x : undefined;
}

export function evaluateSent(
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue, at: Location, what: SentExpression | SentTemplate | SentCondition, sent?: Record<string, Json>,
): SampleResult {
  const s = docSetup(workflow, catalogue);
  const startsWhen = isObject(workflow) && isObject(workflow.start) && Array.isArray(workflow.start.startsWhen) ? workflow.start.startsWhen : [];
  const binding = startsWhen.find((b) => isObject(b) && b.id === at.item);
  const entry = s.catalogue.entry(binding?.trigger);
  const trigger = entry?.kind === "trigger" ? entry : undefined;
  const fields = trigger ? s.catalogue.fields(trigger, "event") : [];
  // With no trigger, every sent field is untyped, so each reads as absent rather than failing the check.
  const type: CelType = trigger ? sentType(fields) : t.dyn;
  const given = sent ?? (trigger && isObject(trigger.sample) ? trigger.sample.event : {});
  const data = withoutNulls(given);

  const place: SentPlace = { in: "sent", fields: fieldKinds(fields) };
  const env = environmentFor(s, { groupsKey: "sent__groups", sent: type });
  let compiled: { cel: string; kind?: ValueKind };
  if (Array.isArray(what)) {
    const r = compileTextTemplate(what, place, s.world);
    if (!r.ok) return OTHER;
    compiled = { cel: r.cel, kind: "text" };
  } else if (at.part !== undefined && CONDITION_PARTS.has(at.part)) {
    const r = compileCondition(what, place, s.world);
    if (!r.ok) return OTHER;
    compiled = { cel: r.cel, kind: "yesNo" };
  } else {
    const r = compileExpression(what, place, s.world);
    if (!r.ok) return OTHER;
    compiled = r.kind === undefined ? { cel: r.cel } : { cel: r.cel, kind: r.kind };
  }
  const context: Record<string, JsonValue> = { sent: isObject(data) ? (data as JsonValue) : {} };
  return withKind(run(env, compiled.cel, context), compiled.kind);
}
