/**
 * A published version read once for the request views, the story and the test host: the definition with
 * its origin map, the authored source it was compiled from, and the catalogue. Every engine element a
 * reader meets is turned into an authored Location here, through the origin map (E-7, E-18), never by
 * the shape of an ID.
 */
import type { Origin, PublishedDefinition, Wait } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { findWaitDef, splitElement } from "../../kernel/decide/definition.ts";
import { authoredStageOf } from "../../kernel/stuck/index.ts";
import { CatalogueIndex } from "../check/context.ts";
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Location, StageId, Status } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Catalogue } from "../contract/catalogue.ts";
import { stageGraph, type StageGraph } from "../facts/graph.ts";
import { indexDocument, type DocIndex, type IndexedItem } from "../index-doc.ts";
import type { OperationSort } from "./types.ts";

/** What a reader needs of one published version: the definition, its authored source and the catalogue. */
export interface PublishedVersion {
  definition: PublishedDefinition;
  source: AuthoredWorkflow;
  catalogue: Catalogue;
}

/** The part of an authored stage an engine stage belongs to (core-api.md 8, `RequestView.stage`). */
export type StagePart = "whenThisStageStarts" | "tasks" | "afterTheyRespond" | "arrows";

function asLocation(o: Origin | undefined): Location | undefined {
  const item = o?.item[0];
  if (item === undefined) return undefined;
  return o?.part === null || o?.part === undefined ? { item } : { item, part: o.part };
}

export class Reading {
  readonly def: PublishedDefinition;
  readonly source: AuthoredWorkflow;
  readonly catalogue: CatalogueIndex;
  readonly ix: DocIndex;
  readonly graph: StageGraph;
  readonly valueIds: ReadonlySet<string>;
  readonly directory: string;

  constructor(p: PublishedVersion) {
    this.def = p.definition;
    this.source = p.source;
    this.catalogue = new CatalogueIndex(p.catalogue);
    this.ix = indexDocument(p.source);
    this.graph = stageGraph(this.ix);
    this.valueIds = new Set(this.ix.valueIds);
    const c: unknown = p.catalogue;
    const dir = typeof c === "object" && c !== null ? (c as Record<string, unknown>)["directoryConnection"] : undefined;
    this.directory = typeof dir === "string" ? dir : "directory";
  }

  item(id: string | undefined): IndexedItem | undefined {
    return id === undefined ? undefined : this.ix.byId.get(id);
  }

  kindOf(id: string | undefined): string | undefined {
    return this.item(id)?.kind;
  }

  /** The Location an origin key names, or undefined when the map has no such key. */
  origin(key: string): Location | undefined {
    return asLocation(this.def.origins[key]);
  }

  /** A field's origin, else its element's. */
  originOf(key: string, field: string | null | undefined): Location | undefined {
    return (field ? this.origin(`${key}#${field}`) : undefined) ?? this.origin(key);
  }

  /** Where an element named by a full ID came from: a transition, a wait or a stage, field first. */
  locate(element: string | null | undefined, field?: string | null): Location | undefined {
    if (!element) return undefined;
    for (const kind of ["transition", "wait", "stage"]) {
      const at = this.originOf(`${kind}:${element}`, field);
      if (at !== undefined) return at;
    }
    return undefined;
  }

  /**
   * The authored stage an engine stage belongs to, by the kernel's one mapper (`authoredStageOf`);
   * undefined for the root and for a stage the source does not hold.
   */
  authoredStage(engineStage: string | null | undefined): StageId | undefined {
    return this.stageOfItem(authoredStageOf(this.def, engineStage ?? null));
  }

  /**
   * The authored stage an item names: the stage itself, or the stage an item inside one is in. The kernel's
   * mapper names an item it cannot place in a stage from the definition alone: Try it's step for an
   * unfinished action, which has no transitions to follow.
   */
  stageOfItem(id: string | null | undefined): StageId | undefined {
    const found = this.item(id ?? undefined);
    if (found === undefined) return undefined;
    // The document index holds stages under their stage IDs.
    return (found.kind === "stage" ? found.id : found.stage) as StageId | undefined;
  }

  /** Which part of its authored stage an engine stage is; undefined for an ending. */
  stagePart(engineStage: string): StagePart | undefined {
    const at = this.origin(`stage:${engineStage}`);
    const found = this.item(at?.item);
    if (found === undefined) return undefined;
    if (found.kind === "stage") return at?.part === "tasks" ? "tasks" : at?.part === "arrows" ? "arrows" : undefined;
    if (found.kind === "arrow") return "arrows";
    if (found.kind === "action") {
      const view = found.stage === undefined ? undefined : this.ix.stageById.get(found.stage);
      return view?.arrival.some((a) => a.id === found.id) ? "whenThisStageStarts" : "afterTheyRespond";
    }
    return undefined;
  }

  /** The authored task of a person wait. */
  taskOf(element: string): string | undefined {
    const item = this.origin(`wait:${element}`)?.item;
    return this.kindOf(item) === "task" ? item : undefined;
  }

  /**
   * The authored action a call wait makes, when the wait is the action's own call (`A__run.A`), not a
   * read the compiler added for it (`A__groups.A__read`, `T__members`).
   */
  actionOf(element: string): string | undefined {
    const item = this.origin(`wait:${element}`)?.item;
    return item !== undefined && this.kindOf(item) === "action" && splitElement(element).local === item ? item : undefined;
  }

  waitDef(element: string): Wait | undefined {
    return findWaitDef(this.def, element);
  }

  /** The catalogue's sort of an operation; a write that the catalogue calls an await reads as one. */
  sortOf(connection: string, op: string): OperationSort {
    const entry = this.catalogue.entry(`${connection}.${op}`);
    if (entry?.kind === "operation" && (entry.sort === "read" || entry.sort === "write" || entry.sort === "await")) return entry.sort;
    const wait = this.def.root.stages.flatMap((s) => s.waits).find((w) => w.kind === "call" && w.connection === connection && w.op === op);
    return wait?.kind === "call" && wait.effect === "read" ? "read" : "write";
  }

  /** The question IDs of a task's form. */
  questionsOf(task: string | undefined): ReadonlySet<string> {
    const view = task === undefined ? undefined : this.ix.taskById.get(task);
    return new Set(view?.questions.map((q) => q.question.id) ?? []);
  }

  status(id: string | null | undefined): Status | undefined {
    if (!id) return undefined;
    return (Array.isArray(this.source.statuses) ? this.source.statuses : []).find((s) => s.id === id);
  }

  /** The start stage's task: the item of the definition's start wait. */
  startTask(): string | undefined {
    return this.taskOf(this.def.start) ?? this.ix.stageById.get(this.source.start?.stage ?? "")?.tasks[0]?.task.id;
  }
}

const readings = new WeakMap<PublishedDefinition, Reading>();

/** One Reading per definition, kept while it lives. */
export function readingOf(p: PublishedVersion): Reading {
  const known = readings.get(p.definition);
  if (known !== undefined && known.source === p.source) return known;
  const r = new Reading(p);
  readings.set(p.definition, r);
  return r;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/view/refusals.ts\n===
/**
 * A kernel refusal as the contract reports it (core-api.md 2.6 and 7.2): the code and the place the author
 * wrote the rule, never a compiled check, wait or element. A form rule the compiler enforces as a check
 * is reported as the rule the author wrote (compiler.md 12.3).
 */
import type { JsonObject } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { KernelRefusal } from "../../kernel/decide/types.ts";
import type { ExpressionErrorKind } from "../../cel/types.ts";
import type { InvalidDataRule } from "../../schema/types.ts";
import type { ButtonId, Location } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import { readingOf, type PublishedVersion, type Reading } from "./reading.ts";
import type { By, Refusal } from "./types.ts";

/** What the refused input was about. */
export interface RefusalContext {
  /** The person wait acted on (the start wait for a start). */
  element?: string;
  /** The button pressed. */
  button?: string;
  /** The answers sent, to tell an empty multiple choice from one out of its choices. */
  answers?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}

const EXPRESSION_ERRORS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["no-such-key", "index-out-of-range", "absent-value", "wrong-kind", "division-by-zero", "overflow", "other"]);

function expressionError(x: unknown): ExpressionErrorKind {
  return typeof x === "string" && EXPRESSION_ERRORS.has(x) ? (x as ExpressionErrorKind) : "other";
}

const withLocation = <R extends Refusal>(r: R, location: Location | undefined): R => (location === undefined ? r : { ...r, location });

/** The first property an RFC 6901 pointer into the answers names. */
function propertyOf(pointer: unknown): string {
  const first = typeof pointer === "string" ? (pointer.split("/")[1] ?? "") : "";
  return first.replace(/~1/g, "/").replace(/~0/g, "~");
}

function taskLocation(r: Reading, ctx: RefusalContext, part?: string): Location | undefined {
  const task = ctx.element === undefined ? undefined : r.taskOf(ctx.element);
  if (task === undefined) return undefined;
  return part === undefined ? { item: task } : { item: task, part };
}

function invalidData(r: Reading, ctx: RefusalContext, params: JsonObject): Refusal {
  const rule = (typeof params["rule"] === "string" ? params["rule"] : "wrong-kind") as InvalidDataRule;
  const q = propertyOf(params["pointer"]);
  const task = ctx.element === undefined ? undefined : r.taskOf(ctx.element);
  const isQuestion = r.questionsOf(task).has(q);
  const location: Location | undefined = isQuestion ? (rule === "not-a-choice" ? { item: q, part: "choices" } : { item: q }) : taskLocation(r, ctx);
  return withLocation({ code: "invalid-data", params: { rule } }, location);
}

/** A check is reported as the form rule it enforces, by the rule's local name (compiler.md 1.2, 12.3). */
function check(r: Reading, ctx: RefusalContext, params: JsonObject): Refusal {
  const id = typeof params["check"] === "string" ? params["check"] : "";
  const at = r.origin(`check:${ctx.element ?? ""}/${ctx.button ?? ""}/${id}`);
  const local = id.slice(id.lastIndexOf("__") + 2);
  switch (local) {
    case "hidden":
      return withLocation({ code: "invalid-data", params: { rule: "hidden-answered" } }, at);
    case "needed":
      return withLocation({ code: "invalid-data", params: { rule: "required" } }, at);
    case "choice": {
      // One check covers a multiple choice's order and its emptiness; an empty one is `too-short` (core-api.md 2.4).
      const answer = at === undefined ? undefined : ctx.answers?.[at.item];
      if (Array.isArray(answer) && answer.length === 0) return withLocation({ code: "invalid-data", params: { rule: "too-short" } }, { item: at?.item ?? "" });
      return withLocation({ code: "invalid-data", params: { rule: "not-a-choice" } }, at);
    }
    case "requester":
      return withLocation({ code: "invalid-data", params: { rule: "unknown-question" } }, taskLocation(r, ctx) ?? at);
    default: {
      const button = (at?.item ?? ctx.button ?? "") as ButtonId;
      const message = params["message"];
      const out: Refusal = withLocation({ code: "check", params: { button } }, at);
      return typeof message === "string" && message !== "" ? { ...out, message } : out;
    }
  }
}

/** Where a failing expression of a person wait was written: a check's `when`, a lookup input, `may`. */
function ruleErrorLocation(r: Reading, params: JsonObject): Location | undefined {
  const element = typeof params["element"] === "string" ? params["element"] : "";
  const field = typeof params["field"] === "string" ? params["field"] : "";
  const wait = r.waitDef(element);
  const checkAt = /^\/outcomes\/(\d+)\/checks\/(\d+)\/when$/.exec(field);
  if (checkAt !== null && wait?.kind === "person") {
    const outcome = wait.outcomes[Number(checkAt[1])];
    const c = outcome?.checks[Number(checkAt[2])];
    if (outcome !== undefined && c !== undefined) return r.originOf(`check:${element}/${outcome.id}/${c.id}`, "/when");
  }
  const lookupAt = /^\/outcomes\/(\d+)(\/lookups\/.*)$/.exec(field);
  if (lookupAt !== null && wait?.kind === "person") {
    const outcome = wait.outcomes[Number(lookupAt[1])];
    if (outcome !== undefined) return r.originOf(`outcome:${element}/${outcome.id}`, lookupAt[2]);
  }
  return r.locate(element, field);
}

/**
 * `wait-not-open`, from the kernel's params: a completed wait says who completed it (`by`) and with which
 * outcome (`outcome`, the button), also after the request closed (E-27); `requestClosed` is for a wait the
 * close ended.
 */
function waitNotOpen(params: JsonObject): Refusal {
  const state = params["state"];
  if (state === "completed") {
    const p: { state: "completed"; by?: By; button?: ButtonId } = { state: "completed" };
    const by = params["by"];
    const button = params["outcome"];
    if (isRef(by)) p.by = { type: by.type as By["type"], id: by.id };
    if (typeof button === "string" && button !== "") p.button = button as ButtonId;
    return { code: "wait-not-open", params: p };
  }
  if (state === "requestClosed") return { code: "wait-not-open", params: { state: "requestClosed" } };
  return { code: "wait-not-open", params: { state: state === "skipped" ? "skipped" : "cancelled" } };
}

function isRef(x: unknown): x is { type: string; id: string } {
  return typeof x === "object" && x !== null && typeof (x as { type?: unknown }).type === "string" && typeof (x as { id?: unknown }).id === "string";
}

/**
 * A kernel refusal of a turn on a published version, as the contract reports it: the mapping the server and
 * Try it's test host share (core-api.md 7.2). `context` says what the refused input was about.
 */
export function refusalOf(published: PublishedVersion, refusal: KernelRefusal, context: RefusalContext = {}): Refusal {
  return toRefusal(readingOf(published), refusal, context);
}

export function toRefusal(r: Reading, k: KernelRefusal, ctx: RefusalContext = {}): Refusal {
  const p = k.params;
  switch (k.reason) {
    case "wait-not-open":
      return withLocation(waitNotOpen(p), taskLocation(r, ctx));
    case "unknown-outcome":
      return withLocation({ code: "unknown-button", params: { button: (ctx.button ?? String(p["outcome"] ?? "")) as ButtonId } }, taskLocation(r, ctx));
    case "membership-unavailable":
      return { code: "membership-unavailable", params: {} };
    case "not-assignee":
      return withLocation({ code: "not-assignee", params: {} }, taskLocation(r, ctx, "whoIsAsked"));
    case "may":
      return withLocation({ code: "may", params: {} }, taskLocation(r, ctx, "requesterCanAnswer"));
    case "invalid-data":
      return invalidData(r, ctx, p);
    case "source-unavailable":
    case "choice-unknown": {
      const q = typeof p["property"] === "string" ? p["property"] : "";
      return { code: k.reason, params: {}, location: { item: q, part: "choices" } };
    }
    case "check":
      return check(r, ctx, p);
    case "rule-error":
      return withLocation({ code: "rule-error", params: { error: expressionError(p["error"]) } }, ruleErrorLocation(r, p));
    case "not-admin":
      return { code: "not-admin", params: {} };
    case "request-closed":
      return { code: "request-closed", params: {} };
    case "not-started":
      return { code: "not-found", params: { what: "request" } };
    case "unknown-wait":
      // A wait the request never opened (E-27).
      return { code: "not-found", params: { what: "task" } };
    default:
      // already-started, action-error, invalid-action: the host builds every kernel
      // input itself, so none reaches a caller (runtime-api.md 5.1); one that does is a bug.
      return { code: "internal", params: {} };
  }
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/view/replay.ts\n===
/**
 * A request's history folded one turn at a time, with the stuck state after each turn. The request view
 * and the story both read it, so they agree on when a request became stuck (core-api.md sections 8, 9).
 * A turn is the events that share their `turn` (the seq of the input that caused them).
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { evolve } from "../../kernel/evolve.ts";
import { emptyState, type RequestState } from "../../kernel/state.ts";
import { timestamp } from "./ids.ts";
import type { Reading } from "./reading.ts";
import { sameStuck, stuckNow, type StuckOptions } from "./stuck.ts";
import type { Stuck } from "./types.ts";

export interface TurnRecord {
  turn: number;
  events: AnyEventRecord[];
  before: RequestState;
  after: RequestState;
  stuckBefore: Stuck | null;
  /** The stuck state after the turn; `at` is when it began, which may be an earlier turn. */
  stuck: Stuck | null;
}

/** The events of each turn, in order. */
export function turnsOf(events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]): AnyEventRecord[][] {
  const turns: AnyEventRecord[][] = [];
  for (const e of events) {
    const last = turns.at(-1);
    if (last !== undefined && last[0]?.turn === e.turn) last.push(e);
    else turns.push([e]);
  }
  return turns;
}

export function replay(r: Reading, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], options: StuckOptions = {}): TurnRecord[] {
  const out: TurnRecord[] = [];
  let state = emptyState();
  let stuck: Stuck | null = null;
  for (const turn of turnsOf(events)) {
    const before = state;
    for (const e of turn) state = evolve(state, e);
    const now = stuckNow(r, state, options);
    const stuckBefore = stuck;
    if (now === null) stuck = null;
    else {
      const last = turn[turn.length - 1];
      const at: string = stuck !== null && sameStuck(stuck, now) ? stuck.at : timestamp(last?.at ?? "");
      stuck = { ...now, at };
    }
    out.push({ turn: turn[0]?.turn ?? 0, events: turn, before, after: state, stuckBefore, stuck });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The request view (core-api.md section 8), folded from the request's events and the published version.
 * Shared by Try it and the runtime: the live server adds `workflow`, `version` and the open actions'
 * `admin` fields from its own tables; Try it adds the call references.
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, JsonObject } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { TraceEntry } from "../../kernel/decide/types.ts";
import { emptyState } from "../../kernel/state.ts";
import type { Json, Ref, Values } from "../evaluate/types.ts";
import { storyOf } from "../story/story.ts";
import { timestamp } from "./ids.ts";
import { readingOf, type PublishedVersion, type Reading } from "./reading.ts";
import { replay } from "./replay.ts";
import { forViewer, type StuckOptions } from "./stuck.ts";
import { openActions, openTasks, type Viewer } from "./tasks.ts";
import type { By, RequestView, ServerWorkflowId, VersionNumber } from "./types.ts";

export interface ViewOptions extends StuckOptions {
  viewer?: Viewer;
  /** Try it: `decide`'s trace of each turn, for `why.notFitting`. */
  why?: ReadonlyMap<number, readonly TraceEntry[]>;
  /** Try it: give each open action its call reference. */
  calls?: boolean;
  /** Live only. */
  workflow?: ServerWorkflowId;
  version?: VersionNumber;
  /** Add each story entry's events. */
  debug?: boolean;
}

/** The author values of the data: the keys that are value IDs of this version. */
export function valuesOf(r: Reading, data: JsonObject): Values {
  const out: Record<string, Json> = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(data)) if (r.valueIds.has(k)) out[k] = v as Json;
  return out as Values;
}

/** The Requester: the recorded `requester`, else the person who started the request. */
export function requesterOf(data: JsonObject, by: { type: string; id: string } | undefined): Ref | undefined {
  const r = data["requester"];
  if (typeof r === "object" && r !== null && !Array.isArray(r) && r["type"] === "user" && typeof r["id"] === "string") return { type: "user", id: r["id"] };
  return by?.type === "user" ? { type: "user", id: by.id } : undefined;
}

/** Throws when `events` holds no start: a request view needs a request. */
export function requestView(published: PublishedVersion, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], options: ViewOptions = {}): RequestView {
  const r = readingOf(published);
  const records = replay(r, events, options);
  const state = records.at(-1)?.after ?? emptyState();
  const request = state.request;
  if (request === null) throw new Error("a request view needs the request's events from its start");
  const isAdmin = options.viewer?.isAdmin === true;

  const child = state.activeStages.filter((s) => s.stage !== "root").at(-1);
  const authored = r.authoredStage(child?.stage) ?? "";
  const part = child === undefined ? undefined : r.stagePart(child.stage);
  const view: RequestView = {
    requestId: request.id,
    readableId: String(request.readableId),
    stage: part === undefined ? { item: authored } : { item: authored, part },
    startedBy: { type: request.by.type as By["type"], id: request.by.id },
    startedAt: timestamp(request.at),
    updatedAt: timestamp(state.lastAt),
    lastSeq: state.lastSeq,
    values: valuesOf(r, state.data),
    tasks: openTasks(r, request.id, state, options.viewer),
    actions: openActions(r, request.id, state, options.calls === true),
    story: storyOf(r, records, { ...options, admin: isAdmin }),
    viewer: { isAdmin },
  };
  if (options.workflow !== undefined) view.workflow = options.workflow;
  if (options.version !== undefined) view.version = options.version;
  const status = r.status(state.status?.id);
  if (status !== undefined) view.status = status;
  if (state.closed !== null) {
    const ending = state.closed.stage === null ? undefined : r.authoredStage(state.closed.stage);
    view.closed = ending === undefined ? { at: timestamp(state.closed.at), byAdmin: state.closed.stage === null } : { at: timestamp(state.closed.at), ending, byAdmin: false };
  }
  const requester = requesterOf(state.data, request.by);
  if (requester !== undefined) view.requester = requester;
  const stuck = records.at(-1)?.stuck ?? null;
  if (stuck !== null) view.stuck = forViewer(stuck, isAdmin);
  return view;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/view/stuck.ts\n===
/**
 * The stuck state as people see it (core-api.md section 8): the reason, located in the authored workflow,
 * with the engineers' detail for the people who look after stuck requests. It is read from history only:
 * the kernel-level state (`stuckStateOf`, the one rule every reader shares) plus the origin map.
 */
import { nobodyToAsk, stuckStateOf } from "../../kernel/stuck/index.ts";
import { currentWait, type FaultRecord, type RequestState } from "../../kernel/state.ts";
import type { ExpressionErrorKind } from "../../cel/types.ts";
import type { Location } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Unfinished } from "../compile/types.ts";
import type { Reading } from "./reading.ts";
import type { Stuck, StuckDetail } from "./types.ts";

export interface StuckOptions {
  /** Try it: the parts compile could not build; a request stuck in one is `unfinished`. */
  unfinished?: readonly Unfinished[];
  /** How many times a call was delivered, for `admin.attempts`; absent: not known here. */
  attempts?: (element: string) => number | undefined;
}

/** The stuck state now, without `at`, which only history can give. */
export type StuckNow = Omit<Stuck, "at">;

const EXPRESSION_ERRORS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["no-such-key", "index-out-of-range", "absent-value", "wrong-kind", "division-by-zero", "overflow", "other"]);

/** A missing key is reported only when it names something authored: a value or a catalogue field. */
function authoredKey(r: Reading, key: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (typeof key !== "string" || key.includes("__")) return undefined;
  if (r.valueIds.has(key)) return key;
  for (const view of r.ix.stages)
    for (const a of [...view.arrival, ...view.after]) {
      if (a.type !== "useConnection") continue;
      const entry = r.catalogue.entry(a.operation);
      if ([...r.catalogue.fields(entry, "input"), ...r.catalogue.fields(entry, "result")].some((f) => f.id === key)) return key;
    }
  return undefined;
}

function errorDetail(r: Reading, fault: FaultRecord): StuckDetail {
  const detail: StuckDetail = { fault: fault.error.code };
  const params = fault.error.params;
  const kind = params["error"];
  if (typeof kind === "string" && EXPRESSION_ERRORS.has(kind)) detail.error = kind as ExpressionErrorKind;
  const key = authoredKey(r, params["key"]);
  if (key !== undefined) detail.key = key;
  if (typeof params["index"] === "number") detail.index = params["index"];
  if (fault.error.detail !== "") detail.text = fault.error.detail;
  return detail;
}

function failedCallDetail(state: RequestState, fault: FaultRecord, options: StuckOptions): StuckDetail {
  const detail: StuckDetail = { fault: "call-failed" };
  const code = fault.error.params["code"];
  if (typeof code === "string") detail.failureCode = code;
  const attempts = options.attempts?.(fault.element);
  if (attempts !== undefined) detail.attempts = attempts;
  const call = [...state.waits].reverse().find((w) => w.id.element === fault.element && w.outcome === "failed");
  const message = call?.data?.["message"];
  if (typeof message === "string" && message !== "") detail.outsideText = message;
  return detail;
}

/** The open task nobody can answer, located at its "Who is asked". */
function nobodyLocation(r: Reading, state: RequestState): Location | undefined {
  for (const active of state.activeStages) {
    const stage = r.def.root.stages.find((s) => s.id === active.stage);
    for (const w of stage?.waits ?? []) {
      const instance = currentWait(state, `${active.stage}.${w.id}`, active.activation, "");
      if (instance?.status !== "open" || instance.kind !== "person" || instance.role !== "obligation") continue;
      if (!nobodyToAsk(r.def, state, instance)) continue;
      const rule = r.def.nobodyToAsk?.find((x) => x.wait === instance.id.element);
      const task = r.taskOf(instance.id.element);
      const fallback: Location | undefined = task === undefined ? undefined : { item: task, part: "whoIsAsked" };
      return (rule === undefined ? undefined : r.origin(`nobody:${rule.id}`)) ?? fallback;
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}

/** The request's stuck state now, or null. `admin` is always filled; a reader drops it for others. */
export function stuckNow(r: Reading, state: RequestState, options: StuckOptions = {}): StuckNow | null {
  const s = stuckStateOf(r.def, state);
  if (s === null) return null;
  switch (s.reason) {
    case "action-failed": {
      const fault = state.faults.find((f) => f.error.code === "call-failed");
      if (fault === undefined) return { reason: "action-failed" };
      // A directory read step's read is located at the part that named the group.
      const location = r.originOf(`wait:${fault.element}`, "/args/groups") ?? r.locate(fault.element, fault.error.field);
      const out: StuckNow = { reason: "action-failed", admin: failedCallDetail(state, fault, options) };
      return location === undefined ? out : { ...out, location };
    }
    case "error": {
      const fault = state.faults[0];
      if (fault === undefined) return { reason: "error" };
      const location = r.locate(fault.element, fault.error.field);
      const out: StuckNow = { reason: "error", admin: errorDetail(r, fault) };
      return location === undefined ? out : { ...out, location };
    }
    case "nothing-fits": {
      // Compile's unfinished parts name the engine stage a request that gets there is stuck in.
      const unfinished = s.stage === null ? undefined : options.unfinished?.find((u) => u.stage === s.stage);
      if (unfinished !== undefined) return { reason: "unfinished", location: unfinished.location };
      const stage = r.authoredStage(s.stage);
      return stage === undefined ? { reason: "nothing-fits" } : { reason: "nothing-fits", location: { item: stage, part: "arrows" } };
    }
    case "nobody-to-ask": {
      const location = nobodyLocation(r, state);
      return location === undefined ? { reason: "nobody-to-ask" } : { reason: "nobody-to-ask", location };
    }
  }
}

/** Two stuck states are the same when reason and location are. */
export function sameStuck(a: Pick<Stuck, "reason" | "location"> | null, b: Pick<Stuck, "reason" | "location"> | null): boolean {
  if (a === null || b === null) return a === b;
  return a.reason === b.reason && a.location?.item === b.location?.item && a.location?.part === b.location?.part;
}

/** The view a reader gives: `admin` only for the people who look after stuck requests. */
export function forViewer(stuck: Stuck, isAdmin: boolean): Stuck {
  if (isAdmin || stuck.admin === undefined) return stuck;
  const out: Stuck = { ...stuck };
  delete out.admin;
  return out;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/authored/view/tasks.ts\n===
/**
 * Open tasks and open actions as people see them (core-api.md section 8), with each button's state for one
 * viewer: the viewer-level refusals in the order the engine checks them (wait-not-open,
 * membership-unavailable, not-assignee, may), the first that applies. Answers are not looked at here;
 * that is `formState`'s job, and the act checks everything again.
 */
import type { PersonWaitOpened } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { evaluateBool } from "../../kernel/decide/expressions.ts";
import { splitElement } from "../../kernel/decide/definition.ts";
import type { RequestState, WaitInstance } from "../../kernel/state.ts";
import type { ButtonId } from "../contract/authored-format.ts";
import type { Ref } from "../evaluate/types.ts";
import { callRef, taskInstanceId, timestamp } from "./ids.ts";
import type { Reading } from "./reading.ts";
import type { ButtonState, CallRef, OpenAction, OpenTask, Refusal, RequestId } from "./types.ts";

/** Who looks at the request. */
export interface Viewer {
  as?: Ref;
  /** Sees the admin fields; may close, and retry where Retry is offered. */
  isAdmin: boolean;
  /** The groups a user is in now; absent: the directory could not be asked. */
  groupsOf?: (user: string) => readonly string[] | undefined;
}

function viewerRefusal(r: Reading, state: RequestState, w: WaitInstance, as: Ref, viewer: Viewer): Refusal | undefined {
  const task = r.taskOf(w.id.element);
  const at = (part: string) => (task === undefined ? {} : { location: { item: task, part } });
  if (w.status !== "open" || state.closed !== null) {
    // A completed wait says who completed it, also after the request closed (E-27).
    if (w.status === "completed") {
      const params: Extract<Refusal, { code: "wait-not-open" }>["params"] = { state: "completed" };
      if (w.by !== null) params.by = { type: w.by.type as "user" | "connection" | "system", id: w.by.id };
      if (w.outcome !== "") params.button = w.outcome as ButtonId;
      return { code: "wait-not-open", params };
    }
    return { code: "wait-not-open", params: { state: state.closed !== null ? "requestClosed" : w.status === "skipped" ? "skipped" : "cancelled" } };
  }
  const opened = w.opened as PersonWaitOpened;
  const asksGroup = opened.assignees.some((a) => a.type === "group");
  let member = false;
  if (asksGroup && as.type === "user") {
    const groups = viewer.groupsOf?.(as.id);
    if (groups === undefined) return { code: "membership-unavailable", params: {} };
    member = opened.assignees.some((a) => a.type === "group" && groups.includes(a.id));
  }
  const direct = as.type === "user" && opened.assignees.some((a) => a.type === "user" && a.id === as.id);
  if (!direct && !member) return { code: "not-assignee", params: {}, ...at("whoIsAsked") };
  const wait = r.waitDef(w.id.element);
  if (wait?.kind !== "person") return undefined;
  const may = evaluateBool(r.def, state, { kind: "actor", stage: splitElement(w.id.element).stage }, wait.may, { actor: { type: as.type, id: as.id } });
  if (may.kind === "error") return { code: "rule-error", params: { error: may.failure.error }, ...at("requesterCanAnswer") };
  if (!may.value) return { code: "may", params: {}, ...at("requesterCanAnswer") };
  return undefined;
}

export function buttonStates(r: Reading, state: RequestState, w: WaitInstance, viewer: Viewer | undefined): ButtonState[] {
  const as = viewer?.as;
  if (as === undefined || viewer === undefined) return [];
  const refusal = viewerRefusal(r, state, w, as, viewer);
  return (w.opened as PersonWaitOpened).outcomes.map((o) => ({ button: o.id as ButtonId, available: refusal === undefined, refusals: refusal === undefined ? [] : [refusal] }));
}

/** Recorded references as the contract's `Ref`: users and groups only. */
export function asRefs(list: readonly { type: string; id: string }[]): Ref[] {
  return list.flatMap((a): Ref[] => (a.type === "user" ? [{ type: "user", id: a.id }] : a.type === "group" ? [{ type: "group", id: a.id }] : []));
}

export function openTask(r: Reading, requestId: RequestId, state: RequestState, w: WaitInstance, viewer: Viewer | undefined): OpenTask {
  const task = r.taskOf(w.id.element) ?? "";
  const askedOf = asRefs((w.opened as PersonWaitOpened).assignees);
  return { requestId, task: taskInstanceId(w.openedSeq), location: { item: task }, askedOf, openedAt: timestamp(w.openedAt), buttonStates: buttonStates(r, state, w, viewer) };
}

/** The open person waits of a request, in open order. */
export function openTasks(r: Reading, requestId: RequestId, state: RequestState, viewer: Viewer | undefined): OpenTask[] {
  if (state.closed !== null) return [];
  return state.waits.filter((w) => w.status === "open" && w.kind === "person").map((w) => openTask(r, requestId, state, w, viewer));
}

/** The open calls of authored actions; a read the compiler added is not an action. */
export function openActions(r: Reading, requestId: RequestId, state: RequestState, withCalls: boolean): OpenAction[] {
  if (state.closed !== null) return [];
  return state.waits.flatMap((w): OpenAction[] => {
    if (w.status !== "open" || w.kind !== "call") return [];
    const action = r.actionOf(w.id.element);
    const opened = w.opened;
    if (action === undefined || opened.kind !== "call") return [];
    const out: OpenAction = { location: { item: action }, sort: r.sortOf(opened.connection, opened.op), openedAt: timestamp(w.openedAt) };
    if (withCalls) out.call = callRef(requestId, w.openedSeq) satisfies CallRef;
    return [out];
  });
}

/**
 * The engine-owned CEL environment (profile cel-1, decision E-18).
 *
 * This is the only module that imports the CEL library. It wraps it behind a small interface:
 * - `check`: parse and type-check against declared variable types; problems carry a source range.
 * - `evaluate`: a value, absent (`optional.none()`), or an error.
 * - `reads`: each request-rooted path the expression selected, with the value at its end or absent
 *   (`reads.ts`). Constants are not recorded.
 *
 * How it works:
 * - Two library environments. The check environment declares every variable with its type, so a typo
 *   or a type mix is a check problem. The evaluation environment declares every variable `dyn`; the
 *   values are typed by `jsonToCel` instead, as Maps. The typed environment cannot evaluate them: it
 *   checks each value against its registered object types, so two equal references compare unequal and an
 *   index into an empty list fails with the wrong error.
 * - Library functions that do not meet cel-1 (`matches`, `timestamp`, `int`, `lowerAscii`, `upperAscii`,
 *   `getDayOfYear`) cannot be re-registered: the library refuses an overlapping overload. The wrapper
 *   renames each call in the source to an engine function (`cel1_*`) before handing it to the library,
 *   and maps ranges and names back. Authored source may not use the `cel1_` prefix.
 * - What the library registers and cel-1 refuses (definition-format.md section 5.3, "Refused") is refused
 *   at check: a time-zone argument, `bytes.json()`, a literal pattern with `\p` or `\P`, and
 *   `duration + timestamp`. The last is also refused at run time, where a `dyn` operand can hide it.
 * - An empty list literal that a comprehension ranges over is passed to the library as `dyn([])`,
 *   because the library fails to type-check `[].all(x, x > 0)`.
 * - Evaluation errors are reported as the contract's ExpressionErrorKind plus a specific `detail`, with the
 *   missing key or list position as fields. A timestamp outside the years 0001 to 9999 cannot leave an
 *   expression (`invalid-timestamp`).
 */
import { Environment, EvaluationError, Optional, type ASTNode, type TypeDeclaration } from "@marcbachmann/cel-js";
import { Duration, UnsignedInt } from "@marcbachmann/cel-js/evaluator";
import {
  CelFunctionFailure,
  daysToSeconds,
  intFromDouble,
  intFromString,
  intFromTimestamp,
  intFromUint,
  inTimestampRange,
  lowerAscii,
  parseDate,
  parseRfc3339,
  re2Matches,
  timestampFromSeconds,
  upperAscii,
  usesUnicodeClass,
  utcDateString,
  utcDayOfYear,
} from "./functions.ts";
import { ContextTypeError, jsonToCel } from "./json.ts";
import { deriveReadChains, resolveReads, type ReadChain } from "./reads.ts";
import {
  REQUEST_ROOTED_VARIABLES,
  type CelDeclarations,
  type CelNode,
  type CelProblem,
  type CelResult,
  type CelType,
  type ExpressionErrorKind,
  type JsonValue,
  type CelRead,
  type SourceRange,
} from "./types.ts";

/** The pinned library. A change is a new CEL profile and a new definition format (spec section 7). */
export const CEL_LIBRARY = { name: "@marcbachmann/cel-js", version: "8.0.0" } as const;
export const CEL_PROFILE = "cel-1";

/** Library options, written out so that no behaviour depends on a library default. */
export const CEL_LIBRARY_OPTIONS = {
  enableOptionalTypes: true,
  // A call argument such as `{'template': 'ticket', 'fields': data.form}` mixes value types.
  homogeneousAggregateLiterals: false,
  unlistedVariablesAreDyn: false,
  limits: { maxAstNodes: 100000, maxDepth: 250, maxListElements: 1000, maxMapEntries: 1000, maxCallArguments: 32 },
} as const;

const INTERNAL_PREFIX = "cel1_";
const TS = "google.protobuf.Timestamp";
const GPD = "google.protobuf.Duration";

/** Global calls renamed to an engine function. */
const RENAMED_GLOBALS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { timestamp: "cel1_timestamp", int: "cel1_int" };
/** Receiver calls renamed to an engine function. */
const RENAMED_METHODS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  matches: "cel1_matches",
  lowerAscii: "cel1_lowerAscii",
  upperAscii: "cel1_upperAscii",
  // The library counts the day of the year in the host's time zone (definition-format.md section 5.3).
  getDayOfYear: "cel1_getDayOfYear",
};
/** Receiver calls the library registers and cel-1 refuses: `bytes.json()` reads untyped JSON numbers. */
const REFUSED_METHODS = new Set(["json"]);
const COMPREHENSIONS = new Set(["all", "exists", "exists_one", "map", "filter"]);
const TIME_ZONE_METHODS = new Set([
  "getDate",
  "getDayOfMonth",
  "getDayOfWeek",
  "getDayOfYear",
  "getFullYear",
  "getHours",
  "getMilliseconds",
  "getMinutes",
  "getMonth",
  "getSeconds",
]);

export interface CheckedExpression {
  readonly source: string;
  /** The result type as the library names it (`bool`, `string`, `optional<string>`, `map<string, dyn>`). */
  readonly type: string;
  readonly tree: CelNode;
  readonly readChains: readonly ReadChain[];
}

export type CheckResult = { ok: true; expression: CheckedExpression } | { ok: false; problems: CelProblem[] };

export interface CelEnvironment {
  check(source: string): CheckResult;
  evaluate(expression: CheckedExpression, context: Readonly<Record<string, JsonValue>>): CelResult;
  reads(expression: CheckedExpression, context: Readonly<Record<string, JsonValue>>): CelRead[];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- source rewriting

interface Rename {
  oldStart: number;
  oldName: string;
  newName: string;
}

class SourceMap {
  // Each entry: where the rename starts in the new and old source, and the length change.
  private readonly entries: { newStart: number; oldStart: number; oldLen: number; newLen: number }[] = [];
  constructor(renames: readonly Rename[]) {
    let shift = 0;
    for (const r of renames) {
      this.entries.push({ newStart: r.oldStart + shift, oldStart: r.oldStart, oldLen: r.oldName.length, newLen: r.newName.length });
      shift += r.newName.length - r.oldName.length;
    }
  }
  toOld(pos: number): number {
    let shift = 0;
    for (const e of this.entries) {
      if (pos < e.newStart) break;
      if (pos < e.newStart + e.newLen) return e.oldStart + Math.min(pos - e.newStart, e.oldLen);
      shift += e.newLen - e.oldLen;
    }
    return pos - shift;
  }
  range(r: SourceRange): SourceRange {
    return { start: this.toOld(r.start), end: this.toOld(r.end) };
  }
}

function applyRenames(source: string, renames: readonly Rename[]): string {
  let out = "";
  let at = 0;
  for (const r of renames) {
    out += source.slice(at, r.oldStart) + r.newName;
    at = r.oldStart + r.oldName.length;
  }
  return out + source.slice(at);
}

function publicNames(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(/cel1_(\w+)/g, "$1");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- library AST to the engine's tree

function rangeOf(n: ASTNode): SourceRange {
  return { start: n.range?.start ?? n.start, end: n.range?.end ?? n.end };
}

function toTree(n: ASTNode): CelNode {
  const range = rangeOf(n);
  switch (n.op) {
    case "value": {
      const v: unknown = n.args;
      if (v instanceof UnsignedInt) return { op: "literal", value: v.valueOf(), range };
      return { op: "literal", value: v as string | number | bigint | boolean | null | Uint8Array, range };
    }
    case "id":
      return { op: "ident", name: n.args, range };
    case ".":
    case ".?":
      return { op: "select", optional: n.op === ".?", operand: toTree(n.args[0]), field: n.args[1], range };
    case "[]":
    case "[?]":
      return { op: "index", optional: n.op === "[?]", operand: toTree(n.args[0]), index: toTree(n.args[1]), range };
    case "call":
      return { op: "call", name: n.args[0], target: null, args: n.args[1].map(toTree), range };
    case "rcall":
      return { op: "call", name: n.args[0], target: toTree(n.args[1]), args: n.args[2].map(toTree), range };
    case "list":
      return { op: "list", elements: n.args.map(toTree), range };
    case "map":
      return { op: "map", entries: n.args.map(([k, v]) => [toTree(k), toTree(v)] as [CelNode, CelNode]), range };
    case "!_":
    case "-_":
      return { op: "operator", operator: n.op, args: [toTree(n.args)], range };
    case "?:":
      return { op: "operator", operator: n.op, args: n.args.map(toTree), range };
    case "||":
    case "&&":
    case "!=":
    case "==":
    case "in":
    case "+":
    case "-":
    case "*":
    case "/":
    case "%":
    case "<":
    case "<=":
    case ">":
    case ">=":
      return { op: "operator", operator: n.op, args: n.args.map(toTree), range };
    default: {
      const op: string = (n as { op: string }).op;
      throw new LibraryShapeError(`unknown AST operator '${op}'`);
    }
  }
}

class LibraryShapeError extends Error {}

/** Finds renames and cel-1 violations in the authored tree. */
function scanTree(source: string, tree: CelNode): { renames: Rename[]; problems: CelProblem[] } {
  const renames: Rename[] = [];
  const problems: CelProblem[] = [];
  const nameAt = (name: string, from: number, before: number): number => {
    const at = source.indexOf(name, from);
    return at >= 0 && at < before ? at : -1;
  };
  const visit = (n: CelNode): void => {
    switch (n.op) {
      case "literal":
        return;
      case "ident":
        if (n.name.startsWith(INTERNAL_PREFIX)) {
          problems.push({ code: "unknown-variable", message: `unknown variable '${n.name}'`, range: n.range });
        }
        return;
      case "select":
        visit(n.operand);
        return;
      case "index":
        visit(n.operand);
        visit(n.index);
        return;
      case "list":
        n.elements.forEach(visit);
        return;
      case "map":
        n.entries.forEach(([k, v]) => {
          visit(k);
          visit(v);
        });
        return;
      case "operator":
        n.args.forEach(visit);
        return;
      case "call": {
        if (n.name.startsWith(INTERNAL_PREFIX)) {
          problems.push({ code: "unknown-function", message: `unknown function '${n.name}'`, range: n.range });
        }
        const replacement = n.target ? RENAMED_METHODS[n.name] : RENAMED_GLOBALS[n.name];
        if (n.target && TIME_ZONE_METHODS.has(n.name) && n.args.length === 1) {
          problems.push({ code: "time-zone-not-allowed", message: `${n.name}() with a time zone: cel-1 is UTC only`, range: n.range });
        }
        if (n.target && REFUSED_METHODS.has(n.name)) {
          problems.push({ code: "unknown-function", message: `unknown function '${n.name}': not in cel-1`, range: n.range });
        }
        const pattern = n.args[0];
        if (n.target && n.name === "matches" && pattern?.op === "literal" && typeof pattern.value === "string" && usesUnicodeClass(pattern.value)) {
          // E-20: Unicode tables differ between JavaScript engines.
          problems.push({ code: "unicode-class-not-allowed", message: "a pattern may not use \\p or \\P in cel-1", range: pattern.range });
        }
        // Library 8.0.0 fails with a plain Error when it type-checks some comprehensions over an
        // empty list literal ("[].all(x, x > 0)"). An empty list is typed dyn there instead.
        if (n.target?.op === "list" && n.target.elements.length === 0 && COMPREHENSIONS.has(n.name)) {
          const { start, end } = n.target.range;
          if (source.slice(start, end).replace(/\s/g, "") !== "[]") throw new LibraryShapeError("unexpected list range");
          renames.push({ oldStart: start, oldName: source.slice(start, end), newName: "dyn([])" });
        }
        if (replacement) {
          const from = n.target ? n.target.range.end : n.range.start;
          const before = n.args[0]?.range.start ?? n.range.end;
          const at = nameAt(n.name, from, before);
          if (at < 0) throw new LibraryShapeError(`cannot locate '${n.name}' in the source`);
          renames.push({ oldStart: at, oldName: n.name, newName: replacement });
        }
        if (n.target) visit(n.target);
        n.args.forEach(visit);
        return;
      }
    }
  };
  visit(tree);
  renames.sort((a, b) => a.oldStart - b.oldStart);
  return { renames, problems };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- types

function deepEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (a === b) return true;
  if (a instanceof Map && b instanceof Map) {
    if (a.size !== b.size) return false;
    for (const [k, v] of a) if (!b.has(k) || !deepEqual(v, b.get(k))) return false;
    return true;
  }
  if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) return a.length === b.length && a.every((v, i) => deepEqual(v, b[i]));
  return false;
}

/** Registers object types in the check environment, one library message type per distinct shape. */
class TypeRegistry {
  private readonly names = new Map<string, string>();
  private readonly used = new Set<string>();
  private readonly env: Environment;
  constructor(env: Environment) {
    this.env = env;
  }

  typeString(type: CelType, hint: string): string {
    switch (type.kind) {
      case "string":
      case "int":
      case "double":
      case "bool":
      case "dyn":
        return type.kind;
      case "list":
        return `list<${this.typeString(type.element, `${hint}_item`)}>`;
      case "map":
        return `map<string, ${this.typeString(type.value, `${hint}_value`)}>`;
      case "object": {
        const fields: Record<string, string> = {};
        for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(type.fields)) fields[k] = this.typeString(v, `${hint}_${k}`);
        const shape = JSON.stringify(Object.entries(fields).sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)));
        const known = this.names.get(shape);
        if (known) return known;
        let name = `Obj_${hint.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_]/g, "_")}`;
        for (let i = 2; this.used.has(name); i++) name = `Obj_${hint}_${i}`;
        this.used.add(name);
        this.names.set(shape, name);
        this.env.registerType(name, { fields });
        // The library has no equality for message types; cel-1 compares objects by value.
        this.env.registerOperator(`${name} == ${name}`, (x: unknown, y: unknown) => deepEqual(x, y));
        return name;
      }
    }
  }
}

function registerEngineFunctions(env: Environment): void {
  const wrap =
    <A extends unknown[], R>(fn: (...args: A) => R) =>
    (...args: A): R => {
      try {
        return fn(...args);
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof CelFunctionFailure) throw new EvaluationError({ code: error.code, message: error.message });
        throw error;
      }
    };
  env
    .registerFunction("string.cel1_matches(string): bool", wrap((s: string, p: string) => re2Matches(s, p)))
    .registerFunction("string.cel1_lowerAscii(): string", wrap((s: string) => lowerAscii(s)))
    .registerFunction("string.cel1_upperAscii(): string", wrap((s: string) => upperAscii(s)))
    .registerFunction(`cel1_timestamp(string): ${TS}`, wrap((s: string) => parseRfc3339(s)))
    .registerFunction(`cel1_timestamp(int): ${TS}`, wrap((i: bigint) => timestampFromSeconds(i)))
    .registerFunction(`cel1_timestamp(${TS}): ${TS}`, (d: Date) => d)
    .registerFunction(`date(string): ${TS}`, wrap((s: string) => parseDate(s)))
    .registerFunction(`days(int): ${GPD}`, wrap((n: bigint) => new Duration(daysToSeconds(n), 0)))
    .registerFunction(`asDate(${TS}): string`, wrap((d: Date) => utcDateString(d)))
    .registerFunction(`${TS}.cel1_getDayOfYear(): int`, (d: Date) => utcDayOfYear(d))
    .registerFunction("cel1_int(int): int", (i: bigint) => i)
    .registerFunction("cel1_int(double): int", wrap((d: number) => intFromDouble(d)))
    .registerFunction("cel1_int(string): int", wrap((s: string) => intFromString(s)))
    .registerFunction("cel1_int(uint): int", wrap((u: UnsignedInt) => intFromUint(u.valueOf())))
    .registerFunction(`cel1_int(${TS}): int`, wrap((d: Date) => intFromTimestamp(d)));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- duration + timestamp

/** Calls `fn` on every node of a library AST. */
function forEachLibraryNode(n: ASTNode, fn: (n: ASTNode) => void): void {
  fn(n);
  switch (n.op) {
    case "value":
    case "id":
      return;
    case ".":
    case ".?":
      forEachLibraryNode(n.args[0], fn);
      return;
    case "call":
      n.args[1].forEach((a) => forEachLibraryNode(a, fn));
      return;
    case "rcall":
      forEachLibraryNode(n.args[1], fn);
      n.args[2].forEach((a) => forEachLibraryNode(a, fn));
      return;
    case "map":
      n.args.forEach(([k, v]) => {
        forEachLibraryNode(k, fn);
        forEachLibraryNode(v, fn);
      });
      return;
    case "!_":
    case "-_":
      forEachLibraryNode(n.args, fn);
      return;
    default:
      n.args.forEach((a) => forEachLibraryNode(a, fn));
  }
}

const DURATION_PLUS_TIMESTAMP = `no such overload: ${GPD} + ${TS} (write timestamp + duration)`;

/**
 * cel-1 refuses `duration + timestamp`: the library registers it with the result typed `duration` while
 * the value is a timestamp (definition-format.md section 5.3). At check, from the checked operand types:
 * a `dyn` left operand is refused too, because the only overload with a timestamp on the right is this one.
 */
function durationPlusTimestamp(ast: ASTNode): SourceRange | null {
  let found: SourceRange | null = null;
  forEachLibraryNode(ast, (n) => {
    if (found || n.op !== "+") return;
    const [left, right] = n.args.map((a) => (a as ASTNode & { checkedType?: TypeDeclaration }).checkedType);
    if (!left || !right || right.unwrappedType.name !== TS) return;
    if (left.kind === "dyn" || left.unwrappedType.name === GPD) found = rangeOf(n);
  });
  return found;
}

type BinaryHandle = (left: unknown, right: unknown, ast: unknown, ev: unknown) => unknown;

/**
 * The same refusal at run time, where both operands may be typed `dyn`. Wraps the handler the library
 * stored on each checked `+` node (library 8.0.0 internals; pinned with the profile).
 */
function guardDurationPlusTimestamp(ast: ASTNode): void {
  forEachLibraryNode(ast, (n) => {
    if (n.op !== "+") return;
    const node = n as ASTNode & { handle?: BinaryHandle };
    const handle = node.handle;
    if (typeof handle !== "function") throw new LibraryShapeError("a checked '+' node has no handler");
    node.handle = (left, right, a, ev) => {
      if (left instanceof Duration && right instanceof Date) {
        throw new EvaluationError({ code: "no-such-overload", message: DURATION_PLUS_TIMESTAMP, range: rangeOf(n) });
      }
      return handle(left, right, a, ev);
    };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- CEL to JSON

class NotJsonError extends Error {
  readonly code: string;
  constructor(code: string, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.code = code;
  }
}

/**
 * A CEL value as JSON. A null at any depth is an error, kind `wrong-kind`, detail `null-value`: the engine
 * never writes null (kernel spec section 2, Values), so no caller has to look for one.
 */
function celToJson(v: unknown): JsonValue {
  if (v === null) throw new NotJsonError("null-value", "an expression gave null");
  if (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "boolean") return v;
  if (typeof v === "bigint") {
    if (v > BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) || v < -BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)) {
      throw new NotJsonError("int-out-of-range", `integer ${v} is outside +/-(2^53 - 1)`);
    }
    return Number(v);
  }
  if (typeof v === "number") {
    if (!Number.isFinite(v)) throw new NotJsonError("double-not-finite", `${v} cannot be held in JSON`);
    return v;
  }
  if (v instanceof UnsignedInt) return celToJson(v.valueOf());
  if (v instanceof Date) {
    // Outside 0001 to 9999 an RFC 3339 text cannot be written (E-26).
    if (!inTimestampRange(v)) throw new NotJsonError("invalid-timestamp", "a timestamp outside years 0001 to 9999 cannot leave an expression");
    return v.toISOString();
  }
  if (v instanceof Duration) return v.toString();
  if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.map(celToJson);
  if (v instanceof Map) {
    const entries: [string, JsonValue][] = [];
    for (const [k, x] of v) {
      if (typeof k !== "string") throw new NotJsonError("not-json", "a map key that is not a string cannot be held in JSON");
      if (x !== undefined) entries.push([k, celToJson(x)]);
    }
    return Object.fromEntries(entries);
  }
  if (v instanceof Optional) throw new NotJsonError("not-json", "an optional value inside a list or map cannot be held in JSON");
  if (typeof v === "object" && v !== undefined && Object.getPrototypeOf(v) === Object.prototype) {
    return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(v as Record<string, unknown>).map(([k, x]) => [k, celToJson(x)]));
  }
  throw new NotJsonError("not-json", `a value of type ${Object.prototype.toString.call(v)} cannot be held in JSON`);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- evaluation error kinds

/** Specific causes (kebab-case) to the contract's ExpressionErrorKind. Anything not listed is "other". */
const ERROR_KINDS: Readonly<Record<string, ExpressionErrorKind>> = {
  "no-such-key": "no-such-key",
  "index-out-of-bounds": "index-out-of-range",
  "optional-value-missing": "absent-value",
  "no-matching-overload": "wrong-kind",
  "no-such-overload": "wrong-kind",
  "field-type-mismatch": "wrong-kind",
  "variable-type-mismatch": "wrong-kind",
  "list-item-type-mismatch": "wrong-kind",
  "cannot-index-type": "wrong-kind",
  "context-type-mismatch": "wrong-kind",
  "null-value": "wrong-kind",
  "division-by-zero": "division-by-zero",
  "modulo-by-zero": "division-by-zero",
  "numeric-overflow": "overflow",
  "int-out-of-range": "overflow",
  "days-out-of-range": "overflow",
  "double-not-finite": "overflow",
};

function errorKind(detail: string): ExpressionErrorKind {
  return ERROR_KINDS[detail] ?? "other";
}

function evalError(detail: string, message: string): CelResult {
  return { kind: "error", code: errorKind(detail), detail, message };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the environment

interface Compiled {
  run: (context: Record<string, unknown>) => unknown;
  map: SourceMap;
}

const compiledByExpression = new WeakMap<CheckedExpression, Compiled>();

function errorFields(error: unknown, map: SourceMap, source: string): { code: string; message: string; range: SourceRange; libraryCode?: string } {
  const e = error as { code?: unknown; summary?: unknown; message?: unknown; range?: SourceRange };
  const libraryCode = typeof e.code === "string" ? e.code : undefined;
  const summary = typeof e.summary === "string" ? e.summary : String(e.message ?? error);
  const range = e.range ? map.range(e.range) : { start: 0, end: source.length };
  const out = { code: (libraryCode ?? "library-internal-error").replace(/_/g, "-"), message: publicNames(summary), range };
  return libraryCode ? { ...out, libraryCode } : out;
}

/**
 * The missing key or list position of a library error, as fields (E-26). A field selection names its key in
 * the node; an index's key is known only at run time, so it is read from the library's message, whose form
 * is pinned with the library version.
 */
function missingPlace(error: unknown, detail: string): { key?: string; index?: number } {
  const e = error as { node?: { op?: unknown; args?: unknown }; summary?: unknown };
  const summary = typeof e.summary === "string" ? e.summary : "";
  if (detail === "no-such-key") {
    const node = e.node;
    if ((node?.op === "." || node?.op === ".?") && Array.isArray(node.args) && typeof node.args[1] === "string") return { key: node.args[1] };
    const m = /^No such key: ([\s\S]*)$/.exec(summary);
    return m?.[1] === undefined ? {} : { key: m[1] };
  }
  if (detail === "index-out-of-bounds") {
    const m = /index (-?\d+)/.exec(summary);
    return m?.[1] === undefined ? {} : { index: Number(m[1]) };
  }
  return {};
}

export function createCelEnvironment(declarations: CelDeclarations): CelEnvironment {
  const checkEnv = new Environment(CEL_LIBRARY_OPTIONS);
  const evalEnv = new Environment(CEL_LIBRARY_OPTIONS);
  registerEngineFunctions(checkEnv);
  registerEngineFunctions(evalEnv);

  const types = new TypeRegistry(checkEnv);
  const declared = new Map<string, CelType>();
  for (const [name, type] of Object.entries(declarations.variables)) declared.set(name, type);
  const constants = declarations.constants ?? {};
  const constantCel: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [name, c] of Object.entries(constants)) {
    if (declared.has(name)) throw new Error(`'${name}' is declared as both a variable and a constant`);
    constantCel[name] = jsonToCel(c.value, c.type, [name]);
  }
  // Constants are declared as typed variables: the library types an index into a registered constant as dyn.
  for (const [name, type] of [...declared, ...Object.entries(constants).map(([n, c]) => [n, c.type] as const)]) {
    checkEnv.registerVariable(name, types.typeString(type, name));
    evalEnv.registerVariable(name, "dyn");
  }
  // Only request-rooted paths are reads; constants are in the definition (kernel spec section 5, E-20).
  const requestRooted = declarations.requestRooted ?? REQUEST_ROOTED_VARIABLES.filter((n) => declared.has(n));
  for (const name of requestRooted) {
    if (!declared.has(name)) throw new Error(`'${name}' is marked request-rooted but is not a declared variable`);
  }
  const roots = new Set<string>(requestRooted);

  function check(source: string): CheckResult {
    const whole: SourceRange = { start: 0, end: source.length };
    let tree: CelNode;
    try {
      tree = toTree(checkEnv.parse(source).ast);
    } catch (error) {
      return { ok: false, problems: [errorFields(error, new SourceMap([]), source)] };
    }
    let renames: Rename[];
    let problems: CelProblem[];
    try {
      ({ renames, problems } = scanTree(source, tree));
    } catch (error) {
      return { ok: false, problems: [{ code: "library-internal-error", message: String(error), range: whole }] };
    }
    if (problems.length > 0) return { ok: false, problems };

    const rewritten = applyRenames(source, renames);
    const map = new SourceMap(renames);
    let type: string;
    let run: Compiled["run"];
    try {
      const typed = checkEnv.parse(rewritten);
      const checked = typed.check();
      if (!checked.valid) return { ok: false, problems: [errorFields(checked.error, map, source)] };
      const refused = durationPlusTimestamp(typed.ast);
      if (refused) return { ok: false, problems: [{ code: "no-such-overload", message: DURATION_PLUS_TIMESTAMP, range: map.range(refused) }] };
      type = publicNames(checked.type ?? "dyn");
      const parsed = evalEnv.parse(rewritten);
      const dynCheck = parsed.check();
      if (!dynCheck.valid) return { ok: false, problems: [errorFields(dynCheck.error, map, source)] };
      guardDurationPlusTimestamp(parsed.ast);
      run = parsed;
    } catch (error) {
      return { ok: false, problems: [errorFields(error, map, source)] };
    }
    const expression: CheckedExpression = Object.freeze({ source, type, tree, readChains: deriveReadChains(tree, roots) });
    compiledByExpression.set(expression, { run, map });
    return { ok: true, expression };
  }

  function evaluate(expression: CheckedExpression, context: Readonly<Record<string, JsonValue>>): CelResult {
    const compiled = compiledByExpression.get(expression);
    if (!compiled) return evalError("not-checked", "the expression was not checked by this module");
    const celContext: Record<string, unknown> = { ...constantCel };
    try {
      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(context)) {
        const type = declared.get(name);
        if (type) celContext[name] = jsonToCel(value, type, [name]);
      }
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof ContextTypeError) return evalError(error.code, error.message);
      throw error;
    }
    try {
      const result = compiled.run(celContext);
      if (result instanceof Promise) {
        result.catch(() => undefined);
        return evalError("async-not-allowed", "an expression returned a Promise");
      }
      if (result instanceof Optional) {
        return result.hasValue() ? { kind: "value", value: celToJson(result.value()) } : { kind: "absent" };
      }
      return { kind: "value", value: celToJson(result) };
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof NotJsonError) return evalError(error.code, error.message);
      const f = errorFields(error, compiled.map, expression.source);
      const out: CelResult = { kind: "error", code: errorKind(f.code), detail: f.code, message: f.message, range: f.range, ...missingPlace(error, f.code) };
      return f.libraryCode ? { ...out, libraryCode: f.libraryCode } : out;
    }
  }

  function reads(expression: CheckedExpression, context: Readonly<Record<string, JsonValue>>): CelRead[] {
    return resolveReads(expression.readChains, context);
  }

  return { check, evaluate, reads };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the function inventory

/** A library overload the wrapper hides (renamed, refused) cannot be called from authored source. */
function reachable(f: { name: string; receiverType: string | null; params: readonly unknown[] }): boolean {
  if (f.name.startsWith(INTERNAL_PREFIX)) return true;
  if (f.receiverType === null) return RENAMED_GLOBALS[f.name] === undefined;
  if (RENAMED_METHODS[f.name] !== undefined || REFUSED_METHODS.has(f.name)) return false;
  return !(f.receiverType === TS && TIME_ZONE_METHODS.has(f.name) && f.params.length === 1);
}

/**
 * Every function and macro overload an authored expression can call, as signatures with public names
 * (`string.contains(string): bool`, `int(double): int`), sorted. Read from the library's registry, so a
 * library change shows here; the inventory test pins it (E-23).
 */
export function celFunctionSignatures(): string[] {
  const env = new Environment(CEL_LIBRARY_OPTIONS);
  registerEngineFunctions(env);
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const f of env.getDefinitions().functions) if (reachable(f)) out.add(publicNames(f.signature));
  return [...out].sort();
}

 * differ, that file decides (E-23). Offered: what an authored value can reach. Accepted but not offered:
 * bytes and unsigned integers and their functions, `null`, `type()`.

 * function the environment accepts against this list, so the two cannot disagree. Pure data.

/** contract/core-api.md section 6.4. A `ValueKind` is as the value's JSON reads in CEL. */
export type FormulaType =
  | ValueKind
  | "int"
  | "timestamp" | "duration" | "map" | "any"
  | `listOf:${string}` | `optionalOf:${string}`;

export interface FormulaFunction {
  name: string;
  style: "function" | "method" | "macro" | "operator";
  overloads: { receiver?: FormulaType; args: FormulaType[]; returns: FormulaType }[];
}

/** A `FormulaFunction` with its one-line meaning, for the frontend's writers (not screen text). */

  meaning: string;
}

/**
 * The engine's replacements for library functions that do not meet the cel-1 profile,
 * and the added `date()`, `days()` and `asDate()`. Pure functions; `environment.ts` registers them with the library.
 */
import { RE2JS } from "@bufbuild/re2";

/** A function failed. `environment.ts` turns it into a CEL evaluation error. */
export class CelFunctionFailure extends Error {
  readonly code: string;
  constructor(code: string, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "CelFunctionFailure";
    this.code = code;
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- regular expressions (RE2)

const patternCache = new Map<string, RE2JS>();
const PATTERN_CACHE_LIMIT = 256;

/** Compiles an RE2 pattern, or throws `invalid-regular-expression`. */
export function compileRe2(pattern: string): RE2JS {
  const cached = patternCache.get(pattern);
  if (cached) return cached;
  let compiled: RE2JS;
  try {
    compiled = RE2JS.compile(pattern);
  } catch (error) {
    const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("invalid-regular-expression", `invalid RE2 pattern: ${detail}`);
  }
  if (patternCache.size >= PATTERN_CACHE_LIMIT) patternCache.clear();
  patternCache.set(pattern, compiled);
  return compiled;
}

/**
 * True if an RE2 pattern uses a Unicode class (`\p` or `\P`). cel-1 refuses them because Unicode
 * tables differ between JavaScript engines (E-20). Text quoted by `\Q...\E` is literal and skipped.
 */
export function usesUnicodeClass(pattern: string): boolean {
  for (let i = 0; i < pattern.length; i++) {
    if (pattern[i] !== "\\") continue;
    const next = pattern[i + 1];
    if (next === "p" || next === "P") return true;
    if (next === "Q") {
      const end = pattern.indexOf("\\E", i + 2);
      if (end < 0) return false;
      i = end + 1;
      continue;
    }
    i++;
  }
  return false;
}

/** CEL `string.matches(string)`: true if the RE2 pattern matches any substring. */
export function re2Matches(input: string, pattern: string): boolean {
  if (usesUnicodeClass(pattern)) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("unicode-class-not-allowed", `pattern uses \\p or \\P, which cel-1 refuses: '${pattern}'`);
  }
  return compileRe2(pattern).test(input);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- time

const MIN_EPOCH_MS = utcMs(1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0); // 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z
const MAX_EPOCH_MS = utcMs(9999, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, 999); // 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z

function utcMs(year: number, month: number, day: number, h: number, m: number, s: number, ms: number): number {
  const d = new Date(0);
  d.setUTCFullYear(year, month - 1, day); // setUTCFullYear does not map years 0-99 to 1900-1999
  d.setUTCHours(h, m, s, ms);
  return d.getTime();
}

function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
  if (month === 2) return (year % 4 === 0 && year % 100 !== 0) || year % 400 === 0 ? 29 : 28;
  return [4, 6, 9, 11].includes(month) ? 30 : 31;
}

const RFC3339 = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[Tt](\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:\.(\d{1,9}))?(?:([Zz])|([+-])(\d{2}):(\d{2}))$/;
const FULL_DATE = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/;

function validDate(year: number, month: number, day: number): boolean {
  return year >= 1 && month >= 1 && month <= 12 && day >= 1 && day <= daysInMonth(year, month);
}

/**
 * CEL `timestamp(string)` under cel-1: RFC 3339 `date-time` only, with a mandatory offset.
 * Fractions beyond milliseconds are truncated (the library keeps timestamps as JS `Date`).
 * Leap seconds (`:60`) are rejected.
 */
export function parseRfc3339(text: string): Date {
  const m = RFC3339.exec(text);
  const fail = (): never => {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("invalid-timestamp", `timestamp() requires an RFC 3339 date-time, got '${text}'`);
  };
  if (!m) return fail();
  const year = Number(m[1]);
  const month = Number(m[2]);
  const day = Number(m[3]);
  const hour = Number(m[4]);
  const minute = Number(m[5]);
  const second = Number(m[6]);
  if (!validDate(year, month, day) || hour > 23 || minute > 59 || second > 59) return fail();
  const millis = m[7] === undefined ? 0 : Number(m[7].padEnd(9, "0").slice(0, 3));
  let offsetMinutes = 0;
  if (m[8] === undefined) {
    const oh = Number(m[10]);
    const om = Number(m[11]);
    if (oh > 23 || om > 59) return fail();
    offsetMinutes = (m[9] === "-" ? -1 : 1) * (oh * 60 + om);
  }
  const ms = utcMs(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millis) - offsetMinutes * 60_000;
  if (ms < MIN_EPOCH_MS || ms > MAX_EPOCH_MS) return fail();
  return new Date(ms);
}

/** cel-1 `date(string)`: a `YYYY-MM-DD` string read as 00:00 UTC. Anything else, or a date that does not exist, is an error. */
export function parseDate(text: string): Date {
  const m = FULL_DATE.exec(text);
  if (!m || !validDate(Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]), Number(m[3]))) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("invalid-date", `date() requires a YYYY-MM-DD date, got '${text}'`);
  }
  return new Date(utcMs(Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]), Number(m[3]), 0, 0, 0, 0));
}

/** CEL `timestamp(int)`: Unix seconds. */
export function timestampFromSeconds(seconds: bigint): Date {
  const ms = Number(seconds) * 1000;
  if (!Number.isFinite(ms) || ms < MIN_EPOCH_MS || ms > MAX_EPOCH_MS) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("invalid-timestamp", "timestamp() argument out of range");
  }
  return new Date(ms);
}

/** Whether a timestamp lies within the years 0001 to 9999, the only ones that may leave an expression (E-26). */
export function inTimestampRange(value: Date): boolean {
  const ms = value.getTime();
  return Number.isFinite(ms) && ms >= MIN_EPOCH_MS && ms <= MAX_EPOCH_MS;
}

/** cel-1 `asDate(timestamp)`: the UTC date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (E-23). Years outside 0001 to 9999 are an error. */
export function utcDateString(value: Date): string {
  if (!inTimestampRange(value)) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("invalid-timestamp", "asDate() of a timestamp outside years 0001 to 9999");
  }
  const year = value.getUTCFullYear();
  const pad = (n: number, width: number): string => String(n).padStart(width, "0");
  return `${pad(year, 4)}-${pad(value.getUTCMonth() + 1, 2)}-${pad(value.getUTCDate(), 2)}`;
}

/** CEL `timestamp.getDayOfYear()` under cel-1: from 0, in UTC whatever the host's time zone. */
export function utcDayOfYear(value: Date): bigint {
  const year = value.getUTCFullYear();
  let day = value.getUTCDate() - 1;
  for (let month = 1; month <= value.getUTCMonth(); month++) day += daysInMonth(year, month);
  return BigInt(day);
}

/**
 * cel-1 `days(int)`: whole days as seconds (E-23). Beyond +/-3,650,000 days is `days-out-of-range`: kind
 * `overflow` like an integer leaving its range, but a cause of its own (E-26).
 */
export const DAYS_LIMIT = 3_650_000n;
export function daysToSeconds(days: bigint): bigint {
  if (days > DAYS_LIMIT || days < -DAYS_LIMIT) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("days-out-of-range", `days(${days}) is beyond +/-3,650,000 days`);
  }
  return days * 86_400n;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- integers

export const INT64_MIN = -(2n ** 63n);
export const INT64_MAX = 2n ** 63n - 1n;

function checkInt64(value: bigint): bigint {
  if (value < INT64_MIN || value > INT64_MAX) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("int-out-of-range", `integer out of int64 range: ${value}`);
  }
  return value;
}

/** CEL `int(double)`: truncates toward zero; NaN, infinities and values outside int64 are errors. */
export function intFromDouble(value: number): bigint {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) throw new CelFunctionFailure("int-out-of-range", `int() of ${value}`);
  // Doubles at or beyond 2^63 cannot be represented; -2^63 can.
  if (value >= 9223372036854775808 || value < -9223372036854775808) {
    throw new CelFunctionFailure("int-out-of-range", `int() of ${value} is outside int64`);
  }
  return BigInt(Math.trunc(value));
}

/** CEL `int(string)`: a decimal integer with an optional sign. */
export function intFromString(value: string): bigint {
  if (!/^[+-]?\d+$/.test(value)) throw new CelFunctionFailure("invalid-int", `int() cannot parse '${value}'`);
  return checkInt64(BigInt(value));
}

/** CEL `int(uint)`. */
export function intFromUint(value: bigint): bigint {
  return checkInt64(value);
}

/** CEL `int(timestamp)`: Unix seconds, floored. */
export function intFromTimestamp(value: Date): bigint {
  return BigInt(Math.floor(value.getTime() / 1000));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- strings

/** CEL `lowerAscii`: changes only A-Z. */
export function lowerAscii(value: string): string {
  return value.replace(/[A-Z]/g, (c) => String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0) + 32));
}

/** CEL `upperAscii`: changes only a-z. */
export function upperAscii(value: string): string {
  return value.replace(/[a-z]/g, (c) => String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0) - 32));
}
