===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/decide/waits.ts\n===
/**
 * Opening and ending waits (kernel spec section 2, Wait; event-payloads.md section 5.8).
 * - A person wait records its assignees resolved, not expanded; a reference whose type is not `user` or
 *   `group` is dropped and not recorded (E-17).
 * - A call wait records its arguments; one whose expression gave `optional.none()` is left out (L13). Its
 *   key is the explicit `idempotencyKey`, or the derived key.
 * An expression that fails while opening throws a `TurnFault` naming the wait and the field.
 */
import { isJsonObject, type CallWait, type ChildStage, type Json, type JsonObject, type PersonWait, type PublishedDefinition, type Ref, type WaitId } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { currentWait, type RequestState } from "../state.ts";
import { findStage, fullId, pointerSegment } from "./definition.ts";
import { evaluate } from "./expressions.ts";
import { expressionFault, plainFault } from "./faults.ts";
import type { TurnLog } from "./turn-log.ts";

/**
 * The derived idempotency key (spec section 2, Call): `<request ID>/<element ID>@<activation>#<seq>`, with
 * `[<key>]` after the element ID when the wait's key is not empty. Each entry of the stage acts again.
 */
export function derivedIdempotencyKey(requestId: string, wait: WaitId): string {
  return `${requestId}/${wait.element}${wait.key === "" ? "" : `[${wait.key}]`}@${wait.activation}#${wait.seq}`;
}

/** The next instance of `(element, activation, key)`: one above the current instance (spec section 2). */
function nextId(state: RequestState, element: string, activation: string): WaitId {
  const current = currentWait(state, element, activation, "");
  return { element, activation, key: "", seq: (current?.id.seq ?? 0) + 1 };
}

function isUserOrGroup(v: Json): v is { type: string; id: string } {
  return isJsonObject(v) && (v["type"] === "user" || v["type"] === "group") && typeof v["id"] === "string";
}

function openPerson(def: PublishedDefinition, log: TurnLog, stage: string, w: PersonWait, id: WaitId): void {
  const r = evaluate(def, log.state, { kind: "stage", stage }, w.assignees);
  if (r.kind === "error") throw expressionFault(id.element, "/assignees", r.failure);
  if (r.kind === "absent" || !Array.isArray(r.value)) {
    throw expressionFault(id.element, "/assignees", { error: "wrong-kind", detail: "not-a-list", message: "assignees did not give a list" });
  }
  const assignees: Ref[] = r.value.filter(isUserOrGroup).map((x) => ({ type: x.type, id: x.id }));
  log.emit("WaitOpened", {
    wait: id,
    kind: "person",
    role: w.role,
    assignees,
    outcomes: w.outcomes.map((o) => ({ id: o.id, schema: o.schema })),
  });
}

function idempotencyKey(def: PublishedDefinition, log: TurnLog, stage: string, w: CallWait, id: WaitId): string {
  if (w.idempotencyKey === null) return derivedIdempotencyKey(log.requestId, id);
  const r = evaluate(def, log.state, { kind: "stage", stage }, w.idempotencyKey);
  if (r.kind === "error") throw expressionFault(id.element, "/idempotencyKey", r.failure);
  const length = r.kind === "value" && typeof r.value === "string" ? [...r.value].length : 0;
  if (r.kind !== "value" || typeof r.value !== "string" || length < 1 || length > 255) {
    throw plainFault(id.element, "key-invalid", "/idempotencyKey");
  }
  return r.value;
}

function openCall(def: PublishedDefinition, log: TurnLog, stage: string, w: CallWait, id: WaitId): void {
  const args: JsonObject = {};
  for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(w.args)) {
    const r = evaluate(def, log.state, { kind: "stage", stage }, source);
    if (r.kind === "error") throw expressionFault(id.element, `/args/${pointerSegment(name)}`, r.failure);
    if (r.kind === "value") args[name] = r.value;
  }
  const key = idempotencyKey(def, log, stage, w, id);
  log.emit("WaitOpened", { wait: id, kind: "call", role: null, connection: w.connection, op: w.op, effect: w.effect, args, idempotencyKey: key });
}

/** Opens every wait of a stage just entered, in declared order (spec section 3, event order). */
export function openStageWaits(def: PublishedDefinition, log: TurnLog, stage: ChildStage, activation: string): void {
  for (const w of stage.waits) {
    const id = nextId(log.state, fullId(stage.id, w.id), activation);
    if (w.kind === "person") openPerson(def, log, stage.id, w, id);
    else openCall(def, log, stage.id, w, id);
  }
}

/** Cancels (with a cause) or skips every open wait of one activation, in declared order. */
export function endStageWaits(log: TurnLog, stage: ChildStage, activation: string, how: { skip: true } | { cause: string }): void {
  for (const w of stage.waits) {
    const element = fullId(stage.id, w.id);
    for (const instance of log.state.waits) {
      if (instance.id.element !== element || instance.id.activation !== activation || instance.status !== "open") continue;
      if ("skip" in how) log.emit("WaitSkipped", { wait: instance.id });
      else log.emit("WaitCancelled", { wait: instance.id, cause: how.cause });
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Closes the request: every wait still open is cancelled (cause `request-closed`); no `StageExited` is
 * recorded (spec section 2). `stage` is the final stage, or null for an admin.
 */
export function closeRequest(def: PublishedDefinition, log: TurnLog, stage: string | null): void {
  for (const s of log.state.activeStages) {
    const stageDef = findStage(def, s.stage);
    if (stageDef !== undefined) endStageWaits(log, stageDef, s.activation, { cause: "request-closed" });
  }
  log.emit("RequestClosed", { stage });
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/errors.ts\n===
/**
 * A history `evolve` cannot fold: one that `decide` could not have written (a gap in seq, a wait completed
 * that was never opened, an event type or version this core does not know). Replay stops rather than guess,
 * so a rebuild reports a damaged history instead of building a wrong state. Codes are kebab-case.
 */
export type EvolveErrorCode =
  | "request-mismatch"
  | "seq-gap"
  | "unknown-event-type"
  | "unknown-event-version"
  | "not-started"
  | "already-started"
  | "duplicate-activation"
  | "stage-not-active"
  | "duplicate-wait"
  | "unknown-wait"
  | "wait-not-open"
  | "wait-still-open"
  | "unknown-patch-op";

export class EvolveError extends Error {
  readonly code: EvolveErrorCode;
  readonly seq: number;
  constructor(code: EvolveErrorCode, seq: number, message: string) {
    super(`event ${seq}: ${code}: ${message}`);
    this.name = "EvolveError";
    this.code = code;
    this.seq = seq;
  }
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/evolve.ts\n===
/**
 * evolve: the fold of one event into the request state (kernel spec sections 3 and 5). The only code replay
 * uses (architecture.md, "decide records, evolve replays"): every consequence is already spelled out as an
 * event, so evolve never evaluates CEL and never reads a definition. It never branches on an open enum's
 * value (spec section 5: `DataSet.source`, `WaitCancelled.cause`, `Faulted.kind`, `StageExited.mode`, wait
 * `kind` and `role`, `by.type`, `trigger.kind`): those are stored as recorded.
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, WaitId } from "../format/index.ts";
import { EVENT_TYPES } from "../format/index.ts";
import { EvolveError } from "./errors.ts";
import { applyPatch } from "./patch.ts";
import { emptyState, sameWait, type RequestState, type WaitInstance } from "./state.ts";

/** The event versions this core reads. Every type is at v 1 (event-payloads.md section 1); a later v brings an upcaster. */
const KNOWN_VERSION = 1;

function waitName(id: WaitId): string {
  return `${id.element}${id.key === "" ? "" : `[${id.key}]`}@${id.activation}#${id.seq}`;
}

function updateWait(
  state: RequestState,
  seq: number,
  id: WaitId,
  change: (w: WaitInstance) => WaitInstance,
  mustBeOpen: boolean,
): WaitInstance[] {
  const index = state.waits.findIndex((w) => sameWait(w.id, id));
  const current = index < 0 ? undefined : state.waits[index];
  if (current === undefined) throw new EvolveError("unknown-wait", seq, `${waitName(id)} was never opened`);
  if (mustBeOpen && current.status !== "open") {
    throw new EvolveError("wait-not-open", seq, `${waitName(id)} is ${current.status}`);
  }
  if (!mustBeOpen && current.status === "open") {
    throw new EvolveError("wait-still-open", seq, `${waitName(id)} is still open`);
  }
  const waits = state.waits.slice();
  waits[index] = change(current);
  return waits;
}

function checkEnvelope(state: RequestState, event: AnyEventRecord): void {
  const { seq } = event;
  if (!(EVENT_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(event.type)) {
    throw new EvolveError("unknown-event-type", seq, `unknown event type ${String(event.type)}`);
  }
  if (event.v !== KNOWN_VERSION) {
    throw new EvolveError("unknown-event-version", seq, `${event.type} v ${event.v} is not known to this core`);
  }
  if (seq !== state.lastSeq + 1) {
    throw new EvolveError("seq-gap", seq, `expected seq ${state.lastSeq + 1}`);
  }
  if (state.request === null && event.type !== "RequestStarted") {
    throw new EvolveError("not-started", seq, `${event.type} before RequestStarted`);
  }
  if (state.request !== null && event.requestId !== state.requestId) {
    throw new EvolveError("request-mismatch", seq, `event of request ${event.requestId} in request ${state.requestId}`);
  }
}

/** The fold of one event. Returns a new state; neither the state nor the event is changed. */
export function evolve(state: RequestState, event: AnyEventRecord): RequestState {
  checkEnvelope(state, event);
  const { seq, at, turn } = event;
  const base: RequestState = { ...state, requestId: event.requestId, lastSeq: seq, lastAt: at, lastTurn: turn };

  switch (event.type) {
    case "RequestStarted": {
      if (state.request !== null) throw new EvolveError("already-started", seq, "a second RequestStarted");
      const p = event.payload;
      return {
        ...base,
        definition: { workflow: p.workflow, version: p.version },
        request: { id: event.requestId, by: p.by, at, readableId: p.readableId },
        start: { input: p.input, trigger: p.trigger },
      };
    }

    case "StageEntered": {
      const p = event.payload;
      if (state.activeStages.some((s) => s.activation === p.activation)) {
        throw new EvolveError("duplicate-activation", seq, `activation ${p.activation} is already active`);
      }
      const entered = { activation: p.activation, stage: p.stage, parentActivation: p.parentActivation, status: p.status, enteredSeq: seq };
      return { ...base, activeStages: [...state.activeStages, entered], stageEntries: state.stageEntries + 1, status: p.status };
    }

    case "StageExited": {
      const p = event.payload;
      if (!state.activeStages.some((s) => s.activation === p.activation)) {
        throw new EvolveError("stage-not-active", seq, `activation ${p.activation} (${p.stage}) is not active`);
      }
      return { ...base, activeStages: state.activeStages.filter((s) => s.activation !== p.activation) };
    }

    case "WaitOpened": {
      const p = event.payload;
      if (state.waits.some((w) => sameWait(w.id, p.wait))) {
        throw new EvolveError("duplicate-wait", seq, `${waitName(p.wait)} is already opened`);
      }
      const opened: WaitInstance = {
        id: p.wait,
        kind: p.kind,
        role: p.role,
        opened: p,
        openedSeq: seq,
        openedTurn: turn,
        openedAt: at,
        status: "open",
        outcome: "",
        data: null,
        by: null,
        evidence: null,
        cause: null,
        endedSeq: null,
        endedAt: null,
        late: null,
      };
      return { ...base, waits: [...state.waits, opened] };
    }

    case "WaitCompleted": {
      const p = event.payload;
      const waits = updateWait(
        state,
        seq,
        p.wait,
        (w) => ({ ...w, status: "completed", outcome: p.outcome, data: p.data, by: p.by, evidence: p.evidence, endedSeq: seq, endedAt: at }),
        true,
      );
      return { ...base, waits };
    }

    case "WaitCancelled": {
      const p = event.payload;
      const waits = updateWait(state, seq, p.wait, (w) => ({ ...w, status: "cancelled", cause: p.cause, endedSeq: seq, endedAt: at }), true);
      return { ...base, waits };
    }

    case "WaitSkipped": {
      const p = event.payload;
      const waits = updateWait(state, seq, p.wait, (w) => ({ ...w, status: "skipped", endedSeq: seq, endedAt: at }), true);
      return { ...base, waits };
    }

    case "CallResultLate": {
      // A result after the wait ended (spec section 2, Results): kept on the wait, never visible to conditions.
      const p = event.payload;
      const waits = updateWait(state, seq, p.wait, (w) => ({ ...w, late: { outcome: p.outcome, data: p.data, seq, at } }), false);
      return { ...base, waits };
    }

    case "DataSet": {
      const p = event.payload;
      const unknown = p.patch.map((op): string => op.op).find((op) => op !== "set" && op !== "remove");
      if (unknown !== undefined) throw new EvolveError("unknown-patch-op", seq, `patch op ${unknown}`);
      return { ...base, data: applyPatch(state.data, p.patch) };
    }

    case "TransitionFired": {
      const p = event.payload;
      return { ...base, fired: [...state.fired, { stage: p.stage, activation: p.activation, transition: p.transition, seq }] };
    }

    case "Faulted": {
      const p = event.payload;
      return { ...base, faults: [...state.faults, { kind: p.kind, element: p.element, error: p.error, seq, turn, at }] };
    }

    case "Overridden": {
      // Clearing a fault has no event of its own: a retry clears every fault here (spec section 4). The
      // re-entry and a close are the events that follow.
      const p = event.payload;
      const faults = p.actions.some((a) => a.type === "retry") ? [] : state.faults;
      const adminTurn = { by: p.by, reason: p.reason, actions: p.actions, seq, at };
      return { ...base, faults, adminTurns: [...state.adminTurns, adminTurn] };
    }

    case "RequestClosed": {
      // Closing ends any fault (spec section 4); it records no StageExited (spec section 2), so the
      // stages it closed in stay in activeStages.
      return { ...base, closed: { stage: event.payload.stage, seq, at }, faults: [] };
    }
  }
}

/** Every event folded in order onto `from` (by default the empty state). */
export function fold(events: Iterable<AnyEventRecord>, from: RequestState = emptyState()): RequestState {
  let state = from;
  for (const event of events) state = evolve(state, event);
  return state;
}

/**
 * The context a notification rule or an event rule reads (integrations.md sections 12.2 and 13.5;
 * definition-format.md section 4): `event` (the matched event's payload, or `{reason, stage}` for `Stuck`),
 * `request` (`{id, by, at}`), `data` (the request's data as of the event) and the constants.
 *
 * `event` is read as `dyn`, so every number in it is an `int`. `data` is typed by `types.data` and each
 * constant by `types.constants`, as in `decide`. One environment per definition, kept while it lives.
 */
import { createCelEnvironment, t, type CelEnvironment, type CelType, type CheckResult, type JsonValue } from "../../cel/index.ts";
import type { Json, PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { constantsFor, dataType, REQUEST_TYPE } from "../decide/environment.ts";
import type { RequestState } from "../state.ts";

/** Why a rule's expression gave no usable value. */
export interface RuleFailure {
  /** The expression's source. */
  expr: string;
  /** Kebab-case: the expression module's detail, or `not-a-bool`, `not-a-list`, `null-value`, `absent`. */
  code: string;
  message: string;
}

export type RuleValue = { kind: "value"; value: Json } | { kind: "absent" } | { kind: "error"; failure: RuleFailure };

/** What one rule evaluation reads: the payload as `event`, and the request as folded to that event. */
export interface RuleScope {
  event: unknown;
  state: RequestState;
}

interface Prepared {
  env: CelEnvironment;
  checked: Map<string, CheckResult>;
}

const environments = new WeakMap<PublishedDefinition, Prepared>();

function prepared(def: PublishedDefinition): Prepared {
  let p = environments.get(def);
  if (p === undefined) {
    const variables: Record<string, CelType> = { event: t.dyn, request: REQUEST_TYPE, data: dataType(def) };
    p = { env: createCelEnvironment({ variables, constants: constantsFor(def, variables) }), checked: new Map() };
    environments.set(def, p);
  }
  return p;
}

/**
 * Evaluates one rule expression. Never throws on a failing expression. A result holding null is an error
 * (`null-value`), as everywhere an expression's value leaves CEL (spec section 2, Values).
 */
export function evaluateRule(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: RuleScope, source: string): RuleValue {
  const { env, checked } = prepared(def);
  let check = checked.get(source);
  if (check === undefined) {
    check = env.check(source);
    checked.set(source, check);
  }
  if (!check.ok) {
    const problem = check.problems[0];
    return { kind: "error", failure: { expr: source, code: problem?.code ?? "check-failed", message: problem?.message ?? "" } };
  }
  const context: Record<string, JsonValue> = { event: scope.event as JsonValue, data: scope.state.data };
  const request = scope.state.request;
  if (request !== null) context["request"] = { id: request.id, by: { type: request.by.type, id: request.by.id }, at: request.at };
  const result = env.evaluate(check.expression, context);
  if (result.kind === "error") return { kind: "error", failure: { expr: source, code: result.detail, message: result.message } };
  if (result.kind === "absent") return { kind: "absent" };
  return { kind: "value", value: result.value as Json };
}

/** A rule's `when`: anything but `true` or `false` is a failure, never false. */
export function evaluateWhen(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: RuleScope, source: string): { kind: "bool"; value: boolean } | { kind: "error"; failure: RuleFailure } {
  const r = evaluateRule(def, scope, source);
  if (r.kind === "error") return r;
  if (r.kind === "value" && typeof r.value === "boolean") return { kind: "bool", value: r.value };
  return { kind: "error", failure: { expr: source, code: "not-a-bool", message: "a condition did not give true or false" } };
}

/**
 * Which notification rules a committed turn sets off, to whom, with what message (kernel spec section 7;
 * integrations.md section 12). Pure: the notifier sends, expands groups and logs rule errors; this only
 * works out what to send.
 *
 * - A rule on a recorded event type matches each event of the turn of that type (and element, when the
 *   rule names one) for which its `when` is true. A rule on `WaitOpened` matches only a wait still open at
 *   the end of the turn.
 * - A rule on `Stuck` matches a turn after which the request is stuck in another state than before; its
 *   event is `{reason, stage}`, `stage` the authored stage (`authoredStageOf`), and its source is the turn's last event.
 * - `when`, recipients and message values read `data` as of the matched event.
 * - Messages are in event order, then in the rules' declared order.
 * - A rule whose expression errors sends nothing for that event; the error is returned, and the turn's
 *   other rules still apply.
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, Json, NotificationRule, PublishedDefinition, Ref, ValueKind } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { isJsonObject } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { RequestState } from "../state.ts";
import { authoredStageOf } from "../stuck/index.ts";
import { evaluateRule, evaluateWhen, type RuleFailure, type RuleScope } from "./context.ts";
import { matchesEvent, newlyStuck, readTurn, STUCK, type TurnContext, type TurnView } from "./turn.ts";

/** A recipient as the notifier receives it: a reference as recorded (a group is not expanded), or the workflow admins. */
export type NotifyRecipient = Ref | { type: "workflowAdmins" };

/** A message part with its value worked out. `value` is left out when the expression gave `optional.none()`. */
export type NotifyPart = { text: string } | { kind: ValueKind; value?: Json };

export type NotifyMessage = { words: string } | { parts: NotifyPart[] };

/** The event a rule matched. For `Stuck`: `type` "Stuck", the turn's last event's `seq` and `at`, payload `{reason, stage}`. */
export interface MatchedEvent {
  type: string;
  seq: number;
  at: string;
  payload: unknown;
}

export interface Notification {
  rule: string;
  requestId: string;
  event: MatchedEvent;
  to: NotifyRecipient[];
  /** Resolved references that are neither a user nor a group, skipped (integrations.md section 12.3). */
  skipped: Json[];
  message: NotifyMessage;
}

export interface NotifyRuleError {
  rule: string;
  /** The matched event's seq: with the request and the rule, the error's key. */
  seq: number;
  failure: RuleFailure;
}

export interface NotifyResult {
  messages: Notification[];
  errors: NotifyRuleError[];
}

class RuleError extends Error {
  readonly failure: RuleFailure;
  constructor(failure: RuleFailure) {
    super(failure.message);
    this.failure = failure;
  }
}

function value(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: RuleScope, source: string): Json | undefined {
  const r = evaluateRule(def, scope, source);
  if (r.kind === "error") throw new RuleError(r.failure);
  return r.kind === "value" ? r.value : undefined;
}

function recipients(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: RuleScope, rule: NotificationRule): { to: NotifyRecipient[]; skipped: Json[] } {
  const to: NotifyRecipient[] = [];
  const skipped: Json[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const add = (r: NotifyRecipient): void => {
    const key = JSON.stringify([r.type, "id" in r ? r.id : ""]);
    if (!seen.has(key)) {
      seen.add(key);
      to.push(r);
    }
  };
  for (const recipient of rule.send.to) {
    if (recipient.type === "workflowAdmins") {
      add({ type: "workflowAdmins" });
      continue;
    }
    const list = value(def, scope, recipient.expr);
    if (!Array.isArray(list)) {
      const code = list === undefined ? "absent" : "not-a-list";
      throw new RuleError({ expr: recipient.expr, code, message: "recipients did not give a list" });
    }
    for (const item of list) {
      const isRef = isJsonObject(item) && typeof item["id"] === "string";
      if (isRef && (item["type"] === "user" || item["type"] === "group")) add({ type: item["type"], id: item["id"] as string });
      else skipped.push(item);
    }
  }
  return { to, skipped };
}

function message(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: RuleScope, rule: NotificationRule): NotifyMessage {
  const m = rule.send.message;
  if ("words" in m) return { words: m.words };
  return {
    parts: m.parts.map((p): NotifyPart => {
      if ("text" in p) return { text: p.text };
      const v = value(def, scope, p.value);
      return v === undefined ? { kind: p.kind } : { kind: p.kind, value: v };
    }),
  };
}

function apply(def: PublishedDefinition, rule: NotificationRule, scope: RuleScope, event: MatchedEvent, requestId: string, out: NotifyResult): void {
  try {
    const when = evaluateWhen(def, scope, rule.when);
    if (when.kind === "error") throw new RuleError(when.failure);
    if (!when.value) return;
    const { to, skipped } = recipients(def, scope, rule);
    out.messages.push({ rule: rule.id, requestId, event, to, skipped, message: message(def, scope, rule) });
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof RuleError)) throw error;
    out.errors.push({ rule: rule.id, seq: event.seq, failure: error.failure });
  }
}

function matchTurn(def: PublishedDefinition, view: TurnView): NotifyResult {
  const out: NotifyResult = { messages: [], errors: [] };
  const stuck = newlyStuck(view);
  view.events.forEach((e: AnyEventRecord, i) => {
    const state = view.asOf[i] as RequestState;
    const last = i === view.events.length - 1;
    for (const rule of def.notifications) {
      if (rule.on.event === STUCK) {
        if (!last || stuck === null || rule.on.element !== null) continue;
        const payload = { reason: stuck.reason, stage: authoredStageOf(def, stuck.stage) };
        apply(def, rule, { event: payload, state }, { type: STUCK, seq: e.seq, at: e.at, payload }, e.requestId, out);
      } else if (matchesEvent(rule.on, e, view)) {
        apply(def, rule, { event: e.payload, state }, { type: e.type, seq: e.seq, at: e.at, payload: e.payload }, e.requestId, out);
      }
    }
  });
  return out;
}

/**
 * The messages a committed turn sends. `before` is the request before the turn's first event (the empty
 * state for a start turn), `events` the turn's events in order, `after` the request after the last one.
 */
export function matchNotifications(
  definition: PublishedDefinition,
  before: RequestState,
  events: readonly AnyEventRecord[],
  after: RequestState,
  context: TurnContext = {},
): NotifyResult {
  return matchTurn(definition, readTurn(definition, before, events, after, context));
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/notify/outbound.ts\n===
/**
 * The outbound events a committed turn publishes (integrations.md section 13): the CloudEvents of the six
 * types.
 *
 * | Type | Rule ID | Source event | When |
 * |---|---|---|---|
 * | `request.started@1` | `$request.started` | `RequestStarted` | Always, in the start turn |
 * | `request.statusChanged@1` | `$request.statusChanged` | The turn's last `StageEntered` of a child stage | The status ID after the turn differs from the one before it |
 * | `request.stuck@1` | `$request.stuck` | The turn's last event | Stuck after the turn, in another state than before |
 * | `request.unstuck@1` | `$request.unstuck` | The turn's last event | Stuck before the turn, not after it |
 * | `request.ended@1` | `$request.ended` | `RequestClosed` | Always; `stage` is the authored ending, null when an admin closed it |
 * | `request.told@1` | The event rule's ID | The rule's `on` event | The rule's `when` is true |
 *
 * Order: by source seq, then the platform rules in the table's order, then the event rules in declared order.
 * A turn whose input is a `CallResultLate` publishes nothing.
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, By, EventRule, Json, PublishedDefinition, StartTrigger, StatusRef } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { RequestState } from "../state.ts";
import { authoredStageOf } from "../stuck/index.ts";
import { evaluateRule, evaluateWhen, type RuleFailure, type RuleScope } from "./context.ts";
import { matchesEvent, newlyStuck, readTurn, STUCK, type TurnContext, type TurnView } from "./turn.ts";

export type OutboundType =
  | "request.started@1"
  | "request.statusChanged@1"
  | "request.stuck@1"
  | "request.unstuck@1"
  | "request.ended@1"
  | "request.told@1";

export interface StartedData {
  startedBy: By;
  trigger: StartTrigger | null;
}
export interface StatusChangedData {
  from: StatusRef | null;
  to: StatusRef | null;
}
export interface StuckData {
  reason: string;
  /** The authored stage (`authoredStageOf`). */
  stage: string | null;
}
export interface UnstuckData extends StuckData {
  by: By;
}
export interface EndedData {
  status: StatusRef | null;
  closedBy: "workflow" | "admin";
  by: By | null;
  /** The authored ending the request finished at (`authoredStageOf`); null when an admin closed it. */
  stage: string | null;
}
export interface ToldData {
  told: { id: string; words: string };
  values: { [name: string]: Json };
}

/** The CloudEvent as sent (integrations.md section 13.1). */
export interface OutboundEventBody {
  specversion: "1.0";
  id: string;
  source: string;
  type: OutboundType;
  subject: string;
  time: string;
  datacontenttype: "application/json";
  workflow: string;
  workflowversion: number;
  readableid: string;
  data: StartedData | StatusChangedData | StuckData | UnstuckData | EndedData | ToldData;
}

/** One event to post: `(requestId, seq, ruleId)` makes its ID, and the body is what a subscriber receives. */
export interface OutboundRow {
  ruleId: string;
  seq: number;
  body: OutboundEventBody;
}

export interface OutboundRuleError {
  rule: string;
  seq: number;
  failure: RuleFailure;
}

export interface OutboundResult {
  events: OutboundRow[];
  errors: OutboundRuleError[];
}

export interface OutboundContext extends TurnContext {
  /** The installation's absolute URI, without a trailing slash; `source` is it plus `/workflows/<workflow>`. Default "". */
  deploymentUri?: string;
}

/** `<request ID>/<seq>/<rule ID>`: the request, the source event's number and the rule. */
export function outboundEventId(requestId: string, seq: number, ruleId: string): string {
  return `${requestId}/${seq}/${ruleId}`;
}

/** The status of the active child stage, null when it has none (integrations.md section 13.2). */
function statusOf(state: RequestState): StatusRef | null {
  const child = state.activeStages.filter((s) => s.stage !== "root").at(-1);
  return child?.status ?? null;
}

/** The `by` of the turn's input event. A `CallResultLate` has none; it publishes nothing anyway. */
function inputBy(events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]): By {
  const input = events[0];
  if (input !== undefined && "by" in input.payload) return input.payload.by;
  return { type: "system", id: "engine" };
}

class RuleError extends Error {
  readonly failure: RuleFailure;
  constructor(failure: RuleFailure) {
    super(failure.message);
    this.failure = failure;
  }
}

function toldData(def: PublishedDefinition, rule: EventRule, scope: RuleScope): ToldData | null {
  const when = evaluateWhen(def, scope, rule.when);
  if (when.kind === "error") throw new RuleError(when.failure);
  if (!when.value) return null;
  const values: { [name: string]: Json } = {};
  for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(rule.values)) {
    const r = evaluateRule(def, scope, source);
    if (r.kind === "error") throw new RuleError(r.failure);
    if (r.kind === "value") values[name] = r.value;
  }
  return { told: { id: rule.told.id, words: rule.told.words }, values };
}

function publish(def: PublishedDefinition, view: TurnView, context: OutboundContext): OutboundResult {
  const out: OutboundResult = { events: [], errors: [] };
  const { events, after } = view;
  const last = events[events.length - 1];
  if (last === undefined || after.request === null || events[0]?.type === "CallResultLate") return out;
  const workflow = after.definition?.workflow ?? def.workflow;
  const version = after.definition?.version ?? def.version;
  const source = `${context.deploymentUri ?? ""}/workflows/${workflow}`;
  const readableid = String(after.request.readableId);
  const row = (ruleId: string, type: OutboundType, e: AnyEventRecord, data: OutboundEventBody["data"]): void => {
    out.events.push({
      ruleId,
      seq: e.seq,
      body: {
        specversion: "1.0",
        id: outboundEventId(e.requestId, e.seq, ruleId),
        source,
        type,
        subject: e.requestId,
        time: e.at,
        datacontenttype: "application/json",
        workflow,
        workflowversion: version,
        readableid,
        data,
      },
    });
  };

  // Compared once per turn, so a stage passed through inside the turn publishes nothing.
  const fromStatus = statusOf(view.before);
  const toStatus = statusOf(after);
  const statusSource = events.filter((e) => e.type === "StageEntered" && e.payload.stage !== "root").at(-1);
  const statusChanged = (fromStatus?.id ?? null) !== (toStatus?.id ?? null) && statusSource !== undefined;
  const { stuckBefore, stuckAfter } = view;
  const stuck = newlyStuck(view);

  events.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (e.type === "RequestStarted") row("$request.started", "request.started@1", e, { startedBy: e.payload.by, trigger: e.payload.trigger });
    if (statusChanged && e === statusSource) row("$request.statusChanged", "request.statusChanged@1", e, { from: fromStatus, to: toStatus });
    if (e === last && stuck !== null) row("$request.stuck", "request.stuck@1", e, { reason: stuck.reason, stage: authoredStageOf(def, stuck.stage) });
    if (e === last && stuckBefore !== null && stuckAfter === null) {
      row("$request.unstuck", "request.unstuck@1", e, { reason: stuckBefore.reason, stage: authoredStageOf(def, stuckBefore.stage), by: inputBy(events) });
    }
    if (e.type === "RequestClosed") {
      const admin = e.payload.stage === null;
      const ending = e.payload.stage === null ? null : authoredStageOf(def, e.payload.stage);
      row("$request.ended", "request.ended@1", e, { status: statusOf(after), closedBy: admin ? "admin" : "workflow", by: admin ? inputBy(events) : null, stage: ending });
    }
    const state = view.asOf[i] as RequestState;
    for (const rule of def.events ?? []) {
      let scope: RuleScope;
      if (rule.on.event === STUCK) {
        if (e !== last || stuck === null || rule.on.element !== null) continue;
        scope = { event: { reason: stuck.reason, stage: authoredStageOf(def, stuck.stage) }, state };
      } else if (matchesEvent(rule.on, e, view)) {
        scope = { event: e.payload, state };
      } else continue;
      try {
        const data = toldData(def, rule, scope);
        if (data !== null) row(rule.id, "request.told@1", e, data);
      } catch (error) {
        if (!(error instanceof RuleError)) throw error;
        out.errors.push({ rule: rule.id, seq: e.seq, failure: error.failure });
      }
    }
  });
  return out;
}

/**
 * The outbound events a committed turn publishes. `before` is the request before the turn's first event
 * (the empty state for a start turn), `events` the turn's events in order, `after` the request after them.
 */
export function outboundEvents(
  definition: PublishedDefinition,
  before: RequestState,
  events: readonly AnyEventRecord[],
  after: RequestState,
  context: OutboundContext = {},
): OutboundResult {
  return publish(definition, readTurn(definition, before, events, after, context), context);
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/notify/turn.ts\n===
/**
 * What the notifier and the publisher read of one committed turn: the state as of each of its events, and
 * the stuck state before and after it (integrations.md sections 11.5, 12 and 13). Shared so that both match
 * a rule's `on` and `Stuck` the same way.
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, PublishedDefinition, RuleOn } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { stuckStateOf, type StuckState } from "../stuck/index.ts";
import { evolve } from "../evolve.ts";
import { findWait, type RequestState } from "../state.ts";

/** The rule `on` name that matches a change of the stuck state; no recorded event type is named so. */
export const STUCK = "Stuck";

/**
 * Optional inputs a caller already has. The stuck state is worked out once per turn (integrations.md
 * section 11.5); a host that keeps it passes it here, otherwise it is worked out from `before` and `after`.
 */
export interface TurnContext {
  stuckBefore?: StuckState | null;
  stuckAfter?: StuckState | null;
}

export interface TurnView {
  before: RequestState;
  events: readonly AnyEventRecord[];
  /** `asOf[i]` is the request folded up to and including `events[i]`. */
  asOf: RequestState[];
  after: RequestState;
  stuckBefore: StuckState | null;
  stuckAfter: StuckState | null;
}

export function readTurn(def: PublishedDefinition, before: RequestState, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], after: RequestState, context: TurnContext = {}): TurnView {
  const asOf: RequestState[] = [];
  let state = before;
  for (const e of events) {
    state = evolve(state, e);
    asOf.push(state);
  }
  const stuckBefore = context.stuckBefore !== undefined ? context.stuckBefore : stuckStateOf(def, before);
  const stuckAfter = context.stuckAfter !== undefined ? context.stuckAfter : stuckStateOf(def, after);
  return { before, events, asOf, after, stuckBefore, stuckAfter };
}

export function sameStuck(a: StuckState | null, b: StuckState | null): boolean {
  return a === null || b === null ? a === b : a.reason === b.reason && a.stage === b.stage;
}

/** The stuck state after the turn when it is stuck and differs from the state before it; else null. */
export function newlyStuck(view: TurnView): StuckState | null {
  return view.stuckAfter !== null && !sameStuck(view.stuckBefore, view.stuckAfter) ? view.stuckAfter : null;
}

/**
 * The element a rule's `on.element` is compared with (definition-format.md section 3.6), or undefined for an
 * event type that takes no element (`RequestStarted`, `Overridden`).
 */
function elementOf(event: AnyEventRecord): string | null | undefined {
  switch (event.type) {
    case "WaitOpened":
    case "WaitCompleted":
    case "WaitCancelled":
    case "WaitSkipped":
    case "CallResultLate":
      return event.payload.wait.element;
    case "Faulted":
    case "DataSet":
      return event.payload.element;
    case "StageEntered":
    case "StageExited":
    case "RequestClosed":
      return event.payload.stage;
    case "TransitionFired":
      return `${event.payload.stage}.${event.payload.transition}`;
    case "RequestStarted":
    case "Overridden":
      return undefined;
  }
}

/**
 * Whether a rule `on` a recorded event type matches this event of the turn. A rule on `WaitOpened` matches
 * only a wait still open at the end of the turn: a wait completed in the same turn (the start wait) is
 * nobody's task (spec section 7), and neither is one cancelled or skipped in it.
 */
export function matchesEvent(on: RuleOn, event: AnyEventRecord, view: TurnView): boolean {
  if (on.event !== event.type) return false;
  if (on.element !== null && elementOf(event) !== on.element) return false;
  if (event.type === "WaitOpened" && findWait(view.after, event.payload.wait)?.status !== "open") return false;
  return true;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/patch.ts\n===
/**
 * applyPatch: a `DataSet` patch applied to the data document (spec section 5; event-payloads.md section 5.11).
 * Copy on write: neither the document nor the patch is changed.
 */
import { isJsonObject, type Json, type JsonObject, type PatchOp } from "../format/index.ts";

/**
 * `set` replaces the value at the path and creates missing parents; there is no merge and no array position.
 * A parent that holds something other than an object is replaced by a new object (spec section 2, Set).
 */
function setAt(doc: JsonObject, path: readonly string[], value: Json): JsonObject {
  const [head, ...rest] = path;
  if (head === undefined) return doc;
  if (rest.length === 0) return { ...doc, [head]: value };
  const current = Object.hasOwn(doc, head) ? doc[head] : undefined;
  return { ...doc, [head]: setAt(isJsonObject(current) ? current : {}, rest, value) };
}

/** `remove` of a path that is not there changes nothing (E-24). Emptied parents stay. */
function removeAt(doc: JsonObject, path: readonly string[]): JsonObject {
  const [head, ...rest] = path;
  if (head === undefined || !Object.hasOwn(doc, head)) return doc;
  if (rest.length === 0) {
    const copy = { ...doc };
    delete copy[head];
    return copy;
  }
  const current = doc[head];
  if (!isJsonObject(current)) return doc;
  const next = removeAt(current, rest);
  return next === current ? doc : { ...doc, [head]: next };
}

export function applyPatch(doc: JsonObject, patch: readonly PatchOp[]): JsonObject {
  let out = doc;
  for (const op of patch) out = op.op === "set" ? setAt(out, op.path, op.value) : removeAt(out, op.path);
  return out;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/publish/check-definition.ts\n===
/**
 * checkDefinition: the checks a published definition must pass before any request runs on it (kernel spec
 * section 6, definition-format.md section 9, integrations.md, compiler.md section 14.2).
 *
 * It runs after validateDefinitionShape and assumes the shape is valid. Checks that need the authored source
 * are not made here: the definition alone does not hold them.
 *
 * The catalogue is the optional second argument (E-27): `contract/catalogue.ts`'s `Catalogue`, typed loosely
 * because the kernel takes nothing from the authored format. The checks that need it are built with the
 * server; until then it is accepted and not read. They are:
 * - a lookup's `connection` and `source` name a data-source entry; every required input is mapped; each
 *   input has the input's type; `storedField` and `labelField` are fields of the entry's item;
 * - `types.results` equals the schema derived from each operation's catalogue entry;
 * - a call's `args` fit the operation's argument types;
 * - a nobody-to-ask membership read is on the catalogue's directory connection;
 * - trigger bindings: the trigger exists, `sent` fields read may be absent only through has() or optional
 *   syntax, the Requester mapping is valid, the connection is set up, each data expression fits its property.
 */
import type { CelNode } from "../../cel/index.ts";
import type { PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { checkStructure, checkTypes } from "./expressions.ts";
import { checkCanEnd, checkCoverage, checkCycles, knownOnEntry } from "./flow.ts";
import { checkIds } from "./ids.ts";
import { modelOf } from "./model.ts";
import { pointer, PUBLISH_WARNINGS, type PublishProblem, type Report } from "./problems.ts";
import { checkReferences } from "./references.ts";
import { sitesOf } from "./sites.ts";

/** Every problem of the definition, in the order the checks run; [] when it may be published. */
export function checkDefinition(definition: PublishedDefinition, catalogue?: object): PublishProblem[] {
  void catalogue;
  const problems: PublishProblem[] = [];
  const report: Report = (code, at, params = {}) => {
    problems.push({ code, severity: PUBLISH_WARNINGS.has(code) ? "warning" : "error", pointer: at, params });
  };
  const model = modelOf(definition);

  checkIds(definition, report);
  checkReferences(model, report);

  const checked = checkTypes(model, sitesOf(definition), report);
  const byPointer = new Map(checked.map((c) => [c.site.pointer, c]));
  const stagePointer = (stage: string): string | undefined => {
    const entry = model.stages.get(stage);
    return entry === undefined ? undefined : pointer("root", "stages", entry.index);
  };
  const definite = (stage: string, transition: number, set: number): boolean => {
    const c = byPointer.get(`${stagePointer(stage)}${pointer("transitions", transition, "set", set, "expr")}`);
    return c !== undefined && c.type !== null && !c.type.startsWith("optional<");
  };
  const whenTree = (stage: string, transition: number): CelNode | undefined =>
    byPointer.get(`${stagePointer(stage)}${pointer("transitions", transition, "when")}`)?.tree ?? undefined;

  const entry = knownOnEntry(model, definite);
  checkCanEnd(model, report);
  checkCycles(model, whenTree, report);
  checkCoverage(model, whenTree, report);
  checkStructure(model, checked, entry, report);
  return problems;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/publish/environment.ts\n===
/**
 * The CEL environments the publish check type-checks in: one per place an expression can sit, declaring
 * exactly the variables the kernel or its readers give at run time (definition-format.md section 4).
 *
 * The four kernel scopes (stage, actor, check, lookup) are `decide`'s own (`decide/environment.ts`), so an
 * expression that passes here type-checks the same way there.
 *
 * Two more scopes are for the blocks `decide` never reads: notification and event rules (`event`,
 * `request`, `data`, constants) and trigger bindings (`sent`, constants). `event` and `sent` are typed
 * `dyn`: the event payload types and the catalogue's sent fields are not part of the definition.
 */
import { createCelEnvironment, t, type CelEnvironment, type CelType, type JsonValue } from "../../cel/index.ts";
import type { PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { constantsFor, dataType, REQUEST_TYPE, schemaType, variablesFor, type Scope } from "../decide/environment.ts";

export type CheckScope =
  | Scope
  /** Notification and event rules: `event`, `request`, `data` and the constants. */
  | { kind: "rule" }
  /** Trigger bindings: `sent` and the constants. */
  | { kind: "binding" };

function variablesOf(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: CheckScope): Record<string, CelType> {
  switch (scope.kind) {
    case "rule":
      return { event: t.dyn, request: REQUEST_TYPE, data: dataType(def) };
    case "binding":
      return { sent: t.dyn };
    default:
      return variablesFor(def, scope);
  }
}

/**
 * The typed environment of a scope, and a lenient one with the same names, every one `dyn`. The lenient
 * one gives an expression's tree even when it does not type-check, so the structural checks still run.
 */
export interface ScopeEnvironments {
  typed: CelEnvironment;
  lenient: CelEnvironment;
}

export function environmentsFor(def: PublishedDefinition, scope: CheckScope): ScopeEnvironments {
  const variables = variablesOf(def, scope);
  const constants = constantsFor(def, variables);
  const dyn = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(variables).map((k) => [k, t.dyn]));
  const dynConstants: Record<string, { type: CelType; value: JsonValue }> = Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(constants).map(([name, c]) => [name, { type: t.dyn, value: c.value }]),
  );
  return {
    typed: createCelEnvironment({ variables, constants }),
    lenient: createCelEnvironment({ variables: dyn, constants: dynConstants }),
  };
}

/** The declared CEL type at a data path, from types.data; undefined where nothing declares it. */
export function declaredDataType(def: PublishedDefinition, path: readonly string[]): CelType | undefined {
  const [first, ...rest] = path;
  if (first === undefined) return undefined;
  const schema = def.types.data[first];
  if (schema === undefined) return undefined;
  let type: CelType = schemaType(schema);
  for (const segment of rest) {
    if (type.kind === "object") {
      const next = type.fields[segment];
      if (next === undefined) return undefined;
      type = next;
    } else if (type.kind === "map") type = type.value;
    else return undefined;
  }
  return type;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/publish/expressions.ts\n===
/**
 * The publish checks on each CEL field (kernel spec sections 2 and 6, definition-format.md sections 4, 5
 * and 9). In two passes:
 *
 * 1. Types: every expression parses and type-checks in the environment of its place, and gives the type
 *    its field takes. A Set's type is compared with its path's declared type. Whether a Set always writes
 *    (its type is not optional) feeds the dataflow of `flow.ts`.
 * 2. Structure, on the expression's tree: no map literal key starts with `$`; every wait read is in
 *    scope; an opening expression reads no wait of its own stage; a wait's `.data` is read only under a
 *    test that the wait's outcome is one outcome; an outcome is compared only with outcomes it can have,
 *    and a call's `failed` only with `onFailure: outcome`; a data path that may be absent is read only
 *    through `has()` or optional syntax; a lookup's input does not read `request.id`.
 */
import type { CelNode, CelProblem, CelType } from "../../cel/index.ts";
import type { JsonSchema } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { declaredDataType, environmentsFor, type CheckScope, type ScopeEnvironments } from "./environment.ts";
import type { Known } from "./flow.ts";
import { matchWait, nameableOutcomes, pathKey, waitsInScope, type Model, type ScopedWait } from "./model.ts";
import type { Report } from "./problems.ts";
import { OPENING_ROLES, type Site } from "./sites.ts";
import { chainAt, chainsOf, conjuncts, equalityWithLiteral, inLiteralList, isChainNode, namePath, type Chain } from "./tree.ts";

export interface CheckedSite {
  site: Site;
  /** The checked result type, as the CEL module names it; null when it did not type-check. */
  type: string | null;
  /** The tree, from the typed check or else from the lenient one; null when it does not parse. */
  tree: CelNode | null;
  /** The type-check problems, reported as `expression-invalid` unless a more exact problem explains them. */
  problems: CelProblem[];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- pass 1: types

function unwrapOptional(type: string): { optional: boolean; inner: string } {
  const m = /^optional<(.*)>$/.exec(type);
  return m === null ? { optional: false, inner: type } : { optional: true, inner: m[1] as string };
}

function fitsExpected(type: string, expected: Site["expected"]): boolean {
  if (type === "dyn" || expected === "any") return true;
  if (expected === "bool") return type === "bool";
  if (expected === "string") return type === "string";
  return type.startsWith("list<") || type === "list";
}

/** The JSON a CEL type becomes when it leaves an expression (format section 5.5); null when unknown. */
function jsonKindOfCel(type: string): string | null {
  if (type === "string" || type === "google.protobuf.Timestamp" || type === "google.protobuf.Duration") return "string";
  if (type === "int" || type === "uint") return "int";
  if (type === "double") return "double";
  if (type === "bool") return "bool";
  if (type.startsWith("list<") || type === "list") return "list";
  if (type.startsWith("map<") || type === "map" || type.startsWith("Obj_")) return "object";
  return null;
}

function jsonKindOfDeclared(type: CelType): string | null {
  switch (type.kind) {
    case "dyn":
      return null;
    case "map":
    case "object":
      return "object";
    default:
      return type.kind;
  }
}

export function checkTypes(model: Model, sites: readonly Site[], report: Report): CheckedSite[] {
  const envs = new Map<string, ScopeEnvironments>();
  const envFor = (scope: CheckScope): ScopeEnvironments => {
    const key = JSON.stringify(scope);
    let e = envs.get(key);
    if (e === undefined) {
      e = environmentsFor(model.def, scope);
      envs.set(key, e);
    }
    return e;
  };
  return sites.map((site) => {
    const env = envFor(site.scope);
    const typed = env.typed.check(site.source);
    if (typed.ok) {
      const type = typed.expression.type;
      const { optional, inner } = unwrapOptional(type);
      const optionalAllowed = site.expected === "any";
      if ((optional && !optionalAllowed) || !fitsExpected(optional ? inner : type, site.expected)) {
        report("expression-wrong-type", site.pointer, { expected: site.expected, type });
      }
      if (site.role === "set" && site.setPath !== undefined) {
        const declared = declaredDataType(model.def, site.setPath);
        const want = declared === undefined ? null : jsonKindOfDeclared(declared);
        const got = jsonKindOfCel(inner);
        if (want !== null && got !== null && want !== got && !(want === "double" && got === "int")) {
          report("set-type-mismatch", site.pointer, { path: [...site.setPath], declared: want, type });
        }
      }
      return { site, type, tree: typed.expression.tree, problems: [] };
    }
    const unicode = typed.problems.find((p) => p.code === "unicode-class-not-allowed");
    if (unicode !== undefined) report("pattern-unicode-class", site.pointer, { start: unicode.range.start, end: unicode.range.end });
    const lenient = env.lenient.check(site.source);
    const tree = lenient.ok ? lenient.expression.tree : null;
    return { site, type: null, tree, problems: unicode === undefined ? typed.problems : [] };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- pass 2: structure

interface Guards {
  /** Waits (`<stage>.<id>`) whose outcome is tested to be one outcome. */
  waits: ReadonlySet<string>;
  /** Data paths tested present with `has()` or `.hasValue()`, with their prefixes. */
  paths: ReadonlySet<string>;
}

const NO_GUARDS: Guards = { waits: new Set(), paths: new Set() };

function waitKey(w: ScopedWait): string {
  return `${w.stage}.${w.wait.id}`;
}

function withPrefixes(into: Set<string>, path: readonly string[]): void {
  for (let i = 1; i <= path.length; i++) into.add(pathKey(path.slice(0, i)));
}

/** The guards a condition gives where it is true: its conjuncts' one-outcome tests and presence tests. */
function guardsOf(n: CelNode | null | undefined, waits: readonly ScopedWait[], base: Guards): Guards {
  if (n === null || n === undefined) return base;
  const out = { waits: new Set(base.waits), paths: new Set(base.paths) };
  for (const c of conjuncts(n)) {
    const eq = equalityWithLiteral(c, "==");
    if (eq !== null) {
      const m = matchWait(waits, eq.chain);
      if (m !== null && m.rest.length === 1 && m.rest[0]?.name === "outcome") out.waits.add(waitKey(m.wait));
      continue;
    }
    if (c.op === "call" && c.name === "has" && c.target === null && c.args.length === 1) {
      const arg = c.args[0] as CelNode;
      const { chain } = isChainNode(arg) ? chainAt(arg) : { chain: null };
      if (chain?.root === "data") withPrefixes(out.paths, namePath(chain));
      continue;
    }
    if (c.op === "call" && c.name === "hasValue" && c.target !== null && c.args.length === 0 && isChainNode(c.target)) {
      const { chain } = chainAt(c.target);
      if (chain?.root === "data") withPrefixes(out.paths, namePath(chain));
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function propertiesOf(schema: JsonSchema | undefined): Record<string, JsonSchema> | undefined {
  const props = schema?.["properties"];
  return props !== undefined && typeof props === "object" && !Array.isArray(props) ? (props as Record<string, JsonSchema>) : undefined;
}

/**
 * Whether `segment` is `required` by the declared schema of the present data path `parent` (types.data):
 * a value written there has that property, or reading it would fail its type anyway.
 */
function requiredBelow(model: Model, parent: readonly string[], segment: string): boolean {
  const [first, ...rest] = parent;
  if (first === undefined) return false;
  let schema: JsonSchema | undefined = model.def.types.data[first];
  for (const s of rest) schema = propertiesOf(schema)?.[s];
  const required = schema?.["required"];
  const props = propertiesOf(schema);
  return Array.isArray(required) && required.includes(segment) && props !== undefined && Object.hasOwn(props, segment);
}

interface SiteContext {
  model: Model;
  site: Site;
  waits: readonly ScopedWait[];
  /** Data paths present wherever this expression runs; null when every path is (an unreached stage). */
  known: Known;
  hasData: boolean;
  hasWaits: boolean;
  report: Report;
  /** Set when a read of a wait out of scope explains a type-check failure. */
  outOfScope: boolean;
}

function checkDataRead(cx: SiteContext, chain: Chain, upTo: number, g: Guards): void {
  if (cx.known === null) return;
  const names = namePath(chain).slice(0, upTo);
  // Each prefix is reached only when the one before it is present.
  for (let i = 0; i < names.length; i++) {
    const prefix = names.slice(0, i + 1);
    const key = pathKey(prefix);
    const present = cx.known.has(key) || g.paths.has(key) || (i > 0 && requiredBelow(cx.model, prefix.slice(0, -1), prefix[i] as string));
    if (present) continue;
    if (!chain.segments.slice(0, i + 1).some((s) => s.optional)) cx.report("data-path-maybe-absent", cx.site.pointer, { path: prefix });
    return;
  }
}

function checkWaitRead(cx: SiteContext, chain: Chain, g: Guards): void {
  if (chain.segments.length === 0) return;
  const m = matchWait(cx.waits, chain);
  if (m === null) {
    const names = namePath(chain).join(".");
    if (!cx.waits.some((w) => w.wait.id.startsWith(`${names}.`))) {
      cx.outOfScope = true;
      cx.report("wait-out-of-scope", cx.site.pointer, { path: names });
    }
    return;
  }
  if (OPENING_ROLES.has(cx.site.role) && m.wait.stage === cx.site.stage) {
    cx.report("opening-reads-sibling-wait", cx.site.pointer, { wait: m.wait.wait.id });
  }
  if (m.rest[0]?.name === "data" && !g.waits.has(waitKey(m.wait))) {
    cx.report("wait-data-unguarded", cx.site.pointer, { wait: m.wait.wait.id });
  }
}

function checkOutcomeValue(cx: SiteContext, chain: Chain, value: string): void {
  const m = matchWait(cx.waits, chain);
  if (m === null || m.rest.length !== 1 || m.rest[0]?.name !== "outcome") return;
  const w = m.wait.wait;
  if (w.kind === "call" && value === "failed" && w.onFailure !== "outcome") {
    cx.report("failed-not-handled", cx.site.pointer, { wait: w.id });
  } else if (!nameableOutcomes(w).includes(value)) {
    cx.report("outcome-unknown", cx.site.pointer, { wait: w.id, outcome: value });
  }
}

function visit(cx: SiteContext, n: CelNode, g: Guards): void {
  const chainRead = (chain: Chain, upTo?: number): void => {
    if (chain.root === "data" && cx.hasData) checkDataRead(cx, chain, upTo ?? chain.segments.length, g);
    if (chain.root === "waits" && cx.hasWaits) checkWaitRead(cx, chain, g);
  };
  if (isChainNode(n)) {
    const { chain, base } = chainAt(n);
    // A chain stops at a non-literal index, so that index is visited with the base.
    if (chain !== null) chainRead(chain);
    else visit(cx, base, g);
    return;
  }
  switch (n.op) {
    case "literal":
      return;
    case "ident":
      return;
    case "index":
      visit(cx, n.operand, g);
      visit(cx, n.index, g);
      return;
    case "select":
      visit(cx, n.operand, g);
      return;
    case "list":
      n.elements.forEach((e) => visit(cx, e, g));
      return;
    case "map":
      for (const [k, v] of n.entries) {
        if (k.op === "literal" && typeof k.value === "string" && k.value.startsWith("$")) {
          cx.report("map-key-dollar", cx.site.pointer, { key: k.value });
        }
        visit(cx, k, g);
        visit(cx, v, g);
      }
      return;
    case "call": {
      if (n.name === "has" && n.target === null && n.args.length === 1) {
        const arg = n.args[0] as CelNode;
        if (isChainNode(arg)) {
          const { chain, base } = chainAt(arg);
          // has(a.b) tests b: only what is before it must be present.
          if (chain !== null) chainRead(chain, Math.max(0, chain.segments.length - 1));
          else visit(cx, base, g);
          return;
        }
      }
      if (n.target) visit(cx, n.target, g);
      n.args.forEach((a) => visit(cx, a, g));
      return;
    }
    case "operator": {
      const args = n.args;
      if (n.operator === "==" || n.operator === "!=") {
        const eq = equalityWithLiteral(n, n.operator);
        if (eq !== null) checkOutcomeValue(cx, eq.chain, eq.value);
      }
      if (n.operator === "in") {
        const m = inLiteralList(n);
        if (m !== null) for (const v of m.values) checkOutcomeValue(cx, m.chain, v);
      }
      if (n.operator === "&&" && args.length === 2) {
        const [a, b] = args as [CelNode, CelNode];
        visit(cx, a, guardsOf(b, cx.waits, g));
        visit(cx, b, guardsOf(a, cx.waits, g));
        return;
      }
      if (n.operator === "?:" && args.length === 3) {
        const [c, t, f] = args as [CelNode, CelNode, CelNode];
        visit(cx, c, g);
        visit(cx, t, guardsOf(c, cx.waits, g));
        visit(cx, f, g);
        return;
      }
      args.forEach((a) => visit(cx, a, g));
      return;
    }
  }
}

/**
 * A lookup's input does not read `request.id`: on the start form the choices are listed before a request
 * exists, so the page and the act would see different IDs. Reading the whole `request` reads its ID too.
 */
function checkLookupInput(tree: CelNode, site: Site, report: Report): void {
  const reads = chainsOf(tree).some((c) => c.root === "request" && (c.segments.length === 0 || c.segments[0]?.name === "id"));
  if (reads) report("lookup-reads-request-id", site.pointer);
}

/** Pass 2, after the dataflow: the structural checks on every tree, then the type-check problems left. */
export function checkStructure(model: Model, checked: readonly CheckedSite[], entry: ReadonlyMap<string, Known>, report: Report): void {
  const whenTrees = new Map<string, CelNode | null>();
  for (const c of checked) if (c.site.role === "when") whenTrees.set(c.site.pointer, c.tree);
  for (const c of checked) {
    const { site } = c;
    const scope = site.scope.kind;
    const hasWaits = scope === "stage" || scope === "actor" || scope === "check";
    const waits = hasWaits && site.stage !== null ? waitsInScope(model, site.stage) : [];
    // Rules see the data as of any event, so nothing is known present there.
    const known: Known = site.stage === null ? new Set() : (entry.get(site.stage) ?? null);
    // Data reads are judged only on an expression that type-checks: a key types.data does not declare is
    // a type-check problem, not an absent path.
    const hasData = scope !== "binding" && c.type !== null;
    const cx: SiteContext = { model, site, waits, known, hasData, hasWaits, report, outOfScope: false };
    if (c.tree !== null) {
      let g = NO_GUARDS;
      if (site.role === "set" && site.transition !== undefined) {
        const whenPointer = site.pointer.replace(/\/set\/\d+\/expr$/, "/when");
        g = guardsOf(whenTrees.get(whenPointer), waits, NO_GUARDS);
      }
      visit(cx, c.tree, g);
      if (site.role === "lookup-input") checkLookupInput(c.tree, site, report);
    }
    const first = c.problems[0];
    if (first !== undefined && !cx.outOfScope) {
      report("expression-invalid", site.pointer, { celCode: first.code, message: first.message, start: first.range.start, end: first.range.end });
    }
  }
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/publish/flow.ts\n===
/**
 * The checks on the graph of child stages and transitions (kernel spec section 6):
 * - which data paths are present on entry to each stage, on every route (a dataflow over the transitions);
 * - every stage can reach a final stage;
 * - every cycle passes a condition on a wait opened inside the cycle;
 * - each stage's transitions cover every combination of its waits' outcomes, or it has an `otherwise`.
 */
import type { CelNode } from "../../cel/index.ts";
import type { ChildStage } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { countingOutcomes, countsForCompletion, isPrefix, matchWait, pathKey, waitsInScope, type Model } from "./model.ts";
import { pointer, type Report } from "./problems.ts";
import { chainsOf, readCondition } from "./tree.ts";

/** Paths known to be present, each with all its prefixes; `null` is "every path" (a stage not yet reached). */
export type Known = Set<string> | null;

/** Whether a Set always writes a value (its expression is not optional), by stage ID, transition and set index. */
export type SetIsDefinite = (stage: string, transition: number, set: number) => boolean;

function withPrefixes(into: Set<string>, path: readonly string[]): void {
  for (let i = 1; i <= path.length; i++) into.add(pathKey(path.slice(0, i)));
}

function parse(key: string): string[] {
  return JSON.parse(key) as string[];
}

/** The paths known after a transition's Sets, from those known before it. */
function afterSets(known: Set<string>, stage: ChildStage, ti: number, definite: SetIsDefinite): Set<string> {
  const out = new Set(known);
  const transition = stage.transitions[ti];
  if (transition === undefined) return out;
  transition.set.forEach((s, si) => {
    const isDefinite = definite(stage.id, ti, si);
    for (const key of [...out]) {
      const k = parse(key);
      // A definite Set replaces the value at its path: what was below it may be gone. An optional one may remove it.
      if (isDefinite ? isPrefix(s.path, k) && k.length > s.path.length : isPrefix(s.path, k)) out.delete(key);
    }
    if (isDefinite) withPrefixes(out, s.path);
  });
  return out;
}

function intersect(a: Known, b: Set<string>): Set<string> {
  if (a === null) return new Set(b);
  return new Set([...a].filter((k) => b.has(k)));
}

/** The paths present on entry to each child stage, whatever route led there. */
export function knownOnEntry(model: Model, definite: SetIsDefinite): Map<string, Known> {
  const entry = new Map<string, Known>();
  for (const id of model.stages.keys()) entry.set(id, null);
  // A request starts in root.initial with no data.
  const initial = model.stages.get(model.def.root.initial);
  if (initial !== undefined) entry.set(initial.stage.id, new Set());
  for (let changed = true, rounds = 0; changed && rounds < 10000; rounds++) {
    changed = false;
    const incoming = new Map<string, Known>();
    if (initial !== undefined) incoming.set(initial.stage.id, new Set());
    for (const { stage } of model.stages.values()) {
      const from = entry.get(stage.id);
      if (from === null || from === undefined) continue;
      stage.transitions.forEach((t, ti) => {
        if (!model.stages.has(t.to)) return;
        incoming.set(t.to, intersect(incoming.get(t.to) ?? null, afterSets(from, stage, ti, definite)));
      });
    }
    for (const { stage } of model.stages.values()) {
      const next = incoming.get(stage.id);
      if (next === undefined || next === null) continue;
      const before = entry.get(stage.id);
      if (before === null || before === undefined || before.size !== next.size || [...next].some((k) => !before.has(k))) {
        entry.set(stage.id, next);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }
  return entry;
}

/** Every stage can reach a final stage. */
export function checkCanEnd(model: Model, report: Report): void {
  const ends = new Set<string>();
  for (const { stage } of model.stages.values()) if (stage.final) ends.add(stage.id);
  for (let changed = true; changed; ) {
    changed = false;
    for (const { stage } of model.stages.values()) {
      if (!ends.has(stage.id) && stage.transitions.some((t) => ends.has(t.to))) {
        ends.add(stage.id);
        changed = true;
      }
    }
  }
  for (const { stage, index } of model.stages.values()) {
    if (!ends.has(stage.id)) report("stage-cannot-end", pointer("root", "stages", index), { stage: stage.id });
  }
}

/** Trees of each transition's `when`, by stage ID and transition index; absent where it did not parse. */
export type WhenTree = (stage: string, transition: number) => CelNode | undefined;

/**
 * Every cycle passes a condition on a wait opened inside it. A transition is such a condition when its
 * `when` reads a wait of its own stage, which the cycle entered, or it is an `otherwise` of a stage with
 * an obligation or a call. So the transitions that are not form no cycle among themselves.
 */
export function checkCycles(model: Model, whenTree: WhenTree, report: Report): void {
  const free = new Map<string, { to: string; at: string }[]>();
  for (const { stage, index } of model.stages.values()) {
    const scope = waitsInScope(model, stage.id).filter((w) => w.stage === stage.id);
    stage.transitions.forEach((t, ti) => {
      if (!model.stages.has(t.to)) return;
      let gated: boolean;
      if (t.otherwise) gated = stage.waits.some(countsForCompletion);
      else {
        const tree = whenTree(stage.id, ti);
        gated = tree !== undefined && chainsOf(tree).some((c) => matchWait(scope, c) !== null);
      }
      if (!gated) {
        const list = free.get(stage.id) ?? [];
        list.push({ to: t.to, at: pointer("root", "stages", index, "transitions", ti) });
        free.set(stage.id, list);
      }
    });
  }
  const reaches = (from: string, target: string): boolean => {
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    const stack = [from];
    while (stack.length > 0) {
      const s = stack.pop() as string;
      if (s === target) return true;
      if (seen.has(s)) continue;
      seen.add(s);
      for (const e of free.get(s) ?? []) stack.push(e.to);
    }
    return false;
  };
  for (const [stage, edges] of free) {
    for (const e of edges) if (reaches(e.to, stage)) report("cycle-without-wait", e.at, { stage, to: e.to });
  }
}

/** At most this many combinations are tried per stage; beyond it the stage needs an `otherwise`. */
const MAX_COMBINATIONS = 4096;

/**
 * Each stage's transitions cover every combination of its waits' outcomes, or the stage has an
 * `otherwise` (spec section 6). A combination completes every obligation and call with one of its
 * counting outcomes; it is covered when some transition's `when` is true in it, whatever the data. A
 * stage with no such wait has one empty combination, covered by any transition (compiler.md 14.2).
 */
export function checkCoverage(model: Model, whenTree: WhenTree, report: Report): void {
  for (const { stage, index } of model.stages.values()) {
    if (stage.final || stage.transitions.some((t) => t.otherwise)) continue;
    const at = pointer("root", "stages", index);
    const counted = stage.waits.filter(countsForCompletion);
    if (counted.length === 0) {
      if (stage.transitions.length === 0) report("outcomes-not-covered", at, { stage: stage.id, combination: {} });
      continue;
    }
    const total = counted.reduce((n, w) => n * Math.max(1, countingOutcomes(w).length), 1);
    if (total > MAX_COMBINATIONS) {
      report("outcomes-not-covered", at, { stage: stage.id, combinations: total, limit: MAX_COMBINATIONS });
      continue;
    }
    const scope = waitsInScope(model, stage.id);
    const trees = stage.transitions.map((_, ti) => whenTree(stage.id, ti));
    const combination: Record<string, string> = {};
    const tryAll = (i: number): boolean => {
      const w = counted[i];
      if (w === undefined) {
        const covered = trees.some(
          (tree) =>
            tree !== undefined &&
            readCondition(tree, (chain, value) => {
              const m = matchWait(scope, chain);
              if (m === null || m.wait.stage !== stage.id || m.rest.length !== 1) return undefined;
              const outcome = combination[m.wait.wait.id];
              if (outcome === undefined) return undefined;
              if (m.rest[0]?.name === "outcome") return outcome === value;
              if (m.rest[0]?.name === "status") return value === "completed";
              return undefined;
            }) === true,
        );
        if (!covered) report("outcomes-not-covered", at, { stage: stage.id, combination: { ...combination } });
        return covered;
      }
      for (const o of countingOutcomes(w)) {
        combination[w.id] = o;
        // Report the first uncovered combination only.
        if (!tryAll(i + 1)) return false;
      }
      return true;
    };
    tryAll(0);
  }
}
