/**
 * Identifiers (definition-format.md section 2): each ID matches its pattern and is unique where it must
 * be; no wait ID visible in a scope equals another or is a `.`-prefix of another, because a dotted ID is
 * nested field access in `waits`; data keys, path segments and schema property names are Names.
 */
import type { JsonSchema, PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { pointer, type Report } from "./problems.ts";

export const NAME = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$/;
const DOTTED = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63})*$/;
const WORKFLOW = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$/;
const CONNECTION = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$/;
const ENTRY = /^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}@[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$/;
const SCHEMA_REF = /^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}(?:\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63})*)@([1-9][0-9]*)$/;
const RESERVED_CONNECTIONS = new Set(["engine", "system", "platform"]);
const MAX_VERSION = 2147483647;

/** Names a constant may not have: CEL keywords and type names, the context variables, and the wrapper's prefix. */
const RESERVED_CONSTANTS = new Set([
  ...["true", "false", "null", "in", "as", "break", "const", "continue", "else", "for", "function", "if", "import", "let", "loop"],
  ...["package", "namespace", "return", "var", "void", "while"],
  ...["int", "uint", "double", "bool", "string", "bytes", "list", "map", "null_type", "type", "dyn", "timestamp", "duration"],
  ...["data", "request", "actor", "input", "waits", "item", "event", "sent", "now", "optional", "cel", "google"],
]);

export function parseSchemaRef(ref: string): { id: string; version: number } | null {
  const m = SCHEMA_REF.exec(ref);
  return m === null ? null : { id: m[1] as string, version: Number(m[2]) };
}

function unique(report: Report, kind: string, items: readonly { id: string; at: string }[]): void {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const { id, at } of items) {
    if (seen.has(id)) report("id-duplicate", at, { kind, id });
    seen.add(id);
  }
}

function connection(report: Report, id: string, at: string): void {
  if (!CONNECTION.test(id)) report("id-invalid", at, { kind: "connection", id });
  else if (RESERVED_CONNECTIONS.has(id)) report("connection-reserved", at, { id });
}

function version(report: Report, v: number, at: string): void {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(v) || v < 1 || v > MAX_VERSION) report("version-out-of-range", at, { version: v });
}

/** Every property name in a schema, at any depth, is a Name. */
function schemaProperties(report: Report, schema: unknown, at: string): void {
  if (schema === null || typeof schema !== "object" || Array.isArray(schema)) return;
  const s = schema as Record<string, unknown>;
  const props = s["properties"];
  if (props !== null && typeof props === "object" && !Array.isArray(props)) {
    for (const [name, sub] of Object.entries(props)) {
      const p = `${at}${pointer("properties", name)}`;
      if (!NAME.test(name)) report("schema-property-invalid", p, { property: name });
      schemaProperties(report, sub, p);
    }
  }
  for (const key of ["items", "additionalProperties"]) schemaProperties(report, s[key], `${at}${pointer(key)}`);
}

function paths(report: Report, path: readonly string[], at: string): void {
  path.forEach((segment, i) => {
    if (!NAME.test(segment)) report("path-segment-invalid", `${at}${pointer(i)}`, { segment });
  });
}

export function checkIds(def: PublishedDefinition, report: Report): void {
  if (!WORKFLOW.test(def.workflow)) report("id-invalid", pointer("workflow"), { kind: "workflow", id: def.workflow });
  version(report, def.version, pointer("version"));

  const stageIds: { id: string; at: string }[] = [];
  def.root.stages.forEach((stage, i) => {
    const at: (string | number)[] = ["root", "stages", i];
    const p = pointer(...at, "id");
    if (!NAME.test(stage.id) || stage.id === "root") report("id-invalid", p, { kind: "stage", id: stage.id });
    stageIds.push({ id: stage.id, at: p });
    const locals: { id: string; at: string }[] = [];
    stage.waits.forEach((w, wi) => {
      const wp = [...at, "waits", wi];
      if (!DOTTED.test(w.id)) report("id-invalid", pointer(...wp, "id"), { kind: "wait", id: w.id });
      locals.push({ id: w.id, at: pointer(...wp, "id") });
      if (w.kind === "person") {
        const outcomes: { id: string; at: string }[] = [];
        w.outcomes.forEach((o, oi) => {
          const op = [...wp, "outcomes", oi];
          if (!NAME.test(o.id)) report("id-invalid", pointer(...op, "id"), { kind: "outcome", id: o.id });
          outcomes.push({ id: o.id, at: pointer(...op, "id") });
          const checks = o.checks.map((c, ci) => ({ id: c.id, at: pointer(...op, "checks", ci, "id") }));
          for (const c of checks) if (!NAME.test(c.id)) report("id-invalid", c.at, { kind: "check", id: c.id });
          unique(report, "check", checks);
          o.lookups.forEach((l, li) => {
            const lp = [...op, "lookups", li];
            connection(report, l.connection, pointer(...lp, "connection"));
            if (!ENTRY.test(l.source)) report("id-invalid", pointer(...lp, "source"), { kind: "source", id: l.source });
            for (const [field, name] of [
              ["property", l.property],
              ["storedField", l.storedField],
              ["labelField", l.labelField],
            ] as const) {
              if (!NAME.test(name)) report("id-invalid", pointer(...lp, field), { kind: field, id: name });
            }
          });
        });
        unique(report, "outcome", outcomes);
      } else {
        connection(report, w.connection, pointer(...wp, "connection"));
        if (!ENTRY.test(w.op)) report("id-invalid", pointer(...wp, "op"), { kind: "op", id: w.op });
      }
    });
    stage.transitions.forEach((tr, ti) => {
      const tp = [...at, "transitions", ti];
      if (!DOTTED.test(tr.id)) report("id-invalid", pointer(...tp, "id"), { kind: "transition", id: tr.id });
      locals.push({ id: tr.id, at: pointer(...tp, "id") });
      tr.set.forEach((s, si) => paths(report, s.path, pointer(...tp, "set", si, "path")));
    });
    unique(report, "local", locals);

    // The waits of one scope: this stage's.
    const own = stage.waits.map((w, wi) => ({ w, at: pointer(...at, "waits", wi, "id") }));
    for (const a of own) {
      for (const b of own) if (b.w.id.startsWith(`${a.w.id}.`)) report("wait-id-prefix", b.at, { wait: b.w.id, prefix: a.w.id });
    }
  });
  unique(report, "stage", stageIds);

  const statuses = def.statuses.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, at: pointer("statuses", i, "id") }));
  for (const s of statuses) if (!NAME.test(s.id)) report("id-invalid", s.at, { kind: "status", id: s.id });
  unique(report, "status", statuses);

  for (const name of Object.keys(def.constants)) {
    if (!NAME.test(name) || RESERVED_CONSTANTS.has(name) || name.startsWith("cel1_")) {
      report("id-invalid", pointer("constants", name), { kind: "constant", id: name });
    }
  }
  for (const key of Object.keys(def.types.data)) {
    if (!NAME.test(key)) report("id-invalid", pointer("types", "data", key), { kind: "data", id: key });
  }
  for (const [conn, ops] of Object.entries(def.types.results)) {
    connection(report, conn, pointer("types", "results", conn));
    for (const op of Object.keys(ops)) if (!ENTRY.test(op)) report("id-invalid", pointer("types", "results", conn, op), { kind: "op", id: op });
  }

  for (const [ref, pinned] of Object.entries(def.schemas)) {
    const at = pointer("schemas", ref);
    const parsed = parseSchemaRef(ref);
    if (parsed === null) report("id-invalid", at, { kind: "schema", id: ref });
    else if (parsed.id !== pinned.id || parsed.version !== pinned.version) report("schema-ref-mismatch", at, { ref, id: pinned.id, version: pinned.version });
    version(report, pinned.version, `${at}/version`);
    schemaProperties(report, pinned.schema, `${at}/schema`);
  }
  const typed: [string, Record<string, JsonSchema>][] = [
    [pointer("types", "data"), def.types.data],
    [pointer("types", "constants"), def.types.constants],
  ];
  for (const [base, map] of typed) for (const [k, s] of Object.entries(map)) schemaProperties(report, s, `${base}${pointer(k)}`);
  for (const [conn, ops] of Object.entries(def.types.results)) {
    for (const [op, s] of Object.entries(ops)) schemaProperties(report, s, pointer("types", "results", conn, op));
  }

  const rules = def.notifications.map((r, i) => ({ id: r.id, at: pointer("notifications", i, "id") }));
  for (const r of rules) if (!DOTTED.test(r.id)) report("id-invalid", r.at, { kind: "notification", id: r.id });
  unique(report, "notification", rules);

  const bindings = (def.triggers ?? []).map((b, i) => ({ id: b.id, at: pointer("triggers", i, "id") }));
  (def.triggers ?? []).forEach((b, i) => {
    if (!NAME.test(b.id)) report("id-invalid", pointer("triggers", i, "id"), { kind: "binding", id: b.id });
    connection(report, b.connection, pointer("triggers", i, "connection"));
    if (!ENTRY.test(b.event)) report("id-invalid", pointer("triggers", i, "event"), { kind: "trigger", id: b.event });
  });
  unique(report, "binding", bindings);

  const events = (def.events ?? []).map((e, i) => ({ id: e.id, at: pointer("events", i, "id") }));
  (def.events ?? []).forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!NAME.test(e.id)) report("id-invalid", pointer("events", i, "id"), { kind: "event", id: e.id });
    if (!NAME.test(e.told.id)) report("id-invalid", pointer("events", i, "told", "id"), { kind: "told", id: e.told.id });
    for (const name of Object.keys(e.values)) if (!NAME.test(name)) report("id-invalid", pointer("events", i, "values", name), { kind: "toldValue", id: name });
  });
  unique(report, "event", events);

  const nobody = (def.nobodyToAsk ?? []).map((r, i) => ({ id: r.id, at: pointer("nobodyToAsk", i, "id") }));
  (def.nobodyToAsk ?? []).forEach((r, i) => {
    if (r.id !== `${r.wait}__nobody`) report("id-invalid", pointer("nobodyToAsk", i, "id"), { kind: "nobodyToAsk", id: r.id, expected: `${r.wait}__nobody` });
  });
  unique(report, "nobodyToAsk", nobody);
}

/**
 * The definition as the publish checks read it: child stages by ID, the waits each scope sees, and which
 * outcomes of a wait count (a call's `failed` counts only with `onFailure: outcome`, spec section 6).
 */
import type { ChildStage, PublishedDefinition, Wait } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { Chain } from "./tree.ts";

export interface StageEntry {
  stage: ChildStage;
  index: number;
}

export interface Model {
  def: PublishedDefinition;
  /** Child stages by ID; the first of a duplicated ID wins (the duplicate is reported apart). */
  stages: Map<string, StageEntry>;
}

export function modelOf(def: PublishedDefinition): Model {
  const stages = new Map<string, StageEntry>();
  def.root.stages.forEach((stage, index) => {
    if (!stages.has(stage.id)) stages.set(stage.id, { stage, index });
  });
  return { def, stages };
}

export interface ScopedWait {
  wait: Wait;
  /** The stage that declares it. */
  stage: string;
}

/** The waits an expression declared on `stage` sees: the stage's own. */
export function waitsInScope(model: Model, stage: string): ScopedWait[] {
  return (model.stages.get(stage)?.stage.waits ?? []).map((wait) => ({ wait, stage }));
}

/** The wait a `waits.<...>` chain names, and the segments after its ID. */
export function matchWait(waits: readonly ScopedWait[], chain: Chain): { wait: ScopedWait; rest: Chain["segments"] } | null {
  if (chain.root !== "waits") return null;
  let best: { wait: ScopedWait; rest: Chain["segments"] } | null = null;
  for (const w of waits) {
    const parts = w.wait.id.split(".");
    if (parts.length > chain.segments.length) continue;
    if (!parts.every((p, i) => chain.segments[i]?.name === p)) continue;
    if (best === null || parts.length > best.wait.wait.id.split(".").length) best = { wait: w, rest: chain.segments.slice(parts.length) };
  }
  return best;
}

/** The outcomes of a wait that a completed instance can have, as the coverage check counts them. */
export function countingOutcomes(wait: Wait): string[] {
  if (wait.kind === "person") return wait.outcomes.map((o) => o.id);
  return wait.onFailure === "outcome" ? ["ok", "failed"] : ["ok"];
}

/** Every outcome ID a condition may compare with: a call's `failed` included, since reading it is its own check. */
export function nameableOutcomes(wait: Wait): string[] {
  return wait.kind === "person" ? wait.outcomes.map((o) => o.id) : ["ok", "failed"];
}

/** Obligations and calls: the waits a completed combination is made of (options do not count, spec section 2). */
export function countsForCompletion(wait: Wait): boolean {
  return wait.kind === "call" || wait.role === "obligation";
}

export function pathKey(path: readonly string[]): string {
  return JSON.stringify(path);
}

export function isPrefix(a: readonly string[], b: readonly string[]): boolean {
  return a.length <= b.length && a.every((s, i) => s === b[i]);
}

export type PublishCode = keyof typeof PUBLISH_CHECKS;

/** The codes that do not stop publishing. Every other code is an error. */
export const PUBLISH_WARNINGS: ReadonlySet<PublishCode> = new Set<PublishCode>();

export interface PublishProblem {
  code: PublishCode;
  /** An error stops publishing; a warning is shown and does not. */
  severity: "error" | "warning";
  /** RFC 6901 pointer into the definition: the field the problem is about. */
  pointer: string;
  params: { [name: string]: Json };
}

/** RFC 6901: a pointer from its segments, each escaped. */
export function pointer(...segments: readonly (string | number)[]): string {
  return segments.map((s) => `/${String(s).replace(/~/g, "~0").replace(/\//g, "~1")}`).join("");
}

export type Report = (code: PublishCode, at: string, params?: { [name: string]: Json }) => void;

/**
 * The publish checks on how a definition's parts refer to each other, without reading its CEL: the start
 * wait and root.initial, transition targets and statuses, final stages and `otherwise`, Sets and keys,
 * schemas and declared types, rules, bindings, lookups, nobody-to-ask rules and the origin map (kernel spec
 * sections 2 and 6, definition-format.md section 9, integrations.md sections 9.11, 11.5, 12 and 13.5).
 */
import { EVENT_TYPES, type JsonSchema, type PublishedDefinition, type RuleOn, type Wait } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { checkSchemaProfile, SchemaProfileError, validateBySchema } from "../../schema/index.ts";
import { ROOT, splitElement } from "../decide/definition.ts";
import { isPrefix, type Model } from "./model.ts";
import { pointer, type Report } from "./problems.ts";

/** The words keys of format 1 (E-21): the platform's words file is not part of core. */
export const FORMAT_1_WORDS: readonly string[] = ["task.assigned", "request.stuck"];

/** The event types whose rules may narrow to an element (definition-format.md section 3.6). */
const ELEMENT_EVENTS = new Set([
  "WaitOpened",
  "WaitCompleted",
  "WaitCancelled",
  "WaitSkipped",
  "CallResultLate",
  "Faulted",
  "DataSet",
  "StageEntered",
  "StageExited",
  "RequestClosed",
  "TransitionFired",
]);

const MEMBERS_OP = "membersOf@1";

function findWait(model: Model, full: string): { wait: Wait; stage: string } | undefined {
  const { stage, local } = splitElement(full);
  const wait = model.stages.get(stage)?.stage.waits.find((w) => w.id === local);
  return wait === undefined ? undefined : { wait, stage };
}

function objectSchema(schema: JsonSchema | undefined): { properties: Record<string, JsonSchema>; required: string[] } {
  const props = schema?.["properties"];
  const required = schema?.["required"];
  return {
    properties: props !== undefined && typeof props === "object" && !Array.isArray(props) ? (props as Record<string, JsonSchema>) : {},
    required: Array.isArray(required) ? required.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === "string") : [],
  };
}

/** The person schema: a user Ref, `{type: "user", id}` (definition-format.md section 3.13). */
function isPersonSchema(schema: JsonSchema | undefined): boolean {
  const { properties } = objectSchema(schema);
  const type = properties["type"];
  return type !== undefined && type["const"] === "user" && properties["id"] !== undefined;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- stages

function checkStages(model: Model, report: Report): void {
  const def = model.def;
  const initial = model.stages.get(def.root.initial);
  if (initial === undefined) report("initial-unknown", pointer("root", "initial"), { stage: def.root.initial });

  const start = splitElement(def.start);
  const startWait = initial?.stage.waits.find((w) => w.id === start.local);
  if (start.stage !== def.root.initial || startWait === undefined || startWait.kind !== "person") {
    report("start-not-person-wait-of-initial", pointer("start"), { start: def.start, initial: def.root.initial });
  }

  const statuses = new Set(def.statuses.map((s) => s.id));
  def.root.stages.forEach((stage, i) => {
    const at: (string | number)[] = ["root", "stages", i];
    if (stage.status !== null && !statuses.has(stage.status)) report("status-unknown", pointer(...at, "status"), { status: stage.status });
    if (stage.final && (stage.waits.length > 0 || stage.transitions.length > 0)) report("final-stage-not-empty", pointer(...at), { stage: stage.id });

    stage.waits.forEach((w, wi) => {
      if (w.kind === "call" && w.effect === "read" && (w.keyScope !== "activation" || w.idempotencyKey !== null)) {
        report("read-key-scope", pointer(...at, "waits", wi, "keyScope"), { wait: w.id });
      }
    });

    const otherwise = stage.transitions.flatMap((t, i) => (t.otherwise ? [i] : []));
    otherwise.slice(1).forEach((i) => report("otherwise-twice", pointer(...at, "transitions", i, "otherwise")));
    if (otherwise.length > 0 && otherwise[0] !== stage.transitions.length - 1) {
      report("otherwise-not-last", pointer(...at, "transitions", otherwise[0] as number, "otherwise"));
    }

    stage.transitions.forEach((t, ti) => {
      const tp = [...at, "transitions", ti];
      if (!model.stages.has(t.to)) report("transition-target-unknown", pointer(...tp, "to"), { stage: t.to });
      t.set.forEach((s, j) => {
        const clash = t.set.slice(0, j).findIndex((e) => isPrefix(e.path, s.path) || isPrefix(s.path, e.path));
        if (clash >= 0) report("set-overlap", pointer(...tp, "set", j, "path"), { path: [...s.path], overlaps: [...(t.set[clash]?.path ?? [])] });
      });
    });
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- schemas and types

function profile(report: Report, schema: unknown, at: string): boolean {
  const problems = checkSchemaProfile(schema);
  for (const p of problems) report("schema-not-in-profile", `${at}${p.pointer}`, { problem: p.code });
  return problems.length === 0;
}

function checkSchemasAndTypes(model: Model, report: Report): void {
  const def = model.def;
  const used = new Set<string>();
  const stages = def.root.stages.map((stage, i) => ({ stage, at: ["root", "stages", i] as (string | number)[] }));
  const setKeys = new Set<string>();
  const calls = new Set<string>();
  for (const { stage, at } of stages) {
    stage.waits.forEach((w, wi) => {
      if (w.kind === "person") {
        w.outcomes.forEach((o, oi) => {
          used.add(o.schema);
          if (!Object.hasOwn(def.schemas, o.schema)) report("schema-unknown", pointer(...at, "waits", wi, "outcomes", oi, "schema"), { schema: o.schema });
        });
      } else {
        calls.add(JSON.stringify([w.connection, w.op]));
        if (def.types.results[w.connection]?.[w.op] === undefined) {
          report("types-result-missing", pointer(...at, "waits", wi, "op"), { connection: w.connection, op: w.op });
        }
      }
    });
    stage.transitions.forEach((t, ti) => {
      t.set.forEach((s, si) => {
        const key = s.path[0];
        if (key === undefined) return;
        setKeys.add(key);
        if (!Object.hasOwn(def.types.data, key)) report("types-data-missing", pointer(...at, "transitions", ti, "set", si, "path"), { key });
      });
    });
  }
  for (const [ref, pinned] of Object.entries(def.schemas)) {
    if (!used.has(ref)) report("schema-unused", pointer("schemas", ref), { schema: ref });
    profile(report, pinned.schema, pointer("schemas", ref, "schema"));
  }
  for (const [key, schema] of Object.entries(def.types.data)) {
    if (!setKeys.has(key)) report("types-data-unused", pointer("types", "data", key), { key });
    profile(report, schema, pointer("types", "data", key));
  }
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(def.constants)) {
    const schema = def.types.constants[name];
    if (schema === undefined) {
      report("types-constant-missing", pointer("constants", name), { constant: name });
      continue;
    }
    try {
      const failures = validateBySchema(schema, value);
      for (const f of failures) report("constant-does-not-fit", `${pointer("constants", name)}${f.pointer}`, { constant: name, rule: f.rule });
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof SchemaProfileError)) throw error;
    }
  }
  for (const [name, schema] of Object.entries(def.types.constants)) {
    if (!Object.hasOwn(def.constants, name)) report("types-constant-unused", pointer("types", "constants", name), { constant: name });
    profile(report, schema, pointer("types", "constants", name));
  }
  for (const [conn, ops] of Object.entries(def.types.results)) {
    for (const [op, schema] of Object.entries(ops)) {
      if (!calls.has(JSON.stringify([conn, op]))) report("types-result-unused", pointer("types", "results", conn, op), { connection: conn, op });
      profile(report, schema, pointer("types", "results", conn, op));
    }
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- rules, bindings, lookups, nobody-to-ask

type ElementKind = "wait" | "call" | "transition" | "stage" | "final";

/** The kinds of element each event type's `on.element` can name (definition-format.md section 3.6). */
const ELEMENT_KINDS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly ElementKind[]>> = {
  WaitOpened: ["wait"],
  WaitCompleted: ["wait"],
  WaitCancelled: ["wait"],
  WaitSkipped: ["wait"],
  CallResultLate: ["call"],
  // Waits and transitions share one namespace because these two name either (format section 2).
  Faulted: ["wait", "transition"],
  DataSet: ["wait", "transition"],
  StageEntered: ["stage"],
  StageExited: ["stage"],
  RequestClosed: ["final"],
  TransitionFired: ["transition"],
};

/** The kinds of element an ID names in the definition: a stage (the root included), a wait or a transition. */
function kindsOf(model: Model, id: string): Set<ElementKind> {
  const out = new Set<ElementKind>();
  const stage = model.stages.get(id)?.stage;
  if (id === ROOT || stage !== undefined) out.add("stage");
  if (stage?.final === true) out.add("final");
  const { stage: s, local } = splitElement(id);
  if (local !== "") {
    const owner = model.stages.get(s)?.stage;
    const wait = owner?.waits.find((w) => w.id === local);
    if (wait !== undefined) out.add("wait");
    if (wait?.kind === "call") out.add("call");
    if (owner?.transitions.some((t) => t.id === local)) out.add("transition");
  }
  return out;
}

function checkOn(model: Model, report: Report, on: RuleOn, at: string): void {
  if (on.event !== "Stuck" && !(EVENT_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(on.event)) report("rule-event-unknown", `${at}/on/event`, { event: on.event });
  else if (on.element !== null && !ELEMENT_EVENTS.has(on.event)) report("rule-element-not-allowed", `${at}/on/element`, { event: on.event });
  else if (on.element !== null) {
    const wanted = ELEMENT_KINDS[on.event] ?? [];
    const kinds = kindsOf(model, on.element);
    if (!wanted.some((k) => kinds.has(k))) report("rule-element-unknown", `${at}/on/element`, { event: on.event, element: on.element });
  }
}

function checkRulesAndBindings(model: Model, report: Report): void {
  const def = model.def;
  def.notifications.forEach((r, i) => {
    checkOn(model, report, r.on, pointer("notifications", i));
    if ("words" in r.send.message && !FORMAT_1_WORDS.includes(r.send.message.words)) {
      report("words-unknown", pointer("notifications", i, "send", "message", "words"), { words: r.send.message.words });
    }
  });
  (def.events ?? []).forEach((e, i) => checkOn(model, report, e.on, pointer("events", i)));

  const start = findWait(model, def.start);
  const startOutcomes = start?.wait.kind === "person" ? start.wait.outcomes : [];
  (def.triggers ?? []).forEach((b, i) => {
    const outcome = startOutcomes.find((o) => o.id === b.outcome);
    if (outcome === undefined) {
      report("binding-button-missing", pointer("triggers", i, "outcome"), { outcome: b.outcome });
      return;
    }
    const { properties, required } = objectSchema(def.schemas[outcome.schema]?.schema);
    for (const key of Object.keys(b.data)) {
      if (!Object.hasOwn(properties, key)) report("binding-answer-invalid", pointer("triggers", i, "data", key), { property: key });
    }
    for (const key of required) {
      if (!Object.hasOwn(b.data, key)) report("binding-answer-missing", pointer("triggers", i, "data"), { property: key });
    }
  });

  const stages = def.root.stages.map((stage, i) => ({ stage, at: ["root", "stages", i] as (string | number)[] }));
  for (const { stage, at } of stages) {
    stage.waits.forEach((w, wi) => {
      if (w.kind !== "person") return;
      w.outcomes.forEach((o, oi) => {
        const { properties } = objectSchema(def.schemas[o.schema]?.schema);
        o.lookups.forEach((l, li) => {
          const lp = pointer(...at, "waits", wi, "outcomes", oi, "lookups", li);
          const property = properties[l.property];
          if (property === undefined) report("lookup-property-unknown", `${lp}/property`, { property: l.property });
          else if (l.answer === "person" && !isPersonSchema(property)) report("lookup-person-not-person-schema", `${lp}/answer`, { property: l.property });
        });
      });
    });
  }

  const judged = new Set<string>();
  const membersStages = new Set<string>();
  (def.nobodyToAsk ?? []).forEach((r, i) => {
    const at = pointer("nobodyToAsk", i);
    const target = findWait(model, r.wait);
    if (target === undefined || target.wait.kind !== "person") report("nobody-wait-not-person", `${at}/wait`, { wait: r.wait });
    if (judged.has(r.wait)) report("nobody-wait-twice", `${at}/wait`, { wait: r.wait });
    judged.add(r.wait);
    if (r.members === null) return;
    const members = findWait(model, r.members);
    const ok =
      members !== undefined &&
      members.wait.kind === "call" &&
      members.wait.op === MEMBERS_OP &&
      members.wait.effect === "read" &&
      members.wait.onFailure === "outcome" &&
      members.stage === splitElement(r.wait).stage;
    if (!ok) report("nobody-members-invalid", `${at}/members`, { members: r.members });
    else membersStages.add(members.stage);
  });
  for (const id of membersStages) {
    const entry = model.stages.get(id);
    entry?.stage.transitions.forEach((t, ti) => {
      if (t.otherwise) report("nobody-members-with-otherwise", pointer("root", "stages", entry.index, "transitions", ti, "otherwise"), { stage: id });
    });
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- origins

/** Every element key, with the pointers of the element's fields that hold CEL. */
function elementKeys(def: PublishedDefinition): Map<string, Set<string>> {
  const out = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  out.set(`stage:${ROOT}`, new Set());
  for (const stage of def.root.stages) {
    out.set(`stage:${stage.id}`, new Set());
    for (const w of stage.waits) {
      const full = `${stage.id}.${w.id}`;
      const fields = new Set<string>();
      if (w.kind === "person") {
        fields.add("/assignees").add("/may");
        for (const o of w.outcomes) {
          const of = new Set<string>();
          o.lookups.forEach((l, li) => {
            // A lookup's origin points at the lookup itself (integrations.md section 11.2).
            of.add(pointer("lookups", li));
            for (const name of Object.keys(l.inputs)) of.add(pointer("lookups", li, "inputs", name));
          });
          out.set(`outcome:${full}/${o.id}`, of);
          for (const c of o.checks) out.set(`check:${full}/${o.id}/${c.id}`, new Set(["/when"]));
        }
      } else {
        for (const name of Object.keys(w.args)) fields.add(pointer("args", name));
        if (w.idempotencyKey !== null) fields.add("/idempotencyKey");
      }
      out.set(`wait:${full}`, fields);
    }
    for (const t of stage.transitions) {
      const fields = new Set<string>(t.when === null ? [] : ["/when"]);
      t.set.forEach((_, i) => fields.add(pointer("set", i, "expr")));
      out.set(`transition:${stage.id}.${t.id}`, fields);
    }
  }
  for (const r of def.notifications) {
    const fields = new Set<string>(["/when"]);
    r.send.to.forEach((to, i) => {
      if (to.type === "expr") fields.add(pointer("send", "to", i, "expr"));
    });
    if ("parts" in r.send.message) {
      r.send.message.parts.forEach((p, i) => {
        if ("value" in p) fields.add(pointer("send", "message", "parts", i, "value"));
      });
    }
    out.set(`rule:${r.id}`, fields);
  }
  for (const b of def.triggers ?? []) out.set(`trigger:${b.id}`, new Set(["/when", ...Object.keys(b.data).map((k) => pointer("data", k))]));
  for (const e of def.events ?? []) out.set(`event:${e.id}`, new Set(["/when", ...Object.keys(e.values).map((k) => pointer("values", k))]));
  for (const r of def.nobodyToAsk ?? []) out.set(`nobody:${r.id}`, new Set());
  return out;
}

function checkOrigins(def: PublishedDefinition, report: Report): void {
  const elements = elementKeys(def);
  for (const key of elements.keys()) {
    if (!Object.hasOwn(def.origins, key)) report("origin-missing", pointer("origins"), { key });
  }
  for (const key of Object.keys(def.origins)) {
    const at = pointer("origins", key);
    const hash = key.indexOf("#");
    const element = hash < 0 ? key : key.slice(0, hash);
    const fields = elements.get(element);
    if (fields === undefined) report("origin-unknown-element", at, { key });
    else if (hash >= 0 && !fields.has(key.slice(hash + 1))) report("origin-field-not-cel", at, { key });  }
}

export function checkReferences(model: Model, report: Report): void {
  checkStages(model, report);
  checkSchemasAndTypes(model, report);
  checkRulesAndBindings(model, report);
  checkOrigins(model.def, report);
}

/**
 * Every CEL field of a definition, with where it sits (its pointer), the scope it is evaluated in
 * (definition-format.md section 4) and the type its field takes.
 */
import type { PublishedDefinition, Transition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import type { CheckScope } from "./environment.ts";
import { pointer } from "./problems.ts";

/** What a field's expression must give: a boolean, a list, a string, or anything (optional allowed). */
export type Expected = "bool" | "list" | "string" | "any";

export type SiteRole =
  | "assignees"
  | "may"
  | "check"
  | "lookup-input"
  | "arg"
  | "key"
  | "when"
  | "set"
  | "rule-when"
  | "recipient"
  | "part"
  | "event-when"
  | "event-value"
  | "binding-when"
  | "binding-data";

export interface Site {
  pointer: string;
  source: string;
  scope: CheckScope;
  role: SiteRole;
  expected: Expected;
  /** The stage whose waits and data the expression sees; null for rules and bindings. */
  stage: string | null;
  /** For a Set: its transition, whose `when` guards it, and the path it writes. */
  transition?: Transition;
  setPath?: readonly string[];
}

/** Opening expressions: evaluated when the wait opens, before the stage's later waits exist (spec section 6). */
export const OPENING_ROLES: ReadonlySet<SiteRole> = new Set(["assignees", "arg", "key"]);

export function sitesOf(def: PublishedDefinition): Site[] {
  const out: Site[] = [];
  def.root.stages.forEach((stage, i) => {
    const at: (string | number)[] = ["root", "stages", i];
    const id = stage.id;
    const inStage = { kind: "stage", stage: id } as const;
    stage.waits.forEach((w, wi) => {
      const wp = [...at, "waits", wi];
      if (w.kind === "person") {
        out.push({ pointer: pointer(...wp, "assignees"), source: w.assignees, scope: inStage, role: "assignees", expected: "list", stage: id });
        out.push({ pointer: pointer(...wp, "may"), source: w.may, scope: { kind: "actor", stage: id }, role: "may", expected: "bool", stage: id });
        w.outcomes.forEach((o, oi) => {
          const op = [...wp, "outcomes", oi];
          o.checks.forEach((c, ci) => {
            const scope = { kind: "check", stage: id, schema: o.schema } as const;
            out.push({ pointer: pointer(...op, "checks", ci, "when"), source: c.when, scope, role: "check", expected: "bool", stage: id });
          });
          o.lookups.forEach((l, li) => {
            for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(l.inputs)) {
              const scope = { kind: "lookup", schema: o.schema } as const;
              out.push({ pointer: pointer(...op, "lookups", li, "inputs", name), source, scope, role: "lookup-input", expected: "any", stage: id });
            }
          });
        });
      } else {
        for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(w.args)) {
          out.push({ pointer: pointer(...wp, "args", name), source, scope: inStage, role: "arg", expected: "any", stage: id });
        }
        if (w.idempotencyKey !== null) {
          out.push({ pointer: pointer(...wp, "idempotencyKey"), source: w.idempotencyKey, scope: inStage, role: "key", expected: "string", stage: id });
        }
      }
    });
    stage.transitions.forEach((tr, ti) => {
      const tp = [...at, "transitions", ti];
      if (tr.when !== null) out.push({ pointer: pointer(...tp, "when"), source: tr.when, scope: inStage, role: "when", expected: "bool", stage: id });
      tr.set.forEach((s, si) => {
        out.push({ pointer: pointer(...tp, "set", si, "expr"), source: s.expr, scope: inStage, role: "set", expected: "any", stage: id, transition: tr, setPath: s.path });
      });
    });
  });
  def.notifications.forEach((r, ri) => {
    const rp = ["notifications", ri];
    out.push({ pointer: pointer(...rp, "when"), source: r.when, scope: { kind: "rule" }, role: "rule-when", expected: "bool", stage: null });
    r.send.to.forEach((to, i) => {
      if (to.type === "expr") out.push({ pointer: pointer(...rp, "send", "to", i, "expr"), source: to.expr, scope: { kind: "rule" }, role: "recipient", expected: "list", stage: null });
    });
    if ("parts" in r.send.message) {
      r.send.message.parts.forEach((p, i) => {
        if ("value" in p) out.push({ pointer: pointer(...rp, "send", "message", "parts", i, "value"), source: p.value, scope: { kind: "rule" }, role: "part", expected: "any", stage: null });
      });
    }
  });
  (def.events ?? []).forEach((e, ei) => {
    out.push({ pointer: pointer("events", ei, "when"), source: e.when, scope: { kind: "rule" }, role: "event-when", expected: "bool", stage: null });
    for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(e.values)) {
      out.push({ pointer: pointer("events", ei, "values", name), source, scope: { kind: "rule" }, role: "event-value", expected: "any", stage: null });
    }
  });
  (def.triggers ?? []).forEach((b, bi) => {
    out.push({ pointer: pointer("triggers", bi, "when"), source: b.when, scope: { kind: "binding" }, role: "binding-when", expected: "bool", stage: null });
    for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(b.data)) {
      out.push({ pointer: pointer("triggers", bi, "data", name), source, scope: { kind: "binding" }, role: "binding-data", expected: "any", stage: null });
    }
  });
  return out;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/publish/tree.ts\n===
/**
 * Reading an expression's tree for the structural publish checks: selection chains, the tests that guard
 * a read, and a three-valued reading of a condition when the stage's waits have given known outcomes.
 */
import type { CelNode } from "../../cel/index.ts";

export interface Segment {
  name: string | number;
  /** Selected with `.?` or `[?]`. */
  optional: boolean;
}

/** A selection chain: a root name and the fields or literal indexes selected from it, in order. */
export interface Chain {
  root: string;
  segments: Segment[];
}

function literalKey(n: CelNode): string | number | undefined {
  if (n.op !== "literal") return undefined;
  if (typeof n.value === "string") return n.value;
  if (typeof n.value === "number" || typeof n.value === "bigint") return Number(n.value);
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * The longest chain that ends at `n`, and the node it starts from. When that node is a name, the chain
 * is rooted there; otherwise the chain hangs off a computed value and has no root.
 */
export function chainAt(n: CelNode): { chain: Chain | null; base: CelNode } {
  const segments: Segment[] = [];
  let at = n;
  for (;;) {
    if (at.op === "select") {
      segments.unshift({ name: at.field, optional: at.optional });
      at = at.operand;
      continue;
    }
    if (at.op === "index") {
      const key = literalKey(at.index);
      if (key === undefined) break;
      segments.unshift({ name: key, optional: at.optional });
      at = at.operand;
      continue;
    }
    break;
  }
  return { chain: at.op === "ident" ? { root: at.name, segments } : null, base: at };
}

/** The string segments of a chain, up to its first list index. */
export function namePath(chain: Chain): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const s of chain.segments) {
    if (typeof s.name !== "string") break;
    out.push(s.name);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The top-level conjuncts of a condition: `a && (b && c)` gives a, b, c. */
export function conjuncts(n: CelNode): CelNode[] {
  if (n.op === "operator" && n.operator === "&&") return n.args.flatMap(conjuncts);
  return [n];
}

export function isChainNode(n: CelNode): boolean {
  return n.op === "select" || (n.op === "index" && literalKey(n.index) !== undefined);
}

/** `<chain> == 'lit'` or `'lit' == <chain>`: the chain and the literal. */
export function equalityWithLiteral(n: CelNode, operator: "==" | "!="): { chain: Chain; value: string } | null {
  if (n.op !== "operator" || n.operator !== operator || n.args.length !== 2) return null;
  const [a, b] = n.args as [CelNode, CelNode];
  for (const [x, y] of [
    [a, b],
    [b, a],
  ] as const) {
    if (y.op === "literal" && typeof y.value === "string" && isChainNode(x)) {
      const { chain } = chainAt(x);
      if (chain !== null) return { chain, value: y.value };
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/** `<chain> in ['a', 'b']`: the chain and the literals, when every member is a string literal. */
export function inLiteralList(n: CelNode): { chain: Chain; values: string[] } | null {
  if (n.op !== "operator" || n.operator !== "in" || n.args.length !== 2) return null;
  const [x, list] = n.args as [CelNode, CelNode];
  if (list.op !== "list" || !isChainNode(x)) return null;
  const values: string[] = [];
  for (const e of list.elements) {
    if (e.op !== "literal" || typeof e.value !== "string") return null;
    values.push(e.value);
  }
  const { chain } = chainAt(x);
  return chain === null ? null : { chain, values };
}

/** Every node of a tree, the root first. */
export function forEachNode(n: CelNode, fn: (n: CelNode) => void): void {
  fn(n);
  switch (n.op) {
    case "literal":
    case "ident":
      return;
    case "select":
      forEachNode(n.operand, fn);
      return;
    case "index":
      forEachNode(n.operand, fn);
      forEachNode(n.index, fn);
      return;
    case "call":
      if (n.target) forEachNode(n.target, fn);
      n.args.forEach((a) => forEachNode(a, fn));
      return;
    case "list":
      n.elements.forEach((e) => forEachNode(e, fn));
      return;
    case "map":
      n.entries.forEach(([k, v]) => {
        forEachNode(k, fn);
        forEachNode(v, fn);
      });
      return;
    case "operator":
      n.args.forEach((a) => forEachNode(a, fn));
      return;
  }
}

/** Every maximal chain rooted at a name, each once (a chain's own prefixes are not listed again). */
export function chainsOf(n: CelNode): Chain[] {
  const out: Chain[] = [];
  const visit = (x: CelNode): void => {
    if (isChainNode(x)) {
      const { chain, base } = chainAt(x);
      if (chain !== null) out.push(chain);
      else visit(base);
      return;
    }
    switch (x.op) {
      case "literal":
        return;
      case "ident":
        out.push({ root: x.name, segments: [] });
        return;
      case "select":
      case "index":
        visit(x.operand);
        if (x.op === "index") visit(x.index);
        return;
      case "call":
        if (x.target) visit(x.target);
        x.args.forEach(visit);
        return;
      case "list":
        x.elements.forEach(visit);
        return;
      case "map":
        x.entries.forEach(([k, v]) => {
          visit(k);
          visit(v);
        });
        return;
      case "operator":
        x.args.forEach(visit);
        return;
    }
  };
  visit(n);
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- three-valued reading

export type Tri = true | false | "unknown";

/**
 * Reads a condition as true, false or unknown, given what a test on a wait gives: `known` maps a
 * comparison of a wait chain with a string literal to its answer, or undefined when it is unknown.
 */
export function readCondition(n: CelNode, known: (chain: Chain, value: string) => boolean | undefined): Tri {
  if (n.op === "literal" && typeof n.value === "boolean") return n.value;
  if (n.op !== "operator") return "unknown";
  const arg = (i: number): CelNode => n.args[i] as CelNode;
  switch (n.operator) {
    case "&&": {
      const a = readCondition(arg(0), known);
      const b = readCondition(arg(1), known);
      if (a === false || b === false) return false;
      return a === true && b === true ? true : "unknown";
    }
    case "||": {
      const a = readCondition(arg(0), known);
      const b = readCondition(arg(1), known);
      if (a === true || b === true) return true;
      return a === false && b === false ? false : "unknown";
    }
    case "!_": {
      const a = readCondition(arg(0), known);
      return a === "unknown" ? a : !a;
    }
    case "?:": {
      const c = readCondition(arg(0), known);
      if (c !== "unknown") return readCondition(arg(c ? 1 : 2), known);
      const a = readCondition(arg(1), known);
      const b = readCondition(arg(2), known);
      return a === b ? a : "unknown";
    }
    case "==":
    case "!=": {
      const eq = equalityWithLiteral(n, n.operator);
      if (eq === null) return "unknown";
      const r = known(eq.chain, eq.value);
      if (r === undefined) return "unknown";
      return n.operator === "==" ? r : !r;
    }
    case "in": {
      const m = inLiteralList(n);
      if (m === null) return "unknown";
      let any: Tri = false;
      for (const v of m.values) {
        const r = known(m.chain, v);
        if (r === true) return true;
        if (r === undefined) any = "unknown";
      }
      return any;
    }
    default:
      return "unknown";
  }
}

/**
 * The request state: what `evolve` folds a request's events into (kernel spec sections 3 and 5;
 * architecture.md "decide records, evolve replays"). `decide`, the stuck state, the request views and the
 * projections read it. It is plain data, never mutated: `evolve` returns a new state.
 *
 * Shape
 *
 * | Field | Holds | From |
 * |---|---|---|
 * | `requestId`, `lastSeq`, `lastAt`, `lastTurn` | The envelope of the last event applied. `lastSeq + 1` is the next event's seq. | every event |
 * | `definition` | `{workflow, version}` the request runs on. Taken from the events, never assumed fixed for the request's life (spec section 3). | `RequestStarted` |
 * | `request` | `{id, by, at, readableId}`. `id`, `by` and `at` are CEL's `request`. | `RequestStarted` |
 * | `start` | The start input and `trigger` as recorded. | `RequestStarted` |
 * | `closed` | `{stage, seq, at}` once the request is closed; `stage` null when an admin closed it. | `RequestClosed` |
 * | `activeStages` | The active stages as a set (spec section 2), in entry order: `{activation, stage, parentActivation, status, enteredSeq}`. A closed request keeps the stages it closed in (closing records no `StageExited`). | `StageEntered` adds; `StageExited` removes |
 * | `stageEntries` | How many `StageEntered` events the request has. Activation IDs are `a<n>`, n counting them from 1 (event-payloads.md section 3.1), so `decide` names the next one `a${stageEntries + 1}`. | `StageEntered` |
 * | `status` | The `status` of the last `StageEntered`: the request's status (data model, `requests.status`). | `StageEntered` |
 * | `waits` | Every wait instance ever opened, in open order. One per `(element, activation, key, seq)`; the current instance of `(element, activation, key)` is the one with the highest `seq` (spec section 2), whatever its predecessors did. | `WaitOpened` adds; `WaitCompleted`, `WaitCancelled`, `WaitSkipped`, `CallResultLate` update |
 * | `data` | The data document. Never holds null. | `DataSet` |
 * | `fired` | Every transition that fired: `{stage, activation, transition, seq}`. A transition fires at most once per activation of its declaring stage (spec section 2). | `TransitionFired` |
 * | `faults` | Every fault not cleared, in order: the recorded `Faulted` payload plus `seq`, `turn`, `at`. | `Faulted` adds; a `retry` action and `RequestClosed` clear all |
 * | `adminTurns` | Every `Overridden` as recorded, with `seq` and `at`. | `Overridden` |
 *
 * A wait instance: `id` (the WaitId), `kind` and `role` as recorded, `opened` (the `WaitOpened` payload as
 * recorded, so `decide` reads the assignees, outcomes, connection, op, args and key by `kind`),
 * `openedSeq`, `openedTurn`, `openedAt`, `status` (`open`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `skipped`), and, once
 * completed, `outcome`, `data`, `by`, `evidence`, `endedSeq`, `endedAt`. `cause` is the `WaitCancelled` cause.
 * `late` is a call result recorded after the wait ended (`CallResultLate`): never visible to conditions.
 *
 * What `evolve` leaves to its readers, because applying it would mean branching on an open enum
 * (spec section 5): which open waits are obligations (`role`) and which are calls (`kind`). `decide` and the
 * stuck state read those fields as recorded.
 */
import type { AdminAction, By, Evidence, FaultError, JsonObject, StartTrigger, StatusRef, WaitId, WaitOpened } from "../format/index.ts";

export type WaitStatus = "open" | "completed" | "cancelled" | "skipped";

export interface WaitInstance {
  id: WaitId;
  kind: string;
  role: string | null;
  opened: WaitOpened;
  openedSeq: number;
  openedTurn: number;
  openedAt: string;
  status: WaitStatus;

  outcome: string;
  /** The completion's data; null until completed. */
  data: JsonObject | null;
  /** Who completed it; null until completed. */
  by: By | null;
  /** The completion's evidence: null for a call, and until completed. */
  evidence: Evidence | null;
  /** The cancellation's cause as recorded; null unless cancelled. */
  cause: string | null;
  /** The seq and time of the event that completed, cancelled or skipped it; null while open. */
  endedSeq: number | null;
  endedAt: string | null;
  /** A result recorded after the wait ended (`CallResultLate`). */

}

/** The state before any event: what `evolve` folds a history onto. */
export function emptyState(): RequestState {
  return {
    requestId: "",
    lastSeq: 0,
    lastAt: "",
    lastTurn: 0,
    definition: null,
    request: null,
    start: null,
    closed: null,
    activeStages: [],
    stageEntries: 0,
    status: null,
    waits: [],
    data: {},
    fired: [],
    faults: [],
    adminTurns: [],

export function sameWait(a: WaitId, b: WaitId): boolean {
  return a.element === b.element && a.activation === b.activation && a.key === b.key && a.seq === b.seq;
}

/** The instance with this exact ID, or undefined. */
export function findWait(state: RequestState, id: WaitId): WaitInstance | undefined {
  return state.waits.find((w) => sameWait(w.id, id));
}

/** Whether the instance with this exact ID is open (a closed request has none open). */
export function isWaitOpen(state: RequestState, id: WaitId): boolean {
  return findWait(state, id)?.status === "open";
}

/** The current instance of `(element, activation, key)`: the highest `seq` (spec section 2), or undefined. */
export function currentWait(state: RequestState, element: string, activation: string, key: string): WaitInstance | undefined {
  let found: WaitInstance | undefined;
  for (const w of state.waits) {
    if (w.id.element === element && w.id.activation === activation && w.id.key === key && (found === undefined || w.id.seq > found.id.seq)) {
      found = w;
    }
  }
  return found;
}

/** Every open instance, in open order. */
export function openWaits(state: RequestState): WaitInstance[] {
  return state.waits.filter((w) => w.status === "open");
}

/** Whether the transition has fired in this activation of its declaring stage. */
export function hasFired(state: RequestState, stage: string, activation: string, transition: string): boolean {
  return state.fired.some((f) => f.stage === stage && f.activation === activation && f.transition === transition);
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/stuck/authored-stage.ts\n===
/**
 * The authored stage of an engine stage, found through the definition's origin map (integrations.md section
 * 11.5). A definition with no origin map reports the engine stage itself.
 *
 * The origin of `stage:<engine stage>` names an authored item (its `item[0]`). That item is an authored
 * stage when it is the engine stage's own ID (an ending, or a hand-written stage), or when some engine
 * stage's origin names it with the part `tasks` or `arrows` (the steps a compiled stage runs its tasks and
 * its arrows in, compiler.md section 12). Otherwise it is a smaller item, such as an action that runs inside
 * a stage: the authored stage is then the first one found breadth-first along the transitions. A compiled
 * stage is left only through its own arrows step, so the first one found is the stage the action is in.
 * An item that is an arrow (Try it's step for an unfinished part, which has no transitions) is in the
 * stage that arrow leaves: the authored stage whose arrows step has a transition the arrow made.
 */
import type { PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { findStage, ROOT } from "../decide/definition.ts";

const STAGE_PARTS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["tasks", "arrows"]);

function originItem(def: PublishedDefinition, engineStage: string): { item: string; part: string | null } | undefined {
  const origin = def.origins[`stage:${engineStage}`];
  const item = origin?.item[0];
  return item === undefined ? undefined : { item, part: origin?.part ?? null };
}

/** The items the origin map names as authored stages. */
function authoredStages(def: PublishedDefinition): Set<string> {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const [key, origin] of Object.entries(def.origins)) {
    if (!key.startsWith("stage:") || key.includes("#")) continue;
    const item = origin.item[0];
    if (item === undefined) continue;
    if (STAGE_PARTS.has(origin.part ?? "") || item === key.slice("stage:".length)) out.add(item);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The authored stage whose arrows step has a transition made by the authored arrow `item`. */
function stageLeftBy(def: PublishedDefinition, item: string): string | undefined {
  for (const s of def.root.stages) {
    const o = originItem(def, s.id);
    if (o === undefined || o.part !== "arrows") continue;
    if (s.transitions.some((t) => def.origins[`transition:${s.id}.${t.id}`]?.item[0] === item)) return o.item;
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * The authored stage `engineStage` belongs to; the engine stage itself when the definition has no origin map
 * or the map does not name it; null for the root and for null.
 */
export function authoredStageOf(def: PublishedDefinition, engineStage: string | null): string | null {
  if (engineStage === null) return null;
  if (Object.keys(def.origins).length === 0) return engineStage;
  if (engineStage === ROOT) return null;
  const first = originItem(def, engineStage);
  if (first === undefined) return engineStage;
  const stages = authoredStages(def);
  if (stages.has(first.item)) return first.item;
  const seen = new Set<string>([engineStage]);
  const queue = [engineStage];
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const at = queue.shift() as string;
    for (const t of findStage(def, at)?.transitions ?? []) {
      if (seen.has(t.to)) continue;
      seen.add(t.to);
      const o = originItem(def, t.to);
      if (o !== undefined && stages.has(o.item)) return o.item;
      queue.push(t.to);
    }
  }
  return stageLeftBy(def, first.item) ?? first.item;
}

===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/stuck/stuck-state.ts\n===
/**
 * The stuck state a reader works out after a turn (kernel spec sections 3 and 7; integrations.md section
 * 11.5). It is never recorded and `decide` never reads it. The first row that applies:
 *
 * | State | reason |
 * |---|---|
 * | A fault not cleared, `error.code: call-failed` | `action-failed` |
 * | A fault not cleared, any other code | `error` |
 * | Nothing fits (`nothingFits`) | `nothing-fits` |
 * | An open obligation matches its `nobodyToAsk` rule | `nobody-to-ask` |
 *
 * `stage` is the engine stage: of the fault's element, of the active child stage for `nothing-fits`, of the
 * first matching wait in declared order for `nobody-to-ask`. A reader that reports it maps it with
 * `authoredStageOf`.
 */
import { isJsonObject, type Json, type NobodyToAskRule, type PersonWaitOpened, type PublishedDefinition } from "../../format/index.ts";
import { ROOT, splitElement } from "../decide/definition.ts";
import { currentWait, openWaits, type RequestState, type WaitInstance } from "../state.ts";

export type StuckStateReason = "action-failed" | "nobody-to-ask" | "nothing-fits" | "error";

export interface StuckState {
  reason: StuckStateReason;
  stage: string | null;
}

/**
 * Stuck with nothing that fits (spec section 3): open, no fault, and no open obligation and no open call.
 * A person wait that nobody is able to answer is still an open obligation.
 */
export function nothingFits(state: RequestState): boolean {
  if (state.request === null || state.closed !== null || state.faults.length > 0) return false;
  return !openWaits(state).some((w) => w.kind === "call" || (w.kind === "person" && w.role === "obligation"));
}

class ShapeError extends Error {}

function refId(v: Json | undefined, type: string): string | null {
  return isJsonObject(v) && v["type"] === type && typeof v["id"] === "string" ? v["id"] : null;
}

/** The Requester: `data.requester` when present, else `request.by` when it is a user. A `requester` that is not a user reference is a shape error. */
function requester(state: RequestState): string | null {
  if (Object.hasOwn(state.data, "requester")) {
    const fromData = refId(state.data["requester"], "user");
    if (fromData === null) throw new ShapeError("requester is not a user reference");
    return fromData;
  }
  return state.request?.by.type === "user" ? state.request.by.id : null;
}

/**
 * The members a membership read recorded for one group; [] after a failed read or for a group missing from
 * the result; null while unknown. An entry whose `id` is not a group reference is a shape error.
 */
function membersOf(read: WaitInstance | undefined, group: string): string[] | null {
  if (read === undefined || read.status !== "completed") return null;
  if (read.outcome !== "ok") return [];
  const groups = read.data?.["groups"];
  if (!Array.isArray(groups)) throw new ShapeError("groups is not a list");
  const ids = groups.map((g) => {
    const id = isJsonObject(g) ? refId(g["id"], "group") : null;
    if (id === null) throw new ShapeError("a groups entry has no group reference");
    return id;
  });
  const entry = groups[ids.indexOf(group)];
  if (entry === undefined) return [];
  const members = (entry as { members?: Json }).members;
  if (!Array.isArray(members)) throw new ShapeError("members is not a list");
  return members.map((m) => {
    const id = refId(m, "user");
    if (id === null) throw new ShapeError("a member is not a user reference");
    return id;
  });
}

/**
 * Whether nobody can answer an open person wait (E-24): the users asked directly plus the recorded members of
 * the groups asked, less the Requester when the rule excludes them, is empty. A group whose members are
 * unknown means no match. A rule that cannot be worked out counts as no match.
 */
export function nobodyToAsk(def: PublishedDefinition, state: RequestState, wait: WaitInstance): boolean {
  const rule: Pick<NobodyToAskRule, "members" | "excludeRequester"> = def.nobodyToAsk?.find((r) => r.wait === wait.id.element) ?? { members: null, excludeRequester: false };
  const opened = wait.opened as PersonWaitOpened;
  try {
    const people = new Set(opened.assignees.filter((a) => a.type === "user").map((a) => a.id));
    const read = rule.members === null ? undefined : currentWait(state, rule.members, wait.id.activation, "");
    for (const g of opened.assignees.filter((a) => a.type === "group")) {
      const members = rule.members === null ? null : membersOf(read, g.id);
      if (members === null) return false;
      for (const m of members) people.add(m);
    }
    const who = requester(state);
    if (rule.excludeRequester && who !== null) people.delete(who);
    return people.size === 0;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ShapeError) return false;
    throw error;
  }
}

/** The request's stuck state, or null when it is not stuck. A closed request is never stuck. */
export function stuckStateOf(def: PublishedDefinition, state: RequestState): StuckState | null {
  if (state.closed !== null) return null;
  const failed = state.faults.find((f) => f.error.code === "call-failed");
  if (failed !== undefined) return { reason: "action-failed", stage: splitElement(failed.element).stage };
  const other = state.faults[0];
  if (other !== undefined) return { reason: "error", stage: splitElement(other.element).stage };
  if (nothingFits(state)) return { reason: "nothing-fits", stage: state.activeStages.find((s) => s.stage !== ROOT)?.stage ?? null };
  for (const stage of def.root.stages) {
    const active = state.activeStages.find((s) => s.stage === stage.id);
    if (active === undefined) continue;
    for (const w of stage.waits) {
      const instance = currentWait(state, `${stage.id}.${w.id}`, active.activation, "");
      if (instance?.status === "open" && instance.kind === "person" && instance.role === "obligation" && nobodyToAsk(def, state, instance)) {
        return { reason: "nobody-to-ask", stage: stage.id };
      }
    }
  }
  return null;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/kernel/turn.ts\n===
/**
 * One turn on its own (kernel spec section 3; E-26): validate the input against the state, decide, and fold
 * the events with evolve. The server and every host run this one function, so they record the same events
 * and reach the same state. The stuck state is worked out from that state (`stuck/`), never recorded.
 *
 * Not part of it: the call-result check (`validateCallResult`), which runs before the turn, and the lookups
 * the caller makes before it takes the request's lock (`lookupsToMake`).
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, PublishedDefinition } from "../format/index.ts";
import { decide } from "./decide/decide.ts";
import type { DecideContext, DecideInput, DropReason, KernelRefusal, TraceEntry } from "./decide/types.ts";
import { evolve } from "./evolve.ts";
import type { RequestState } from "./state.ts";

export type TurnResult =
  /** Accepted: the events to append, in order, and the state they fold to. `events` is [] for a dropped result. */
  | { ok: true; events: AnyEventRecord[]; state: RequestState; trace: TraceEntry[]; dropped: DropReason | null }
  /** Refused: nothing is appended and the state is unchanged. */
  | { ok: false; refusals: KernelRefusal[]; state: RequestState };

export function turn(definition: PublishedDefinition, state: RequestState, input: DecideInput, context: DecideContext): TurnResult {
  const result = decide(definition, state, input, context);
  if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, refusals: result.refusals, state };
  let next = state;
  for (const event of result.events) next = evolve(next, event);
  return { ok: true, events: result.events, state: next, trace: result.trace, dropped: result.dropped };
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/schema/equal.ts\n===
/**
 * JSON equality by value, as `enum`, `const` and `uniqueItems` compare (definition-format.md section 6):
 * object key order does not matter; numbers compare by value, so 1 and 1.0 are equal.
 */
export function jsonEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (a === b) return true;
  if (Array.isArray(a)) {
    return Array.isArray(b) && a.length === b.length && a.every((x, i) => jsonEqual(x, b[i]));
  }
  if (a === null || b === null || typeof a !== "object" || typeof b !== "object" || Array.isArray(b)) return false;
  const ka = Object.keys(a);
  const kb = Object.keys(b);
  if (ka.length !== kb.length) return false;
  const ob = b as Record<string, unknown>;
  const oa = a as Record<string, unknown>;
  return ka.every((k) => Object.hasOwn(ob, k) && jsonEqual(oa[k], ob[k]));
}

/**
 * The formats jsonschema-1 asserts (definition-format.md section 6). Written out, not taken from `Date`,
 * so the result is the same in every JavaScript engine.
 */
import type { SchemaFormat } from "./types.ts";

function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
  if (month === 2) return (year % 4 === 0 && year % 100 !== 0) || year % 400 === 0 ? 29 : 28;
  return [4, 6, 9, 11].includes(month) ? 30 : 31;
}

function realDate(year: number, month: number, day: number): boolean {
  return month >= 1 && month <= 12 && day >= 1 && day <= daysInMonth(year, month);
}

const DATE = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/;

/** `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date. */
export function isDate(s: string): boolean {
  const m = DATE.exec(s);
  return m !== null && realDate(Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]), Number(m[3]));
}

const DATE_TIME = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[Tt](\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:\.\d+)?(?:[Zz]|([+-])(\d{2}):(\d{2}))$/;

/**
 * RFC 3339 `date-time`: the offset (`Z` or `+hh:mm`) is mandatory. A leap second (`:60`) is refused, as cel-1's
 * `timestamp()` refuses it (E-26), so every value the schema accepts can be read in an expression.
 */
export function isDateTime(s: string): boolean {
  const m = DATE_TIME.exec(s);
  if (m === null) return false;
  const [hour, minute, second] = [Number(m[4]), Number(m[5]), Number(m[6])];
  if (!realDate(Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]), Number(m[3]))) return false;
  if (hour > 23 || minute > 59 || second > 59) return false;
  if (m[7] !== undefined && (Number(m[8]) > 23 || Number(m[9]) > 59)) return false;
  return true;
}

/**
 * The directory's immutable object ID. Its pattern is unknown (it depends on the existing application,
 * definition-format.md section 12 item 6); until it is known: 1 to 255 characters, none of them whitespace
 * or a control character.
 */
export function isDirectoryObjectId(s: string): boolean {
  return s.length >= 1 && s.length <= 255 && !/[\s\p{Cc}]/u.test(s);
}

export function matchesFormat(format: SchemaFormat, s: string): boolean {
  switch (format) {
    case "date":
      return isDate(s);
    case "date-time":
      return isDateTime(s);
    case "directory-object-id":
      return isDirectoryObjectId(s);
  }
}

===\nengine/packages/core/src/schema/profile.ts\n===
/**
 * checkSchemaProfile: is a schema within profile jsonschema-1 (definition-format.md section 6)?
 * Any keyword or format outside the profile is refused (a publish error), and so is a keyword whose value
 * is not what 2020-12 allows for it. A schema holds no null and no key starting with `$` (section 1).
 */
import { jsonEqual } from "./equal.ts";
import { pointerChild } from "./pointer.ts";
import { SCHEMA_FORMATS, SCHEMA_KEYWORDS, SCHEMA_TYPES, type SchemaProfileProblem } from "./types.ts";

type Out = SchemaProfileProblem[];

function isObject(v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> {
  return v !== null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);
}

function isNonNegativeInteger(v: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof v === "number" && Number.isSafeInteger(v) && v >= 0;
}

/** JSON with no null (an `enum` member or a `const`). */
function isJsonNoNull(v: unknown): boolean {
  if (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "boolean") return true;
  if (typeof v === "number") return Number.isFinite(v);
  if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.every(isJsonNoNull);
  if (isObject(v)) return Object.entries(v).every(([k, x]) => !k.startsWith("$") && isJsonNoNull(x));
  return false;
}

function isTypeName(v: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof v === "string" && (SCHEMA_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(v);
}

function distinct(values: unknown[]): boolean {
  return values.every((x, i) => values.findIndex((y) => jsonEqual(x, y)) === i);
}

function bad(out: Out, pointer: string): void {
  out.push({ pointer, code: "invalid-keyword-value" });
}

/** A subschema where 2020-12 allows a boolean too (`additionalProperties`, `items`). */
function schemaOrBoolean(v: unknown, p: string, out: Out): void {
  if (typeof v !== "boolean") schema(v, p, out);
}

function keyword(name: string, v: unknown, p: string, out: Out): void {
  switch (name) {
    case "type":
      if (isTypeName(v)) return;
      if (Array.isArray(v) && v.length > 0 && v.every(isTypeName) && distinct(v)) return;
      return bad(out, p);
    case "properties":
      if (!isObject(v)) return bad(out, p);
      for (const [prop, sub] of Object.entries(v)) {
        if (prop.startsWith("$")) bad(out, pointerChild(p, prop));
        else schema(sub, pointerChild(p, prop), out);
      }
      return;
    case "required":
      if (!Array.isArray(v) || !v.every((x) => typeof x === "string") || !distinct(v)) bad(out, p);
      return;
    case "additionalProperties":
    case "items":
      return schemaOrBoolean(v, p, out);
    case "uniqueItems":
      if (typeof v !== "boolean") bad(out, p);
      return;
    case "enum":
      if (!Array.isArray(v) || v.length === 0 || !v.every(isJsonNoNull) || !distinct(v)) bad(out, p);
      return;
    case "const":
      if (!isJsonNoNull(v)) bad(out, p);
      return;
    case "format":
      if (typeof v !== "string") return bad(out, p);
      if (!(SCHEMA_FORMATS as readonly string[]).includes(v)) out.push({ pointer: p, code: "format-not-in-profile" });
      return;
    case "minLength":
    case "maxLength":
      if (!isNonNegativeInteger(v)) bad(out, p);
      return;
  }
}

function schema(v: unknown, p: string, out: Out): void {
  if (!isObject(v)) {
    out.push({ pointer: p, code: "not-a-schema" });
    return;
  }
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(v)) {
    const at = pointerChild(p, name);
    if (!(SCHEMA_KEYWORDS as readonly string[]).includes(name)) {
      out.push({ pointer: at, code: "keyword-not-in-profile" });
      continue;
    }
    keyword(name, value, at, out);
  }
}

/** Every way `value` falls outside jsonschema-1; [] when it is a schema of the profile. */
export function checkSchemaProfile(value: unknown): SchemaProfileProblem[] {
  const out: Out = [];
  schema(value, "", out);
  return out;
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/schema/types.ts\n===
/**
 * The vocabulary of profile jsonschema-1 (definition-format.md section 6) and of its failures.
 */

/** The keywords of jsonschema-1, and no other. */
export type SchemaKeyword =
  | "type"
  | "properties"
  | "required"
  | "additionalProperties"
  | "items"
  | "uniqueItems"
  | "enum"
  | "const"
  | "format"
  | "minLength"
  | "maxLength";

export const SCHEMA_KEYWORDS: readonly SchemaKeyword[] = [
  "type",
  "properties",
  "required",
  "additionalProperties",
  "items",
  "uniqueItems",
  "enum",
  "const",
  "format",
  "minLength",
  "maxLength",
];

/** The formats jsonschema-1 asserts, and no other. */
export type SchemaFormat = "date" | "date-time" | "directory-object-id";
export const SCHEMA_FORMATS: readonly SchemaFormat[] = ["date", "date-time", "directory-object-id"];

/** The JSON types a `type` keyword may name. `null` is not one: no data value holds null (spec section 2, Values). */
export type SchemaType = "string" | "number" | "integer" | "boolean" | "object" | "array";
export const SCHEMA_TYPES: readonly SchemaType[] = ["string", "number", "integer", "boolean", "object", "array"];

/** contract/core-api.md section 2.6: the rule of an `invalid-data` refusal. Closed list there; open for a minor version. */
export type InvalidDataRule =
  | "required"
  | "wrong-kind"
  | "not-a-choice"
  | "too-long"
  | "too-short"
  | "out-of-range"
  | "bad-format"
  | "unknown-question"
  | "hidden-answered";

/** One way the data fails its schema. */
export interface SchemaFailure {
  /** RFC 6901 pointer into the data; for `required`, the pointer of the missing property. */
  pointer: string;
  /** The keyword that failed; null for a rule of the profile itself (a null or non-JSON value, an integer beyond +/-(2^53 - 1), a key starting with `$`). */
  keyword: SchemaKeyword | null;
  rule: InvalidDataRule;
}

/** One way a schema falls outside the profile. Codes are kebab-case. */
export interface SchemaProfileProblem {
  /** RFC 6901 pointer into the schema. */
  pointer: string;
  code: "not-a-schema" | "keyword-not-in-profile" | "format-not-in-profile" | "invalid-keyword-value";
}
===\nengine/packages/core/src/schema/validate.ts\n===
/**
 * validateBySchema: the validator of profile jsonschema-1 (definition-format.md section 6).
 * 2020-12 semantics for the profile's keywords only; no coercion, no removal of unknown properties,
 * no defaults: the data is never changed. Written here, not taken from a library: the profile is pinned per
 * definition format for good, and it must run in a browser without code generation.
 *
 * Every failure is returned, with a pointer into the data, the keyword and its InvalidDataRule
 * (contract/core-api.md section 2.6). Once a value has the wrong kind (`type`, or a profile rule), the other
 * keywords on that value are not reported: they would repeat the same fault.
 */
import { matchesFormat } from "./formats.ts";
import { jsonEqual } from "./equal.ts";
import { pointerChild } from "./pointer.ts";
import { checkSchemaProfile } from "./profile.ts";
import type { InvalidDataRule, SchemaFailure, SchemaFormat, SchemaKeyword, SchemaProfileProblem, SchemaType } from "./types.ts";

/** Thrown when a schema outside the profile is used for validation: publish refuses such a schema, so this is a bug. */
export class SchemaProfileError extends Error {
  readonly problems: SchemaProfileProblem[];
  constructor(problems: SchemaProfileProblem[]) {
    super(`schema is not within jsonschema-1: ${problems.map((p) => `${p.pointer || "(root)"} ${p.code}`).join(", ")}`);
    this.name = "SchemaProfileError";
    this.problems = problems;
  }
}

/** A schema as the validator reads it, after checkSchemaProfile accepted it. */
interface Schema {
  type?: SchemaType | SchemaType[];
  properties?: Record<string, Schema>;
  required?: string[];
  additionalProperties?: Schema | boolean;
  items?: Schema | boolean;
  uniqueItems?: boolean;
  enum?: unknown[];
  const?: unknown;
  format?: SchemaFormat;
  minLength?: number;
  maxLength?: number;
}

type Out = SchemaFailure[];

const MAX_EXACT = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; // 2^53 - 1

function fail(out: Out, pointer: string, keyword: SchemaKeyword | null, rule: InvalidDataRule): void {
  out.push({ pointer, keyword, rule });
}

function isPlainObject(v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> {
  if (v === null || typeof v !== "object" || Array.isArray(v)) return false;
  const proto: unknown = Object.getPrototypeOf(v);
  return proto === Object.prototype || proto === null;
}

function hasType(v: unknown, type: SchemaType): boolean {
  switch (type) {
    case "string":
      return typeof v === "string";
    case "number":
      return typeof v === "number";
    case "integer":
      return typeof v === "number" && Number.isInteger(v);
    case "boolean":
      return typeof v === "boolean";
    case "object":
      return isPlainObject(v);
    case "array":
      return Array.isArray(v);
  }
}

/**
 * The profile's own rules, whatever the schema says. Returns false when the value cannot be read further.
 * - Null, and anything that is not JSON, is never data (spec section 2, Values: the engine never writes null).
 * - An integral number beyond +/-(2^53 - 1) is refused (definition-format.md section 6, Numbers).
 */
function profileRules(v: unknown, p: string, out: Out): boolean {
  if (typeof v === "number") {
    if (!Number.isFinite(v)) return (fail(out, p, null, "wrong-kind"), false);
    if (Number.isInteger(v) && Math.abs(v) > MAX_EXACT) return (fail(out, p, null, "out-of-range"), false);
    return true;
  }
  if (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "boolean" || Array.isArray(v) || isPlainObject(v)) return true;
  fail(out, p, null, "wrong-kind");
  return false;
}

/** Minimum and maximum length count Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units. */
function codePoints(s: string): number {
  return Array.from(s).length;
}

function validateObject(s: Schema, v: Record<string, unknown>, p: string, out: Out): void {
  for (const name of s.required ?? []) {
    if (!Object.hasOwn(v, name)) fail(out, pointerChild(p, name), "required", "required");
  }
  for (const [key, x] of Object.entries(v)) {
    const at = pointerChild(p, key);
    // No data key starts with `$` (spec section 2, Values).
    if (key.startsWith("$")) {
      fail(out, at, null, "wrong-kind");
      continue;
    }
    const declared = s.properties !== undefined && Object.hasOwn(s.properties, key) ? s.properties[key] : undefined;
    if (declared !== undefined) {
      validate(declared, x, at, out);
      continue;
    }
    const extra = s.additionalProperties;
    // At the top level a key the schema does not have is an answer to no question; inside an answer it is
    // a field that answer does not have, so the answer has the wrong kind (E-27).
    if (extra === false) fail(out, at, "additionalProperties", p === "" ? "unknown-question" : "wrong-kind");
    else if (extra !== undefined && extra !== true) validate(extra, x, at, out);
    else profileAll(x, at, out);
  }
}

function validateArray(s: Schema, v: unknown[], p: string, out: Out): void {
  v.forEach((x, i) => {
    const at = pointerChild(p, i);
    if (s.items === false) fail(out, at, "items", "wrong-kind");
    else if (s.items !== undefined && s.items !== true) validate(s.items, x, at, out);
    else profileAll(x, at, out);
  });
  if (s.uniqueItems === true) {
    v.forEach((x, i) => {
      if (v.findIndex((y) => jsonEqual(x, y)) < i) fail(out, pointerChild(p, i), "uniqueItems", "wrong-kind");
    });
  }
}

/** A value under no schema (an undeclared property allowed by default): only the profile's own rules apply. */
function profileAll(v: unknown, p: string, out: Out): void {
  validate({}, v, p, out);
}

function validate(s: Schema, v: unknown, p: string, out: Out): void {
  if (!profileRules(v, p, out)) return;
  if (s.type !== undefined) {
    const types = Array.isArray(s.type) ? s.type : [s.type];
    if (!types.some((t) => hasType(v, t))) return fail(out, p, "type", "wrong-kind");
  }
  if (Object.hasOwn(s, "const") && !jsonEqual(v, s.const)) fail(out, p, "const", "wrong-kind");
  if (s.enum !== undefined && !s.enum.some((x) => jsonEqual(v, x))) fail(out, p, "enum", "not-a-choice");
  if (typeof v === "string") {
    if (s.format !== undefined && !matchesFormat(s.format, v)) fail(out, p, "format", "bad-format");
    if (s.minLength !== undefined && codePoints(v) < s.minLength) fail(out, p, "minLength", "too-short");
    if (s.maxLength !== undefined && codePoints(v) > s.maxLength) fail(out, p, "maxLength", "too-long");
  }
  if (Array.isArray(v)) validateArray(s, v, p, out);
  else if (isPlainObject(v)) validateObject(s, v, p, out);
}

/**
 * Every way `data` fails `schema`; [] when it is valid. `schema` must be within jsonschema-1
 * (checkSchemaProfile); a schema outside it throws SchemaProfileError rather than be read in part.
 */
export function validateBySchema(schema: unknown, data: unknown): SchemaFailure[] {
  const problems = checkSchemaProfile(schema);
  if (problems.length > 0) throw new SchemaProfileError(problems);
  const out: Out = [];
  validate(schema as Schema, data, "", out);
  return out;
}
