/**
 * engine/spec/kernel/replay-only.yaml: every case, translated to event JSON and folded by evolve. Each case's
 * expectState is asserted, and the fields the cases name in `needs` that expectState alone does not read.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { fold, type RequestState } from "../../src/kernel/index.ts";
import { loadReplayCases } from "./cases/load.ts";
import { stateMismatches } from "./cases/state-match.ts";
import { createTranslator } from "./cases/translate.ts";

const cases = loadReplayCases();

function replay(id: string): RequestState {
  const c = cases.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (c === undefined) throw new Error(`no case ${id}`);
  return fold(createTranslator().history(c.history));
}

describe("replay-only.yaml", () => {
  it("has the cases R1, R2, R4 and R10", () => {
    expect(cases.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual(["R1", "R2", "R4", "R10"]);
  });

  for (const c of cases) {
    it(`${c.id}: ${c.name}`, () => {
      const events = createTranslator().history(c.history);
      const state = fold(events);
      expect(stateMismatches(state, c.expectState)).toEqual([]);
    });
  }

  it("R1: the active stages are a set, and leaving one leaves its sibling and its parent active", () => {
    expect(replay("R1").activeStages.map((s) => s.activation)).toEqual(["a1", "a3"]);
  });

  it("R2: a second instance of a wait is its own instance", () => {
    const items = replay("R2").waits.filter((w) => w.id.element === "PendingApproval.items");
    expect(items.map((w) => [w.id.key, w.id.seq, w.status])).toEqual([
      ["", 1, "completed"],
      ["", 2, "open"],
    ]);
  });

  it("R10: a start by a connection's event keeps the trigger, the connection as starter, and the stage names", () => {
    const state = replay("R10");
    expect(state.request?.by).toEqual({ type: "connection", id: "helpdesk" });
    expect(state.fired).toEqual([{ stage: "Request", activation: "a2", transition: "t_submit", seq: 6 }]);
    const form = state.waits[0];
    expect(form?.by).toEqual({ type: "connection", id: "helpdesk" });
    expect((form?.opened as { assignees: unknown }).assignees).toEqual([]);
  });
});
===\nengine/packages/core/test/kernel/stuck-fuzz.test.ts\n===
/**
 * The stuck state over random turn sequences (kernel spec v2.20 section 3; integrations.md section 11.5), on
 * the demo definition, on compiled fixtures and on a small maze that reaches every reason. After every turn:
 *
 * - the stuck state is the spec's definition, worked out here from the state on its own: closed is never
 *   stuck; a fault is `action-failed` (a failed call) or `error`; open with no fault and no open obligation
 *   and no open call is `nothing-fits`; else an open obligation nobody can answer is `nobody-to-ask`;
 * - nothing is recorded for it: every event is of a stored type;
 * - a notification rule on `Stuck` sends exactly when the state after the turn is stuck and differs from the
 *   state before it, and the outbound `request.stuck@1` and `request.unstuck@1` follow the same change.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { EVENT_TYPES, type AnyEventRecord, type NotificationRule, type PublishedDefinition, type WaitId } from "../../src/format/index.ts";
import { emptyState, evolve, openWaits, turn, type DecideInput, type RequestState } from "../../src/kernel/index.ts";
import { matchNotifications, outboundEvents } from "../../src/kernel/notify/index.ts";
import { nobodyToAsk, stuckStateOf, type StuckState } from "../../src/kernel/stuck/index.ts";
import { fixture } from "../authored/fixtures.ts";
import { Compiled, KernelRun, PEOPLE, pickWith, random, randomAnswers } from "../authored/host/walk.ts";
import { adminAction, dataValue, isRecord, parseBy, parseWait } from "./cases/notation.ts";
import { expandTurns, loadExampleDefinition, loadWorkflowCases } from "./cases/workflow-cases.ts";
import { call, definition as definitionOf, final, outcome, person, rita, stage, when } from "./decide/build.ts";

const FUZZ_RULE: NotificationRule = { id: "n_fuzz_stuck", on: { event: "Stuck", element: null }, when: "true", send: { message: { words: "request.stuck" }, to: [{ type: "workflowAdmins" }] } };

/** The definition with one more rule on Stuck, so every definition walked has one. */
const withStuckRule = (def: PublishedDefinition): PublishedDefinition => ({ ...def, notifications: [...def.notifications, FUZZ_RULE] });

/** The spec's stuck state, worked out from the state alone (not with `nothingFits`). */
function expected(def: PublishedDefinition, s: RequestState): StuckState | null {
  if (s.closed !== null) return null;
  if (s.faults.length > 0) {
    const failed = s.faults.find((f) => f.error.code === "call-failed");
    const f = failed ?? s.faults[0];
    return { reason: failed === undefined ? "error" : "action-failed", stage: f?.element.split(".")[0] ?? null };
  }
  const open = openWaits(s);
  const obligations = open.filter((w) => w.kind === "person" && w.role === "obligation");
  if (!open.some((w) => w.kind === "call") && obligations.length === 0) {
    return { reason: "nothing-fits", stage: s.activeStages.find((a) => a.stage !== "root")?.stage ?? null };
  }
  const order = def.root.stages.flatMap((st) => st.waits.map((w) => `${st.id}.${w.id}`));
  const nobody = obligations.filter((w) => nobodyToAsk(def, s, w)).sort((a, b) => order.indexOf(a.id.element) - order.indexOf(b.id.element))[0];
  return nobody === undefined ? null : { reason: "nobody-to-ask", stage: nobody.id.element.split(".")[0] ?? null };
}

const same = (a: StuckState | null, b: StuckState | null): boolean => JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);

/** How often the walks saw each reason and each change, so a walk that never reaches one is noticed. */
const seen: Record<string, number> = {};
const count = (k: string): void => {
  seen[k] = (seen[k] ?? 0) + 1;
};

/** Checks every turn of a request's events; returns the first disagreement, or null. */
function checkTurns(def: PublishedDefinition, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]): string | null {
  let before = emptyState();
  let i = 0;
  while (i < events.length) {
    const t = events[i]?.turn;
    const turnEvents: AnyEventRecord[] = [];
    while (i < events.length && events[i]?.turn === t) turnEvents.push(events[i++] as AnyEventRecord);
    let after = before;
    for (const e of turnEvents) {
      if (!EVENT_TYPES.includes(e.type)) return `turn ${t}: an event of type ${e.type} was recorded`;
      after = evolve(after, e);
    }
    const was = stuckStateOf(def, before);
    const is = stuckStateOf(def, after);
    const want = expected(def, after);
    const where = `turn ${t} (${turnEvents.map((e) => e.type).join(",")})`;
    if (!same(is, want)) return `${where}: stuck ${JSON.stringify(is)}, the spec says ${JSON.stringify(want)}`;
    count(is === null ? "none" : is.reason);
    const changed = is !== null && !same(was, is);
    if (changed) count(was === null ? "became stuck" : "changed while stuck");
    if (was !== null && is === null) count("unstuck");

    const fired = matchNotifications(def, before, turnEvents, after).messages.filter((m) => m.rule === FUZZ_RULE.id);
    if (fired.length !== (changed ? 1 : 0)) return `${where}: the Stuck rule sent ${fired.length} messages; the state went ${JSON.stringify(was)} -> ${JSON.stringify(is)}`;
    if (changed && JSON.stringify((fired[0]?.event.payload as { reason: string }).reason) !== JSON.stringify(is.reason)) return `${where}: the Stuck message names another reason`;

    const out = outboundEvents(def, before, turnEvents, after).events.map((e) => e.body.type);
    const late = turnEvents[0]?.type === "CallResultLate";
    if (late && !same(was, is)) return `${where}: a late result changed the stuck state`;
    const stuckOut = out.filter((x) => x === "request.stuck@1").length;
    const unstuckOut = out.filter((x) => x === "request.unstuck@1").length;
    if (!late && stuckOut !== (changed ? 1 : 0)) return `${where}: ${stuckOut} request.stuck@1 events`;
    if (!late && unstuckOut !== (was !== null && is === null ? 1 : 0)) return `${where}: ${unstuckOut} request.unstuck@1 events`;
    before = after;
  }
  return null;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the demo definition

const demo = withStuckRule(loadExampleDefinition("change-request-demo"));

type Template =
  | { kind: "start"; input: DecideInput }
  | { kind: "aimed"; element: string; build: (wait: WaitId) => DecideInput }
  | { kind: "admin"; input: DecideInput };

/** Every input of every demo case, as a template that can be aimed at the instance open now. */
function demoTemplates(): Template[] {
  const out: Template[] = [];
  const { cases } = loadWorkflowCases("change-request-demo");
  for (const c of cases) {
    for (const t of expandTurns(c, cases)) {
      const [kind, body] = Object.entries(t.input ?? {})[0] ?? [];
      if (!isRecord(body)) continue;
      const data = (v: unknown) => dataValue(v ?? {}, true) as Record<string, never>;
      if (kind === "start") {
        const i = body["input"] as Record<string, unknown>;
        out.push({ kind: "start", input: { kind: "start", requestId: "req-1", readableId: 1, by: parseBy(body["by"]), outcome: String(i["outcome"]), data: data(i["data"]), trigger: null } });
      } else if (kind === "act") {
        const by = parseBy(body["by"]);
        const o = String(body["outcome"]);
        const d = data(body["data"]);
        out.push({ kind: "aimed", element: parseWait(body["wait"]).element, build: (wait) => ({ kind: "act", by, wait, outcome: o, data: d }) });
      } else if (kind === "callResult") {
        const o = body["outcome"] as "ok" | "failed";
        const d = data(body["data"]);
        out.push({ kind: "aimed", element: parseWait(body["wait"]).element, build: (wait) => ({ kind: "callResult", wait, outcome: o, data: d }) });
      } else if (kind === "admin") {
        out.push({ kind: "admin", input: { kind: "admin", by: parseBy(body["by"]), reason: "x", actions: (body["actions"] as unknown[]).map((a) => adminAction(a)) } });
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

const at = (n: number): string => new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 15, 9, 30, 0) + n * 1000).toISOString().replace("Z", "000Z");

function demoWalk(seed: number, steps: number, all: Template[]): AnyEventRecord[] {
  const rnd = random(seed);
  const pick = pickWith(rnd);
  const starts = all.filter((t) => t.kind === "start");
  const first = turn(demo, emptyState(), pick(starts).input as DecideInput, { at: at(0), memberships: { groups: [] }, lookups: {} });
  if (!first.ok) return [];
  let state = first.state;
  const events = [...first.events];
  for (let i = 1; i <= steps && state.closed === null; i++) {
    const open = state.waits.filter((w) => w.status === "open");
    const ended = state.waits.filter((w) => w.status !== "open" && w.kind === "call");
    const choices: (() => DecideInput)[] = all.flatMap((t) => {
      if (t.kind === "admin") return [() => t.input];
      if (t.kind !== "aimed") return [];
      const w = open.find((x) => x.id.element === t.element);
      return w === undefined ? [] : [() => t.build(w.id)];
    });
    for (const w of open.filter((x) => x.kind === "call")) choices.push(() => ({ kind: "callResult", wait: w.id, outcome: "failed", data: { code: "down", message: "" } }));
    for (const w of ended) choices.push(() => ({ kind: "callResult", wait: w.id, outcome: "ok", data: {} }));
    const r = turn(demo, state, pick(choices)(), { at: at(i), memberships: { groups: ["grp-a", "grp-d-leads", "grp-b"] }, lookups: {}, isAdmin: true });
    if (!r.ok) continue;
    state = r.state;
    events.push(...r.events);
  }
  return events;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ a maze that reaches every reason

/**
 * Only an option open (nothing fits), an option that moves on or back into the same stage, a call that
 * faults, a Set that errors, a task nobody is asked (nobody to ask), and an ending.
 */
const maze: PublishedDefinition = withStuckRule(
  definitionOf({
    stages: [
      stage("Start", { waits: [person("form")], transitions: [when("t_go", "true", "Idle")] }),
      stage("Idle", {
        waits: [person("nudge", { role: "option", outcomes: [outcome("work"), outcome("again"), outcome("fetch"), outcome("boom"), outcome("lonely")] })],
        transitions: [
          when("t_work", "waits.nudge.outcome == 'work'", "Work"),
          when("t_again", "waits.nudge.outcome == 'again'", "Idle"),
          when("t_fetch", "waits.nudge.outcome == 'fetch'", "Fetch"),
          when("t_boom", "waits.nudge.outcome == 'boom'", "Idle", [{ path: ["n"], expr: "1 / 0" }]),
          when("t_lonely", "waits.nudge.outcome == 'lonely'", "Lonely"),
        ],
      }),
      stage("Fetch", { waits: [call("get", { onFailure: "fault" })], transitions: [when("t_got", "waits.get.outcome == 'ok'", "Idle")] }),
      stage("Lonely", { waits: [person("nobody", { assignees: "[]" }), person("leave", { role: "option" })], transitions: [when("t_leave", "waits.leave.outcome == 'done'", "Idle")] }),
      stage("Work", {
        waits: [person("task", { outcomes: [outcome("done"), outcome("finish"), outcome("nothing")] })],
        transitions: [when("t_done", "waits.task.outcome == 'done'", "Idle"), when("t_finish", "waits.task.outcome == 'finish'", "Done")],
      }),
      final("Done"),
    ],
  }),
);

function mazeWalk(seed: number, steps: number): AnyEventRecord[] {
  const rnd = random(seed);
  const pick = pickWith(rnd);
  const first = turn(maze, emptyState(), { kind: "start", requestId: "req-1", readableId: 1, by: rita, outcome: "done", data: {}, trigger: null }, { at: at(0) });
  if (!first.ok) throw new Error("the maze does not start");
  let state = first.state;
  const events = [...first.events];
  for (let i = 1; i <= steps && state.closed === null; i++) {
    const choices: DecideInput[] = [];
    for (const w of state.waits) {
      if (w.opened.kind === "person") for (const o of w.opened.outcomes) choices.push({ kind: "act", by: rita, wait: w.id, outcome: o.id, data: {} });
      if (w.opened.kind === "call") {
        choices.push({ kind: "callResult", wait: w.id, outcome: "ok", data: {} });
        choices.push({ kind: "callResult", wait: w.id, outcome: "failed", data: { code: "down", message: "" } });
      }
    }
    if (rnd() < 0.2) choices.push({ kind: "admin", by: rita, reason: "x", actions: [{ type: "retry" }] });
    if (rnd() < 0.03) choices.push({ kind: "admin", by: rita, reason: "x", actions: [{ type: "close" }] });
    const r = turn(maze, state, pick(choices), { at: at(i), isAdmin: true });
    if (!r.ok) continue;
    state = r.state;
    events.push(...r.events);
  }
  return events;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ compiled fixtures

const ADMIN = "dir-user-admin";
const PRIYA = "dir-user-priya-raman";

/** A walk on a compiled fixture as Try it runs it: calls answered by the fakes, random answers, retry and close. */
function compiledWalk(name: "change-request" | "integrated-sample" | "several-at-once", seed: number, steps: number): { def: PublishedDefinition; events: AnyEventRecord[] } {
  const rnd = random(seed);
  const pick = pickWith(rnd);
  // On every other seed of the integrated sample the deploy fails, and so does the issue that follows it.
  const failing = name === "integrated-sample" && seed % 2 === 1;
  const c = new Compiled(fixture(name), failing ? { calls: { "deploy.runPipeline@1": { mode: "fail", error: { code: "tests-failed" } }, "jira.createIssue@1": { mode: "fail", error: { code: "permission-denied" } } } } : {});
  // The kernel reads only the definition; the rule on Stuck is added to what the run uses.
  (c as { def: PublishedDefinition }).def = withStuckRule(c.def);
  const run = new KernelRun(c, 1, { seconds: 0 });
  const start = c.r.startTask() ?? "";
  for (let i = 0; i < 50 && run.state.request === null; i++) {
    const button = pick(c.s.ix.taskById.get(start)?.buttons ?? [])?.id ?? "";
    const { input, context } = run.startInput(PRIYA, button, randomAnswers(c, start, rnd, {}, 0));
    run.apply(input, context);
  }
  for (let step = 0; step < steps && run.state.closed === null && run.state.request !== null; step++) {
    const open = run.state.waits.filter((w) => w.status === "open" && w.kind === "person");
    if (rnd() < 0.15 || open.length === 0) {
      const action = rnd() < 0.8 ? "retry" : "close";
      run.apply({ kind: "admin", by: { type: "user", id: ADMIN }, reason: "x", actions: [{ type: action }] }, { isAdmin: true });
      continue;
    }
    const w = pick(open);
    const task = c.r.taskOf(w.id.element) ?? "";
    const button = pick((w.opened.kind === "person" ? w.opened.outcomes : []).map((o) => o.id));
    const { input, context } = run.actInput(pick([PRIYA, ...PEOPLE]), w.id, button, randomAnswers(c, task, rnd, {}, 0.1));
    run.apply(input, context);
  }
  return { def: c.def, events: run.events };
}

describe("the stuck state over random turns (spec v2.20)", () => {
  it("on the demo definition and the maze: the spec's definition after every turn, and Stuck fires exactly when it changes", () => {
    const all = demoTemplates();
    expect(new Set(all.map((t) => t.kind))).toEqual(new Set(["start", "aimed", "admin"]));
    const failures: string[] = [];
    for (let seed = 1; seed <= 200 && failures.length === 0; seed++) {
      const f = checkTurns(demo, demoWalk(seed, 40, all)) ?? checkTurns(maze, mazeWalk(seed, 60));
      if (f !== null) failures.push(`seed ${seed}: ${f}`);
    }
    expect(failures).toEqual([]);
    for (const k of ["action-failed", "error", "nothing-fits", "nobody-to-ask", "became stuck", "changed while stuck", "unstuck"]) expect(seen[k] ?? 0, `${k}: ${JSON.stringify(seen)}`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  for (const name of ["change-request", "integrated-sample", "several-at-once"] as const) {
    it(`on the compiled ${name}: the same after every turn`, () => {
      const failures: string[] = [];
      let stuck = 0;
      for (let seed = 1; seed <= 25 && failures.length === 0; seed++) {
        const { def, events } = compiledWalk(name, seed, 30);
        const before = seen["became stuck"] ?? 0;
        const f = checkTurns(def, events);
        if (f !== null) failures.push(`seed ${seed}: ${f}`);
        stuck += (seen["became stuck"] ?? 0) - before;
      }
      expect(failures).toEqual([]);
      expect(stuck).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    });
  }
});

/**
 * authoredStageOf (integrations.md section 11.5, E-27): the authored stage of an engine stage through the
 * definition's origin map; the engine stage itself when there is no origin map. Checked on a hand-built
 * chain, on the hand-written demo, and for every engine stage of the compiled fixtures against the stage
 * the authored document puts the origin's item in.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { compile } from "../../../src/authored/compile/index.ts";
import type { AuthoredWorkflow } from "../../../src/authored/contract/authored-format.ts";
import { indexDocument } from "../../../src/authored/index-doc.ts";
import type { PublishedDefinition } from "../../../src/format/index.ts";
import { authoredStageOf } from "../../../src/kernel/stuck/index.ts";
import { catalogue, fixture } from "../../authored/fixtures.ts";
import { loadExampleDefinition } from "../cases/workflow-cases.ts";
import { definition, final, stage, when } from "../decide/build.ts";

const origin = (item: string[], part: string | null = null) => ({ item, part, composite: null });

/** A compiled-like chain: an action step, the tasks step and the route step of one authored stage, then an ending. */
function chain(): PublishedDefinition {
  const def = definition({
    stages: [
      stage("act_a__run", { transitions: [when("t_next", "true", "act_b__run")] }),
      stage("act_b__run", { transitions: [when("t_next", "true", "st_s__tasks")] }),
      stage("st_s__tasks", { transitions: [when("t_next", "true", "st_s__route")] }),
      stage("st_s__route", { transitions: [when("t_end", "true", "st_end")] }),
      final("st_end"),
    ],
  });
  def.origins = {
    "stage:root": origin(["wf_x"]),
    "stage:act_a__run": origin(["act_a"]),
    "stage:act_b__run": origin(["act_b"]),
    "stage:st_s__tasks": origin(["st_s"], "tasks"),
    "stage:st_s__route": origin(["st_s"], "arrows"),
    "stage:st_end": origin(["st_end"]),
  };
  return def;
}

describe("authoredStageOf", () => {
  it("is the engine stage itself when the definition has no origin map, and null for null", () => {
    const def = chain();
    def.origins = {};
    expect(authoredStageOf(def, "act_a__run")).toBe("act_a__run");
    expect(authoredStageOf(def, null)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("follows the origin map: a stage's own steps name it; an action's step finds the stage it runs in", () => {
    const def = chain();
    expect(["act_a__run", "act_b__run", "st_s__tasks", "st_s__route", "st_end"].map((s) => authoredStageOf(def, s))).toEqual(["st_s", "st_s", "st_s", "st_s", "st_end"]);
    expect(authoredStageOf(def, "root")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("a hand-written definition with an origin map reports its stages by their own names", () => {
    const def = loadExampleDefinition("change-request-demo");
    for (const s of def.root.stages) expect(authoredStageOf(def, s.id)).toBe(s.id);
  });

  /** The stage the authored document puts the origin's item in: the item itself when it is a stage. */
  function documentStage(source: AuthoredWorkflow, def: PublishedDefinition, engineStage: string): string | null {
    const item = def.origins[`stage:${engineStage}`]?.item[0];
    const found = item === undefined ? undefined : indexDocument(source).byId.get(item);
    if (found === undefined) return null;
    return found.kind === "stage" ? found.id : (found.stage ?? null);
  }

  for (const name of ["change-request", "several-at-once", "integrated-sample"] as const) {
    it(`${name}: agrees with the document's stage of each engine stage's origin item`, () => {
      const source = fixture(name);
      const r = compile(source, catalogue(), { mode: "tryIt" });
      if (!r.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.findings));
      const differ = r.published.root.stages
        .map((s) => [s.id, authoredStageOf(r.published, s.id), documentStage(source, r.published, s.id)])
        .filter(([, mine, theirs]) => mine !== theirs);
      expect(differ).toEqual([]);
    });
  }

  it("Try it's step for an unfinished arrow is in the stage the arrow leaves (E-28)", () => {
    const source = fixture("change-request");
    const arrow = source.stages.flatMap((s) => ("arrows" in s ? s.arrows : [])).find((a) => a.id === "ar_da_approve");
    if (arrow === undefined) throw new Error("no ar_da_approve");
    arrow.goTo = null;
    const r = compile(source, catalogue(), { mode: "tryIt" });
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.findings));
    expect(r.published.origins["stage:ar_da_approve__unfinished"]?.item).toEqual(["ar_da_approve"]);
    expect(authoredStageOf(r.published, "ar_da_approve__unfinished")).toBe(documentStage(source, r.published, "ar_da_approve__unfinished"));
    expect(authoredStageOf(r.published, "ar_da_approve__unfinished")).toBe("st_domain_approval");
  });

  it("integrated-sample: the look-up action's step is in the stage that runs it (integrated-sample.md I9)", () => {
    const r = compile(fixture("integrated-sample"), catalogue(), { mode: "tryIt" });
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.findings));
    expect(authoredStageOf(r.published, "act_look_up_service__run")).toBe("st_find_owner");
  });
});

/**
 * turn on its own (kernel spec section 3; E-26): decide, the fold of its events, and the refusal that leaves
 * the state as it was.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { decide, emptyState, fold, turn, type RequestState } from "../../src/kernel/index.ts";
import { at, definition, person, rita, stage, waitId, when } from "./decide/build.ts";

const def = definition({
  stages: [
    stage("Start", { waits: [person("form")], transitions: [when("t_go", "true", "Idle")] }),
    stage("Idle", { waits: [person("nudge", { role: "option" })], transitions: [when("t_on", "waits.nudge.outcome == 'done'", "Work")] }),
    stage("Work", { waits: [person("task")] }),
  ],
});
const start = { kind: "start", requestId: "req-1", readableId: 1, by: rita, outcome: "done", data: {}, trigger: null } as const;

describe("turn", () => {
  it("returns decide's events and trace, and the state they fold to", () => {
    const r = turn(def, emptyState(), start, { at: at(0) });
    const d = decide(def, emptyState(), start, { at: at(0) });
    if (!r.ok || !d.ok) throw new Error("refused");
    expect(r.events).toEqual(d.events);
    expect(r.trace).toEqual(d.trace);
    expect(r.dropped).toBeNull();
    expect(r.state).toEqual(fold(d.events));
  });

  it("records nothing for a request left with nothing that fits; a later turn returns the state its events fold to", () => {
    const first = turn(def, emptyState(), start, { at: at(0) });
    if (!first.ok) throw new Error("refused");
    expect(first.events.map((e) => e.type)).not.toContain("Faulted");
    const next = turn(def, first.state, { kind: "act", by: rita, wait: waitId("Idle.nudge", "a3"), outcome: "done", data: {} }, { at: at(1) });
    if (!next.ok) throw new Error("refused");

    expect(r.state).toBe(before);

/**
 * T27: the cel-spec conformance "simple" tests, run against the pinned library itself (not the wrapper),
 * with the options the wrapper uses. Data from @bufbuild/cel-spec 0.6.2.
 *
 * This file and t30 import the library directly: they measure the library. Source code outside
 * src/cel/environment.ts may not (see test/boundaries.test.ts).
 *
 * Skipped, not failed: tests that bind or expect protobuf messages, enums or type values, tests with a
 * container, check-only tests and tests that expect unknowns. Those features are outside cel-1.
 */
import { Environment, Optional } from "@marcbachmann/cel-js";
import { Duration, UnsignedInt } from "@marcbachmann/cel-js/evaluator";
import { tests as conformance } from "@bufbuild/cel-spec/testdata/conformance.js";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

type Pv = Record<string, unknown>;
class Skip extends Error {}

function b64(s: string): Uint8Array {
  return Uint8Array.from(atob(s), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));
}

/** Proto JSON `cel.expr.Value` to a library runtime value. */
function toRuntime(v: Pv): unknown {
  if ("nullValue" in v) return null;
  if ("boolValue" in v) return v["boolValue"];
  if ("int64Value" in v) return BigInt(v["int64Value"] as string);
  if ("uint64Value" in v) return new UnsignedInt(BigInt(v["uint64Value"] as string));
  if ("doubleValue" in v) return Number(v["doubleValue"]);
  if ("stringValue" in v) return v["stringValue"];
  if ("bytesValue" in v) return b64(v["bytesValue"] as string);
  if ("listValue" in v) return (((v["listValue"] as Pv)["values"] ?? []) as Pv[]).map(toRuntime);
  if ("mapValue" in v) {
    const m = new Map<unknown, unknown>();
    for (const e of ((v["mapValue"] as Pv)["entries"] ?? []) as { key: Pv; value: Pv }[]) m.set(toRuntime(e.key), toRuntime(e.value));
    return m;
  }
  throw new Skip(`value kind ${Object.keys(v).join(",")}`);
}

/** A canonical, comparable form of a runtime value. */
function canon(v: unknown): unknown {
  if (v === null || typeof v === "boolean" || typeof v === "string") return v;
  if (typeof v === "bigint") return { int: v.toString() };
  if (v instanceof UnsignedInt) return { uint: v.valueOf().toString() };
  if (typeof v === "number") return { double: Number.isNaN(v) ? "NaN" : Object.is(v, -0) ? "0" : String(v) };
  if (v instanceof Uint8Array) return { bytes: Array.from(v).join(",") };
  if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.map(canon);
  if (v instanceof Date) return { ts: v.toISOString() };
  if (v instanceof Duration) return { dur: v.toString() };
  if (v instanceof Optional) return { optional: v.hasValue() ? canon(v.value()) : null };
  if (v instanceof Map || (typeof v === "object" && v !== null && Object.getPrototypeOf(v) === Object.prototype)) {
    const entries = v instanceof Map ? [...v.entries()] : Object.entries(v);
    return { map: entries.map(([k, x]) => [JSON.stringify(canon(k)), canon(x)]).sort(([a], [b]) => String(a).localeCompare(String(b))) };
  }
  return { other: Object.prototype.toString.call(v) };
}

interface Original {
  name?: string;
  expr: string;
  container?: string;
  disableMacros?: boolean;
  checkOnly?: boolean;
  bindings?: Record<string, { value?: Pv }>;
  value?: Pv;
  typedResult?: { result?: Pv };
  evalError?: unknown;
  anyEvalErrors?: unknown;
  unknown?: unknown;
  anyUnknowns?: unknown;
}
interface Suite {
  name: string;
  suites?: Suite[];
  tests?: { original: Original }[];
}

type Verdict = "pass" | "fail" | "skip";

function runOne(o: Original): Verdict {
  if (o.container || o.checkOnly || o.unknown !== undefined || o.anyUnknowns !== undefined) return "skip";
  let bindings: Record<string, unknown>;
  let expected: unknown;
  const expectError = o.evalError !== undefined || o.anyEvalErrors !== undefined;
  try {
    bindings = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(o.bindings ?? {}).map(([k, b]) => [k, toRuntime(b.value ?? {})]));
    expected = expectError ? undefined : o.value ? toRuntime(o.value) : o.typedResult?.result ? toRuntime(o.typedResult.result) : true;
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof Skip) return "skip";
    throw e;
  }
  const env = new Environment({ unlistedVariablesAreDyn: true, enableOptionalTypes: true, homogeneousAggregateLiterals: false });
  let actual: unknown;
  try {
    actual = env.evaluate(o.expr, bindings);
    if (actual instanceof Promise) return "fail";
  } catch {
    return expectError ? "pass" : "fail";
  }
  if (expectError) return "fail";
  return JSON.stringify(canon(actual)) === JSON.stringify(canon(expected)) ? "pass" : "fail";
}

function collect(s: Suite, prefix: string, out: Map<string, { pass: number; fail: number; skip: number; failed: string[] }>): void {
  for (const t of s.tests ?? []) {
    const key = prefix;
    const row = out.get(key) ?? { pass: 0, fail: 0, skip: 0, failed: [] };
    const v = runOne(t.original);
    row[v]++;
    if (v === "fail") row.failed.push(t.original.name ?? t.original.expr);
    out.set(key, row);
  }
  for (const c of s.suites ?? []) collect(c, prefix || c.name, out);
}

/** The baseline for @marcbachmann/cel-js 8.0.0 with the wrapper's options, measured 2026-11-15. */
const BASELINE_PASS = 1122;
/** Files that test CEL extensions (cel-go's ext packages), not the standard definitions. */
const EXTENSION = /_ext$/;

describe("T27 cel-spec conformance against the library", () => {
  it("records the pass rate per file and does not fall below the baseline", () => {
    const rows = new Map<string, { pass: number; fail: number; skip: number; failed: string[] }>();
    collect(conformance as unknown as Suite, "", rows);
    let pass = 0;
    let fail = 0;
    let skip = 0;
    const std = { pass: 0, fail: 0, skip: 0 };
    const table: string[] = ["| File | Pass | Fail | Skipped |", "|---|---|---|---|"];
    for (const [name, r] of [...rows].sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))) {
      pass += r.pass;
      fail += r.fail;
      skip += r.skip;
      if (!EXTENSION.test(name)) {
        std.pass += r.pass;
        std.fail += r.fail;
        std.skip += r.skip;
      }
      table.push(`| ${name} | ${r.pass} | ${r.fail} | ${r.skip} |`);
    }
    table.push(`| standard files (no _ext) | ${std.pass} | ${std.fail} | ${std.skip} |`);
    table.push(`| total | ${pass} | ${fail} | ${skip} |`);
    console.log(`T27 conformance\n${table.join("\n")}`);
    for (const [name, r] of rows) if (r.failed.length) console.log(`T27 failed in ${name}: ${r.failed.join(", ")}`);
    expect(pass).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(BASELINE_PASS);
  });
});
===\nengine/packages/core/test/library/t30-side-by-side.test.ts\n===
/**
 * T30: two versions of the library installed side by side (8.0.0, and 7.6.1 under the npm alias
 * `cel-js-v7`), loaded in one process, run on the corpus. Shows that two definition formats pinned to
 * different library versions can run in one engine.
 *
 * Runs the library directly with every variable `dyn`, as the wrapper's evaluation environment does.
 * Cases that need the wrapper's engine functions (date, the renamed functions) are left out.
 */
import * as v8 from "@marcbachmann/cel-js";
import * as v7 from "cel-js-v7";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { jsonToCel, t, type JsonValue } from "../../src/cel/index.ts";
import { cases, demoDeclarations } from "../cel/corpus.ts";

type Lib = { Environment: new (opts: object) => { registerVariable(n: string, t: string): unknown; evaluate(e: string, c: object): unknown } };

const OPTIONS = { enableOptionalTypes: true, homogeneousAggregateLiterals: false, unlistedVariablesAreDyn: false };
const USES_ENGINE_FUNCTIONS = /\b(date|timestamp|int|matches|lowerAscii|upperAscii|cel1_\w+)\s*\(|getHours/;

function describeValue(v: unknown): string {
  return JSON.stringify(v, (_k, x: unknown) => {
    if (typeof x === "bigint") return `${x}n`;
    if (x instanceof Map) return Object.fromEntries(x);
    if (x && typeof x === "object" && typeof (x as { hasValue?: unknown }).hasValue === "function") {
      const o = x as { hasValue(): boolean; value(): unknown };
      return { optional: o.hasValue() ? o.value() : null };
    }
    return x;
  });
}

function run(lib: Lib, source: string, context: Record<string, JsonValue>): string {
  const env = new lib.Environment(OPTIONS);
  const names = [...Object.keys(demoDeclarations.variables), ...Object.keys(demoDeclarations.constants ?? {})];
  for (const n of names) env.registerVariable(n, "dyn");
  const ctx: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [n, c] of Object.entries(demoDeclarations.constants ?? {})) ctx[n] = jsonToCel(c.value, t.dyn);
  for (const [n, v] of Object.entries(context)) ctx[n] = jsonToCel(v, t.dyn);
  try {
    return `value ${describeValue(env.evaluate(source, ctx))}`;
  } catch (e) {
    const err = e as { code?: string; name?: string; message?: string };
    return `error ${err.name ?? "?"} ${err.code ?? err.message?.split("\n")[0] ?? ""}`;
  }
}

describe("T30 two library versions side by side", () => {
  it("loads 8.0.0 and 7.6.1 in one process and runs the corpus on both", () => {
    expect(v8.Environment).not.toBe(v7.Environment);
    const rows = cases.filter((c) => c.context && !USES_ENGINE_FUNCTIONS.test(c.source));
    const diffs: string[] = [];
    for (const c of rows) {
      const a = run(v8 as unknown as Lib, c.source, c.context ?? {});
      const b = run(v7 as unknown as Lib, c.source, c.context ?? {});
      if (a !== b) diffs.push(`${c.id}: 8.0.0 ${a} | 7.6.1 ${b}`);
    }
    console.log(`T30 ran ${rows.length} cases on both versions; ${diffs.length} differ${diffs.length ? `\n${diffs.join("\n")}` : ""}`);
    expect(rows.length).toBeGreaterThan(30);
  });
});

    expect(kernel.sameWait(wait, { ...wait, seq: wait.seq + 1 })).toBe(false);

    // Answered: every button refused wait-not-open, saying who answered with which button.
    const approve = kernel.turn(published.definition, state, { kind: "act", by: { type: "user", id: "marcus" }, wait: opened.payload.wait, outcome: "btn_da_approve", data: { q_eng_lead: { type: "user", id: "diego" } } }, { at: "2026-11-16T09:00:01.000000Z", memberships: { groups: ["dir-group-payments-approvers"] }, lookups: { q_eng_lead: { found: true, label: "Diego" } } });
    if (!approve.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(approve.refusals));
    const after = core.buttonStates(published, { form: "task", events: [...events, ...approve.events], task }, viewer("olu", []));
    const refusal = { code: "wait-not-open", params: { state: "completed", by: { type: "user", id: "marcus" }, button: "btn_da_approve" }, location: { item: "tk_domain_approval" } };
    expect(after).toEqual(buttons.map((button) => ({ button, available: false, refusals: [refusal] })));
  });
});

describe("the authored stage, across the two entries", () => {
  it("the kernel's authoredStageOf maps every engine stage the root compiles to an authored stage, or null for the root", () => {
    const parsed = core.parse(rawFixture("change-request"));
    if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(parsed.problems));
    const compiled = core.compile(parsed.workflow, catalogue());
    if (!compiled.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(compiled.findings));
    const def = compiled.published;
    for (const s of def.root.stages) {
      const authored = kernel.authoredStageOf(def, s.id);
      expect(authored === null || parsed.workflow.stages.some((st) => st.id === authored)).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});

/** checkSchemaProfile: only the keywords and formats of jsonschema-1 (definition-format.md section 6). */
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { checkSchemaProfile, SCHEMA_KEYWORDS } from "../../src/schema/index.ts";

describe("checkSchemaProfile", () => {
  it("accepts every keyword of the profile, with a valid value", () => {
    const schema = {
      type: "object",
      properties: { a: { type: "string", minLength: 1, maxLength: 9, format: "date", enum: ["2026-01-01"] }, b: { const: { x: [1] } } },
      required: ["a"],
      additionalProperties: { type: "array", items: { type: ["string", "number"] }, uniqueItems: true },
    };
    expect(checkSchemaProfile(schema)).toEqual([]);
    expect(SCHEMA_KEYWORDS).toHaveLength(11);
  });

  it("refuses any keyword outside the profile, at any depth", () => {
    for (const keyword of ["pattern", "minimum", "maximum", "oneOf", "anyOf", "allOf", "not", "if", "prefixItems", "minItems", "default", "title", "description", "patternProperties", "dependentRequired"]) {
      expect(checkSchemaProfile({ [keyword]: 1 }), keyword).toEqual([{ pointer: `/${keyword}`, code: "keyword-not-in-profile" }]);
    }
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ properties: { a: { items: { minimum: 0 } } } })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/properties/a/items/minimum", code: "keyword-not-in-profile" }]);
  });

  it("refuses $ keywords: no key starts with $ (definition-format.md section 1)", () => {
    for (const keyword of ["$schema", "$id", "$ref", "$defs"]) {
      expect(checkSchemaProfile({ [keyword]: "x" }), keyword).toEqual([{ pointer: `/${keyword}`, code: "keyword-not-in-profile" }]);
    }
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ properties: { $x: {} } })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/properties/$x", code: "invalid-keyword-value" }]);
  });

  it("refuses a format outside the profile", () => {
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ format: "email" })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/format", code: "format-not-in-profile" }]);
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ format: "date" })).toEqual([]);
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ format: "date-time" })).toEqual([]);
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ format: "directory-object-id" })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("refuses a keyword whose value 2020-12 does not allow, and null anywhere", () => {
    const bad = [
      { type: "null" },
      { type: "text" },
      { type: [] },
      { type: ["string", "string"] },
      { required: "a" },
      { required: ["a", "a"] },
      { uniqueItems: "yes" },
      { enum: [] },
      { enum: [null] },
      { enum: ["a", "a"] },
      { const: null },
      { minLength: -1 },
      { maxLength: 1.5 },
      { properties: [] },
      { format: 1 },
    ];
    for (const schema of bad) expect(checkSchemaProfile(schema), JSON.stringify(schema)).toEqual([{ pointer: `/${Object.keys(schema)[0]}`, code: "invalid-keyword-value" }]);
  });

  it("refuses a subschema that is not a schema, but allows a boolean for additionalProperties and items", () => {
    expect(checkSchemaProfile(true)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", code: "not-a-schema" }]);
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ properties: { a: "string" } })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/properties/a", code: "not-a-schema" }]);
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ additionalProperties: false, items: true })).toEqual([]);
    expect(checkSchemaProfile({ items: [{}] })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/items", code: "not-a-schema" }]);
  });

  it("accepts every schema and declared type of the demo definition", () => {
    const demo = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../../../design/examples/change-request-demo.definition.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) as {
      schemas: Record<string, { schema: unknown }>;
      types: { data: Record<string, unknown>; constants: Record<string, unknown>; results: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>> };
    };
    const all = [
      ...Object.values(demo.schemas).map((s) => s.schema),
      ...Object.values(demo.types.data),
      ...Object.values(demo.types.constants),
      ...Object.values(demo.types.results).flatMap((ops) => Object.values(ops)),
    ];
    expect(all.length).toBeGreaterThan(10);
    expect(all.flatMap(checkSchemaProfile)).toEqual([]);
  });
});
===\nengine/packages/core/test/schema/validate.test.ts\n===
/** validateBySchema, profile jsonschema-1 (definition-format.md section 6), keyword by keyword. */
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { SchemaProfileError, validateBySchema, type SchemaFailure } from "../../src/schema/index.ts";

function v(schema: unknown, data: unknown): SchemaFailure[] {
  return validateBySchema(schema, data);
}

const person = {
  type: "object",
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ["type", "id"],
  properties: { type: { const: "user" }, id: { type: "string", format: "directory-object-id" } },
};

describe("type", () => {
  it("accepts each JSON type and refuses the others as wrong-kind", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "string" }, "x")).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "boolean" }, false)).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "object" }, {})).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "array" }, [])).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "string" }, 3)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "object" }, [])).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "array" }, {})).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });

  it("does not coerce: a numeric string is not a number, and 'true' is not a boolean", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "number" }, "3")).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "boolean" }, "true")).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });

  it("reads integer as a number with no fraction, so 3.0 is one and 3.5 is not", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "integer" }, 3.0)).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "integer" }, 3.5)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "number" }, 3)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("accepts a list of types (choiceFromConnection's stored is string or number)", () => {
    expect(v({ type: ["string", "number"] }, 4)).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: ["string", "number"] }, true)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });

  it("reports nothing else about a value of the wrong kind", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "string", minLength: 2, enum: ["ab"] }, 1)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });
});

describe("the profile's own rules", () => {
  it("refuses null and anything that is not JSON, whatever the schema", () => {
    expect(v({}, null)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({}, undefined)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({}, Number.NaN)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "object" }, { a: null })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/a", keyword: null, rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "object" }, new Date(0))).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });

  it("refuses an integer beyond +/-(2^53 - 1) as out-of-range, whatever its schema", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "number" }, 2 ** 53)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "out-of-range" }]);
    expect(v({}, -(2 ** 60))).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "out-of-range" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "number" }, 2 ** 53 - 1)).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "number" }, 1e300 + 0.5)).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: null, rule: "out-of-range" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "number" }, 0.5)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("refuses a data key starting with $", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "object", additionalProperties: true }, { $redacted: true })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/$redacted", keyword: null, rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });
});

describe("properties, required, additionalProperties", () => {
  const form = {
    type: "object",
    additionalProperties: false,
    required: ["title", "domain"],
    properties: { title: { type: "string", minLength: 1 }, domain: { type: "string" } },
  };

  it("validates each declared property at its pointer", () => {
    expect(v(form, { title: "", domain: 1 })).toEqual([
      { pointer: "/title", keyword: "minLength", rule: "too-short" },
      { pointer: "/domain", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" },
    ]);
  });

  it("reports a missing required property at its own pointer", () => {
    expect(v(form, {})).toEqual([
      { pointer: "/title", keyword: "required", rule: "required" },
      { pointer: "/domain", keyword: "required", rule: "required" },
    ]);
  });

  it("refuses an unknown property with additionalProperties false, and does not remove it", () => {
    const data = { title: "t", domain: "A", extra: 1 };
    expect(v(form, data)).toEqual([{ pointer: "/extra", keyword: "additionalProperties", rule: "unknown-question" }]);
    expect(data).toEqual({ title: "t", domain: "A", extra: 1 });
  });

  it("a property inside an answer that its schema does not have is wrong-kind, not unknown-question (E-27)", () => {
    const choice = { type: "object", additionalProperties: false, properties: { q: { type: "object", additionalProperties: false, properties: { stored: { type: "string" } } } } };
    expect(v(choice, { q: { stored: "a", extra: 1 } })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/q/extra", keyword: "additionalProperties", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ type: "array", items: { type: "object", additionalProperties: false } }, [{ a: 1 }])).toEqual([{ pointer: "/0/a", keyword: "additionalProperties", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v(choice, { r: 1 })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/r", keyword: "additionalProperties", rule: "unknown-question" }]);
  });

  it("validates undeclared properties by an additionalProperties schema (a map)", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "object", additionalProperties: { type: "string" } }, { A: "x", B: 2 })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/B", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });

  it("allows undeclared properties when additionalProperties is absent or true", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "object", properties: {} }, { a: [1] })).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "object", additionalProperties: true }, { a: 1 })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("escapes ~ and / in pointers (RFC 6901)", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "object", additionalProperties: false }, { "a/b~c": 1 })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/a~1b~0c", keyword: "additionalProperties", rule: "unknown-question" }]);
  });

  it("ignores required and properties on a value that is not an object", () => {
    expect(v({ required: ["a"], properties: { a: { type: "string" } } }, "x")).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("items, uniqueItems", () => {
  it("validates every item at its index", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }, ["a", 1, "c", false])).toEqual([
      { pointer: "/1", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" },
      { pointer: "/3", keyword: "type", rule: "wrong-kind" },
    ]);
  });

  it("refuses every item under items false", () => {
    expect(v({ type: "array", items: false }, [])).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "array", items: false }, [1])).toEqual([{ pointer: "/0", keyword: "items", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
  });

  it("refuses a repeated item by value, object key order ignored", () => {
    const people = { type: "array", items: person, uniqueItems: true };
    expect(v(people, [{ type: "user", id: "a" }, { id: "a", type: "user" }])).toEqual([{ pointer: "/1", keyword: "uniqueItems", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v(people, [{ type: "user", id: "a" }, { type: "user", id: "b" }])).toEqual([]);
    expect(v({ type: "array", uniqueItems: false }, [1, 1])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("enum, const", () => {
  it("refuses a value not in enum as not-a-choice", () => {
    const choice = { type: "string", enum: ["ch_a", "ch_b"] };
    expect(v(choice, "ch_a")).toEqual([]);
    expect(v(choice, "ch_c")).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "enum", rule: "not-a-choice" }]);
    expect(v({ enum: [{ a: 1, b: 2 }] }, { b: 2, a: 1 })).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("refuses a value other than const as wrong-kind (a group where a person is asked)", () => {
    expect(v(person, { type: "user", id: "lee" })).toEqual([]);
    expect(v(person, { type: "group", id: "grp-a" })).toEqual([{ pointer: "/type", keyword: "const", rule: "wrong-kind" }]);
    expect(v({ const: 1 }, 1.0)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("format", () => {
  it("date: YYYY-MM-DD and a real calendar date", () => {
    const date = { type: "string", format: "date" };
    expect(v(date, "2024-02-29")).toEqual([]);
    for (const bad of ["2023-02-29", "2026-13-01", "2026-04-31", "2026-1-01", "20260101", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", " 2026-01-01"]) {
      expect(v(date, bad), bad).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "format", rule: "bad-format" }]);
    }
    expect(v(date, "1900-02-29")).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "format", rule: "bad-format" }]);
    expect(v(date, "2000-02-29")).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("date-time: RFC 3339 with a mandatory offset, and no leap second (E-26)", () => {
    const dt = { type: "string", format: "date-time" };
    for (const ok of ["2026-11-15T09:30:00Z", "2026-11-15T09:30:00.123456Z", "2026-11-15t09:30:00+05:30", "2016-12-31T23:59:59Z"]) {
      expect(v(dt, ok), ok).toEqual([]);
    }
    const leap = ["2016-12-31T23:59:60Z", "2016-12-31T23:59:60.5+00:00"];
    for (const bad of ["2026-11-15T09:30:00", "2026-11-15 09:30:00Z", "2026-11-15T24:00:00Z", "2026-11-15T09:60:00Z", "2026-02-30T09:30:00Z", "2026-11-15T09:30:00+24:00", "2026-11-15T09:30Z", ...leap]) {
      expect(v(dt, bad), bad).toEqual([{ pointer: "", keyword: "format", rule: "bad-format" }]);
    }
  });

  it("directory-object-id: a non-empty string without whitespace or control characters", () => {

    expect(v(id, "dir-user-priya-raman")).toEqual([]);
    expect(v(id, "6f1c8a2e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001")).toEqual([]);

  });

  it("applies only to strings", () => {
    expect(v({ format: "date" }, 3)).toEqual([]);
  });

/**
 * engine/spec is a copy of workflow-platform/engine made by `npm run sync-spec`
 * (engine/scripts/sync-spec.mjs): the same files with LF endings, plus SOURCE.md, which names the
 * spec's version. This fails when the copy differs from the source; it is skipped when the source
 * repo is not on disk.
 */
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, relative } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

const engine = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../", import.meta.url));
const source = join(engine, "..", "..", "workflow-platform", "engine");
const target = join(engine, "spec");
const present = existsSync(source);

function filesUnder(root: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const walk = (dir: string): void => {
    for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      const path = join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(path);
      else out.push(relative(root, path).split("\\").join("/"));
    }
  };
  walk(root);
  return out.sort();
}

const lf = (text: string): string => text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");

if (!present) {
  console.warn(`spec-copy: skipped, the spec's source is not on disk (${source})`);
}

describe.skipIf(!present)("engine/spec is the spec package's copy (run `npm run sync-spec` when this fails)", () => {
  it("has the same files", () => {
    expect(filesUnder(target).filter((name) => name !== "SOURCE.md")).toEqual(filesUnder(source));
  });

  it("each file equals its source with LF endings", () => {
    const stale = filesUnder(source).filter((name) => {
      const path = join(target, name);
      return !existsSync(path) || readFileSync(path, "utf8") !== lf(readFileSync(join(source, name), "utf8"));
    });
    expect(stale, "files that differ from the source").toEqual([]);
  });

  it("SOURCE.md names the spec's version", () => {
    const title = readFileSync(join(source, "kernel", "kernel-spec.md"), "utf8").split(/\r?\n/)[0];
    const version = /spec (v\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/.exec(title ?? "")?.[1];
    expect(version).toBeDefined();
    expect(readFileSync(join(target, "SOURCE.md"), "utf8")).toContain(`(kernel spec ${version})`);
  });
});

===\nengine/packages/server/src/api/authoring/handlers.ts\n===
/**
 * The authoring API over HTTP (contract/authoring-api.md section 5): Hono routes whose handlers are functions
 * from a Request to a Response, so tests and the development host call them without a socket (E-30). Each
 * handler checks the body's shape, asks the adapter for the caller, calls the function and maps its `Result`.
 * It adds no rule. An unknown path or method answers `not-found` (`path`).
 */
import { Hono } from "hono";

import type { CallerAdapter } from "../caller.ts";
import { BodyProblem, integer, nonEmptyString, object, optionalString, refs, shapeOf, string, type Fields } from "../shared/body.ts";
import { asCaller, errorResponse, guarded, notFoundPath, readJson, resultResponse, apiError } from "../shared/http.ts";
import { DRAFT_LIMIT } from "./operations.ts";
import type { AuthoringApi, CreateWorkflowArgs, PublishArgs, SaveDraftArgs, Settings } from "./types.ts";

/** Where the development host mounts the API (authoring-api.md section 1). */
export const DEFAULT_BASE = "/api/workflow/v1";

/**
 * A request body may be 64 KiB larger than the largest draft (E-31), so that a draft over its limit is refused
 * by the save's own `too-large`, in its documented place after `stale-revision`.
 */
export const BODY_LIMIT = DRAFT_LIMIT + 64 * 1024;

/** A version number in a path; anything else names no version. */
const VERSION_IN_PATH = /^[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$/;

/** Reads the body and checks its shape; a failure is the error response. */
async function bodyOf<T>(request: Request, read: (body: unknown) => T): Promise<{ ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; response: Response }> {
  const json = await readJson(request, BODY_LIMIT);
  if (!json.ok) return { ok: false, response: errorResponse(json.errors) };
  const shaped = shapeOf(() => read(json.value));
  return shaped.ok ? shaped : { ok: false, response: errorResponse([apiError("invalid-body", shaped.params)]) };
}

function createArgs(body: unknown): CreateWorkflowArgs {
  const o = object(body, "", ["name", "description"]);
  const description = optionalString(o, "description");
  return { name: nonEmptyString(o, "name"), ...(description === undefined ? {} : { description }) };
}

function saveArgs(body: unknown): SaveDraftArgs {
  const o = object(body, "", ["baseRevision", "authored"]);
  const baseRevision = integer(o, "baseRevision", 1);
  if (!("authored" in o) || o["authored"] === undefined) throw new BodyProblem("/authored", "missing");
  return { baseRevision, authored: o["authored"] };
}

function publishArgs(body: unknown): PublishArgs {
  const o = object(body, "", ["revision", "coreVersion"]);
  return { revision: integer(o, "revision", 1), coreVersion: string(o, "coreVersion") };
}

/** A `SettingsRead` may be sent back: `changedBy` and `changedAt` are accepted and ignored. */
function settingsArgs(body: unknown): Settings {
  const o: Fields = object(body, "", ["name", "description", "authors", "stuckRequestsGoTo", "changedBy", "changedAt"]);
  const settings: Settings = { name: nonEmptyString(o, "name"), description: string(o, "description"), authors: refs(o, "authors") };
  // An empty list is refused by `saveSettings` itself.
  if ("stuckRequestsGoTo" in o) settings.stuckRequestsGoTo = refs(o, "stuckRequestsGoTo");
  return settings;
}


export interface AuthoringHttpOptions {
  /** Default `/api/workflow/v1`. */
  base?: string;
}

/** The routes, mounted at `base`. `app.fetch(request)` answers a Request. */
export function authoringRoutes(api: AuthoringApi, callers: CallerAdapter, options: AuthoringHttpOptions = {}): Hono {
  const base = options.base ?? DEFAULT_BASE;
  const app = new Hono().basePath(base);
  const workflowPath = (id: string): string => `${base}/workflows/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`;

  app.get("/meta", () => guarded(async () => resultResponse(await api.getMeta(), 200)));

  app.get("/catalogue", (c) => asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => resultResponse(await api.getCatalogue(caller), 200)));

  app.get("/workflows", (c) => asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => resultResponse(await api.listWorkflows(caller), 200)));

  app.post("/workflows", (c) =>
    asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => {
      const args = await bodyOf(c.req.raw, createArgs);
      if (!args.ok) return args.response;
      return resultResponse(await api.createWorkflow(caller, args.value), 201, (d) => ({ Location: `${workflowPath(d.workflow)}/draft` }));
    }),
  );

  app.get("/workflows/:id/draft", (c) => asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => resultResponse(await api.getDraft(caller, c.req.param("id")), 200)));

  app.put("/workflows/:id/draft", (c) =>
    asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => {
      const args = await bodyOf(c.req.raw, saveArgs);
      if (!args.ok) return args.response;
      return resultResponse(await api.saveDraft(caller, c.req.param("id"), args.value), 200);
    }),
  );

  app.post("/workflows/:id/versions", (c) =>
    asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => {
      const args = await bodyOf(c.req.raw, publishArgs);
      if (!args.ok) return args.response;
      const id = c.req.param("id");
      return resultResponse(await api.publish(caller, id, args.value), 201, (r) => ({ Location: `${workflowPath(id)}/versions/${r.version}` }));
    }),
  );

  app.get("/workflows/:id/versions", (c) => asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => resultResponse(await api.listVersions(caller, c.req.param("id")), 200)));

  app.get("/workflows/:id/versions/:n", (c) =>
    asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => {
      const n = c.req.param("n");
      const version = VERSION_IN_PATH.test(n) ? Number(n) : -1;
      return resultResponse(await api.getVersion(caller, c.req.param("id"), version), 200, () => ({ "Cache-Control": "private, max-age=31536000, immutable" }));
    }),
  );

  app.get("/workflows/:id/settings", (c) => asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => resultResponse(await api.getSettings(caller, c.req.param("id")), 200)));

  app.put("/workflows/:id/settings", (c) =>
    asCaller(callers, c.req.raw, async (caller) => {
      const args = await bodyOf(c.req.raw, settingsArgs);
      if (!args.ok) return args.response;
      return resultResponse(await api.saveSettings(caller, c.req.param("id"), args.value), 200);
    }),
  );

  app.notFound(() => notFoundPath());

  return app;
}

﻿/** The authoring API (contract/authoring-api.md). */

/**
 * The authoring API as plain functions taking the `Caller` (contract/authoring-api.md section 5). The HTTP
 * handlers in `handlers.ts` add no rule. The bindings of runtime-api.md section 5.3 are the runtime API's.
 *
 * Outside lookups (the caller's groups) are made before any transaction; a write locks the workflow's row.
 */
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import {
  blankWorkflow,
  check,
  compile,
  coreVersion,
  meta,
  parse,
  upgrade,
  type ApiError,
  type AuthoredWorkflow,
  type Caller,
  type Catalogue,
  type CatalogueRef,
  type Finding,
  type Ref,
  type Result,
} from "@workflow/core";
import { checkDefinition, type By, type JsonObject, type PublishedDefinition, type PublishProblem } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import {
  highestVersion,
  insertWorkflow,
  listVersionRows,
  listWorkflowRows,
  lockWorkflow,
  readDraft,
  readSettings,
  readVersionRow,
  writeDraft,
  writeSettings,
  type DraftRow,
  type SettingsRecord,
  type VersionRow,
} from "../../store/authoring.ts";
import type { Db, Queryable } from "../../store/db.ts";
import { insertDefinition } from "../../store/definitions.ts";
import type { CatalogueRegistry } from "../shared/catalogue.ts";
import { apiError, failure, success } from "../shared/http.ts";
import { admits, groupsOnce, readWorkflowPeople, type Memberships } from "../shared/people.ts";

import type {
  AuthoringApi,
  Draft,
  May,
  PublishResult,
  SavedDraft,
  Settings,
  SettingsRead,
  Version,
  VersionSummary,
  WorkflowSummary,
} from "./types.ts";

/** A draft is at most 1 MiB (authoring-api.md section 3). */
export const DRAFT_LIMIT = 1024 * 1024;


export interface AuthoringDeps {
  db: Db;
  catalogue: CatalogueRegistry;
  memberships: Memberships;
  /** Default: the system clock. */
  clock?: () => Date;
  /** Default: `wf-` and a random UUID, which fits the definition format's workflow ID. */
  newWorkflowId?: () => string;
  /** The kernel publish check; default core's `checkDefinition`. Replaceable so a test can make it refuse. */
  kernelCheck?: (definition: PublishedDefinition, catalogue: Catalogue) => PublishProblem[];
}

const ALL: May = { edit: true, publish: true, settings: true };
const NONE: May = { edit: false, publish: false, settings: false };

const userBy = (caller: Caller): By => ({ type: "user", id: caller.user });

/** A stored `by` as a `Ref`: authors and savers are always users. */
const refOf = (by: By): Ref => ({ type: by.type === "user" ? "user" : "group", id: by.id });

/** The ISO time with milliseconds that the contract's `Timestamp` is. */
const timestamp = (d: Date): string => d.toISOString();

function counts(findings: readonly Finding[]): { todo: number; worthKnowing: number } {
  return { todo: findings.filter((f) => f.severity === "todo").length, worthKnowing: findings.filter((f) => f.severity === "worthKnowing").length };
}

export function createAuthoringApi(deps: AuthoringDeps): AuthoringApi {
  const { db } = deps;
  const clock = deps.clock ?? (() => new Date());
  const newWorkflowId = deps.newWorkflowId ?? (() => `wf-${randomUUID()}`);
  const kernelCheck = deps.kernelCheck ?? ((definition: PublishedDefinition, catalogue: Catalogue) => checkDefinition(definition, catalogue));

  /** The caller's flags: everything for a platform admin or an author; nothing otherwise, also when the directory is down. */
  async function mayOf(caller: Caller, authors: readonly Ref[], groups: () => Promise<readonly string[] | "unavailable">): Promise<May> {
    if (caller.platformAdmin) return ALL;
    return (await admits(authors, caller, groups)) === "yes" ? ALL : NONE;
  }

  /** For a save, publish or settings save: `not-found`, `forbidden` or `membership-unavailable`, or null when the caller may. */
  async function mustBeAuthor(caller: Caller, workflow: string, groups: () => Promise<readonly string[] | "unavailable">): Promise<ApiError | null> {
    const people = await readWorkflowPeople(db, workflow);
    if (people === null) return apiError("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
    if (caller.platformAdmin) return null;
    const admitted = await admits(people.authors, caller, groups);
    if (admitted === "yes") return null;
    return admitted === "unavailable" ? apiError("membership-unavailable", {}) : apiError("forbidden", { need: "author" });
  }


  function draftOf(row: DraftRow, may: May): Draft {
    return {
      workflow: row.workflow,
      revision: row.revision,
      authored: upgrade(row.authored as unknown as AuthoredWorkflow),
      savedAt: row.savedAt,
      savedBy: refOf(row.savedBy),
      ...(row.basedOnVersion === null ? {} : { basedOnVersion: row.basedOnVersion }),
      may,
    };
  }

  /** The draft as the caller sees it; null when there is no such workflow. */
  async function readDraftFor(q: Queryable, caller: Caller, workflow: string, groups: () => Promise<readonly string[] | "unavailable">): Promise<Draft | null> {
    const row = await readDraft(q, workflow);
    const people = await readWorkflowPeople(q, workflow);
    if (row === null || people === null) return null;
    return draftOf(row, await mayOf(caller, people.authors, groups));
  }

  function versionSummaryOf(r: VersionRow): VersionSummary {
    // A hand-written definition has no revision, core or format: shown as 0, "" and 0.
    return {
      version: r.version,
      publishedAt: r.publishedAt,
      publishedBy: refOf(r.publishedBy),
      fromRevision: r.fromRevision ?? 0,
      coreVersion: r.coreVersion ?? "",
      formatVersion: r.formatVersion ?? 0,
      openRequests: r.openRequests,
    };
  }

  function settingsReadOf(record: SettingsRecord, changedBy: By, changedAt: string): SettingsRead {
    return {
      name: record.name,
      description: record.description,
      authors: record.authors,
      ...(record.stuckRequestsGoTo === undefined ? {} : { stuckRequestsGoTo: record.stuckRequestsGoTo }),
      changedBy: refOf(changedBy),
      changedAt,
    };
  }

  return {
    async listWorkflows(caller) {
      const groups = groupsOnce(deps.memberships, caller);
      const rows = await listWorkflowRows(db);
      const out: WorkflowSummary[] = [];
      for (const r of rows) {
        out.push({
          id: r.id,
          name: r.name,
          description: r.description,
          ...(r.liveVersion === null ? {} : { liveVersion: r.liveVersion }),
          draft: {
            revision: r.draft.revision,
            savedAt: r.draft.savedAt,
            savedBy: refOf(r.draft.savedBy),
            // Changed since live: never published, or the live version was published from another revision.
            changedSinceLive: r.liveFromRevision !== r.draft.revision,
            todo: r.draft.todo,
            worthKnowing: r.draft.worthKnowing,
          },
          triggers: { live: r.liveTriggers as CatalogueRef[], draft: r.draftTriggers as CatalogueRef[] },
          openRequests: r.openRequests,
          stuckRequests: r.stuckRequests,
          may: await mayOf(caller, r.authors, groups),
        });
      }
      return success(out);
    },

    async createWorkflow(caller, args) {
      const authored = blankWorkflow();
      const found = counts(check(authored, deps.catalogue.current()));
      const id = newWorkflowId();
      const at = timestamp(clock());
      await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await insertWorkflow(tx, {
          id,
          name: args.name,
          description: args.description ?? "",
          by: userBy(caller),
          at,
          authored: authored as unknown as JsonObject,
          todo: found.todo,
          worthKnowing: found.worthKnowing,
        });
      });
      const draft = await readDraftFor(db, caller, id, groupsOnce(deps.memberships, caller));
      if (draft === null) throw new Error(`workflow ${id} was not stored`);
      return success(draft);
    },

    async getDraft(caller, workflow) {
      const draft = await readDraftFor(db, caller, workflow, groupsOnce(deps.memberships, caller));
      return draft === null ? failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" }) : success(draft);
    },

    async saveDraft(caller, workflow, args) {
      const groups = groupsOnce(deps.memberships, caller);
      const refused = await mustBeAuthor(caller, workflow, groups);
      if (refused !== null) return { ok: false, errors: [refused] };

      // Pure work before the lock; reported in the documented order once the revision is known to be current.
      const size = Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(args.authored) ?? "", "utf8");
      const version = (args.authored as { formatVersion?: unknown } | null)?.formatVersion;
      const { min, max } = meta.authoredFormatVersions;
      const unsupported = typeof version === "number" && (version < min || version > max) ? { version, min, max } : null;
      const parsed = size > DRAFT_LIMIT || unsupported !== null ? null : parse(upgrade(args.authored as AuthoredWorkflow));
      const found = parsed?.ok === true ? counts(check(parsed.workflow, deps.catalogue.current())) : null;

      return db.transaction(async (tx): Promise<Result<SavedDraft>> => {
        if (!(await lockWorkflow(tx, workflow))) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
        const current = await readDraft(tx, workflow);
        if (current === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
        if (args.baseRevision !== current.revision) {
          const draft = await readDraftFor(tx, caller, workflow, groups);
          if (draft === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
          return failure("stale-revision", { currentRevision: current.revision, draft });
        }
        if (size > DRAFT_LIMIT) return failure("too-large", { limit: DRAFT_LIMIT });
        if (unsupported !== null) return failure("authored-format-unsupported", unsupported);
        if (parsed === null || !parsed.ok || found === null) return failure("invalid-document", { problems: parsed?.ok === false ? parsed.problems : [] });
        const saved: DraftRow = {
          workflow,
          revision: current.revision + 1,
          authored: args.authored as JsonObject,
          savedBy: userBy(caller),
          savedAt: timestamp(clock()),
          basedOnVersion: await highestVersion(tx, workflow),
          todo: found.todo,
          worthKnowing: found.worthKnowing,
        };
        await writeDraft(tx, saved);
        return success({ revision: saved.revision, savedAt: saved.savedAt, todo: saved.todo, worthKnowing: saved.worthKnowing });
      });
    },

    async publish(caller, workflow, args) {
      const groups = groupsOnce(deps.memberships, caller);
      const refused = await mustBeAuthor(caller, workflow, groups);
      if (refused !== null) return { ok: false, errors: [refused] };
      const catalogue = deps.catalogue.current();

      // Thrown inside the transaction so that it rolls back; answered `internal`, nothing written.
      class KernelRefused extends Error {}
      try {
        return await db.transaction(async (tx): Promise<Result<PublishResult>> => {
          if (!(await lockWorkflow(tx, workflow))) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
          if (args.coreVersion !== coreVersion) {
            return failure("core-version-mismatch", { serverCoreVersion: coreVersion, serverFormatVersion: meta.definitionFormatVersion });
          }
          const current = await readDraft(tx, workflow);
          if (current === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
          if (args.revision !== current.revision) {
            const draft = await readDraftFor(tx, caller, workflow, groups);
            if (draft === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
            return failure("stale-revision", { currentRevision: current.revision, draft });
          }
          const parsed = parse(upgrade(current.authored as unknown as AuthoredWorkflow));
          if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`the stored draft of ${workflow} does not parse`);
          const version = ((await highestVersion(tx, workflow)) ?? 0) + 1;
          const compiled = compile(parsed.workflow, catalogue, { mode: "publish", workflow, version, compiler: coreVersion });
          if (!compiled.ok) return failure("has-todo", { findings: compiled.findings });
          const problems = kernelCheck(compiled.published, catalogue);
          if (problems.some((p) => p.severity === "error")) throw new KernelRefused(JSON.stringify(problems));
          await insertDefinition(tx, {
            workflow,
            version,
            document: compiled.published,
            // The source as saved and published, not parse's reading of it.
            authored: upgrade(current.authored as unknown as AuthoredWorkflow) as unknown as JsonObject,
            fromRevision: current.revision,
            coreVersion,
            formatVersion: parsed.workflow.formatVersion,
            catalogueVersion: catalogue.version,
            publishedBy: userBy(caller),
            publishedAt: timestamp(clock()),
          });
          return success({ version, findings: compiled.findings.filter((f) => f.severity === "worthKnowing") });
        });
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof KernelRefused) {
          // A bug in core: the compiler's output fails the kernel's own check (core-api.md section 12).
          console.error("the kernel publish check refused a compiled definition", error.message);
          return failure("internal", {});
        }
        throw error;
      }
    },

    async listVersions(_caller, workflow) {
      if ((await readWorkflowPeople(db, workflow)) === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
      return success((await listVersionRows(db, workflow)).map(versionSummaryOf));
    },

    async getVersion(_caller, workflow, version) {
      if ((await readWorkflowPeople(db, workflow)) === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
      const row = await readVersionRow(db, workflow, version);
      if (row === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "version" });
      return success<Version>({ ...versionSummaryOf(row), authored: row.authored as unknown as AuthoredWorkflow });
    },

    async getSettings(_caller, workflow) {
      const row = await readSettings(db, workflow);
      return row === null ? failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" }) : success(settingsReadOf(row.record, row.changedBy, row.changedAt));
    },

    async saveSettings(caller, workflow, settings: Settings) {
      // A body's shape first (invalid-body), then who may (authoring-api.md section 5, operation 9).
      if (settings.stuckRequestsGoTo !== undefined && settings.stuckRequestsGoTo.length === 0) {
        return failure("invalid-body", { field: "/stuckRequestsGoTo", problem: "empty" });
      }
      const refused = await mustBeAuthor(caller, workflow, groupsOnce(deps.memberships, caller));
      if (refused !== null) return { ok: false, errors: [refused] };
      if (settings.authors.length === 0) return failure("last-author", {});
      const after: SettingsRecord = {
        name: settings.name,
        description: settings.description,
        authors: settings.authors,
        ...(settings.stuckRequestsGoTo === undefined ? {} : { stuckRequestsGoTo: settings.stuckRequestsGoTo }),
      };
      const by = userBy(caller);
      const at = timestamp(clock());
      return db.transaction(async (tx): Promise<Result<SettingsRead>> => {
        if (!(await lockWorkflow(tx, workflow))) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
        const before = await readSettings(tx, workflow);
        if (before === null) return failure("not-found", { what: "workflow" });
        await writeSettings(tx, workflow, before.record, after, by, at);
        return success(settingsReadOf(after, by, at));
      });
    },

    async getMeta() {
      return success(meta);
    },

    async getCatalogue() {
      return success(deps.catalogue.current());
    },
  };
}

/**
 * The authoring API's types, as contract/authoring-api.md section 3 gives them. Shared types (`Ref`,
 * `Finding`, `CoreMeta`, `Draft` ...) are core's.
 */
import type {
  AuthoredWorkflow,
  Caller,
  Catalogue,
  CatalogueRef,
  CoreMeta,
  Draft,
  Finding,
  Ref,
  Result,
  ServerWorkflowId,
  Timestamp,
  VersionNumber,
} from "@workflow/core";

export interface May {
  edit: boolean;
  publish: boolean;
  settings: boolean;
}

export interface WorkflowSummary {
  id: ServerWorkflowId;
  name: string;
  /** May be "". */
  description: string;
  /** The highest published version; absent: never published. */
  liveVersion?: VersionNumber;
  draft: { revision: number; savedAt: Timestamp; savedBy: Ref; changedSinceLive: boolean; todo: number; worthKnowing: number };
  /** The catalogue triggers its "Starts when" bindings use, document order, no repeats. */
  triggers: { live: CatalogueRef[]; draft: CatalogueRef[] };
  /** Not closed, all versions. */
  openRequests: number;
  /** Stuck, for any reason. */
  stuckRequests: number;
  may: May;
}

/** A draft as the API returns it: core's `Draft` (authoring-api.md section 3). */
export type { Draft };

export interface SavedDraft {
  revision: number;
  savedAt: Timestamp;
  todo: number;
  worthKnowing: number;
}

/** `findings`: Worth knowing only. */
export interface PublishResult {
  version: VersionNumber;
  findings: Finding[];
}

export interface VersionSummary {
  version: VersionNumber;
  publishedAt: Timestamp;
  publishedBy: Ref;
  fromRevision: number;
  coreVersion: string;
  formatVersion: number;
  /** Requests on this version not closed. */
  openRequests: number;
}

/** As published, not upgraded; the compiled definition stays on the server. */
export interface Version extends VersionSummary {
  authored: AuthoredWorkflow;
}

export interface Settings {
  name: string;
  /** May be "". */
  description: string;
  /** At least one; users and groups. */
  authors: Ref[];
  /** Absent: the authors; never an empty list. */
  stuckRequestsGoTo?: Ref[];
}

export interface SettingsRead extends Settings {
  /** Who made the last change; the creator until the first save. */
  changedBy: Ref;
  changedAt: Timestamp;
}

export interface CreateWorkflowArgs {
  name: string;
  description?: string;
}

export interface SaveDraftArgs {
  baseRevision: number;
  /** Any JSON: the server parses it. */
  authored: unknown;
}

export interface PublishArgs {
  revision: number;
  coreVersion: string;
}

/** The authoring API's operations (authoring-api.md section 5), as plain functions. */
export interface AuthoringApi {
  listWorkflows(caller: Caller): Promise<Result<WorkflowSummary[]>>;
  createWorkflow(caller: Caller, args: CreateWorkflowArgs): Promise<Result<Draft>>;
  getDraft(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId): Promise<Result<Draft>>;
  saveDraft(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId, args: SaveDraftArgs): Promise<Result<SavedDraft>>;
  publish(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId, args: PublishArgs): Promise<Result<PublishResult>>;
  listVersions(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId): Promise<Result<VersionSummary[]>>;
  getVersion(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId, version: VersionNumber): Promise<Result<Version>>;
  getSettings(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId): Promise<Result<SettingsRead>>;
  saveSettings(caller: Caller, workflow: ServerWorkflowId, settings: Settings): Promise<Result<SettingsRead>>;
  getMeta(): Promise<Result<CoreMeta>>;
  getCatalogue(caller: Caller): Promise<Result<Catalogue>>;

}
