===\nengine/packages/server/src/hooks/inbound.ts\n===
/**
 * The inbound endpoint, door 1 (integrations.md 9.6 to 9.10; runtime-api.md section 8):
 * `POST /hooks/v1/events/{connection}`. Before any transaction: the body's size, the connection, its status,
 * the connector's verify and parse, and each event against its trigger's fields. Then, for every workflow
 * whose highest version has a binding on this connection for a parsed event, in workflow ID order: the
 * dedupe, core's binding mapping, the pause, and the start turn. Every answer and every workflow's result is
 * one `inbound_log` row; a start writes its row in its own transaction, and that row's unique index is the
 * dedupe. A refused start, a pause included, is listed and can be run again from its row (`rerun`).
 */
import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { CatalogueEntry, Location, Ref, Refusal, Result } from "@workflow/core";
import { mapBinding, type By, type Json, type JsonObject, type PublishedDefinition } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import { toApiError } from "../api/runtime/refusals.ts";
import type { RetriedStart } from "../api/runtime/types.ts";
import type { CatalogueRegistry } from "../api/shared/catalogue.ts";
import { engineHeaders } from "../api/shared/http.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";
import type { Connectors, RawRequest } from "../connectors/types.ts";
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "../store/definitions.ts";
import { formatAt } from "../turn/turns.ts";
import type { Turns } from "../turn/types.ts";

export const HOOKS_PATH = "/hooks/v1/events/:connection";
/** 256 KiB. */
export const HOOK_BODY_LIMIT = 262_144;

export interface InboundProblem {
  code: string;
  where: Location | null;
  params: JsonObject;
}

export type InboundResult =
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "started"; binding: string; requestId: string; readableId: number }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "duplicate"; binding: string; requestId: string; readableId: number }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "notMatched" }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "paused"; binding: string }
  | { workflow: string; version: number; result: "refused"; binding: string; problems: InboundProblem[] };

/** A start that could not be made now; nothing was started for that workflow. */
type Unavailable = { workflow: string; version: number; result: "unavailable"; code: "busy" | "source-unavailable" };

export interface HooksDeps {
  db: Db;
  turns: Turns;
  definitions: DefinitionReader;
  catalogue: CatalogueRegistry;
  connectors: Connectors;
  log: Log;
  clock?: () => Date;
}

export interface Hooks {
  /** The hook's answer to one request for `connection`. */
  handle(connection: string, request: Request): Promise<Response>;
  /** Runs a refused start again for its workflow, on that workflow's live version (integrations.md 9.10). */
  rerun(id: number, workflow: string, by: Ref): Promise<Result<RetriedStart>>;
}

/** The hook as a route. */
export function hookRoutes(hooks: Hooks): Hono {
  const app = new Hono();
  app.post(HOOKS_PATH, (c) => hooks.handle(c.req.param("connection"), c.req.raw));
  return app;
}

const json = (status: number, body: unknown, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Response =>
  new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8", ...engineHeaders(), ...headers } });

async function readBody(request: Request): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {
  const declared = Number(request.headers.get("content-length") ?? "NaN");
  if (Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > HOOK_BODY_LIMIT) return null;
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  let size = 0;
  if (request.body !== null) {
    const reader = request.body.getReader();
    for (;;) {
      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      size += value.byteLength;
      if (size > HOOK_BODY_LIMIT) {
        await reader.cancel();
        return null;
      }
      chunks.push(value);
    }
  }
  return Buffer.concat(chunks);
}

/** Whether a sent value fits a trigger field's kind; a missing required field does not. */
function fits(entry: Extract<CatalogueEntry, { kind: "trigger" }>, event: JsonObject): boolean {
  const isObject = (v: Json | undefined): v is JsonObject => typeof v === "object" && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v);
  return entry.event.every((f) => {
    const v = event[f.id];
    if (v === undefined) return !f.required;
    switch (f.kind) {
      case "text":
      case "longText":
        return typeof v === "string";
      case "choice":
        return typeof v === "string" && (f.choices ?? []).some((c) => c.value === v);
      case "choiceFromConnection":
        return isObject(v) && (typeof v["stored"] === "string" || typeof v["stored"] === "number") && typeof v["label"] === "string";
      case "person":
        return isObject(v) && v["type"] === "user" && typeof v["id"] === "string";
      default:
        return true;
    }
  });
}

export function createHooks(deps: HooksDeps): Hooks {
  const { db, log } = deps;
  const clock = deps.clock ?? (() => new Date());

  interface Row {
    connection: string | null;
    eventId?: string | null;
    workflow?: string;
    version?: number;
    binding?: string;
    result?: string;
    code?: string;
    problems?: InboundProblem[];
    requestId?: string;
    sent?: JsonObject;
    by?: Ref;
    retryOf?: number;
  }
  async function write(r: Row): Promise<void> {
    await db.query(
      `INSERT INTO inbound_log (at, connection, event_id, workflow, version, binding, result, code, problems, request_id, sent, by, retry_of)
       VALUES ($1::timestamptz, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9::jsonb, $10, $11::jsonb, $12::jsonb, $13)`,
      [
        formatAt(clock()),
        r.connection,
        r.eventId ?? null,
        r.workflow ?? null,
        r.version ?? null,
        r.binding ?? null,
        r.result ?? null,
        r.code ?? null,
        r.problems === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(r.problems),
        r.requestId ?? null,
        r.sent === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(r.sent),
        r.by === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(r.by),
        r.retryOf ?? null,
      ],
    );
  }

  /** A hook answer before any workflow: one row, and a log line for a final refusal. */
  async function refuse(connection: string | null, status: number, error: string, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<Response> {
    await write({ connection, code: error });
    if (status !== 503) log({ kind: "inbound-refused", ...(connection === null ? {} : { connection }), code: error });
    return json(status, { error }, headers);
  }

  async function startedRow(connection: string, eventId: string, workflow: string) {
    const rows = await db.query<{ version: number; binding: string; request_id: string; readable_id: number | string }>(
      `SELECT l.version, l.binding, l.request_id, r.readable_id FROM inbound_log l JOIN requests r ON r.id = l.request_id
       WHERE l.connection = $1 AND l.event_id = $2 AND l.workflow = $3 AND l.result = 'started'`,
      [connection, eventId, workflow],
    );
    const r = rows[0];
    return r === undefined ? undefined : { version: Number(r.version), binding: r.binding, requestId: r.request_id, readableId: Number(r.readable_id) };
  }

  /** Steps 1 to 8 of integrations.md 9.7 for one workflow. */
  async function startFor(
    def: PublishedDefinition,
    connection: string,
    eventId: string,
    sent: { [event: string]: JsonObject },
    again?: { by: Ref; retryOf: number },
  ): Promise<InboundResult | Unavailable> {
    const { workflow, version } = def;
    const duplicate = async (): Promise<InboundResult | undefined> => {
      const s = await startedRow(connection, eventId, workflow);
      return s === undefined ? undefined : { workflow, version: s.version, result: "duplicate", binding: s.binding, requestId: s.requestId, readableId: s.readableId };
    };
    const earlier = await duplicate();
    if (earlier !== undefined) return earlier;
    for (const binding of def.triggers ?? []) {
      const event = binding.connection === connection ? sent[binding.event] : undefined;
      if (event === undefined) continue;
      // Its `when` alone first: an event this binding takes is refused as paused before its mapping runs.
      const taken = mapBinding(def, { ...binding, data: {} }, event);
      if (taken.kind === "notMatched") continue;
      if (taken.kind === "start") {
        const paused = await db.query("SELECT 1 FROM workflow_settings WHERE workflow = $1 AND $2 = ANY (paused_bindings)", [workflow, binding.id]);
        if (paused.length > 0) return { workflow, version, result: "paused", binding: binding.id };
      }
      const run = taken.kind === "start" ? mapBinding(def, binding, event) : taken;
      if (run.kind === "notMatched") continue;
      if (run.kind === "mappingError") {
        return { workflow, version, result: "refused", binding: binding.id, problems: [{ code: "mapping-error", where: run.location as Location, params: { error: run.error } }] };
      }
      let out;
      try {
        out = await deps.turns.start({
          workflow,
          version,
          by: { type: "connection", id: connection },
          outcome: run.outcome,
          data: run.data,
          trigger: { kind: "event", id: binding.id, connection, event: binding.event, eventId },
          inbound: { sent, ...(again === undefined ? {} : { by: again.by as By, retryOf: again.retryOf }) },
        });
      } catch {
        return { workflow, version, result: "unavailable", code: "busy" };
      }
      if (out.ok) return { workflow, version, result: "started", binding: binding.id, requestId: out.requestId, readableId: out.readableId };
      const reasons = out.refusals.map((r) => r.reason);
      if (reasons.includes("already-started")) return (await duplicate()) ?? { workflow, version, result: "unavailable", code: "busy" };
      if (reasons.includes("busy") || reasons.includes("not-found")) return { workflow, version, result: "unavailable", code: "busy" };
      if (reasons.includes("source-unavailable")) return { workflow, version, result: "unavailable", code: "source-unavailable" };
      const published = await deps.definitions.published(db, workflow, version);
      if (published === null) return { workflow, version, result: "unavailable", code: "busy" };
      const problems = out.refusals.map((k): InboundProblem => {
        const e = toApiError(published, k, { element: def.start, button: run.outcome, answers: run.data as never });
        return { code: e.code, where: e.location ?? null, params: e.params as JsonObject };
      });
      return { workflow, version, result: "refused", binding: binding.id, problems };
    }
    return { workflow, version, result: "notMatched" };
  }

  /** Writes a result's row (a start wrote its own) and its log line. */
  async function record(r: InboundResult | Unavailable, connection: string, eventId: string, sent: JsonObject, again?: { by: Ref; retryOf: number }): Promise<void> {
    if (r.result === "started") return;
    const base: Row = {
      connection,
      eventId,
      workflow: r.workflow,
      ...(r.version > 0 ? { version: r.version } : {}),
      result: r.result,
      sent,
      ...(again === undefined ? {} : { by: again.by, retryOf: again.retryOf }),
    };
    if (r.result === "refused") {
      await write({ ...base, binding: r.binding, code: r.problems[0]?.code ?? "refused", problems: r.problems });
      log({ kind: "start-refused", connection, binding: r.binding, code: r.problems[0]?.code ?? "refused" });
    } else if (r.result === "paused") {
      await write({ ...base, binding: r.binding, code: "paused" });
      log({ kind: "start-refused", connection, binding: r.binding, code: "paused" });
    } else if (r.result === "duplicate") {
      await write({ ...base, binding: r.binding, requestId: r.requestId });
    } else if (r.result === "unavailable") {
      await write({ ...base, code: r.code });
    } else {
      await write(base);
    }
  }

  /** The highest version of each workflow with a binding on this connection for one of the events, in workflow ID order. */
  async function candidates(connection: string, events: readonly string[]): Promise<PublishedDefinition[]> {
    const rows = await db.query<{ workflow: string; version: number }>(
      `SELECT d.workflow, d.version FROM definitions d
       WHERE d.version = (SELECT max(x.version) FROM definitions x WHERE x.workflow = d.workflow)
         AND d.document->'triggers' @> $1::jsonb
       ORDER BY d.workflow`,
      [JSON.stringify([{ connection }])],
    );
    const out: PublishedDefinition[] = [];
    for (const r of rows) {
      const def = await deps.definitions.get(db, r.workflow, Number(r.version));
      if (def?.triggers?.some((t) => t.connection === connection && events.includes(t.event))) out.push(def);
    }
    return out;
  }

  return {
    async handle(connection, request) {
      const body = await readBody(request);
      const catalogue = deps.catalogue.current();
      const known = catalogue.entries.some((e) => e.connection === connection && e.kind === "trigger");
      if (body === null) return refuse(known ? connection : null, 413, "too-large");
      if (!known) return refuse(null, 404, "unknown-connection");
      const trigger = deps.connectors.trigger?.(connection);
      if (catalogue.connections.find((c) => c.id === connection)?.status !== "ready" || trigger === undefined) {
        return refuse(connection, 503, "connection-unavailable", { "Retry-After": "300" });
      }
      const headers: { [name: string]: string } = {};
      request.headers.forEach((value, name) => (headers[name.toLowerCase()] = value));
      const raw: RawRequest = { method: request.method, headers, body };
      const verified = await trigger.verify(raw);
      if (verified.answer !== "ok") return refuse(connection, 401, "unauthenticated");
      const parsed = await trigger.parse(raw);
      if (parsed.answer === "unparsable") return refuse(connection, 400, "unparsable");
      if (parsed.answer === "unavailable") {
        log({ kind: "directory-unavailable", connection });
        return refuse(connection, 503, "unavailable", { "Retry-After": "60" });
      }
      if (parsed.answer === "ignored") {
        await write({ connection, eventId: parsed.eventId, code: "ignored" });
        return json(200, { eventId: parsed.eventId, results: [] });
      }
      for (const [name, event] of Object.entries(parsed.events)) {
        const entry = catalogue.entries.find((e) => e.id === `${connection}.${name}`);
        if (entry?.kind !== "trigger" || !fits(entry, event)) return refuse(connection, 400, "event-invalid");
      }
      const results: InboundResult[] = [];
      let unavailable = false;
      for (const def of await candidates(connection, Object.keys(parsed.events))) {
        const r = await startFor(def, connection, parsed.eventId, parsed.events);
        await record(r, connection, parsed.eventId, parsed.events);
        if (r.result === "unavailable") unavailable = true;
        else results.push(r);
      }
      if (unavailable) return json(503, { error: "unavailable" }, { "Retry-After": "60" });
      return json(200, { eventId: parsed.eventId, results });
    },

    async rerun(id, workflow, by) {
      const rows = await db.query<{ connection: string; event_id: string; sent: { [event: string]: JsonObject } }>(
        "SELECT connection, event_id, sent FROM inbound_log WHERE id = $1 AND workflow = $2 AND result IN ('refused', 'paused') AND sent IS NOT NULL",
        [id, workflow],
      );
      const row = rows[0];
      if (row === undefined) return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: "not-found", params: { what: "refusedStart" } }] };
      const live = (await candidates(row.connection, Object.keys(row.sent))).find((d) => d.workflow === workflow);
      const again = { by, retryOf: id };
      const r: InboundResult | Unavailable = live === undefined ? { workflow, version: 0, result: "notMatched" } : await startFor(live, row.connection, row.event_id, row.sent, again);
      // A run again that could not be made now writes nothing.
      if (r.result === "unavailable") return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: r.code, params: {} }] };
      await record(r, row.connection, row.event_id, row.sent, again);
      switch (r.result) {
        case "started":
          return { ok: true, value: { result: "started", requestId: r.requestId, readableId: String(r.readableId), binding: r.binding as never, version: r.version } };
        case "duplicate":
          return { ok: true, value: { result: "duplicate", requestId: r.requestId, readableId: String(r.readableId) } };
        case "paused":
          return { ok: true, value: { result: "paused", binding: r.binding as never } };
        case "refused":
          return {
            ok: true,
            value: { result: "refused", binding: r.binding as never, refusals: r.problems.map((p) => ({ code: p.code, params: p.params, ...(p.where === null ? {} : { location: p.where }) }) as Refusal) },
          };
        default:
          return { ok: true, value: { result: "notMatched" } };
      }
    },
  };
}

/**
 * @workflow/server: the engine's server (decision E-3). Folders: `store` (schema, events, the tables read from
 * them), `turn` (the turn transaction), `api` (the authoring and runtime APIs over HTTP), `connectors` (the
 * connector interface and its in-memory implementation), `config` (the configuration, the catalogue built from
 * it, the log), `workers` (the worker loop: calls, notifications, outbound events), and, still empty, `hooks`,
 * `mock` and `dev-host`.
 */
export * from "./store/index.ts";
export * from "./turn/index.ts";
export * from "./config/index.ts";
export * from "./workers/index.ts";
export * from "./api/authoring/index.ts";
// The runtime API as a namespace: its contract types (`RequestRow`, `Page` ...) share names with the store's and the authoring API's.
export * as runtime from "./api/runtime/index.ts";
export * as connectors from "./connectors/index.ts";
export { devHeaderCaller, DEV_PLATFORM_ADMIN_HEADER, DEV_USER_HEADER, type CallerAdapter } from "./api/caller.ts";
export { fixedCatalogue, type CatalogueRegistry } from "./api/shared/catalogue.ts";
export type { Memberships } from "./api/shared/people.ts";

import { CEL_PROFILE, compile, coreVersion, meta, type AuthoredWorkflow, type Catalogue, type Finding } from "@workflow/core";
import { checkDefinition, type PublishProblem } from "@workflow/core/kernel";

export interface ServerInfo {
  coreVersion: string;
  celProfile: string;
  definitionFormatVersion: number;
}

/** What the API will report so that a stale browser bundle of core can be detected (E-3). */
export function serverInfo(): ServerInfo {
  return { coreVersion, celProfile: CEL_PROFILE, definitionFormatVersion: meta.definitionFormatVersion };
}

/** A definition may be published when no problem of the kernel's publish check is an error (E-27). */
export function publishable(problems: readonly PublishProblem[]): boolean {
  return problems.every((p) => p.severity !== "error");
}

/**
 * The publish step as the server will run it: compile the draft, then run the kernel's publish check on
 * the result, with the catalogue. Either step may refuse; a warning does not.
 */
export function publishCheck(
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow,
  catalogue: Catalogue,
): { ok: true; warnings: PublishProblem[] } | { ok: false; findings: Finding[] } | { ok: false; problems: PublishProblem[] } {
  const compiled = compile(workflow, catalogue);
  if (!compiled.ok) return { ok: false, findings: compiled.findings };
  const problems = checkDefinition(compiled.published, catalogue);
  return publishable(problems) ? { ok: true, warnings: problems } : { ok: false, problems };
}

/**
 * The mock systems as the hosts register them (mock-systems.md section 2): one connector per connection of
 * the mock catalogue (contract/fixtures/catalogue.json), each declaring that connection's entries, and the
 * seed configuration with fixed test secrets. The catalogue the server builds from them is that fixture,

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import type { Catalogue } from "@workflow/core";
import type { ConnectorDefinition, ConnectorParts, EngineConfig, EntryDeclaration } from "../config/config.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";
import {
  HELPDESK_SECRET,
  mockDeploy,
  mockDirectory,
  mockHelpdesk,
  mockJira,
  mockMessages,
  mockReporting,
  mockServiceCatalog,
  type MockDeploy,
  type MockDirectory,

export const MOCK_CATALOGUE = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../../../../contract/fixtures/catalogue.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) as Catalogue;

export interface Mocks {
  directory: MockDirectory;
  servicecatalog: MockServiceCatalog;
  helpdesk: MockHelpdesk;
  jira: MockJira;
  deploy: MockDeploy;
  messages: MockMessages;
  reporting: MockReporting;
  /** The connectors, for `loadConfig`. */
  registry: ConnectorDefinition[];
  /** The seed configuration. */
  config: EngineConfig;
  /** The environment the configuration's secrets are read from: fixed test values. */
  env: Record<string, string>;
}

const ENV = { MOCK_HELPDESK_INBOUND: HELPDESK_SECRET };

/** The entries the mock catalogue gives a connection, as a connector declares them. */
function entriesOf(connection: string): EntryDeclaration[] {
  return MOCK_CATALOGUE.entries
    .filter((e) => e.connection === connection)
    .map((e) => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(e).filter(([k]) => k !== "id" && k !== "connection" && k !== "status")) as EntryDeclaration);
}

/**
 * Fresh mock systems on `clock`, with the connectors and configuration that use them. `log` gets a line per
 * message sent and event received. `requestOf` names the request a call's idempotency key belongs to, for
 * what the mocks remember; without it they remember none.
 */
export function createMocks(clock: () => Date = () => new Date(), log?: Log, requestOf: (key: string) => Promise<string | null> = async () => null): Mocks {
  const rec: Recorder = { clock, requestOf };
  const directory = mockDirectory(rec);
  const servicecatalog = mockServiceCatalog(rec);
  let helpdeskSecret = "";
  const helpdesk = mockHelpdesk(directory, clock, () => helpdeskSecret);
  const jira = mockJira(rec);
  const deploy = mockDeploy(rec);
  const messages = mockMessages(log, clock);
  const reporting = mockReporting(log);

  const parts: Record<string, (secret: (slot: string) => string) => ConnectorParts> = {
    directory: () => ({ directory, operation: directory.operation }),
    servicecatalog: () => ({ dataSource: servicecatalog.dataSource, operation: servicecatalog.operation }),
    helpdesk: (secret) => {
      helpdeskSecret = secret("inbound");
      return { trigger: helpdesk.trigger };
    },
    jira: () => ({ operation: jira.operation }),
    deploy: () => ({ operation: deploy.operation }),
    messages: () => ({ notifier: messages }),
    reporting: () => ({}),
  };
  const registry: ConnectorDefinition[] = Object.entries(parts).map(([connection, open]) => ({
    name: `mock-${connection}`,
    secrets: connection === "helpdesk" ? ["inbound"] : [],
    entries: () => entriesOf(connection),
    open: (c) => open(c.secret),
  }));
  const config: EngineConfig = {
    directoryConnection: MOCK_CATALOGUE.directoryConnection,
    notifyConnection: MOCK_CATALOGUE.notifyConnection,
    deploymentUri: "http://dev-host.localhost",
    connections: MOCK_CATALOGUE.connections.map((c) => ({
      id: c.id,
      connector: `mock-${c.id}`,
      label: c.label,
      ...(c.description === null ? {} : { description: c.description }),
      status: c.status,
      config: {},
      secrets: c.id === "helpdesk" ? { inbound: "MOCK_HELPDESK_INBOUND" } : {},
    })),
    subscribers: [{ url: "http://reporting.mock.test/events" }],
  };
  return { directory, servicecatalog, helpdesk, jira, deploy, messages, reporting, registry, config, env: { ...ENV } };
}

/**
 * What the mock of `connection` received, oldest first, only `request`'s when given: messages as sent,
 * outbound event bodies as posted, calls with their answers; the helpdesk receives nothing.
 */
export function receivedBy(mocks: Mocks, connection: string, request?: string): unknown[] {
  const mine = (r: string | null): boolean => request === undefined || r === request;
  switch (connection) {
    case "messages":
      return mocks.messages.received.filter((m) => mine(m.request));
    case "reporting":
      return mocks.reporting.received.map((r) => r.event).filter((e) => mine(e.subject));
    case "directory":
    case "servicecatalog":
    case "jira":
    case "deploy":
      return mocks[connection].received.filter((c) => mine(c.request));
    default:
      return [];
  }
}

/**
 * The dev host's `--seed`: the three sample workflows of contract/fixtures, created, given their settings
 * and published through the authoring API as Sam Carter, the demo's author, so the runtime screens have
 * something to show. A workflow that already exists is left as it is.
 */
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { coreVersion, type Caller, type Ref, type Result } from "@workflow/core";
import { createAuthoringApi } from "../api/authoring/operations.ts";
import type { CatalogueRegistry } from "../api/shared/catalogue.ts";
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";

const SAMPLES = ["change-request", "several-at-once", "integrated-sample"] as const;
const SAM: Caller = { user: "dir-user-sam-carter", platformAdmin: false };

const fixture = (name: string): unknown => JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL(`../../../../../contract/fixtures/${name}`, import.meta.url), "utf8"));

function must<T>(r: Result<T>, what: string): T {
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`seed: ${what}: ${JSON.stringify(r.errors)}`);
  return r.value;
}

/** Publishes each sample not yet there as version 1; returns the workflow IDs published. */
export async function seedSamples(db: Db, catalogue: CatalogueRegistry, clock: () => Date): Promise<string[]> {
  const records = fixture("records.json") as Record<string, { name: string; description: string; stuckRequestsGoTo: Ref[] }>;
  const published: string[] = [];
  for (const id of SAMPLES) {
    if ((await db.query("SELECT 1 FROM workflows WHERE id = $1", [id])).length > 0) continue;
    const record = records[id];
    if (record === undefined) throw new Error(`seed: no record for ${id}`);
    const api = createAuthoringApi({ db, catalogue, clock, memberships: { memberships: async () => ({ groups: [] }) }, newWorkflowId: () => id });
    must(await api.createWorkflow(SAM, { name: record.name, description: record.description }), `create ${id}`);
    const saved = must(await api.saveDraft(SAM, id, { baseRevision: 1, authored: fixture(`${id}.authored.json`) }), `save ${id}`);
    const stuckRequestsGoTo = record.stuckRequestsGoTo.map(({ type, id: ref }) => ({ type, id: ref }));
    must(await api.saveSettings(SAM, id, { name: record.name, description: record.description, authors: [{ type: "user", id: SAM.user }], stuckRequestsGoTo }), `settings ${id}`);
    must(await api.publish(SAM, id, { revision: saved.revision, coreVersion }), `publish ${id}`);
    published.push(id);
  }
  return published;
}

/**
 * The seven mock systems (engine/design/mock-systems.md), in memory: a directory, a service catalog, a
 * helpdesk that sends events to the hook, a ticket system (Jira), a deploy pipeline, the messages
 * connection and a reporting system that receives outbound events. Each keeps its state in plain fields a
 * test or the dev host can read, and has at most two switches: `failNext` (the next call fails clearly) and
 * `down` (nothing answers). Counters start at the seed, so every run sees the same IDs. Each also remembers
 * what it was sent (`received`, the newest 1,000), for the dev host's control surface.
 */
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import type { OutboundEventBody } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { JsonObject } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Subscriber } from "../config/config.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";
import { directoryOperation } from "../connectors/directory-source.ts";
import type {
  CallAnswer,
  DataSourceConnector,
  Directory,
  DirectoryEntry,
  Notifier,
  OperationConnector,
  OutgoingMessage,
  ParseAnswer,
  RawRequest,
  StatusAnswer,
  TriggerConnector,
} from "../connectors/types.ts";

const user = (slug: string): string => `dir-user-${slug}`;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what a mock received

/** How many items a mock remembers; the oldest go first. */
export const RECEIVED_LIMIT = 1000;

/** Adds `item`, dropping the oldest beyond the limit. */
export function remember<T>(list: T[], item: T): void {
  list.push(item);
  if (list.length > RECEIVED_LIMIT) list.splice(0, list.length - RECEIVED_LIMIT);
}

/** What a mock answered a call or status question; `none` is no answer (down, or the directory could not be read). */
export type ReceivedAnswer = Exclude<CallAnswer | StatusAnswer, { answer: "unknown" }> | { answer: "none"; detail: string };

/** One call (or an await's status question) a mock received. */
export interface CallItem {
  at: string;
  /** The request whose call it is; null when the host cannot tell. */
  request: string | null;
  operation: string;
  kind: "call" | "status";
  key: string;
  /** The call's input as sent; for a status question `{ jobRef }`. */
  input: JsonObject;
  answer: ReceivedAnswer;
}

/** What a mock needs to remember a call: the time, and the request a call's key belongs to. */
export interface Recorder {
  clock: () => Date;
  requestOf(key: string): Promise<string | null>;
}

const NO_RECORDER: Recorder = { clock: () => new Date(), requestOf: async () => null };

/** `op`, remembering each call and status question in `list`. */
function recorded(op: OperationConnector, list: CallItem[], rec: Recorder): OperationConnector {
  const keep = async <A extends CallAnswer | StatusAnswer>(kind: CallItem["kind"], opName: string, key: string, input: JsonObject, ask: () => Promise<A>): Promise<A> => {
    const request = await rec.requestOf(key).catch(() => null);
    const item = (answer: ReceivedAnswer): void => remember(list, { at: rec.clock().toISOString(), request, operation: opName, kind, key, input, answer });
    try {
      const answer = await ask();
      item(answer.answer === "unknown" ? { answer: "none", detail: answer.detail } : (answer as ReceivedAnswer));
      return answer;
    } catch (error) {
      item({ answer: "none", detail: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
      throw error;
    }
  };
  const status = op.status?.bind(op);
  return {
    call: (req) => keep("call", req.op, req.key, req.args, () => op.call(req)),
    ...(status === undefined ? {} : { status: (req: Parameters<typeof status>[0]) => keep("status", req.op, req.key, { jobRef: req.jobRef }, () => status(req)) }),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- directory

export interface MockDirectory extends Directory {
  down: boolean;
  /** Group ID to its members' IDs; a test may change it. */
  readonly members: Map<string, string[]>;
  /** A person's ID by email; null when nobody has it; "unavailable" when down. */
  findUser(email: string): "unavailable" | string | null;
  /** The recorded read `membersOf@1` through these reads, remembering each call. */
  operation: OperationConnector;
  /** Every recorded read received, oldest first. */
  readonly received: CallItem[];
}

export function mockDirectory(rec: Recorder = NO_RECORDER): MockDirectory {
  const received: CallItem[] = [];
  const members = new Map(GROUPS.map((g) => [g.id, [...g.members]]));
  const entryOf = (type: "user" | "group", id: string): DirectoryEntry | undefined => {
    if (type === "user") {
      const p = PEOPLE.find((x) => x.id === id);
      return p && { type, id, label: p.name, detail: p.email };
    }
    const g = GROUPS.find((x) => x.id === id);
    return g && { type, id, label: g.name, detail: g.detail };
  };
  const up = (): void => {
    if (dir.down) throw new Error("the directory is down");
  };
  const dir: MockDirectory = {
    down: false,
    members,
    async groupsOf(id) {
      up();
      return [...members].filter(([, users]) => users.includes(id)).map(([g]) => g);
    },
    async membersOf(id) {
      up();
      return (members.get(id) ?? []).flatMap((u) => entryOf("user", u) ?? []);
    },
    async search(query, types, limit) {
      up();
      const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();
      const all = [...(types.includes("user") ? PEOPLE.map((p) => entryOf("user", p.id)) : []), ...(types.includes("group") ? GROUPS.map((g) => entryOf("group", g.id)) : [])];
      return all
        .flatMap((e) => e ?? [])
        .filter((e) => q === "" || e.label.toLowerCase().includes(q) || (e.detail ?? "").toLowerCase().includes(q))
        .sort((a, b) => a.label.localeCompare(b.label))
        .slice(0, limit);
    },
    async lookup(refs) {
      up();
      return refs.flatMap((r) => entryOf(r.type, r.id) ?? []);
    },
    findUser(email) {
      if (dir.down) return "unavailable";
      return PEOPLE.find((p) => p.email === email.toLowerCase())?.id ?? null;
    },
    operation: { call: async () => ({ answer: "unknown", detail: "not set up" }) },
    received,
  };
  dir.operation = recorded(directoryOperation(dir), received, rec);
  return dir;
}

export interface Service {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  tier: string;
  status: "active" | "retired";
  owner?: string;
}

export interface MockServiceCatalog {
  failNext: boolean;
  down: boolean;
  /** The services; a test may add, rename or retire one. */
  readonly services: Service[];
  dataSource: DataSourceConnector;
  operation: OperationConnector;
  /** Every operation call received, oldest first (its list and get reads are not kept). */
  readonly received: CallItem[];
}

/** The seeded services. */
export const SERVICES: readonly Service[] = [
  { id: "svc-payments-api", name: "Payments API", tier: "Tier 1", status: "active", owner: user("diego-santos") },
  { id: "svc-ledger", name: "Ledger", tier: "Tier 2", status: "active" },
  { id: "svc-docs-site", name: "Docs site", tier: "Tier 3", status: "active", owner: user("mei-lin") },
  { id: "svc-old-billing", name: "Old billing", tier: "Tier 3", status: "retired", owner: user("diego-santos") },
];

export function mockServiceCatalog(rec: Recorder = NO_RECORDER): MockServiceCatalog {
  const services: Service[] = SERVICES.map((s) => ({ ...s }));
  const received: CallItem[] = [];
  const item = (s: Service): JsonObject => ({ id: s.id, name: s.name, tier: s.tier, status: s.status, ...(s.owner === undefined ? {} : { owner: { type: "user", id: s.owner } }) });
  const listed = (inputs: JsonObject): Service[] => services.filter((s) => inputs["status"] === undefined || s.status === inputs["status"]).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
  const sc: MockServiceCatalog = {
    failNext: false,
    down: false,
    services,
    received,
    dataSource: {
      async list(req) {
        if (sc.down) return { answer: "unavailable", detail: "the service catalog is down" };
        const q = req.search?.toLowerCase();
        const hits = listed(req.inputs).filter((s) => q === undefined || s.name.toLowerCase().includes(q));
        const offset = Number.parseInt(req.cursor ?? "0", 10) || 0;
        return { answer: "ok", items: hits.slice(offset, offset + req.limit).map(item), next: offset + req.limit < hits.length ? String(offset + req.limit) : null };
      },
      async get(req) {
        if (sc.down) return { answer: "unavailable", detail: "the service catalog is down" };
        const found = listed(req.inputs).find((s) => item(s)[req.field] === req.value);
        return found === undefined ? { answer: "notFound" } : { answer: "found", item: item(found) };
      },
    },
    operation: recorded(
      {
        async call(req): Promise<CallAnswer> {
          if (sc.down) return { answer: "unknown", detail: "the service catalog is down" };
          const asked = req.args["serviceId"];
          const id = typeof asked === "object" && asked !== null && !Array.isArray(asked) ? asked["stored"] : asked;
          const found = services.find((s) => s.id === id);
          if (sc.failNext || found === undefined) {
            sc.failNext = false;
            return { answer: "failed", code: "service-not-found", message: `No service with ID ${String(id)}.` };
          }
          return { answer: "ok", data: item(found) };
        },
      },
      received,
      rec,
    ),
  };
  return sc;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpdesk (door 1)

/** The helpdesk's fixed test secret for Standard Webhooks: "whsec_" + base64 of its key. */
export const HELPDESK_SECRET = `whsec_${Buffer.from("dev-host-helpdesk-inbound-key").toString("base64")}`;

export interface Ticket {
  key: string;
  title: string;
  description?: string;
  category: string;
  priority?: string;
  service: { id: string; name: string };
  reporterEmail?: string;
  url?: string;
  createdAt?: string;
}

const SAMPLE_TICKET: Ticket = {
  key: "HD-2291",
  title: "Raise payment API rate limit",
  description: "Checkout is throttled at peak.",
  category: "Service change",
  priority: "high",
  service: { id: "svc-payments-api", name: "Payments API" },
  reporterEmail: "priya.raman@example.test",
};

export interface MockHelpdesk {
  trigger: TriggerConnector;
  /** A signed delivery of a new ticket, the sample ticket changed by `fields`. */
  ticketEvent(fields?: Partial<Ticket>, options?: { secret?: string; at?: Date }): { headers: Record<string, string>; body: string };
  /** Posts that delivery to `{hooks}/hooks/v1/events/helpdesk`; the hook's status and JSON answer. */
  send(hooks: string, fields?: Partial<Ticket>, options?: { secret?: string; at?: Date }): Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown }>;
}

function sign(secret: string, id: string, timestamp: string, body: string): string {
  const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ""), "base64");
  return createHmac("sha256", key).update(`${id}.${timestamp}.${body}`).digest("base64");
}

export function mockHelpdesk(directory: MockDirectory, clock: () => Date, secret: () => string): MockHelpdesk {
  const header = (req: RawRequest, name: string): string => req.headers[name] ?? "";
  const ticketEvent: MockHelpdesk["ticketEvent"] = (fields = {}, options = {}) => {
    const t = { ...SAMPLE_TICKET, ...fields };
    const data = { ...t, url: t.url ?? `http://helpdesk.mock.test/tickets/${t.key}`, createdAt: t.createdAt ?? (options.at ?? clock()).toISOString() };
    const body = JSON.stringify({ type: "ticketCreated", data });
    const id = `${t.key}.created`;
    const timestamp = String(Math.floor((options.at ?? clock()).getTime() / 1000));
    return { body, headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "webhook-id": id, "webhook-timestamp": timestamp, "webhook-signature": `v1,${sign(options.secret ?? HELPDESK_SECRET, id, timestamp, body)}` } };
  };
  return {
    ticketEvent,
    async send(hooks, fields, options) {
      const { headers, body } = ticketEvent(fields, options);
      const res = await fetch(`${hooks}/hooks/v1/events/helpdesk`, { method: "POST", headers, body });
      return { status: res.status, body: await res.json() };
    },
    trigger: {
      async verify(req) {
        const id = header(req, "webhook-id");
        const timestamp = header(req, "webhook-timestamp");
        const signatures = header(req, "webhook-signature").split(" ").filter((s) => s.startsWith("v1,"));
        if (id === "" || timestamp === "" || signatures.length === 0) return { answer: "refused", code: "unsigned" };
        if (Math.abs(clock().getTime() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 300 || !/^\d+$/.test(timestamp)) return { answer: "refused", code: "stale" };
        const expected = Buffer.from(sign(secret(), id, timestamp, Buffer.from(req.body).toString("utf8")));
        const ok = signatures.some((s) => {
          const given = Buffer.from(s.slice(3));
          return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
        });
        return ok ? { answer: "ok" } : { answer: "refused", code: "bad-signature" };
      },
      async parse(req): Promise<ParseAnswer> {
        const eventId = header(req, "webhook-id");
        let parsed: { type?: unknown; data?: Record<string, unknown> };
        try {
          parsed = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(req.body).toString("utf8")) as typeof parsed;
        } catch {
          return { answer: "unparsable", detail: "the body is not JSON" };
        }
        if (parsed.type !== "ticketCreated") return { answer: "ignored", eventId, detail: `type ${String(parsed.type)}` };
        const d = parsed.data ?? {};
        const event: JsonObject = {};
        for (const f of ["key", "title", "description", "category", "priority", "url"]) if (typeof d[f] === "string") event[f] = d[f] as string;
        const service = d["service"] as { id?: unknown; name?: unknown } | undefined;
        if (typeof service?.id === "string") event["service"] = { stored: service.id, label: typeof service.name === "string" ? service.name : service.id };
        if (typeof d["reporterEmail"] === "string") {
          const found = directory.findUser(d["reporterEmail"]);
          if (found === "unavailable") return { answer: "unavailable", detail: "the directory is down" };
          if (found !== null) event["reporter"] = { type: "user", id: found };
        }
        return { answer: "events", eventId, events: { "ticketCreated@1": event } };
      },
    },
  };
}

/**
 * What the helpdesk can be told to send: the sample ticket with these changed. One option per field of the
 * catalogue's `helpdesk.ticketCreated@1` event, all text.
 */
export interface HelpdeskSendOptions {
  key?: string;
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  /** Only "Service change" starts the integrated sample. */
  category?: string;
  /** The catalogue's choices are low, medium, high and critical; anything else is sent as given. */
  priority?: string;
  /** A service ID; its name is the seeded service's, or the ID. */
  service?: string;
  /** An email; becomes the Requester. */
  reporter?: string;
  /** The ticket's link; default `http://helpdesk.mock.test/tickets/{key}`. */
  url?: string;
}

/** The options' names, in the catalogue's order: what the dev host's send route and the script accept. */
export const HELPDESK_SEND_FIELDS: readonly (keyof HelpdeskSendOptions)[] = ["key", "title", "description", "category", "priority", "service", "reporter", "url"];

/**
 * Makes the helpdesk send a new-ticket event to the hook at `origin`, signed with the dev host's helpdesk
 * secret at `clock`'s time: the hook's HTTP status and its JSON answer. The one implementation behind
 * `scripts/helpdesk-event.mjs` and the dev host's `POST /dev/mocks/helpdesk/send`.
 */
export async function sendHelpdeskEvent(origin: string, options: HelpdeskSendOptions = {}, clock: () => Date = () => new Date()): Promise<{ status: number; answer: unknown }> {
  const fields: Partial<Ticket> = {};
  if (options.key !== undefined) fields.key = options.key;
  if (options.title !== undefined) fields.title = options.title;
  if (options.description !== undefined) fields.description = options.description;
  if (options.category !== undefined) fields.category = options.category;
  if (options.priority !== undefined) fields.priority = options.priority;
  if (options.url !== undefined) fields.url = options.url;
  if (options.reporter !== undefined) fields.reporterEmail = options.reporter;
  if (options.service !== undefined) fields.service = { id: options.service, name: SERVICES.find((s) => s.id === options.service)?.name ?? options.service };
  const { status, body } = await mockHelpdesk(mockDirectory(), clock, () => "").send(origin, fields);
  return { status, answer: body };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- ticket system (Jira)

export interface MockJira {
  failNext: boolean;
  down: boolean;
  /** Every issue created, oldest first, with the idempotency key it was sent with. */
  readonly issues: { key: string; project: string; summary: string; description?: string; idempotencyKey: string }[];
  operation: OperationConnector;
  /** Every call received, oldest first. */
  readonly received: CallItem[];
}

export function mockJira(rec: Recorder = NO_RECORDER): MockJira {
  const next = new Map<string, number>();
  const received: CallItem[] = [];
  const jira: MockJira = {
    failNext: false,
    down: false,
    issues: [],
    received,
    operation: recorded({
      async call(req): Promise<CallAnswer> {
        if (jira.down) return { answer: "unknown", detail: "Jira is down" };
        if (jira.failNext) {
          jira.failNext = false;
          return { answer: "failed", code: "permission-denied", message: "The platform may not create issues in this project." };
        }
        // The create is plain: the key is stored, never looked up (integrations.md section 3).
        const project = String(req.args["project"] ?? "OPS");
        const n = next.get(project) ?? 101;
        next.set(project, n + 1);
        const key = `${project}-${n}`;
        const description = req.args["description"];
        jira.issues.push({ key, project, summary: String(req.args["summary"] ?? ""), ...(typeof description === "string" ? { description } : {}), idempotencyKey: req.key });
        return { answer: "ok", data: { key, url: `http://jira.mock.test/browse/${key}` } };
      },
    }, received, rec),
  };
  return jira;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- deploy pipeline (await)

export interface MockDeploy {
  failNext: boolean;
  down: boolean;
  /** How many status questions a run answers before it ends; the earlier ones answer `running`. */
  questionsUntilDone: number;
  readonly runs: { id: string; key: string; fails: boolean; asked: number; state: "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" }[];
  operation: OperationConnector;
  /** Every call and status question received, oldest first. */
  readonly received: CallItem[];
}

export function mockDeploy(rec: Recorder = NO_RECORDER): MockDeploy {
  let n = 5001;
  const runLink = (id: string): JsonObject => ({ runLink: `http://deploy.mock.test/runs/${id}` });
  const received: CallItem[] = [];
  const deploy: MockDeploy = {
    failNext: false,
    down: false,
    questionsUntilDone: 2,
    runs: [],
    received,
    operation: recorded({
      async call(req): Promise<CallAnswer> {
        if (deploy.down) return { answer: "unknown", detail: "the pipeline is down" };
        const last = deploy.runs.filter((r) => r.key === req.key).at(-1);
        if (last?.state === "running") return { answer: "accepted", jobRef: last.id };
        if (last?.state === "succeeded") return { answer: "ok", data: runLink(last.id), jobRef: last.id };
        const run = { id: `run-${n++}`, key: req.key, fails: deploy.failNext, asked: 0, state: "running" as const };
        deploy.failNext = false;
        deploy.runs.push(run);
        return { answer: "accepted", jobRef: run.id };
      },
      async status(req) {
        if (deploy.down) return { answer: "unknown", detail: "the pipeline is down" };
        const run = deploy.runs.find((r) => r.id === req.jobRef);
        if (run === undefined) return { answer: "unknown", detail: `no run ${req.jobRef}` };
        if (run.state === "running") {
          run.asked += 1;
          if (run.asked < deploy.questionsUntilDone) return { answer: "running", jobRef: run.id };
          run.state = run.fails ? "failed" : "succeeded";
        }
        return run.state === "failed" ? { answer: "failed", code: "tests-failed", message: "3 of 412 tests failed.", jobRef: run.id } : { answer: "ok", data: runLink(run.id), jobRef: run.id };
      },
    }, received, rec),
  };
  return deploy;
}

/** One message the notifier sent, as the control surface lists it. */
export interface MessageItem {
  at: string;
  request: string;
  /** The notification rule, or the platform's built-in code. */
  rule: string;
  /** The one person it went to: the notifier sends one message per person. */
  to: string;

  message: OutgoingMessage["message"];
}

export interface MockMessages extends Notifier {
  down: boolean;
  /** Every message sent, one per recipient, oldest first. */
  readonly sent: OutgoingMessage[];
  /** The same, as the control surface lists them, with when each was sent; the newest 1,000. */
  readonly received: MessageItem[];
}

export function mockMessages(log?: Log, clock: () => Date = () => new Date()): MockMessages {
  const m: MockMessages = {
    down: false,
    sent: [],
    received: [],
    async send(message) {
      if (m.down) throw new Error("the messages connection is down");
      m.sent.push(message);
      remember(m.received, { at: clock().toISOString(), request: message.requestId, rule: message.rule, to: message.to, message: message.message });
      log?.({ kind: "mock-message-sent", request: message.requestId, rule: message.rule, detail: message.to });
    },
  };
  return m;
}

export function mockReporting(log?: Log): MockReporting {

    down: false,
    received: [],
    async post(subscriber: Subscriber, event: OutboundEventBody) {
      if (r.down) throw new Error(`${subscriber.url} answered 503`);
      r.received.push({ url: subscriber.url, event });

    },
  };

/**
 * The attempts log (data model section 4): one row per refused input that is an attempt, written in its own
 * transaction after the turn rolled back. Not history.
 */
import type { By, Json } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";
import { AT_SQL } from "./events.ts";

export interface AttemptRow {
  at: string;
  requestId: string | null;
  actor: By;
  /** What was attempted: the wait and outcome, or the admin actions; and every refusal with its params. */
  input: Json;
  /** The first refusal's reason. */
  reason: string;
}

export async function logAttempt(q: Queryable, row: AttemptRow): Promise<void> {
  await q.query("INSERT INTO attempts_log (at, request_id, actor, input, reason) VALUES ($1::timestamptz, $2, $3::jsonb, $4::jsonb, $5)", [
    row.at,
    row.requestId,
    JSON.stringify(row.actor),
    JSON.stringify(row.input),
    row.reason,
  ]);
}

export async function listAttempts(q: Queryable, requestId?: string): Promise<AttemptRow[]> {
  const rows = await q.query(
    `SELECT ${AT_SQL("at")} AS at, request_id, actor, input, reason FROM attempts_log ${requestId === undefined ? "" : "WHERE request_id = $1"} ORDER BY id`,
    requestId === undefined ? [] : [requestId],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({
    at: r["at"] as string,
    requestId: (r["request_id"] as string | null) ?? null,
    actor: r["actor"] as By,
    input: r["input"] as Json,
    reason: r["reason"] as string,
  }));
}

/**
 * The authoring tables (data model sections 2 and 4): `workflows`, `workflow_settings`, `settings_log`,
 * `drafts`, and the reads of `definitions` and `requests` the authoring API makes. Times are written as
 * RFC 3339 strings and read back with milliseconds, as the contract's `Timestamp` is.
 */
import type { By, JsonObject } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";

/** A time column as the contract's `Timestamp`: RFC 3339, UTC, milliseconds. */
export const MS_SQL = (column: string): string => `to_char(${column} AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')`;

/** A user or group reference as stored. */
export interface StoredRef {
  type: "user" | "group";
  id: string;
}

/** The settings record as the log keeps it (authoring-api.md `Settings`). */
export interface SettingsRecord {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  authors: StoredRef[];
  stuckRequestsGoTo?: StoredRef[];
}

export interface NewWorkflow {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  description: string;
  by: By;
  at: string;
  authored: JsonObject;
  todo: number;
  worthKnowing: number;
}

/** Creates the workflow, its settings (the creator as the only author), the first settings log row and draft revision 1. */
export async function insertWorkflow(q: Queryable, w: NewWorkflow): Promise<void> {
  const authors: StoredRef[] = [{ type: "user", id: w.by.id }];
  const record: SettingsRecord = { name: w.name, description: w.description, authors };
  await q.query("INSERT INTO workflows (id, name, description, created_by, created_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb, $5::timestamptz)", [
    w.id,
    w.name,
    w.description,
    JSON.stringify(w.by),
    w.at,
  ]);
  await q.query("INSERT INTO workflow_settings (workflow, authors, stuck_requests_go_to) VALUES ($1, $2::jsonb, NULL)", [w.id, JSON.stringify(authors)]);
  await q.query("INSERT INTO settings_log (workflow, by, at, before, after) VALUES ($1, $2::jsonb, $3::timestamptz, NULL, $4::jsonb)", [
    w.id,
    JSON.stringify(w.by),
    w.at,
    JSON.stringify(record),
  ]);
  await q.query(
    `INSERT INTO drafts (workflow, revision, authored, saved_by, saved_at, based_on_version, todo, worth_knowing)
     VALUES ($1, 1, $2::jsonb, $3::jsonb, $4::timestamptz, NULL, $5, $6)`,
    [w.id, JSON.stringify(w.authored), JSON.stringify(w.by), w.at, w.todo, w.worthKnowing],
  );
}

/** Locks the workflow's row for the rest of the transaction. False when there is no such workflow. */
export async function lockWorkflow(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await q.query("SELECT id FROM workflows WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE", [workflow])).length > 0;
}

export async function workflowExists(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await q.query("SELECT id FROM workflows WHERE id = $1", [workflow])).length > 0;
}

export interface DraftRow {
  workflow: string;
  revision: number;
  authored: JsonObject;
  savedBy: By;
  savedAt: string;
  basedOnVersion: number | null;
  todo: number;
  worthKnowing: number;
}

export async function readDraft(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<DraftRow | null> {
  const rows = await q.query<{
    workflow: string;
    revision: number;
    authored: JsonObject;
    saved_by: By;
    saved_at: string;
    based_on_version: number | null;
    todo: number;
    worth_knowing: number;
  }>(
    `SELECT workflow, revision, authored, saved_by, ${MS_SQL("saved_at")} AS saved_at, based_on_version, todo, worth_knowing
     FROM drafts WHERE workflow = $1`,
    [workflow],
  );
  const r = rows[0];
  if (r === undefined) return null;
  return {
    workflow: r.workflow,
    revision: r.revision,
    authored: r.authored,
    savedBy: r.saved_by,
    savedAt: r.saved_at,
    basedOnVersion: r.based_on_version,
    todo: r.todo,
    worthKnowing: r.worth_knowing,
  };
}

/** Overwrites the draft with the next revision. */
export async function writeDraft(q: Queryable, d: DraftRow): Promise<void> {
  await q.query(
    `UPDATE drafts SET revision = $2, authored = $3::jsonb, saved_by = $4::jsonb, saved_at = $5::timestamptz, based_on_version = $6, todo = $7, worth_knowing = $8
     WHERE workflow = $1`,
    [d.workflow, d.revision, JSON.stringify(d.authored), JSON.stringify(d.savedBy), d.savedAt, d.basedOnVersion, d.todo, d.worthKnowing],
  );
}

export async function highestVersion(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const rows = await q.query<{ v: number | string | null }>("SELECT max(version) AS v FROM definitions WHERE workflow = $1", [workflow]);
  const v = rows[0]?.v;
  return v === null || v === undefined ? null : Number(v);
}

/** One row of the workflows list, before the caller's flags are worked out. */
export interface WorkflowListRow {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  description: string;
  authors: StoredRef[];
  liveVersion: number | null;
  liveFromRevision: number | null;
  draft: { revision: number; savedAt: string; savedBy: By; todo: number; worthKnowing: number };
  liveTriggers: string[];
  draftTriggers: string[];
  openRequests: number;
  stuckRequests: number;
}

/** Every workflow, newest draft first. The triggers are read in SQL so that no document is loaded. */
export async function listWorkflowRows(q: Queryable): Promise<WorkflowListRow[]> {
  const rows = await q.query<Record<string, unknown>>(
    `SELECT w.id, w.name, w.description, s.authors,
            d.revision, ${MS_SQL("d.saved_at")} AS saved_at, d.saved_by, d.todo, d.worth_knowing,
            jsonb_path_query_array(d.authored, '$.start.startsWhen[*].trigger') AS draft_triggers,
            live.version AS live_version, live.from_revision AS live_from_revision,
            coalesce(jsonb_path_query_array(live.authored, '$.start.startsWhen[*].trigger'), '[]'::jsonb) AS live_triggers,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM requests r WHERE r.workflow = w.id AND r.closed_at IS NULL) AS open_requests,
            (SELECT count(*) FROM requests r WHERE r.workflow = w.id AND r.stuck IS NOT NULL) AS stuck_requests
     FROM workflows w
     JOIN drafts d ON d.workflow = w.id
     JOIN workflow_settings s ON s.workflow = w.id
     LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT version, from_revision, authored FROM definitions WHERE workflow = w.id ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1
     ) live ON true
     ORDER BY d.saved_at DESC, w.id`,
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({
    id: r["id"] as string,
    name: r["name"] as string,
    description: r["description"] as string,
    authors: r["authors"] as StoredRef[],
    liveVersion: r["live_version"] === null ? null : Number(r["live_version"]),
    liveFromRevision: r["live_from_revision"] === null ? null : Number(r["live_from_revision"]),
    draft: {
      revision: Number(r["revision"]),
      savedAt: r["saved_at"] as string,
      savedBy: r["saved_by"] as By,
      todo: Number(r["todo"]),
      worthKnowing: Number(r["worth_knowing"]),
    },
    liveTriggers: strings(r["live_triggers"]),
    draftTriggers: strings(r["draft_triggers"]),
    openRequests: Number(r["open_requests"]),
    stuckRequests: Number(r["stuck_requests"]),
  }));
}

/** The strings of a JSON array, in order, each once. An unfinished draft may hold other things there. */
function strings(value: unknown): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return [];
  return [...new Set(value.filter((v): v is string => typeof v === "string"))];
}

export interface VersionRow {
  version: number;
  publishedAt: string;
  publishedBy: By;
  fromRevision: number | null;
  coreVersion: string | null;
  formatVersion: number | null;
  openRequests: number;
}

const VERSION_COLUMNS = `d.version, ${MS_SQL("d.published_at")} AS published_at, d.published_by, d.from_revision, d.core_version, d.format_version,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM requests r WHERE r.workflow = d.workflow AND r.definition_version = d.version AND r.closed_at IS NULL) AS open_requests`;

function versionRow(r: Record<string, unknown>): VersionRow {
  return {
    version: Number(r["version"]),
    publishedAt: r["published_at"] as string,
    publishedBy: r["published_by"] as By,
    fromRevision: r["from_revision"] === null ? null : Number(r["from_revision"]),
    coreVersion: (r["core_version"] as string | null) ?? null,
    formatVersion: r["format_version"] === null ? null : Number(r["format_version"]),
    openRequests: Number(r["open_requests"]),
  };
}

/** The workflow's versions, newest first. */
export async function listVersionRows(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<VersionRow[]> {
  const rows = await q.query(`SELECT ${VERSION_COLUMNS} FROM definitions d WHERE d.workflow = $1 ORDER BY d.version DESC`, [workflow]);
  return rows.map(versionRow);
}

export async function readVersionRow(q: Queryable, workflow: string, version: number): Promise<(VersionRow & { authored: JsonObject }) | null> {
  const rows = await q.query(`SELECT ${VERSION_COLUMNS}, d.authored FROM definitions d WHERE d.workflow = $1 AND d.version = $2`, [workflow, version]);
  const r = rows[0];
  return r === undefined ? null : { ...versionRow(r), authored: r["authored"] as JsonObject };
}

/** The settings record and its last change. */
export interface SettingsRow {
  record: SettingsRecord;
  changedBy: By;
  changedAt: string;
  pausedBindings: string[];
}

export async function readSettings(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<SettingsRow | null> {
  const rows = await q.query<Record<string, unknown>>(
    `SELECT w.name, w.description, s.authors, s.stuck_requests_go_to, s.paused_bindings, l.by, ${MS_SQL("l.at")} AS at
     FROM workflows w
     JOIN workflow_settings s ON s.workflow = w.id
     JOIN LATERAL (SELECT by, at FROM settings_log WHERE workflow = w.id AND NOT (after ? 'pausedBindings') ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1) l ON true
     WHERE w.id = $1`,
    [workflow],
  );
  const r = rows[0];
  if (r === undefined) return null;
  const goTo = r["stuck_requests_go_to"] as StoredRef[] | null;
  const record: SettingsRecord = {
    name: r["name"] as string,
    description: r["description"] as string,
    authors: r["authors"] as StoredRef[],
    ...(goTo === null || goTo.length === 0 ? {} : { stuckRequestsGoTo: goTo }),
  };
  return { record, changedBy: r["by"] as By, changedAt: r["at"] as string, pausedBindings: (r["paused_bindings"] as string[]) ?? [] };
}

/** Replaces the settings record and logs the change with the record before and after. */
export async function writeSettings(q: Queryable, workflow: string, before: SettingsRecord, after: SettingsRecord, by: By, at: string): Promise<void> {
  await q.query("UPDATE workflows SET name = $2, description = $3 WHERE id = $1", [workflow, after.name, after.description]);
  await q.query("UPDATE workflow_settings SET authors = $2::jsonb, stuck_requests_go_to = $3::jsonb WHERE workflow = $1", [
    workflow,
    JSON.stringify(after.authors),
    after.stuckRequestsGoTo === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(after.stuckRequestsGoTo),
  ]);
  await q.query("INSERT INTO settings_log (workflow, by, at, before, after) VALUES ($1, $2::jsonb, $3::timestamptz, $4::jsonb, $5::jsonb)", [
    workflow,
    JSON.stringify(by),
    at,
    JSON.stringify(before),
    JSON.stringify(after),
  ]);
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/db.ts\n===
/**
 * Database access (decision E-30): plain SQL behind one small interface, with two adapters, PGlite for tests
 * and the dev host, node-postgres for a real Postgres. No ORM.
 *
 * Parameters are `$1`, `$2` ... Pass JSON values as strings (`JSON.stringify`) and cast them in the SQL
 * (`$1::jsonb`): node-postgres turns a JS array into a Postgres array, which is wrong for a jsonb column.
 * Read bigint columns through `Number()`: PGlite gives a number, node-postgres a string.
 */
import { PGlite } from "@electric-sql/pglite";
import pg from "pg";

export type Row = Record<string, unknown>;

/** What both a connection and a transaction can do. */
export interface Queryable {
  /** One statement, with parameters. */
  query<R extends Row = Row>(sql: string, params?: readonly unknown[]): Promise<R[]>;
  /** Several statements, no parameters (the schema files). */
  exec(sql: string): Promise<void>;
}

export interface Db extends Queryable {
  readonly kind: "pglite" | "postgres";
  /** Runs `fn` in one transaction: committed when it returns, rolled back when it throws (the error is rethrown). */
  transaction<T>(fn: (tx: Queryable) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

/** The SQLSTATE of a database error, or undefined for any other error. */
export function sqlState(error: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (typeof error !== "object" || error === null) return undefined;
  const code = (error as { code?: unknown }).code;
  return typeof code === "string" ? code : undefined;
}

export const SQLSTATE = {
  uniqueViolation: "23505",
  lockNotAvailable: "55P03",
} as const;

/** A PGlite database. Without `dataDir` it lives in memory. PGlite serves one connection: queries and transactions run one at a time. */
export async function createPgliteDb(dataDir?: string): Promise<Db> {
  const pglite = dataDir === undefined ? await PGlite.create() : await PGlite.create(dataDir);
  return pgliteDb(pglite);
}

export function pgliteDb(pglite: PGlite): Db {
  return {
    kind: "pglite",
    async query<R extends Row>(sql: string, params?: readonly unknown[]) {
      return (await pglite.query<R>(sql, params === undefined ? undefined : [...params])).rows;
    },
    async exec(sql: string) {
      await pglite.exec(sql);
    },
    transaction<T>(fn: (tx: Queryable) => Promise<T>) {
      return pglite.transaction(async (tx) =>
        fn({
          async query<R extends Row>(sql: string, params?: readonly unknown[]) {
            return (await tx.query<R>(sql, params === undefined ? undefined : [...params])).rows;
          },
          async exec(sql: string) {
            await tx.exec(sql);
          },
        }),
      );
    },
    close: () => pglite.close(),
  };
}

/** A real Postgres through a node-postgres pool. Each transaction takes its own connection from the pool. */
export function postgresDb(pool: pg.Pool): Db {
  return {
    kind: "postgres",
    async query<R extends Row>(sql: string, params?: readonly unknown[]) {
      return (await pool.query<R>(sql, params === undefined ? undefined : [...params])).rows;
    },
    async exec(sql: string) {
      await pool.query(sql);
    },
    async transaction<T>(fn: (tx: Queryable) => Promise<T>) {
      const client = await pool.connect();
      try {
        await client.query("BEGIN");
        const result = await fn({
          async query<R extends Row>(sql: string, params?: readonly unknown[]) {
            return (await client.query<R>(sql, params === undefined ? undefined : [...params])).rows;
          },
          async exec(sql: string) {
            await client.query(sql);
          },
        });
        await client.query("COMMIT");
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        await client.query("ROLLBACK").catch(() => undefined);
        throw error;
      } finally {
        client.release();
      }
    },
    close: () => pool.end(),
  };
}

export function createPostgresDb(connectionString: string): Db {
  return postgresDb(new pg.Pool({ connectionString }));
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/definitions.ts\n===
/**
 * The `definitions` table (data model section 2): one row per published version, never changed. Writing a
 * version is the authoring API's publish; the turn reads them. A row never changes, so a read is cached.
 */
import { parse, type AuthoredWorkflow, type Catalogue, type PublishedVersion } from "@workflow/core";
import type { By, JsonObject, PublishedDefinition } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";

export interface DefinitionRow {
  workflow: string;
  version: number;
  /** The published definition, every default written out. */
  document: PublishedDefinition;
  /** The authored source as published, or a hand-written definition. */
  authored: JsonObject;
  fromRevision: number | null;
  coreVersion: string | null;
  formatVersion: number | null;
  /** The catalogue version it was compiled against; absent or null for a hand-written definition. */
  catalogueVersion?: string | null;
  publishedBy: By;
  publishedAt: string;
}

/** Inserts a version. `schemas` is taken from the document. */
export async function insertDefinition(q: Queryable, row: DefinitionRow): Promise<void> {
  if (row.document.workflow !== row.workflow || row.document.version !== row.version) {
    throw new Error(`insertDefinition: the document is ${row.document.workflow}@${row.document.version}, the row ${row.workflow}@${row.version}`);
  }
  await q.query(
    `INSERT INTO definitions (workflow, version, document, authored, from_revision, core_version, format_version, schemas, published_by, published_at, catalogue_version)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, $4::jsonb, $5, $6, $7, $8::jsonb, $9::jsonb, $10::timestamptz, $11)`,
    [
      row.workflow,
      row.version,
      JSON.stringify(row.document),
      JSON.stringify(row.authored),
      row.fromRevision,
      row.coreVersion,
      row.formatVersion,
      JSON.stringify(row.document.schemas),
      JSON.stringify(row.publishedBy),
      row.publishedAt,
      row.catalogueVersion ?? null,
    ],
  );
}

/** Reads published definitions, caching each version once read. */
export interface DefinitionReader {
  /** The version, or null when it was never published. */
  get(q: Queryable, workflow: string, version: number): Promise<PublishedDefinition | null>;
  /** The highest published version, or null when the workflow has none. */
  highest(q: Queryable, workflow: string): Promise<number | null>;
  /**
   * The version as core's readers take it: the definition, its authored source and the current catalogue.
   * Null when it was never published or has no authored source: a hand-written definition, which is for the
   * kernel's tests and which the runtime API does not serve (E-31).
   */
  published(q: Queryable, workflow: string, version: number): Promise<PublishedVersion | null>;
}

/** `catalogue` gives the catalogue now: readers use the current one (E-31). */
export function createDefinitionReader(catalogue: () => Catalogue): DefinitionReader {
  const cache = new Map<string, PublishedDefinition>();
  const sources = new Map<string, AuthoredWorkflow | null>();
  const reader: DefinitionReader = {
    async published(q, workflow, version) {
      const definition = await reader.get(q, workflow, version);
      if (definition === null) return null;
      const key = JSON.stringify([workflow, version]);
      let source = sources.get(key);
      if (source === undefined) {
        const rows = await q.query<{ authored: unknown }>("SELECT authored FROM definitions WHERE workflow = $1 AND version = $2", [workflow, version]);
        const parsed = parse(rows[0]?.authored);
        // The source as stored, not parse's reading of it, as every reader of a version takes it.
        source = parsed.ok ? (rows[0]?.authored as AuthoredWorkflow) : null;
        sources.set(key, source);
      }
      return source === null ? null : { definition, source, catalogue: catalogue() };
    },
    async get(q, workflow, version) {
      const key = JSON.stringify([workflow, version]);
      const hit = cache.get(key);
      if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
      const rows = await q.query<{ document: PublishedDefinition }>("SELECT document FROM definitions WHERE workflow = $1 AND version = $2", [workflow, version]);
      const document = rows[0]?.document;
      if (document === undefined) return null;
      cache.set(key, document);
      return document;
    },
    async highest(q, workflow) {
      const rows = await q.query<{ v: number | string | null }>("SELECT max(version) AS v FROM definitions WHERE workflow = $1", [workflow]);
      const v = rows[0]?.v;
      return v === null || v === undefined ? null : Number(v);
    },
  };
  return reader;
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/events.ts\n===
/**
 * The `events` table (data model section 2): append a turn's events, load a request's events, fold them.
 * `at` is kept to the microsecond: it is written as the RFC 3339 string core gives and read back in the
 * same form (six fractional digits, UTC), never through a JS Date, which keeps only milliseconds.
 */
import { fold, type AnyEventRecord, type RequestState } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";

/** `at` as core writes it: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`. */
export const AT_SQL = (column: string): string => `to_char(${column} AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"')`;

interface EventRow extends Record<string, unknown> {
  request_id: string;
  seq: number;
  type: string;
  at: string;
  turn: number;
  v: number;
  engine_build: string;
  payload: unknown;
}

function toRecord(row: EventRow): AnyEventRecord {
  return {
    requestId: row.request_id,
    seq: Number(row.seq),
    type: row.type,
    at: row.at,
    turn: Number(row.turn),
    v: Number(row.v),
    engineBuild: row.engine_build,
    payload: row.payload,
  } as AnyEventRecord;
}

/** The highest `seq` stored for the request; 0 when it has none. */
export async function lastSeq(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<number> {
  const rows = await q.query<{ last: number | string | null }>("SELECT max(seq) AS last FROM events WHERE request_id = $1", [requestId]);
  return Number(rows[0]?.last ?? 0);
}

/**
 * Appends events of one request. They must continue the stored history without a gap: the first has
 * `seq` one above the highest stored, and each the next. Run it under the request's lock; the primary key
 * `(request_id, seq)` is the second guard against two writers.
 */
export async function appendEvents(q: Queryable, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]): Promise<void> {
  const first = events[0];
  if (first === undefined) return;
  const after = await lastSeq(q, first.requestId);
  events.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (e.requestId !== first.requestId) throw new Error(`appendEvents: events of two requests (${first.requestId}, ${e.requestId})`);
    if (e.seq !== after + 1 + i) throw new Error(`appendEvents: request ${e.requestId} has seq ${after}; event ${i} has seq ${e.seq}, expected ${after + 1 + i}`);
  });
  const params: unknown[] = [];
  const values = events.map((e) => {
    params.push(e.requestId, e.seq, e.type, e.at, e.turn, e.v, e.engineBuild, JSON.stringify(e.payload));
    const n = params.length - 8;
    return `($${n + 1}, $${n + 2}, $${n + 3}, $${n + 4}::timestamptz, $${n + 5}, $${n + 6}, $${n + 7}, $${n + 8}::jsonb)`;
  });
  await q.query(`INSERT INTO events (request_id, seq, type, at, turn, v, engine_build, payload) VALUES ${values.join(", ")}`, params);
}

/** Every event of the request, in `seq` order. [] for a request that does not exist. */
export async function loadEvents(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<AnyEventRecord[]> {
  const rows = await q.query<EventRow>(
    `SELECT request_id, seq, type, ${AT_SQL("at")} AS at, turn, v, engine_build, payload FROM events WHERE request_id = $1 ORDER BY seq`,
    [requestId],
  );
  return rows.map(toRecord);
}

/** The request's state: its events folded with core's `fold`. There are no snapshots (data model section 1). */
export async function loadState(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<{ events: AnyEventRecord[]; state: RequestState }> {
  const events = await loadEvents(q, requestId);
  return { events, state: fold(events) };
}

/** Every request ID that has events, in no particular order. */
export async function requestIds(q: Queryable): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await q.query<{ request_id: string }>("SELECT DISTINCT request_id FROM events")).map((r) => r.request_id);
}
