/**
 * The engine's job table (data model section 5). The turn enqueues inside its transaction, so a job exists
 * exactly when its turn committed. A request's notify jobs run in order on the queue `notify:<id>` and its
 * publish jobs on `publish:<id>`, so a mail outage does not hold back outbound events, nor a subscriber that
 * is down people's messages; each call has a queue of its own, so a call that is tried again holds nobody up.
 */
import type { WaitId } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";

/** One opened call: send it, ask for its status, record its result. */
export interface CallJob {
  kind: "call";
  requestId: string;
  wait: WaitId;
}

/** A turn whose events may match a notification rule. */
export interface NotifyJob {
  kind: "notify";
  requestId: string;
  firstSeq: number;
  lastSeq: number;
}

/** Every committed turn that appended events: its outbound events. */
export interface PublishJob {
  kind: "publish";
  requestId: string;
  firstSeq: number;
  lastSeq: number;
}

export type Job = CallJob | NotifyJob | PublishJob;

/** The wait's derived key: `<request>/<element>[<key>]@<activation>#<seq>`, the key part left out when empty. */
export function waitKeyOf(requestId: string, w: WaitId): string {
  return `${requestId}/${w.element}${w.key === "" ? "" : `[${w.key}]`}@${w.activation}#${w.seq}`;
}

export function queueOf(job: Job): string {
  return job.kind === "call" ? `call:${waitKeyOf(job.requestId, job.wait)}` : `${job.kind}:${job.requestId}`;
}

/** Inserts the jobs, due at `runAt` (the turn's time). */
export async function enqueueJobs(q: Queryable, jobs: readonly Job[], runAt: string): Promise<void> {
  for (const job of jobs) {
    const { kind, ...payload } = job;
    await q.query("INSERT INTO jobs (kind, queue, payload, run_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3::jsonb, $4::timestamptz)", [kind, queueOf(job), JSON.stringify(payload), runAt]);
  }
}

/** The queued jobs, oldest first; optionally of one request. */
export async function listJobs(q: Queryable, requestId?: string): Promise<Job[]> {
  const rows = await q.query<{ kind: string; payload: Record<string, unknown> }>(
    requestId === undefined ? "SELECT kind, payload FROM jobs ORDER BY id" : "SELECT kind, payload FROM jobs WHERE payload->>'requestId' = $1 ORDER BY id",
    requestId === undefined ? [] : [requestId],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({ kind: r.kind, ...r.payload }) as Job);
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/lock.ts\n===
/**
 * The request's lock (data model section 1, step 1): its `requests` row, taken `FOR UPDATE` inside the
 * transaction and waited for at most the lock timeout. A turn and a rebuild of the request's read tables both
 * take it, so neither writes a request's rows while the other is running. A start's request has no row yet,
 * so it locks nothing. Waiting past the timeout fails with SQLSTATE 55P03 (`SQLSTATE.lockNotAvailable`).
 */
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";

/** How long a turn or a rebuild waits for a request's lock by default. */
export const DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;

export async function lockRequest(tx: Queryable, requestId: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<void> {
  await tx.query(`SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '${Math.max(0, Math.trunc(timeoutMs))}ms'`);
  await tx.query("SELECT id FROM requests WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE", [requestId]);
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/migrate.ts\n===
/**
 * The schema runner (decision E-30): applies the numbered SQL files of `schema/` in order, each in its own
 * transaction with the row that records it, and skips those already recorded in `schema_migrations`.
 */
import { readdir, readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import type { Db } from "./db.ts";

const SCHEMA_DIR = new URL("./schema/", import.meta.url);
const NAME = /^(\d{3})_[a-z0-9_]+\.sql$/;

export interface SchemaFile {
  name: string;
  sql: string;
}

/** The schema files in order. Every `.sql` file must be named `NNN_words.sql`, with no number used twice. */
export async function schemaFiles(dir: URL = SCHEMA_DIR): Promise<SchemaFile[]> {
  const names = (await readdir(dir)).filter((n) => n.endsWith(".sql")).sort();
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const files: SchemaFile[] = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    const m = NAME.exec(name);
    if (m === null) throw new Error(`schema file ${name} is not named NNN_words.sql`);
    const number = m[1] as string;
    if (seen.has(number)) throw new Error(`schema number ${number} is used twice`);
    seen.add(number);
    files.push({ name, sql: await readFile(new URL(name, dir), "utf8") });
  }
  return files;
}

/** Applies every schema file not yet applied, in order. Returns the names it applied. */
export async function migrate(db: Db, files?: readonly SchemaFile[]): Promise<string[]> {
  await db.exec("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (name text PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())");
  const done = new Set((await db.query<{ name: string }>("SELECT name FROM schema_migrations")).map((r) => r.name));
  const applied: string[] = [];
  for (const file of files ?? (await schemaFiles())) {
    if (done.has(file.name)) continue;
    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.exec(file.sql);
      await tx.query("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (name) VALUES ($1)", [file.name]);
    });
    applied.push(file.name);
  }
  return applied;
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/pending-calls.ts\n===
/**
 * `pending_calls` (data model section 5): one row per opened call whose result is not recorded. The turn
 * inserts it with the call's job, deletes it when it records the result (`WaitCompleted`, `CallResultLate`)
 * or drops it, and sets `wait_closed` when the wait is cancelled or skipped. The call job keeps the rest.
 */
import type { AnyEventRecord, WaitId } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "./db.ts";
import { AT_SQL } from "./events.ts";

const WAIT = "request_id = $1 AND element = $2 AND activation = $3 AND key = $4 AND seq = $5";
const waitParams = (requestId: string, w: WaitId): unknown[] => [requestId, w.element, w.activation, w.key, w.seq];

export async function deletePendingCall(q: Queryable, requestId: string, wait: WaitId): Promise<void> {
  await q.query(`DELETE FROM pending_calls WHERE ${WAIT}`, waitParams(requestId, wait));
}

/** Applies a turn's events to `pending_calls`. */
export async function applyCallEvents(q: Queryable, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]): Promise<void> {
  for (const e of events) {
    switch (e.type) {
      case "WaitOpened": {
        const p = e.payload;
        if (p.kind !== "call") break;
        await q.query(
          `INSERT INTO pending_calls (request_id, element, activation, key, seq, connection, op, args, effect, idempotency_key, opened_at)
           VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8::jsonb, $9, $10, $11::timestamptz)`,
          [...waitParams(e.requestId, p.wait), p.connection, p.op, JSON.stringify(p.args), p.effect, p.idempotencyKey, e.at],
        );
        break;
      }
      case "WaitCompleted":
      case "CallResultLate":
        await deletePendingCall(q, e.requestId, e.payload.wait);
        break;
      case "WaitCancelled":
      case "WaitSkipped":
        await q.query(`UPDATE pending_calls SET wait_closed = true WHERE ${WAIT}`, waitParams(e.requestId, e.payload.wait));
        break;
      default:
        break;
    }
  }
}

export interface PendingCallRow {
  requestId: string;
  wait: WaitId;
  connection: string;
  op: string;
  args: unknown;
  effect: string;
  idempotencyKey: string;
  waitClosed: boolean;
  /** The outside job of an await, once known; never overwritten. */
  jobRef: string | null;
  attempts: number;
  openedAt: string;
  lastAttemptAt: string | null;
  lastError: string | null;
}

const COLUMNS = `request_id, element, activation, key, seq, connection, op, args, effect, idempotency_key, wait_closed, job_ref, attempts,
  ${AT_SQL("opened_at")} AS opened_at, ${AT_SQL("last_attempt_at")} AS last_attempt_at, last_error`;

function rowOf(r: Record<string, unknown>): PendingCallRow {
  return {
    requestId: r["request_id"] as string,
    wait: { element: r["element"] as string, activation: r["activation"] as string, key: r["key"] as string, seq: Number(r["seq"]) },
    connection: r["connection"] as string,
    op: r["op"] as string,
    args: r["args"],
    effect: r["effect"] as string,
    idempotencyKey: r["idempotency_key"] as string,
    waitClosed: r["wait_closed"] as boolean,
    jobRef: (r["job_ref"] as string | null) ?? null,
    attempts: Number(r["attempts"]),
    openedAt: r["opened_at"] as string,
    lastAttemptAt: (r["last_attempt_at"] as string | null) ?? null,
    lastError: (r["last_error"] as string | null) ?? null,
  };
}

export async function listPendingCalls(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<PendingCallRow[]> {
  const rows = await q.query(`SELECT ${COLUMNS} FROM pending_calls WHERE request_id = $1 ORDER BY opened_at, element, activation, key, seq`, [requestId]);
  return rows.map(rowOf);
}

export async function readPendingCall(q: Queryable, requestId: string, wait: WaitId): Promise<PendingCallRow | null> {
  const rows = await q.query(`SELECT ${COLUMNS} FROM pending_calls WHERE ${WAIT}`, waitParams(requestId, wait));
  return rows[0] === undefined ? null : rowOf(rows[0]);
}

/** One send is about to be made. */
export async function countAttempt(q: Queryable, requestId: string, wait: WaitId, at: string): Promise<void> {
  await q.query(`UPDATE pending_calls SET attempts = attempts + 1, last_attempt_at = $6::timestamptz WHERE ${WAIT}`, [...waitParams(requestId, wait), at]);
}

/** Keeps the await's job reference; one already set is never overwritten. */
export async function keepJobRef(q: Queryable, requestId: string, wait: WaitId, jobRef: string): Promise<void> {
  await q.query(`UPDATE pending_calls SET job_ref = coalesce(job_ref, $6) WHERE ${WAIT}`, [...waitParams(requestId, wait), jobRef]);
}

export async function setLastError(q: Queryable, requestId: string, wait: WaitId, error: string | null): Promise<void> {
  await q.query(`UPDATE pending_calls SET last_error = $6 WHERE ${WAIT}`, [...waitParams(requestId, wait), error]);
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/store/projections.ts\n===
/**
 * The projections (data model section 3): `requests` and `open_waits`, written from a request's folded
 * state in the turn's transaction, and rebuilt from `events` alone by replaying a request's events turn by
 * turn under the request's lock and updating its rows in place. Both paths use the same functions, so a
 * rebuild gives the same rows.
 *
 * `requests.stuck` is the stuck state of integrations.md section 11.5: worked out once per turn with
 * core's `stuckStateOf`, its stage mapped with `authoredStageOf`, and its `at` the `at` of the last event of
 * the turn in which the request entered that state. It needs the request's definition (rule matching and
 * the origin map), a version that never changes.
 *
 * `requests.stage` and `requests.stuck_view` are what a request list shows (runtime-api.md 6.2): the
 * authored stage and the stuck state as core's request view gives them, read from the request's own version
 * and its events, so that a list reads no events. Null for a version with no authored source.
 */
import { requestView, type Location, type PublishedVersion, type Stuck } from "@workflow/core";
import { authoredStageOf, fold, stuckStateOf, type AnyEventRecord, type PublishedDefinition, type RequestState } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import { SQLSTATE, sqlState, type Db, type Queryable } from "./db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "./definitions.ts";
import { AT_SQL, loadEvents, requestIds } from "./events.ts";
import { DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, lockRequest } from "./lock.ts";

/** `requests.stuck`. */
export interface StoredStuck {
  reason: string;
  /** The authored stage; null for the root or no stage. */
  stage: string | null;
  at: string;
}

/** A `requests` row, as written and as read back. */
export interface RequestRow {
  id: string;
  readableId: number;
  workflow: string;
  definitionVersion: number;
  status: string | null;
  statusLabel: string | null;
  activeStages: { activation: string; stage: string; parentActivation: string | null }[];
  data: unknown;
  startedBy: unknown;
  startedAt: string;
  closedAt: string | null;
  fault: string | null;
  faultElement: string | null;
  stuck: StoredStuck | null;
  lastSeq: number;
  updatedAt: string;
  /** The authored stage as the request view gives it; null for a version with no authored source. */
  stage: Location | null;
  /** The stuck state as a list shows it: the request view's, without the admin detail. */
  stuckView: ListedStuck | null;
}

/** `RequestView.stuck` without `admin`. */
export type ListedStuck = Omit<Stuck, "admin">;

/** What a request list shows that only the version's authored source can say. */
export interface Listed {
  stage: Location | null;
  stuckView: ListedStuck | null;
}

/** An `open_waits` row. */
export interface OpenWaitRow {
  requestId: string;
  element: string;
  activation: string;
  key: string;
  seq: number;
  kind: string;
  role: string | null;
  assigneeUsers: string[];
  assigneeGroups: string[];
  openedAt: string;
}

/** The stuck state after a turn, keeping the earlier `at` while the request stays in the same state. */
export function stuckAfterTurn(def: PublishedDefinition, previous: StoredStuck | null, state: RequestState): StoredStuck | null {
  const s = stuckStateOf(def, state);
  if (s === null) return null;
  const stage = authoredStageOf(def, s.stage);
  if (previous !== null && previous.reason === s.reason && previous.stage === stage) return previous;
  return { reason: s.reason, stage, at: state.lastAt };
}

/** The stage a request is in for each version: the request view's stage depends on the version and the engine stage alone. */
const stages = new WeakMap<PublishedDefinition, Map<string, Location>>();

/**
 * The request's authored stage and its stuck state as the request view gives them. The view is built from the
 * events only when the stage is not known yet for this version and engine stage, or the request is stuck.
 */
export function listedOf(published: PublishedVersion | null, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], state: RequestState, stuck: StoredStuck | null): Listed {
  if (published === null) return { stage: null, stuckView: null };
  // The request view's stage is that of the last active stage below the root.
  const engineStage = state.activeStages.filter((s) => s.stage !== "root").at(-1)?.stage ?? "";
  let known = stages.get(published.definition);
  if (known === undefined) stages.set(published.definition, (known = new Map()));
  const stage = known.get(engineStage);
  if (stage !== undefined && stuck === null) return { stage, stuckView: null };
  const view = requestView(published, events);
  known.set(engineStage, view.stage);
  if (view.stuck === undefined) return { stage: view.stage, stuckView: null };
  const { reason, at, location } = view.stuck;
  return { stage: view.stage, stuckView: location === undefined ? { reason, at } : { reason, at, location } };
}

/** The request's row. `fault` is `error` while a fault is not cleared; a fault is only ever an error. */
export function requestRowOf(state: RequestState, stuck: StoredStuck | null, listed: Listed): RequestRow {
  const { request, definition } = state;
  if (request === null || definition === null) throw new Error(`request ${state.requestId} has not started`);
  const fault = state.faults[0] ?? null;
  return {
    id: request.id,
    readableId: request.readableId,
    workflow: definition.workflow,
    definitionVersion: definition.version,
    status: state.status?.id ?? null,
    statusLabel: state.status?.label ?? null,
    activeStages: state.activeStages.map((s) => ({ activation: s.activation, stage: s.stage, parentActivation: s.parentActivation })),
    data: state.data,
    startedBy: request.by,
    startedAt: request.at,
    closedAt: state.closed?.at ?? null,
    fault: fault === null ? null : "error",
    faultElement: fault?.element ?? null,
    stuck,
    lastSeq: state.lastSeq,
    updatedAt: state.lastAt,
    stage: listed.stage,
    stuckView: listed.stuckView,
  };
}

/** One row per open wait instance, person or call; assignees as recorded, not expanded. */
export function openWaitRowsOf(state: RequestState): OpenWaitRow[] {
  return state.waits
    .filter((w) => w.status === "open")
    .map((w) => {
      const assignees = w.opened.kind === "person" ? w.opened.assignees : [];
      return {
        requestId: state.requestId,
        element: w.id.element,
        activation: w.id.activation,
        key: w.id.key,
        seq: w.id.seq,
        kind: w.kind,
        role: w.role,
        assigneeUsers: assignees.filter((a) => a.type === "user").map((a) => a.id),
        assigneeGroups: assignees.filter((a) => a.type === "group").map((a) => a.id),
        openedAt: w.openedAt,
      };
    });
}

/** Writes the request's projection rows from its state after a turn. */
export async function writeProjections(q: Queryable, state: RequestState, stuck: StoredStuck | null, listed: Listed): Promise<void> {
  const r = requestRowOf(state, stuck, listed);
  await q.query(
    `INSERT INTO requests (id, readable_id, workflow, definition_version, status, status_label, active_stages, data,
       started_by, started_at, closed_at, fault, fault_element, stuck, last_seq, updated_at, stage, stuck_view)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7::jsonb, $8::jsonb, $9::jsonb, $10::timestamptz, $11::timestamptz, $12, $13, $14::jsonb, $15, $16::timestamptz,
       $17::jsonb, $18::jsonb)
     ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
       readable_id = EXCLUDED.readable_id, workflow = EXCLUDED.workflow, definition_version = EXCLUDED.definition_version,
       status = EXCLUDED.status, status_label = EXCLUDED.status_label, active_stages = EXCLUDED.active_stages, data = EXCLUDED.data,
       started_by = EXCLUDED.started_by, started_at = EXCLUDED.started_at, closed_at = EXCLUDED.closed_at, fault = EXCLUDED.fault,
       fault_element = EXCLUDED.fault_element, stuck = EXCLUDED.stuck, last_seq = EXCLUDED.last_seq, updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at,
       stage = EXCLUDED.stage, stuck_view = EXCLUDED.stuck_view`,
    [
      r.id,
      r.readableId,
      r.workflow,
      r.definitionVersion,
      r.status,
      r.statusLabel,
      JSON.stringify(r.activeStages),
      JSON.stringify(r.data),
      JSON.stringify(r.startedBy),
      r.startedAt,
      r.closedAt,
      r.fault,
      r.faultElement,
      r.stuck === null ? null : JSON.stringify(r.stuck),
      r.lastSeq,
      r.updatedAt,
      r.stage === null ? null : JSON.stringify(r.stage),
      r.stuckView === null ? null : JSON.stringify(r.stuckView),
    ],
  );
  await q.query("DELETE FROM open_waits WHERE request_id = $1", [state.requestId]);
  for (const w of openWaitRowsOf(state)) {
    await q.query(
      `INSERT INTO open_waits (request_id, element, activation, key, seq, kind, role, assignee_users, assignee_groups, opened_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7,
         ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($8::jsonb)), ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($9::jsonb)), $10::timestamptz)`,
      [w.requestId, w.element, w.activation, w.key, w.seq, w.kind, w.role, JSON.stringify(w.assigneeUsers), JSON.stringify(w.assigneeGroups), w.openedAt],
    );
  }
}

/** The stored stuck state of a request, or null (also when it has no row yet). */
export async function readStoredStuck(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<StoredStuck | null> {
  const rows = await q.query<{ stuck: StoredStuck | null }>("SELECT stuck FROM requests WHERE id = $1", [requestId]);
  return rows[0]?.stuck ?? null;
}

/** A request's events split into turns: consecutive events with the same `turn`. */
export function turnsOf(events: readonly AnyEventRecord[]): AnyEventRecord[][] {
  const turns: AnyEventRecord[][] = [];
  for (const e of events) {
    const last = turns[turns.length - 1];
    if (last !== undefined && last[0]?.turn === e.turn) last.push(e);
    else turns.push([e]);
  }
  return turns;
}

/** Deletes a request's projection rows. */
export async function deleteProjections(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<void> {
  await q.query("DELETE FROM open_waits WHERE request_id = $1", [requestId]);
  await q.query("DELETE FROM requests WHERE id = $1", [requestId]);
}

export interface RebuildOptions {
  /** How long to wait for the request's lock before answering `busy`; default as a turn's, 5000 ms. */
  lockTimeoutMs?: number;
}

/**
 * Rebuilds one request's projection rows from its events, in one transaction under the request's lock, the
 * one a turn takes: replays the events turn by turn, working out the stuck state after each turn as the turn
 * transaction does, then writes the rows in place. `busy` when the lock was not obtained in time, as a turn
 * is refused; `none` for a request with no events.
 */
export async function rebuildRequest(db: Db, definitions: DefinitionReader, requestId: string, options: RebuildOptions = {}): Promise<"rebuilt" | "none" | "busy"> {
  try {
    return await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await lockRequest(tx, requestId, options.lockTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS);
      const events = await loadEvents(tx, requestId);
      if (events.length === 0) return "none";
      let state: RequestState | undefined;
      let stuck: StoredStuck | null = null;
      let def: PublishedDefinition | null = null;
      for (const turn of turnsOf(events)) {
        state = fold(turn, state);
        const runsOn = state.definition;
        if (runsOn === null) throw new Error(`request ${requestId} has no RequestStarted`);
        def = await definitions.get(tx, runsOn.workflow, runsOn.version);
        if (def === null) throw new Error(`request ${requestId} runs on ${runsOn.workflow}@${runsOn.version}, which is not in definitions`);
        stuck = stuckAfterTurn(def, stuck, state);
      }
      if (state === undefined || def === null) return "none";
      const published = await definitions.published(tx, def.workflow, def.version);
      await writeProjections(tx, state, stuck, listedOf(published, events, state, stuck));
      return "rebuilt";
    });
  } catch (error) {
    if (sqlState(error) === SQLSTATE.lockNotAvailable) return "busy";
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * Rebuilds every request's projection rows, request by request, each in its own transaction under its lock.
 * A request whose lock is held past the timeout is tried once more after the others; still busy, it throws.
 * Returns how many requests were rebuilt.
 */
export async function rebuildAll(db: Db, definitions: DefinitionReader, options: RebuildOptions = {}): Promise<number> {
  let rebuilt = 0;
  const busy: string[] = [];
  for (const id of await requestIds(db)) {
    const done = await rebuildRequest(db, definitions, id, options);
    if (done === "rebuilt") rebuilt += 1;
    if (done === "busy") busy.push(id);
  }
  const still: string[] = [];
  for (const id of busy) {
    const done = await rebuildRequest(db, definitions, id, options);
    if (done === "rebuilt") rebuilt += 1;
    if (done === "busy") still.push(id);
  }
  if (still.length > 0) throw new Error(`rebuildAll: requests ${still.join(", ")} stayed busy`);
  return rebuilt;
}

/** The request's row as stored, or null. Times in the events' form. */
export async function readRequestRow(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<RequestRow | null> {
  const rows = await q.query(
    `SELECT id, readable_id, workflow, definition_version, status, status_label, active_stages, data, started_by,
       ${AT_SQL("started_at")} AS started_at, ${AT_SQL("closed_at")} AS closed_at, fault, fault_element, stuck, last_seq,
       ${AT_SQL("updated_at")} AS updated_at, stage, stuck_view
     FROM requests WHERE id = $1`,
    [requestId],
  );
  const r = rows[0];
  if (r === undefined) return null;
  return {
    id: r["id"] as string,
    readableId: Number(r["readable_id"]),
    workflow: r["workflow"] as string,
    definitionVersion: Number(r["definition_version"]),
    status: (r["status"] as string | null) ?? null,
    statusLabel: (r["status_label"] as string | null) ?? null,
    activeStages: r["active_stages"] as RequestRow["activeStages"],
    data: r["data"],
    startedBy: r["started_by"],
    startedAt: r["started_at"] as string,
    closedAt: (r["closed_at"] as string | null) ?? null,
    fault: (r["fault"] as string | null) ?? null,
    faultElement: (r["fault_element"] as string | null) ?? null,
    stuck: (r["stuck"] as StoredStuck | null) ?? null,
    lastSeq: Number(r["last_seq"]),
    updatedAt: r["updated_at"] as string,
    stage: (r["stage"] as Location | null) ?? null,
    stuckView: (r["stuck_view"] as ListedStuck | null) ?? null,
  };
}

/** The request's open waits as stored, in key order. */
export async function readOpenWaits(q: Queryable, requestId: string): Promise<OpenWaitRow[]> {
  const rows = await q.query(
    `SELECT request_id, element, activation, key, seq, kind, role, assignee_users, assignee_groups, ${AT_SQL("opened_at")} AS opened_at
     FROM open_waits WHERE request_id = $1 ORDER BY element, activation, key, seq`,
    [requestId],
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({
    requestId: r["request_id"] as string,
    element: r["element"] as string,
    activation: r["activation"] as string,
    key: r["key"] as string,
    seq: Number(r["seq"]),
    kind: r["kind"] as string,
    role: (r["role"] as string | null) ?? null,
    assigneeUsers: r["assignee_users"] as string[],
    assigneeGroups: r["assignee_groups"] as string[],
    openedAt: r["opened_at"] as string,
  }));
}

-- History (data model section 2): never updated, never deleted.
-- A typed `by` is stored as jsonb {type, id}; an id is text matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$.

CREATE TABLE events (
  request_id   text        NOT NULL CHECK (request_id ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$'),
  seq          int         NOT NULL CHECK (seq >= 1),
  type         text        NOT NULL,
  at           timestamptz NOT NULL,
  turn         int         NOT NULL,
  v            smallint    NOT NULL,
  engine_build text        NOT NULL,
  payload      jsonb       NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (request_id, seq)
);

CREATE TABLE definitions (
  workflow          text        NOT NULL,
  version           int         NOT NULL CHECK (version >= 1),
  document          jsonb       NOT NULL,
  authored          jsonb       NOT NULL,
  from_revision     int,
  core_version      text,
  format_version    int,
  catalogue_version text,
  schemas           jsonb       NOT NULL,
  published_by      jsonb       NOT NULL,
  published_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (workflow, version)
);

-- The data model takes UPDATE and DELETE away from the application's role. PGlite has one role, so a trigger
-- refuses them here too. TRUNCATE is not refused: tests empty the tables with it.
CREATE FUNCTION refuse_history_change() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append-only: rows are never updated or deleted', TG_TABLE_NAME USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege';
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER events_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON events
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_history_change();
CREATE TRIGGER definitions_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON definitions
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refuse_history_change();

===\nengine/packages/server/src/turn/jobs-for-turn.ts\n===
/**
 * The jobs a committed turn enqueues (data model section 1, steps 6 and 7): one call job per call the turn
 * opened; one notify job when any of the turn's events matches a notification rule, decided with core's
 * matcher (a rule whose expression errored counts, so the job can log it); one publish job for every turn.
 */
import { matchNotifications, type AnyEventRecord, type PublishedDefinition, type RequestState } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Job } from "../store/jobs.ts";

export function jobsForTurn(def: PublishedDefinition, before: RequestState, events: readonly AnyEventRecord[], after: RequestState): Job[] {
  const first = events[0];
  const last = events[events.length - 1];
  if (first === undefined || last === undefined) return [];
  const jobs: Job[] = [];
  for (const e of events) {
    if (e.type === "WaitOpened" && e.payload.kind === "call") jobs.push({ kind: "call", requestId: e.requestId, wait: e.payload.wait });
  }
  const matched = matchNotifications(def, before, events, after);
  if (matched.messages.length > 0 || matched.errors.length > 0) jobs.push({ kind: "notify", requestId: first.requestId, firstSeq: first.seq, lastSeq: last.seq });
  jobs.push({ kind: "publish", requestId: first.requestId, firstSeq: first.seq, lastSeq: last.seq });
  return jobs;
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/turn/turns.ts\n===
/**
 * The turn transaction (kernel spec section 3; data model section 1) around core's `turn`:
 *
 * 0. Without a lock: fold the request's events, refuse an act on a wait that is not open, and make the
 *    lookups the input needs (the actor's groups, the data-source answers). No outside call after this.
 * 1. In one transaction: lock the `requests` row (a start has none yet), waiting at most the lock timeout.
 * 2. Load and fold the request's events.
 * 3. Run core's `turn`. Refused: nothing is written; an attempt is logged after, in its own transaction.
 * 4. Append the events, then in the same transaction: the read tables, `pending_calls`, the start's client
 *    token or its `inbound_log` row, and the jobs.
 * 5. Commit.
 */
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import {
  emptyState,
  isWaitOpen,
  lookupsToMake,
  sameWait,
  turn as coreTurn,
  validateCallResult,
  type By,
  type DecideContext,
  type DecideInput,
  type JsonObject,
  type LookupAnswer,
  type PlannedLookup,
  type PublishedDefinition,
  type RequestState,
  type StartInput,
} from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import { coreVersion } from "@workflow/core";
import { logAttempt } from "../store/attempts.ts";
import { SQLSTATE, sqlState, type Db, type Queryable } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "../store/definitions.ts";
import { appendEvents, loadState } from "../store/events.ts";
import { enqueueJobs } from "../store/jobs.ts";
import { DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, lockRequest } from "../store/lock.ts";
import { applyCallEvents, deletePendingCall } from "../store/pending-calls.ts";
import { listedOf, readStoredStuck, stuckAfterTurn, writeProjections } from "../store/projections.ts";
import { jobsForTurn } from "./jobs-for-turn.ts";
import type {
  ActTurnInput,
  LockedRequest,
  StartTurnInput,
  TurnAccepted,
  TurnLookups,
  TurnOutcome,
  TurnRefusal,
  TurnRefused,
  Turns,
  TurnsOptions,
} from "./types.ts";


/** A time as the events record it: RFC 3339 UTC with six fractional digits. */
export function formatAt(d: Date): string {
  return d.toISOString().replace("Z", "000Z");
}

/** What an attempt writes to the attempts log when the turn refuses it. */
interface AttemptOf {
  requestId: string | null;
  actor: By;
  input: JsonObject;
}

/** What a turn runs, worked out under the lock. */
interface Plan {
  input: DecideInput;
  context: DecideContext;
  /** null: a refusal writes no attempts-log row. */
  attempt: AttemptOf | null;
}

type Planner = (locked: LockedRequest & { at: string }) => Plan | { refuse: TurnRefusal; attempt: AttemptOf };

interface Refused {
  at: string;
  attempt: AttemptOf | null;
  refusals: TurnRefusal[];
}

const refusal = (reason: TurnRefusal["reason"], params: JsonObject = {}): TurnRefused => ({ ok: false, refusals: [{ reason, attempt: false, params }] });


/** Whether the act's wait needs the actor's groups: the actor is a user and the recorded assignees include a group. */
function needsMemberships(state: RequestState, input: ActTurnInput): boolean {
  if (input.by.type !== "user") return false;
  const opened = state.waits.find((w) => sameWait(w.id, input.wait))?.opened;
  return opened?.kind === "person" && opened.assignees.some((a) => a.type === "group");
}

async function memberships(lookups: TurnLookups, userId: string): Promise<{ groups: readonly string[] } | "unavailable"> {
  try {
    return await lookups.memberships(userId);
  } catch {
    return "unavailable";
  }
}

async function answers(lookups: TurnLookups, planned: readonly PlannedLookup[]): Promise<Record<string, LookupAnswer>> {
  const out: Record<string, LookupAnswer> = {};
  for (const p of planned) {
    try {
      out[p.property] = await lookups.lookup(p);
    } catch {
      out[p.property] = { unavailable: true };
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function withRefusals(input: JsonObject, refusals: readonly TurnRefusal[]): JsonObject {
  return { ...input, refusals: refusals.map((r) => ({ reason: r.reason, params: r.params })) };
}

export function createTurns(db: Db, definitions: DefinitionReader, options: TurnsOptions): Turns {
  const clock = options.clock ?? (() => new Date());
  const engineBuild = options.engineBuild ?? `server 0.0.0, core ${coreVersion}`;
  const newRequestId = options.newRequestId ?? (() => randomUUID());
  const lockTimeoutMs = options.lockTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS;

  /** The turn's time: the given one or the clock's, never earlier than the request's last event. */
  function timeOf(given: string | undefined, lastAt: string): string {
    const at = given ?? formatAt(clock());
    return lastAt > at ? lastAt : at;
  }

  async function definitionOf(q: Queryable, state: RequestState): Promise<PublishedDefinition> {
    const runsOn = state.definition;
    if (runsOn === null) throw new Error(`request ${state.requestId} has not started`);
    const def = await definitions.get(q, runsOn.workflow, runsOn.version);
    if (def === null) throw new Error(`request ${state.requestId} runs on ${runsOn.workflow}@${runsOn.version}, which is not in definitions`);
    return def;
  }

  /** A refusal, and its attempts-log row when it is an attempt; a binding's start is logged in `inbound_log` instead. */
  async function logIfAttempt(at: string, attempt: AttemptOf | null, refusals: readonly TurnRefusal[]): Promise<TurnRefused> {
    const first = refusals[0];
    if (attempt !== null && first !== undefined && refusals.some((r) => r.attempt)) {
      await logAttempt(db, { at, requestId: attempt.requestId, actor: attempt.actor, input: withRefusals(attempt.input, refusals), reason: first.reason });
    }
    return { ok: false, refusals: refusals.map((r) => ({ reason: r.reason, attempt: r.attempt, params: r.params })) };
  }

  /**
   * Steps 1 to 5 for one request. `startDefinition` is set for a start, whose request has no events yet.
   * `alsoWrite` writes what only this kind of input writes, in the same transaction.
   */
  async function locked(
    requestId: string,
    startDefinition: PublishedDefinition | null,
    given: string | undefined,
    plan: Planner,
    alsoWrite?: (tx: Queryable, accepted: TurnAccepted) => Promise<void>,
  ): Promise<TurnOutcome> {
    let refused: Refused | null = null;
    let outcome: TurnOutcome;
    try {
      outcome = await db.transaction(async (tx): Promise<TurnOutcome> => {
        await lockRequest(tx, requestId, lockTimeoutMs);
        const { events, state } = await loadState(tx, requestId);
        const definition = state.definition === null && startDefinition !== null ? startDefinition : await definitionOf(tx, state);
        const stuckBefore = await readStoredStuck(tx, requestId);
        const at = timeOf(given, state.lastAt);
        const planned = plan({ state, definition, stuck: stuckBefore, at });
        if ("refuse" in planned) {
          refused = { at, attempt: planned.attempt, refusals: [planned.refuse] };
          return { ok: false, refusals: [] };
        }

        const result = coreTurn(definition, state, planned.input, planned.context);
        if (!result.ok) {
          refused = { at: planned.context.at, attempt: planned.attempt, refusals: result.refusals };
          return { ok: false, refusals: [] };
        }
        const after = result.state;
        const stuck = result.events.length === 0 ? stuckBefore : stuckAfterTurn(definition, stuckBefore, after);
        const accepted: TurnAccepted = {
          ok: true,
          requestId,
          readableId: after.request?.readableId ?? 0,
          workflow: definition.workflow,
          version: definition.version,
          events: result.events,
          state: after,
          stuck,
          lastSeq: after.lastSeq,
          stopped: stuck !== null,
          trace: result.trace,
          dropped: result.dropped,
          replayed: false,
        };
        if (result.events.length === 0) {
          // A dropped result: nothing is recorded, and the call it answered is no longer pending.
          if (planned.input.kind === "callResult") await deletePendingCall(tx, requestId, planned.input.wait);
        } else {
          await appendEvents(tx, result.events);
          const published = await definitions.published(tx, definition.workflow, definition.version);
          await writeProjections(tx, after, stuck, listedOf(published, [...events, ...result.events], after, stuck));
          await applyCallEvents(tx, result.events);
          await enqueueJobs(tx, jobsForTurn(definition, state, result.events, after), planned.context.at);
          await alsoWrite?.(tx, accepted);
        }
        await options.beforeCommit?.(tx, accepted);
        return accepted;
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (sqlState(error) === SQLSTATE.lockNotAvailable) return refusal("busy");
      throw error;
    }
    // Assigned inside the transaction's callback, which the compiler cannot see.
    const r = refused as Refused | null;
    return r === null ? outcome : logIfAttempt(r.at, r.attempt, r.refusals);
  }

  /** The unlocked read of step 0: the request's state and definition, or `not-started`. */
  async function unlocked(requestId: string): Promise<{ state: RequestState; definition: PublishedDefinition } | TurnRefused> {
    const { state } = await loadState(db, requestId);
    if (state.request === null) return refusal("not-started", { requestId });
    return { state, definition: await definitionOf(db, state) };
  }

  /** A start whose client token was used before: the first request again, or `client-token-reused`. */
  async function replay(by: By, token: { token: string; argsHash: string }): Promise<TurnOutcome | null> {
    const rows = await db.query<{ id: string; client_args_hash: string }>("SELECT id, client_args_hash FROM requests WHERE started_by = $1::jsonb AND client_token = $2", [
      JSON.stringify({ type: by.type, id: by.id }),
      token.token,
    ]);
    const row = rows[0];
    if (row === undefined) return null;
    if (row.client_args_hash !== token.argsHash) return refusal("client-token-reused", { requestId: row.id });
    const { state } = await loadState(db, row.id);
    const definition = await definitionOf(db, state);
    const stuck = await readStoredStuck(db, row.id);
    return {
      ok: true,
      requestId: row.id,
      readableId: state.request?.readableId ?? 0,
      workflow: definition.workflow,
      version: definition.version,
      events: [],
      state,
      stuck,
      lastSeq: state.lastSeq,
      stopped: stuck !== null,
      trace: [],
      dropped: null,
      replayed: true,
    };
  }

  /** A start through a binding whose event already started a request of this workflow. */
  async function startedByEvent(workflow: string, trigger: StartTurnInput["trigger"]): Promise<TurnRefused | null> {
    if (trigger === undefined || trigger === null || trigger.kind !== "event") return null;
    const rows = await db.query<{ request_id: string }>("SELECT request_id FROM inbound_log WHERE connection = $1 AND event_id = $2 AND workflow = $3 AND result = 'started'", [
      trigger["connection"],
      trigger["eventId"],
      workflow,
    ]);
    const row = rows[0];
    return row === undefined ? null : refusal("already-started", { requestId: row.request_id });
  }

  return {
    async start(input) {
      const version = input.version ?? (await definitions.highest(db, input.workflow));
      if (version === null) return refusal("not-found", { workflow: input.workflow });
      const definition = await definitions.get(db, input.workflow, version);
      if (definition === null) return refusal("not-found", { workflow: input.workflow, version });
      const trigger = input.trigger ?? null;
      if (input.clientToken !== undefined) {
        const earlier = await replay(input.by, input.clientToken);
        if (earlier !== null) return earlier;
      }
      const duplicate = await startedByEvent(input.workflow, trigger);
      if (duplicate !== null) return duplicate;

      const n = await db.query<{ n: number | string }>("SELECT nextval('request_readable_id') AS n");
      const readableId = Number(n[0]?.n);
      const requestId = newRequestId(readableId);
      // A start has no earlier event; its time is fixed now, since a lookup input may read request.at.
      const at = timeOf(input.at, "");
      const startInput: StartInput = { kind: "start", requestId, readableId, by: input.by, outcome: input.outcome, data: input.data, trigger };
      const looked = await answers(options.lookups, lookupsToMake(definition, emptyState(), startInput, at));
      // A binding's refused start is the hook's `inbound_log` row, not an attempt.
      const attempt: AttemptOf | null = trigger === null ? { requestId: null, actor: input.by, input: { kind: "start", workflow: input.workflow, version, outcome: input.outcome } } : null;

      try {
        return await locked(
          requestId,
          definition,
          at,
          () => ({ input: startInput, context: { at, engineBuild, lookups: looked }, attempt }),
          async (tx, accepted) => {
            if (input.clientToken !== undefined) {
              await tx.query("UPDATE requests SET client_token = $2, client_args_hash = $3 WHERE id = $1", [accepted.requestId, input.clientToken.token, input.clientToken.argsHash]);
            }
            if (trigger !== null && trigger.kind === "event") {
              await tx.query(
                `INSERT INTO inbound_log (at, connection, event_id, workflow, version, binding, result, request_id, sent, by, retry_of)
                 VALUES ($1::timestamptz, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, 'started', $7, $8::jsonb, $9::jsonb, $10)`,
                [
                  at,
                  trigger["connection"],
                  trigger["eventId"],
                  input.workflow,
                  version,
                  trigger.id,
                  accepted.requestId,
                  input.inbound?.sent === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(input.inbound.sent),
                  input.inbound?.by === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(input.inbound.by),
                  input.inbound?.retryOf ?? null,
                ],
              );
            }
          },
        );
      } catch (error) {
        // Two starts with one token, or for one event, at once: the second's insert fails and it answers as the first.
        if (sqlState(error) !== SQLSTATE.uniqueViolation) throw error;
        const again = input.clientToken === undefined ? null : await replay(input.by, input.clientToken);
        const dup = again ?? (await startedByEvent(input.workflow, trigger));
        if (dup === null) throw error;
        return dup;
      }
    },

    async act(input) {
      const read = await unlocked(input.requestId);
      if ("ok" in read) return read;
      const { state, definition } = read;
      const actInput = { kind: "act", by: input.by, wait: input.wait, outcome: input.outcome, data: input.data } as const;
      const attempt: AttemptOf = { requestId: input.requestId, actor: input.by, input: { kind: "act", wait: { ...input.wait }, outcome: input.outcome } };
      const open = state.closed === null && isWaitOpen(state, input.wait);
      if (!open) {
        // Refused from the unlocked read, with no lookup (runtime API section 4.3 step 2).
        const at = timeOf(input.at, state.lastAt);
        const result = coreTurn(definition, state, actInput, { at, engineBuild });
        if (!result.ok) return logIfAttempt(at, attempt, result.refusals);
      }
      const groups = needsMemberships(state, input) ? await memberships(options.lookups, input.by.id) : undefined;
      const looked = await answers(options.lookups, lookupsToMake(definition, state, actInput));
      return locked(input.requestId, null, input.at, ({ at }) => ({
        input: actInput,
        context: groups === undefined ? { at, engineBuild, lookups: looked } : { at, engineBuild, lookups: looked, memberships: groups },
        attempt,
      }));
    },

    async callResult(input) {
      const read = await unlocked(input.requestId);
      if ("ok" in read) return read;
      // Checked before the turn, as the call job checks it. A wait that is not a call is left to the kernel.
      const check = validateCallResult(read.definition, input.wait, { outcome: input.outcome, data: input.data });
      if (!check.ok && check.reason !== "unknown-call") return { ...refusal("result-invalid", { reason: check.reason }), resultInvalid: check };
      const opened = read.state.waits.find((w) => sameWait(w.id, input.wait))?.opened;
      const actor: By = opened?.kind === "call" ? { type: "connection", id: opened.connection } : { type: "system", id: "engine" };
      return locked(input.requestId, null, input.at, ({ at }) => ({
        input: { kind: "callResult", wait: input.wait, outcome: input.outcome, data: input.data },
        context: { at, engineBuild },
        attempt: { requestId: input.requestId, actor, input: { kind: "callResult", wait: { ...input.wait }, outcome: input.outcome } },
      }));
    },

    async admin(input) {
      const read = await unlocked(input.requestId);
      if ("ok" in read) return read;
      return locked(input.requestId, null, input.at, (lockedRequest) => {
        const { state, at } = lockedRequest;
        const attemptOf = (actions: unknown[]): AttemptOf => ({
          requestId: input.requestId,
          actor: input.by,
          input: { kind: "admin", reason: input.reason, actions: actions as JsonObject[] },
        });
        // The caller's refusals that come before `stale` (not-admin, reason-required), then `stale`, then the
        // planner's (runtime-api.md 5.1).
        const first = input.refuseFirst?.(lockedRequest) ?? null;
        if (first !== null) return { refuse: first, attempt: attemptOf([]) };
        if (input.isAdmin && input.expectedLastSeq !== undefined && input.expectedLastSeq !== state.lastSeq) {
          return { refuse: { reason: "stale", attempt: false, params: { lastSeq: state.lastSeq } }, attempt: attemptOf([]) };
        }
        let actions = input.actions;
        if (typeof actions === "function") {
          const planned = actions(lockedRequest);
          if ("refuse" in planned) return { refuse: planned.refuse, attempt: attemptOf([]) };
          actions = planned.actions;
        }
        return {
          input: { kind: "admin", by: input.by, reason: input.reason, actions },
          context: { at, engineBuild, isAdmin: input.isAdmin },
          attempt: attemptOf(actions),
        };
      });
    },
  };
}

/** What the turn transaction takes and returns. */
import type {
  AdminAction,
  AnyEventRecord,
  By,
  CallResultCheck,
  DropReason,
  JsonObject,
  LookupAnswer,
  PlannedLookup,
  PublishedDefinition,
  RefusalReason,
  RequestState,
  StartTrigger,
  TraceEntry,
  WaitId,
} from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { StoredStuck } from "../store/projections.ts";

/**
 * The live lookups made before a request is locked (kernel spec section 2, Person; data model section 1
 * step 0). Supplied by the caller: the directory and the data sources are outside systems. A lookup that
 * throws counts as one that could not be made.
 */
export interface TurnLookups {
  /** The user's group IDs now, or "unavailable" when the directory cannot be asked. */
  memberships(userId: string): Promise<{ groups: readonly string[] } | "unavailable">;
  /** One answer looked up in its data source by its stored value (core's `lookupsToMake` plans them). */
  lookup(planned: PlannedLookup): Promise<LookupAnswer>;
}

/** Refusals the server adds to the kernel's. None of them is an attempt. */
export type ServerRefusalReason =
  /** The request's lock was not obtained in time (runtime API section 4.3 step 4). */
  | "busy"
  /** An admin turn's `expectedLastSeq` is not the request's last seq; params `{lastSeq}`. */
  | "stale"
  /** No such workflow, version or request; params name which. */
  | "not-found"
  /** The start's client token started a request with other arguments. */
  | "client-token-reused"
  /** A call result that does not fit its declared shape; the call stays pending. */
  | "result-invalid";

export interface TurnRefusal {
  /** The kernel's, the server's, or an admin planner's own (such as the runtime API's `not-stuck`). */
  reason: RefusalReason | ServerRefusalReason | (string & {});
  /** Whether it was written to the attempts log. */
  attempt: boolean;
  params: JsonObject;
}

export interface TurnAccepted {
  ok: true;
  requestId: string;
  readableId: number;
  workflow: string;
  version: number;
  /** The events appended, in order; [] for a dropped call result and for a replayed start. */
  events: AnyEventRecord[];
  /** The request's state after the turn. */
  state: RequestState;
  /** `requests.stuck` after the turn. */
  stuck: StoredStuck | null;
  lastSeq: number;
  /** The request is stuck after the turn, for any reason (runtime API `stopped`). */
  stopped: boolean;
  trace: TraceEntry[];
  dropped: DropReason | null;
  /** A start whose client token had already started this request: nothing was written. */
  replayed: boolean;
}

export interface TurnRefused {
  ok: false;
  /** The first failing step's refusals, every one of that step. */
  refusals: TurnRefusal[];
  /** Set with `result-invalid`: core's call-result check. */
  resultInvalid?: Extract<CallResultCheck, { ok: false }>;
}

export type TurnOutcome = TurnAccepted | TurnRefused;

interface Timed {
  /** The turn's time, for tests; default the clock, never earlier than the request's last event. */
  at?: string;
}

export interface StartTurnInput extends Timed {
  workflow: string;
  /** The version whose start form was shown; absent: the highest. */
  version?: number;
  by: By;
  outcome: string;
  data: JsonObject;
  /** A start through a binding: the trigger to record. The turn also inserts its `inbound_log` row, result `started`. */
  trigger?: StartTrigger | null;
  /** For that row: the parsed events, and for a run again the admin and the refused row it runs again. */
  inbound?: { sent?: JsonObject; by?: By; retryOf?: number };
  /** A person's start: the token and the hash of the start's arguments (runtime API section 3.3). */
  clientToken?: { token: string; argsHash: string };
}

export interface ActTurnInput extends Timed {
  requestId: string;
  by: By;
  wait: WaitId;
  outcome: string;
  data: JsonObject;
}

export interface CallResultTurnInput extends Timed {
  requestId: string;
  wait: WaitId;
  outcome: "ok" | "failed";
  data: JsonObject;
}

/** What an admin planner sees: the request under its lock. */
export interface LockedRequest {
  state: RequestState;
  definition: PublishedDefinition;
  stuck: StoredStuck | null;
}

/** Works out an admin turn's actions under the lock (Retry needs the stuck state), or refuses. */
export type AdminPlanner = (locked: LockedRequest) => { actions: AdminAction[] } | { refuse: TurnRefusal };

export interface AdminTurnInput extends Timed {
  requestId: string;
  by: By;
  reason: string;
  /** Decided by the caller (spec section 4: who is an admin is decided outside the kernel). */
  isAdmin: boolean;
  /** Run under the lock after `refuseFirst` and the `stale` check. */
  actions: AdminAction[] | AdminPlanner;
  /**
   * The caller's refusals that come before `stale` in its documented order (the runtime API's not-admin and
   * reason-required), run first under the lock; null to go on.
   */
  refuseFirst?: (locked: LockedRequest) => TurnRefusal | null;
  /** Checked under the lock when the caller is an admin, after `refuseFirst`: a mismatch refuses `stale`. */
  expectedLastSeq?: number;
}

export interface TurnsOptions {
  lookups: TurnLookups;
  /** The clock for a turn's time; default the system clock. */
  clock?: () => Date;
  /** The envelope's `engineBuild`. */
  engineBuild?: string;
  /** A new request's ID from its readable ID; default a random UUID. */
  newRequestId?: (readableId: number) => string;
  /** How long a turn waits for the request's lock before `busy`; default 5000 ms. */
  lockTimeoutMs?: number;
  /** For tests: runs inside the transaction after everything is written, before the commit. */
  beforeCommit?: (tx: Queryable, accepted: TurnAccepted) => Promise<void>;
}

export interface Turns {
  start(input: StartTurnInput): Promise<TurnOutcome>;
  act(input: ActTurnInput): Promise<TurnOutcome>;
  callResult(input: CallResultTurnInput): Promise<TurnOutcome>;
  admin(input: AdminTurnInput): Promise<TurnOutcome>;
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/workers/call.ts\n===
/**
 * The call job (integrations.md 10.2 and 10.3): one per opened call, on its own queue. Each time it runs it
 * reads the call's `pending_calls` row and:
 *
 * 1. No row: done. A closed wait whose call was never sent, or is a read: the row is deleted, nothing recorded.
 * 2. Without a job reference: sends the call with the recorded key. With one (an await running outside): asks
 *    for that job's status.
 * 3. `ok` or `failed`: the result turn, which records `WaitCompleted`, or `CallResultLate` for a closed wait.
 * 4. `accepted` (keeps the job reference) or `running`: runs again after the entry's poll interval.
 * 5. No answer, an answer that does not fit or names another job, or a connection that is not ready: runs
 *    again later with the same key. Never recorded.
 */
import type { Catalogue, Operation } from "@workflow/core";
import type { JsonObject, WaitId } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Log, LogLine } from "../config/log.ts";
import type { CatalogueRegistry } from "../api/shared/catalogue.ts";
import { within } from "../connectors/lookups.ts";
import type { CallAnswer, Connectors, StatusAnswer } from "../connectors/types.ts";
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { CallJob } from "../store/jobs.ts";
import { waitKeyOf } from "../store/jobs.ts";
import { countAttempt, deletePendingCall, keepJobRef, readPendingCall, setLastError } from "../store/pending-calls.ts";
import type { Turns } from "../turn/types.ts";
import { backoffSeconds, type JobHandler, type JobOutcome } from "./loop.ts";

export interface CallJobDeps {
  db: Db;
  turns: Turns;
  connectors: Connectors;
  catalogue: CatalogueRegistry;
  log: Log;
  clock: () => Date;
}

function operationOf(catalogue: Catalogue, entry: string): Operation | undefined {
  const e = catalogue.entries.find((x) => x.id === entry);
  if (e?.kind !== "operation" || e.status !== "ready") return undefined;
  return catalogue.connections.find((c) => c.id === e.connection)?.status === "ready" ? e : undefined;
}

export function callJob(deps: CallJobDeps): JobHandler {
  const { db, log } = deps;
  return async ({ job, attempts }): Promise<JobOutcome> => {
    const { requestId, wait } = job as CallJob;
    const row = await readPendingCall(db, requestId, wait);
    if (row === null) return "done";
    if (row.waitClosed && (row.attempts === 0 || row.effect === "read")) {
      await deletePendingCall(db, requestId, wait);
      return "done";
    }
    const entry = `${row.connection}.${row.op}`;
    const ids: Omit<LogLine, "kind"> = { request: requestId, wait: waitKeyOf(requestId, wait), connection: row.connection, entry };
    const again = async (code: string, detail: string | null = null): Promise<JobOutcome> => {
      await setLastError(db, requestId, wait, detail ?? code);
      return { againAfter: backoffSeconds(attempts), error: code };
    };
    const op = operationOf(deps.catalogue.current(), entry);
    const connector = deps.connectors.operation(row.connection);
    if (op === undefined || connector === undefined) {
      log({ kind: "call-attempt", ...ids, code: "not-ready" });
      return again("not-ready");
    }
    const now = deps.clock();
    if (row.waitClosed) log({ kind: "call-outcome-unknown", ...ids });
    if (now.getTime() - Date.parse(row.openedAt) > op.expectedWithinSeconds * 1000) log({ kind: "call-overdue", ...ids });

    let answer: CallAnswer | StatusAnswer;
    try {
      if (row.jobRef === null) {
        await countAttempt(db, requestId, wait, now.toISOString());
        answer = await within(connector.call({ op: row.op, args: row.args as JsonObject, key: row.idempotencyKey }), op.timeoutSeconds * 1000);
      } else {
        if (connector.status === undefined) throw new Error(`${entry} cannot be asked for its status`);
        answer = await within(connector.status({ op: row.op, key: row.idempotencyKey, jobRef: row.jobRef }), op.timeoutSeconds * 1000);
      }
    } catch (error) {
      answer = { answer: "unknown", detail: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) };
    }
    log({ kind: "call-attempt", ...ids, code: answer.answer });
    if (answer.answer === "unknown") return again("unknown", answer.detail);

    // An await op names its job in every answer but `unknown`, and only the job the row holds counts.
    const isAwait = op.sort === "await";
    const jobRef = "jobRef" in answer ? answer.jobRef : undefined;
    if ((answer.answer === "accepted" || answer.answer === "running") && !isAwait) {
      log({ kind: "result-invalid", ...ids });
      return again("result-invalid");
    }
    if (isAwait && (jobRef === undefined || jobRef === "" || jobRef.length > 255)) {
      log({ kind: "result-invalid", ...ids });
      return again("result-invalid");
    }
    if (isAwait && row.jobRef !== null && jobRef !== row.jobRef) {
      log({ kind: "job-mismatch", ...ids });
      return again("job-mismatch");
    }
    if (isAwait && row.jobRef === null && jobRef !== undefined) await keepJobRef(db, requestId, wait, jobRef);
    if (answer.answer === "accepted" || answer.answer === "running") return { againAfter: op.await?.pollSeconds ?? 60 };

    const data: JsonObject = answer.answer === "ok" ? answer.data : { code: answer.code, message: answer.message };
    return resultTurn(deps, requestId, wait, answer.answer, data, ids, again);
  };
}

async function resultTurn(
  deps: CallJobDeps,
  requestId: string,
  wait: WaitId,
  outcome: "ok" | "failed",
  data: JsonObject,
  ids: Omit<LogLine, "kind">,
  again: (code: string) => Promise<JobOutcome>,
): Promise<JobOutcome> {
  const out = await deps.turns.callResult({ requestId, wait, outcome, data });
  if (out.ok) return "done";
  const reason = out.refusals[0]?.reason ?? "internal";
  if (reason === "result-invalid") {
    deps.log({ kind: "result-invalid", ...ids });
    return again("result-invalid");
  }
  if (reason === "busy") return again("busy");
  throw new Error(`the call result was refused: ${reason}`);
}

/** The worker loop and its three jobs: calls, notifications and outbound events. */
import type { CatalogueRegistry } from "../api/shared/catalogue.ts";
import type { Subscriber } from "../config/config.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";
import type { Connectors } from "../connectors/types.ts";
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "../store/definitions.ts";
import type { Turns } from "../turn/types.ts";
import { callJob } from "./call.ts";
import { createWorkerLoop, type WorkerLoop } from "./loop.ts";
import { notifyJob } from "./notify.ts";
import { publishJob, type OutboundSink } from "./publish.ts";

export { backoffSeconds, createWorkerLoop, type JobHandler, type JobOutcome, type TakenJob, type WorkerLoop, type WorkerLoopOptions } from "./loop.ts";
export { callJob, type CallJobDeps } from "./call.ts";
export { notifyJob, type NotifyJobDeps } from "./notify.ts";
export { httpSink, memorySink, publishJob, type OutboundSink, type PublishJobDeps } from "./publish.ts";

export interface WorkerDeps {
  db: Db;
  turns: Turns;
  definitions: DefinitionReader;
  connectors: Connectors;
  catalogue: CatalogueRegistry;
  subscribers: readonly Subscriber[];
  /** Where outbound events go; the plain HTTP sink when not given. */
  sink?: OutboundSink;
  deploymentUri: string;
  log: Log;
  clock?: () => Date;
  name?: string;
}

/**
 * The server's worker loop over every kind of job. A call's lock is stale after the longest operation timeout
 * plus 30 s; the others' after 60 s.
 */
export function createWorker(deps: WorkerDeps): WorkerLoop {
  const clock = deps.clock ?? (() => new Date());
  const longest = Math.max(0, ...deps.catalogue.current().entries.map((e) => (e.kind === "operation" ? e.timeoutSeconds : 0)));
  return createWorkerLoop({
    db: deps.db,
    log: deps.log,
    clock,
    ...(deps.name === undefined ? {} : { name: deps.name }),
    lockSeconds: { call: longest + 30 },
    handlers: {
      call: callJob({ db: deps.db, turns: deps.turns, connectors: deps.connectors, catalogue: deps.catalogue, log: deps.log, clock }),
      notify: notifyJob({ db: deps.db, definitions: deps.definitions, connectors: deps.connectors, log: deps.log }),
      publish: publishJob({ db: deps.db, definitions: deps.definitions, subscribers: deps.subscribers, ...(deps.sink === undefined ? {} : { sink: deps.sink }), deploymentUri: deps.deploymentUri, log: deps.log }),
    },
  });
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/workers/loop.ts\n===
/**
 * One worker loop over the jobs table (data model section 5). A job is taken in its own short transaction
 * (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, the oldest due job whose queue has no older job), its handler runs outside any
 * transaction, and then the job is deleted, or put back with a later run time. A job whose lock is older than
 * its kind's limit was left by a worker that died, and is taken again.
 */
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { Job } from "../store/jobs.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";

export interface TakenJob {
  id: number;
  /** The job as enqueued. */
  job: Job;
  /** How many times it has been taken, this time included. */
  attempts: number;
}

/** Done, or run again after some seconds (a poll, or a try that got no answer), keeping `error` as the last error. */
export type JobOutcome = "done" | { againAfter: number; error?: string };

export type JobHandler = (taken: TakenJob) => Promise<JobOutcome>;

/** 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, then every 15 min, without limit. */
export function backoffSeconds(attempts: number): number {
  return [10, 30, 60, 300][attempts - 1] ?? 900;
}

export interface WorkerLoopOptions {
  db: Db;
  handlers: { [K in Job["kind"]]: JobHandler };
  log: Log;
  clock?: () => Date;
  /** This worker's name in `locked_by`. */
  name?: string;
  /** Seconds after which a job's lock is stale, by kind. Default 60. */
  lockSeconds?: Partial<Record<Job["kind"], number>>;
}

export interface WorkerLoop {
  /** Takes one due job and runs it; false when no job is due. */
  runOnce(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Runs due jobs until none is due; returns how many ran. Throws after `max`, so a test cannot loop for ever. */
  runUntilIdle(max?: number): Promise<number>;
  /** Polls every `intervalMs` until stopped. */
  start(intervalMs?: number): void;
  /** Stops polling and waits for the job that is running. */
  stop(): Promise<void>;
}

export function createWorkerLoop(options: WorkerLoopOptions): WorkerLoop {
  const { db, handlers, log } = options;
  const clock = options.clock ?? (() => new Date());
  const name = options.name ?? `worker-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;
  const lock = (kind: Job["kind"]): number => options.lockSeconds?.[kind] ?? 60;

  async function take(now: string): Promise<TakenJob | null> {
    return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      const rows = await tx.query<{ id: number | string; kind: Job["kind"]; payload: Record<string, unknown>; attempts: number }>(
        `SELECT id, kind, payload, attempts FROM jobs j
         WHERE run_at <= $1::timestamptz
           AND (locked_at IS NULL OR locked_at < $1::timestamptz - make_interval(secs => CASE kind WHEN 'call' THEN $2::float8 WHEN 'notify' THEN $3::float8 ELSE $4::float8 END))
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jobs e WHERE e.queue = j.queue AND e.id < j.id)
         ORDER BY run_at, id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`,
        [now, lock("call"), lock("notify"), lock("publish")],
      );
      const row = rows[0];
      if (row === undefined) return null;
      await tx.query("UPDATE jobs SET locked_at = $2::timestamptz, locked_by = $3, attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = $1", [row.id, now, name]);
      return { id: Number(row.id), job: { kind: row.kind, ...row.payload } as Job, attempts: row.attempts + 1 };
    });
  }

  async function putBack(taken: TakenJob, seconds: number, error: string | null): Promise<void> {
    await db.query(
      "UPDATE jobs SET run_at = $2::timestamptz, locked_at = NULL, locked_by = NULL, last_error = $3 WHERE id = $1 AND locked_by = $4",
      [taken.id, new Date(clock().getTime() + seconds * 1000).toISOString(), error, name],
    );
  }

  async function runOnce(): Promise<boolean> {
    const taken = await take(clock().toISOString());
    if (taken === null) return false;
    let outcome: JobOutcome;
    try {
      outcome = await handlers[taken.job.kind](taken);
    } catch (error) {
      log({ kind: "job-failed", request: taken.job.requestId, code: taken.job.kind, detail: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
      await putBack(taken, backoffSeconds(taken.attempts), String(error));
      return true;
    }
    if (outcome === "done") await db.query("DELETE FROM jobs WHERE id = $1 AND locked_by = $2", [taken.id, name]);
    else await putBack(taken, outcome.againAfter, outcome.error ?? null);
    return true;
  }

  let running: Promise<void> | null = null;
  let stopped = false;
  return {
    runOnce,
    async runUntilIdle(max = 1000) {
      let n = 0;
      while (await runOnce()) {
        n += 1;
        if (n >= max) throw new Error(`runUntilIdle: still busy after ${max} jobs`);
      }
      return n;
    },
    start(intervalMs = 1000) {
      if (running !== null) return;
      stopped = false;
      running = (async () => {
        while (!stopped) {
          let ran = false;
          try {
            ran = await runOnce();
          } catch (error) {
            log({ kind: "job-failed", detail: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
          }
          if (!ran && !stopped) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
        }
      })();
    },
    async stop() {
      stopped = true;
      await running;
      running = null;
    },
  };
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/workers/notify.ts\n===
/**
 * The notify job (integrations.md 12.3): one per turn whose events could match a notification rule. Core's
 * matcher works out the messages; each is sent to every person it names through the notify connection. A
 * group is expanded through the directory and the workflow admins are read from the settings when sending. A
 * person who may not answer a task is not told about it. A rule whose expression errors is a log line. A job
 * that fails runs again, so a message can be sent twice.
 */
import { matchNotifications, type PersonWaitOpened } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import { lookAfterStuck, mayNotAnswer, readWorkflowPeople } from "../api/shared/people.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";
import type { Connectors } from "../connectors/types.ts";
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "../store/definitions.ts";
import type { NotifyJob } from "../store/jobs.ts";
import type { JobHandler } from "./loop.ts";
import { readTurn } from "./read-turn.ts";

export interface NotifyJobDeps {
  db: Db;
  definitions: DefinitionReader;
  connectors: Connectors;
  log: Log;
}

export function notifyJob(deps: NotifyJobDeps): JobHandler {
  const { db, connectors, log } = deps;
  return async ({ job }) => {
    const { requestId, firstSeq, lastSeq } = job as NotifyJob;
    const { definition, before, events, after } = await readTurn(db, deps.definitions, requestId, firstSeq, lastSeq);
    const result = matchNotifications(definition, before, events, after);
    for (const e of result.errors) log({ kind: "rule-error", request: requestId, rule: e.rule, code: e.failure.code });
    const people = async (refs: readonly { type: string; id?: string }[]): Promise<Set<string>> => {
      const out = new Set<string>();
      for (const r of refs) {
        if (r.type === "user" && r.id !== undefined) out.add(r.id);
        if (r.type === "group" && r.id !== undefined) for (const m of await connectors.directory.membersOf(r.id)) if (m.type === "user") out.add(m.id);
        if (r.type === "workflowAdmins") {
          const settings = await readWorkflowPeople(db, definition.workflow);
          for (const id of settings === null ? [] : await people(lookAfterStuck(settings))) out.add(id);
        }
      }
      return out;
    };
    for (const m of result.messages) {
      const to = await people(m.to);
      const opened = m.event.type === "WaitOpened" ? (m.event.payload as PersonWaitOpened) : null;
      const excluded = opened?.kind === "person" ? mayNotAnswer(definition, after, opened.wait.element) : null;
      if (excluded !== null) to.delete(excluded);
      for (const person of to) {
        await connectors.notifier.send({
          to: person,
          requestId,
          readableId: after.request?.readableId ?? 0,
          workflow: definition.workflow,
          version: definition.version,
          rule: m.rule,
          event: m.event,
          message: m.message,
        });
      }
    }
    return "done";
  };
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/workers/publish.ts\n===
/**
 * The publish job (integrations.md 13.4): one per turn that appended events, on the request's publish queue, so a
 * request's turns are published in order. Core works out the turn's outbound events; each is posted, in
 * order, to every subscriber address in the configuration: by plain HTTP unless a sink is given (the
 * in-memory sinks of the tests and the reporting mock). A post that is not acknowledged fails the job, which
 * runs again from the turn's first event: delivery is at least once. Nothing is stored.
 */
import { outboundEvents, type OutboundEventBody } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Subscriber } from "../config/config.ts";
import type { Log } from "../config/log.ts";
import type { Db } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "../store/definitions.ts";
import type { PublishJob } from "../store/jobs.ts";
import type { JobHandler } from "./loop.ts";
import { readTurn } from "./read-turn.ts";

/** Where outbound events go. `post` resolves when the address acknowledged the event, else rejects. */
export interface OutboundSink {
  post(subscriber: Subscriber, event: OutboundEventBody): Promise<void>;
}

/** A sink that keeps what it received, for tests. `failPost(n)` makes the n-th post from now fail. */
export function memorySink(): OutboundSink & { received: { url: string; event: OutboundEventBody }[]; failPost(n: number): void } {
  let posts = 0;
  const failing = new Set<number>();
  const received: { url: string; event: OutboundEventBody }[] = [];
  return {
    received,
    failPost: (n) => failing.add(posts + n),
    async post(subscriber, event) {
      posts += 1;
      if (failing.delete(posts)) throw new Error(`${subscriber.url} did not acknowledge`);
      received.push({ url: subscriber.url, event });
    },
  };
}

/**
 * The plain HTTP sink: each event POSTed as JSON (`application/cloudevents+json`) to the subscriber's http or
 * https address, unsigned. Any 2xx within the timeout acknowledges; any other answer, an error or the timeout
 * rejects, so the job runs again later. An address that is not http or https rejects too.
 */
export function httpSink(options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): OutboundSink {
  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? 10_000;
  return {
    async post(subscriber, event) {
      const protocol = URL.canParse(subscriber.url) ? new URL(subscriber.url).protocol : "";
      if (protocol !== "http:" && protocol !== "https:") throw new Error(`${subscriber.url} is not an http or https address`);
      const res = await fetch(subscriber.url, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "content-type": "application/cloudevents+json" },
        body: JSON.stringify(event),
        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),
      });
      await res.body?.cancel();
      if (res.status < 200 || res.status > 299) throw new Error(`${subscriber.url} answered ${res.status}`);
    },
  };
}

export interface PublishJobDeps {
  db: Db;
  definitions: DefinitionReader;
  subscribers: readonly Subscriber[];
  /** Where events go; the plain HTTP sink when not given. */
  sink?: OutboundSink;
  deploymentUri: string;
  log: Log;
}

export function publishJob(deps: PublishJobDeps): JobHandler {
  const sink = deps.sink ?? httpSink();
  return async ({ job }) => {
    const { requestId, firstSeq, lastSeq } = job as PublishJob;
    const { definition, before, events, after } = await readTurn(deps.db, deps.definitions, requestId, firstSeq, lastSeq);
    const out = outboundEvents(definition, before, events, after, { deploymentUri: deps.deploymentUri });
    for (const e of out.errors) deps.log({ kind: "rule-error", request: requestId, rule: e.rule, code: e.failure.code });
    for (const row of out.events) for (const s of deps.subscribers) await sink.post(s, row.body);
    return "done";
  };
}
===\nengine/packages/server/src/workers/read-turn.ts\n===
/** One committed turn as the notify and publish jobs read it: the request before it, its events, after it, and its own version. */
import { emptyState, fold, type AnyEventRecord, type PublishedDefinition, type RequestState } from "@workflow/core/kernel";
import type { Queryable } from "../store/db.ts";
import type { DefinitionReader } from "../store/definitions.ts";
import { loadEvents } from "../store/events.ts";

export interface ReadTurn {
  definition: PublishedDefinition;
  before: RequestState;
  events: AnyEventRecord[];
  after: RequestState;
}

export async function readTurn(q: Queryable, definitions: DefinitionReader, requestId: string, firstSeq: number, lastSeq: number): Promise<ReadTurn> {
  const all = await loadEvents(q, requestId);
  const earlier = all.filter((e) => e.seq < firstSeq);
  const events = all.filter((e) => e.seq >= firstSeq && e.seq <= lastSeq);
  const before = earlier.length === 0 ? emptyState() : fold(earlier);
  const after = fold(events, before);
  const runsOn = after.definition;
  const definition = runsOn === null ? null : await definitions.get(q, runsOn.workflow, runsOn.version);
  if (definition === null) throw new Error(`request ${requestId} has no stored version`);
  return { definition, before, events, after };
}

/**
 * Two authors saving or publishing one workflow at the same moment, on two connections of a real Postgres
 * (E-11: PGlite serves one connection and cannot show it). The workflow row's lock serialises them: one
 * wins and the other is `stale-revision`; two publishes never make the same version. Skipped unless
 * DATABASE_URL names a Postgres the tests may use; each run works in a schema of its own and drops it after.
 *
 *   $env:DATABASE_URL = "postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres"; npx vitest run packages/server/test/api/authoring/concurrency.pg.test.ts
 */
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import pg from "pg";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { blankWorkflow } from "@workflow/core";
import { postgresDb, type Db } from "../../../src/store/db.ts";
import { migrate } from "../../../src/store/migrate.ts";
import { resetDb } from "../../helpers.ts";
import { create, harness, withTodo, type Harness } from "./setup.ts";

const url = process.env["DATABASE_URL"];
const schema = `wf_test_${randomUUID().replaceAll("-", "")}`;

describe.skipIf(url === undefined)("authoring on a real Postgres (skipped: set DATABASE_URL to a Postgres the tests may use)", () => {
  let pool: pg.Pool;
  let db: Db;
  let h: Harness;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const admin = new pg.Pool({ connectionString: url, max: 1 });
    await admin.query(`CREATE SCHEMA ${schema}`);
    await admin.end();
    pool = new pg.Pool({ connectionString: url, max: 6, options: `-c search_path=${schema}` });
    db = postgresDb(pool);
    await migrate(db);
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    if (db === undefined) return;
    await pool.query(`DROP SCHEMA ${schema} CASCADE`);
    await db.close();
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await resetDb(db);
    h = harness(db);
  });

  it("two saves on one revision at once: one is saved, the other is stale-revision", async () => {
    const id = await create(h);
    const caller = { user: "u-ann", platformAdmin: false };
    const results = await Promise.all([
      h.api.saveDraft(caller, id, { baseRevision: 1, authored: blankWorkflow() }),
      h.api.saveDraft(caller, id, { baseRevision: 1, authored: withTodo(blankWorkflow()) }),
    ]);
    expect(results.filter((r) => r.ok)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(results.flatMap((r) => (r.ok ? [] : r.errors.map((e) => e.code)))).toEqual(["stale-revision"]);
  });

  it("two publishes at once make versions 1 and 2", async () => {
    const id = await create(h);
    const caller = { user: "u-ann", platformAdmin: false };
    const results = await Promise.all([1, 2].map(() => h.api.publish(caller, id, { revision: 1, coreVersion: "0.0.0" })));
    expect(results.map((r) => (r.ok ? r.value.version : 0)).sort()).toEqual([1, 2]);
  });
});
