===\nengine/spec/open-questions.md\n===
# Workflow engine: open questions

Everything undecided, in one place, against `kernel/kernel-spec.md` v2.20. Each item says who can answer it. A planner should not invent answers to sections 1 and 2; for sections 3 to 5, state the assumption made.

## 1. The authoring backend

The first release lets an author build a workflow without writing code, try it, and publish it. The backend that sits between an author and a published definition is designed outside this package, with the editor. This table says what each piece is and what it needs from the engine. Answered by: the authoring design; "who may author" by the product owner.

| Piece | Status | What it needs from the engine |
|---|---|---|
| Drafts | Designed. The engine stores one draft per workflow beside its published versions; a published version stores the authored source beside the compiled definition. | `workflows`, `drafts` and the authoring columns of `definitions` (`kernel/data-model.md`). |
| The authored format | Designed. The editor's format is compiled at publish straight into kernel elements. One authored stage becomes a chain of engine stages; authored IDs carry through as value, outcome, wait and status IDs. | Publish, the publish checks and the origin map (spec sections 6 and 7). Engine stage IDs are recorded for ever, so the compiler's stage names are fixed before anything is published. |
| Author-defined questions | Designed. A question has a value kind (`integrations.md` section 8.1); the compiler derives the JSON Schema and the per-outcome checks; a question's choices may come from a data source. | Schema validation, checks, and the outcome's `lookups` (spec section 2; `integrations.md` section 11). |
| Using outside data and triggering outside actions | Designed. An author picks entries of the catalogue: operations, data sources, triggers. A platform admin writes connections in the configuration. | The catalogue and connections (`integrations.md` section 8), call waits, trigger bindings, the `events` block. |
| Trying a workflow before publishing | Designed. A draft runs in the browser on the same pure code (`decide`, `evolve`, checks, compile) with an in-memory host: calls answer from the catalogue's samples, sends go to a test outbox, nothing is stored on the server. | `decide` and `evolve` stay pure. |
| Problems in plain language | Designed. The engine reports a problem as a code, a location in the authored workflow and parameters, never a location in the compiled definition; the editor words it. | The origin map (spec section 7). |
| Who may author | Open. Assumed: any signed-in user may create a workflow and becomes its first author; its authors edit, publish and change its settings; platform admins may do the same. | `definitions.published_by`; `workflow_settings.authors`. |

## 2. Needs the existing codebase

Answered by: reading the application the engine is built into.

- **IDs.** The type of a request ID (uuid or bigint; decided: it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`); whether `by` is stored as two columns or as jsonb. Decided: a user or group ID is the directory's immutable object ID, never an email or a name (`kernel/kernel-spec.md`, section 2, Values). The pattern of a directory object ID.
- **Readable request numbers.** Their display format, and the number they start above.
- **Database conventions.** Migration tool naming, schema name, timestamp conventions.
- **User directory.** Which API gives group membership and group members, and its limits and failure modes. (The reference form is decided: `{type, id}` with the immutable object ID.)
- **Email and Slack service.** Its interface, how recipients are addressed, and how it sends the platform's words.
- **Sign-in.** How the signed-in user reaches the engine API, and how the platform-admin entitlement is checked.
- **Jira.** The connection in use, and for the full workflow the project, epic and field mapping.
- **Background jobs.** How the job workers are hosted beside a Next.js application.
- **Mounting.** Where the engine API (`{base}`) and the hook for outside systems (`{hooks}`) are mounted, and how the hook is reachable over TLS. The deployment URI that names the platform in outbound events.
- **Configuration and secrets.** Where the deployment's configuration lives (connections, outbound addresses) and which secret store supplies the values it names.
- **Logs.** Where the server's structured log lines go and who watches them.
- **Helpdesk.** The real helpdesk's signing scheme, and whether it carries a signed timestamp.
- **Lists.** Which lists, filters and sorts the pages need. A filter on a data field is covered by the index on `requests.data`; a sort on one needs a generated column.

## 3. Engine choices

Answered by: the build team. Each open one has a default a planner may assume.

Answered:

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Which CEL library for JavaScript | `@marcbachmann/cel-js`, pinned to an exact version (8.0.0), behind an engine-owned wrapper that replaces its regular expressions, timestamp parsing and date reading. The wrapper defines the expression profile `cel-1`. |
| The concrete JSON format of a published definition | Designed as format 1, field for field as spec sections 2 and 7 and `integrations.md` sections 9.1, 11.2, 11.5, 12.1 and 13.3 name them. Kept outside this package with the authoring design. A long-lived contract once a request runs on it. |
| The exact JSON field names of each event payload | Designed, every event type at `v: 1`, as spec section 5 and `integrations.md` section 7.3 name them. |
| Refusal reasons beyond the spec's | `kernel/data-model.md` `attempts_log` lists every reason. Beyond spec sections 2 and 4: `mapping-error` for a start by a connection. A retry of a request that is not stuck is answered `not-stuck`, and of one stuck with `nothing-fits` or `error`, `not-retryable` (`integrations.md` section 10.4). |
| Connector timeouts, retry spacing and a retry limit | A timeout per catalogue entry (default 30 s, 10 s for a data source); retries after 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, then every 15 min, without limit; each try past the entry's expected time writes a log line (`integrations.md` section 10.2). |
| The job queue | The engine's own `jobs` table, taken by polling workers with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (`kernel/data-model.md`). |
| Development stack | Node LTS, TypeScript, npm, Vitest. Postgres; tests and the dev host run on PGlite, and the cases that test concurrency on real Postgres. The API is plain functions with thin web-standard request handlers over them. All cheap to change. |

Still open:

| Question | Default to assume |
|---|---|
| How the publish check types the request's data document of a hand-written definition. No author declares a data schema. | Infer it from the type of every Set expression (start data reaches the document only through Sets on the first stage's transitions). |
| A pattern for the workflow ID. It is in every `RequestStarted` and has none. | `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$`, the demo's spelling. |
| How long the logs are kept. Nothing is deleted in the first build. | Keep everything until volume says otherwise. |

## 4. Product questions that do not block the first build

Answered by: the product owner.

- **The no-approval path in the demo.** Such a request could go straight to development. The demo definition still assigns an eng lead and creates a ticket first. Confirm.
- **Rejecting.** Is a reason required, and is it shown to the requester? The definitions assume yes.
- **The event vocabulary is provisional** until a second workflow has been built on it.
- **Personal data.** Which values are personal, and the retention policy. Erasure is not designed in the first build.

## 5. Known limits

Answered by: the engine owner, unless an item says otherwise.

1. **Outside the package.** The integrated sample workflow and its cases, and the JSON formats of definitions and events, are kept with the authoring design. Decide whether the package carries copies, so that it alone is enough to plan the build.
2. **Replay protection depends on the outside system.** Verifying an inbound request is the connector's job. A real system whose scheme has no signed timestamp can have an old event that never started a request replayed into a newer binding; only the dedupe stops a replay of one that started.
3. **Nobody to ask for a group is a snapshot.** The match reads the recorded membership read. A person added to the group after the read can act while the request shows "nobody to ask". A retry of a group task ends its turn not stuck, so `request.unstuck@1` is published, then `request.stuck@1` if the new read again finds nobody.
4. **Retry** still starts a second outside job where a stage holds an await under "again" and something else that is stuck with `action-failed` or `nobody-to-ask`.
5. **A paused binding drops events.** The outside system must send them again after the resume.
6. **A slow call tells nobody.** It is not stuck, and its overdue state is a log line only.
7. **Who may author** (section 1). The product owner.
===\nengine/spec/workflows/change-request-demo/definition.md\n===
# Change request (demo): workflow definition

The workflow the first build must run. It is a simplified Change Management: one approval, a ticket, a release task, a rejection branch and a no-approval branch. It is written by hand in the kernel's terms (`kernel/kernel-spec.md`). Its test cases are in `test-cases.yaml`, next to this file.

## Behaviour

The requester starts a request by submitting the form. A request names one primary domain. It only moves forward.

| Primary domain | Approval | Eng lead |
|---|---|---|
| Needs approval | The domain's approvers are asked. One approves or rejects. A rejection ends the request as rejected. | Picked by the approver, who must pick one to approve. |
| Needs no approval | None. | The first member of the domain's eng-lead group, read from the directory. |

Then a Jira ticket is created, and the eng lead marks the request released.

## Definition

```
start: Request.form
constants: approverGroup, engLeadGroup, noApprovalDomains, jiraProject
statuses:
  - { id: pendingApproval, label: "Pending approval",   color: amber  }
  - { id: assigningLead,   label: "Assigning eng lead", color: blue   }
  - { id: creatingTicket,  label: "Creating ticket",    color: blue   }
  - { id: inDevelopment,   label: "In development",     color: purple }
  - { id: released,        label: "Released",           color: green  }
  - { id: rejected,        label: "Rejected",           color: red    }
root:
  initial: Request
  stages:
    Request:                                # the start stage; status null; passed through in the start turn
      waits:
        form: person { assignees: [request.by],
                       outcomes: [ { id: submit, schema: changeForm } ] }
      transitions:
        t_skip:    when waits.form.outcome == 'submit'
                        && waits.form.data.primaryDomain in noApprovalDomains
                   set [ { path: [form], expr: waits.form.data } ]                  ->  AssignLead
        t_approve: when waits.form.outcome == 'submit'
                   set [ { path: [form], expr: waits.form.data } ]                  ->  Pending

    Pending:        status: pendingApproval
      waits:
        primary.members:  call { connection: directory, op: membersOf@1, effect: read, onFailure: outcome,
                                 args: { groups: [approverGroup[data.form.primaryDomain]] } }
        primary.decision: person { assignees: [approverGroup[data.form.primaryDomain]],
                                   may: actor != request.by,
                                   outcomes: [ { id: approve, schema: { engLead: user, required } },
                                               { id: reject,  schema: { reason: string, required } } ] }
      transitions:
        t_reject: when waits.primary.decision.outcome == 'reject'                   ->  Rejected
        t_accept: when waits.primary.decision.outcome == 'approve'
                  set [ { path: [engLead], expr: waits.primary.decision.data.engLead } ]  ->  CreateTicket

    AssignLead:     status: assigningLead
      waits:
        leads: call { connection: directory, op: membersOf@1, effect: read,
                      args: { groups: [engLeadGroup[data.form.primaryDomain]] } }
      transitions:
        t_lead: when waits.leads.outcome == 'ok'
                set [ { path: [engLead], expr: waits.leads.data.groups[0].members[0] } ]  ->  CreateTicket

    CreateTicket:   status: creatingTicket
      waits:
        ticket: call { connection: jira, op: createIssue@1, effect: write,
                       idempotencyKey: 'ticket.' + request.id,
                       args: { project:     jiraProject[data.form.primaryDomain],
                               summary:     data.form.title,
                               assignee:    data.engLead,
                               description: 'Title: ' + data.form.title + '\nPrimary domain: ' + data.form.primaryDomain } }
      transitions:
        t_ticket: when waits.ticket.outcome == 'ok'
                  set [ { path: [ticket], expr: waits.ticket.data.key } ]           ->  InDevelopment

    InDevelopment:  status: inDevelopment
      waits:
        release.task: person { assignees: [data.engLead], outcomes: [ { id: released, schema: {} } ] }
      transitions:
        t_release: when waits.release.task.outcome == 'released'                    ->  Released

    Released: final   status: released
    Rejected: final   status: rejected

nobodyToAsk:
  - { id: Request.form__nobody,              wait: Request.form,              members: null,                    excludeRequester: false }
  - { id: Pending.primary.decision__nobody,  wait: Pending.primary.decision,  members: Pending.primary.members,  excludeRequester: true  }
  - { id: InDevelopment.release.task__nobody, wait: InDevelopment.release.task, members: null,                  excludeRequester: false }
```

The form (`changeForm`) has two required fields: `title` (text) and `primaryDomain` (text). The schema does not list the allowed domains; the page offers them. A domain with no entry in the constants is an expression error when the request starts (case D9).

People and groups are references `{type, id}` throughout: `approverGroup` and `engLeadGroup` map a domain to a group reference, `membersOf@1` takes a list of group references and returns `{groups: [{id: <group reference>, members: [<user reference>, ...]}]}`, the approver's `engLead` is a user reference, and `engLead` is passed to Jira's `assignee` as one. The Jira connector maps the reference to a Jira account.

Stages, waits and transitions are listed in declared order; publish writes each as an array in that order. `primary.members`, `primary.decision` and `release.task` are local IDs like any other; the dot is nested field access in CEL.

Both Request transitions test the outcome rather than using `otherwise`, so their Sets' reads of `waits.form.data` are guarded (spec section 6). The first that is true fires, so the behaviour is that of `otherwise`.

## Published elements

| Stage | Waits, in declared order | Defaults written at publish |
|---|---|---|
| Request | `form` (the start wait) | `role: obligation`, `may: true`, `submit` checks `[]` |
| Pending | `primary.members` (read call), `primary.decision` | members: `keyScope: activation`; decision: `role: obligation`, checks `[]` on both outcomes |
| AssignLead | `leads` (read call) | `onFailure: fault`, `keyScope: activation` |
| CreateTicket | `ticket` (write call) | `onFailure: fault` |
| InDevelopment | `release.task` | `role: obligation`, `may: true`, `released` checks `[]` |

Publish adds the default notification rules `n_task` and `n_stopped` (`integrations.md`).

## Notes

- **Request** is never seen: the start turn completes `form` with the requester's input and a Request transition fires in the same turn. Its assignee is the requester, but the start turn does not check it. Its status is null.
- **No eligible approver never blocks submission.** The request waits in Pending and is stuck with `nobody-to-ask`, and `n_stopped` alerts the workflow admins. A failed membership read (`onFailure: outcome`) does not fault the request; it contributes nobody from its groups, and the approval asks only the group, so nobody can answer. Either way the approval stays open, and a member who can approve still can; Retry reads the group again. No transition reads `primary.members`.
- **The requester cannot approve their own request.** Membership is checked when the person acts.
- **AssignLead and CreateTicket last as long as their calls.** Both calls have `onFailure: fault`: a failed result faults the request. An empty eng-lead group is an expression error (`members[0]`) and also faults it. A failed call is stuck with `action-failed`, and an admin may retry (clear the fault and re-enter the stage) or close the request; an expression error is stuck with `error`, and only Close is offered.
- **The ticket's idempotency key is the same on every entry of CreateTicket** (`ticket.<request ID>`). The Jira connector is a plain create with no duplicate check. A retry after a clear failure is safe. If Jira created the ticket but the result was lost, a retry creates a second ticket; that is accepted (see `integrations.md`).
- **The Jira arguments are placeholders.** `jiraProject` is a constant keyed by primary domain. The description is an argument like any other: text the definition builds from the form's values.
- **Every value a stage reads is set on every route into it:** `engLead` by `t_accept` or `t_lead`, `ticket` by `t_ticket`.

## What it leaves out

Compared with the existing Change Management: other domains and the path where every domain must approve; optional decisions; the ticket's product-owner and approved-by fields; the Jira epic; admin skips, jumps to another stage and data edits.

## Open

- A no-approval request could go straight to development. This definition still assigns an eng lead and creates a ticket on that path, because the release task needs an assignee and In development reads the ticket. Proposed, not confirmed by the product owner.
- The approver picks the eng lead "from a list that comes from the directory". The engine validates that the value is a user. Restricting it to a directory-fed list of choices is a question whose choices come from the directory's `groupMembers@1` data source, looked up again when the approver acts (`integrations.md`, section 11). This hand-written definition does not use one.
===\nengine/spec/workflows/change-request-demo/test-cases.yaml\n===
# Test cases for the change request demo, against kernel/kernel-spec.md v2.20.
#
# These are the cases the first build must pass. They are data, not code. Each case is: a list of
# inputs, and for each input either the exact events the engine must append (in order) or a
# refusal. No harness exists yet and the cases have never been run.
#
# Conventions
# - The definition under test is definition.md, next to this file.
# - Three local element IDs are dotted: primary.decision, primary.members, release.task.
# - Activation IDs are symbolic: a1 is the root, a2 is Request, a3 the next stage entered, and so on.
# - A wait is written <stage>.<element>@<activation>. seq is 1 everywhere and omitted.
# - Envelope fields (requestId, seq, at, turn, v, engineBuild) are not listed. `turn` of every
#   event in a block is the seq of that block's first event.
# - Payload fields not listed are not asserted.
# - People and group IDs in the fixtures (rita, grp-a) stand for immutable directory object IDs.
# - `by: rita` is short for { type: user, id: rita }; `by: "connection:directory"` for
#   { type: connection, id: directory }. Wherever a person or group appears (assignees, constants,
#   call arguments and results, answers, patches, state), "user:lee" and "group:grp-a" are short for
#   { type: user, id: lee } and { type: group, id: grp-a }. A person or group is never a bare ID.
# - `evidence.memberOf` lists group IDs, as recorded.
# - `stuck` in finalState is the request's stuck state, { reason, ... } or null.
# - `faulted` in finalState is false (no fault) or `error` (an error fault).
# - A start input is { by, input: { outcome, data } }: the requester acting on the start wait,
#   Request.form.
# - A patch is written in full: an ordered list of { op, path, value }, path a list of segments.
# - `status` on StageEntered is { id, label }, or null.
# - `notify` lists the notification rules the notifier must match for that turn. It is checked
#   against the notifier, not the engine: notifications are not history events.
# - In an idempotency key, `{requestId}` stands for the request's ID.
# - Admin turns use the two actions, retry and close. `{ retry: {} }` is short for { type: retry },
#   and likewise for close.
# - `finalState` is a subset match on the request's state; `absent` means the path is not present.

===\nfrontend/README.md\n===
# frontend

The editor (authors build workflows) and the pages people use to start and answer requests. Design decisions F1-F10: `../docs/08-frontend-design.md`. Words: `../../workflow/spec/editor-model.md` (the mockups folder beside this repo).

Vite + React 19 + TypeScript (strict), zustand + immer, React Router (hash routes), Radix primitives, @xyflow/react + dagre. Plain CSS: tokens as CSS variables in `src/ui/tokens.css`, one CSS module per component.

## Install, run, test

Needs Node 24 or later on `PATH`. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1` before installing: no browser is downloaded, the system Chrome is used.

```
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173 (strict port)
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint, including the folder rules below
npm run test         # vitest: unit and rendered tests
npm run build        # into dist/; npm run preview serves it on 5173
npm run e2e          # Playwright in the system Chrome; starts the dev server itself if none is running
```

Set `PW_CHANNEL=msedge` to use Edge instead of Chrome (e2e and shoot).

## Two modes: the stand-in, or the engine's real server

The server side of the services (drafts, publish, requests, tasks, the directory, who is signed in) runs in one of two ways, chosen once at start-up by `VITE_ENGINE_URL` (`src/services/index.ts`). The engine's core runs in the browser either way.

- **Stand-in (default).** Without the variable: the in-browser stand-in, kept in localStorage. `npm run dev` on 5173, as above.
- **HTTP.** With the variable set to the engine's address, every server call goes to the engine over HTTP (`src/services/http`). Start the engine's development host first, then a second dev server on another port:

```
# engine/ (the engine owner's folder; this only runs it)
npm run dev-host -- --seed                  # http://127.0.0.1:8787, three sample workflows published, no requests

# frontend/
$env:VITE_ENGINE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8787"; npx vite --port 5183
```

In HTTP mode the development footer says "Engine at <address>" beside the core version (and warns if the engine runs another core), "Reset sample data" is replaced by "restart the engine to start from nothing", and "Add sample requests" starts a few requests as the sample people. The host signs one person in for every tab ("Signed in as" switches it for all of them).

The smoke run in the real UI against the real engine: `$env:ENGINE_APP_URL = "http://localhost:5183"; npx playwright test tests/e2e/engine-http.spec.ts` (skipped without `ENGINE_APP_URL`). The HTTP services' unit tests replay answers recorded from the development host (`src/services/http/__fixtures__`); record them again with `node tools/record-engine-fixtures.mjs` against a freshly started `--seed` host.

## Screenshots

With `npm run dev` (or preview) running:

```
npm run shoot -- /w/change-request editor            # shots/editor.png at 1440x900
npm run shoot -- /ui-reference ui --full             # whole page
npm run shoot -- /tasks tasks --width 1280 --height 800
```

`shots/` is git-ignored.

## Routes

| Route | Screen | From |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | Workflows | `features/workflows` |
| `/w/:workflowId` | Editor, Diagram tab | `features/diagram` + `features/panel` |
| `/w/:workflowId/words` | In words | `features/inwords` |
| `/w/:workflowId/values` | Values | `features/values` |
| `/w/:workflowId/form/:stageId/:taskId` | Form editor | `features/forms` |
| `/w/:workflowId/try` | Try it | `features/tryit` |
| `/connections` | Connections | `features/connections` |
| `/start/:workflowId`, `/tasks`, `/requests`, `/requests/:requestId` | Pages people use | `features/requests` |
| `/ui-reference` | Every primitive | `src/app` |

Editor routes share the editor top bar (`src/app/EditorLayout.tsx`); the others share the app frame (`src/app/AppLayout.tsx`).

## Folder rules (enforced by `npm run lint`)

```
src/contract   the contract, from ../contract (below)   imports nothing
src/words      every label a person reads (F5)          imports nothing
src/services   the async interface to the engine (F4)   contract, @workflow/core (the only importer)
src/model      the document store and derivations       contract, services, words
src/ui         tokens and primitives (F8)               words
src/features/* one folder per feature                   contract, services, model, words, ui, its own folder
src/app        routes and the two frames                everything
```

A feature never imports another feature: features share only through `model`, `words` and `ui`. Import across folders with the `@/` alias (`@/ui`, `@/words`); import inside your own folder with `./`.

## The engine's core

The engine's core, `@workflow/core` (`../engine/packages/core`), is linked by `file:` and consumed as TypeScript source: `src/services/README.md`, "How core is linked". Only `src/services` imports it; everything else reaches it through `@/services`. Never write, build or install inside `../engine`.

## The contract

The authored workflow format, the catalogue types and the fixtures live in the repo's `contract/` folder and are imported, not copied. The alias `@contract` points there (Vite, Vitest and `tsconfig.json`; the dev server is allowed to read it). Only `src/contract` imports `@contract/...`; everything else imports `@/contract` (the types and constants) or `@/contract/fixtures` (the four sample workflows and their Settings records, keyed `change-request`, `blank`, `several-at-once`, `integrated-sample`). The lint rule counts `@contract/...` as `src/contract`.

## Adding a screen without touching shared files

1. Work only in `src/features/<yours>/` and `src/words/<yours>.ts` (plus tests).
2. Replace the placeholder component your `index.tsx` exports (its README names it). Keep the export's name: the route table in `src/app/routes.tsx` already points at it.
3. Put your labels in `src/words/<yours>.ts`, keys starting with `<yours>.`; use them with `t('<yours>.key', { name })`. That includes the words of any top-bar slot you own. Shared vocabulary (`word.*`, `version.*`, `glossary.*`, the `top.*` words `src/app` draws) is in `core.ts`: ask before changing it.
4. Build from `@/ui` primitives and the tokens; style with a CSS module in your folder. Check `/ui-reference` first.
5. Need something from another feature? Ask for it to move into `model` (data) or `ui` (a primitive), never import it. To show another feature's part on your screen, use its model slot: `<Slot name="StageActions" stageId={id} place="stageStarts" />` from `@/model` (see `src/model/slots.ts`).

The slots (all props with doc comments in `src/model/slots.ts`): `StageActions` (`features/actions`); `WhenBuilder`, `FormulaEditor` (`features/conditions`); `ValueField`, `ValueChip`, `MessageField`, `ListDialog` (`features/values`); `KindChooser`, `ReadOnlyDiagram` (`features/diagram`); `FormView` (`features/forms`); `AlsoStartsFrom` (`features/connections`). `FormView` is the one form renderer (F6): the form editor's preview, Try it and the live start and task pages all show a task's form with it, passing the document (`doc`), the task, the answers and values, and on live pages the engine's `buttonStates` and `refusals`; it calls `core.formState` itself. `ReadOnlyDiagram` is the diagram without editing (Try it, the request page), taking `doc` (default: the open draft) and where the request is, has been and is stuck. `AlsoStartsFrom` is "+ Also start it from another system" on the start stage's panel. Each is filled by its owner's real component (`src/app/slots.ts`). The editing slots are controlled: you pass the part of the document as `value` and store what `onChange` gives with your own named command, e.g. `<Slot name="ValueField" at={{ item: task.id, part: 'whoIsAsked' }} label={t('word.whoIsAsked')} value={task.whoIsAsked} onChange={(next) => run(...)} />`. Replace the component with that name in your folder and it appears wherever the slot is used.

The open workflow (its draft in the editor store, Settings, what you may do, the catalogue, versions, To do and Worth knowing, facts, values in scope, the describe `env`, autosave, publish, "Show me") is the editor session in `src/model/session`, exported from `@/model`; `src/model/session/README.md` lists every name with an example. `EditorLayout` opens and closes it, so inside the editor just use the hooks (`useDoc()`, `useSettings()`, `useFindingsFor(id, { deep: true })`, `useValuesInScope(at)`, `useDescribeEnv()` ...). Never call `authoring.saveDraft` or `core.check` for the open workflow yourself. The demo workflows of the stand-in are `change-request` (version 3 live), `several-at-once` and `integrated-sample` (`/w/change-request`); "Reset sample data" in the app frame's footer (development only) starts them again from the seed.

The editor's top bar is made of slots too: `WorkflowName` and `SaveStatus` (`features/workflows`), `VersionState`, `TodoButton`, `PublishButton` (`features/todo`), `SettingsButton` (`features/panel`), `TryItButton` (`features/tryit`).
6. Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`; screenshot with `npm run shoot` and compare with the mockups in `../../workflow/mockups/shots/`.

A new route, a new top-bar slot or a new model slot is the one change that needs `src/app` (and `src/model/slots.ts`); ask the frontend owner.
===\nfrontend/eslint.config.js\n===
import js from '@eslint/js';
import globals from 'globals';
import reactHooks from 'eslint-plugin-react-hooks';
import tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const src = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), 'src');

/** Which part of src a file belongs to: "ui", "model", "features/diagram", "app" ... or null outside src. */
function layerOf(file) {
  const rel = path.relative(src, file).split(path.sep);
  if (rel[0] === '..' || path.isAbsolute(rel.join('/'))) return null;
  if (rel[0] === 'features') return rel.length > 2 ? `features/${rel[1]}` : 'features';
  return rel.length > 1 ? rel[0] : null;
}

/** What each part may import from (besides itself and third-party packages). */
const allowed = {
  contract: [],
  words: [],
  services: ['contract'],
  model: ['contract', 'services', 'words'],
  ui: ['words'],
  feature: ['contract', 'services', 'model', 'words', 'ui'],
  app: ['contract', 'services', 'model', 'words', 'ui', 'features/*'],
};

/**
 * The folder rules from docs/08-frontend-design.md: a feature imports model, services, words, ui,
 * contract and its own folder, never another feature; ui imports nothing from features, model or services.
 */
const boundaries = {
  meta: { type: 'problem', schema: [] },
  create(context) {
    const from = layerOf(context.filename);
    if (!from) return {};
    const check = (node) => {
      const spec = node.source?.value;
      if (typeof spec !== 'string') return;
      // The engine's core: only src/services imports it, and only its root entry (never the kernel
      // entry, never a deep path). Everything else reaches it through the services interface.
      if (spec === '@workflow/core' || spec.startsWith('@workflow/core/')) {
        if (spec !== '@workflow/core') {
          context.report({ node: node.source, message: `Import only '@workflow/core' (the root entry), never '${spec}'.` });
        } else if (from !== 'services') {
          context.report({ node: node.source, message: `Only src/services may import '@workflow/core'; ${from} goes through '@/services'.` });
        }
        return;
      }
      let target;
      if (spec.startsWith('@/')) target = path.join(src, spec.slice(2));
      else if (spec.startsWith('@contract/')) target = path.join(src, 'contract'); // the repo's contract/ counts as src/contract
      else if (spec.startsWith('.')) target = path.resolve(path.dirname(context.filename), spec);
      else return; // a package
      const to = layerOf(target.endsWith(path.sep) ? target : `${target}${path.sep}x`) ?? layerOf(target);
      if (!to || to === from) return;
      const rules = from.startsWith('features/') ? allowed.feature : allowed[from] ?? [];
      const ok = rules.some((r) => r === to || (r === 'features/*' && to.startsWith('features/')));
      if (!ok) {
        context.report({
          node: node.source,
          message:
            `${from} may not import from ${to}. Allowed: ${rules.join(', ') || 'nothing in src'}.` +
            (from.startsWith('features/') ? ' Features share only through model, words or ui.' : ''),
        });
      }
    };
    return { ImportDeclaration: check, ExportNamedDeclaration: check, ExportAllDeclaration: check, ImportExpression: check };
  },
};

export default tseslint.config(
  { ignores: ['dist', 'node_modules', 'shots', 'test-results', 'playwright-report'] },
  {
    files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
    extends: [js.configs.recommended, ...tseslint.configs.recommended],
    languageOptions: { ecmaVersion: 2022, globals: { ...globals.browser } },
    plugins: { 'react-hooks': reactHooks, local: { rules: { boundaries } } },
    rules: {
      ...reactHooks.configs.recommended.rules,
      'local/boundaries': 'error',
      // Unused names are tsc's job (noUnusedLocals / noUnusedParameters in tsconfig.json; core compiles
      // with them too): off here so nothing is reported twice. A parameter starting with `_` may stay unused.
      '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars': 'off',
    },
  },
  {
    files: ['**/*.{js,mjs}', '*.config.ts'],
    languageOptions: { globals: { ...globals.node } },
    extends: [js.configs.recommended],
  },
);

import { useState } from 'react';
import { NavLink, Outlet } from 'react-router-dom';
import { t, type WordKey } from '@/words';
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/ui';
import { DevPerson } from './DevPerson';
import { DevReset } from './DevReset';
import s from './layout.module.css';

const nav: readonly { to: string; label: WordKey; icon: IconName; end?: boolean }[] = [
  { to: '/', label: 'word.workflows', icon: 'workflow', end: true },
  { to: '/tasks', label: 'word.myTasks', icon: 'task' },
  { to: '/requests', label: 'word.requests', icon: 'history' },
  { to: '/connections', label: 'word.connections', icon: 'connected' },
];

/**
 * The frame of the pages outside the editor: the people who start and answer requests, and authors'
 * lists. On the development host it also says who is signed in and lets the tester switch person;
 * the page below is then shown again from the start (mounted afresh, so it asks the services again).
 */
export function AppLayout() {
  const [signIns, setSignIns] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className={s.appFrame}>
      <header className={s.appTop}>
        {/* The product's mark, not a link: "Workflows" in the menu beside it already goes there, and
            two links of one name side by side would be two Tab stops that say the same. */}
        <span className={s.brand} aria-hidden="true">
          <span className={s.brandMark}>
            <Icon name="workflow" />
          </span>
          {t('nav.brand')}
        </span>
        <nav aria-label={t('nav.label')} className={s.nav}>
          {nav.map((item) => (
            <NavLink key={item.to} to={item.to} end={item.end} className={s.navLink}>
              <Icon name={item.icon} />
              {t(item.label)}
            </NavLink>
          ))}
        </nav>
        {import.meta.env.DEV && <DevPerson onChanged={() => setSignIns((n) => n + 1)} />}
      </header>
      <main className={s.appMain}>
        <Outlet key={signIns} />
      </main>
      {import.meta.env.DEV && (
        <footer className={s.appFoot}>
          <DevReset onChanged={() => setSignIns((n) => n + 1)} />
        </footer>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/app/DevPerson.tsx\n===
import { useEffect, useId, useState } from 'react';
import { useServices, type Person } from '@/services';
import { t } from '@/words';
import { Icon, Select } from '@/ui';
import s from './layout.module.css';

/**
 * "Signed in as", for the development host only (rendered under import.meta.env.DEV, and only when
 * the session offers people to switch to): who is signed in (`session.whoAmI`), and a list of the
 * people the development host offers (`session.people`). Choosing someone signs in as them
 * (`session.signInAs`) and calls `onChanged`, so the frame shows its page again as that person:
 * the request pages can be tried as the requester, an approver and the person who looks after
 * stuck requests. Marked "For development only" in words, not by colour alone.
 */
export function DevPerson({ onChanged }: { onChanged: (person: Person) => void }) {
  const services = useServices();
  const [me, setMe] = useState<Person | null>(null);
  const [people, setPeople] = useState<Person[]>([]);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(false);
  const id = useId();

  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    void Promise.all([services.session.whoAmI().catch(() => null), services.session.people().catch(() => [])]).then(([who, all]) => {
      if (!live) return;
      setMe(who);
      setPeople(all);
    });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, [services]);

  if (!me || people.length === 0) return null;

  const choose = async (personId: string) => {
    const person = people.find((p) => p.ref.id === personId);
    if (!person || busy) return;
    setBusy(true);
    setFailed(false);
    const result = await services.session.signInAs(person.ref).catch(() => null);
    setBusy(false);
    if (result?.ok) {
      setMe(result.value);
      onChanged(result.value);
    } else {
      setFailed(true);
    }
  };

  // The person signed in is always in the list, even if the development host does not offer them.
  const options = (people.some((p) => p.ref.id === me.ref.id) ? people : [me, ...people]).map((p) => ({ value: p.ref.id, label: p.label }));

  return (
    <div className={s.devPerson} role="group" aria-labelledby={`${id}-dev`}>
      <span id={`${id}-dev`} className={s.devLabel}>
        {t('top.dev.label')}
      </span>
      <label htmlFor={id} className={s.devPersonLabel}>
        <Icon name="person" size={14} />
        {t('top.dev.signedInAs')}
      </label>
      <Select
        id={id}
        className={s.devPersonSelect}
        value={me.ref.id}
        options={options}
        aria-busy={busy || undefined}
        aria-describedby={failed ? `${id}-failed` : undefined}
        onChange={(e) => void choose(e.target.value)}
      />
      {failed && (
        <span id={`${id}-failed`} role="alert" className={s.devPersonFailed}>
          <Icon name="error" size={14} />
          {t('top.dev.switchFailed')}
        </span>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/app/DevReset.tsx\n===
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { coreVersion, useServices, type SampleRequestKind, type SampleRequestsReport } from '@/services';
import { t, type WordKey } from '@/words';
import { Button, Dialog, DialogClose } from '@/ui';
import s from './layout.module.css';

const SAMPLE_WORDS: Record<SampleRequestKind, WordKey> = {
  finished: 'top.dev.sample.finished',
  inDevelopment: 'top.dev.sample.inDevelopment',
  waitingForApproval: 'top.dev.sample.waitingForApproval',
  nobodyToAsk: 'top.dev.sample.nobodyToAsk',
  actionFailed: 'top.dev.sample.actionFailed',
  refusedStart: 'top.dev.sample.refusedStart',
};

/** What "Add sample requests" did, in words. */
export function sampleReportWords(report: SampleRequestsReport): string {
  const added = report.added.map((a) => (a.readableId ? t('top.dev.sample.number', { what: t(SAMPLE_WORDS[a.kind]), n: a.readableId }) : t(SAMPLE_WORDS[a.kind])));
  const leftOut = report.skipped.filter((x) => x.why === 'notOffered').map((x) => t(SAMPLE_WORDS[x.kind]));
  const failed = report.skipped.filter((x) => x.why === 'failed').map((x) => t(SAMPLE_WORDS[x.kind]));
  return [
    added.length ? t('top.dev.samplesAdded', { list: added.join(', ') }) : t('top.dev.samplesNone'),
    leftOut.length ? t('top.dev.samplesLeftOut', { list: leftOut.join(', ') }) : '',
    failed.length ? t('top.dev.samplesFailed', { list: failed.join(', ') }) : '',
  ].filter(Boolean).join(' ');
}

/**
 * The development footer (rendered under import.meta.env.DEV), from what the services offer:
 * "Reset sample data" when the data can be reset from the page (the stand-in), else that the engine
 * starts from nothing when restarted; "Add sample requests" when the services offer it (the engine
 * over HTTP); and, quietly, the version of the engine's core the browser runs (`coreVersion`), the
 * engine's address when there is one, and a notice when the engine's core is another version.
 */
export function DevReset({ onChanged }: { onChanged?: () => void }) {
  const services = useServices();
  const dev = services.dev;
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false);
  const [said, setSaid] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [engineCore, setEngineCore] = useState<string | 'unreached' | null>(null);
  const address = dev?.engineAddress;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!address) return;
    let alive = true;
    services.authoring
      .getMeta()
      .then((m) => alive && setEngineCore(m.ok ? m.value.coreVersion : null))
      .catch(() => alive && setEngineCore('unreached'));
    return () => {
      alive = false;
    };
  }, [services, address]);

  const addSamples = async () => {
    if (!dev?.addSampleRequests || adding) return;
    setAdding(true);
    setSaid(t('top.dev.addingSamples'));
    try {
      setSaid(sampleReportWords(await dev.addSampleRequests()));
      onChanged?.();
    } catch {
      setSaid(t('top.dev.samplesError'));
    } finally {
      setAdding(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className={s.devFoot}>
      <div className={s.dev}>
        <span className={s.devLabel}>{t('top.dev.label')}</span>
        {dev?.addSampleRequests && (
          <Button variant="quiet" size="sm" icon="play" aria-describedby="dev-samples-said" disabledReason={adding ? t('top.dev.addingSamples') : undefined} onClick={() => void addSamples()}>
            {t('top.dev.addSamples')}
          </Button>
        )}
        {dev?.resetSampleData ? (
          <Dialog
            title={t('top.dev.reset')}
            description={t('top.dev.resetHint')}
            open={open}
            onOpenChange={setOpen}
            trigger={
              <Button variant="quiet" size="sm" icon="history">
                {t('top.dev.reset')}
              </Button>
            }
            footer={
              <>
                <DialogClose asChild>
                  <Button>{t('common.cancel')}</Button>
                </DialogClose>
                <Button
                  variant="danger"
                  onClick={() => {
                    dev.resetSampleData?.();
                    window.location.reload();
                  }}
                >
                  {t('top.dev.reset')}
                </Button>
              </>
            }
          />
        ) : (
          address && <span>{t('top.dev.resetRestart')}</span>
        )}
        {address && <span>{t('top.dev.engine', { address })}</span>}
        <span>{t('top.dev.coreVersion', { version: coreVersion })}</span>
      </div>
      {address && engineCore === 'unreached' && (
        <p role="alert" className={s.devNotice}>
          {t('top.dev.engineUnreached', { address })}
        </p>
      )}
      {address && engineCore && engineCore !== 'unreached' && engineCore !== coreVersion && (
        <p role="alert" className={s.devNotice}>
          {t('top.dev.engineCore', { engine: engineCore, page: coreVersion })}
        </p>
      )}
      <p id="dev-samples-said" role="status" className={s.devSaid}>
        {said}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/app/DiagramTab.tsx\n===
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type CSSProperties, type KeyboardEvent, type PointerEvent } from 'react';
import { DiagramView } from '@/features/diagram';
import { StagePanel } from '@/features/panel';
import { TODO_BAR_PLACE_ID } from '@/features/todo';
import { t } from '@/words';
import s from './layout.module.css';

export const PANEL_MIN = 400;
export const PANEL_MAX = 640;
export const PANEL_DEFAULT = 480;
export const PANEL_WIDTH_KEY = 'editor.panelWidth';
const STEP = 16;

const clamp = (n: number) => Math.min(PANEL_MAX, Math.max(PANEL_MIN, Math.round(n)));

function storedWidth(): number {
  try {
    const n = Number(localStorage.getItem(PANEL_WIDTH_KEY));
    return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? clamp(n) : PANEL_DEFAULT;
  } catch {
    return PANEL_DEFAULT;
  }
}

/**
 * The Diagram tab: the graph and the stage panel side by side. The panel's left edge is a
 * separator: drag it, or focus it and use the arrow keys (Home and End for the narrowest and
 * widest), to set the panel between 400 and 640px; the width is remembered in this browser.
 */
export function DiagramTab() {
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(storedWidth);
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false);
  const workspace = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(PANEL_WIDTH_KEY, String(width));
    } catch {
      // Storage unavailable: the width lasts for this page only.
    }
  }, [width]);

  const fromPointer = (clientX: number) => {
    const right = workspace.current?.getBoundingClientRect().right;
    if (right !== undefined) setWidth(clamp(right - clientX));
  };

  const onPointerDown = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (e.button !== 0) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
    e.currentTarget.focus();
    setDragging(true);
  };
  const onPointerMove = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (dragging) fromPointer(e.clientX);
  };
  const onPointerUp = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (!dragging) return;
    e.currentTarget.releasePointerCapture(e.pointerId);
    setDragging(false);
  };

  // The separator sits on the panel's left edge: moving it left (ArrowLeft) widens the panel.
  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const next =
      e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowUp' ? width + STEP
      : e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === 'ArrowDown' ? width - STEP
      : e.key === 'Home' ? PANEL_MIN
      : e.key === 'End' ? PANEL_MAX
      : null;
    if (next === null) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    setWidth(clamp(next));
  };

  return (
    <div ref={workspace} className={s.workspace} style={{ '--panel-w': `${width}px` } as CSSProperties}>
      <DiagramView />
      <div
        role="separator"
        tabIndex={0}
        aria-orientation="vertical"
        aria-label={t('top.panelResize')}
        aria-valuemin={PANEL_MIN}
        aria-valuemax={PANEL_MAX}
        aria-valuenow={width}
        className={s.resizer}
        data-dragging={dragging || undefined}
        onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
        onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
        onPointerUp={onPointerUp}
        onPointerCancel={onPointerUp}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      />
      {/* The To do "Show me" strip goes in the empty place above the panel (mockup 09-publish). */}
      <div className={s.panelColumn}>
        <div id={TODO_BAR_PLACE_ID} />
        <StagePanel />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/app/EditorLayout.test.tsx\n===
import { afterEach, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { act, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor, within } from '@testing-library/react';
import { createMemoryRouter, RouterProvider } from 'react-router-dom';
import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import type { StageId } from '@/contract';
import { getStage, indexDoc, resetSessionForTests, reveal, SlotsProvider, useEditor, useSession } from '@/model';
import { createStandinServices, ServicesProvider, type Services } from '@/services';
import { PANEL_WIDTH_KEY } from './DiagramTab';
import { routes } from './routes';
import { slots } from './slots';

function renderAt(path: string, services: Services = createStandinServices().services) {
  const router = createMemoryRouter(routes, { initialEntries: [path] });
  render(
    <StrictMode>
      <ServicesProvider services={services}>
        <SlotsProvider slots={slots}>
          <RouterProvider router={router} />
        </SlotsProvider>
      </ServicesProvider>
    </StrictMode>,
  );
  return { router, services };
}

// jsdom draws nothing, so it has no scrollIntoView; the screens that show a revealed item call it.
beforeAll(() => {
  if (!Element.prototype.scrollIntoView) Element.prototype.scrollIntoView = () => undefined;
});

afterEach(() => {
  resetSessionForTests();
  localStorage.removeItem(PANEL_WIDTH_KEY);
});

describe('the editor route', () => {
  it('opens the demo workflow and shows its name', async () => {
    renderAt('/w/change-request');
    expect(screen.getByText('Opening the workflow ...')).toBeInTheDocument();
    await waitFor(() => expect(useSession.getState().status).toBe('ready'));
    const name = useSession.getState().settings?.name ?? '';
    expect(name).toBe('Change request');
    await waitFor(() => expect(document.title).toBe(name));
    expect(screen.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Views of this workflow' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(useEditor.getState().doc?.stages.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('fits the top bar to its width, and the save state is never one of the things it gives up', async () => {
    renderAt('/w/change-request');
    await waitFor(() => expect(useSession.getState().status).toBe('ready'));
    const bar = screen.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Views of this workflow' }).closest('header')!;
    await waitFor(() => expect(bar.dataset.fit).toBeDefined());
    // Glossary keeps its word as its name even when only its icon shows.
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Glossary' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    // Nothing marks the save line as something the bar may hide (round 2 hid "All changes saved").
    const line = screen.getByText('All changes saved');
    expect(line.closest('[data-calm], [data-topbar-label], [data-topbar-shrink]')).toBeNull();
    act(() => void useEditor.getState().run('stage.rename', { stage: 'st_released' as StageId, name: 'Shipped' }));
    expect(screen.getByText('Not saved yet').closest('[data-calm], [data-topbar-label], [data-topbar-shrink]')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('does not undo or redo while a dialog is in front, so the dialog stays true of the document', async () => {
    renderAt('/w/change-request');
    await waitFor(() => expect(useSession.getState().status).toBe('ready'));
    const released = 'st_released' as StageId;
    const nameNow = () => getStage(useEditor.getState().doc!, released)?.name;
    act(() => void useEditor.getState().run('stage.rename', { stage: released, name: 'Shipped' }));

    // A key pressed on a button inside a dialog (the Publish dialog's "Publish version 4", say).
    const dialog = document.createElement('div');
    dialog.setAttribute('role', 'dialog');
    const inside = document.createElement('button');
    dialog.appendChild(inside);
    document.body.appendChild(dialog);
    fireEvent.keyDown(inside, { key: 'z', ctrlKey: true });
    expect(nameNow()).toBe('Shipped');

    // A modal dialog open anywhere: a key that reaches the page does nothing either.
    dialog.setAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
    fireEvent.keyDown(document.body, { key: 'z', ctrlKey: true });
    expect(nameNow()).toBe('Shipped');
    dialog.remove();

    fireEvent.keyDown(document.body, { key: 'z', ctrlKey: true });
    expect(nameNow()).not.toBe('Shipped');
    act(() => {
      const d = document.createElement('div');
      d.setAttribute('role', 'alertdialog');
      d.setAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
      document.body.appendChild(d);
    });
    fireEvent.keyDown(document.body, { key: 'y', ctrlKey: true });
    expect(nameNow()).not.toBe('Shipped');
    document.querySelector('[role="alertdialog"]')?.remove();
  });

  it('opens read only for someone who may not change the workflow, and says why', async () => {
    const { services } = createStandinServices();
    await services.session.signInAs({ type: 'user', id: 'dir-user-priya-raman' });
    renderAt('/w/change-request', services);
    await waitFor(() => expect(useSession.getState().status).toBe('ready'));
    expect(useSession.getState().may.edit).toBe(false);
    expect(await screen.findByText(/You can look at this workflow but not change it/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('Read only')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('button', { name: /^Undo/ })).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Not saved. Trying again.')).toBeNull();
    const released = 'st_released' as StageId;
    const before = getStage(useEditor.getState().doc!, released)?.name;
    act(() => void useEditor.getState().run('stage.rename', { stage: released, name: 'Not mine' }));
    expect(getStage(useEditor.getState().doc!, released)?.name).toBe(before);
    expect(useEditor.getState().saveState).toBe('saved');
  });

  it('says when the workflow does not exist, with a way back', async () => {
    renderAt('/w/no-such-workflow');
    expect(await screen.findByText('This workflow does not exist')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Go to Workflows' })).toHaveAttribute('href', '/');
  });

  it('undoes and redoes with the keyboard and the buttons, but not while typing', async () => {
    renderAt('/w/change-request');
    await waitFor(() => expect(useSession.getState().status).toBe('ready'));
    const released = 'st_released' as StageId;
    const nameNow = () => getStage(useEditor.getState().doc!, released)?.name;
    const before = nameNow();
    act(() => void useEditor.getState().run('stage.rename', { stage: released, name: 'Shipped' }));

    box.remove();

  });

  it('turns a reveal into navigation to the view that shows the item', async () => {

import { useEffect, useRef, type RefObject } from 'react';
import { Link, NavLink, Outlet, useLocation, useNavigate, useParams } from 'react-router-dom';
import {
  closeWorkflow, openWorkflow, revealPath, revealTarget, setSettingsOpener, useCanRedo, useCanUndo, useEditor, useMay, useRevealRequest,
  useSaveState, useSessionStatus, useSessionWorkflowId, useSettings, type CommandName,
} from '@/model';
import { useServices } from '@/services/context';
import { t, type WordKey } from '@/words';
import { Button, Callout, EmptyState, Icon, Tooltip, buttonClass, tabStyles } from '@/ui';
import { SettingsButton } from '@/features/panel';
import { TodoButton, PublishButton, VersionState } from '@/features/todo';
import { TryItButton } from '@/features/tryit';
import { SaveStatus, WorkflowName } from '@/features/workflows';
import { Glossary } from './Glossary';
import { useTopBarFit } from './topBarFit';
import s from './layout.module.css';

/**
 * The editor's frame: opens the workflow named in the route (and closes it on leaving), the top bar
 * from the mockups, then the active tab. For authors. This file draws only the back link, undo and
 * redo, the three tabs and the Glossary; everything else in the bar is a slot exported by the
 * feature that owns it. It also turns a "Show me" (reveal) into navigation.
 */
export function EditorLayout() {
  const { workflowId = '' } = useParams();
  const services = useServices();
  const status = useSessionStatus();
  const openId = useSessionWorkflowId();

  useEffect(() => {
    void openWorkflow(services, workflowId);
    return () => closeWorkflow();
  }, [services, workflowId]);

  const ready = status === 'ready' && openId === workflowId;
  // Someone who may not change the workflow sees it read only: the session refuses every edit.
  const mayEdit = useMay().edit;
  const readOnly = ready && !mayEdit;
  const unsaved = useSaveState() !== 'saved';
  const name = useSettings()?.name;
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!ready || !name) return;
    const before = document.title;
    document.title = name;
    return () => {
      document.title = before;
    };
  }, [ready, name]);
  useUndoKeys(ready && !readOnly);
  useRevealNavigation(workflowId, ready);
  const barRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  useTopBarFit(barRef, ready);
  const settingsRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useSettingsOpener(settingsRef, ready);

  const back = (
    <Tooltip content={t('top.back')}>
      <Link to="/" className={buttonClass('quiet', 'md', s.iconLink)} aria-label={t('top.back')}>
        <Icon name="arrow-left" />
      </Link>
    </Tooltip>
  );

  if (!ready) {
    const shown = openId === workflowId ? status : 'loading';
    return (
      <div className={s.frame}>
        <header className={s.editorTop}>{back}</header>
        <main className={s.editorMain}>
          <div className={s.state} role={shown === 'loading' ? 'status' : undefined}>
            {shown === 'notFound' ? (
              <EmptyState
                icon="search"
                title={t('top.notFound.title')}
                action={
                  <Link to="/" className={buttonClass('primary')}>
                    {t('common.backHome')}
                  </Link>
                }
              >
                {t('top.notFound.text')}
              </EmptyState>
            ) : shown === 'error' ? (
              <EmptyState
                icon="warning"
                title={t('top.error.title')}
                action={
                  <Button
                    variant="primary"
                    onClick={() => {
                      closeWorkflow();
                      void openWorkflow(services, workflowId);
                    }}
                  >
                    {t('top.error.retry')}
                  </Button>
                }
              >
                {t('top.error.text')}
              </EmptyState>
            ) : (
              <p className={s.loading}>{t('top.loading')}</p>
            )}
          </div>
        </main>
      </div>
    );
  }

  const base = `/w/${workflowId}`;
  const tabs = [
    { to: base, end: true, icon: 'workflow', label: t('top.tab.diagram') },
    { to: `${base}/words`, end: false, icon: 'book', label: t('top.tab.inWords') },
    { to: `${base}/values`, end: false, icon: 'grid', label: t('top.tab.values') },
  ] as const;

  return (
    <div className={readOnly ? `${s.frame} ${s.frameNoted}` : s.frame}>
      <header className={s.editorTop} ref={barRef}>
        <div className={s.left}>
          {back}
          <div className={s.nameSlot}>
            <WorkflowName />
          </div>
          <VersionState />
        </div>

        <div className={s.center}>
          <nav aria-label={t('top.tabs')} className={`${tabStyles.list} ${s.tabs}`}>
            {tabs.map((tab) => (
              <NavLink key={tab.to} to={tab.to} end={tab.end} className={tabStyles.tab}>
                <Icon name={tab.icon} />
                {tab.label}
              </NavLink>
            ))}
          </nav>
          <Glossary />
        </div>

        <div className={s.right}>
          {readOnly ? (
            // Nothing can be changed, so there is nothing to undo or save: the bar says "Read only" instead.
            <div className={s.saveSlot}>
              <span className={s.readOnlyTag}>
                <Icon name="lock" size={14} />
                {t('top.readOnly')}
              </span>
            </div>
          ) : (
            <>
              <UndoRedo />
              {/* The save state is always shown in words, whatever the width (see topBarFit.ts). */}
              <div className={s.saveSlot}>
                <SaveStatus />
              </div>
            </>
          )}
          <div className={s.settingsSlot} ref={settingsRef}>
            <SettingsButton />
          </div>
          <TodoButton />
          <TryItButton />
          <PublishButton />
        </div>
      </header>
      {readOnly && (
        <div className={s.readOnlyNote}>
          <Callout icon="lock">
            {t('top.readOnly.note')}
            {unsaved && ` ${t('top.readOnly.lost')}`}
          </Callout>
        </div>
      )}
      <main className={s.editorMain}>
        <Outlet />
      </main>
    </div>
  );
}

// ── "Settings" links ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Tells the session how a "Settings" link inside a sentence opens Settings (openSettings() from
 * '@/model'): by pressing the top bar's Settings button, a popover trigger. The popover then takes
 * the focus, and gives it back to that button when it closes.
 */
function useSettingsOpener(ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, active: boolean) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!active) return;
    return setSettingsOpener(() => {
      const button = ref.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button[aria-haspopup="dialog"]') ?? ref.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button');
      if (!button) return;
      button.scrollIntoView?.({ block: 'nearest' });
      if (button.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') button.focus();
      else button.click();
    });
  }, [ref, active]);
}

// ── Undo and redo ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const CHANGE_WORDS: Record<string, WordKey> = {
  stage: 'top.change.stage',
  arrow: 'top.change.arrow',
  task: 'top.change.task',
  button: 'top.change.button',
  page: 'top.change.form',
  question: 'top.change.form',
  choice: 'top.change.form',
  item: 'top.change.form',
  text: 'top.change.form',
  action: 'top.change.action',
  value: 'top.change.value',
  list: 'top.change.list',
  column: 'top.change.list',
  row: 'top.change.list',
  cell: 'top.change.list',
  sample: 'top.change.sample',
  startsWhen: 'top.change.startsWhen',
  status: 'top.change.status',
  told: 'top.change.told',
  diagram: 'top.change.diagram',
};

/** What a command changed, in words ("a change to a stage"), from the group its name starts with. */
function changeWords(name: CommandName | undefined): string {
  const group = name ? String(name).split('.')[0] ?? '' : '';
  return t(CHANGE_WORDS[group] ?? 'top.change.other');
}

function UndoRedo() {
  const canUndo = useCanUndo();
  const canRedo = useCanRedo();
  const undoName = useEditor((st) => st.past[st.past.length - 1]?.name);
  const redoName = useEditor((st) => st.future[0]?.name);
  const undoLabel = canUndo ? t('top.undoWhat', { what: changeWords(undoName) }) : t('top.undo');
  const redoLabel = canRedo ? t('top.redoWhat', { what: changeWords(redoName) }) : t('top.redo');
  return (
    <div className={s.undo}>
      <HistoryButton icon="undo" label={undoLabel} keys={t('top.undoKeys')} enabled={canUndo} onPress={() => useEditor.getState().undo()} />
      <HistoryButton icon="redo" label={redoLabel} keys={t('top.redoKeys')} enabled={canRedo} onPress={() => useEditor.getState().redo()} />
    </div>
  );
}

/** An undo or redo button: greyed but still focusable when there is nothing to undo, so its tooltip still explains it. */
function HistoryButton(props: { icon: 'undo' | 'redo'; label: string; keys: string; enabled: boolean; onPress: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Tooltip content={`${props.label} (${props.keys})`}>
      <button
        type="button"
        className={buttonClass('quiet', 'md', s.iconLink)}
        aria-label={props.label}
        aria-keyshortcuts={props.icon === 'undo' ? 'Control+Z' : 'Control+Shift+Z Control+Y'}
        aria-disabled={!props.enabled || undefined}
        onClick={() => props.enabled && props.onPress()}
      >
        <Icon name={props.icon} />
      </button>
    </Tooltip>
  );
}

/** True when the key goes to a text box, where the browser's own undo applies. */
function isTyping(target: EventTarget | null): boolean {
  if (!(target instanceof HTMLElement)) return false;
  if (target.isContentEditable) return true;
  if (target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement) return true;
  if (target instanceof HTMLInputElement) {
    return !['button', 'checkbox', 'radio', 'submit', 'reset', 'range', 'color', 'file', 'image'].includes(target.type);
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * True while a dialog or popover is in front of the editor: the key went to something inside one,
 * or a modal dialog is open anywhere. Undo then does nothing, so what a dialog says (the Publish
 * dialog's list of changes, the stage delete question) stays true of the document behind it.
 */
function dialogInFront(target: EventTarget | null): boolean {
  if (target instanceof Element && target.closest('[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"]')) return true;
  return document.querySelector('[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"], [role="alertdialog"][aria-modal="true"]') !== null;
}

/**
 * Ctrl+Z undoes; Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y redo (Cmd on a Mac), except while typing in a text box and
 * while a dialog is in front. Only while the workflow on screen is the one open in the session.
 */
function useUndoKeys(enabled: boolean) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!enabled) return;
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (!(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) || e.altKey || e.defaultPrevented) return;
      const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
      const undo = key === 'z' && !e.shiftKey;
      const redo = (key === 'z' && e.shiftKey) || (key === 'y' && !e.shiftKey);
      if (!undo && !redo) return;
      if (isTyping(e.target) || dialogInFront(e.target)) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      if (undo) useEditor.getState().undo();
      else useEditor.getState().redo();
    };
    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey);
  }, [enabled]);
}

// ── Show me ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** Turns each new reveal request into navigation to the view that shows the item. */
function useRevealNavigation(workflowId: string, ready: boolean) {
  const request = useRevealRequest();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const { pathname } = useLocation();
  const handled = useRef<number | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!ready || !request || handled.current === request.nonce) return;
    handled.current = request.nonce;
    const path = revealPath(workflowId, revealTarget(useEditor.getState().doc, request.location));
    if (decodeURIComponent(pathname) !== decodeURIComponent(path)) navigate(path);
  }, [ready, request, workflowId, navigate, pathname]);
}

/** fill="surface" -> fill="var(--surface)"; "none" stays. */
const withTokens = (svg: string) => svg.replace(/(fill|stroke)="([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)"/g, (m, attr: string, token: string) => (token === 'none' ? m : `${attr}="var(--${token})"`));

/**
 * A line of the Glossary, with "(change this in Settings)" drawn as a link that opens the
 * workflow's Settings (editor-model.md section 9), after the Glossary has closed.
 */
function Line({ text, onSettings }: { text: string; onSettings: () => void }) {
  const parts = settingsLinked(text);
  const linkable = canOpenSettings();
  return (
    <>
      {parts.map((part, i) =>
        typeof part === 'string' ? (
          part
        ) : isSettingsLink(part) && linkable ? (
          <button key={i} type="button" className={s.link} title={t('top.settingsLinkTitle')} onClick={onSettings}>
            {part.text}
          </button>
        ) : 'chip' in part ? (
          part.label
        ) : (
          part.text
        ),
      )}
    </>
  );
}

/** The Glossary button in the editor's top bar and its popover: the seven words, one line each. */
export function Glossary() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const toSettings = () => {
    setOpen(false);
    // Once the Glossary has closed (and given the focus back to its button), Settings opens and takes it.
    requestAnimationFrame(() => openSettings());
  };
  return (
    <Popover
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={setOpen}
      title={t('glossary.title')}
      sub={t('glossary.sub')}
      width={500}
      align="center"
      trigger={
        <Button variant="quiet" size="sm" icon="help" title={t('top.glossaryTitle')}>
          {/* The top bar never gives this word up (the frontend owner's ruling, fix round 2). */}
          <span data-topbar-label="">{t('top.glossary')}</span>
        </Button>
      }
      footer={
        <>
          <Icon name="info" size={14} />
          <span>{t('glossary.foot')}</span>
        </>
      }
    >
      <ul className={s.list}>
        {glossary.map((g) => (
          <li key={g.word} className={s.item}>
            <svg viewBox="0 0 64 40" className={s.pic} aria-hidden="true" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: withTokens(pics[g.pic]) }} />
            <div>
              <div className={s.word}>{t(g.word)}</div>
              <div className={s.line}>
                <Line text={t(g.line)} onSettings={toSettings} />
              </div>
              <div className={s.where}>
                <Icon name="eye" size={13} />
                {t(g.where)}
              </div>
            </div>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Popover>
  );
}

===\nfrontend/src/app/README.md\n===
# app

The route table and the two frames (docs/08-frontend-design.md: "routes and the development host").

- `main.tsx`: mounts `ServicesProvider` with the app's services (`src/services`), `SlotsProvider` with `slots.ts`, and the router. In development only it puts the editor store on the page as `window.__editor` (for end-to-end tests and the console).
- `public/favicon.ico` (beside `src`): the icon the browser asks for on every page, so no page load logs a 404.
- `routes.tsx`: hash routes; every screen is a component exported from a feature's `index.tsx`. Builders replace the component in their folder, not the route.
- `EditorLayout.tsx`: the editor's frame for authors. Opens the workflow named in the route with `openWorkflow` (and `closeWorkflow` on leaving), shows "Opening the workflow ...", "This workflow does not exist" (with a link back) or "could not be opened" (with Try again) until it is ready, and sets the page title to the workflow's name. The top bar draws the back link, Undo and Redo (with what they undo in their name and tooltip), the Diagram | In words | Values tabs and the Glossary; everything else is a slot exported by its feature: `WorkflowName` and `SaveStatus` (`features/workflows`), `VersionState`, `TodoButton` and `PublishButton` (`features/todo`), `SettingsButton` (`features/panel`), `TryItButton` (`features/tryit`). Keys: Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y redo (Cmd on a Mac), except in a text box and while a dialog or popover is in front (so the Publish dialog, the stage delete question and the conflict dialog stay true of the document behind them), and only for the workflow on screen. It turns a `reveal(location)` into navigation (`revealTarget` in `src/model/session`).
- `DiagramTab.tsx`: the Diagram tab: `DiagramView` (features/diagram), a separator, `StagePanel` (features/panel). The panel's width is `--panel-w` (480px by default), set on the workspace; the author drags the separator, or focuses it and uses the arrow keys, Home and End, between 400 and 640px; remembered in localStorage (`editor.panelWidth`).
- `slots.ts`: fills the model slots (`src/model/slots.ts`): `StageActions` (`features/actions`), `WhenBuilder`, `FormulaEditor` (`features/conditions`), `ValueField`, `ValueChip`, `MessageField`, `ListDialog` (`features/values`), `KindChooser` (`features/diagram`).
- `AppLayout.tsx`: the simpler frame for the pages people use (Workflows, My tasks, Requests, Connections). Its brand mark is not a link (the menu's "Workflows" goes there), so the frame has one link of that name. On the development host only (`import.meta.env.DEV`, and only when `session.people()` offers anyone): `DevPerson.tsx` at the right of its top bar, marked "For development only": "Signed in as [person]" (`session.whoAmI`, `people`, `signInAs`), so the request pages can be tried as the requester, an approver and the person who looks after stuck requests; changing person mounts the page afresh, so it asks the services again as the new person. Its footer has `DevReset.tsx`: "Reset sample data", marked the same way, which asks first, then starts the stand-in again from its seed and reloads.
- `topBarFit.ts`: keeps the editor's top bar on one row without overlapping (the frontend owner's ruling, fix round 2). The workflow's name is cut with "..." after 28 characters at every width (its tooltip and accessible name keep the whole name). The bar has three groups that never shrink (name and version; tabs and Glossary; the right-hand buttons). When they do not fit, `useTopBarFit` raises `data-fit` on the bar one level at a time (and lists every level reached in `data-gave`, so CSS writes `[data-gave~="3"]`): 1 the version line shortens ("Version 3 is live" reads "v 3 live": a slot puts its whole words in `<span data-topbar-long="">` and the short form in `<span data-topbar-short="" aria-hidden="true">`, both inside `data-topbar-shrink`); 2 the tabs keep their words but take less padding, and the gaps narrow; 3 the buttons take less padding; 4 the tabs lose their icons; 5 Glossary, Settings, Try it and Publish lose their icons; 6 the bar wraps onto two rows (and `--top-h` follows its height). Never given up: the word "Glossary", the save state in words, and the To do and Worth knowing counts. At 1440px the bar stays on one row in every state, also with a 37-character name and To do, Worth knowing and "Publish · 2 to do first" all shown (level 5); at 1280 that case wraps; `tests/e2e/topbar.spec.ts` checks it.
- `routeFocus.ts`: after a change of page (Submit on the start page, "Edit form", a task opened from My tasks), focus left on nothing (the pressed button is gone) goes to the new page's place for it: an element marked `data-page-focus` (such as a "started" note), else its `h1` (given `tabindex="-1"`, not put in the Tab order). A page that puts the focus somewhere itself is left alone. Started once in `main.tsx` with `followRouteFocus(router)`.
- "Settings" links: `EditorLayout` tells the session how to open Settings (`setSettingsOpener`: it presses the top bar's Settings button, inside `.settingsSlot`), so any screen can open it with `openSettings()` from `@/model`, for the "Settings" link part of a sentence (`isSettingsLink`). The Glossary's Stuck line uses it (`settingsLinked`).
- `Glossary.tsx`: the Glossary popover (words only). `UiReference.tsx`: `/ui-reference` (its sample text is in `src/words/reference.ts`).
- The only folder allowed to import from every feature. Nothing imports from `app`.

import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { act, cleanup, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import { useEffect, useRef, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { createMemoryRouter, RouterProvider, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';

/** A page whose button goes to another page (and is gone once there), as Submit on the start page does. */
function From() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Start a request</h1>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => navigate('/to')}>
        Submit
      </button>
    </main>
  );
}

function To({ marked, own }: { marked?: boolean; own?: boolean }) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (own) ref.current?.focus();
  }, [own]);
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Request 1006</h1>
      {marked && (
        <p data-page-focus="" tabIndex={-1}>
          Your request is started
        </p>
      )}
      {own && <input ref={ref} aria-label="Name" />}
    </main>
  );
}

let stop: (() => void) | undefined;
afterEach(() => {
  stop?.();
  cleanup();
});

function open(to: ReactElement) {
  const router = createMemoryRouter([
    { path: '/', element: <From /> },
    { path: '/to', element: to },
  ]);
  stop = followRouteFocus(router);
  render(<RouterProvider router={router} />);
  return router;
}

describe('focus after a change of page (review fix2-app n3)', () => {
  it('goes to the new page\'s heading when the pressed button is gone', async () => {
    open(<To />);
    const submit = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    submit.focus();
    act(() => submit.click());
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Request 1006' })).toHaveFocus());
    // Not put in the Tab order.
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Request 1006' })).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
  });

  it('goes to a place the page marks for it (a "started" note) before the heading', async () => {
    open(<To marked />);
    const submit = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    submit.focus();
    act(() => submit.click());
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText('Your request is started')).toHaveFocus());
  });

  it('leaves the focus where the new page put it', async () => {
    open(<To own />);

    submit.focus();
    act(() => submit.click());
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Name' })).toHaveFocus());
