group('what happens when another system fails (A, one sentence for In words and the action card)', () => {
  const ig = fixture('integrated-sample');
  const env = { catalogue: fixtureCatalogue, stuckPeople: sam };
  const action = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string) => getAction(doc, id) as UseConnection;

  it('Stop: three sentences: asked again when unreachable or unclear; who is told when slow; stuck only on a clear failure', () => {
    const words = describeIfItFails(ig, action(ig, 'act_look_up_service'), env);
    expect(words.stops).toBe(true);
    expect(toText(words.askedAgain)).toBe(
      'If Service catalog cannot be reached or its answer is unclear, Service catalog is asked again and the request is not stuck.',
    );
    // The catalogue's expected time (expectedWithinSeconds 300); the first mention says who they are.
    expect(toText(words.slow ?? [])).toBe(
      'If Service catalog has not answered after 5 minutes, Sam Carter, who looks after stuck requests, is told; the request is not stuck.',
    );
    // The second mention is short.
    expect(toText(words.failed)).toBe('If Service catalog says it failed, the request is stuck here and Sam Carter is told.');
    expect(toText(words.sentence)).toBe(`${toText(words.askedAgain)} ${toText(words.slow ?? [])} ${toText(words.failed)}`);
    const card = describeIfItFails(ig, action(ig, 'act_look_up_service'), { ...env, stuckPeople: platform }, { settingsHint: true });
    expect(toText(card.slow ?? [])).toBe(
      'If Service catalog has not answered after 5 minutes, Platform team, who look after stuck requests, are told (change this in Settings); the request is not stuck.',
    );
    expect(links(card.slow ?? [])).toEqual(['Settings']);
    expect(toText(card.failed)).toBe('If Service catalog says it failed, the request is stuck here and Platform team are told.');
    // Already said who they are elsewhere: both short.
    const short = describeIfItFails(ig, action(ig, 'act_look_up_service'), env, { short: true });
    expect(toText(short.slow ?? [])).toBe('If Service catalog has not answered after 5 minutes, Sam Carter is told; the request is not stuck.');
  });

  it('a Wait for: not reported back after its time; without a catalogue no time is known, so no slow sentence', () => {
    const words = describeIfItFails(ig, action(ig, 'act_run_pipeline'), env);
    expect(toText(words.askedAgain)).toBe(
      'If Deploy pipeline cannot be reached or its answer is unclear, Deploy pipeline is asked again and the request is not stuck.',
    );
    expect(toText(words.slow ?? [])).toBe(
      'If Deploy pipeline has not reported back after 30 minutes, Sam Carter, who looks after stuck requests, is told; the request is not stuck.',
    );
    const unknown = describeIfItFails(ig, action(ig, 'act_run_pipeline'), { stuckPeople: sam });
    expect(unknown.slow).toBeUndefined();
    expect(toText(unknown.sentence)).toBe(`${toText(unknown.askedAgain)} ${toText(unknown.failed)}`);
  });

  it('says a time the catalogue gives in plain words', () => {
    expect([1, 45, 60, 90, 900, 3600, 7200, 86400, 172800].map(durationWords)).toEqual([
      '1 second', '45 seconds', '1 minute', '2 minutes', '15 minutes', '1 hour', '2 hours', '1 day', '2 days',
    ]);
  });

  it('Carry on: says what each named value records, and only the ones named', () => {
    const doc = fixture('integrated-sample');
    const run = action(doc, 'act_run_pipeline');
    const failed = () => toText(describeIfItFails(doc, run, env).failed);
    expect(failed()).toBe('If Deploy pipeline says it failed, the request carries on: Deploy failed is Yes and what went wrong is saved as Deploy failure code.');
    run.saveFailureAs = { failed: 'v_deploy_failed' };
    expect(failed()).toBe('If Deploy pipeline says it failed, the request carries on and Deploy failed is Yes.');
    run.saveFailureAs = { code: 'v_deploy_failure_code' };
    expect(failed()).toBe('If Deploy pipeline says it failed, the request carries on and what went wrong is saved as Deploy failure code.');
    run.saveFailureAs = {};
    expect(failed()).toBe('If Deploy pipeline says it failed, the request carries on.');
  });

  it('In words says the same, with a group in "Stuck requests go to" agreeing in number', () => {
    const text = describeInWords(ig, { catalogue: fixtureCatalogue, stuckPeople: platform }).map(paragraphText).join(' ');
    expect(text).toContain('If Jira says it failed, the request is stuck here and Platform team are told.');
    expect(text).not.toContain('cannot be reached the request is stuck');
  });
});

    expect(heldValueText(cr, false, env)).toBe('No');

    expect(heldValueText(cr, { $redacted: true }, env)).toBe('removed');
    expect(heldValueText(cr, 'ch_risk_gone', env)).not.toContain('ch_');
    expect(describeHeldValue(cr, { type: 'group', id: 'g_payments' }, env)).toEqual([{ chip: 'group', label: 'Payments approvers', id: 'g_payments' }]);
  });

  it('says a failure code by the words the catalogue gives it, never the code', () => {
    expect(heldValueText(ig, 'tests-failed', env, 'v_deploy_failure_code')).toBe('The tests failed');
    expect(heldValueText(ig, 'no-such-code', env, 'v_deploy_failure_code')).toBe('a problem the other system did not name');
    expect(failureCodeWords(fixtureCatalogue, 'deploy.runPipeline@1', 'rolled-back')).toBe('The deployment was rolled back');
    // The same text held in an ordinary value is said as it is.
    expect(heldValueText(ig, 'tests-failed', env, 'v_summary')).toBe('tests-failed');
  });

  it('a saved failure code is a choice: its choices are the catalogue\'s codes and labels, and a { failureCode } constant reads as its label (E-29)', () => {
    expect(valueChoices(ig, fixtureCatalogue, 'v_deploy_failure_code')?.map((c) => [c.constant, c.label])).toEqual(
      (fixtureCatalogue.entries.find((e) => e.id === 'deploy.runPipeline@1') as { failureCodes: { code: string; label: string }[] }).failureCodes.map((f) => [{ failureCode: f.code }, f.label]),

    const clause = { allOf: [{ left: { value: 'v_deploy_failure_code' }, words: 'choice.is', right: { failureCode: 'tests-failed' } }] } as Condition;

  it('a link value: an issue key whose address the catalogue names (addressOf) is the link\'s words; an address alone reads without "http://"', () => {
    // integrated-sample's Fix deployment saves the issue's key and its address; the catalogue says url is the address of key (E-32).

    expect(addressValueOf(ig, fixtureCatalogue, 'v_fix_issue_link')).toBeUndefined();
    // Look up a service saves two results too, neither of them an address: no link, and no guess by count.
    expect(addressValueOf(ig, fixtureCatalogue, 'v_service_owner')).toBeUndefined();
    // Without the catalogue's word nothing is paired.
    const plain = structuredClone(fixtureCatalogue);
    for (const e of plain.entries) if (e.kind === 'operation') for (const f of e.result ?? []) delete f.addressOf;
    expect(addressValueOf(ig, plain, 'v_fix_issue')).toBeUndefined();
    const values = { v_fix_issue: 'CHG-101', v_fix_issue_link: 'http://jira.mock.test/browse/CHG-101', v_run_link: 'https://deploy.mock.test/runs/run-5001/' };

    expect(describeHeldValue(ig, values.v_fix_issue_link, linked, 'v_fix_issue_link')).toEqual([
      { text: 'jira.mock.test/browse/CHG-101', href: 'http://jira.mock.test/browse/CHG-101', link: 'web' },

    // The pipeline run is the one result of its action: the address, as a link, without "https://" and the closing "/".
    expect(describeHeldValue(ig, values.v_run_link, linked, 'v_run_link')).toEqual([

/**
 * The parts of a stage that are not arrows or actions, in words: who is asked, the status line,
 * where a question's choices come from, and a "Starts when" binding on the start stage.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Choices, Stage, StartsWhen, Task } from '@/contract';
import { find } from '../lookup';
import { connectionLabel, entryOf, labelAfterConnection } from './catalogue';
import { describeCondition } from './condition';
import { describeExpression, formulaWords } from './expression';
import { deletedName, listChip, statusChip } from './names';
import { chip, gap, joinPhrases, lowerFirst, missing, phrase, w, type DescribeEnv, type Phrase } from './phrase';

/** "Primary domain's approvers", "Eng lead (if empty, use ...)", or "Nobody is asked yet" (missing). */
export function describeWhoIsAsked(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, task: Task, options: { short?: boolean } = {}): Phrase {
  if (!task.whoIsAsked) return [missing(w('describe.nobodyAsked'))];
  return describeExpression(doc, task.whoIsAsked, {}, options);
}

/**
 * The status line of a stage box: "Waiting for approval", "If sent back: Needs changes", or both
 * ("Checking the service · if sent back: Needs changes"); "No status yet" (missing) when neither.
 */
export function describeStatus(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, stage: Stage): Phrase {
  const status = stage.status ? statusChip(doc, stage.status) : undefined;
  const ifSentBack = stage.kind !== 'ending' && stage.ifSentBackStatus ? statusChip(doc, stage.ifSentBackStatus) : undefined;
  if (status && ifSentBack) return phrase('describe.status.both', { status, ifSentBack });
  if (ifSentBack) return phrase('describe.status.ifSentBack', { status: ifSentBack });
  if (status) return [status];
  return [missing(w('describe.status.none'))];
}

/** Where a question's choices come from. */
export function describeChoicesSource(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, choices: Choices | undefined, env: DescribeEnv = {}): Phrase {
  switch (choices?.from) {
    case 'typedIn': {
      const items = (choices.choices ?? []).map((c) => [c.label ? chip('constant', c.label, c.id) : chip('constant', w('describe.noName'), c.id, true)]);
      return phrase('describe.choices.typedIn', { choices: items.length ? joinPhrases(items, 'and') : gap() });
    }
    case 'list': {
      const list = choices.list ? listChip(doc, choices.list) : gap();
      if (!choices.shownColumn) return phrase('describe.choices.list', { list });
      const entry = find(doc, choices.shownColumn);
      const column = entry?.kind === 'column' ? entry.item.name || w('describe.noName') : missing(deletedName(doc, choices.shownColumn));
      return phrase('describe.choices.listShowing', { list, column });
    }
    case 'directory':
      return phrase('describe.choices.directory', { group: describeExpression(doc, choices.peopleIn, env) });
    case 'source': {
      if (!choices.source) return phrase('describe.choices.sourceNone', { gap: gap() });
      const entry = entryOf(env.catalogue, choices.source);
      const connection = chip('connection', connectionLabel(env.catalogue, entry, choices.source), entry?.connection);
      return phrase('describe.choices.source', { connection, source: entry?.label ?? choices.source });
    }
    case 'formula':
      return formulaWords(choices.formula?.readsAs);
    default:
      return [missing(w('describe.choices.none'))];
  }
}

/**
 * "Starts when Helpdesk: a ticket is created, only when Ticket: Category is Change; Requester from
 * Ticket: Raised by". The Requester part is said only when the binding names one.
 */
export function describeStartsWhen(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, binding: StartsWhen, env: DescribeEnv = {}): Phrase {
  const startsWhen = describeStartsWhenName(binding, env);
  if (!binding.trigger || !binding.onlyWhen) return withRequester(doc, binding, env, startsWhen);
  const condition = describeCondition(doc, binding.onlyWhen, { ...env, trigger: binding.trigger });
  return withRequester(doc, binding, env, phrase('describe.startsWhen.onlyWhen', { startsWhen, condition }));
}

/**
 * The name of a "Starts when", the same everywhere it is named (In words, the To do place, Try it,
 * "Starts that were refused", the card's own controls): "Starts when Helpdesk: a ticket is created".
 * The connection is named once: a catalogue label that ends "in Helpdesk" loses those words
 * (`labelAfterConnection`). "Starts when …" (missing) before a trigger is chosen.
 */
export function describeStartsWhenName(binding: Pick<StartsWhen, 'trigger'>, env: DescribeEnv = {}): Phrase {
  if (!binding.trigger) return phrase('describe.startsWhen.none', { gap: gap() });
  const entry = entryOf(env.catalogue, binding.trigger);
  const connection = chip('connection', connectionLabel(env.catalogue, entry, binding.trigger), entry?.connection);
  const label = labelAfterConnection(env.catalogue, binding.trigger);
  return phrase('describe.startsWhen', { connection, trigger: label ? lowerFirst(label) : binding.trigger });
}

function withRequester(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, binding: StartsWhen, env: DescribeEnv, said: Phrase): Phrase {
  if (!binding.requester) return said;
  const requester = describeExpression(doc, binding.requester, { ...env, trigger: binding.trigger });
  return phrase('describe.startsWhen.requester', { startsWhen: said, requester });
}

/**
 * Who is told about a stuck request, said one way everywhere: the editor (action cards, To do,
 * In words), Try it and the request pages. One person: "Sam Carter, who looks after stuck requests,
 * is told"; a group or several: "Platform team, who look after stuck requests, are told"; in the
 * past for what already happened ("was told", "were told"). The words are in src/words/describe.ts.
 */
import { chip, joinPhrases, phrase, settingsLink, toText, type Phrase } from './phrase';
import type { WordKey } from '@/words';
import { verbNumber } from './verb';

/** One of the people in "Stuck requests go to", by the name the directory gives. `group`: a group (it reads as many). */
export interface StuckPerson {
  name: string;
  group?: boolean;
}

export interface StuckToldOptions {
  /** "is told" (default) or "was told". */
  tense?: 'present' | 'past';
  /** "Sam Carter is told": for a second mention, once the first has said who they are. */
  short?: boolean;
  /** Ends with "(change this in Settings)", "Settings" being the link part (editor-model.md section 9). */
  settingsHint?: boolean;
}

/**
 * "Sam Carter, who looks after stuck requests, is told", "Platform team, who look after stuck
 * requests, are told", "Sam Carter and Priya Raman, who look after stuck requests, were told"; "the
 * people who look after stuck requests are told" when nobody is known (yet). Lower case first, for
 * the middle of a sentence; the names are person and group chips.
 */
export function describeStuckTold(people: readonly StuckPerson[] | undefined, options: StuckToldOptions = {}): Phrase {
  const tense = options.tense ?? 'present';
  const known = (people ?? []).filter((p) => p.name.trim());
  let told: Phrase;
  if (known.length === 0) told = phrase(`describe.stuck.nobody.${tense}` as WordKey);
  else {
    const number = verbNumber(known.map((p) => ({ kind: p.group ? 'group' : 'person' })));
    const who = joinPhrases(known.map((p) => [chip(p.group ? 'group' : 'person', p.name.trim())]), 'and');
    const key = `describe.stuck.${options.short ? 'short.' : ''}${number}.${tense}` as WordKey;
    told = phrase(key, { who });
  }
  if (!options.settingsHint) return told;
  return phrase('describe.stuck.withHint', { told, hint: phrase('describe.changeInSettings', { settings: settingsLink() }) });
}

/** The same as plain text: "Sam Carter, who looks after stuck requests, is told (change this in Settings)". */
export const stuckToldText = (people: readonly StuckPerson[] | undefined, options: StuckToldOptions = {}): string =>
  toText(describeStuckTold(people, options));

===\nfrontend/src/model/describe/value-card.ts\n===
/**
 * The small value card (editor-model.md section 9, "Getting into things from where you see them";
 * mockup 01-editor, value-card) in words: where a value is filled ("Domain approval · by the
 * question Eng lead"), the "If empty, use ..." its uses fall back to, and every place that uses it
 * ("Create Jira issue · In Jira this is called Assignee", "Domain approval · Needed to press
 * Approve"). One line per place, each with the location that shows it. The words are in
 * src/words/describe.ts ("describe.card.*").
 */
import type { Action, AuthoredWorkflow, Expression, Location } from '@/contract';
import { find, getQuestion, getTask } from '../lookup';
import { eachExpression, fillSites, referencesTo, type Reference } from '../walk';
import { actionName } from './action';
import { arrowLabel } from './arrow';
import { describeExpression } from './expression';
import { connectionField, locationCrumbs } from './location';
import { itemName } from './names';
import { failureChoices } from './value-choices';
import { joinPhrases, phrase, toText, w, type DescribeEnv, type Phrase } from './phrase';

/** One line of the card: the stage it is in, and what it is there. */
export interface ValueCardLine {
  /** What the line shows when clicked. */
  location: Location;
  /** The stage's name ("Create Jira issue"); empty for a place outside any stage. */
  stage: string;
  /** What it is there: "by the question Eng lead", "In Jira this is called Assignee", "Who is asked". */
  what: string;
}

export interface ValueCardWords {
  /** "Filled at": one line per place that fills it. */
  filled: ValueCardLine[];
  /** "If empty, use ...": each distinct fallback its uses have, as a phrase with chips. */
  ifEmptyUse: Phrase[];
  /** "Used in N places": one line per item that reads it, plus the buttons its question is needed to press. */
  used: ValueCardLine[];
  /**
   * For a value an action saves what went wrong in (a choice of failure codes, E-29): "A choice of:
   * The tests failed, The deployment failed or ...", by the catalogue's labels.
   */
  choices?: string;
}

function stageIdOf(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string): string | undefined {
  const entry = find(doc, id);
  if (!entry) return undefined;
  return entry.kind === 'stage' ? entry.id : entry.parents.stage;
}

const stageName = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string): string => {
  const stage = stageIdOf(doc, id);
  return stage ? itemName(doc, stage) : '';
};

/** Where a stage sits in the document, to list places in the order a request meets them. */
function stageOrder(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): (id: string) => number {
  const order = new Map<string, number>((doc.stages ?? []).map((s, i) => [s.id, i]));
  return (id) => order.get(stageIdOf(doc, id) ?? '') ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
}

function fillWhat(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, r: Reference, env: DescribeEnv): string {
  const action = () => {
    const e = find(doc, r.owner.id);
    return e?.kind === 'action' ? toText(actionName(doc, e.item as Action, env, true)) : '';
  };
  switch (r.how) {
    case 'savedAs':
      return toText(phrase('describe.card.by.savedAs', { name: getQuestion(doc, r.owner.id)?.label ?? '' }));
    case 'saveAs':
      return toText(phrase('describe.card.by.saveAs', { name: action() }));
    case 'saveResults':
      return toText(phrase('describe.card.by.saveResults', { name: action() }));
    case 'saveFailureAs':
      return toText(phrase('describe.card.by.saveFailureAs', { name: action() }));
    case 'savesButtonPressedAs':
      return w('describe.card.by.savesButtonPressedAs');
    case 'savesAnsweredByAs':
      return w('describe.card.by.savesAnsweredByAs');
    default:
      return '';
  }
}

/** What a reading place is, said for the card: the connection's own name, the action, or the part. */
function useWhat(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, r: Reference, env: DescribeEnv): string {
  const entry = find(doc, r.owner.id);
  const part = r.location.part ?? '';
  if (entry?.kind === 'action') {
    const [head = '', ...rest] = part.split('.');
    if (head === 'inputs' && rest.length) {
      const field = connectionField(entry, 'inputs', rest.join('.'), env);
      if (field.connection) return toText(phrase('describe.card.calledIn', { connection: field.connection, field: field.label }));
    }
    // A notification, a saved value: the action's own name says what it does with it ("Notify Eng lead").
    if (head === 'to' || head === 'save' || head === '') return toText(actionName(doc, entry.item as Action, env, true));
  }
  // An arrow is said as the arrow it is ("The arrow "Approve pressed""), never by the "Then go to" it sits under.
  if (entry?.kind === 'arrow') return toText(phrase('describe.card.arrow', { arrow: arrowLabel(doc, entry.item) }));
  if (entry?.kind === 'question' && part.startsWith('choices.inputs.')) {
    const field = connectionField(entry, 'inputs', part.slice('choices.inputs.'.length), env);
    if (field.connection) return toText(phrase('describe.card.calledIn', { connection: field.connection, field: field.label }));
  }
  const crumbs = locationCrumbs(doc, r.location, env);
  const stage = stageName(doc, r.owner.id);
  return (crumbs[0] === stage ? crumbs.slice(1) : crumbs).join(w('describe.where.separator'));
}

/** "Needed to press Approve": the buttons that need a question that fills the value, one line per task. */
function neededToPress(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, fills: Reference[]): ValueCardLine[] {
  const lines: ValueCardLine[] = [];
  for (const r of fills) {
    if (r.how !== 'savedAs') continue;
    const question = getQuestion(doc, r.owner.id);
    const task = getTask(doc, find(doc, r.owner.id)?.parents.task);
    if (!question || !task) continue;
    const buttons = (task.buttons ?? []).filter((b) => question.neededForEveryButton || (b.neededToPress ?? []).includes(question.id));
    const first = buttons[0];
    if (!first) continue;
    lines.push({
      location: { item: first.id, part: 'neededToPress' },
      stage: stageName(doc, task.id),
      what: toText(phrase('describe.card.neededToPress', { buttons: joinPhrases(buttons.map((b) => [b.label || itemName(doc, b.id)]), 'and') })),
    });
  }
  return lines;
}

/** The "If empty, use" fallbacks written on the value's uses, each once, most used first. */
export function fallbacksOf(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, valueId: string): Expression[] {
  const counts = new Map<string, { expr: Expression; n: number }>();
  const visit = (node: unknown) => {
    if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.forEach(visit);
    if (!node || typeof node !== 'object') return;
    const o = node as { value?: unknown; steps?: unknown[]; ifEmptyUse?: Expression };
    if (o.value === valueId && !(o.steps ?? []).length && o.ifEmptyUse) {
      const key = JSON.stringify(o.ifEmptyUse);
      const seen = counts.get(key);
      if (seen) seen.n += 1;
      else counts.set(key, { expr: o.ifEmptyUse, n: 1 });
    }
    for (const child of Object.values(o)) if (child && typeof child === 'object') visit(child);
  };
  eachExpression(doc, (node) => visit(node));
  return [...counts.values()].sort((a, b) => b.n - a.n).map((c) => c.expr);
}

/** The value card in words: where the value is filled, its "If empty, use", and every place that uses it. */
export function describeValueCard(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, valueId: string, env: DescribeEnv = {}): ValueCardWords {
  const order = stageOrder(doc);
  const fills = fillSites(doc, valueId);
  const filled = fills.map((r) => ({ location: r.location, stage: stageName(doc, r.owner.id), what: fillWhat(doc, r, env) }));

  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const reads = referencesTo(doc, valueId).filter((r) => {
    if (r.how !== 'value' && r.how !== 'chip') return false;
    if (seen.has(r.owner.id)) return false;
    seen.add(r.owner.id);
    return true;
  });
  const used = [
    ...neededToPress(doc, fills),
    ...reads.map((r) => ({ location: r.location, stage: stageName(doc, r.owner.id), what: useWhat(doc, r, env) })),
  ]
    .map((line, i) => ({ line, i }))
    .sort((a, b) => order(a.line.location.item) - order(b.line.location.item) || a.i - b.i)
    .map(({ line }) => line);

  const failures = failureChoices(doc, env.catalogue, valueId);
  const choices = failures?.length ? toText(phrase('describe.card.choices', { choices: joinPhrases(failures.map((c) => [c.label]), 'or') })) : undefined;
  return { filled, ifEmptyUse: fallbacksOf(doc, valueId).map((e) => describeExpression(doc, e, env)), used, ...(choices ? { choices } : {}) };
}
===\nfrontend/src/model/describe/value-choices.ts\n===
/**
 * The choices a value holds, when the document says what they are: a question's typed-in choices,
 * the rows of the list it is answered from, the buttons of the task whose "Button pressed" it is, or
 * the failure codes of the operations that save what went wrong in it (E-29: a choice whose choices
 * are the catalogue's failure codes, labelled by the catalogue). One source for the "when" builder's
 * pick list, a held value's words and the Values tab.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Catalogue, Constant, UseConnection } from '@/contract';
import { find, getQuestion, getTask } from '../lookup';
import { fillSites } from '../walk';
import { entryOf } from './catalogue';
import { rowChip } from './expression';
import { buttonChip } from './names';
import { w } from './phrase';

export interface ValueChoice {
  /** The constant a clause writes for it: `{ choice }`, `{ row }`, `{ button }` or `{ failureCode }`. */
  constant: Constant;
  /** What the request holds for it (core-api.md 2.4): the choice, row or button ID, or the code. */
  value: string;
  label: string;
}

/** The "Use a connection" actions that save their failure code as this value, in document order. */
export function failureCodeActions(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, valueId: string): UseConnection[] {
  const out: UseConnection[] = [];
  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    for (const action of [...(stage.whenThisStageStarts ?? []), ...(stage.afterTheyRespond ?? [])]) {
      if (action.type === 'useConnection' && action.saveFailureAs?.code === valueId) out.push(action);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The failure codes saved in this value, each once, labelled by the catalogue (where two operations
 * give one code two labels, the first action in document order gives it, as core does). Undefined
 * when no action saves its failure code as this value.
 */
export function failureChoices(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue | null | undefined, valueId: string): ValueChoice[] | undefined {
  const actions = failureCodeActions(doc, valueId);
  if (!actions.length) return undefined;
  const out: ValueChoice[] = [];
  for (const action of actions) {
    const entry = entryOf(catalogue ?? undefined, action.operation);
    if (entry?.kind !== 'operation') continue;
    for (const f of entry.failureCodes ?? []) {
      if (!out.some((c) => c.value === f.code)) out.push({ constant: { failureCode: f.code }, value: f.code, label: f.label || unnamedProblem() });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** The words the catalogue gives a failure code of one operation ("The tests failed"); undefined when it gives none. */
export function failureCodeWords(catalogue: Catalogue | null | undefined, operation: string | undefined, code: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (typeof code !== 'string') return undefined;
  const entry = entryOf(catalogue ?? undefined, operation);
  return entry?.kind === 'operation' ? (entry.failureCodes ?? []).find((f) => f.code === code)?.label || undefined : undefined;
}

/** "a problem the other system did not name": a failure code whose label cannot be found. Never the code. */
export const unnamedProblem = (): string => w('describe.held.failureUnknown');

/**
 * A failure code in words: its label from the operations that save into `valueId`, or, with no value
 * given, from any operation of the document's actions that save a failure code; else the words for an
 * unnamed problem.
 */
export function failureCodeLabel(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue | null | undefined, code: string, valueId?: string): string {
  const values = valueId ? [valueId] : [...new Set(allFailureValues(doc))];
  for (const v of values) {
    const found = failureChoices(doc, catalogue, v)?.find((c) => c.value === code);
    if (found) return found.label;
  }
  return unnamedProblem();
}

function allFailureValues(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    for (const action of [...(stage.whenThisStageStarts ?? []), ...(stage.afterTheyRespond ?? [])]) {
      if (action.type === 'useConnection' && action.saveFailureAs?.code) out.push(action.saveFailureAs.code);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** The choices of a value (see the file's comment); undefined when the document does not say them. */
export function valueChoices(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, catalogue: Catalogue | null | undefined, valueId: string): ValueChoice[] | undefined {
  for (const site of fillSites(doc, valueId)) {
    if (site.how === 'savedAs') {
      const choices = getQuestion(doc, site.owner.id)?.choices;
      if (!choices) continue;
      if (choices.from === 'typedIn') return choices.choices.map((c) => ({ constant: { choice: c.id }, value: c.id, label: c.label }));
      if (choices.from === 'list') {
        const list = find(doc, choices.list);
        if (list?.kind !== 'list') continue;
        return list.item.rows.map((r) => ({ constant: { row: r.id }, value: r.id, label: rowChip(doc, r.id).label }));
      }
    }
    if (site.how === 'savesButtonPressedAs') {
      const task = getTask(doc, site.owner.id);
      if (task) return task.buttons.map((b) => ({ constant: { button: b.id }, value: b.id, label: buttonChip(doc, b.id).label }));
    }
  }
  return failureChoices(doc, catalogue, valueId);
}
===\nfrontend/src/model/describe/verb.ts\n===
/**
 * Whether the subject of a sentence takes a singular or a plural verb, decided in one place for
 * every sentence the model says about people ("Sam Carter is asked", "Platform team are asked",
 * "Sam Carter and Priya Raman were told"). A group is many people, so it always takes the plural
 * verb, as British English has it for a team; several names take it too; one person takes the
 * singular. A name whose kind is not known (an author's value, a task's own name) is judged by its
 * words: a last word ending in a single "s" ("Domain approvers") reads as many.
 *
 * Word keys come in pairs ending `.one` and `.many` (`describe.stuck.one.present`,
 * `inwords.asked.many`); `verbNumber` says which of the two to use.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Expression } from '@/contract';
import { find } from '../lookup';
import { soundsPlural } from './names';

export type VerbNumber = 'one' | 'many';

/** One name in the subject. `kind` 'unknown': a name whose kind the document does not say. */
export interface VerbSubject {
  kind: 'person' | 'group' | 'unknown';
  /** The name, for judging an unknown kind by its words. */
  name?: string;
}

/**
 * 'many' for a group, for several names, or for an unknown name that reads as many; 'one' for one
 * person or one unknown name that reads as one. No subject at all is 'many' ("the people who look
 * after stuck requests are told").
 */
export function verbNumber(subjects: VerbSubject | readonly VerbSubject[]): VerbNumber {
  const all = Array.isArray(subjects) ? (subjects as readonly VerbSubject[]) : [subjects as VerbSubject];
  if (all.length !== 1) return 'many';
  const one = all[0] as VerbSubject;
  if (one.kind === 'group') return 'many';
  if (one.kind === 'person') return 'one';
  return one.name && soundsPlural(one.name) ? 'many' : 'one';
}

/** True when `verbNumber` says 'many'. */
export const takesPlural = (subjects: VerbSubject | readonly VerbSubject[]): boolean => verbNumber(subjects) === 'many';

const has = (node: unknown, key: string): boolean => !!node && typeof node === 'object' && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(node, key);

/** True when a value reference gives a group: a column of kind group, a directory step, or a group question. */
export function refersToGroup(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, expression: Expression): boolean {
  const ref = expression as { value?: string; steps?: Array<{ column?: string; directory?: string }> };
  const last = ref.steps?.[ref.steps.length - 1];
  if (last?.directory) return true;
  if (last?.column) {
    const column = find(doc, last.column);
    return column?.kind === 'column' && column.item.kind === 'group';
  }
  if (!ref.value) return false;
  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    for (const task of stage.tasks ?? []) {
      for (const page of task.form?.pages ?? []) {
        for (const item of page.items ?? []) {
          if (item.type === 'question' && item.savedAs === ref.value) return item.kind === 'group';
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * Who an expression names (who is asked, Notify's "to"), as the subject of a verb: the Requester
 * and a person are one person; a group is a group; people are each a person; a value that holds a
 * group is a group; anything else is judged by `name`, the words it is said with. Without its
 * "If empty, use": that is a subject of its own.
 */
export function subjectsOf(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, expression: Expression | undefined, name?: string): VerbSubject[] {
  const e = (expression ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
  const steps = (e.steps as unknown[] | undefined) ?? [];
  if (has(e, 'request') && steps.length === 0 && e.request === 'requester') return [{ kind: 'person' }];
  if (has(e, 'person')) return [{ kind: 'person' }];
  if (has(e, 'group')) return [{ kind: 'group' }];
  if (has(e, 'people')) {
    const n = Array.isArray(e.people) ? e.people.length : 2;
    return Array.from({ length: Math.max(n, 1) }, () => ({ kind: 'person' as const }));
  }
  if (has(e, 'value') && expression && refersToGroup(doc, expression)) return [{ kind: 'group' }];
  return [{ kind: 'unknown', ...(name ? { name } : {}) }];
}

===\nfrontend/src/model/form-order.ts\n===
/**
 * What a form's "Show when" may read (editor-model.md section 5, the form editor): the answers given
 * before it on the same form, never its own question's answer nor anything after it. A question, a
 * text or a page is shown or hidden as the form is filled in from the top, so a "Show when" that
 * read its own answer, or one further down, would hide something by an answer not given yet.
 *
 * Core's `valuesInScope` at a question's, text's or page's `showWhen` lists every answer of the same
 * form (core-api.md section 5: "a question or page reads ... the answers on the same form"), its own
 * and the later ones too. A picker for a "Show when" leaves out `laterAnswersAt(doc, at)`.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Location, Question } from '@/contract';
import { find } from './lookup';
import { fillSites } from './walk';

/**
 * The values a "Show when" at `at` must not offer: the answer of the question at `at` itself (for a
 * page, of every question on it), and the answers of the questions after it on the same form, unless
 * that value is also filled somewhere other than this form's own or later questions (then it may
 * hold an earlier value, from a stage before or a request sent back). Empty for any other place.
 */
export function laterAnswersAt(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, at: Location | null | undefined): Set<string> {
  const out = new Set<string>();
  const entry = at ? find(doc, at.item) : undefined;
  if (!entry || (entry.kind !== 'question' && entry.kind !== 'text' && entry.kind !== 'page')) return out;
  const task = find(doc, entry.parents.task);
  if (task?.kind !== 'task') return out;
  const pages = task.item.form?.pages ?? [];
  // The form's items from the top, and where `at` stands among them.
  const items = pages.flatMap((page) => (page.items ?? []).map((item) => ({ page: page.id, item })));
  const from = entry.kind === 'page' ? items.findIndex((x) => x.page === entry.id) : items.findIndex((x) => x.item.id === entry.id);
  if (from < 0) return out;
  const notYet = items.slice(from).map((x) => x.item).filter((i): i is Question => i.type === 'question');
  const notYetIds = new Set<string>(notYet.map((q) => q.id));
  const own = entry.kind === 'question' ? entry.item.savedAs : undefined;
  for (const q of notYet) {
    if (!q.savedAs) continue;
    const elsewhere = fillSites(doc, q.savedAs).some((r) => !notYetIds.has(r.owner.id));
    if (q.savedAs === own || !elsewhere) out.add(q.savedAs);
  }
  return out;
}

===\nfrontend/src/model/graph.ts\n===
/**
 * Stages and arrows as a graph: "Reached from" (arrows into a stage), arrows out of a stage, and
 * the order a request meets the stages (breadth-first from the start stage, then stages no arrow
 * reaches, endings last), used by In words and the layout.
 */
import type { Arrow, AuthoredWorkflow, Stage, StageId } from '@/contract';
import { getStage } from './lookup';

export interface ArrowFrom {
  /** The stage the arrow belongs to. */
  from: Stage;
  arrow: Arrow;
}

/** True when `stageId` is the start stage. */
export function isStartStage(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, stageId: string): boolean {
  return doc.start?.stage === stageId;
}

/** The arrows of a stage, in the order they are checked. Empty for an ending or an unknown stage. */
export function arrowsOutOf(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, stageId: string): Arrow[] {
  const stage = getStage(doc, stageId);
  return stage && stage.kind !== 'ending' ? (stage.arrows ?? []) : [];
}

/** "Reached from": every arrow, from any stage, that goes to `stageId`, in document order. */
export function arrowsInto(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, stageId: string): ArrowFrom[] {
  const into: ArrowFrom[] = [];
  for (const from of doc.stages ?? []) {
    if (from.kind === 'ending') continue;
    for (const arrow of from.arrows ?? []) if (arrow.goTo === stageId) into.push({ from, arrow });
  }
  return into;
}

/**
 * Stage IDs in the order a request meets them: breadth-first from the start stage following
 * arrows in their checked order; then working stages nothing reaches (document order); endings
 * last (reached ones in the order met, then the others).
 */
export function orderFromStart(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): StageId[] {
  const stages = doc.stages ?? [];
  const known = new Set(stages.map((s) => s.id));
  const met: StageId[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const queue: StageId[] = [];
  if (doc.start?.stage && known.has(doc.start.stage)) {
    queue.push(doc.start.stage);
    seen.add(doc.start.stage);
  }
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const id = queue.shift() as StageId;
    met.push(id);
    for (const arrow of arrowsOutOf(doc, id)) {
      if (arrow.goTo && known.has(arrow.goTo) && !seen.has(arrow.goTo)) {
        seen.add(arrow.goTo);
        queue.push(arrow.goTo);
      }
    }
  }
  const isEnding = (id: string) => getStage(doc, id)?.kind === 'ending';
  const unreached = stages.filter((s) => !seen.has(s.id));
  return [
    ...met.filter((id) => !isEnding(id)),
    ...unreached.filter((s) => s.kind !== 'ending').map((s) => s.id),
    ...met.filter(isEnding),
    ...unreached.filter((s) => s.kind === 'ending').map((s) => s.id),
  ];
}

describe('newId', () => {
  it('makes <prefix>_<6-8 base36> IDs that follow the ID rule', () => {
    const doc = fixture('blank');
    const random = seededRandom(7);
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
      const id = newId(doc, 'st', random);
      expect(id).toMatch(/^st_[0-9a-z]{6,8}$/);
      expect(isWellFormedId(id)).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('is repeatable with the same seed', () => {
    const doc = fixture('blank');
    expect(newId(doc, 'btn', seededRandom(3))).toBe(newId(doc, 'btn', seededRandom(3)));
  });

  it('never returns an ID in the document, in removedNames or already handed out', () => {

    let i = 0;
    const random = () => sequence[i++] ?? 0.5;
    const issued = new Set(['st_bbbbbb']);
    expect(newId(doc, 'st', random, issued)).toBe('st_cccccc');
    expect(issued.has('st_cccccc')).toBe(true);
  });

    const doc = fixture('blank');
    expect(() => newId(doc, 'zz' as 'st')).toThrow();

===\nfrontend/src/model/ids.ts\n===
/**
 * New item IDs: `<prefix>_<6-8 base36 chars>` (authored-format.ts, "ID rule"), unique in the
 * document and never one listed in `removedNames` (an ID is never reused). Randomness is
 * injectable so tests are repeatable.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow } from '@/contract';
import { ID_PATTERN, ITEM_KINDS } from '@/contract';
import { indexDoc } from './lookup';

export type IdPrefix = keyof typeof ITEM_KINDS;
/** A source of numbers in [0, 1), like Math.random. */
export type Random = () => number;

const BASE36 = '0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz';
const idPattern = new RegExp(ID_PATTERN);

/** True when `id` follows the ID rule: matches ID_PATTERN and has no `__`. */
export function isWellFormedId(id: string): boolean {
  return idPattern.test(id) && !id.includes('__');
}

/** Every ID in use or retired: the document's items plus the keys of removedNames. */
export function takenIds(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): Set<string> {
  const taken = new Set(indexDoc(doc).byId.keys());
  for (const id of Object.keys(doc.removedNames ?? {})) taken.add(id);
  return taken;
}

function randomTail(random: Random): string {
  const length = 6 + Math.min(2, Math.floor(random() * 3));
  let tail = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) tail += BASE36[Math.min(35, Math.floor(random() * 36))];
  return tail;
}

/**
 * A fresh ID with this prefix. `alsoTaken` holds IDs handed out but not yet put in the document
 * (several new items in one command).
 */
export function newId<P extends IdPrefix>(
  doc: AuthoredWorkflow,
  prefix: P,
  random: Random = Math.random,
  alsoTaken?: Set<string>,
): `${P}_${string}` {
  if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ITEM_KINDS, prefix)) throw new Error(`Unknown ID prefix: ${prefix}`);
  const taken = takenIds(doc);
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 1000; attempt++) {
    const id = `${prefix}_${randomTail(random)}` as const;
    if (!taken.has(id) && !alsoTaken?.has(id) && isWellFormedId(id)) {
      alsoTaken?.add(id);
      return id;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('Could not find a free ID (is the random source stuck?)');
}

/** A seeded random source (mulberry32), for tests and repeatable runs. */
export function seededRandom(seed: number): Random {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
    let t = a;
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

===\nfrontend/src/model/invariants.ts\n===
/**
 * The document's structural rules, which every command must keep (an unfinished draft is fine;
 * a malformed one is not): IDs unique, well-formed and of the right kind for where they sit;
 * every reference resolves or its target is named in removedNames; at most one "In all other
 * cases" per stage and it is last; the start stage exists and is a working stage with one task.
 * Used by the model's tests after every command, and exported for other builders' tests.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow } from '@/contract';
import { isWellFormedId } from './ids';
import { indexDoc, kindOfId } from './lookup';
import { allReferences } from './walk';

export type StructuralCode =
  | 'badId'
  | 'idKindMismatch'
  | 'duplicateId'
  | 'danglingReference'
  | 'catchAllNotLast'
  | 'twoCatchAlls'
  | 'startStageMissing'
  | 'startStageNotWorking'
  | 'startStageTaskCount';

export interface StructuralProblem {
  code: StructuralCode;
  /** The ID concerned (the item, or the missing target). */
  id: string;
  /** For a dangling reference: where it is. */
  at?: string;
}

/** The IDs the document refers to that are neither in it nor named in removedNames. */
export function unknownTargets(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): Set<string> {
  const { byId } = indexDoc(doc);
  const removed = doc.removedNames ?? {};
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const ref of allReferences(doc)) {
    if (!byId.has(ref.target) && !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(removed, ref.target)) out.add(ref.target);
  }
  return out;
}

/** Every structural problem in the document; empty when it is well-formed. */
export function structuralProblems(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): StructuralProblem[] {
  const problems: StructuralProblem[] = [];
  const { byId, duplicates } = indexDoc(doc);

  for (const [id, entry] of byId) {
    if (!isWellFormedId(id)) problems.push({ code: 'badId', id });
    else if (kindOfId(id) !== entry.kind) problems.push({ code: 'idKindMismatch', id });
  }
  for (const id of duplicates) problems.push({ code: 'duplicateId', id });

  const removed = doc.removedNames ?? {};
  for (const ref of allReferences(doc)) {
    if (!byId.has(ref.target) && !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(removed, ref.target)) {
      problems.push({ code: 'danglingReference', id: ref.target, at: `${ref.location.item}${ref.location.part ? `.${ref.location.part}` : ''}` });
    }
  }

  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    const arrows = stage.arrows ?? [];
    const catchAlls = arrows.filter((a) => a.when?.type === 'inAllOtherCases');
    if (catchAlls.length > 1) problems.push({ code: 'twoCatchAlls', id: stage.id });
    else if (catchAlls.length === 1 && arrows[arrows.length - 1] !== catchAlls[0]) {
      problems.push({ code: 'catchAllNotLast', id: stage.id });
    }
  }

  const start = byId.get(doc.start?.stage ?? '');
  if (!start || start.kind !== 'stage') problems.push({ code: 'startStageMissing', id: doc.start?.stage ?? '' });
  else if (start.item.kind === 'ending') problems.push({ code: 'startStageNotWorking', id: start.id });
  else if ((start.item.tasks ?? []).length !== 1) problems.push({ code: 'startStageTaskCount', id: start.id });

  return problems;
}

===\nfrontend/src/model/lookup.ts\n===
/**
 * Finding things in the document by ID. `indexDoc` lists every item with its kind and its parents
 * (the stage of a task, the task of a button, the page of a question, the section of an action ...).
 * The index of a finished (non-draft) document is memoised per document object; a draft being
 * edited inside a command is indexed afresh each call. Unknown and dangling IDs give undefined.
 */
import { isDraft } from 'immer';
import type {
  Action,
  Arrow,
  AuthoredWorkflow,
  Button,
  Choice,
  Column,
  FormText,
  ItemKind,
  List,
  Page,
  Question,
  Row,
  Stage,
  StartsWhen,
  Status,
  Task,
  ThingTold,
  Value,
  WorkingStage,
} from '@/contract';
import { ITEM_KINDS } from '@/contract';

/** The two action sections of a working stage. */
export type Section = 'whenThisStageStarts' | 'afterTheyRespond';

type ItemByKind = {
  workflow: AuthoredWorkflow;
  stage: Stage;
  status: Status;
  task: Task;
  page: Page;
  question: Question;
  text: FormText;
  choice: Choice;
  button: Button;
  action: Action;
  arrow: Arrow;
  value: Value;
  list: List;
  column: Column;
  row: Row;
  startsWhen: StartsWhen;
  thingTold: ThingTold;
};

/** The items an item sits inside. Only the ones that apply are set. */
export interface Parents {
  stage?: string;
  task?: string;
  page?: string;
  question?: string;
  list?: string;
  section?: Section;
}

/** One item of the document: its kind, the item itself and where it sits. */
export type Entry = {
  [K in ItemKind]: { id: string; kind: K; item: ItemByKind[K]; parents: Parents };
}[ItemKind];

export type EntryOf<K extends ItemKind> = Extract<Entry, { kind: K }>;

export interface DocIndex {
  byId: Map<string, Entry>;
  /** IDs met more than once (a structural problem). */
  duplicates: string[];
}

/** The kind an ID's prefix names, or undefined for an unknown prefix. */
export function kindOfId(id: string): ItemKind | undefined {
  const at = id.indexOf('_');
  if (at <= 0) return undefined;
  const prefix = id.slice(0, at);
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ITEM_KINDS, prefix)
    ? ITEM_KINDS[prefix as keyof typeof ITEM_KINDS]
    : undefined;
}

function buildIndex(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): DocIndex {
  const byId = new Map<string, Entry>();
  const duplicates: string[] = [];
  const add = (entry: Entry) => {
    if (byId.has(entry.id)) duplicates.push(entry.id);
    else byId.set(entry.id, entry);
  };

  add({ id: doc.id, kind: 'workflow', item: doc, parents: {} });
  for (const sw of doc.start?.startsWhen ?? []) add({ id: sw.id, kind: 'startsWhen', item: sw, parents: {} });
  for (const status of doc.statuses ?? []) add({ id: status.id, kind: 'status', item: status, parents: {} });
  for (const told of doc.thingsTold ?? []) add({ id: told.id, kind: 'thingTold', item: told, parents: {} });
  for (const value of doc.values ?? []) add({ id: value.id, kind: 'value', item: value, parents: {} });
  for (const list of doc.lists ?? []) {
    add({ id: list.id, kind: 'list', item: list, parents: {} });
    for (const column of list.columns ?? []) add({ id: column.id, kind: 'column', item: column, parents: { list: list.id } });
    for (const row of list.rows ?? []) add({ id: row.id, kind: 'row', item: row, parents: { list: list.id } });
  }
  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    add({ id: stage.id, kind: 'stage', item: stage, parents: {} });
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    const s = { stage: stage.id };
    for (const section of ['whenThisStageStarts', 'afterTheyRespond'] as const) {
      for (const action of stage[section] ?? []) add({ id: action.id, kind: 'action', item: action, parents: { ...s, section } });
    }
    for (const task of stage.tasks ?? []) {
      add({ id: task.id, kind: 'task', item: task, parents: s });
      const t = { ...s, task: task.id };
      for (const page of task.form?.pages ?? []) {
        add({ id: page.id, kind: 'page', item: page, parents: t });
        const p = { ...t, page: page.id };
        for (const formItem of page.items ?? []) {
          if (formItem.type === 'text') {
            add({ id: formItem.id, kind: 'text', item: formItem, parents: p });
            continue;
          }
          add({ id: formItem.id, kind: 'question', item: formItem, parents: p });
          if (formItem.choices?.from === 'typedIn') {
            for (const choice of formItem.choices.choices ?? []) {
              add({ id: choice.id, kind: 'choice', item: choice, parents: { ...p, question: formItem.id } });
            }
          }
        }
      }
      for (const button of task.buttons ?? []) add({ id: button.id, kind: 'button', item: button, parents: t });
    }
    for (const arrow of stage.arrows ?? []) add({ id: arrow.id, kind: 'arrow', item: arrow, parents: s });
  }
  return { byId, duplicates };
}

const cache = new WeakMap<AuthoredWorkflow, DocIndex>();

/** Every item by ID. Memoised for finished documents; drafts are indexed afresh. */
export function indexDoc(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): DocIndex {
  if (isDraft(doc)) return buildIndex(doc);
  let index = cache.get(doc);
  if (!index) {
    index = buildIndex(doc);
    cache.set(doc, index);
  }
  return index;
}

/** The item with this ID, or undefined. */
export function find(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined): Entry | undefined {
  return id ? indexDoc(doc).byId.get(id) : undefined;
}

function findOf<K extends ItemKind>(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined, kind: K): ItemByKind[K] | undefined {
  const entry = find(doc, id);
  return entry && entry.kind === kind ? (entry.item as ItemByKind[K]) : undefined;
}

/**
 * The stage an item sits in; a stage is its own stage. A "Starts when" is shown with the start
 * stage (its panel's "Also starts from"), so it counts as the start stage's: "Show me" on one of
 * its rows opens that panel.
 */
export function stageOf(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string): Stage | undefined {
  const entry = find(doc, id);
  if (!entry) return undefined;
  if (entry.kind === 'stage') return entry.item;
  if (entry.kind === 'startsWhen') return getStage(doc, doc.start?.stage);
  return getStage(doc, entry.parents.stage);
}

/** The task an item sits in; a task is its own task. */
export function taskOf(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string): Task | undefined {
  const entry = find(doc, id);
  if (!entry) return undefined;
  if (entry.kind === 'task') return entry.item;
  return getTask(doc, entry.parents.task);
}

export const getStage = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'stage');
export const getStatus = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'status');
export const getTask = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'task');
export const getPage = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'page');
export const getQuestion = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'question');
export const getButton = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'button');
export const getArrow = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'arrow');
export const getAction = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'action');
export const getValue = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'value');
export const getList = (doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined) => findOf(doc, id, 'list');

/** The stage if it is a working stage (not an ending). */
export function getWorkingStage(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string | null | undefined): WorkingStage | undefined {
  const stage = getStage(doc, id);
  return stage && stage.kind !== 'ending' ? stage : undefined;
}

/** The name a person knows an item by (stage name, button label, value name ...), '' when it has none. */
export function nameOf(entry: Entry): string {
  switch (entry.kind) {
    case 'stage':
    case 'value':
    case 'list':
    case 'column':
      return entry.item.name ?? '';
    case 'task':
      return entry.item.name ?? '';
    case 'question':
    case 'button':
    case 'choice':
      return entry.item.label ?? '';
    case 'page':
      return entry.item.title ?? '';
    case 'status':
    case 'thingTold':
      return entry.item.words ?? '';
    default:
      return '';
  }
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { WorkingStage } from '@/contract';
import { makeContext } from './commands/registry';
import { seededRandom } from './ids';
import { defaultStageName, presetStage, presetTask, uniqueName, type NewStageKind } from './presets';
import { fixture } from './testkit';

const build = (kind: NewStageKind, doc = fixture('blank')) => presetStage(doc, kind, makeContext(doc, seededRandom(5)));
const working = (kind: NewStageKind) => {

describe('presets', () => {
  it('Form: one Submit button with its own unfinished arrow', () => {

    expect(stage.kind).toBe('form');

    expect(stage.tasks[0]!.buttons.map((b) => [b.label, b.look])).toEqual([['Submit', 'primary']]);
    expect(stage.tasks[0]!.requesterCanAnswer).toBe(true);
    expect(stage.tasks[0]!.whoIsAsked).toBeUndefined();
    expect(stage.arrows).toEqual([{ id: expect.any(String), when: { type: 'buttonPressed', button: stage.tasks[0]!.buttons[0]!.id }, goTo: null }]);

  it('Approval: Approve / Reject, Reason needed to press Reject, requester cannot answer', () => {

    expect(statuses).toEqual([{ id: stage.status, words: 'Waiting for approval', colour: 'amber' }]);
  });

  it('Work: one Mark done button', () => {

===\nfrontend/src/model/presets.ts\n===
/**
 * What adding a stage of each kind creates (spec/editor-model.md section 3, "Presets fill this
 * anatomy"; the kind is "Kind (of stage)" on screen):
 *   Form       one task, one Submit button.
 *   Approval   one task, Approve / Reject; a Reason question needed to press Reject;
 *              "The requester can't answer their own request" on.
 *   Work       one task, one "Mark done" button.
 *   Automatic  no task; one "When done" arrow.
 *   Ending     status only: named after the ending, in a neutral colour (an existing status
 *              with those words is reused).
 *   Blank      everything empty: one task with nobody asked, an empty form (one page, no
 *              questions) and no buttons, so the panel shows the whole anatomy with "+ Add ..."
 *              lines and the stage can be told from an Automatic one; no arrows, no status.
 * A stage with buttons arrives with one arrow per button, going nowhere yet (a To do until a stage
 * is chosen). Statuses are reused when one with the same words exists (stages showing the same
 * words share one status), otherwise created. These functions build; they do not change the doc.
 */
import type {
  Arrow,
  AuthoredWorkflow,
  Button,
  ButtonId,
  Stage,
  Status,
  Task,
  Value,
  WorkingStageKind,
} from '@/contract';
import { t, type WordKey } from '@/words';
import type { CommandContext } from './commands/types';

export type NewStageKind = WorkingStageKind | 'ending';

/**
 * Words the presets put into the document. They are the author's data once created, but a person
 * reads them, so they belong in src/words (F5); kept here until a model words file exists.
 */
export const PRESET_WORDS = {
  submit: 'Submit',
  approve: 'Approve',
  reject: 'Reject',
  markDone: 'Mark done',
  reason: 'Reason',
  buttonPressed: '{name}: button pressed',
  answeredBy: '{name}: answered by',
} as const;

/**
 * The status each working kind starts with (words and colour); none for Blank. An ending's status
 * is named after the ending instead (`endingStatus`), in a neutral colour: a "Rejected" ending
 * shows "Rejected", never a green "Finished".
 */
export const PRESET_STATUS: Record<Exclude<NewStageKind, 'ending'>, Pick<Status, 'words' | 'colour'> | null> = {
  form: { words: 'Being filled in', colour: 'blue' },
  approval: { words: 'Waiting for approval', colour: 'amber' },
  work: { words: 'In progress', colour: 'purple' },
  automatic: { words: 'Happening by itself', colour: 'blue' },
  blank: null,
};

/** The neutral colour of a status made for a new ending (the author chooses another when it means something). */
export const ENDING_STATUS_COLOUR: Status['colour'] = 'grey';

/** The status a new ending called `name` starts with: its own name, in the neutral colour. */
export function endingStatus(name: string): Pick<Status, 'words' | 'colour'> | null {
  const words = name.trim();
  return words ? { words, colour: ENDING_STATUS_COLOUR } : null;
}

/** `base`, or `base 2`, `base 3` ... whichever is not in `taken` (compared ignoring case). */
export function uniqueName(base: string, taken: Iterable<string>): string {
  const lower = new Set([...taken].map((n) => n.trim().toLowerCase()));
  if (!lower.has(base.toLowerCase())) return base;
  for (let n = 2; ; n++) if (!lower.has(`${base} ${n}`.toLowerCase())) return `${base} ${n}`;
}

/** The kind's word, as the default name of a new stage ("Approval", "Approval 2"). */
export function defaultStageName(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, kind: NewStageKind): string {
  return uniqueName(t(`stageKind.${kind}` as WordKey), (doc.stages ?? []).map((s) => s.name ?? ''));
}

/** An arrow for a button: "When [button] is pressed go to [choose a stage]". */
export function buttonArrow(ctx: CommandContext, button: ButtonId, goTo: Arrow['goTo'] = null): Arrow {
  return { id: ctx.newId('ar'), when: { type: 'buttonPressed', button }, goTo };
}

export interface PresetTask {
  task: Task;
  /** Values the task's questions fill, to add to the registry. */
  values: Value[];
}

/** The task a Form, Approval, Work or Blank stage starts with; for Blank (and any other kind) an empty task with one page. */
export function presetTask(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, kind: NewStageKind, ctx: CommandContext): PresetTask {
  const page = { id: ctx.newId('pg'), items: [] as Task['form']['pages'][number]['items'] };
  const task: Task = {
    id: ctx.newId('tk'),
    groupRule: 'firstAnswerDecides',
    requesterCanAnswer: kind !== 'approval',
    form: { pages: [page] },
    buttons: [],
  };
  const values: Value[] = [];
  const button = (label: string, look: Button['look'], neededToPress: Button['neededToPress'] = []): Button => ({
    id: ctx.newId('btn'),
    label,
    look,
    neededToPress,
  });

  if (kind === 'form') task.buttons.push(button(PRESET_WORDS.submit, 'primary'));
  if (kind === 'work') task.buttons.push(button(PRESET_WORDS.markDone, 'primary'));
  if (kind === 'approval') {
    const value: Value = {
      id: ctx.newId('v'),
      name: uniqueName(PRESET_WORDS.reason, (doc.values ?? []).map((v) => v.name ?? '')),
    };
    const question = { type: 'question' as const, id: ctx.newId('q'), label: PRESET_WORDS.reason, kind: 'longText' as const, savedAs: value.id };
    page.items.push(question);
    values.push(value);
    task.buttons.push(button(PRESET_WORDS.approve, 'primary'), button(PRESET_WORDS.reject, 'danger', [question.id]));
  }
  return { task, values };
}

export interface PresetStage {
  stage: Stage;
  /** Values to add to the registry. */
  values: Value[];
  /** Statuses to add (empty when an existing one is reused). */
  statuses: Status[];
}

/** The status for a new stage of this kind: an existing one with the same words, or a new one. */
function presetStatus(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, kind: NewStageKind, ctx: CommandContext, name: string): { id?: Status['id']; created?: Status } {
  const wanted = kind === 'ending' ? endingStatus(name) : PRESET_STATUS[kind];
  if (!wanted) return {};
  const same = (doc.statuses ?? []).find((s) => (s.words ?? '').trim().toLowerCase() === wanted.words.toLowerCase());
  if (same) return { id: same.id };
  const created: Status = { id: ctx.newId('stat'), ...wanted };
  return { id: created.id, created };
}

/** A new stage of this kind, with its task, buttons, arrows, values and status. */
export function presetStage(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, kind: NewStageKind, ctx: CommandContext, name?: string): PresetStage {
  const id = ctx.newId('st');
  const stageName = name ?? defaultStageName(doc, kind);
  const status = presetStatus(doc, kind, ctx, stageName);
  const statuses = status.created ? [status.created] : [];

  if (kind === 'ending') {
    const stage: Stage = { id, kind: 'ending', name: stageName };
    if (status.id) stage.status = status.id;
    return { stage, values: [], statuses };
  }

  const stage: Stage = { id, kind, name: stageName, whenThisStageStarts: [], tasks: [], afterTheyRespond: [], arrows: [] };
  if (status.id) stage.status = status.id;
  let values: Value[] = [];
  if (kind === 'form' || kind === 'approval' || kind === 'work' || kind === 'blank') {
    const made = presetTask(doc, kind, ctx);
    stage.tasks.push(made.task);
    values = made.values;
    for (const button of made.task.buttons) stage.arrows.push(buttonArrow(ctx, button.id));
  }
  if (kind === 'automatic') stage.arrows.push({ id: ctx.newId('ar'), when: { type: 'whenDone' }, goTo: null });
  return { stage, values, statuses };
}
===\nfrontend/src/model/session/README.md\n===
# model/session

The open workflow: loading it into the editor store, autosave (F9), checking, Settings, publishing and "Show me". Everything here is exported from `@/model`. Screens never call `services.authoring` or `services.core.check` for the open workflow themselves; they use these.

Two stores hold the open workflow:

- the **editor store** (`useEditor`, `../store.ts`): the document, its revision, `saveState` ('saved' | 'unsaved' | 'saving' | 'conflict'), the selection, undo and redo. Read it with `useDoc()`, `useSaveState()`, `useSelection()`, `useStage(id)` ...; change the document only with `useRun()` / `useEditor.getState().run(name, args)`.
- the **session store** (`useSession`, `state.ts`): everything else, below. Written only by this folder.

`src/app/EditorLayout.tsx` opens the workflow named in the route and closes it on leaving, and shows the loading, "This workflow does not exist" and error states, so a screen inside the editor can assume `useSessionStatus() === 'ready'` and `useDoc()` is not null (still guard for null in code; it is null for one render in tests). It also owns the undo and redo keys (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y): they act only on the workflow on screen, never while typing in a text box and never while a dialog or popover is in front, so what a dialog says about the document stays true. Undo and redo themselves are `useEditor.getState().undo()` / `redo()` (`../store.ts`).

`useMay()` and everything the services answer depend on who is signed in (`services.session`). On the development host the app frame (not the editor) offers a person switcher; the editor reads `may` again each time it opens a workflow.

## Opening and closing

| Name | What | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `openWorkflow(services, workflowId)` | Loads the draft, Settings, catalogue and versions; `load`s the draft into the editor store; starts autosave and checking. Resolves when the document is in the store (or the status says why not). Opening the open workflow again returns the same promise; opening another closes the first; safe under StrictMode. | `useEffect(() => { void openWorkflow(services, id); return () => closeWorkflow(); }, [services, id]);` (the frame does this) |
| `closeWorkflow()` | Stops autosave and checking; saves a pending change in the background (the next open waits for it). | as above |
| `AUTOSAVE_QUIET_MS` (800), `CHECK_QUIET_MS` (150) | The quiet periods before a save and before a check. | `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(AUTOSAVE_QUIET_MS)` in a test |
| `SAVE_RETRY_MS` (5000) | A save that failed (not a conflict) is tried again by the session this long after, and again after each further failure, while nothing else changes. Screens need not retry. | `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(SAVE_RETRY_MS)` in a test |
| `resetSessionForTests()` | Forgets the open workflow without saving. Tests only. | `afterEach(() => resetSessionForTests())` |
| `sessionServices()` | The open workflow's services, or null. Rarely needed: prefer `useServices()` from `@/services`. | `sessionServices()?.core.evaluate(...)` |

## Status and data

| Hook | Gives | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `useSessionStatus()` | `'idle' \| 'loading' \| 'ready' \| 'notFound' \| 'error'` | `if (useSessionStatus() !== 'ready') return null;` |
| `useSessionWorkflowId()` | The server's workflow ID (for routes: `/w/${id}/...`), or null. Not the document's own `wf_` id. | `navigate(\`/w/${useSessionWorkflowId()}/try\`)` |
| `useSettings()` | `Settings` (name, description, authors, stuckRequestsGoTo) or null. | `const name = useSettings()?.name ?? ''` |
| `useMay()` | `{ edit, publish, settings }` for the signed-in person (all false until loaded). | `if (!useMay().edit) return <ReadOnlyView />` |
| `useCatalogue()` | The catalogue of connections, or null. | `entryOf(useCatalogue(), ref)` |
| `useVersions()` | `{ versions, live }`: versions newest first, `live` the live version's number or null. | `const { live } = useVersions(); live ? t('version.live', { n: live }) : t('version.notLiveYet')` |
| `useSaveFailure()` | Why the last save failed (`{ kind: 'refused', errors }` or `{ kind: 'unreachable' }`), or null. With `saveState === 'unsaved'`: say "Not saved". | `const failed = useSaveFailure() !== null` |

## Findings and facts

The check (`core.check`) and the facts (`core.facts`) run 150 ms after the document stops changing (and right after loading). They describe `useCheckedDoc()`, which can be a moment behind `useDoc()`.

| Hook / function | Gives | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `useFindings()` | Every `Finding`, document order. | `useFindings().filter((f) => f.severity === 'todo')` |
| `useTodoCount()`, `useWorthKnowingCount()` | The counts (numbers; cheap). | `t('todo.button', { n: useTodoCount() })` |
| `useFindingsFor(itemId, { deep })` | The findings at that item; with `deep: true` also at everything inside it (a stage's tasks, actions, arrows, pages, questions, buttons; a list's columns and rows). To do first, then Worth knowing. Stable array. | `const strip = useFindingsFor(stageId, { deep: true })` |
| `findingsFor(findings, doc, itemId, deep?)` | The same, as a pure function. | in tests and selectors |
| `useCheckedDoc()`, `useCheckIsCurrent()` | The document the findings were worked out for; false while they are a moment behind. | `<p aria-busy={!useCheckIsCurrent()}>` |
| `useFacts()` | `Facts` (stages, arrows, values) or null. | `useFacts()?.values[valueId]?.usedAt.length` |
| `useStageFacts(stageId)` | `{ incoming, reachable }` or undefined. | `useStageFacts(id)?.incoming.map(...)` ("Reached from") |
| `useArrowFacts(arrowId)` | `{ usable, sendsBack, reason?, earlier? }` or undefined. | `useArrowFacts(id)?.sendsBack` ("sends it back") |
| `useValuesInScope(at)` | `{ loading, values }`: `core.valuesInScope` at a `Location`, cached per document object (many components asking about one place cost one call). While loading, `values` is the last answer for that place. `at` may be null. | `const { values } = useValuesInScope({ item: stageId, part: 'tasks' })` |

## Words

| Hook | Gives | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `useDescribeEnv()` | The one `env` every describe function takes. Today `{ catalogue }`: the describe functions read nothing else from outside the document (directory names and the sample request are in the document). Stable. | `toText(describeArrow(doc, arrow, useDescribeEnv()))` |
| `useDirectoryLabel(ref)` | The directory's display name for a `{ type, id }` reference (`directory.lookup`, asked once per page), or undefined until known. Needs a `ServicesProvider` above (the app has one). | `useDirectoryLabel(settings.stuckRequestsGoTo?.[0]) ?? '...'` |
| `useStuckPeople()` | Everyone in "Stuck requests go to" (the authors when none is set) as `StuckPerson[]`, by directory name, groups marked; someone whose name is not known yet is left out until it is. Stable. For `describeStuckTold` and `FindingEnv.stuckPeople`. | `describeFinding(doc, f, { ...env, stuckPeople: useStuckPeople() })` |

## Actions

| Name | What | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `flushSave()` | Saves a pending change now; resolves when every save has settled. | `await flushSave();` before leaving for Try it |
| `reloadDraft()` | Loads the server's current draft into the editor (the author's unsaved edits are lost: say so first) and starts saving again after a conflict. `Promise<Result<void>>`. | `if (saveState === 'conflict') ... onClick={() => void reloadDraft()}` |
| `saveSettings(next)` | Replaces the Settings record; updates `useSettings()` (the record as read back, a `SettingsRead`: also `changedBy` and `changedAt`). `Promise<Result<Settings>>`; refusals, in the server's order: `forbidden`, `invalid-body` (`/stuckRequestsGoTo`, `empty`: "Stuck requests go to" may not be emptied), `last-author`; also `not-found`, `membership-unavailable`. | `await saveSettings({ ...settings, stuckRequestsGoTo: [ref] })` |
| `renameWorkflow(name)` | `saveSettings` with a new name. Not an edit to the document, so not undoable. | `await renameWorkflow(text)` |
| `publish()` | Saves first, then publishes that revision with the browser core's version; refreshes `useVersions()`. Returns `Result<PublishResult>`: `{ ok: true, value: { version, findings } }` or the refusal (`core-version-mismatch`, `stale-revision`, `has-todo` with the server's findings, `forbidden`, `not-found`, `membership-unavailable`; a failed save is returned as its own refusal, so an older draft is never published). | `const r = await publish(); if (r.ok) setPublished(r.value.version); else setRefusal(r.errors[0])` |
| `reveal(location)` | "Show me": selects the location in the editor store and records `{ location, nonce }`. The frame navigates (a stage, task, arrow, action, status, Starts when, thing told: Diagram tab; a page, question, text, choice or button: the form editor of its stage and task, `/w/<id>/form/<stage>/<task>`; a value, list, column or row: Values tab). An item that no longer exists goes to the Diagram tab. | `<Button onClick={() => reveal(finding.location)}>{showMeWords}</Button>` |
| `openSettings()` | Opens the workflow's Settings (the top bar's popover), for the "Settings" link part of a sentence (`isSettingsLink`). False when nothing on screen can open it (outside the editor). `canOpenSettings()` says whether it can; `setSettingsOpener(fn)` is how the editor's frame says how (it returns the function that takes it back). | `isSettingsLink(part) ? <button onClick={() => openSettings()}>{part.text}</button> : ...` |
| `useRevealRequest()` | The last reveal request `{ location, nonce }` or null. The screen that shows the item scrolls it into view and flashes it when `nonce` changes and the item is its own. | `useEffect(() => { if (req?.location.item === id) ref.current?.scrollIntoView(); }, [req?.nonce])` |
| `revealTarget(doc, location)`, `revealPath(workflowId, target)` | Which view shows a location (`{ view: 'diagram' \| 'values' } \| { view: 'form', stageId, taskId }`), and its route. | used by the frame |

## Autosave, exactly

- An edit, undo or redo marks the store 'unsaved'. After 800 ms without another change the draft is saved (`authoring.saveDraft` with the revision): 'saving', then 'saved' with the new revision.
- A change made while a save is in flight is saved right after it (the state stays 'unsaved' until then).
- Undoing back to exactly what was saved needs no save: the state goes back to 'saved'.
- `stale-revision` (someone else saved): 'conflict', and nothing is saved until `reloadDraft()`; further edits keep 'conflict'.
- Any other failure: 'unsaved' and `useSaveFailure()` is set; the next change tries again; a good save clears it.
- The page being hidden or closed (`visibilitychange`, `pagehide`) and `closeWorkflow()` save at once. (A browser shut down by a test tool, such as Playwright's `context.close()` on a persistent context, fires neither, so a change from the last 800 ms is not saved there; closing a tab or leaving the page does fire `pagehide`.)
- Read only: when the signed-in person may not change the workflow (`useMay().edit` false on opening, or a save refused `forbidden`), the session makes the editor store refuse every `run` (refused `notFound`, as when nothing is open), `undo` and `redo` (`./readOnly.ts`), and nothing is saved or tried again. The frame shows "Read only" in place of undo and the save state, and a line under the bar saying why. Screens should still hide or disable their own edit controls when `!useMay().edit`.

## Tests

`session.test.ts` (in-memory stand-in from `createStandinServices()`, fake timers): load, not found, error, StrictMode open-close-open, debounce and revision, a change during a save, conflict and reload, other failures, flush, close, page hide, publish, checking with stale results dropped, `findingsFor` deep, reveal (and which view each kind of item goes to). The frame's own behaviour (undo keys and dialogs, reveal navigation, the top bar) is tested in `src/app/EditorLayout.test.tsx`, `src/app/topBarFit.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/boot.spec.ts`, `tests/e2e/topbar.spec.ts`.
===\nfrontend/src/model/session/caches.ts\n===
/**
 * Small caches behind the session hooks, read with useSyncExternalStore so that many components can
 * ask for the same thing cheaply and get the same object back:
 *  - values in scope at a location, per document object (a new document asks again; until the
 *    answer comes, the last answer for that location is shown with `loading: true`);
 *  - directory names, per reference, for the life of the page.
 */
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, Catalogue, Location } from '@/contract';
import type { Ref, Services, ValueInScope } from '@/services/types';

type Listener = () => void;

function emitter() {
  const listeners = new Set<Listener>();
  return {
    subscribe(listener: Listener) {
      listeners.add(listener);
      return () => {
        listeners.delete(listener);
      };
    },
    emit() {
      for (const l of [...listeners]) l();
    },
  };
}

// ── Values in scope ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface ValuesInScopeResult {
  /** True until the core has answered for the current document. */
  loading: boolean;
  /** The values that exist there; while loading, the last answer for the same place (or none). */
  values: ValueInScope[];
}

const NO_VALUES: ValueInScope[] = [];
export const IDLE_SCOPE: ValuesInScopeResult = { loading: false, values: NO_VALUES };

interface ScopeEntry {
  snap: ValuesInScopeResult;
  started: boolean;
}

const scopeByDoc = new WeakMap<AuthoredWorkflow, Map<string, ScopeEntry>>();
const latestScope = new Map<string, ValueInScope[]>();
const scopeEvents = emitter();

export const subscribeScope = scopeEvents.subscribe;

export const scopeKey = (at: Location): string => `${at.item}#${at.part ?? ''}`;

function scopeEntry(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, key: string): ScopeEntry {
  let byKey = scopeByDoc.get(doc);
  if (!byKey) {
    byKey = new Map();
    scopeByDoc.set(doc, byKey);
  }
  let entry = byKey.get(key);
  if (!entry) {
    entry = { snap: { loading: true, values: latestScope.get(key) ?? NO_VALUES }, started: false };
    byKey.set(key, entry);
  }
  return entry;
}

/** The current answer for (doc, at): a stable object until the answer changes. */
export function scopeSnapshot(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, at: Location): ValuesInScopeResult {
  return scopeEntry(doc, scopeKey(at)).snap;
}

/** Asks the core once per (document, location). */
export function fetchScope(services: Services, catalogue: Catalogue, doc: AuthoredWorkflow, at: Location): void {
  const key = scopeKey(at);
  const entry = scopeEntry(doc, key);
  if (entry.started) return;
  entry.started = true;
  services.core.valuesInScope(doc, catalogue, at).then(
    (values) => {
      entry.snap = { loading: false, values };
      latestScope.set(key, values);
      scopeEvents.emit();
    },
    () => {
      entry.snap = { loading: false, values: entry.snap.values };
      scopeEvents.emit();
    },
  );
}

/** Forgets the last answers (on opening another workflow). */
export function clearScopeCache(): void {
  latestScope.clear();
}

// ── Directory names ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const labels = new Map<string, string>();
const asked = new Set<string>();
const labelEvents = emitter();

export const subscribeLabels = labelEvents.subscribe;
export const refKey = (ref: Ref): string => `${ref.type}:${ref.id}`;
export const labelOf = (key: string): string | undefined => labels.get(key);

/** Looks a reference up once per page; a failed lookup is asked again on the next call. */
export function fetchLabel(services: Services, ref: Ref): void {
  const key = refKey(ref);
  if (asked.has(key)) return;
  asked.add(key);
  services.directory.lookup([{ type: ref.type, id: ref.id }]).then(
    (entries) => {
      const found = entries.find((e) => e.type === ref.type && e.id === ref.id) ?? entries[0];
      if (found) {
        labels.set(key, found.label);
        labelEvents.emit();
      } else {
        asked.delete(key);
      }
    },
    () => {
      asked.delete(key);
    },
  );
}
