===\nfrontend/src/model/walk.ts\n===
/**
 * Walking the document's expressions and references.
 *  - `eachExpression`: every slot holding an Expression, Condition, Template or Sent* expression,
 *    with its Location (authored-format.ts, Location) and the item that owns it.
 *  - `allReferences` / `referencesTo`: every place that points at an ID (value chips, formula
 *    `{{chips}}`, goTo, buttons, questions, statuses, lists, columns, rows, choices, things told,
 *    the places that fill a value, sample answers, diagram positions).
 *  - `fillSites`: the places that fill a value. `usedIn`: the distinct items that read it
 *    ("Used in N places", the format's Value doc comment).
 * Every location follows the contract's LOCATION_PARTS (an arrow's sentence at `when.condition`,
 * its button at `when.button`, a list choice at `choices.list` / `choices.shownColumn`), except the
 * two workflow-level places only the editor reports: `sampleRequest.answers.<value>` and
 * `diagram.positions.<stage>` (paths by the same rule, never in a finding).
 */
import { isDraft } from 'immer';
import type { AuthoredWorkflow, ItemKind, Location, ValueId } from '@/contract';

/** What sort of thing a slot holds. A slot that takes "expression or template" reports which it holds. */
export type SlotSort = 'expression' | 'condition' | 'template' | 'sentExpression' | 'sentCondition' | 'sentTemplate';

export interface Owner {
  id: string;
  kind: ItemKind;
}

export interface SlotVisit {
  location: Location;
  owner: Owner;
  sort: SlotSort;
}

/** How a reference points at its target. The fill kinds are the places that fill a value. */
export type RefHow =
  | 'value' // { value: id } in an expression or template
  | 'chip' // {{id}} inside formula text
  | 'savedAs'
  | 'saveAs'
  | 'saveResults'
  | 'saveFailureAs'
  | 'savesButtonPressedAs'
  | 'savesAnsweredByAs'
  | 'goTo'
  | 'startStage'
  | 'position'
  | 'pressed'
  | 'buttonConstant'
  | 'arrowButton'
  | 'bindingButton'
  | 'neededToPress'
  | 'bindingAnswer'
  | 'status'
  | 'ifSentBackStatus'
  | 'list'
  | 'column'
  | 'cell'
  | 'row'
  | 'choice'
  | 'told'
  | 'sampleAnswer';

export const FILL_HOWS: ReadonlySet<RefHow> = new Set<RefHow>([
  'savedAs',
  'saveAs',
  'saveResults',
  'saveFailureAs',
  'savesButtonPressedAs',
  'savesAnsweredByAs',
]);

export interface Reference {
  target: string;
  how: RefHow;
  location: Location;
  owner: Owner;
}

type Visit = (node: unknown, at: SlotVisit) => void;

const loc = (item: string, part?: string): Location => (part === undefined ? { item } : { item, part });

function sortOf(node: unknown, single: SlotSort, many: SlotSort): SlotSort {
  return Array.isArray(node) ? many : single;
}

/**
 * Calls `visit` for every expression slot in the document, in document order: bindings, then each
 * stage's "When this stage starts", tasks (who is asked, pages, questions, text, buttons),
 * "After they respond", arrows. Absent slots are skipped.
 */
export function eachExpression(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, visit: Visit): void {
  const at = (owner: Owner, part: string, sort: SlotSort, node: unknown) => {
    if (node !== undefined && node !== null) visit(node, { location: loc(owner.id, part), owner, sort });
  };

  for (const sw of doc.start?.startsWhen ?? []) {
    const owner: Owner = { id: sw.id, kind: 'startsWhen' };
    at(owner, 'onlyWhen', 'sentCondition', sw.onlyWhen);
    at(owner, 'requester', 'sentExpression', sw.requester);
    for (const [question, answer] of Object.entries(sw.answers ?? {})) {
      at(owner, `answers.${question}`, sortOf(answer, 'sentExpression', 'sentTemplate'), answer);
    }
  }

  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    const actions = (list: typeof stage.whenThisStageStarts) => {
      for (const action of list ?? []) {
        const owner: Owner = { id: action.id, kind: 'action' };
        at(owner, 'onlyWhen', 'condition', action.onlyWhen);
        switch (action.type) {
          case 'saveValue':
            at(owner, 'save', 'expression', action.save);
            break;
          case 'notify':
            at(owner, 'to', 'expression', action.to);
            at(owner, 'message', 'template', action.message);
            break;
          case 'useConnection':
            for (const [key, input] of Object.entries(action.inputs ?? {})) {
              at(owner, `inputs.${key}`, sortOf(input, 'expression', 'template'), input);
            }
            break;
          case 'tellOtherSystems':
            for (const [key, input] of Object.entries(action.values ?? {})) {
              at(owner, `values.${key}`, sortOf(input, 'expression', 'template'), input);
            }
            break;
        }
      }
    };

    actions(stage.whenThisStageStarts);
    for (const task of stage.tasks ?? []) {
      at({ id: task.id, kind: 'task' }, 'whoIsAsked', 'expression', task.whoIsAsked);
      for (const page of task.form?.pages ?? []) {
        at({ id: page.id, kind: 'page' }, 'showWhen', 'condition', page.showWhen);
        for (const item of page.items ?? []) {
          if (item.type === 'text') {
            const owner: Owner = { id: item.id, kind: 'text' };
            at(owner, 'content', 'template', item.content);
            at(owner, 'showWhen', 'condition', item.showWhen);
            continue;
          }
          const owner: Owner = { id: item.id, kind: 'question' };
          const choices = item.choices;
          if (choices?.from === 'directory') at(owner, 'choices.peopleIn', 'expression', choices.peopleIn);
          if (choices?.from === 'source') {
            for (const [key, input] of Object.entries(choices.inputs ?? {})) {
              at(owner, `choices.inputs.${key}`, sortOf(input, 'expression', 'template'), input);
            }
          }
          if (choices?.from === 'formula') at(owner, 'choices.formula', 'expression', choices.formula);
          at(owner, 'showWhen', 'condition', item.showWhen);
        }
      }
      for (const button of task.buttons ?? []) {
        at({ id: button.id, kind: 'button' }, 'enabledWhen', 'condition', button.enabledWhen);
      }
    }
    actions(stage.afterTheyRespond);
    for (const arrow of stage.arrows ?? []) {
      const owner: Owner = { id: arrow.id, kind: 'arrow' };
      if (arrow.when?.type === 'condition') at(owner, 'when.condition', 'condition', arrow.when.condition);
      at(owner, 'onlyWhen', 'condition', arrow.onlyWhen);
    }
  }
}

const CHIP = /\{\{\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\}\}/g;

/** The value IDs written as `{{id}}` chips in formula text (not request.* or sent.* chips). */
export function chipsIn(formula: string): string[] {
  return [...formula.matchAll(CHIP)].map((m) => m[1] as string);
}

const isString = (x: unknown): x is string => typeof x === 'string';

/** Every reference inside an expression-like node. Clauses of a top-level sentence get their index. */
function scanNode(node: unknown, part: string, emit: (target: string, how: RefHow, part: string) => void): void {
  if (node && typeof node === 'object' && !Array.isArray(node)) {
    const clauses = (node as { allOf?: unknown; anyOf?: unknown }).allOf ?? (node as { anyOf?: unknown }).anyOf;
    if (Array.isArray(clauses)) {
      clauses.forEach((clause, i) => deepScan(clause, `${part}.${i}`, emit));
      return;
    }
  }
  deepScan(node, part, emit);
}

function deepScan(node: unknown, part: string, emit: (target: string, how: RefHow, part: string) => void): void {
  if (Array.isArray(node)) {
    for (const child of node) deepScan(child, part, emit);
    return;
  }
  if (!node || typeof node !== 'object') return;
  const o = node as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (isString(o.value)) emit(o.value, 'value', part);
  if (isString(o.pressed)) emit(o.pressed, 'pressed', part);
  if (isString(o.button)) emit(o.button, 'buttonConstant', part);
  if (isString(o.choice)) emit(o.choice, 'choice', part);
  if (Array.isArray(o.choices) && o.choices.every(isString)) for (const c of o.choices) emit(c, 'choice', part);
  if (isString(o.row)) emit(o.row, 'row', part);
  if (isString(o.column)) emit(o.column, 'column', part);
  if (isString(o.formula)) for (const chip of chipsIn(o.formula)) emit(chip, 'chip', part);
  for (const child of Object.values(o)) if (child && typeof child === 'object') deepScan(child, part, emit);
}

function collectReferences(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): Reference[] {
  const refs: Reference[] = [];
  const add = (target: string | null | undefined, how: RefHow, owner: Owner, part?: string) => {
    if (isString(target)) refs.push({ target, how, owner, location: loc(owner.id, part) });
  };
  const workflow: Owner = { id: doc.id, kind: 'workflow' };

  // Inside expressions.
  eachExpression(doc, (node, { location, owner }) => {
    scanNode(node, location.part ?? '', (target, how, part) => add(target, how, owner, part));
  });

  add(doc.start?.stage, 'startStage', workflow, 'start.stage');
  for (const sw of doc.start?.startsWhen ?? []) {
    const owner: Owner = { id: sw.id, kind: 'startsWhen' };
    add(sw.button, 'bindingButton', owner, 'button');
    for (const question of Object.keys(sw.answers ?? {})) add(question, 'bindingAnswer', owner, `answers.${question}`);
  }

  for (const stage of doc.stages ?? []) {
    const stageOwner: Owner = { id: stage.id, kind: 'stage' };
    add(stage.status, 'status', stageOwner, 'status');
    if (stage.kind === 'ending') continue;
    add(stage.ifSentBackStatus, 'ifSentBackStatus', stageOwner, 'ifSentBackStatus');
    for (const action of [...(stage.whenThisStageStarts ?? []), ...(stage.afterTheyRespond ?? [])]) {
      const owner: Owner = { id: action.id, kind: 'action' };
      if (action.type === 'saveValue') add(action.as, 'saveAs', owner, 'as');
      if (action.type === 'tellOtherSystems') add(action.tell, 'told', owner, 'tell');
      if (action.type === 'useConnection') {
        for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(action.saveResults ?? {})) add(value, 'saveResults', owner, `saveResults.${key}`);
        add(action.saveFailureAs?.failed, 'saveFailureAs', owner, 'saveFailureAs.failed');
        add(action.saveFailureAs?.code, 'saveFailureAs', owner, 'saveFailureAs.code');
      }
    }
    for (const task of stage.tasks ?? []) {
      const owner: Owner = { id: task.id, kind: 'task' };
      add(task.savesButtonPressedAs, 'savesButtonPressedAs', owner, 'savesButtonPressedAs');
      add(task.savesAnsweredByAs, 'savesAnsweredByAs', owner, 'savesAnsweredByAs');
      for (const page of task.form?.pages ?? []) {
        for (const item of page.items ?? []) {
          if (item.type !== 'question') continue;
          const q: Owner = { id: item.id, kind: 'question' };
          add(item.savedAs, 'savedAs', q, 'savedAs');
          if (item.choices?.from === 'list') {
            add(item.choices.list, 'list', q, 'choices.list');
            add(item.choices.shownColumn, 'column', q, 'choices.shownColumn');
          }
        }
      }
      for (const button of task.buttons ?? []) {
        for (const question of button.neededToPress ?? []) add(question, 'neededToPress', { id: button.id, kind: 'button' }, 'neededToPress');
      }
    }
    for (const arrow of stage.arrows ?? []) {
      const owner: Owner = { id: arrow.id, kind: 'arrow' };
      add(arrow.goTo, 'goTo', owner, 'goTo');
      if (arrow.when?.type === 'buttonPressed') add(arrow.when.button, 'arrowButton', owner, 'when.button');
    }
  }

  for (const list of doc.lists ?? []) {
    for (const row of list.rows ?? []) {
      const owner: Owner = { id: row.id, kind: 'row' };
      for (const [column, cell] of Object.entries(row.cells ?? {})) {
        add(column, 'cell', owner, `cells.${column}`);
        deepScan(cell, `cells.${column}`, (target, how, part) => add(target, how, owner, part));
      }
    }
  }

  for (const [value, answer] of Object.entries(doc.sampleRequest?.answers ?? {})) {
    const part = `sampleRequest.answers.${value}`;
    add(value, 'sampleAnswer', workflow, part);
    deepScan(answer, part, (target, how, p) => add(target, how, workflow, p));
  }
  for (const stage of Object.keys(doc.diagram?.positions ?? {})) add(stage, 'position', workflow, `diagram.positions.${stage}`);

  return refs;
}

const refCache = new WeakMap<AuthoredWorkflow, Reference[]>();

/** Every reference in the document. Memoised for finished documents. */
export function allReferences(doc: AuthoredWorkflow): Reference[] {
  if (isDraft(doc)) return collectReferences(doc);
  let refs = refCache.get(doc);
  if (!refs) {
    refs = collectReferences(doc);
    refCache.set(doc, refs);
  }
  return refs;
}

/** Every place that refers to `id`, including the places that fill it if it is a value. */
export function referencesTo(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, id: string): Reference[] {
  return allReferences(doc).filter((r) => r.target === id);
}

/** The places that fill a value (Question.savedAs, SaveValue.as, results, failure, a task's extra answers). */
export function fillSites(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, valueId: ValueId | string): Reference[] {
  return referencesTo(doc, valueId).filter((r) => FILL_HOWS.has(r.how));
}

/** The distinct items that read a value (chips and formula chips, not fills). "Used in N places" is its length. */
export function usedIn(doc: AuthoredWorkflow, valueId: ValueId | string): Owner[] {
  const seen = new Map<string, Owner>();
  for (const r of referencesTo(doc, valueId)) {
    if ((r.how === 'value' || r.how === 'chip') && !seen.has(r.owner.id)) seen.set(r.owner.id, r.owner);
  }
  return [...seen.values()];
}

# Services interface: contract notes

Frontend, 2026-11-16. Since the real core arrived, every type `@workflow/core` exports is core's own, re-exported by `src/services/types-*.ts` (README.md, "Types"); the shapes are core's as built, which `contract/core-api.md` describes (Draft 3 after E-27 and E-28). `authoring-api.md` and `runtime-api.md` (the server, not built yet) are still typed here by hand. This file lists only what still differs from the contract on purpose, what the contract leaves open, and the questions that are still open. The earlier rounds are answered in `contract/CHANGES-draft2.md` section (a).

## Different from the contract on purpose

| # | What | Contract | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every function is async; the client omits `caller`. `CoreService` wraps core's synchronous functions in promises, unchanged otherwise. | core 1, runtime 1.1, authoring 1 | F4: the interface can move into a worker or behind a server. The host supplies `Caller`. |
| 2 | `TestHost` (types-testhost.ts) is core's `TestHost` with each answer in a promise, nothing else: `request` answers core's `{ ok: false, refusals: [not-found] }` for a request the host does not hold (narrow on `"ok" in result`). `HostResult` holds this async host; `core.ts` makes it over core's `createTestHost`. `types.test.ts` checks it against core's. | core 10.2 | The interface is async (F4). |
| 3 | `Result<T, E = ApiError>`: core's `Result<T>` with a second parameter. | core 2.6 | The inbound endpoint for other systems has its own errors (`InboundError`); `Result<T>` is exactly core's (`types.test.ts`). |
| 4 | `SessionService.whoAmI()` and `people()` return the value, not `Result`. | runtime 7 | They fail only when the call cannot be made. `signInAs` keeps its `Result`. |
| 5 | `getCatalogue` is `CatalogueService.getCatalogue`, not on `AuthoringService`. | authoring 5, op. 11 | The `Services` object keeps its `catalogue` member. |
| 6 | `CoreService.formulaFunctions()` gives core's `FORMULA_FUNCTIONS` (`FormulaFunctionEntry[]`, each with its one-line `meaning`). | core 6.4 (a constant) | A constant does not cross an async interface. |
| 7 | `CoreService.upgrade` is core's `upgrade` (E-31). | core 13 | While authored format 0 is the only version it returns the document unchanged. |
| 8 | `RequestRow.stuck` is `ListedStuck` = `Omit<Stuck, 'admin'>`. | runtime 6.2 | The type says what the comment says. |
| 9 | `RefusedStart` and `InboundProblem` are coded unions over the six "Starts when" refusal codes (`StartsWhenRefusalCode`), params typed as in core's `ApiErrorParams`. | runtime 5.4, 8 (`code: string`) | One renderer words them. |
| 10 | `InboundError` (the inbound endpoint's `{ "error": code }`) is a coded record, so `dev.sendSample` can return `Result<InboundAnswer, InboundError>`. | runtime 8 | One failure shape. |
| 11 | `BuiltInMessageParams` is core's three (`task.assigned`, `request.stuck`, `start.refused`) plus the `alert.*` keys of `contract/words/notifications.json`, with params chosen here (Open 1). The outbox's `BuiltInMessage` is core's. | core 10.3 | The words file has all keys; only the alert sender sends the alerts. |
| 12 | `Services.dev?: DevService` with `sendSample(entry, sent?)`: one trigger event delivered as another system would, answered with the inbound endpoint's `InboundAnswer`. | none | Development host only. |
| 13 | Names for parts of core's types (derived from them, so they cannot drift): `ApiErrorCode`, `TaskEndState`, `NotFoundWhat`, `InvalidBodyProblem`, `ChoicesFrom`, `ChangeCode`, `StoryCode`, `RetryableStuckReason`, `ListedStuck`, `CallFailure`, `TryItMessageCode`; and `FormRequestFacts` (`formState`'s `request`), `Redacted` (the erasure marker), which core does not name. | | Callers need to name them. |
| 14 | Per-operation code unions: `StartRefusalCode`, `ActRefusalCode`, `AdminRefusalCode`, `ButtonRefusalCode`, `StartsWhenRefusalCode`, `TryAgainCode`. | runtime 3.3, 4.3, 5.1, 5.4 | Documentation types; refusal lists stay `ApiError[]`. |
| 15 | `RuntimeService.myTasks(args?)`: `args` optional. | runtime 1.1 | Every field of `PageArgs` is optional. |
| 16 | `InboundAnswer` keeps `eventId: string \| null`, `where: Location \| null` and a numeric `readableId`. | runtime 8 | Other systems hold that shape; nowhere else is there a `null`. |
| 17 | `RuntimeService.whilePaused` (`kept` / `refused`) says what a paused "Starts when" does with what is sent; `RefusedStart.code` adds `paused` (E-33). The stand-in keeps and runs again on Resume; the server refuses and lists. | runtime 5.3, 5.4 | Screens word a pause as the engine they talk to runs it. |
| 18 | `DevService` gains optional members: `canSendSample`, `sampleFields`, `engineAddress`, `resetSampleData`, `addSampleRequests`, `mocks`. Over HTTP `answerWaiting` is refused `not-found` (`call`): the mocks answer by themselves. | none | Development host only; screens show what the services offer. |

What is no longer here: the frontend's own `code: 'unknown'` member of every coded union. The browser runs core itself, so every code it reports is one this build was compiled against: `FindingCode` and the other code unions are core's, `describeFinding` has words for exactly core's finding codes (a new code fails to compile, `src/model/describe/finding.test.ts`), and the server's findings come from a core of the same version (publishing is refused on `core-version-mismatch`).

## Left open by the contract (choice made here)

1. **Alert params.** `notifications.json` names the placeholders; core 10.3 says they are filled "from the alert's subject" with no data shape. Chosen: the subject by ID (`workflow`, `request`, `stage`, `action`, `entry`, `connection`, `version`, `subscription`, and for `alert.inbound-refused` `code: InboundErrorCode`).
2. **`task.assigned` params.** Taken: core's `{ stage, task, askedOf }`; `{request}` and `{workflow}` come from the records.
3. **`TestHost.choices` for an unknown question** answers `{ choices: [] }`, as core's host does; core-api.md 10.2 says "any other question gives `{ choices: [] }`".
4. **The `stuck` story entry repeats `at` and `location`** (its params are a whole `Stuck`). Screens read the entry's.
5. **Two "kind conflict" shapes** (`ValueFacts.kind` `{ kind, at }[]`, `ValueInScope.kind` `ValueKind[]`). As core has them.
6. **`stale-revision`'s `draft`** is core's `Draft` (E-32); `Draft` is re-exported from core, so no cast is needed.
7. **Choices `limit`** at most 100 (runtime 3.4), `PageArgs.limit` at most 200 (runtime 1.1): `ChoicesArgs` has its own.
8. **`OpenAction.admin`** is live only and `ButtonState` may hold `membership-unavailable`, which Try it never gives: one type for both.
9. **`dev.sendSample`'s `sent`** is `Record<string, unknown>` where `evaluateSent` and `TestHost.startFrom` take `Record<string, Json>`: the mock system may send what the connector has not read yet.
10. **The contract's types are checked against core's.** `src/contract` re-exports the repo's `contract/authored-format.ts` and `catalogue.ts` (with their constants, which core does not re-export); `types.test.ts` checks that each of those types and core's type of the same name are assignable both ways, so the repo's files and core's synced copy cannot drift apart unnoticed. `finding.test.ts` checks that the finding codes of `core-api.md` section 4 are exactly core's.

## Questions for the engine owner

1. Are the `alert.*` params of Open 1 what the alert sender will hold, or names already resolved?
2. Should `TestHost.choices` answer `not-found` (`question`) like the server instead of `{ choices: [] }` (Open 3)?
3. Will the mock system's "pretend this was sent now" answer with the inbound endpoint's `InboundAnswer` (and `{ "error": code }`), so `dev.sendSample` maps onto it unchanged?
4. `task.assigned` goes to everyone asked, so with "The requester can't answer their own request" a requester in the asked group is told they have something to do. Should the notifier leave the Requester out when the task's rule excludes them?
5. A "Starts when" answer filled from a sent choice field into a typed-in or list choice question can never be one of the `ch_` or `row_` IDs the compiled schema expects, so every such start is refused `invalid-data` / `not-a-choice`, and `check` says nothing beforehand. Is a translation meant (by label, or a mapping the author writes), or which finding should `check` raise (proposed: a To do `startsWhen.choicesDoNotMatch` at `answers.<question>`)?

# services

The one async interface between the frontend and the engine side (docs/08-frontend-design.md, F4), matching `contract/core-api.md`, `authoring-api.md`, `runtime-api.md` and `catalogue.ts`.

- `types.ts` is the interface: `Services` = `core`, `authoring`, `runtime`, `catalogue`, `directory`, `session`, and `dev?` (the development host only). It re-exports every type of the `types-*.ts` files, so callers import from `@/services`.
- `core` is the engine's real core, `@workflow/core` (`core.ts`). Everything about a server (drafts, versions, requests, tasks across requests) has two implementations: the in-browser stand-in (`standin/`, the default) and the engine's server over HTTP (`http/`), chosen in `index.ts` by `VITE_ENGINE_URL` (frontend/README.md, "Two modes"). Only this folder knows which one runs: where they behave differently, the interface says so (`RuntimeService.whilePaused`; the optional members of `DevService`), and screens read that, never the variable.
- Only this folder imports `@workflow/core`, and only its root entry (never `@workflow/core/kernel`, never a deep path): `npm run lint` enforces it. Everything else goes through this interface and the types re-exported here (`@/services`) or in `@/contract`.
- Screens never call `fetch` themselves; they go through `model` or this interface.
- May import: `contract` and `@workflow/core`. Never `ui`, `features`, `model` or `app`.

## How core is linked

Core is consumed as TypeScript source, so no build of the engine is needed and nothing is written in `../engine` (engine/README-dev.md, "How another package consumes core"):

- `package.json`: `"@workflow/core": "file:../engine/packages/core"`. `npm install` links the folder into `node_modules/@workflow/core`; core's own dependencies (the CEL library, RE2) resolve from `../engine/node_modules`, which the engine owner installs.
- Core's package exports put the condition `workflow-source` first (`./src/index.ts`). `vite.config.ts` sets `resolve.conditions: ['workflow-source', ...defaultClientConditions]` and `ssr.resolve.conditions: ['workflow-source', ...defaultServerConditions]` (dev, build and Vitest share the file), and lets the dev server read `../engine/packages/core` and `../engine/node_modules` (`server.fs.allow`). `tsconfig.json` sets `"customConditions": ["workflow-source"]` and `"allowImportingTsExtensions": true` (core's source imports `./x.ts`).
- `tsc` type-checks core's source with the frontend's options, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` included (core compiles with them too). Unused names are tsc's alone: ESLint's `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` is off, so nothing is reported twice (a parameter starting with `_` may stay unused).
- A change in `../engine/packages/core/src` is picked up by the dev server (restart it after the Vite config changes) and by the next `npm run test` / `npm run build`.

**Which core runs:** `coreVersion` (exported here; also `core.meta()`, `meta.coreVersion`) is core's package version. The development build shows it in the app frame's footer beside "Reset sample data" ("Core 0.0.0"); the stand-in's published versions record it too.

## Types

Every type core exports is core's own, re-exported: the shared types (`Json`, `Ref`, `By`, the IDs, `Answers`, `Values`, `ConnectionChoice`, `ChoiceOption`, `Coded`, `TurnResult`, `FormulaRange`), errors and refusals (`ApiError`, `ApiErrorParams`, `Refusal`, `InvalidDataRule`, `ExpressionErrorKind`), findings, parse problems and changes, the results of every core function (`ParseResult`, `Facts`, `ValueInScope`, `FormulaResult`, `EvaluateResult`, `SampleValues`, `FormState`, `CompileResult` ...), the request view, the story, the test host's fakes and outbox, and `ChoicesArgs` / `ChoicesPage`. `src/contract` keeps the repo's `contract/` files (the constants core does not re-export), and `types.test.ts` checks that its types and core's are the same, both ways.

Written here, because core does not have them: the async `CoreService` and `TestHost` / `HostResult` (core's own with promises), `Result<T, E>`, the authoring and runtime services and their shapes, the catalogue, directory, session and dev services, the `alert.*` built-in messages, and a few names for parts of core's types (CONTRACT-NOTES.md, item 13).

## Rules every implementation keeps

- **Everything is async**, even what the core computes synchronously.
- **Refusals are results.** Server calls give `Result<T>` (`{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, errors }`); Try it turns give `TurnResult<T>` (`{ ok: true, ...T }` or `{ ok: false, refusals }`). A rejected promise means the call could not be made at all. `DirectoryService` is the exception: it rejects when the directory cannot be reached.
- **Codes, not words.** Findings, parse problems, errors, story entries, changes and built-in messages are `{ code, location?, params }`. `switch (x.code)` narrows `params`. The codes are core's: every one is known to this build.
- **Locations are authored-format locations**, `{ item, part? }`.
- **History is story entries** (`StoryEntry`), the same from Try it and live.
- **Stuck is one state**, `Stuck { reason, at, location?, admin? }`, the same in `RequestView.stuck`, `RequestRow.stuck` (never `admin`) and the story's `stuck` entry. Retry is offered only for `action-failed` and `nobody-to-ask` (`RetryableStuckReason`); Close for any open request.
- **A person or group is `{ type, id }`** (`Ref`) in every value, answer and shape; names come from `directory.lookup`.
- **No `null`**, except inside an authored document and in the inbound endpoint's answer (`InboundAnswer`).

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `core.ts` | The `core` service over `@workflow/core`: parse, check, facts, values in scope, checkFormula, evaluate, evaluateSent, sampleValues, formState, diff, compile, meta, formulaFunctions, and Try it's `createTestHost` (core's host, each answer in a promise) |
| `index.ts` | The services the app uses: the real core and the stand-in's server side; `coreVersion` |
| `types.ts` | `Services`, the catalogue, directory, session and dev services; re-exports the rest |
| `types-common.ts` | Core's shared types; `Result<T, E>`, `Redacted` |
| `types-errors.ts` | Core's `ApiError` / `Refusal` and params; the per-operation code unions |
| `types-findings.ts` | Core's `ParseProblem`, `Finding`, `FormulaError`, `Change` |
| `types-core.ts` | `CoreService`, and core's result types |
| `types-story.ts` | Core's `StoryEntry`, `MoveWhy`, `ReadOf`, `WhyRead` |
| `types-request.ts` | Core's `RequestView`, `OpenTask`, `OpenAction`, `ButtonState`, `Stuck` |
| `types-testhost.ts` | The async `TestHost`, `HostResult`; core's fakes and outbox; the built-in message codes |
| `types-authoring.ts` | `AuthoringService`: workflows, drafts, publish, versions, Settings |
| `types-runtime.ts` | `RuntimeService`: start, choices, tasks, act, requests, retry and close, bindings, refused starts; the inbound answer |
| `types.test.ts` | Type-level checks: src/contract's types are core's, the async host matches core's, the contract's examples fit |
| `CONTRACT-NOTES.md` | What differs from the contract on purpose, what it leaves open, questions for the engine owner |

## Over HTTP (`http/`)

The engine's development host (engine/DEV-HOST.md) at `VITE_ENGINE_URL`, `{address}/api/workflow/v1`. `client.ts` is the one client: JSON, the contract's `{ errors }` given back as the `Result`'s errors untouched (so `stale-revision` carries its draft), any other failure as `internal`, an engine that cannot be reached as a rejected call (`CannotReachEngine`). One file per area: `authoring.ts`, `runtime.ts`, `people.ts` (catalogue, directory, session; `whoAmI`, `people` and the directory reject on a refusal, `EngineRefused`), `dev.ts` (the host's `{address}/dev` controls: the mock systems' switches and what they received, and "Pretend Helpdesk sent this now" through the Helpdesk mock's send control, because the inbound hook needs a signature the page cannot make), `seed.ts` ("Add sample requests"). `__fixtures__` are answers recorded from the host by `tools/record-engine-fixtures.mjs`; `http.test.ts` checks every call's request against the recorded one and its answer.

## The stand-in (`standin/`)

The stand-in only plays the server and pretends the other systems; it never decides what a workflow does. It holds the server's data (`authoring.ts`: workflows, drafts, publish through core's `compile`; `store.ts`; `seed.ts`, `seed-requests.ts`; `session.ts`; `directory.ts`; `catalogue.ts`) and the live side (`runtime.ts`: the request list and IDs, my tasks, who may retry or close, bindings, held deliveries and refused starts, the pretended other systems' answers). Every live request runs on core's own test host, one host per request (`runs.ts`), and is kept as the moves the engine accepted, run again on a fresh host after a reload; its view, history, tasks, buttons and stuck state are core's `requestView` and `story`. A binding's "Only when" is core's `evaluateSent`. Try it uses core's `createTestHost` directly (`core.ts`). The stand-in's check, facts, scope, evaluate, form state, diff, interpreter, host, outbox and story are all gone.
===\nfrontend/src/services/context.test.tsx\n===
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { render, renderHook, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { ServicesProvider, useServices } from './context';
import type { Services } from './types';

const fake = { session: { whoAmI: async () => ({ ref: { type: 'user', id: 'x' }, label: 'X', platformAdmin: false }) } } as unknown as Services;

function Probe() {
  const services = useServices();
  return <p>{services === fake ? 'got them' : 'wrong'}</p>;
}

describe('ServicesProvider', () => {
  it('hands its services to everything below it', () => {
    render(<ServicesProvider services={fake}><Probe /></ServicesProvider>);
    expect(screen.getByText('got them')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('says what is wrong when nothing provides the services', () => {
    expect(() => renderHook(() => useServices())).toThrow(/ServicesProvider/);
  });
});
===\nfrontend/src/services/context.tsx\n===
/**
 * Hands the services (F4) to every screen: wrap the app in `<ServicesProvider services={...}>`
 * and call `useServices()` below it. Tests pass their own set (e.g. a fresh stand-in in memory).
 */
import { createContext, useContext, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import type { Services } from './types';

const ServicesContext = createContext<Services | null>(null);

export function ServicesProvider({ services, children }: { services: Services; children: ReactNode }) {
  return <ServicesContext.Provider value={services}>{children}</ServicesContext.Provider>;
}

/** The services of the nearest `ServicesProvider`. Throws when there is none: that is a wiring mistake. */
export function useServices(): Services {
  const services = useContext(ServicesContext);
  if (!services) throw new Error('useServices() needs a <ServicesProvider> above it.');
  return services;
}
===\nfrontend/src/services/core-testhost.test.ts\n===
/**
 * `core.createTestHost` is core's own test host behind the async services interface (core.ts): the
 * seed workflows run on it, its answers come through unchanged, and `request` answers core's
 * not-found refusal for a request it does not hold. The behaviour itself is core's and tested there
 * (engine/packages/core/test/authored/host); this pins only what the frontend relies on.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { fixtures } from '@/contract/fixtures';
import { core } from './core';
import { SAMPLE_CATALOGUE } from './standin/catalogue';
import { GROUPS } from './standin/directory';
import type { Fakes, Ref, TestHost } from './types';

const user = (slug: string): Ref => ({ type: 'user', id: `dir-user-${slug}` });
const fakes: Fakes = {
  groups: Object.fromEntries(GROUPS.map((g) => [g.id, [...g.members]])),
  stuckRequestsGoTo: [user('sam-carter')],
  startAt: '2026-11-15T09:00:00.000Z',
};
const form = {
  q_title: 'Rotate payment gateway API keys', q_description: 'Before the freeze.', q_primary_domain: 'row_payments',
  q_planned_release_date: '2026-12-02', q_risk: 'ch_risk_medium',
};

async function host(name: keyof typeof fixtures): Promise<TestHost> {
  const made = await core.createTestHost(fixtures[name], SAMPLE_CATALOGUE, fakes);
  if (!made.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(made.findings));
  return made.host;
}

async function view(h: TestHost, id: string, as?: Ref) {
  const v = await h.request(id, as);
  if (!('requestId' in v)) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(v));
  return v;
}

describe('the test host is core\'s', () => {
  it('makes a host for every seed workflow', async () => {
    for (const name of ['change-request', 'several-at-once', 'integrated-sample'] as const) {
      const made = await core.createTestHost(fixtures[name], SAMPLE_CATALOGUE, fakes);
      expect(made.ok, name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('runs the demo to Released, with the story and the outbox as core gives them', async () => {
    const h = await host('change-request');
    const r = await h.start(user('priya-raman'), 'btn_rf_submit', form);
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.refusals));
    const [approval] = await h.openTasks({ requestId: r.requestId });
    expect(await h.act(user('marcus-lee'), r.requestId, approval!.task, 'btn_da_approve', { q_eng_lead: user('diego-santos') })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    const [development] = await h.openTasks({ requestId: r.requestId });
    expect(await h.act(user('diego-santos'), r.requestId, development!.task, 'btn_dev_mark_released', { q_release_notes: 'Rotated.' })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    const v = await view(h, r.requestId);
    expect(v.closed?.ending).toBe('st_released');
    expect(v.story.at(-1)?.code).toBe('ended');
    expect((await h.outbox(r.requestId)).some((e) => e.kind === 'notification' && 'action' in e.from)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('answers not-found for a request it does not hold, as core does (narrow on "ok" in the result)', async () => {
    const h = await host('change-request');
    expect(await h.request('R99')).toEqual({ ok: false, refusals: [{ code: 'not-found', params: { what: 'request' } }] });
  });

  // For the engine owner: the requester is told "You have something to do" for a task he may not
  // answer. Marcus starts it; the approval asks Payments approvers, which holds him; the task does not
  // let the requester answer, yet task.assigned lists him among the recipients. The outbox shows what
  // the engine sends, so Try it shows it too until core leaves him out.
  it('(engine) task.assigned reaches a requester who may not answer the task', async () => {
    const h = await host('change-request');
    const marcus = user('marcus-lee');
    const r = await h.start(marcus, 'btn_rf_submit', form);
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(JSON.stringify(r.refusals));
    const [task] = (await view(h, r.requestId, marcus)).tasks;
    expect(task!.buttonStates.every((b) => !b.available && b.refusals.some((x) => x.code === 'may'))).toBe(true);
    const assigned = (await h.outbox(r.requestId)).find((e) => e.kind === 'notification' && 'builtIn' in e.from && e.from.builtIn.code === 'task.assigned');
    expect(assigned?.kind === 'notification' && assigned.recipients).toContainEqual(marcus);
  });
});
===\nfrontend/src/services/core.ts\n===
/**
 * The `core` service over the engine's real core, `@workflow/core` (engine/packages/core, consumed
 * as TypeScript source; README.md says how it is linked). Each function is core's own, called as
 * it is and wrapped in a promise (F4): no adapting in between, so what the editor shows is what
 * core answers.
 */
import {
  check, checkFormula, compile, createTestHost, diff, evaluate, evaluateSent, facts, FORMULA_FUNCTIONS, formState, meta, parse,
  sampleValues, upgrade, valuesInScope,
} from '@workflow/core';
import type { CoreService, HostResult, TestHost } from './types';

/**
 * Try it's test host: core's own `createTestHost` (core-api.md 10), each method's answer in a
 * promise (F4). Nothing is adapted: refusals, the request view, the story and the outbox are core's.
 */
function testHost(...args: Parameters<typeof createTestHost>): HostResult {
  const made = createTestHost(...args);
  if (!made.ok) return made;
  const h = made.host;
  const host: TestHost = {
    start: async (as, button, answers, at) => h.start(as, button, answers, at),
    startFrom: async (binding, sent, at) => h.startFrom(binding, sent, at),
    choices: async (args) => h.choices(args),
    openTasks: async (filter) => h.openTasks(filter),
    act: async (as, requestId, task, button, answers, at) => h.act(as, requestId, task, button, answers, at),
    admin: async (as, requestId, action, reason, at) => h.admin(as, requestId, action, reason, at),
    answerCall: async (call, answer, at) => h.answerCall(call, answer, at),
    setCallFake: async (operation, fake) => h.setCallFake(operation, fake),
    outbox: async (requestId) => h.outbox(requestId),
    request: async (requestId, as) => h.request(requestId, as),
  };
  return { ok: true, host, unfinished: made.unfinished, findings: made.findings };
}

export const core: CoreService = {
  meta: async () => meta,
  upgrade: async (workflow) => upgrade(workflow),
  parse: async (doc) => parse(doc),
  check: async (workflow, catalogue) => check(workflow, catalogue),
  facts: async (workflow, catalogue) => facts(workflow, catalogue),
  valuesInScope: async (workflow, catalogue, at) => valuesInScope(workflow, catalogue, at),
  checkFormula: async (workflow, catalogue, at, formula, sample) => checkFormula(workflow, catalogue, at, formula, sample),
  formulaFunctions: async () => FORMULA_FUNCTIONS,
  evaluate: async (workflow, catalogue, at, what, sample, lookups) => evaluate(workflow, catalogue, at, what, sample, lookups),
  evaluateSent: async (workflow, catalogue, at, what, sent) => evaluateSent(workflow, catalogue, at, what, sent),
  sampleValues: async (workflow, sample, catalogue) => sampleValues(workflow, sample, catalogue),
  formState: async (workflow, catalogue, task, answers, values, request, lookups) =>
    formState(workflow, catalogue, task, answers, values, request, lookups),
  diff: async (before, after) => diff(before, after),
  compile: async (workflow, catalogue, options) => compile(workflow, catalogue, options),
  createTestHost: async (workflow, catalogue, fakes) => testHost(workflow, catalogue, fakes),
};

===\nfrontend/src/services/http/authoring.ts\n===
/**
 * `AuthoringService` over the engine's HTTP API (authoring-api.md section 5), operation for
 * operation. The answers are the interface's shapes as sent; only `getCatalogue` (operation 11)
 * lives on `CatalogueService` (catalogue.ts).
 */
import type { AuthoringService } from '../types';
import { path, type HttpClient } from './client';

export function createHttpAuthoring(http: HttpClient): AuthoringService {
  const wf = (id: string) => path('workflows', id);
  return {
    listWorkflows: () => http.call('GET', '/workflows'),
    createWorkflow: (args) => http.call('POST', '/workflows', { name: args.name, ...(args.description === undefined ? {} : { description: args.description }) }),
    getDraft: (workflow) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}/draft`),
    saveDraft: (workflow, args) => http.call('PUT', `${wf(workflow)}/draft`, { baseRevision: args.baseRevision, authored: args.authored }),
    publish: (workflow, args) => http.call('POST', `${wf(workflow)}/versions`, { revision: args.revision, coreVersion: args.coreVersion }),
    listVersions: (workflow) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}/versions`),
    getVersion: (workflow, version) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}/versions/${encodeURIComponent(String(version))}`),
    getSettings: (workflow) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}/settings`),
    saveSettings: (workflow, settings) =>
      http.call('PUT', `${wf(workflow)}/settings`, {
        name: settings.name,
        description: settings.description,
        authors: settings.authors,
        ...(settings.stuckRequestsGoTo === undefined ? {} : { stuckRequestsGoTo: settings.stuckRequestsGoTo }),
      }),
    getMeta: () => http.call('GET', '/meta'),
  };
}
===\nfrontend/src/services/http/client.test.ts\n===
/**
 * The HTTP client's mapping of the engine's answers onto the interface (authoring-api.md section 1,
 * core-api.md 2.6): the contract's failure body as recorded, anything else as `internal`, and an
 * engine that cannot be reached as a rejected call.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { CannotReachEngine, createClient, errorsOf, path, query } from './client';
import { createHttpServices } from './index';
import { EngineRefused } from './people';
import { ADDRESS, fixture, replay } from './replay';

describe('the HTTP client', () => {
  it('a success is its body; the engine core version of the answer is kept', async () => {
    const { fetch } = replay(fixture('meta'));
    const http = createClient(`${ADDRESS}/`, fetch);
    expect(http.address).toBe(ADDRESS);
    expect(await http.call('GET', '/meta')).toEqual({ ok: true, value: fixture('meta').body });
    expect(http.lastCoreVersion()).toBe('0.0.0');
  });

  it('a failure is the contract\'s errors, untouched, whatever the status', async () => {
    for (const name of ['unknown-path', 'save-forbidden', 'publish-has-todo', 'act-wait-not-open', 'retry-stale', 'start-refused']) {
      const f = fixture(name);
      const { fetch } = replay(f);
      const r = await createClient(ADDRESS, fetch).call('GET', '/x');
      expect(r).toEqual({ ok: false, errors: (f.body as { errors: unknown }).errors });
    }
  });

  it('an answer that is not the contract\'s (a proxy page, an empty 502) is internal', async () => {
    const answers = [
      new Response('<html>Bad gateway</html>', { status: 502 }),
      new Response(null, { status: 503 }),
      new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'nope' }), { status: 400 }),
      new Response(null, { status: 200 }),
    ];
    for (const res of answers) {
      const http = createClient(ADDRESS, async () => res);
      expect(await http.call('GET', '/x')).toEqual({ ok: false, errors: [{ code: 'internal', params: {} }] });
    }
    expect(errorsOf({ errors: [] })).toEqual([{ code: 'internal', params: {} }]);
  });

  it('an engine that cannot be reached rejects the call, as every screen already handles', async () => {
    const http = createClient(ADDRESS, async () => {
      throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch');
    });
    await expect(http.call('GET', '/meta')).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(CannotReachEngine);
    const services = createHttpServices(ADDRESS, async () => {
      throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch');
    });
    await expect(services.authoring.listWorkflows()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(CannotReachEngine);
    await expect(services.session.whoAmI()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(CannotReachEngine);
    expect(await services.dev?.mocks?.offered()).toBe(false);
  });

  it('who is signed in and the people let "the directory cannot be reached" through, as a rejection', async () => {
    const unavailable = () => new Response(JSON.stringify({ errors: [{ code: 'membership-unavailable', params: {} }] }), { status: 503 });
    const services = createHttpServices(ADDRESS, async () => unavailable());
    await expect(services.session.whoAmI()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(EngineRefused);
    await expect(services.session.people()).rejects.toThrow('membership-unavailable');
    await expect(services.directory.search('a', ['user'])).rejects.toThrow('membership-unavailable');
    // signInAs keeps its Result.
    expect(await services.session.signInAs({ type: 'user', id: 'x' })).toEqual({ ok: false, errors: [{ code: 'membership-unavailable', params: {} }] });
  });

  it('encodes path segments and leaves empty query entries out', () => {
    expect(path('workflows', 'a b/c')).toBe('/workflows/a%20b%2Fc');
    expect(query({ a: 1, b: undefined, c: '', d: 'x y' })).toBe('?a=1&d=x+y');
    expect(query({})).toBe('');
  });
});
===\nfrontend/src/services/http/client.ts\n===
/**
 * The small HTTP client every HTTP service shares (authoring-api.md section 1, runtime-api.md
 * 1.1): JSON bodies, the engine's base address, and its one failure shape mapped to the
 * interface's `Result`:
 *
 * - success (2xx): `{ ok: true, value: <body> }`;
 * - a failure with the contract's body `{ errors: ApiError[] }`: `{ ok: false, errors }` as sent
 *   (codes, params and locations untouched, so `stale-revision` carries its draft);
 * - any other failure (a body that is not the contract's: a proxy's page, an empty 502): `internal`;
 * - the engine cannot be reached at all (`fetch` rejects): the promise rejects with
 *   `CannotReachEngine`, as every screen already treats a call that could not be made.
 */
import type { ApiError, Result } from '../types';

/** The API's path under the engine's address (authoring-api.md section 1; the development host). */
export const API_BASE = '/api/workflow/v1';

/** The engine could not be reached: the call was not made (or its answer never came). */
export class CannotReachEngine extends Error {
  constructor(readonly address: string, cause?: unknown) {
    super(`The engine at ${address} could not be reached.`, cause === undefined ? undefined : { cause });
    this.name = 'CannotReachEngine';
  }
}

export type Fetch = (input: string, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

export interface HttpClient {
  /** The engine's address, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8787 (no trailing slash). */
  readonly address: string;
  /** Calls `{address}/api/workflow/v1{path}`. */
  call<T>(method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT', path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<Result<T>>;
  /** Calls `{address}{path}` (outside the API, e.g. the development host's `/dev`): the status and the JSON body, if any. */
  raw(method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT', path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown }>;
  /** The `Engine-Core-Version` the engine sent last (every answer carries it). */
  lastCoreVersion(): string | undefined;
}

/** `/api/workflow/v1/x` from parts: each part is one path segment, encoded. */
export const path = (...parts: (string | number)[]): string => parts.map((p) => `/${encodeURIComponent(String(p))}`).join('');

const isApiError = (e: unknown): e is ApiError =>
  !!e && typeof e === 'object' && typeof (e as { code?: unknown }).code === 'string' && typeof (e as { params?: unknown }).params === 'object';

/** A failed answer's errors: the contract's body, else `internal`. */
export function errorsOf(body: unknown): ApiError[] {
  const errors = body && typeof body === 'object' ? (body as { errors?: unknown }).errors : undefined;
  if (Array.isArray(errors) && errors.length > 0 && errors.every(isApiError)) return errors;
  return [{ code: 'internal', params: {} }];
}

export function createClient(address: string, fetchImpl?: Fetch): HttpClient {
  const origin = address.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  const doFetch: Fetch = fetchImpl ?? ((input, init) => fetch(input, init));
  let coreVersion: string | undefined;

  async function send(method: string, url: string, body: unknown): Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown }> {
    let res: Response;
    try {
      res = await doFetch(url, {
        method,
        headers: body === undefined ? { accept: 'application/json' } : { accept: 'application/json', 'content-type': 'application/json' },
        ...(body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw new CannotReachEngine(origin, error);
    }
    coreVersion = res.headers.get('engine-core-version') ?? coreVersion;
    let text: string;
    try {
      text = await res.text();
    } catch (error) {
      throw new CannotReachEngine(origin, error);
    }
    let json: unknown = undefined;
    if (text !== '') {
      try {
        json = JSON.parse(text) as unknown;
      } catch {
        json = undefined;
      }
    }
    return { status: res.status, body: json };
  }

  return {
    address: origin,
    async call<T>(method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT', p: string, body?: unknown): Promise<Result<T>> {
      const answer = await send(method, `${origin}${API_BASE}${p}`, body);
      if (answer.status >= 200 && answer.status < 300 && answer.body !== undefined) return { ok: true, value: answer.body as T };
      return { ok: false, errors: errorsOf(answer.body) };
    },
    raw: (method, p, body) => send(method, `${origin}${p}`, body),
    lastCoreVersion: () => coreVersion,
  };
}

/** A query string from the defined entries (`?a=1&b=x`), or '' when none. */
export function query(entries: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>): string {
  const q = new URLSearchParams();
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(entries)) if (v !== undefined && v !== '') q.set(k, String(v));
  const s = q.toString();
  return s ? `?${s}` : '';
}

/**
 * `DevService` for the engine's development host over HTTP (engine/DEV-HOST.md, "Controlling the
 * mocks from the browser").
 *
 * - The inbound hook (`/hooks/v1/events/{connection}`) is not called from the page: every delivery
 *   must carry the connection's Standard Webhooks signature, made with the connection's secret,
 *   which the page does not hold. Instead the development host's own controls (`{engine}/dev`) make
 *   its Helpdesk mock send (`POST /dev/mocks/helpdesk/send`), signed as the mock signs. They are
 *   probed once (`GET /dev/mocks`); on an engine without them "Pretend ... sent this now" says it is
 *   not available.
 * - Only the Helpdesk mock can send, so only its triggers can be pretended, and only the fields
 *   its send control takes: the ticket's key, title and category, the service by its ID, the
 *   reporter by email. Description, priority and link are the mock's own.
 * - The engine cannot be reset from the page (`resetSampleData` is absent): restarting the
 *   development host starts it from nothing.
 * - `answerWaiting` is not offered: the mock systems answer by themselves (the mock deploy is done
 *   after two status questions, about a minute apart). It is refused `not-found` (`call`).
 */
import type { CatalogueRef } from '@/contract';
import type {
  DevService, DirectoryService, InboundAnswer, InboundError, InboundErrorCode, MockCall, MockMessage, MockSwitches, MockSystem,
  MockSystems, Result,
} from '../types';
import type { HttpClient } from './client';

/** The development host's controls, outside the API. */
export const DEV_BASE = '/dev';

/** The fields of `helpdesk.ticketCreated@1` the Helpdesk mock's send control takes. */
export const HELPDESK_FIELDS: readonly string[] = ['key', 'title', 'category', 'service', 'reporter'];

/** The mock systems that can send an event, by connection. */
const SENDERS = new Set(['helpdesk']);

const INBOUND_CODES: readonly InboundErrorCode[] = [
  'too-large', 'unknown-connection', 'connection-unavailable', 'unauthenticated', 'unparsable', 'event-invalid', 'unavailable',
];

export const connectionOf = (entry: string): string => entry.split('.')[0] ?? '';

const isObject = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> => !!v && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v);

/** The development host refused a control call: its one-line reason. */
export class DevHostRefused extends Error {
  constructor(readonly status: number, reason: string) {
    super(reason);
    this.name = 'DevHostRefused';
  }
}

/**
 * What the Helpdesk mock is asked to send (`{ key?, title?, category?, service?, reporter? }`, all
 * text), from the fields of the catalogue's trigger `helpdesk.ticketCreated@1`: key, title and
 * category as they are; the service by its stored ID; the reporter by the email the directory
 * gives for the person (the hook finds the person by it again).
 */
export async function helpdeskBody(sent: Record<string, unknown>, directory: DirectoryService): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  const body: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const f of ['key', 'title', 'category'] as const) {
    const v = sent[f];
    if (typeof v === 'string' && v !== '') body[f] = v;
  }
  const service = sent['service'];
  if (isObject(service) && typeof service['stored'] === 'string') body['service'] = service['stored'];
  else if (typeof service === 'string' && service !== '') body['service'] = service;
  const reporter = sent['reporter'];
  if (isObject(reporter) && reporter['type'] === 'user' && typeof reporter['id'] === 'string') {
    const found = await directory.lookup([{ type: 'user', id: reporter['id'] }]).catch(() => []);
    const email = found[0]?.detail;
    if (email) body['reporter'] = email;
  }
  return body;
}

/** The hook's answer, as the send control relays it: 200 `InboundAnswer`, or `{ error: code }`. */
export function inboundResult(status: number, answer: unknown): Result<InboundAnswer, InboundError> {
  if (status === 200 && isObject(answer) && Array.isArray(answer['results'])) return { ok: true, value: answer as unknown as InboundAnswer };
  const code = isObject(answer) ? answer['error'] : undefined;
  const known = INBOUND_CODES.find((c) => c === code);
  return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: known ?? 'unavailable', params: {} }] };
}

export function createHttpMocks(http: HttpClient): MockSystems {
  let probe: Promise<boolean> | undefined;
  const offered = () =>
    (probe ??= http
      .raw('GET', `${DEV_BASE}/mocks`)
      .then((r) => r.status === 200 && isObject(r.body) && Array.isArray(r.body['mocks']))
      .catch(() => false));
  /** The body of a 200 answer; otherwise rejects with the host's reason. */
  const answer = async (r: Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown }>): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> => {
    const a = await r;
    if (a.status === 200 && isObject(a.body)) return a.body;
    const reason = isObject(a.body) && typeof a.body['error'] === 'string' ? a.body['error'] : `the development host answered ${a.status}`;
    throw new DevHostRefused(a.status, reason);
  };
  const received = async (connection: string, request?: string): Promise<unknown[]> => {
    const b = await answer(
      http.raw('GET', `${DEV_BASE}/mocks/${encodeURIComponent(connection)}/received${request ? `?request=${encodeURIComponent(request)}` : ''}`),
    );
    return Array.isArray(b['items']) ? b['items'] : [];
  };
  return {
    offered,
    list: async () => {
      const b = await answer(http.raw('GET', `${DEV_BASE}/mocks`));
      return Array.isArray(b['mocks']) ? (b['mocks'] as MockSystem[]) : [];
    },
    set: async (connection: string, switches: MockSwitches) =>
      (await answer(http.raw('PUT', `${DEV_BASE}/mocks/${encodeURIComponent(connection)}`, switches))) as unknown as MockSystem,
    calls: async (connection, request) => (await received(connection, request)) as MockCall[],
    messages: async (request) => (await received('messages', request)) as MockMessage[],
    events: async (request) => (await received('reporting', request)) as Record<string, unknown>[],
  };
}

export function createHttpDev(http: HttpClient, directory: DirectoryService, mocks: MockSystems): Omit<DevService, 'addSampleRequests'> {
  return {
    engineAddress: http.address,
    mocks,
    async canSendSample(entry: CatalogueRef) {
      return SENDERS.has(connectionOf(entry)) && (await mocks.offered());
    },
    sampleFields: (entry: CatalogueRef) => (connectionOf(entry) === 'helpdesk' ? HELPDESK_FIELDS : undefined),
    async sendSample(entry, sent) {
      const connection = connectionOf(entry);
      if (!SENDERS.has(connection) || !(await mocks.offered())) return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: 'unknown-connection', params: {} }] };
      const body = sent ? await helpdeskBody(sent, directory) : {};
      const answer = await http.raw('POST', `${DEV_BASE}/mocks/${encodeURIComponent(connection)}/send`, body);
      // A body the send control refuses (400) is not an answer of the hook: the event could not be read.
      if (answer.status === 400) return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: 'unparsable', params: {} }] };
      if (answer.status !== 200 || !isObject(answer.body)) return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: 'unavailable', params: {} }] };
      return inboundResult(Number(answer.body['status']), answer.body['answer']);
    },
    async answerWaiting() {
      return { ok: false, errors: [{ code: 'not-found', params: { what: 'call' } }] };
    },
  };
}

/**
 * The HTTP services against answers recorded from the engine's development host
 * (`__fixtures__`, tools/record-engine-fixtures.mjs): each call must send the request the
 * recorder sent (method, path, query, body), and turn the recorded answer into the interface's
 * shape.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { fixtureCatalogue } from '@/contract/fixtures';
import type { ButtonId, QuestionId, StartsWhenId } from '@/contract';
import type { Answers, Result, Services } from '../types';
import { createHttpServices } from './index';
import { ADDRESS, expectedRequest, fixture, replay, type Fixture } from './replay';
import { helpdeskBody, inboundResult } from './dev';
import { requestQueryString } from './runtime';

/** The services over a fetch that answers these fixtures in order. */
function over(...names: string[]) {
  const fixtures = names.map(fixture);
  const r = replay(...fixtures);
  return { services: createHttpServices(ADDRESS, r.fetch), sent: r.sent, fixtures };
}

/** Calls once against one fixture: the request must be the recorded one; gives the result. */
async function one<T>(name: string, call: (s: Services) => Promise<T>): Promise<{ result: T; f: Fixture }> {
  const { services, sent, fixtures } = over(name);
  const result = await call(services);
  const f = fixtures[0] as Fixture;
  expect(sent).toEqual([expectedRequest(f)]);
  return { result, f };
}

/** A success with the recorded body as its value. */
function expectValue<T>(result: Result<T>, f: Fixture) {
  expect(result).toEqual({ ok: true, value: f.body });
}

/** A refusal with the recorded errors, and the first one's code. */
function expectErrors<T>(result: Result<T>, f: Fixture, code: string) {
  expect(result).toEqual({ ok: false, errors: (f.body as { errors: unknown[] }).errors });
  expect(!result.ok && result.errors[0]?.code).toBe(code);
}

/**
 * The services over the engine's real server (its development host, engine/DEV-HOST.md), behind
 * the same interface as the stand-in: authoring, runtime, catalogue, directory, session and dev
 * over HTTP; `core` stays the engine's core in the browser (Try it, check, form state).
 */
import type { Services } from '../types';
import { core } from '../core';
import { createHttpAuthoring } from './authoring';
import { createClient, type Fetch } from './client';
import { createHttpDev, createHttpMocks } from './dev';
import { createHttpCatalogue, createHttpDirectory, createHttpSession } from './people';
import { createHttpRuntime } from './runtime';
import { addSampleRequests } from './seed';

export { CannotReachEngine } from './client';
export { EngineRefused } from './people';

export function createHttpServices(address: string, fetchImpl?: Fetch): Services {
  const http = createClient(address, fetchImpl);
  const directory = createHttpDirectory(http);
  const runtime = createHttpRuntime(http);
  const session = createHttpSession(http);
  const mocks = createHttpMocks(http);
  const base = createHttpDev(http, directory, mocks);
  return {
    core,
    authoring: createHttpAuthoring(http),
    runtime,
    catalogue: createHttpCatalogue(http),
    directory,
    session,
    dev: { ...base, addSampleRequests: () => addSampleRequests({ runtime, session, dev: base }) },
  };
}

/**
 * The catalogue (authoring-api.md operation 11), the directory and the session (runtime-api.md 7)
 * over the engine's HTTP API.
 *
 * - `DirectoryService` rejects when the directory cannot be reached (`503 membership-unavailable`)
 *   or when the call is refused for another reason: it has no refusal results.
 * - `SessionService.whoAmI` and `people` are unwrapped from their `Result`; a refusal rejects, so a
 *   "directory cannot be reached" from the engine reaches the screen as a call that could not be made.
 *   `signInAs` keeps its `Result`. The development host signs one person in for every tab and every
 *   later call (`PUT /session`).
 */
import type { CatalogueDirectoryRef, DirectoryEntry } from '@/contract';
import type { ApiError, CatalogueService, DirectoryService, Person, Result, SessionService } from '../types';
import { path, query, type HttpClient } from './client';

/** A refusal where the interface has no refusal result: the call rejects with it. */
export class EngineRefused extends Error {
  constructor(readonly errors: ApiError[]) {
    super(`The engine refused the call: ${errors.map((e) => e.code).join(', ')}.`);
    this.name = 'EngineRefused';
  }
}

export function unwrap<T>(result: Result<T>): T {
  if (result.ok) return result.value;
  throw new EngineRefused(result.errors);
}

export function createHttpCatalogue(http: HttpClient): CatalogueService {
  return { getCatalogue: () => http.call('GET', '/catalogue') };
}

/** The directory search answers at most 50 (runtime-api.md 7). */
const SEARCH_LIMIT = 50;

export function createHttpDirectory(http: HttpClient): DirectoryService {
  return {
    search: async (q, types) =>
      unwrap(await http.call<DirectoryEntry[]>('GET', `/directory/search${query({ q, types: types.join(','), limit: SEARCH_LIMIT })}`)),
    lookup: async (refs: CatalogueDirectoryRef[]) =>
      refs.length === 0 ? [] : unwrap(await http.call<DirectoryEntry[]>('POST', '/directory/lookup', { refs: refs.map((r) => ({ type: r.type, id: r.id })) })),
    membersOf: async (group) =>
      group.type !== 'group' ? [] : unwrap(await http.call<DirectoryEntry[]>('GET', `${path('directory', 'groups', group.id)}/members`)),
  };
}

export function createHttpSession(http: HttpClient): SessionService {
  return {
    whoAmI: async () => unwrap(await http.call<Person>('GET', '/session')),
    signInAs: (person) => http.call('PUT', '/session', { person: { type: person.type, id: person.id } }),
    people: async () => unwrap(await http.call<Person[]>('GET', '/session/people')),
  };
}
===\nfrontend/src/services/http/replay.ts\n===
/**
 * For the HTTP services' tests: a `fetch` that answers from recorded fixtures
 * (`__fixtures__`, made by tools/record-engine-fixtures.mjs against the real development host) and
 * keeps what it was asked, so a test can check the request a service sends against the request
 * the recorder sent.
 */
import { API_BASE, type Fetch } from './client';

export interface Fixture {
  request: { method: string; path: string; body?: unknown; fields?: unknown };
  status: number;
  coreVersion?: string | null;
  body: unknown;
}

const files = import.meta.glob<Fixture>('./__fixtures__/*.json', { eager: true, import: 'default' });

/** The fixture of that name (the file name without `.json`). */
export function fixture(name: string): Fixture {
  const f = files[`./__fixtures__/${name}.json`];
  if (!f) throw new Error(`No fixture ${name}`);
  return f;
}

export const ADDRESS = 'http://engine.test:8787';

export interface Sent {
  method: string;
  /** The path under the API base (or under the address for `/dev`), without the query. */
  path: string;
  /** The query, decoded, as sorted entries. */
  query: [string, string][];
  body: unknown;
}

/** A request as sent, split for comparing: path decoded, query entries sorted. */
export function splitRequest(method: string, url: string, body: unknown): Sent {
  const u = new URL(url, ADDRESS);
  const p = u.pathname.startsWith(API_BASE) ? u.pathname.slice(API_BASE.length) : u.pathname;
  const query = [...u.searchParams.entries()].sort((a, b) => (a[0] + a[1]).localeCompare(b[0] + b[1]));
  return { method, path: decodeURIComponent(p), query, body };
}

/** The fixture's request in the same split form. */
export function expectedRequest(f: Fixture): Sent {
  return splitRequest(f.request.method, f.request.path, f.request.body);
}

/** A fetch answering the fixtures in order; `sent` holds what each call asked. */
export function replay(...fixtures: Fixture[]): { fetch: Fetch; sent: Sent[] } {
  const queue = [...fixtures];
  const sent: Sent[] = [];
  const fetchImpl: Fetch = async (input, init) => {
    const body = typeof init?.body === 'string' ? (JSON.parse(init.body) as unknown) : undefined;
    sent.push(splitRequest(init?.method ?? 'GET', input, body));
    const f = queue.shift();
    if (!f) throw new Error(`No recorded answer left for ${init?.method ?? 'GET'} ${input}`);
    const headers: Record<string, string> = { 'content-type': 'application/json' };
    if (f.coreVersion) headers['engine-core-version'] = f.coreVersion;
    return new Response(f.body === null ? null : JSON.stringify(f.body), { status: f.status, headers });
  };
  return { fetch: fetchImpl, sent };
}
===\nfrontend/src/services/http/runtime.ts\n===
/**
 * `RuntimeService` over the engine's HTTP API (runtime-api.md sections 3 to 6), operation for
 * operation. The answers are the interface's shapes as sent. What the engine does more thinly
 * than the stand-in (E-33) is said, not hidden: `whilePaused` is `refused`, so the screens word a
 * pause as the engine runs it.
 */
import type { RequestQuery, RuntimeService } from '../types';
import { path, query, type HttpClient } from './client';

/** The request list's query string (runtime-api.md 6.2): lists comma-joined, each `valueEquals` as `value.<id>=<JSON>`. */
export function requestQueryString(q: RequestQuery): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const set = (k: string, v: string | number | boolean | undefined) => {
    if (v !== undefined && v !== '') params.set(k, String(v));
  };
  set('workflow', q.workflow);
  if (q.status?.length) set('status', q.status.join(','));
  set('version', q.version);
  set('state', q.state);
  set('stuck', q.stuck);
  set('startedBy', q.startedBy);
  for (const v of q.valueEquals ?? []) params.append(`value.${v.value}`, JSON.stringify(v.equals));
  if (q.include?.length) set('include', q.include.join(','));
  set('sort', q.sort);
  set('order', q.order);
  set('cursor', q.cursor);
  set('limit', q.limit);
  const s = params.toString();
  return s ? `?${s}` : '';
}

export function createHttpRuntime(http: HttpClient): RuntimeService {
  const request = (id: string) => path('requests', id);
  const wf = (id: string) => path('workflows', id);
  return {
    whilePaused: 'refused',

    // 3. Start
    listStartable: () => http.call('GET', '/workflows/startable'),
    startForm: ({ workflow, version }) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}/start-form${query({ version })}`),
    start: (args) =>
      http.call('POST', '/requests', {
        workflow: args.workflow,
        ...(args.version === undefined ? {} : { version: args.version }),
        button: args.button,
        answers: args.answers,
        clientToken: args.clientToken,
      }),
    choices: (args) => http.call('POST', '/choices', args),

    // 4. Tasks
    myTasks: (args = {}) => http.call('GET', `/my-tasks${query({ cursor: args.cursor, limit: args.limit })}`),
    getTask: ({ requestId, task }) => http.call('GET', `${request(requestId)}${path('tasks', task)}`),
    act: ({ requestId, task, button, answers }) => http.call('POST', `${request(requestId)}${path('tasks', task)}/act`, { button, answers }),

    // 5. Stuck requests, bindings and refused starts
    retry: ({ requestId, reason, expectedLastSeq }) => http.call('POST', `${request(requestId)}/retry`, { reason, expectedLastSeq }),
    close: ({ requestId, reason, expectedLastSeq }) => http.call('POST', `${request(requestId)}/close`, { reason, expectedLastSeq }),
    listBindings: ({ workflow }) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}/bindings`),
    setBindingPaused: ({ workflow, binding, paused }) => http.call('PUT', `${wf(workflow)}${path('bindings', binding)}`, { paused }),
    listPausedDeliveries: ({ workflow, binding }) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}${path('bindings', binding)}/paused-deliveries`),
    listRefusedStarts: (args) => http.call('GET', `/refused-starts${query({ workflow: args.workflow, cursor: args.cursor, limit: args.limit })}`),
    retryRefusedStart: ({ id }) => http.call('POST', `${path('refused-starts', id)}/retry`),

    // 6. Reads
    publishedSource: ({ workflow, version }) => http.call('GET', `${wf(workflow)}${path('versions', version)}/source`),
    listRequests: (q) => http.call('GET', `/requests${requestQueryString(q)}`),
    getRequest: (args) => {
      const debug = args.debug ? '?debug=true' : '';
      return 'requestId' in args
        ? http.call('GET', `${request(args.requestId)}${debug}`)
        : http.call('GET', `${path('requests', 'by-number', args.readableId)}${debug}`);
    },
  };
}
