  lookups: KnownLookups;
  completed?: { by: By; at: Timestamp; button: ButtonId; answers: Answers; asMemberOf: Ref[] };
  /** The answers given the last time this task was asked in this request (sent back). */
  earlierAnswers?: Answers;
  /** For the signed-in person, before any answer. */
  buttonStates: ButtonState[];
  lastSeq: Seq;
}

export interface ActArgs {
  requestId: RequestId;
  task: TaskInstanceId;
  button: ButtonId;
  answers: Answers;
}

/** After a turn (act, retry, close). */
export interface TurnDone {
  requestId: RequestId;
  lastSeq: Seq;
  /** The request is stuck after this turn, for any reason (it may already have been; the answer is still recorded). */
  stopped: boolean;
}

// ── Stuck requests (runtime-api.md 5.1) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface AdminArgs {
  requestId: RequestId;
  /** 1 to 2000 characters after trimming; recorded. */
  reason: string;
  /** The `lastSeq` of the page the person acted from; refused with `stale` if the request moved since. */
  expectedLastSeq: Seq;
}

// ── Bindings ("Starts when", runtime-api.md 5.3) ──────────────────────────────────────────────

export interface BindingState {
  binding: StartsWhenId;
  trigger: CatalogueRef;
  /** The highest published version: only its bindings are live. */
  version: VersionNumber;
  paused: boolean;
  /** Deliveries answered `paused` in the last 30 days, run again on resume. */
  held: number;
  /** Who last paused or resumed it. Absent: never paused. */
  changedBy?: Ref;
  changedAt?: Timestamp;
}

/** A binding after a pause or resume. `rerun` and `gone` are present on a resume. */
export type BindingChanged = BindingState & {
  /** The paused deliveries run again. */
  rerun?: number;
  /** Paused deliveries older than 30 days, not run again. */
  gone?: number;
};

/** A delivery a paused binding holds. */
export interface PausedDelivery {
  /** Opaque; names one delivery and one workflow. */
  id: string;
  binding: StartsWhenId;
  /** The sender's ID for the event. */
  eventId: string;
  /** When the delivery was received. */
  at: Timestamp;
}

// ── Refused starts (runtime-api.md 5.4) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

export type RefusedStartId = string;

/**
 * A "Starts when" start refused finally in the last 30 days. `code` and `params` are the first
 * problem's, typed as in `ApiErrorParams`. `location`: the binding part, the question or the
 * button, in the version that refused it.
 */
export type RefusedStart = Coded<
  Pick<ApiErrorParams, StartsWhenRefusalCode> & { paused: Record<string, never> },
  { id: RefusedStartId; workflow: ServerWorkflowId; startsWhen: StartsWhenId; at: Timestamp; location?: Location }
>;

/** Why a "Starts when" start is listed as refused: a final refusal, or `paused` (its binding was paused, E-33; location: the binding). */
export type RefusedStartCode = RefusedStart['code'];

/**
 * What a paused "Starts when" does with what its other system sends. `kept`: held, and run again
 * by itself on Resume (the stand-in). `refused`: the other system is told the start was refused,
 * the start is listed with the refused starts (reason `paused`) and runs only when someone runs it
 * again after Resume; nothing is held (the engine's server, E-33).
 */
export type WhilePaused = 'kept' | 'refused';

/** What running a refused start again gave. */
export type RetriedStart =
  | { result: 'started'; requestId: RequestId; readableId: ReadableId; binding: StartsWhenId; version: VersionNumber }
  /** Already started by this delivery. */
  | { result: 'duplicate'; requestId: RequestId; readableId: ReadableId }
  /** No binding's "only when" was true. */
  | { result: 'notMatched' }
  | { result: 'paused'; binding: StartsWhenId }
  | { result: 'refused'; binding: StartsWhenId; refusals: Refusal[] };

// ── Reads (runtime-api.md 6) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** A published version's document, to turn locations into words and render forms. Never changes. */
export interface PublishedSource {
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;
  authored: AuthoredWorkflow;
  publishedAt: Timestamp;
  publishedBy: Ref;
}

export interface RequestQuery extends PageArgs {
  workflow?: ServerWorkflowId;
  /** Needs `workflow`. */
  status?: StatusId[];
  /** Needs `workflow`. */
  version?: VersionNumber;
  /** Absent: both. */
  state?: 'open' | 'closed';
  /** `true`: the stuck list. Open to everyone; showing it only to admins is the page's choice. */
  stuck?: boolean;
  /** A person's directory ID. */
  startedBy?: string;
  /** Needs `workflow`; all must hold. Equality only; JSON per core-api.md 2.4. */
  valueEquals?: { value: ValueId; equals: Json }[];
  /** Values to return per row, at most 10. */
  include?: ValueId[];
  /** Default `readableId`. */
  sort?: 'readableId' | 'startedAt' | 'updatedAt';
  /** Default `desc`. */
  order?: 'asc' | 'desc';
}

export interface RequestRow {
  requestId: RequestId;
  readableId: ReadableId;
  workflow: ServerWorkflowId;
  version: VersionNumber;
  status?: Status;
  /** Where it is now: `{ item: StageId, part? }` as in `RequestView`. */
  stage: Location;
  startedBy: By;
  startedAt: Timestamp;
  updatedAt: Timestamp;
  closedAt?: Timestamp;
  /** Reason, at, location; never the admin detail. */
  stuck?: ListedStuck;
  /** Only the values asked for with `include`. */
  values?: Values;
  lastSeq: Seq;
}

/** `debug`: fill `StoryEntry.debug` (platform admins only). */
export type GetRequestArgs = ({ requestId: RequestId } | { readableId: ReadableId }) & { debug?: boolean };

// ── The inbound endpoint's answer (runtime-api.md 8), for the development host ────────────────

/** A problem of a refused inbound start. Typed as in `ApiErrorParams`. `where` is `null` when no place applies. */
export type InboundProblem = Coded<Pick<ApiErrorParams, StartsWhenRefusalCode>, { where: Location | null }>;

/** What happened in one candidate workflow. `readableId` is a number here, as other systems receive it. */
export type InboundResult =
  | { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber; result: 'started'; binding: StartsWhenId; requestId: RequestId; readableId: number }
  /** This event had already started a request in this workflow. */
  | { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber; result: 'duplicate'; binding: StartsWhenId; requestId: RequestId; readableId: number }
  /** No binding's "only when" was true. */
  | { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber; result: 'notMatched' }
  /** The first matching binding is paused; the delivery is held. */
  | { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber; result: 'paused'; binding: StartsWhenId }
  | { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber; result: 'refused'; binding: StartsWhenId; problems: InboundProblem[] };

/** The inbound endpoint's 200 answer: one result per candidate workflow, in workflow ID order. Keeps its `null`s. */
export interface InboundAnswer {
  /** `null` only for an ignored delivery without an ID. */
  eventId: string | null;
  results: InboundResult[];
}

/**
 * The inbound endpoint's other answers (`{ "error": code }`). 503 ones (`connection-unavailable`,
 * `unavailable`) are "try again".
 */
export type InboundErrorCode =
  | 'too-large' | 'unknown-connection' | 'connection-unavailable' | 'unauthenticated' | 'unparsable'
  | 'event-invalid' | 'unavailable';

/** An inbound refusal as a coded record, so it fits `Result`. */
export type InboundError = Coded<{ [C in InboundErrorCode]: Record<string, never> }, Record<never, never>>;

// ── The service ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** Every call is made as the signed-in person (`SessionService`). Refusals are results, never exceptions. */
export interface RuntimeService {
  /** What a paused "Starts when" does with what is sent while it is paused (`WhilePaused`). */
  readonly whilePaused: WhilePaused;
  /** Workflows with a published version, by name. */
  listStartable(): Promise<Result<StartableWorkflow[]>>;
  /** Refused `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`). */
  startForm(args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version?: VersionNumber }): Promise<Result<StartForm>>;
  /** Refusals: `StartRefusalCode`, the first failing step's. */
  start(args: StartArgs): Promise<Result<StartResult>>;
  /** Not recorded. Refused `not-found`, `invalid-body` (not a directory or source question), `wait-not-open`, `source-unavailable`. */
  choices(args: ChoicesArgs): Promise<Result<ChoicesPage>>;
  /** The signed-in person's open tasks, oldest first. */
  myTasks(args?: PageArgs): Promise<Result<MyTasksPage>>;
  /** Refused `not-found` (`request`, `task`). */
  getTask(args: { requestId: RequestId; task: TaskInstanceId }): Promise<Result<TaskView>>;
  /** Refusals: `ActRefusalCode`, the first failing step's. */
  act(args: ActArgs): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  /** Only for a request stuck with `action-failed` or `nobody-to-ask`. Refusals: `AdminRefusalCode`. */
  retry(args: AdminArgs): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  /** Any open request, stuck or not. Refusals: `AdminRefusalCode` minus the retry-only ones. */
  close(args: AdminArgs): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  /** The live version's bindings, document order; `[]` when never published. Anyone signed in. */
  listBindings(args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId }): Promise<Result<BindingState[]>>;
  /** Pause or resume without publishing. Refused `not-found`, `not-admin`, `membership-unavailable`. */
  setBindingPaused(args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; binding: StartsWhenId; paused: boolean }): Promise<Result<BindingChanged>>;
  /** Oldest first. Admins only. */
  listPausedDeliveries(args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; binding: StartsWhenId }): Promise<Result<PausedDelivery[]>>;
  /** Newest first, last 30 days. Without `workflow`: the workflows the caller looks after. */
  listRefusedStarts(args: { workflow?: ServerWorkflowId } & PageArgs): Promise<Result<Page<RefusedStart>>>;
  /** Runs the start again on the live version's bindings. Refused `not-found` (`refusedStart`), `not-admin`, and the try-again codes. */
  retryRefusedStart(args: { id: RefusedStartId }): Promise<Result<RetriedStart>>;
  /** Refused `not-found` (`workflow`, `version`). */
  publishedSource(args: { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber }): Promise<Result<PublishedSource>>;
  listRequests(query: RequestQuery): Promise<Result<Page<RequestRow>>>;
  /** Refused `not-found` (`request`). */
  getRequest(args: GetRequestArgs): Promise<Result<RequestView>>;
}

/**
 * Try it's test host (core-api.md section 10): runs a test request on a draft in the browser,
 * acting as anyone, with every other system pretended and everything that would have been sent
 * collected in a Test outbox. Also the codes of the platform's built-in messages (the keys of
 * contract/words/notifications.json).
 *
 * The fakes, the outbox and the built-in messages are core's own types. `TestHost` and
 * `HostResult` are written here, because the services interface is async (F4): each method is

  Json, Location, OpenTask, OutboxEntry, Ref, Refusal, RequestId, RequestView, ServerWorkflowId, StartFromResult,
  StartsWhenId, StageId, TaskInstanceId, Timestamp, TurnResult, VersionNumber, ActionId, Answers, ChoicesArgs, ChoicesPage,
} from '@workflow/core';
import type { InboundErrorCode } from './types-runtime';

export type {
  BuiltInMessage, BuiltInTold, CallAnswer, CallFake, Fakes, MessagePart, OutboxEntry, StartFromResult,
} from '@workflow/core';

/** A failure as a failed call is recorded. `message` absent: the sample's message when the code matches, else `""`. */
export type CallFailure = Extract<CallFake, { mode: 'fail' }>['error'];

// ── Built-in messages (core-api.md 10.3, contract/words/notifications.json) ───────────────────

/**
 * Params per built-in message code: the keys of `contract/words/notifications.json`. Core's three
 * (the ones a Try it request sends) plus the `alert.*` ones, which the server's workers send and
 * whose params are chosen here (CONTRACT-NOTES.md).
 */
export interface BuiltInMessageParams extends CoreBuiltInMessageParams {
  'alert.call-overdue': { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; entry: CatalogueRef; connection: string };
  'alert.job-left-running': { request: RequestId; workflow: ServerWorkflowId; stage: StageId; action: ActionId };
  'alert.rule-failed': { workflow: ServerWorkflowId; version: VersionNumber; action: ActionId };
  'alert.call-outcome-unknown': { request: RequestId; workflow: ServerWorkflowId; action: ActionId; connection: string };
  'alert.publish-failed': { request: RequestId; workflow: ServerWorkflowId };
  'alert.inbound-refused': { connection: string; code: InboundErrorCode };
  'alert.delivery-stuck': { connection: string };
  'alert.directory-unavailable': { connection: string };
  'alert.source-unavailable': { entry: CatalogueRef; connection: string };
  'alert.catalogue-rejected': { entry: CatalogueRef; connection: string };
  'alert.subscription-failing': { subscription: string };
}

export type BuiltInMessageCode = keyof BuiltInMessageParams;

/** The built-in messages a Try it request can send (alerts come from the server's workers only). */
export type TryItMessageCode = keyof CoreBuiltInMessageParams;

// ── The host ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * One Try it session on one draft. Held in memory only. `as` is the person acted as. Refusals are
 * the runtime's codes in the runtime's order; a refusal is a result (`ok: false`), never a
 * rejected promise. `membership-unavailable` and `source-unavailable` never occur.
 */
export interface TestHost {
  /** A person submits the start form. Refused `unfinished` when the start task has a To do that stops it. */
  start(as: Ref, button: ButtonId, answers: Answers, at?: Timestamp): Promise<TurnResult<{ requestId: RequestId }>>;
  /**
   * Another system starts a request through a binding with what it sent (field id to value).
   * Refusals: `not-found` (`binding`), `unfinished`, `mapping-error`, `invalid-data`, `choice-unknown`,
   * `check`, `rule-error`; a refused start also puts one `start.refused` message in the outbox.
   */
  startFrom(binding: StartsWhenId, sent: Record<string, Json>, at?: Timestamp): Promise<TurnResult<StartFromResult>>;
  /** Choices of a directory or data-source question, from the fakes (runtime-api.md 3.4). Other questions: `[]`. */
  choices(args: ChoicesArgs): Promise<ChoicesPage>;
  /**
   * Tasks waiting for an answer, across test requests or for one, optionally only those asking one
   * person. `buttonStates` are for `as`; without `as` they are `[]`.
   */
  openTasks(filter?: { requestId?: RequestId; askedOf?: Ref; as?: Ref }): Promise<OpenTask[]>;
  /** `as` presses a button. */
  act(as: Ref, requestId: RequestId, task: TaskInstanceId, button: ButtonId, answers: Answers, at?: Timestamp): Promise<TurnResult>;
  /**
   * Retry or close a test request, as one of `Fakes.stuckRequestsGoTo` (else `not-admin`). Retry
   * only for `action-failed` and `nobody-to-ask` (else `not-stuck` / `not-retryable`); close for any open request.
   */
  admin(as: Ref, requestId: RequestId, action: 'retry' | 'close', reason: string, at?: Timestamp): Promise<TurnResult>;
  /** Answers a held call. */
  answerCall(call: CallRef, answer: CallAnswer, at?: Timestamp): Promise<TurnResult>;
  /** How an operation is pretended for calls opened from now on. */
  setCallFake(operation: CatalogueRef, fake: CallFake): Promise<void>;
  /** Everything that would have been sent, oldest first. */
  outbox(requestId?: RequestId): Promise<OutboxEntry[]>;
  /**
   * The test request as its page shows it, story included (with `why` on every move), seen by
   * `as`: `buttonStates` are theirs, and `viewer.isAdmin` (and `stuck.admin`) when `as` is in
   * `stuckRequestsGoTo`. Without `as` the button states are `[]`. A request this host does not hold
   * answers `{ ok: false, refusals: [not-found] }` (`what: "request"`): narrow on `"ok" in result`.
   */
  request(requestId: RequestId, as?: Ref): Promise<RequestView | { ok: false; refusals: Refusal[] }>;
}

/**
 * A new host, or the workflow-level To dos that stop Try it altogether (`workflow.noStart`,
 * `start.notOneTask`, `compile.internal`). `unfinished`: the parts with a To do that stops a
 * request from running; a request that gets there is stuck with `unfinished`.
 */
export type HostResult =
  | { ok: true; host: TestHost; unfinished: Location[]; findings: Finding[] }
  | { ok: false; findings: Finding[] };

/**
 * Type-level checks for the services interface: the types are core's own (`@workflow/core`),
 * src/contract's types are the very types core re-exports (assignable both ways, so the repo's
 * contract/ files and core's copy of them can never drift apart unnoticed), the hand-written
 * shapes match core's where they wrap it, and the shared shapes accept what the contract's
 * examples hold. Most checks are compile-time (`npx tsc --noEmit`); the runtime part only proves the
 * sample values below are well formed.
 */
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type * as Core from '@workflow/core';
import type * as Contract from '@/contract';
import type {
  ApiError, BuiltInMessageCode, Change, ChoicesPage, EvaluateResult, Finding, FormStateResult, InboundAnswer,
  ListedStuck, OutboxEntry, ParseProblem, RefusedStart, RequestView, Result, RetryableStuckReason, Services,
  StoryEntry, Stuck, TestHost, TurnResult,
} from './types';

/** Fails to compile unless A and B are the same type. */
type Equal<A, B> = (<T>() => T extends A ? 1 : 2) extends (<T>() => T extends B ? 1 : 2) ? true : false;
/** Fails to compile unless A and B are assignable to each other. */
type Same<A, B> = [A] extends [B] ? ([B] extends [A] ? true : false) : false;
function assertType<T extends true>(): T | undefined {
  return undefined;
}

/** Narrowing on `code` gives typed params. */
function describeFinding(f: Finding): string {
  switch (f.code) {
    case 'value.mayBeEmpty':
      assertType<Equal<typeof f.params.value, Contract.Location>>();
      return f.params.value.item;
    case 'arrow.neverUsed':
      return f.params.reason;
    default:
      return f.code;
  }
}

function describeError(e: ApiError): string {
  // Core types the current draft `unknown`: the Draft is the server's (authoring-api.md 3).
  if (e.code === 'stale-revision') return String(e.params.draft.revision);
  if (e.code === 'has-todo') return String(e.params.findings.length);
  if (e.code === 'not-retryable') return e.params.reason;
  return e.code;
}

/** Retry is offered only for the two retryable reasons. */
function offersRetry(s: Stuck): s is Stuck & { reason: RetryableStuckReason } {
  return s.reason === 'action-failed' || s.reason === 'nobody-to-ask';
}

===\nfrontend/src/services/types.ts\n===
/**
 * The one async interface the whole frontend calls to reach the engine side (F4), matching the
 * engine owner's Draft 3 (contract/core-api.md, authoring-api.md, runtime-api.md, catalogue.ts).
 * Two implementations sit behind it: the in-browser stand-in and the real client. Types only.
 *
 * Every function is async, even what the core computes synchronously. Expected refusals are
 * results (`ok: false`), never exceptions; a rejected promise means the call could not be made.
 * What differs from the drafts on purpose, and what is still open: CONTRACT-NOTES.md.
 */
import type { ActionId, Catalogue, CatalogueRef, DirectoryApi } from '@/contract';
import type { Ref, RequestId, Result, Timestamp } from './types-common';
import type { AuthoringService } from './types-authoring';
import type { CoreService } from './types-core';
import type { InboundAnswer, InboundError, RuntimeService, TurnDone } from './types-runtime';

export type * from './types-common';
export type * from './types-errors';
export type * from './types-findings';
export type * from './types-core';
export type * from './types-story';
export type * from './types-request';
export type * from './types-testhost';
export type * from './types-authoring';
export type * from './types-runtime';

/**
 * The catalogue of connections, as set up by a platform admin (authoring-api.md operation 11,
 * `GET {base}/catalogue`). Read-only to the editor; `directoryConnection` names the directory.
 */
export interface CatalogueService {
  getCatalogue(): Promise<Result<Catalogue>>;
}

/**
 * People and groups (catalogue.ts `DirectoryApi`; runtime-api.md 7): search, names for references,
 * a group's people. Rejects when the directory cannot be reached (`membership-unavailable` over HTTP).
 */
export type DirectoryService = DirectoryApi;

/** The signed-in person (runtime-api.md 7). */
export interface Person {
  ref: Ref;
  /** Display name. */
  label: string;
  /** Holds the platform's admin entitlement: may do everything an author or a stuck-requests person may. */
  platformAdmin: boolean;
}

/**
 * Who is signed in (runtime-api.md 7, development-host HTTP). `whoAmI` and `people` are unwrapped
 * from their `Result`: they fail only when the call cannot be made. Outside the development host
 * `signInAs` is refused with `forbidden` (`need: 'devHost'`) and `people` gives an empty list.
 */
export interface SessionService {
  whoAmI(): Promise<Person>;
  signInAs(person: Ref): Promise<Result<Person>>;
  /** The people the development host offers to switch to. */
  people(): Promise<Person[]>;
}

/**
 * The development host only: things a real deployment does not offer.
 */
export interface DevService {
  /**
   * "Pretend this other system sent this now": delivers one event of the trigger `entry` to the
   * inbound endpoint, with `sent` as its fields (absent: the trigger's catalogue sample event).
   * Answers as the inbound endpoint does: per candidate workflow started, `notMatched` (did not
   * fit), `refused` with its problems, `duplicate` (already started) or `paused`; or one of the
   * endpoint's own refusals. Today the stand-in answers; later the mock system's control call.
   */
  sendSample(entry: CatalogueRef, sent?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<Result<InboundAnswer, InboundError>>;
  /**
   * "Pretend <connection> answered now": the other system answers an action a request is waiting
   * on (a "Wait for", held until answered), as it would: succeeded with the operation's catalogue
   * sample result, or failed with one of the operation's catalogue failure codes. The engine then
   * carries the request on. Refused `not-found` (`request`; `call` when that action is not waiting),
   * `invalid-body` (`/answer/code`) for a code the operation does not have.
   */
  answerWaiting(args: { requestId: RequestId; action: ActionId; answer: WaitingAnswer }): Promise<Result<TurnDone>>;
  /**
   * Whether `sendSample` can deliver an event of this trigger on this engine. Absent: always. The
   * engine's development host can only make its mock systems send (and only when it offers its
   * development controls); a trigger it cannot send for is "not available on this engine".
   */
  canSendSample?(entry: CatalogueRef): Promise<boolean>;
  /**
   * The trigger's fields `sendSample` passes on; the other system fills the rest in itself.
   * Absent (or `undefined`): every field.
   */
  sampleFields?(entry: CatalogueRef): readonly string[] | undefined;
  /** The engine's address when the services talk to a real engine over HTTP. Absent: the in-browser stand-in. */
  engineAddress?: string;
  /**
   * Throws every change and request away and starts again from the sample workflows. Absent: this
   * engine cannot be reset from the page (the development host starts from nothing when restarted).
   */
  resetSampleData?(): void;
  /**
   * Starts a few sample requests as the sample people, so the lists are not empty (the development
   * host over HTTP; the stand-in starts with its own). Says what it added and what it left out.
   */
  addSampleRequests?(): Promise<SampleRequestsReport>;
  /** The development host's mock systems: their switches and what they received. Absent: not offered. */
  mocks?: MockSystems;
}

/** How another system answers a waiting action in `dev.answerWaiting`. */
export type WaitingAnswer = { outcome: 'ok' } | { outcome: 'failed'; code: string };

/** One sample request `addSampleRequests` adds, by what it shows. */
export type SampleRequestKind = 'waitingForApproval' | 'inDevelopment' | 'nobodyToAsk' | 'finished' | 'refusedStart' | 'actionFailed';

export interface SampleRequestsReport {
  /** What was added; `readableId` absent for a refused start (it is no request). */
  added: { kind: SampleRequestKind; readableId?: string }[];
  /** What was left out: the engine does not offer what it needs, or a step was refused. */
  skipped: { kind: SampleRequestKind; why: 'notOffered' | 'failed' }[];
}

/** A mock system's switches (the development host's `/dev/mocks`). */
export interface MockSwitches {
  /** The next call fails clearly; resets after that call. */
  failNext?: boolean;
  /** Every call goes unanswered until switched back. */
  down?: boolean;
}

export interface MockSystem {
  connection: string;
  label: string;
  switches: MockSwitches;
}

/** How a mock system answered a call (engine/DEV-HOST.md, "Controlling the mocks from the browser"). */
export type MockCallAnswer =
  | { answer: 'ok'; data: Record<string, unknown>; jobRef?: string }
  | { answer: 'failed'; code: string; message: string; jobRef?: string }
  | { answer: 'accepted'; jobRef: string }
  /** Status questions only. */
  | { answer: 'running'; jobRef: string }
  /** No answer: the mock is down. */
  | { answer: 'none'; detail: string };

/** A call a mock system received (jira, deploy, servicecatalog, directory). */
export interface MockCall {
  /** When it was answered. */
  at: Timestamp;
  /** The request whose call it is. */
  request: RequestId | null;
  /** E.g. `createIssue@1`. */
  operation: string;
  /** `status`: a "Wait for" action's status question. */
  kind: 'call' | 'status';
  /** The idempotency key it was sent with. */
  key: string;
  /** The call's input as sent; for a status question `{ jobRef }`. */
  input: Record<string, unknown>;
  answer: MockCallAnswer;
}

/** A message the mock messages system received: one per person. */
export interface MockMessage {
  at: Timestamp;
  request: RequestId;
  /** The notification rule, or the platform's built-in code. */
  rule: string;
  /** The person's directory ID. */
  to: string;
  /** Exactly as sent. */
  message: { words: string } | { parts: ({ text: string } | { kind: string; value?: unknown })[] };
}

/**
 * The development host's mock systems (`{engine}/dev`, engine/DEV-HOST.md). `offered()` probes
 * once whether this engine has them; every other call rejects when it does not, or when the host
 * refuses (its one-line reason is the error's message).
 */
export interface MockSystems {
  /** Whether this engine offers the mock controls (probed once). */
  offered(): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Every mock, in catalogue order, with only the switches it has. */
  list(): Promise<MockSystem[]>;
  /** Sets switches of one mock; answers its entry. */
  set(connection: string, switches: MockSwitches): Promise<MockSystem>;
  /** The calls a calling mock received (`jira`, `deploy`, `servicecatalog`, `directory`), oldest first; `request` narrows to one request. */
  calls(connection: string, request?: RequestId): Promise<MockCall[]>;
  /** The messages sent, oldest first. */
  messages(request?: RequestId): Promise<MockMessage[]>;
  /** The outbound events posted to the reporting mock, oldest first, each body exactly as posted. */
  events(request?: RequestId): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>;
}

export interface Services {
  core: CoreService;
  authoring: AuthoringService;
  runtime: RuntimeService;
  catalogue: CatalogueService;
  directory: DirectoryService;
  session: SessionService;
  /** Present on the development host only. */
  dev?: DevService;
}

import { forwardRef, type ButtonHTMLAttributes, type MouseEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Icon, type IconName } from './Icon';
import { Tooltip } from './Tooltip';
import s from './Button.module.css';

export type ButtonVariant = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'quiet' | 'danger';
export type ButtonSize = 'sm' | 'md';

/** The class names of a button, for a link that must look like one (e.g. a router link). */
export function buttonClass(variant: ButtonVariant = 'secondary', size: ButtonSize = 'md', extra?: string) {
  return [s.btn, s[variant], size === 'sm' ? s.sm : undefined, extra].filter(Boolean).join(' ');
}

type ButtonProps = Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, 'disabled'> & {
  variant?: ButtonVariant;
  size?: ButtonSize;
  icon?: IconName;
  /** Small text after the label, e.g. "· 2 to do first" on a blocked Publish. */
  after?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Why the button cannot be pressed. When given, the button is greyed but still focusable,
   * and the reason shows as a tooltip and is read out with the label.
   */
  disabledReason?: string;
  children?: ReactNode;
};

export const Button = forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(function Button(
  { variant = 'secondary', size = 'md', icon, after, disabledReason, className, children, onClick, type = 'button', ...rest },
  ref,
) {
  const blocked = Boolean(disabledReason);
  const button = (
    <button
      ref={ref}
      type={type}
      className={buttonClass(variant, size, [blocked ? s.blocked : undefined, className].filter(Boolean).join(' '))}
      aria-disabled={blocked || undefined}
      onClick={(e: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
        if (blocked) {
          e.preventDefault();
          return;
        }
        onClick?.(e);
      }}
      {...rest}
    >
      {icon && <Icon name={icon} size={size === 'sm' ? 14 : 16} />}
      {children}
      {after && <span className={s.after}>{after}</span>}
      {blocked && <span className="visually-hidden">: {disabledReason}</span>}
    </button>
  );
  return blocked ? <Tooltip content={disabledReason}>{button}</Tooltip> : button;
});

type IconButtonProps = Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, 'children'> & {
  icon: IconName;
  /** Read out and shown as a tooltip: an icon alone never explains itself. */
  label: string;
  variant?: ButtonVariant;
  size?: ButtonSize;
  /** false for a button whose icon needs no explaining and that receives focus on open (a close button). */
  tooltip?: boolean;
};

export const IconButton = forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, IconButtonProps>(function IconButton(
  { icon, label, variant = 'quiet', size = 'md', tooltip = true, className, type = 'button', ...rest },
  ref,
) {
  const button = (
    <button
      ref={ref}
      type={type}
      aria-label={label}
      className={buttonClass(variant, size, [s.icon, className].filter(Boolean).join(' '))}
      {...rest}
    >
      <Icon name={icon} size={size === 'sm' ? 14 : 16} />
    </button>
  );
  return tooltip ? <Tooltip content={label}>{button}</Tooltip> : button;
});

import type { HTMLAttributes, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Icon, type IconName } from './Icon';
import s from './Card.module.css';

type CardProps = Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, 'title'> & {
  /** Optional heading row. */
  title?: ReactNode;
  /** Quiet line under the title. */
  sub?: ReactNode;
  /** Controls on the right of the heading row. */
  actions?: ReactNode;
  /** No inner padding (for lists and tables that run edge to edge). */
  flush?: boolean;
  as?: 'section' | 'div' | 'article';
};

export function Card({ title, sub, actions, flush, as: Tag = 'section', className, children, ...rest }: CardProps) {
  return (
    <Tag className={[s.card, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')} {...rest}>
      {(title || actions) && (
        <header className={s.head}>
          <div className={s.headText}>
            {title && <h2 className={s.title}>{title}</h2>}
            {sub && <p className={s.sub}>{sub}</p>}
          </div>
          {actions}
        </header>
      )}
      <div className={flush ? undefined : s.body}>{children}</div>
    </Tag>
  );
}

type EmptyStateProps = {
  icon?: IconName;
  title: ReactNode;
  children?: ReactNode;
  /** A button or link that starts the thing that is missing. */
  action?: ReactNode;
};

/** What is (not yet) here, said plainly, with the way forward. */
export function EmptyState({ icon = 'info', title, children, action }: EmptyStateProps) {
  return (
    <div className={s.empty}>
      <div className={s.emptyIcon}>
        <Icon name={icon} size={22} />
      </div>
      <div className={s.emptyTitle}>{title}</div>
      {children && <div className={s.emptyText}>{children}</div>}
      {action && <div className={s.emptyAction}>{action}</div>}
    </div>
  );
}

type CalloutProps = {
  /** neutral: a plain note (grey). info: worth reading (accent). todo: needs doing (amber). danger: something went wrong (red). */
  tone?: 'neutral' | 'info' | 'todo' | 'danger';
  icon?: IconName;
  children: ReactNode;
  /** Controls at the end of the line (e.g. Copy, Print). */
  actions?: ReactNode;
};

const toneIcon: Record<NonNullable<CalloutProps['tone']>, IconName> = {
  neutral: 'info',
  info: 'info',
  todo: 'todo',
  danger: 'error',
};

export function Callout({ tone = 'neutral', icon, children, actions }: CalloutProps) {
  return (
    <div className={`${s.callout} ${s[tone]}`} role={tone === 'danger' ? 'alert' : undefined}>
      <Icon name={icon ?? toneIcon[tone]} />
      <div className={s.calloutText}>{children}</div>
      {actions && <div className={s.calloutActions}>{actions}</div>}
    </div>
  );
}

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Icon, type IconName } from './Icon';
import s from './Chip.module.css';

export type ValueKind = 'text' | 'longtext' | 'number' | 'yesno' | 'date' | 'choice' | 'multichoice' | 'person' | 'group';

type ChipProps = {
  children: ReactNode;
  /**
   * value: a value (tinted, with its kind's icon). button: a task's button.
   * action: something the workflow does by itself (bolt, its own tint, never read as a button).
   * person / group: someone from the directory.
   */
  variant?: 'value' | 'button' | 'action' | 'person' | 'group';
  /** For a value: its kind, shown as the icon. */
  kind?: ValueKind;
  /** Quiet text after the name, e.g. the stage a value comes from. */
  src?: ReactNode;
  size?: 'sm' | 'md';
  /** Makes the chip a button (e.g. a value chip opens its card). */
  onClick?: () => void;
  /** Read out when the chip is a button, if the name alone is not enough. */
  label?: string;
};

const variantIcon: Partial<Record<NonNullable<ChipProps['variant']>, IconName>> = {
  action: 'bolt',
  person: 'person',
  group: 'group',
};

export function Chip({ children, variant = 'value', kind, src, size = 'md', onClick, label }: ChipProps) {
  const icon: IconName | undefined = variant === 'value' ? (kind ?? 'text') : variantIcon[variant];
  const className = [s.chip, s[variant], size === 'sm' ? s.sm : undefined].filter(Boolean).join(' ');
  const inner = (
    <>
      {icon && <Icon name={icon} size={size === 'sm' ? 13 : 14} />}
      <span className={s.name}>{children}</span>
      {src && <span className={s.src}>{src}</span>}
    </>
  );
  return onClick ? (
    <button type="button" className={className} onClick={onClick} aria-label={label}>
      {inner}
    </button>
  ) : (
    <span className={className}>{inner}</span>
  );
}

/** DateField: a date shown and typed as "2 Dec 2026", read leniently, with a calendar button. */
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { DateField, formatDateText, parseDateText } from './DateField';

describe('parseDateText and formatDateText', () => {
  it('reads a date as people write it, and only a real calendar day', () => {
    for (const typed of ['2 Dec 2026', '2 dec 2026', '2 December 2026', 'Dec 2, 2026', '2/12/2026', '02.12.2026', '2026-12-02', ' 2  Dec.  2026 ']) {
      expect(parseDateText(typed), typed).toBe('2026-12-02');
    }
    for (const typed of ['', 'soon', '31 Feb 2026', '2 Xyz 2026', '13/13/2026', '2026-02-30']) expect(parseDateText(typed), typed).toBeUndefined();
    expect(parseDateText('29 Feb 2028')).toBe('2028-02-29');
  });

  it('writes a date as the editor does everywhere', () => {
    expect(formatDateText('2026-12-02')).toBe('2 Dec 2026');
    expect(formatDateText(undefined)).toBe('');
  });
});

function Harness({ onAnswer }: { onAnswer(v: string | undefined): void }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | undefined>('2026-12-02');
  return (
    <>
      <label htmlFor="d">Planned release date</label>
      <DateField
        id="d"
        value={value}
        onChange={(next) => {
          setValue(next);
          onAnswer(next);
        }}
        calendarLabel="Choose the date for Planned release date from a calendar"
        invalidText="Write a date such as 2 Dec 2026."
      />
    </>
  );
}

describe('DateField', () => {
  it('shows "2 Dec 2026", answers as it is typed, and says so when what is typed is not a date', () => {
    const onAnswer = vi.fn();
    render(<Harness onAnswer={onAnswer} />);
    const box = screen.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Planned release date' });
    expect(box).toHaveValue('2 Dec 2026');
    fireEvent.change(box, { target: { value: '5/1/2027' } });
    expect(onAnswer).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('2027-01-05');
    fireEvent.blur(box);
    expect(box).toHaveValue('5 Jan 2027');
    fireEvent.change(box, { target: { value: 'next week' } });
    expect(onAnswer).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(undefined);
    fireEvent.blur(box);
    expect(box).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    expect(box).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Write a date such as 2 Dec 2026.');
    fireEvent.change(box, { target: { value: '' } });
    expect(box).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid');
  });

  it('has one calendar button, named for its date; the browser\'s own box is never reached or read', () => {
    render(<Harness onAnswer={() => undefined} />);
    expect(screen.getAllByRole('button')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Choose the date for Planned release date from a calendar' })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getAllByRole('textbox')).toHaveLength(1);
    const picker = document.querySelector('input[type="date"]')!;
    expect(picker).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
    expect(picker).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    // A date picked from the calendar is shown as the editor writes it.
    fireEvent.change(picker, { target: { value: '2027-03-09' } });
    expect(screen.getByRole('textbox')).toHaveValue('9 Mar 2027');
  });
});
===\nfrontend/src/ui/DateField.tsx\n===
/**
 * A date as people write it, in one text box with one accessible name: it shows "2 Dec 2026" and
 * reads what is typed leniently ("2 Dec 2026", "2 december 2026", "Dec 2 2026", "2/12/2026",
 * "2.12.2026", "2026-12-02"), plus a calendar button beside it that opens the browser's own date
 * picker. The browser's date box itself is not shown: it writes dates in the browser's own format
 * and adds unnamed parts ("Month", "Day", "Year") that read the same for every date on a page.
 * The value is `YYYY-MM-DD` (core-api.md 2.4), or undefined for none.
 */
import { forwardRef, useId, useRef, useState, type InputHTMLAttributes } from 'react';
import { t } from '@/words';
import { Icon } from './Icon';
import s from './DateField.module.css';
import f from './Field.module.css';

const ISO = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/;

/** The short month names, January first: the words the editor writes dates with everywhere. */
const months = (): string[] => t('describe.months').split(' ');

/** "2026-12-02" as "2 Dec 2026"; anything else as it is. */
export function formatDateText(iso: string | undefined): string {
  const m = ISO.exec(iso ?? '');
  const month = m ? months()[Number(m[2]) - 1] : undefined;
  if (!m || !month) return iso ?? '';
  return `${Number(m[3])} ${month} ${m[1]}`;
}

/** What is typed, read as a real calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`); undefined when it does not read as one. */
export function parseDateText(text: string): string | undefined {
  const typed = text.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/,/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
  if (!typed) return undefined;
  const names = months().map((n) => n.toLowerCase());
  // "dec", "dec.", "december": a word of at least three letters that starts like a month.
  const monthOf = (word: string) => (word.length < 3 ? 0 : names.findIndex((n) => word.startsWith(n) || n.startsWith(word)) + 1);
  let y: number;
  let m: number;
  let d: number;
  let p: RegExpExecArray | null;
  if ((p = /^(\d{4})-(\d{1,2})-(\d{1,2})$/.exec(typed))) [y, m, d] = [Number(p[1]), Number(p[2]), Number(p[3])];
  else if ((p = /^(\d{1,2})[/.-](\d{1,2})[/.-](\d{4})$/.exec(typed))) [d, m, y] = [Number(p[1]), Number(p[2]), Number(p[3])];
  else if ((p = /^(\d{1,2}) ([a-z]+)\.? (\d{4})$/.exec(typed))) [d, m, y] = [Number(p[1]), monthOf(p[2]!), Number(p[3])];
  else if ((p = /^([a-z]+)\.? (\d{1,2}) (\d{4})$/.exec(typed))) [m, d, y] = [monthOf(p[1]!), Number(p[2]), Number(p[3])];
  else return undefined;
  if (!m || m > 12 || !d || y < 1 || y > 9999) return undefined;
  if (d > new Date(Date.UTC(y, m, 0)).getUTCDate()) return undefined;
  return `${String(y).padStart(4, '0')}-${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

type Props = Omit<InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>, 'value' | 'onChange' | 'type' | 'defaultValue'> & {
  /** `YYYY-MM-DD`, or undefined for none. */
  value: string | undefined;
  /** Each time the box reads as a date, that date; undefined when it is emptied or stops reading as one. */
  onChange(next: string | undefined): void;
  /** The calendar button's name: says which date it is for ("Choose the date for Planned release date"). */
  calendarLabel: string;
  /** Shown under the box when what is typed does not read as a date, once the box is left. */
  invalidText: string;
};

/** The date box with its calendar button. Every other prop goes to the text box (its id, aria-describedby ...). */
export const DateField = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, Props>(function DateField(
  { value, onChange, calendarLabel, invalidText, placeholder, className, disabled, onBlur, ...rest },
  ref,
) {
  const shown = formatDateText(value);
  const [text, setText] = useState(shown);
  const [seen, setSeen] = useState(value);
  const [bad, setBad] = useState(false);
  const picker = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const hintId = useId();
  if (seen !== value) {
    // The value changed from outside (or from the calendar): show it, unless it is what is being typed.
    setSeen(value);
    if (parseDateText(text) !== value) setText(shown);
    setBad(false);
  }
  const describedBy = [rest['aria-describedby'], bad ? hintId : undefined].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined;
  return (
    <span className={s.box}>
      <span className={s.row}>
        <input
          ref={ref}
          type="text"
          inputMode="text"
          autoComplete="off"
          className={[f.control, s.text, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}
          placeholder={placeholder ?? formatDateText('2026-12-02')}
          value={text}
          disabled={disabled}
          {...rest}
          aria-invalid={bad || rest['aria-invalid'] || undefined}
          aria-describedby={describedBy}
          onChange={(e) => {
            const next = e.target.value;
            setText(next);
            const date = parseDateText(next);
            if (date || !next.trim()) setBad(false);
            if (date !== value) onChange(date);
          }}
          onBlur={(e) => {
            const date = parseDateText(text);
            if (date) setText(formatDateText(date));
            setBad(!date && text.trim() !== '');
            onBlur?.(e);
          }}
        />
        <button
          type="button"
          className={s.calendar}
          aria-label={calendarLabel}
          title={calendarLabel}
          disabled={disabled}
          onClick={() => {
            const el = picker.current;
            if (!el) return;
            try {
              el.showPicker();
            } catch {
              el.focus();
            }
          }}
        >
          <Icon name="calendar" size={16} />
        </button>
        {/* The browser's own picker, opened by the button; never reached with Tab and never read out. */}
        <input
          ref={picker}
          type="date"
          className={s.picker}
          tabIndex={-1}
          aria-hidden="true"
          value={value ?? ''}
          disabled={disabled}
          onChange={(e) => {
            const date = e.target.value || undefined;
            setText(formatDateText(date));
            setBad(false);
            onChange(date);
          }}
        />
      </span>
      {bad && (
        <span id={hintId} className={s.bad}>
          {invalidText}
        </span>
      )}
    </span>
  );
});

import * as RD from '@radix-ui/react-dialog';
import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { t } from '@/words';
import { IconButton } from './Button';
import s from './Overlay.module.css';

type DialogProps = {
  title: string;
  /** One line under the title; read out when the dialog opens. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  children?: ReactNode;
  /** The buttons at the bottom, primary last. Wrap a button in DialogClose to close on press. */
  footer?: ReactNode;
  trigger?: ReactElement;
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
  width?: number;
  closeLabel?: string;
};

/** A modal dialog. Focus stays inside it until it closes (Radix). */
export function Dialog({ title, description, children, footer, trigger, open, onOpenChange, width = 520, closeLabel = t('common.close') }: DialogProps) {
  return (
    <RD.Root open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
      {trigger && <RD.Trigger asChild>{trigger}</RD.Trigger>}
      <RD.Portal>
        <RD.Overlay className={s.scrim} />
        {/* With no description the dialog is described by nothing (not by its title a second time). */}
        <RD.Content className={s.modal} style={{ width }} {...(description ? {} : { 'aria-describedby': undefined })}>
          <div className={s.modalHead}>
            <RD.Title className={s.modalTitle}>{title}</RD.Title>
            <RD.Close asChild>
              <IconButton icon="close" label={closeLabel} size="sm" tooltip={false} />
            </RD.Close>
          </div>
          {description && <RD.Description className={s.modalDesc}>{description}</RD.Description>}
          {children && <div className={s.modalBody}>{children}</div>}
          {footer && <div className={s.modalFoot}>{footer}</div>}
        </RD.Content>
      </RD.Portal>
    </RD.Root>
  );
}

export const DialogClose = RD.Close;

===\nfrontend/src/ui/Field.tsx\n===
import {
  createContext,
  forwardRef,
  useContext,
  useId,
  type InputHTMLAttributes,
  type ReactNode,
  type SelectHTMLAttributes,
  type TextareaHTMLAttributes,
} from 'react';
import { Icon } from './Icon';
import s from './Field.module.css';

type FieldIds = { id: string; describedBy?: string; invalid: boolean };
const FieldContext = createContext<FieldIds | null>(null);

type FieldProps = {
  label: ReactNode;
  hint?: ReactNode;
  /** Shown under the control, in words, and tied to it for screen readers. */
  error?: ReactNode;
  /** One control: TextInput, TextArea or Select. It picks up the label, hint and error by itself. */
  children: ReactNode;
};

/** A label, an optional hint and error, tied to the one control inside. */
export function Field({ label, hint, error, children }: FieldProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const hintId = hint ? `${id}-hint` : undefined;
  const errorId = error ? `${id}-error` : undefined;
  const describedBy = [hintId, errorId].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined;
  return (
    <div className={s.field}>
      <label className={s.label} htmlFor={id}>
        {label}
      </label>
      <FieldContext.Provider value={{ id, describedBy, invalid: Boolean(error) }}>{children}</FieldContext.Provider>
      {hint && (
        <div id={hintId} className={s.hint}>
          {hint}
        </div>
      )}
      {error && (
        <div id={errorId} className={s.error}>
          <Icon name="error" size={14} />
          <span>{error}</span>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

function useField(ownId?: string) {
  const f = useContext(FieldContext);
  return {
    id: ownId ?? f?.id,
    'aria-describedby': f?.describedBy,
    'aria-invalid': f?.invalid || undefined,
  };
}

export const TextInput = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>>(function TextInput(
  { className, id, type = 'text', ...rest },
  ref,
) {
  return <input ref={ref} type={type} className={[s.control, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')} {...useField(id)} {...rest} />;
});

export const TextArea = forwardRef<HTMLTextAreaElement, TextareaHTMLAttributes<HTMLTextAreaElement>>(function TextArea(
  { className, id, rows = 3, ...rest },
  ref,
) {
  return (
    <textarea
      ref={ref}
      rows={rows}
      className={[s.control, s.textarea, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}
      {...useField(id)}
      {...rest}
    />
  );
});

type SelectProps = SelectHTMLAttributes<HTMLSelectElement> & {
  options: readonly { value: string; label: string }[];
};

/** A native select: the most accessible choice for a short list. */
export const Select = forwardRef<HTMLSelectElement, SelectProps>(function Select({ className, id, options, ...rest }, ref) {
  return (
    <select ref={ref} className={[s.control, s.select, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')} {...useField(id)} {...rest}>
      {options.map((o) => (
        <option key={o.value} value={o.value}>
          {o.label}
        </option>
      ))}
    </select>
  );
});

type CheckboxProps = Omit<InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>, 'type'> & {
  label: ReactNode;
  hint?: ReactNode;
};

export const Checkbox = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, CheckboxProps>(function Checkbox(
  { label, hint, className, id, ...rest },
  ref,
) {
  const ownId = useId();
  const inputId = id ?? ownId;
  const hintId = hint ? `${inputId}-hint` : undefined;
  return (
    <div className={[s.checkRow, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}>
      <input ref={ref} id={inputId} type="checkbox" className={s.checkbox} aria-describedby={hintId} {...rest} />
      <div>
        <label htmlFor={inputId} className={s.checkLabel}>
          {label}
        </label>
        {hint && (
          <div id={hintId} className={s.hint}>
            {hint}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
});

/* Icons ported from the mockup kit: 16x16, 1.5 stroke, hand-written. Decorative unless given a label. */
const paths = {
  // kinds of value

export type IconName = keyof typeof paths;
export const iconNames = Object.keys(paths) as IconName[];

type IconProps = {
  name: IconName;
  /** 14, 16 (default) or 20 */
  size?: number;
  /** Give a label only when the icon carries meaning on its own; otherwise it is hidden from screen readers. */
  label?: string;
  className?: string;
};

export function Icon({ name, size = 16, label, className }: IconProps) {
  return (
    <svg
      viewBox="0 0 16 16"
      width={size}
      height={size}
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth={1.5}
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
      className={className}
      style={{ flex: 'none', display: 'block' }}
      role={label ? 'img' : undefined}
      aria-label={label}
      aria-hidden={label ? undefined : true}
      focusable="false"
      // the paths are constants in this file, never user input
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: paths[name] }}
    />
  );
}

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { t } from '@/words';
import { Icon } from './Icon';
import s from './Mark.module.css';

type MarkProps = {
  /** todo: must be done before publishing (amber). worth: will not stop you (blue). */
  variant: 'todo' | 'worth';
  /** What it is about, in words. The mark always carries its own label too: never colour alone. */
  children?: ReactNode;
};

export function Mark({ variant, children }: MarkProps) {
  const label = t(variant === 'todo' ? 'mark.todo' : 'mark.worth');
  return (
    <span className={`${s.mark} ${s[variant]}`}>
      <Icon name={variant === 'todo' ? 'todo' : 'info'} size={14} />
      <span className={s.label}>
        {label}
        {children ? ':' : ''}
      </span>
      {children && <span className={s.text}>{children}</span>}
    </span>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/ui/Menu.tsx\n===
import * as RM from '@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu';
import { Fragment, type ReactElement } from 'react';
import { Icon, type IconName } from './Icon';
import s from './Overlay.module.css';

export type MenuItem =
  | { label: string; onSelect: () => void; icon?: IconName; danger?: boolean; disabled?: boolean }
  | { group: string }
  | 'separator';

type MenuProps = {
  trigger: ReactElement;
  items: readonly MenuItem[];
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end';
};

/** A list of commands under a button. Arrow keys move, Enter chooses, Escape closes (Radix). */
export function Menu({ trigger, items, align = 'start' }: MenuProps) {
  return (
    <RM.Root>
      <RM.Trigger asChild>{trigger}</RM.Trigger>
      <RM.Portal>
        <RM.Content className={`${s.popover} ${s.menu}`} align={align} sideOffset={6} collisionPadding={12}>
          {items.map((item, i) => (
            <Fragment key={i}>
              {item === 'separator' ? (
                <RM.Separator className={s.menuSep} />
              ) : 'group' in item ? (
                <RM.Label className={s.menuGroup}>{item.group}</RM.Label>
              ) : (
                <RM.Item
                  className={[s.menuItem, item.danger ? s.menuDanger : undefined].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}
                  onSelect={item.onSelect}
                  disabled={item.disabled}
                >
                  {item.icon && <Icon name={item.icon} />}
                  {item.label}
                </RM.Item>
              )}
            </Fragment>
          ))}
        </RM.Content>
      </RM.Portal>
    </RM.Root>
  );
}

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import s from './Page.module.css';

type PageProps = {
  title: ReactNode;
  /** One line under the title: what this page is for. */
  lead?: ReactNode;
  /** Controls on the right of the title (search, the main button). */
  actions?: ReactNode;
  /** narrow: reading width (forms, a request). wide: lists and tables. */
  width?: 'narrow' | 'wide';
  children: ReactNode;
};

/** A page's title row and body, for the pages outside the editor. */
export function Page({ title, lead, actions, width = 'wide', children }: PageProps) {
  return (
    <div className={`${s.page} ${width === 'narrow' ? s.narrow : ''}`}>
      <header className={s.head}>
        <div className={s.headText}>
          <h1 className={s.title}>{title}</h1>
          {/* A div, not a p: a lead may hold block content (the request page's breadcrumb nav). */}
          {lead && <div className={s.lead}>{lead}</div>}
        </div>
        {actions && <div className={s.actions}>{actions}</div>}
      </header>
      <div className={s.body}>{children}</div>
    </div>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/ui/Popover.tsx\n===
import * as RP from '@radix-ui/react-popover';
import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { t } from '@/words';
import { IconButton } from './Button';
import s from './Overlay.module.css';

type PopoverProps = {
  /** The button that opens it. */
  trigger: ReactElement;
  /** Heading of the popover; also its accessible name. */
  title: string;
  /** A quiet line beside the title. */
  sub?: ReactNode;
  children: ReactNode;
  footer?: ReactNode;
  width?: number;
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end';
  open?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
  closeLabel?: string;
};

export function Popover({
  trigger,
  title,
  sub,
  children,
  footer,
  width = 360,
  align = 'start',
  open,
  onOpenChange,
  closeLabel = t('common.close'),
}: PopoverProps) {
  return (
    <RP.Root open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
      <RP.Trigger asChild>{trigger}</RP.Trigger>
      <RP.Portal>
        <RP.Content
          className={s.popover}
          style={{ width }}
          align={align}
          sideOffset={8}
          collisionPadding={12}
          aria-label={title}
        >
          <div className={s.popHead}>
            <div className={s.popTitle}>{title}</div>
            {sub && <span className={s.popSub}>{sub}</span>}
            <RP.Close asChild>
              <IconButton icon="close" label={closeLabel} size="sm" tooltip={false} className={s.popClose} />
            </RP.Close>
          </div>
          <div className={s.popBody}>{children}</div>
          {footer && <div className={s.popFoot}>{footer}</div>}
        </RP.Content>
      </RP.Portal>
    </RP.Root>
  );
}
===\nfrontend/src/ui/README.md\n===
# ui

Design tokens and primitives (docs/08-frontend-design.md, F8). The company's own look replaces this folder and nothing else changes.

- `tokens.css`: colours, type, spacing, radii, shadows as CSS variables, ported from the mockup kit. Everything else uses the variables, never raw colours.
- One primitive per file, each with its own CSS module: Button, IconButton, Icon, Field, TextInput, TextArea, Select, Checkbox, Popover, Dialog, Menu, Tabs, Tooltip, Chip, Mark, Card, EmptyState, Callout, DateField (a date shown and typed as "2 Dec 2026", read leniently by `parseDateText`, with a calendar button that opens the browser's picker; the value is `YYYY-MM-DD`), ExternalLink (a link to another system's page, opening in a new tab: for the model's `WebLink` parts).
- Import from `@/ui` (the barrel), never from a file inside it. `/ui-reference` shows every primitive.
- May import: `words` only. Never `features`, `model`, `services` or `app`.
- Primitives know nothing about workflows: no stage, arrow or value logic here. Add a primitive only when two features need it.

===\nfrontend/src/ui/Tabs.tsx\n===
import * as RT from '@radix-ui/react-tabs';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Icon, type IconName } from './Icon';
import s from './Tabs.module.css';

/** Class names of the segmented tabs, for navigation links that must look the same (the editor's top bar). */
export const tabStyles = { list: s.list, tab: s.tab } as const;

type Tab = { value: string; label: string; icon?: IconName; content: ReactNode };

type TabsProps = {
  /** Read out for the row of tabs. */
  label: string;
  tabs: readonly Tab[];
  defaultValue?: string;
  value?: string;
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void;
  /** "segmented" (grey track, as in the top bar) or "line" (underline, inside panels). */
  look?: 'segmented' | 'line';
};

export function Tabs({ label, tabs, defaultValue, value, onValueChange, look = 'segmented' }: TabsProps) {
  return (
    <RT.Root defaultValue={defaultValue ?? tabs[0]?.value} value={value} onValueChange={onValueChange}>
      <RT.List aria-label={label} className={look === 'line' ? s.lineList : s.list}>
        {tabs.map((tab) => (
          <RT.Trigger key={tab.value} value={tab.value} className={look === 'line' ? s.lineTab : s.tab}>
            {tab.icon && <Icon name={tab.icon} />}
            {tab.label}
          </RT.Trigger>
        ))}
      </RT.List>
      {tabs.map((tab) => (
        <RT.Content key={tab.value} value={tab.value} className={s.content}>
          {tab.content}
        </RT.Content>
      ))}
    </RT.Root>
  );
}

===\nfrontend/src/ui/Tooltip.tsx\n===
import * as RT from '@radix-ui/react-tooltip';
import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react';
import s from './Tooltip.module.css';

type TooltipProps = {
  /** What the tooltip says. Never the only place important information lives. */
  content: ReactNode;
  /** One focusable element (a button or link). */
  children: ReactElement;
  side?: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right';
};

export function Tooltip({ content, children, side = 'bottom' }: TooltipProps) {
  return (
    <RT.Provider delayDuration={300}>
      <RT.Root>
        <RT.Trigger asChild>{children}</RT.Trigger>
        <RT.Portal>
          <RT.Content className={s.tip} side={side} sideOffset={6} collisionPadding={8}>
            {content}
            <RT.Arrow className={s.arrow} />
          </RT.Content>
        </RT.Portal>
      </RT.Root>
    </RT.Provider>
  );
}

===\nfrontend/src/words/README.md\n===
# words

Every label and sentence a person reads (docs/08-frontend-design.md, F5). Engine words never reach a screen.

- `core.ts`: the shared vocabulary from `spec/editor-model.md` section 1, the Glossary, the kinds, versions, and the parts of the top bar that `src/app` draws (back, tabs, Glossary). Change it only with the product owner.
- One file per feature (`workflows.ts`, `diagram.ts`, ...): that feature's own labels, including its top-bar slots (`todo.publish`, `tryit.button`, `panel.settings`, `workflows.saved`). Every key starts with the feature's name (`diagram.addStage`). Add keys only to your feature's file.
- `reference.ts`: sample text for `/ui-reference` (src/app).
- `index.ts` merges them; use `t('key', { name: 'value' })` for `{name}` substitution, and `WordKey` for typed keys.
- `tests/unit/words.test.ts` fails on a key in the wrong file or a key defined twice.
- Imports nothing from the rest of `src`.

// Words for src/model/describe/finding.ts: every To do and Worth knowing item said once, the same
// on the stage box, the stage panel's strip, the To do drawer and In words. Every key starts with
// "findings.". Per finding: `short` (under a stage box, at most about 8 words), `cause` (what is
// wrong, with the things' current names), `effect` (what would happen to a request), `fix` (the
// label of the one obvious fix). Never the engine's terms, never an ID, never blame.

/**
 * Every label a person reads (F5). Import `t` and `WordKey` from here.
 * Shared vocabulary lives in core.ts; each feature adds its own words in its own file
 * (keys prefixed with the feature's name), so no builder edits a shared file.
 */
import { core } from './core';
import { workflows } from './workflows';
import { diagram } from './diagram';
import { panel } from './panel';
import { values } from './values';
import { conditions } from './conditions';
import { forms } from './forms';
import { actions } from './actions';
import { connections } from './connections';
import { inwords } from './inwords';
import { todo } from './todo';
import { tryit } from './tryit';
import { requests } from './requests';
import { reference } from './reference';
import { describe } from './describe';
import { findings } from './findings';

/** Each feature's words, by the prefix its keys must carry. Checked by tests/unit/words.test.ts. */
export const wordFiles = {
  core,
  workflows,
  diagram,
  panel,
  values,
  conditions,
  forms,
  actions,
  connections,
  inwords,
  todo,
  tryit,
  requests,
  reference,
  describe,
  findings,
} as const;

export const words = {
  ...core,
  ...workflows,
  ...diagram,
  ...panel,
  ...values,
  ...conditions,
  ...forms,
  ...actions,
  ...connections,
  ...inwords,
  ...todo,
  ...tryit,
  ...requests,
  ...reference,
  ...describe,
  ...findings,
} as const;

export type WordKey = keyof typeof words;
export type WordParams = Record<string, string | number>;

/** The words for `key`, with each {name} replaced by params.name. A missing param is left as {name}, so it shows up. */
export function t(key: WordKey, params?: WordParams): string {
  const text: string = words[key];
  if (!params) return text;
  return text.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (whole, name: string) =>
    Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(params, name) ? String(params[name]) : whole,
  );
}

/** The seven Glossary words, in the order shown (spec section 9). */
export const glossary = [
  { word: 'word.stage', line: 'glossary.stage.line', where: 'glossary.stage.where', pic: 'stage' },
  { word: 'word.task', line: 'glossary.task.line', where: 'glossary.task.where', pic: 'task' },
  { word: 'word.arrow', line: 'glossary.arrow.line', where: 'glossary.arrow.where', pic: 'arrow' },
  { word: 'word.value', line: 'glossary.value.line', where: 'glossary.value.where', pic: 'value' },
  { word: 'word.kind', line: 'glossary.kind.line', where: 'glossary.kind.where', pic: 'kind' },
  { word: 'word.todo', line: 'glossary.todo.line', where: 'glossary.todo.where', pic: 'todo' },
  { word: 'word.stuck', line: 'glossary.stuck.line', where: 'glossary.stuck.where', pic: 'stuck' },
] as const satisfies readonly { word: WordKey; line: WordKey; where: WordKey; pic: string }[];

export type StageKind = 'form' | 'approval' | 'work' | 'automatic' | 'ending' | 'blank';
export const stageKinds: readonly StageKind[] = ['form', 'approval', 'work', 'automatic', 'ending', 'blank'];

// Words for features/tryit. Every key starts with "tryit.".
// `{name}` marks where a name or a chip goes. The built-in messages, the stuck reasons and the

import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';

/** The editor store the dev build puts on the page (src/app/main.tsx), seen from the test. */
type Action = { id: string; type: string; to?: unknown; message?: unknown[] };
type EditorOnPage = {
  getState(): {
    doc: { stages: { id: string; kind: string; whenThisStageStarts?: Action[] }[] } | null;
    saveState: string;
    select(selection: { item: string } | null): void;
  };
};
type Win = Window & { __editor?: EditorOnPage };

const startActions = (page: import('@playwright/test').Page, stage: string) =>
  page.evaluate((id) => (window as Win).__editor?.getState().doc?.stages.find((s) => s.id === id)?.whenThisStageStarts ?? [], stage);

/**
 * Opens a stage in the panel through the store's selection (what clicking its box does). Clicking a
 * box was flaky while the diagram settles its layout: the click could land on a neighbour.
 */
async function openStage(page: import('@playwright/test').Page, stage: string) {
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as Win).__editor?.getState().doc);
  await expect
    .poll(async () => {
      await page.evaluate((id) => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().select({ item: id }), stage);
      return page.locator('[data-section="whenThisStageStarts"]').count();
    })
    .toBeGreaterThan(0);
}

test('add Notify to a stage, choose who and write the message', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/#/w/change-request');
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as Win).__editor?.getState().doc);
  const box = page.locator('.react-flow__node[data-id="st_development"]');
  await openStage(page, 'st_development');

  const section = page.locator('[data-section="whenThisStageStarts"]');
  await section.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add an action or save a value' }).click();
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu');
  await expect(menu.getByRole('group', { name: 'Built in' })).toBeVisible();
  await menu.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /^Notify/ }).click();

  await expect.poll(async () => (await startActions(page, 'st_development')).map((a) => a.type)).toEqual(['notify']);
  const card = section.locator('[data-action-id]').first();
  await expect(card).toContainText("If this can't be sent, the request carries on.");

  // Who: the value picker (features/values). Its button is named after the slot's label.
  await card.getByRole('button', { name: /^Who is notified/ }).click();
  await page.getByRole('option', { name: /^Requester/ }).first().click();
  // The message (features/values' MessageField).
  const message = card.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Message' });
  await message.click();
  await page.keyboard.type('Work on your change has started');
  await message.blur();

  await expect.poll(async () => (await startActions(page, 'st_development'))[0]).toMatchObject({
    type: 'notify',
    to: { request: 'requester' },
  });
  await expect
    .poll(async () => JSON.stringify((await startActions(page, 'st_development'))[0]?.message ?? []))
    .toContain('Work on your change has started');
  await expect(card.getByRole('button', { expanded: true }).first()).toContainText('Notify Requester');

  // Its chip on the stage box, when the diagram draws boxes.
  if (await box.count()) await expect(box).toContainText('Notify Requester');

  // Done closes it and puts focus back on its name.
  await card.getByRole('button', { name: 'Done' }).click();
  await expect(card.getByRole('button', { expanded: false }).first()).toBeFocused();
  await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().saveState)).toBe('saved');
});

for (const height of [800, 600]) {
  test(`the add menu stays inside a ${height}px window and below the top bar`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height });
    await page.goto('/#/w/change-request');
    await openStage(page, 'st_domain_approval');

    const section = page.locator('[data-section="afterTheyRespond"]');
    const button = section.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add an action or save a value' });

    const menu = page.getByRole('menu');
    await expect(menu.getByRole('group', { name: 'Built in' })).toBeVisible();
    // Wait for the placement to settle, then the whole box must be on screen.

    const rect = await menu.boundingBox();
    expect(rect).not.toBeNull();
    expect(rect!.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    expect(rect!.y + rect!.height).toBeLessThanOrEqual(height);
    // It does not cover the top bar.
    if (bar) expect(rect!.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(bar.y + bar.height);
    // The first choice can be clicked with the mouse.
    await menu.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /^Save a value/ }).click();
    await expect(menu).toHaveCount(0);
  });
}

/**
 * Every result name on the card: its arrow sits after the name, on the name's line, and before the
 * value (open-defects actions 1: the arrow wrapped under "Owner").
 */
async function arrowsBetween(card: import('@playwright/test').Locator) {
  return card.evaluate((el) =>
    Array.from(el.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-result-name]')).map((row) => {
      const name = row.querySelector('span')!.getBoundingClientRect();
      const arrow = row.querySelector('svg')!.getBoundingClientRect();
      const value = (row.nextElementSibling as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect();
      const mid = arrow.top + arrow.height / 2;
      return {
        name: row.textContent,
        afterName: arrow.left >= name.right - 1,
        beforeValue: arrow.right <= value.left + 1,
        onNameLine: mid >= name.top && mid <= name.bottom,
      };
    }),
  );
}

for (const width of [1024, 1440]) {
  test(`a result's arrow sits between its name and its value at ${width}px, closed and open, also in a narrow card`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 900 });
    await page.goto('/#/w/integrated-sample');
    await openStage(page, 'st_find_owner');
    const card = page.locator('[data-action-id="act_look_up_service"]');
    const ok = { afterName: true, beforeValue: true, onNameLine: true };
    // Closed, the results it saves, in the catalogue's order; open, every result the catalogue gives (Draft 3 catalogue).
    const closed = ['Tier', 'Owner'].map((name) => ({ name, ...ok }));
    const open = ['Service ID', 'Name', 'Tier', 'Status', 'Owner'].map((name) => ({ name, ...ok }));
    await expect.poll(() => arrowsBetween(card)).toEqual(closed);
    // Open, the editor's rows.
    await card.getByRole('button', { name: /^Look up a service/ }).click();
    await expect(card.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'The value Owner is saved as' })).toBeVisible();
    await expect.poll(() => arrowsBetween(card)).toEqual(open);
    // However narrow the panel gets.
    await card.evaluate((el) => (el.style.width = '240px'));
    await expect.poll(() => arrowsBetween(card)).toEqual(open);
  });
}

import { expect, test, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

/** The editor store the dev build puts on the page (src/app/main.tsx), seen from the test. */
type EditorOnPage = {
  getState(): {
    saveState: string;
    revision: number;
    doc: { stages: { id: string; name: string }[] } | null;
    run(name: string, args: unknown): unknown;
  };
};
type Win = Window & { __editor?: EditorOnPage };

const stageName = (page: Page, id: string) =>
  page.evaluate((stage) => (window as Win).__editor?.getState().doc?.stages.find((s) => s.id === stage)?.name, id);

test('the editor opens the demo workflow, and an edit survives a reload (autosave)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/#/w/change-request');
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Views of this workflow' })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle('Change request');
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor?.getState().revision)).toBe(12);

  const name = 'Shipped to everyone';
  await page.evaluate(
    (n) => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().run('stage.rename', { stage: 'st_released', name: n }),
    name,
  );
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().saveState)).toBe('unsaved');
  await expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().saveState)).toBe('saved');
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().revision)).toBe(13);

  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Views of this workflow' })).toBeVisible();
  await expect.poll(() => stageName(page, 'st_released')).toBe(name);
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().revision)).toBe(13);
});

test('undo and redo work from the keyboard and the top bar', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/#/w/change-request');
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Views of this workflow' })).toBeVisible();
  const before = await stageName(page, 'st_released');
  await page.evaluate(() => (window as Win).__editor!.getState().run('stage.rename', { stage: 'st_released', name: 'Gone live' }));
  await page.locator('body').click({ position: { x: 5, y: 600 } });
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+z');
  expect(await stageName(page, 'st_released')).toBe(before);
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+Shift+z');
  expect(await stageName(page, 'st_released')).toBe('Gone live');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Undo a change to a stage' }).click();
  expect(await stageName(page, 'st_released')).toBe(before);
});

    await page.goto(route);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

import { expect, test, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * features/conditions in the running app: the "when ..." builder in the stage panel and the
 * formula editor. The stage is chosen through the development store (window.__editor), so the
 * test does not depend on how the diagram draws it.
 */

type EditorStore = { getState(): { doc: unknown; select(sel: { item: string }): void } };

async function openStage(page: Page, stageId: string) {
  await page.goto('/#/w/change-request');
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as unknown as { __editor?: EditorStore }).__editor?.getState().doc);
  await page.evaluate((id) => (window as unknown as { __editor: EditorStore }).__editor.getState().select({ item: id }), stageId);
}

const arrow = (page: Page, id: string) =>
  page.evaluate((arrowId) => {
    const doc = (window as unknown as { __editor: EditorStore }).__editor.getState().doc as { stages: { arrows?: { id: string }[] }[] };
    return doc.stages.flatMap((s) => s.arrows ?? []).find((a) => a.id === arrowId);
  }, id);

/**
 * "+ only when ..." on a button's arrow: the panel either fills that arrow's "only when" or adds a
 * new arrow placed above it, so the builder is found by its own controls, not by the arrow's ID.
 */
async function startOnlyWhen(page: Page, arrowId: string) {
  const host = page.locator(`[data-at="${arrowId}"]`).first();
  await host.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
  await host.getByRole('button', { name: '+ only when ...' }).click();
  const when = page.locator('[data-at]').filter({ has: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Write a formula' }) }).first();
  await expect(when.getByRole('button', { name: /^Part 1: answer or value/ })).toBeVisible();
  return when;
}

test.beforeEach(async ({ context }) => {
  await context.clearCookies();
});

    });

  await host.getByRole('button', { name: 'Remove this "when ..."' }).click();
